tokens.description: The Battle of Britain was a campaign of the Second World War in which the Royal Air Force defended the United Kingdom against attacks by the German Luftwaffe. It was the first major military campaign fought entirely by air forces.
tokens.image_credit: Skyden67 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dunkirk evacuation
tokens.title: Allied troops rescued from the beaches
tokens.description: Operation Dynamo evacuated more than 338,000 Allied soldiers from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk, France, between 26 May and 4 June 1940. The troops had been encircled during the Battle of France.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Berlin
tokens.title: Final major battle in Europe
tokens.description: The Battle of Berlin was one of the last major offensives of the European theatre of World War II, fought by the Red Army against German forces in April and May 1945. It ended with the capture of the German capital.
tokens.image_credit: Yevgeny Khaldei / Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuremberg trials
tokens.title: Nazi leaders tried for war crimes
tokens.description: The Nuremberg trials were international criminal trials held in Nuremberg by France, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and the United States. They prosecuted leaders of defeated Nazi Germany for plotting invasions and committing atrocities in the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: Raymond D'Addario · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
tokens.title: Thirteen days on the nuclear brink
tokens.description: The Cuban Missile Crisis was a 13-day confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union over Soviet nuclear missiles deployed in Cuba. It lasted from 16 to 28 October 1962 and is widely considered the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.

tokens.name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
tokens.title: Failed exile landing in Cuba
tokens.description: The Bay of Pigs Invasion was a failed landing in April 1961 on the southwestern coast of Cuba by Cuban exiles of the Democratic Revolutionary Front, backed by the United States. It took place at Playa Giron and influenced relations between Cuba, the United States and the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: Rumlin · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuban Revolution
tokens.title: Castro's forces take Havana
tokens.description: The Cuban Revolution was the military and political movement that overthrew the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, who had ruled Cuba from 1952 to 1959. Castro's forces entered Havana in January 1959.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph: Lester Cole/Corbis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Saigon
tokens.title: North Vietnamese tanks enter Saigon
tokens.description: Saigon, capital of South Vietnam, was captured by North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975, ending the Vietnam War. The fall caused the evacuation of thousands of civilians and American personnel.
tokens.image_credit: Hubert van Es · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
tokens.title: French defeat ends colonial rule
tokens.description: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu was a defeat of French Union forces by the Viet Minh in the First Indochina War, fought from 13 March to 7 May 1954. It took place in northwest Tonkin, deep in the Tai Federation area.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Inchon
tokens.title: MacArthur's amphibious reversal
tokens.description: The Battle of Inchon was an amphibious invasion during the Korean War that resulted in a decisive victory and strategic reversal for the United Nations Command. The landings led to the recapture of Seoul two weeks later.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Partition of India
tokens.title: Independence and division
tokens.description: The Partition of India in 1947 divided British India into the Union of India and the Dominion of Pakistan. The division of the provinces of Bengal and the Punjab followed district-wide religious majorities.
tokens.image_credit: Photo Division, Government of India · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
tokens.title: Shot at Birla House, Delhi
tokens.description: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 in the compound of Birla House in central New Delhi, now the Gandhi Smriti museum. His assassin was Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist from Pune.
tokens.image_credit: Wilson Loo Kok Wee · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salt March
tokens.title: Gandhi marches to Dandi
tokens.description: The Salt March was a 24-day nonviolent civil disobedience march led by Mahatma Gandhi in colonial India, from 12 March to 6 April 1930. It protested the British salt monopoly and ended at the coastal village of Dandi.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Long March
tokens.title: Communist retreat across China
tokens.description: The Long March was a military retreat by the Chinese Communist Party and Red Army from October 1934 to October 1935. About 100,000 troops travelled roughly 10,000 kilometres from Jiangxi to a new headquarters in Yan'an, Shaanxi.

tokens.name: Nanjing Massacre
tokens.title: Atrocities in the captured city
tokens.description: The Nanjing Massacre was the mass rape and murder of Chinese civilians and prisoners of war by the Imperial Japanese Army in Nanjing, between December 1937 and March 1938. It followed the Battle of Nanjing during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
tokens.image_credit: 上野特派员(scanned by Sweeper tamonten (talk on December 25, 2008) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cultural Revolution
tokens.title: Mass political upheaval in China
tokens.description: The Cultural Revolution was a sociopolitical movement in the People's Republic of China, launched by Mao Zedong in 1966 and lasting until his death in 1976. Its stated goal was to purge remnants of capitalist and traditional elements from Chinese society and government.
tokens.image_credit: 《人民画报》 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Chinese Famine
tokens.title: Famine following the Great Leap Forward
tokens.description: The Great Chinese Famine was a famine in the People's Republic of China that occurred between 1959 and 1961. Some scholars also include the years 1958 or 1962.

tokens.name: Iranian Revolution
tokens.title: Monarchy falls in Tehran
tokens.description: The Iranian Revolution culminated in 1979 in the overthrow of the Pahlavi dynasty and the creation of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Ruhollah Khomeini became the country's supreme leader.

tokens.name: Iran hostage crisis
tokens.title: US embassy staff held 444 days
tokens.description: The Iran hostage crisis began on 4 November 1979, when students stormed the US Embassy in Tehran and took 66 Americans hostage. 52 of them were held until 20 January 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soviet-Afghan War
tokens.title: Soviet forces enter Kabul
tokens.description: The Soviet Union and the Communist-led Afghan military fought the Afghan mujahideen from December 1979 to February 1989. The war marked the beginning of the 47-year-long Afghan conflict.
tokens.image_credit: erwinlux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gulf War
tokens.title: Coalition liberates Kuwait
tokens.description: The Gulf War was an armed conflict between Iraq and a 42-country coalition led by the United States, after Iraq invaded Kuwait on 2 August 1990. The American-led coalition liberated Kuwait on 28 February 1991.
tokens.image_credit: US Air Force · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2003 invasion of Iraq
tokens.title: Coalition forces enter Iraq
tokens.description: The 2003 invasion of Iraq was the first stage of the Iraq War and began on 20 March 2003. A United States-led coalition of mainly American, British, Australian and Polish troops conducted it.
tokens.image_credit: Lance Cpl. Brian L. Wickliffe, U.S. Marine Corps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Baghdad 2003
tokens.title: Saddam statue toppled in Firdos Square
tokens.description: The Battle of Baghdad (2003), also known as the Fall of Baghdad, was a military engagement in early April 2003 as part of the invasion of Iraq. Coalition forces led by the US Army 3rd Infantry Division captured the city.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Marine Lieutenant Tim McLaughlin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Saddam Hussein
tokens.title: Found near Tikrit
tokens.description: Saddam Hussein, the deposed president of Iraq, was captured by United States forces in Ad-Dawr, Iraq, on 13 December 2003. The operation was codenamed Operation Red Dawn.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Killing of Osama bin Laden
tokens.title: Raid on Abbottabad compound
tokens.description: On 2 May 2011 the United States conducted Operation Neptune Spear, in which SEAL Team Six killed Osama bin Laden at his compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
tokens.image_credit: Sajjad Ali Qureshi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arab Spring
tokens.title: Uprisings begin in Sidi Bouzid
tokens.description: The Arab Spring was a series of pro-democracy protests, uprisings and armed rebellions that spread across much of the Arab world in the early 2010s. It began in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, after the self-immolation of Mohamed Bouazizi.
tokens.image_credit: cjb · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2011 Egyptian revolution
tokens.title: Tahrir Square uprising
tokens.description: The 2011 Egyptian revolution, also known as the 25 January Revolution, began on 25 January 2011 and spread across Egypt. It consisted of demonstrations, occupations of plazas, civil resistance and strikes against police brutality under Hosni Mubarak.
tokens.image_credit: Mona · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rwandan genocide
tokens.title: One hundred days of mass killing
tokens.description: The Rwandan genocide, also known as the genocide against Tutsi, took place from 7 April to 19 July 1994. Over about 100 days, Hutu militias systematically killed Tutsi and some moderate Hutu and Twa.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Jones, Ph.D. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1994 South African general election
tokens.title: First multiracial elections
tokens.description: The 1994 South African general election was held from 26 to 29 April 1994. It was the first in which citizens of all races could vote, and it marked the end of apartheid.

tokens.name: Sharpeville massacre
tokens.title: Police fire on protesters
tokens.description: The Sharpeville massacre occurred on 21 March 1960, when South African police opened fire on a crowd protesting the apartheid pass laws. It took place outside the police station in the township of Sharpeville.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soweto uprising
tokens.title: Student protest over Afrikaans
tokens.description: The Soweto uprising was a series of protests by black schoolchildren in the Soweto township, South Africa, beginning on 16 June 1976. The students opposed the use of Afrikaans as the medium of instruction in black schools.
tokens.image_credit: Sam Nzima · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Adwa
tokens.title: Ethiopia defeats Italian invasion
tokens.description: The Battle of Adwa was fought on 1 March 1896 near the town of Adwa between Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II and an Italian colonial army. The Ethiopian victory ended the Italian attempt to impose a protectorate over Ethiopia.
tokens.image_credit: Franko Khoury. · PDM-owner · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Isandlwana
tokens.title: Zulu victory over British column
tokens.description: The Battle of Isandlwana was fought on 22 January 1879 in the Anglo-Zulu War. A Zulu force of some 20,000 warriors attacked a British column of about 1,800 troops and won a major victory.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Edwin Fripp · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Rorke's Drift
tokens.title: Defence of a mission station
tokens.description: The Battle of Rorke's Drift was an engagement in the Anglo-Zulu War, fought at a Swedish mission station and British supply depot. A vastly outnumbered British force held the post, and the battle holds the record for the most Victoria Crosses awarded for a single battle.
tokens.image_credit: Alphonse de Neuville · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Suez Crisis
tokens.title: Canal nationalisation leads to invasion
tokens.description: The Suez Crisis was a 1956 invasion of Egypt by the United Kingdom, France and Israel, launched after Egypt nationalised the Suez Canal. The invaders aimed to depose President Gamal Abdel Nasser and regain control of the canal.
tokens.image_credit: United States Army Heritage and Education Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Six-Day War
tokens.title: Rapid war reshapes the Middle East
tokens.description: The Six-Day War was fought from 5 to 10 June 1967 between Israel and a coalition of six Arab states, primarily Egypt, Syria and Jordan. Israel occupied the Sinai Peninsula, the Gaza Strip, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights.
tokens.image_credit: Rafi Rogel (רפי רוגל) · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yom Kippur War
tokens.title: Surprise attack on Yom Kippur
tokens.description: The Yom Kippur War was fought from 6 to 25 October 1973 between Israel and a coalition of Arab states led by Egypt and Syria. Most of the fighting took place in the Sinai Peninsula and the Golan Heights.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oslo Accords
tokens.title: Rabin and Arafat shake hands
tokens.description: The Oslo Accords are two interim agreements between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization, Oslo I signed in Washington in 1993 and Oslo II signed in Taba in 1995. They started the Oslo peace process, based on UN Resolutions 242 and 338.
tokens.image_credit: Vince Musi / The White House · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United States Declaration of Independence
tokens.title: Thirteen colonies declare independence
tokens.description: The founding document of the United States, adopted unanimously by the Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia on 4 July 1776. It was adopted in the Pennsylvania State House, later renamed Independence Hall.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boston Tea Party
tokens.title: Tea thrown into the harbor
tokens.description: The Boston Tea Party was a protest on 16 December 1773, staged by the Sons of Liberty in Boston against British tea policy. Colonists threw a cargo of British tea into Boston Harbor, escalating tensions with Great Britain.
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was Cornischong at lb.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
tokens.title: Shot heard round the world
tokens.description: The Battles of Lexington and Concord on 19 April 1775 were the first major military actions between British troops and Patriot militias in the American Revolutionary War. The fighting took place in Middlesex County, Massachusetts.
tokens.image_credit: Don Troiani · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Yorktown
tokens.title: Cornwallis surrenders
tokens.description: The Siege of Yorktown, fought in Virginia in 1781, was the final major land engagement of the American Revolutionary War. Continental and French forces defeated the British army commanded by Charles Cornwallis.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Louisiana Purchase
tokens.title: US doubles in size
tokens.description: The Louisiana Purchase was the 1803 acquisition by the United States from the French First Republic of about 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River, for $15 million. The transfer ceremony took place in New Orleans.
tokens.image_credit: Matysik · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Alamo
tokens.title: Texian defenders fall in San Antonio
tokens.description: The Battle of the Alamo, fought from February 23 to March 6, 1836, was a pivotal engagement of the Texas Revolution in San Antonio. Mexican troops under Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna took the Alamo Mission after a 13-day siege.
tokens.image_credit: Loadmaster (David R. Tribble) This image was made by Loadmaster (David R. Tribble). Email the author: David R. Tribble Also see my personal gallery at Google Photos · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
tokens.title: Custer's last stand
tokens.description: The Battle of the Little Bighorn, fought on June 25 and 26, 1876 in southeastern Montana, was a defeat of the United States 7th Cavalry Regiment. It is also known as Custer's Last Stand and was the most significant action of the Great Sioux War.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Marion Russell · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wounded Knee Massacre
tokens.title: Lakota killed in South Dakota
tokens.description: The Wounded Knee Massacre was an 1890 armed conflict in South Dakota between the United States Army and Native Americans, part of the Pine Ridge Campaign. Between 250 and 300 Lakota people were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Frederic Remington · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: California gold rush
tokens.title: Gold found at Sutter's Mill
tokens.description: The California gold rush (1848 to 1855) began when gold was found at Sutter's Mill in Coloma on January 24, 1848. It brought about 300,000 people to California and helped the territory grow rapidly into statehood through the Compromise of 1850.
tokens.image_credit: George H. Johnson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Chicago Fire
tokens.title: City center burns
tokens.description: The Great Chicago Fire burned in Chicago, Illinois, from October 8 to 10, 1871. It killed approximately 300 people and destroyed about 17,000 structures.
tokens.image_credit: Currier and Ives · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1906 San Francisco earthquake
tokens.title: Quake and fires devastate city
tokens.description: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake, a magnitude 7.9 event, struck the coast of Northern California on April 18, 1906. Extensive fires broke out in San Francisco and burned for several days.
tokens.image_credit: Chadwick, H. D · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wall Street crash of 1929
tokens.title: Black Tuesday stock collapse
tokens.description: The Wall Street crash of 1929 was a sharp collapse of US stock prices that began on the New York Stock Exchange in October 1929. It eroded confidence in the American banking system and helped trigger the Great Depression.
tokens.image_credit: US-gov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dust Bowl
tokens.title: Dust storms ravage the Great Plains
tokens.description: The Dust Bowl was a period of severe dust storms in the 1930s that damaged farming and ecology across the American and Canadian prairies. Drought and the loss of topsoil from poor farming methods caused it.
tokens.image_credit: Arthur Rothstein · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Katrina
tokens.title: New Orleans floods after levee failures
tokens.description: Hurricane Katrina was a catastrophic tropical cyclone that struck the US Gulf Coast in late August 2005. It caused its greatest damage in and around New Orleans and killed 1,392 people.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montgomery bus boycott
tokens.title: Year-long protest after Rosa Parks arrest
tokens.description: The Montgomery bus boycott was a campaign against racial segregation on the public buses of Montgomery, Alabama, from 1955 to 1956. It began after Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her seat, and it was a foundational event of the civil rights movement.
tokens.image_credit: Gene Herrick for the Associated Press; restored by Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: March on Washington
tokens.title: "I Have a Dream" speech
tokens.description: The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom was held in Washington, D.C., on August 28, 1963, to advocate for the civil and economic rights of African Americans. It is known for Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech.
tokens.image_credit: This photograph was made by Rowland Scherman at the March on Washington. The negatives are in the custody of the National Archives. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Selma to Montgomery marches
tokens.title: Bloody Sunday on Edmund Pettus Bridge
tokens.description: The Selma to Montgomery marches were three protest marches held in 1965 along the 54-mile highway from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama. They demanded voting rights for African Americans and contributed to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
tokens.image_credit: Abernathy Family · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
tokens.title: Shot at the Lorraine Motel
tokens.description: Martin Luther King Jr., an American civil rights activist, was fatally shot on April 4, 1968, at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee. The shooting took place at about 6:01 p.m. local time.
tokens.image_credit: Bubba73 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Watergate scandal
tokens.title: Break-in that toppled a president
tokens.description: The Watergate scandal was a political scandal involving the administration of President Richard Nixon. It began with the June 17, 1972 break-in at the Democratic National Committee headquarters in the Watergate complex in Washington, D.C., and led to Nixon's resignation in August 1974.
tokens.image_credit: Farragutful · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kent State shootings
tokens.title: National Guard fires on students
tokens.description: The Kent State shootings were the killing of four and wounding of nine students by the Ohio National Guard on the Kent State University campus on May 4, 1970. The shootings occurred during a protest against the expansion of the Vietnam War into Cambodia.
tokens.image_credit: Pacificboyksu · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Plassey
tokens.title: Clive wins Bengal for the East India Company
tokens.description: The Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company under Robert Clive over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757. The betrayal of Mir Jafar, the Nawab's commander in chief, was a key factor in the result.
tokens.image_credit: Francis Hayman · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
tokens.title: Uprising begins at Meerut
tokens.description: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 was a major uprising against the rule of the British East India Company in India in 1857 and 1858. It began on 10 May 1857 as a mutiny of sepoys at Meerut and spread to other regions.
tokens.image_credit: Henry Martens · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jallianwala Bagh massacre
tokens.title: Troops fire on a gathering in Amritsar
tokens.description: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar, when British Indian troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired on a large crowd gathered in the garden. The crowd had assembled to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of activists.
tokens.image_credit: Sukanta Pal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Battle of Panipat
tokens.title: Babur founds the Mughal Empire
tokens.description: The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526 between the forces of Babur and Ibrahim Khan Lodi, Sultan of Delhi, in North India. Babur's use of gunpowder firearms and cannons helped him defeat Ibrahim.
tokens.image_credit: 1598 artist · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kalinga War
tokens.title: Ashoka's conquest and turn to peace
tokens.description: The Kalinga War was fought around 261 BCE between the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka and the kingdom of Kalinga on India's east coast. It is presumed to have been fought on the Dhauli hills near Bhubaneswar and was one of the deadliest battles in Indian history.
tokens.image_credit: Sailesh Patnaik · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Haldighati
tokens.title: Maharana Pratap faces Mughal forces
tokens.description: The Battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 between the Mewar forces of Maharana Pratap and the Mughal forces led by Man Singh I of Amber. The Mughals won the field, but Pratap was not captured and retreated.
tokens.image_credit: Chokha · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bhopal disaster
tokens.title: Gas leak at the Union Carbide plant
tokens.description: The Bhopal disaster was a toxic gas leak on 3 December 1984 at the Union Carbide India pesticide plant in Bhopal, India. Over 500,000 people were exposed to methyl isocyanate, in what is considered the world's worst industrial disaster.
tokens.image_credit: Bhopal Medical Appeal, Martin Stott · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
tokens.title: Magnitude 9.1 quake off Sumatra
tokens.description: A magnitude 9.2 to 9.3 undersea earthquake off Aceh, Sumatra, on 26 December 2004 triggered a tsunami that killed about 228,000 people in 14 countries. The token sits on the nearest coast, at Meulaboh, because the epicentre lies at sea.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Photographer's Mate 2nd Class Philip A. McDaniel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa
tokens.title: Heard thousands of kilometres away
tokens.description: The 27 August 1883 eruption of Krakatoa in the Sunda Strait destroyed over 70% of the island and is one of the deadliest volcanic events in recorded history. The token sits on the coastal town of Anyer, Java, about 50 km away, because the volcano lies at sea.
tokens.image_credit: Lithograph: Parker & Coward, Britain; · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora
tokens.title: Year Without a Summer follows
tokens.description: In April 1815 Mount Tambora, a volcano on Sumbawa, Indonesia, erupted in the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded human history, rated VEI 7. It is the most recent confirmed VEI-7 eruption.

tokens.name: Proclamation of Indonesian Independence
tokens.title: Sukarno reads the declaration in Jakarta
tokens.description: The Proclamation of Indonesian Independence was read in Jakarta on 17 August 1945 and signed by Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta. It started the Indonesian National Revolution, which ended when the Netherlands acknowledged Indonesia's independence in 1949.
tokens.image_credit: Frans Mendur (also Frans Mendoer) (1913 – 1971) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Surabaya
tokens.title: Origin of Heroes' Day
tokens.description: The Battle of Surabaya in November 1945 was the largest single battle of the Indonesian National Revolution. It was fought between Indonesian forces and British and British Indian troops, and became a national symbol of Indonesian resistance.
tokens.image_credit: Sergeant Desmond Davis, No. 9 Army Film and Photographic Unit · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: People Power Revolution
tokens.title: Peaceful uprising on EDSA
tokens.description: The People Power Revolution, also called the EDSA Revolution, was a series of demonstrations in Metro Manila from 22 to 25 February 1986. It led to the departure of Ferdinand Marcos and ended his 20-year dictatorship.
tokens.image_credit: Patrick Roque · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Mactan
tokens.title: Lapulapu's forces defeat Magellan
tokens.description: The Battle of Mactan on 27 April 1521 saw Lapulapu's forces defeat a Spanish contingent led by Ferdinand Magellan. Magellan was killed in the fighting on Mactan Island, now part of Cebu, Philippines.
tokens.image_credit: Carl Frances Morano Diaman · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Manila 1945
tokens.title: Month-long urban battle
tokens.description: The Battle of Manila, from 3 February to 3 March 1945, was fought by US and Philippine forces against Imperial Japanese troops in the Philippine capital. The month-long battle devastated the city and killed at least 100,000 civilians.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Unknown photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thrilla in Manila
tokens.title: Ali versus Frazier III
tokens.description: Thrilla in Manila was the third and final boxing match between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, held on 1 October 1975 at the Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City. The bout was conceded after fourteen rounds.
tokens.image_credit: Hariboneagle927 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
tokens.title: Largest naval battle of World War II
tokens.description: The Battle of Leyte Gulf, fought 23 to 26 October 1944, was the largest naval battle of World War II. The Suluan Raid that opened the battle is commemorated at Guiuan on Samar.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bataan Death March
tokens.title: Prisoners marched after Bataan fell
tokens.description: The Bataan Death March was the forced transfer of about 72,000 to 78,000 prisoners of war by the Imperial Japanese Army from April 1942. It ran from Bagac and Mariveles on the Bataan Peninsula to Camp O'Donnell.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Corregidor
tokens.title: Last Allied stand in the Philippines
tokens.description: The Battle of Corregidor, fought on 5 and 6 May 1942, was the culmination of the Japanese campaign to conquer the Philippines. It was fought on the island fortress guarding the entrance to Manila Bay.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Typhoon Haiyan
tokens.title: One of the strongest tropical cyclones recorded
tokens.description: Typhoon Haiyan, known in the Philippines as Super Typhoon Yolanda, struck the Philippines in early November 2013. It is one of the most intense tropical cyclones ever recorded and killed at least 6,300 people in the Visayas alone.
tokens.image_credit: Lawrence Ruiz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Sekigahara
tokens.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins control of Japan
tokens.description: The Battle of Sekigahara, fought on 21 October 1600 in what is now Gifu Prefecture, ended with a victory for Tokugawa Ieyasu. It is often regarded as the most important battle in Japanese history.
tokens.image_credit: Collection of The City of Gifu Museum of History · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Meiji Restoration
tokens.title: Imperial rule restored in Kyoto
tokens.description: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 restored imperial rule to Japan under Emperor Meiji. It led to the Westernisation and rapid industrialisation of the country.
tokens.image_credit: Yūki Somei 結城素明 (1875–1957) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Okinawa
tokens.title: Last major battle of the Pacific
tokens.description: The Battle of Okinawa, codenamed Operation Iceberg, was fought from 1 April to 22 June 1945 on Okinawa island. Its initial invasion was the largest amphibious assault in the Pacific Theater of World War II.
tokens.image_credit: Staff Sergent Walter F. Kleine · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
tokens.title: Flag raised on Mount Suribachi
tokens.description: The Battle of Iwo Jima was a major World War II battle fought from 19 February to 26 March 1945. US Marine, Navy and Army forces captured the Japanese-held island from its fortified garrison.
tokens.image_credit: Joe Rosenthal · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Kantō Earthquake
tokens.title: Quake and fires devastate Tokyo and Yokohama
tokens.description: The Great Kantō Earthquake struck the Kantō Plain of Honshu on 1 September 1923, with an approximate magnitude of 8.0. It devastated Tokyo, Yokohama and the surrounding prefectures, with fires adding to the destruction.
tokens.image_credit: urbzoo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bombing of Tokyo 10 March 1945
tokens.title: Deadliest air raid in history
tokens.description: On the night of 9 and 10 March 1945 the US Army Air Forces firebombed Tokyo in a raid code-named Operation Meetinghouse. Bombs dropped from 279 B-29 bombers burned out much of eastern Tokyo.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Ishikawa Kōyō · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokyo subway sarin attack
tokens.title: Aum Shinrikyo attack on commuters
tokens.description: The Tokyo subway sarin attack was carried out on 20 March 1995 by members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult. Sarin released on three Tokyo Metro lines during rush hour killed 14 people and severely injured 50.
tokens.image_credit: 陸上自衛隊（Japan Ground Self-Defense Force） · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1964 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: First Games held in Asia
tokens.description: The 1964 Summer Olympics, also known as Tokyo 1964, were held from 10 to 24 October 1964 in Tokyo, Japan. They were the first Olympic Games held in the city, and the only ones with spectators before the 2020 edition.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Tsushima
tokens.title: Japan destroys Russian fleet
tokens.description: The Battle of Tsushima was fought on 27 and 28 May 1905 in the Tsushima Strait, the final naval battle of the Russo-Japanese War. The Imperial Russian Navy suffered a devastating defeat, the only decisive engagement between modern steel battleship fleets.
tokens.image_credit: Tōjō Shōtarō · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mongol invasions of Japan
tokens.title: Kamikaze winds scatter the fleet
tokens.description: Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty launched two failed invasions of Japan, in 1274 and 1281. Storms destroyed the Mongol fleets, and the word kamikaze was first used for these typhoons.
tokens.image_credit: Kikuchi Yoosai / (of the reproduction) Tokyo National Museum · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Dan-no-ura
tokens.title: Taira clan defeated at sea
tokens.description: The Battle of Dan-no-ura was a major sea battle of the Genpei War, fought in 1185 in the Kanmon Straits off the southern tip of Honshu. The Minamoto fleet, led by Minamoto no Yoshitsune, defeated the Taira fleet.
tokens.image_credit: Tosa Mitsunobu · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Convention of Kanagawa
tokens.title: Treaty ends Japan's isolation
tokens.description: The Convention of Kanagawa was a treaty signed on 31 March 1854 between the United States and the Tokugawa shogunate. It opened the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate and ended Japan's policy of national seclusion.
tokens.image_credit: Fumihiro Kato · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imjin War
tokens.title: Japan invades Korea
tokens.description: The Imjin War was two Japanese invasions of Korea, in 1592 and 1597, ordered by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Japanese forces withdrew from the Korean Peninsula in 1598.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Myeongnyang
tokens.title: Yi Sun-sin wins with 13 ships
tokens.description: The Battle of Myeongnyang was a naval battle fought on 26 October 1597 in the Myeongnyang Strait near Jindo Island. Admiral Yi Sun-sin led 13 Joseon warships against a much larger Japanese fleet and won.
tokens.image_credit: 알 수 없음. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gwangju Uprising
tokens.title: Citizens rise against martial law
tokens.description: The Gwangju Uprising was a series of student-led demonstrations in Gwangju, South Korea, in May 1980, against the coup and martial law imposed by Chun Doo-hwan. It is also known as the May 18 Democratization Movement.
tokens.image_credit: Schlarpi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of MV Sewol
tokens.title: Ferry disaster off Jindo
tokens.description: The ferry MV Sewol sank on 16 April 2014 on its way from Incheon to Jeju, killing 304 of the 476 people on board. Around 250 of the dead were students from Danwon High School in Ansan.
tokens.image_credit: Trainholic · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1988 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games mark Korea's global arrival
tokens.description: The 1988 Summer Olympics were held from 17 September to 2 October 1988 in Seoul, South Korea, with 159 nations and 8,391 athletes. The Games were centred on the Olympic Park in the Songpa district.
tokens.image_credit: Steve McGill · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2002 FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: First World Cup held in Asia
tokens.description: The 2002 FIFA World Cup was the 17th World Cup, held from 31 May to 30 June 2002 in South Korea and Japan. It was the first World Cup held in Asia and the first hosted by more than one nation.
tokens.image_credit: 문덕관 기증 · KOGL Type 1 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Korean Armistice Agreement
tokens.title: Fighting halts at Panmunjom
tokens.description: The Korean Armistice Agreement brought about a cessation of hostilities in the Korean War when it was signed in 1953 at Panmunjom. It was signed for the United Nations Command, the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteer Army.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Department of Defense (F. Kazukaitis. U.S. Navy) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Karbala
tokens.title: Husayn killed, shaping Shia memory
tokens.description: The Battle of Karbala was fought on 10 October 680 between the forces of Umayyad caliph Yazid I and a small army led by Husayn ibn Ali, at Karbala in modern southern Iraq. Husayn's death is a central event in Shia tradition.
tokens.image_credit: Persian Painter Abbas Al-Musavi. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
tokens.title: Mamluks halt the Mongol advance
tokens.description: The Battle of Ain Jalut was fought on 3 September 1260 between the Mamluks of Egypt and the Ilkhanate near the spring of Ain Jalut in the Jezreel Valley. It was the first major halt to the Mongol advance.

tokens.name: Battle of Hattin
tokens.title: Saladin crushes the Crusader army
tokens.description: The Battle of Hattin was fought on 4 July 1187 between the Crusader states of the Levant and the Ayyubid forces of Saladin. Saladin's victory captured or killed most of the Crusader army.
tokens.image_credit: Almog · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Masada
tokens.title: Last stand of the Zealots
tokens.description: The Siege of Masada took place in 72 to 73 AD, when Roman imperial forces took the hilltop fortress of Masada, then held by the Sicarii, during the First Jewish-Roman War. The siege is recorded mainly by Josephus in The Jewish War.
tokens.image_credit: Matthijs Pool · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Israeli Declaration of Independence
tokens.title: Ben-Gurion proclaims the state in Tel Aviv
tokens.description: The Israeli Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on 14 May 1948 at the Tel Aviv Museum, now Independence Hall, by the body led by David Ben-Gurion. It established the State of Israel.
tokens.image_credit: Rudi Weissenstein · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Entebbe raid
tokens.title: Hostages rescued in Uganda
tokens.description: The Entebbe raid was a 3 July 1976 Israeli counter-terrorist operation in Uganda. It freed hostages held at Entebbe International Airport after an Air France flight was hijacked.
tokens.image_credit: IDF Spokesperson's Unit photographer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gallipoli campaign
tokens.title: Anzac landing at Gallipoli
tokens.description: The Gallipoli campaign was a First World War campaign on the Gallipoli Peninsula from 19 February 1915 to 9 January 1916. Britain, France and the Russian Empire failed to take control of the Turkish straits and force the Ottoman Empire to capitulate.
tokens.image_credit: George Washington Lambert · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Lausanne
tokens.title: Modern Turkey's borders recognised
tokens.description: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed on 24 July 1923 in the Palais de Rumine in Lausanne, Switzerland, after the Lausanne Conference. It officially resolved the conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Allied powers.

tokens.name: Armenian genocide
tokens.title: Arrests in Constantinople begin the atrocities
tokens.description: The Armenian genocide was the systematic destruction of the Armenian people in the Ottoman Empire during World War I, carried out mainly through mass murder and death marches to the Syrian desert.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kosovo
tokens.title: Serbs and Ottomans clash on the Field of Blackbirds
tokens.description: The Battle of Kosovo took place on 15 June 1389 between a Serbian army led by Prince Lazar and an invading Ottoman army under Sultan Murad I. It was one of the largest battles of the Late Middle Ages.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Stefanović · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Poltava
tokens.title: Peter the Great defeats Charles XII
tokens.description: The Battle of Poltava was fought on 8 July 1709 and was the decisive battle of the Great Northern War. A Russian army under Peter I defeated a Swedish army commanded by Carl Gustaf Rehnskiöld.
tokens.image_credit: Pierre-Denis Martin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kursk
tokens.title: Largest tank battle of the war
tokens.description: The Battle of Kursk was a major World War II battle between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union near Kursk in summer 1943, won by the Soviets. It is one of the most-cited turning points of the European war.
tokens.image_credit: Red Army photographer? · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Leningrad
tokens.title: Nine hundred days of blockade
tokens.description: The Siege of Leningrad was a blockade of the Soviet city by Axis forces from 1941 to 1944. The city was never captured, but the siege caused an estimated 1.5 million deaths.
tokens.image_credit: Boris Kudoyarov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Moscow
tokens.title: Soviets halt the German advance
tokens.description: The Battle of Moscow was fought from October 1941 to January 1942 on a 600 km sector of the Eastern Front. The Soviet defence thwarted Germany's attack on the Soviet capital.
tokens.image_credit: Knorring / Олег Кнорринг · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Storming of the Winter Palace
tokens.title: October Revolution in Petrograd
tokens.description: The storming of the Winter Palace in Petrograd, in late October 1917 (Old Style), was a key moment of the Bolshevik October Revolution. The palace now houses the Hermitage Museum.
tokens.image_credit: Ivan Vladimirov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: February Revolution
tokens.title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
tokens.description: The February Revolution was the first of two revolutions in Russia in 1917, with its main events in and near Petrograd. It began with mass protests against food rationing on 23 February Old Style (8 March 1917).
tokens.image_credit: Jones, Stinton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bloody Sunday 1905
tokens.title: Troops fire on petitioners in St Petersburg
tokens.description: Bloody Sunday, 22 January 1905 (9 January O.S.), was the day Imperial Guard soldiers fired on petitioners led by Father Georgy Gapon as they marched towards the Winter Palace in St Petersburg. It is regarded as the start of the Revolution of 1905.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown (Life time: 1905) · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chelyabinsk meteor
tokens.title: Fireball shatters windows across the city
tokens.description: The Chelyabinsk meteor was a superbolide that entered Earth's atmosphere over the southern Ural region of Russia on 15 February 2013. It was caused by an asteroid about 18 metres across that broke up in the air.
tokens.image_credit: Nikita Plekhanov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsar Bomba
tokens.title: Largest nuclear device ever detonated
tokens.description: The Tsar Bomba was a Soviet thermonuclear aerial bomb, tested on 30 October 1961 at Novaya Zemlya in the far north of Russia. Rated at about 50 megatons of TNT, it is the most powerful nuclear weapon ever constructed and tested.

tokens.name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
tokens.title: Soviet flag lowered over the Kremlin
tokens.description: On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union was formally dissolved and ceased to exist as a sovereign state. The Soviet flag was lowered over the Kremlin in Moscow on 25 December 1991, the day Mikhail Gorbachev resigned.

tokens.name: 1993 Russian constitutional crisis
tokens.title: Tanks fire on the White House
tokens.description: In September and October 1993 a conflict between President Boris Yeltsin and the Russian parliament became a constitutional crisis. It ended when Yeltsin used military force against the parliament building, the House of Soviets, in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: Bergmann at Japanese Wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Beslan school siege
tokens.title: School hostage crisis in North Ossetia
tokens.description: The Beslan school siege was a terrorist attack in Beslan, North Ossetia, Russia, from 1 to 3 September 2004. More than 1,100 people, including 777 children, were held hostage in a school building.
tokens.image_credit: Leon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moscow theater hostage crisis
tokens.title: Siege at the Dubrovka theatre
tokens.description: The Moscow theater hostage crisis was the seizure of the Dubrovka Theatre in Moscow by Chechen terrorists on 23 October 2002. Some 912 hostages were taken, and the attackers demanded an end to the Second Chechen War.

tokens.name: Kursk submarine disaster
tokens.title: Submarine lost in the Barents Sea
tokens.description: The Russian nuclear submarine K-141 Kursk sank in the Barents Sea on 12 August 2000, with the loss of all 118 personnel on board. The navy did not start a search for the vessel for over six hours after the explosions.

tokens.name: Soyuz 11
tokens.title: Crew of Salyut 1 lost on return
tokens.description: Soyuz 11 was a 1971 Soviet crewed mission that visited the Salyut 1 space station. The three cosmonauts died when their capsule depressurised while preparing for re-entry.

tokens.name: Salyut 1
tokens.title: First space station launched
tokens.description: Salyut 1 was the world's first space station, launched into low Earth orbit by the Soviet Union on 19 April 1971. The wider Salyut program later flew seven more stations.
tokens.image_credit: Bill Ingalls · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Luna 2
tokens.title: First probe to reach the Moon
tokens.description: Luna 2 was a Soviet spacecraft launched on 12 September 1959 that became the first human-made object to touch the surface of the Moon. It was the sixth Luna programme spacecraft launched to the Moon.

tokens.name: Luna 9
tokens.title: First soft landing on the Moon
tokens.description: Luna 9 was an uncrewed Soviet Luna programme mission that made the first soft landing on the Moon on 3 February 1966. It was the first spacecraft to return images from the lunar surface.
tokens.image_credit: Pline · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vostok 6
tokens.title: First woman in space
tokens.description: Vostok 6 was the first human spaceflight to carry a woman into space, with cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova on board. The mission was flown by the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew Gray · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Voskhod 2
tokens.title: First spacewalk by Alexei Leonov
tokens.description: Voskhod 2 was a Soviet crewed space mission in March 1965 with Pavel Belyayev and Alexei Leonov on board. Leonov became the first person to leave the spacecraft during a spacewalk, lasting 12 minutes.
tokens.image_credit: USSR Post · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sputnik 2
tokens.title: First animal to orbit Earth
tokens.description: Sputnik 2 was launched by the Soviet Union on 3 November 1957 as the second spacecraft in Earth orbit. It was the first to carry an animal into orbit, the space dog Laika.
tokens.image_credit: Laika ac from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mir
tokens.title: Core module launched into orbit
tokens.description: Mir was a space station operated in low Earth orbit from 1986 to 2001, first by the Soviet Union and later by Russia. It was the first modular space station, assembled in orbit between 1986 and 1996.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venera 7
tokens.title: First landing on another planet
tokens.description: Venera 7 was a Soviet spacecraft that made the first successful soft landing on another planet, on Venus on 15 December 1970. It was also the first probe to transmit data from the surface of another planet back to Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Emerezhko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: RDS-1
tokens.title: RDS-1 detonated in Kazakhstan
tokens.description: RDS-1, also called First Lightning, was the first nuclear weapon test conducted by the Soviet Union. It was detonated on 29 August 1949 at the Semipalatinsk Test Site in Kazakhstan, with a yield of 22 kilotons of TNT.
tokens.image_credit: The Official CTBTO Photostream · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Talas
tokens.title: Tang and Abbasid armies meet
tokens.description: The Battle of Talas was fought in July 751 on the Talas River, where the Abbasid army with Karluk allies defeated the Tang army under Gao Xianzhi. The clash was over control of the regions around the Syr Darya.

tokens.name: Battle of Ankara
tokens.title: Timur captures Sultan Bayezid
tokens.description: The Battle of Ankara was fought on 28 July 1402 on the Çubuk plain near Ankara, where Timur defeated the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I. The victory led to the Ottoman Interregnum.

tokens.name: Battle of Chaldiran
tokens.title: Ottomans defeat the Safavids
tokens.description: The Battle of Chaldiran took place on 23 August 1514 and ended with a decisive Ottoman victory over the Safavid Empire. The Ottomans annexed Eastern Anatolia and Upper Mesopotamia from Safavid Iran as a result.
tokens.image_credit: Muin Musavvir · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Nahavand
tokens.title: Arab victory ends Sasanian hopes
tokens.description: The Battle of Nahavand was fought in 642 between the Rashidun forces under An-Numan ibn Muqarrin and the Sasanian army under Yazdegerd III. The Rashidun victory ended organized Sasanid resistance.

tokens.name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
tokens.title: Rashidun army defeats the Sasanians
tokens.description: The Battle of al-Qadisiyyah took place in November 636 between the Rashidun Caliphate and the Sasanian Empire. The Rashidun victory was one of the most significant engagements of the Muslim conquest of Persia.

tokens.name: Battle of the Yarmuk
tokens.title: Arab victory over the Byzantines
tokens.description: The Battle of the Yarmuk was fought in August 636 near the Yarmouk River between the Byzantine Empire and the Rashidun Caliphate. The decisive Arab victory effectively ended Byzantine rule in Syria.

tokens.name: Battle of Badr
tokens.title: First major battle of early Islam
tokens.description: The Battle of Badr was fought on 13 March 624 near the city of Badr in present-day Saudi Arabia. Muhammad's Muslim army defeated a Quraysh force led by Abu Jahl, an early turning point in Islam.
tokens.image_credit: Lütfi Abdullah · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Conquest of Mecca
tokens.title: Muhammad enters Mecca
tokens.description: The conquest of Mecca was a military campaign led by Muhammad and his companions in December 629 or January 630. The fall of the city to Muhammad formally ended the conflict with the Quraysh.

tokens.name: Battle of Karnal
tokens.title: Nader Shah defeats the Mughals
tokens.description: The Battle of Karnal was fought on 24 February 1739, when Nader Shah of Iran defeated the army of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah. The victory paved the way for the Iranian sack of Delhi.

tokens.name: Sack of Delhi 1398
tokens.title: Timur's army takes Delhi
tokens.description: The Sack of Delhi took place on 17 December 1398, when Timur's army fought the forces of Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah and took the city. The Sultan's war elephants were a key part of his defence.
tokens.image_credit: 1435-26 artist · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Talikota
tokens.title: Vijayanagara Empire falls
tokens.description: The Battle of Talikota was fought on 23 January 1565 between the Vijayanagara Empire and an alliance of the Deccan sultanates. The defeat of Aliya Rama Raya led to the eventual collapse of the Vijayanagara polity.

tokens.name: Battle of Buxar
tokens.title: East India Company secures Bengal
tokens.description: The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 and 23 October 1764 between the British East India Company, under Major Hector Munro, and the combined armies of Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and his allies. The defeated Indian rulers submitted to the Company in 1765.

tokens.name: Siege of Seringapatam 1799
tokens.title: Tipu Sultan killed
tokens.description: The Siege of Seringapatam, from 5 April to 4 May 1799, was the final confrontation of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. British forces stormed the fortress, and Tipu Sultan was killed in the battle.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Henry Singleton (1766–1839) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quit India Movement
tokens.title: Gandhi calls for British withdrawal
tokens.description: The Quit India Movement was a campaign launched by Mahatma Gandhi at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee on 8 August 1942. It demanded an end to British rule in India during the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Indira Gandhi
tokens.title: Prime Minister shot in Delhi
tokens.description: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was shot dead on 31 October 1984 at her residence on Safdarjung Road in New Delhi by two of her bodyguards. The killing followed Operation Blue Star, the army action at the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
tokens.image_credit: GaneshBhakt (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi
tokens.title: Bombing at Sriperumbudur
tokens.description: Former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was killed by a suicide bombing at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu on 21 May 1991. The attack killed 17 people, including Gandhi and the bomber, a member of the LTTE.
tokens.image_credit: This Image was created by User:PlaneMad. If you are using the image under the creative commons share alike license please credit the photo CC-by-sa PlaneMad/Wikimedia and include a link to this page.  · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 Mumbai attacks
tokens.title: Coordinated attacks across Mumbai
tokens.description: Ten Lashkar-e-Taiba members carried out twelve coordinated attacks across Mumbai from 26 to 29 November 2008. A total of 175 people died, including nine of the attackers.
tokens.image_credit: Nicholas (Nichalp) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Blue Star
tokens.title: Army action at the Golden Temple
tokens.description: Operation Blue Star was a military operation by the Indian Armed Forces from 1 to 10 June 1984 at the Golden Temple in Amritsar. It aimed to remove Damdami Taksal leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale and militants from the complex.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Army · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Smiling Buddha
tokens.title: India's first nuclear test
tokens.description: Smiling Buddha was India's first nuclear weapon test, a fission device detonated on 18 May 1974. The test took place at the Pokhran Test Range of the Indian Army in Rajasthan.

tokens.name: Pokhran-II
tokens.title: India tests five devices
tokens.description: Pokhran-II, also known as Operation Shakti, was a series of five nuclear weapon tests conducted by India in May 1998. The devices were detonated at the Pokhran Test Range of the Indian Army in Rajasthan.

tokens.name: Chandrayaan-3
tokens.title: India lands near the lunar south pole
tokens.description: Chandrayaan-3 was ISRO's third lunar mission, launched on 14 July 2023 from Sriharikota. Its Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Space Research OrganisationDerivative work: UnpetitproleX · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mars Orbiter Mission
tokens.title: India's first Mars probe launched
tokens.description: Mars Orbiter Mission, nicknamed Mangalyaan, is an Indian space probe launched by ISRO on 5 November 2013. It entered orbit around Mars on 24 September 2014, making ISRO the fourth space agency to reach Mars orbit.
tokens.image_credit: Kevin Gill from Nashua, NH, United States · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Longewala
tokens.title: Outnumbered defenders hold the desert post
tokens.description: The Battle of Longewala (4 to 7 December 1971) was an engagement of the India-Pakistan war of 1971 in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan. Outnumbered Indian defenders held the border post against a Pakistani tank assault.
tokens.image_credit: Vijay Tiwari09 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kargil War
tokens.title: High-altitude conflict in Kashmir
tokens.description: The Kargil War was fought between India and Pakistan from May to July 1999 in the Kargil district of Ladakh, along the Line of Control. Indian forces expelled Pakistani troops and paramilitary fighters from positions they had occupied on the Indian side.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Army · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bangladesh Liberation War
tokens.title: Birth of a new nation
tokens.description: The Bangladesh Liberation War was an armed conflict in which East Pakistan gained independence as Bangladesh with help from India. It began on 25 March 1971, when the Pakistani military launched Operation Searchlight against East Pakistanis.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Navy · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rana Plaza collapse
tokens.title: Garment factory building collapses
tokens.description: The Rana Plaza collapse occurred on 24 April 2013 in Savar, near Dhaka, Bangladesh, when the nine-story commercial building failed structurally. The confirmed death toll was 1,134.
tokens.image_credit: Sharat Chowdhury · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1970 Bhola cyclone
tokens.title: Deadliest tropical cyclone on record
tokens.description: The 1970 Bhola cyclone struck East Pakistan and West Bengal on 12 November 1970 and is the deadliest tropical cyclone on record. Storm surge flooded the low-lying islands of the Ganges Delta, killing at least 300,000 people.
tokens.image_credit: Express Newspapers/Getty Images · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sri Lankan civil war
tokens.title: Conflict ends after 26 years
tokens.description: The Sri Lankan civil war was an armed conflict fought in Sri Lanka from 1983 to 2009 between the government and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam. It ended in 2009 with the defeat of the LTTE in the north-east of the island.
tokens.image_credit: trokilinochchi Mr K.Sathees from Vanni · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1953 British Mount Everest expedition
tokens.title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit
tokens.description: The 1953 British Mount Everest expedition was the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest, when Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the summit on 29 May 1953. The expedition was led by Colonel John Hunt.
tokens.image_credit: Jamling Tenzing Norgay · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: April 2015 Nepal earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.8 near Gorkha
tokens.description: The April 2015 Nepal earthquake, also called the Gorkha earthquake, struck on 25 April 2015 with a magnitude of about 7.8 to 7.9. It killed 8,962 people, with its epicentre east of Gorkha District at Barpak.
tokens.image_credit: Hilmi Hacaloğlu · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1996 Mount Everest disaster
tokens.title: Storm kills eight climbers
tokens.description: Eight climbers died in a blizzard while descending from the summit of Mount Everest on 10 and 11 May 1996. Twelve people died trying to reach the summit that season.
tokens.image_credit: Spphere · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nepalese royal massacre
tokens.title: Royal family killed in Kathmandu
tokens.description: Nine members of the Nepalese royal family, including King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya, were shot dead at Narayanhiti Palace on 1 June 2001. A government inquiry named Crown Prince Dipendra as the gunman.
tokens.image_credit: Suraj Belbase · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Nile
tokens.title: Nelson destroys the French fleet at Aboukir
tokens.description: A British fleet under Horatio Nelson defeated the French fleet of Brueys d'Aigalliers at Aboukir Bay, Egypt, from 1 to 3 August 1798. It was the climax of Napoleon's 1798 Mediterranean campaign.
tokens.image_credit: George Arnald · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Pyramids
tokens.title: Napoleon defeats the Mamluks
tokens.description: Napoleon's French army defeated the Mamluk forces of Murad Bey near Embabeh on 21 July 1798, during the French invasion of Egypt. The battle takes its name from the distant Pyramids of Giza.
tokens.image_credit: François-Louis-Joseph Watteau · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kadesh
tokens.title: Ramesses II versus the Hittites
tokens.description: Ramesses II of the Egyptian Empire fought Muwatalli II of the Hittite Empire at the Orontes River near the stronghold of Kadesh in the early 13th century BC. The battle is recorded in Egyptian reliefs at the Ramesseum.
tokens.image_credit: James Henry Breasted (August 27, 1865 – December 2, 1935) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Megiddo 15th century BC
tokens.title: Thutmose III wins at Megiddo
tokens.description: Pharaoh Thutmose III of Egypt defeated a rebellious coalition of Canaanite vassal states led by the king of Kadesh at Megiddo in the 15th century BC. It is the first battle recorded in relatively reliable detail.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
tokens.title: Howard Carter finds the steps
tokens.description: The tomb of Tutankhamun was found in the Valley of the Kings in 1922 by a team led by Howard Carter. It is the only known near-intact royal burial from ancient Egypt.
tokens.image_credit: Harry Burton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rosetta Stone
tokens.title: Key to reading hieroglyphs unearthed
tokens.description: The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799 near Rashid (Rosetta) in Egypt. Its decree of 196 BC, written in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek, became the key to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs.
tokens.image_credit: Hans Hillewaert · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Opening of the Suez Canal
tokens.title: Mediterranean joined to the Red Sea
tokens.description: The Suez Canal was formally opened on 17 November 1869 with a ceremony at Port Said, when the first ships entered the waterway. The canal links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Édouard Riou · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Zama
tokens.title: Scipio defeats Hannibal
tokens.description: The Battle of Zama was fought in 202 BC in what is now Tunisia, between the Roman army of Scipio Africanus and the Carthaginian army of Hannibal. The Roman victory led to Carthage's capitulation and the end of the Second Punic War.

tokens.name: Hannibal's crossing of the Alps
tokens.title: Elephants and army enter Italy
tokens.description: In 218 BC Hannibal led the Carthaginian army over the Alps into Italy during the Second Punic War. The exact pass and route he used are still debated by historians.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Francisco Goya · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Alesia
tokens.title: Caesar traps Vercingetorix
tokens.description: The Battle of Alesia was fought in 52 BC around the Gallic oppidum of Alesia, in what is now France, between Julius Caesar's Roman army and a Gallic coalition led by Vercingetorix. It was the last major engagement between Gauls and Romans in the Gallic Wars.
tokens.image_credit: Lionel Royer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
tokens.title: Three Roman legions destroyed
tokens.description: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest was fought between 8 and 11 September AD 9 between an alliance of Germanic peoples led by Arminius and three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus. The Roman defeat halted Rome's expansion into Germania east of the Rhine.
tokens.image_credit: Paja Jovanović · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Adrianople
tokens.title: Goths crush Emperor Valens
tokens.description: The Battle of Adrianople was fought on 9 August 378 near Adrianople in the Roman province of Thrace, now Edirne in Turkey. The Gothic rebels led by Fritigern defeated the Eastern Roman army, and Emperor Valens was killed.

tokens.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
tokens.title: Constantine takes Rome
tokens.description: The Battle of the Milvian Bridge was fought on 28 October AD 312 between Constantine I and Maxentius, north of Rome on the Tiber. Constantine's victory set him on the path to becoming sole ruler of the Roman Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Giulio Romano · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sack of Rome 410
tokens.title: Visigoths enter the city
tokens.description: The Visigoths led by King Alaric sacked Rome on 24 August 410. Rome was no longer the capital of the Western Roman Empire at the time, but it kept its standing as the spiritual centre of the Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph-Noël Sylvestre · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
tokens.title: Romans and Visigoths stop Attila
tokens.description: The Battle of the Catalaunian Plains was fought on 20 June 451 between a Roman and Visigothic coalition under Flavius Aetius and the Huns led by Attila. It was one of the last major military operations of the Western Roman Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Johannes de Thurocz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Poitiers
tokens.title: French king captured
tokens.description: The Battle of Poitiers was fought on 19 September 1356 during the Hundred Years' War. An Anglo-Gascon army under Edward, the Black Prince, defeated a larger French force and captured King John II.
tokens.image_credit: Eugène Delacroix · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Crécy
tokens.title: English longbowmen defeat French knights
tokens.description: The Battle of Crécy was fought on 26 August 1346 during the Hundred Years' War. An English army under King Edward III defeated a French army led by King Philip VI.
tokens.image_credit: Loyset Liédet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Bannockburn
tokens.title: Robert the Bruce wins independence
tokens.description: The Battle of Bannockburn was fought on 23 to 24 June 1314 between the army of Robert the Bruce and the army of King Edward II of England. The Scottish victory was a turning point in the First War of Scottish Independence.
tokens.image_credit: Edmund Blair Leighton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Stirling Bridge
tokens.title: Wallace and Moray outwit the English
tokens.description: The Battle of Stirling Bridge was fought on 11 September 1297 during the First War of Scottish Independence. Forces under Andrew Moray and William Wallace defeated an English army led by John de Warenne, Earl of Surrey, near Stirling.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew White Ridley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Culloden
tokens.title: Last pitched battle on British soil
tokens.description: The Battle of Culloden was fought on 16 April 1746 near Inverness in the Scottish Highlands. A British government army under the Duke of Cumberland defeated the Jacobite army of Charles Edward Stuart, ending the 1745 rising.
tokens.image_credit: David Morier · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magna Carta
tokens.title: Charter agreed at Runnymede
tokens.description: Magna Carta was sealed by King John of England at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215. It was a royal charter of rights agreed to settle a dispute with rebel barons.
tokens.image_credit: James William Edmund Doyle / Edmund Evans · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gunpowder Plot
tokens.title: Plot to blow up Parliament foiled
tokens.description: The Gunpowder Plot was a failed 1605 conspiracy by English Catholics led by Robert Catesby to kill King James I by blowing up the House of Lords. Guy Fawkes was arrested in the cellars beneath the Palace of Westminster on 5 November 1605.
tokens.image_credit: ThatsTheBoss · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Fire of London
tokens.title: Fire starts in Pudding Lane
tokens.description: The Great Fire of London ran from 2 to 5 September 1666 and gutted the medieval City of London inside the Roman wall. It started in a bakery in Pudding Lane shortly after midnight.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown artistUnknown artist · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black Death
tokens.title: Plague ships arrive in Sicily
tokens.description: The Black Death reached Europe in October 1347, when Genoese ships arriving from the East docked at Messina in Sicily. The plague pandemic then spread across Europe until 1353.
tokens.image_credit: Alexander Hoernigk · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peterloo Massacre
tokens.title: Cavalry charge a reform rally
tokens.description: The Peterloo Massacre took place at St Peter's Field, Manchester, on 16 August 1819. Yeomanry cavalry charged a crowd of about 60,000 demanding parliamentary reform, killing an estimated eighteen people.
tokens.image_credit: George Cruikshank · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Naseby
tokens.title: Parliamentarians break the Royalists
tokens.description: The Battle of Naseby took place on 14 June 1645 near Naseby in Northamptonshire, during the First English Civil War. Parliament's New Model Army destroyed the main Royalist army of Charles I.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Landseer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Execution of Charles I of England
tokens.title: King beheaded outside Whitehall
tokens.description: Charles I of England was publicly executed on 30 January 1649 outside the Banqueting House on Whitehall, London. The sentence followed his trial by the High Court of Justice during the English Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Exhibition
tokens.title: Crystal Palace showcases industry
tokens.description: The Great Exhibition, also called the Crystal Palace Exhibition, was held in Hyde Park, London, from 1 May to 15 October 1851. It was the first of the modern world's fairs, showing industry from many nations.
tokens.image_credit: J. McNeven · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Somme
tokens.title: Bloodiest day in British Army history
tokens.description: The Battle of the Somme was fought from 1 July to 18 November 1916 on both sides of the upper Somme river in France. British Empire and French forces attacked the German Empire in a First World War offensive.
tokens.image_credit: Ivor Castle · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Verdun
tokens.title: Ten months of attrition
tokens.description: The Battle of Verdun was fought from 21 February to 18 December 1916 on the Western Front in France. It was the longest battle of the First World War, with the German 5th Army attacking the French defences around Verdun.
tokens.image_credit: Collection DocAnciens/docpix.fr · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Passchendaele
tokens.title: Mud and shellfire in Flanders
tokens.description: The Third Battle of Ypres, also called the Battle of Passchendaele, was an Allied offensive on the Western Front from July to November 1917. It fought for the ridges east and south of Ypres in West Flanders, Belgium.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Hurley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Battle of the Marne
tokens.title: Paris saved by the Allies
tokens.description: The First Battle of the Marne was fought from 5 to 12 September 1914 as the German army advanced on Paris. The French and British counterattack that followed is known in France as the Miracle on the Marne.
tokens.image_credit: No attribution · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Christmas truce
tokens.title: Soldiers sing and meet in no man's land
tokens.description: The Christmas truce was a series of widespread unofficial ceasefires mainly along the Western Front around Christmas 1914. It came five months after the war began, when the fighting on the front had stalled.
tokens.image_credit: A. C. Michael (Arthur Cadwgan Michael, 1881‒1965) · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Armistice of 11 November 1918
tokens.title: Signed in a railway carriage at Compiègne
tokens.description: The Armistice of 11 November 1918 ended the fighting on land, at sea and in the air in World War I. It was signed in a railway carriage in the Compiegne Forest, near the town of Compiegne, France.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Versailles
tokens.title: Peace terms signed in the Hall of Mirrors
tokens.description: The Treaty of Versailles was a peace treaty signed on 28 June 1919. It ended the state of war between Germany and most of the Allied Powers after World War I, and was signed in the Palace of Versailles.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Jutland
tokens.title: Largest naval battle of World War I
tokens.description: The Battle of Jutland was a naval battle between the British Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet from 31 May to 1 June 1916. It was the largest naval battle and the only full-scale clash of battleships in the First World War.
tokens.image_credit: photographer not identified · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: RMS Lusitania
tokens.title: Liner torpedoed off Ireland
tokens.description: RMS Lusitania, a British Cunard liner, was torpedoed by a German U-boat on 7 May 1915, about 20 km off the Old Head of Kinsale, Ireland. The sinking killed about 1,200 people and turned many countries' opinion against Germany.
tokens.image_credit: UnknownUnknown · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Easter Rising
tokens.title: Irish rebels seize the GPO
tokens.description: The Easter Rising was an armed insurrection in Ireland during Easter Week in April 1916. Irish republicans launched it against British rule to establish an independent Irish Republic while the United Kingdom fought the First World War.
tokens.image_credit: Keogh Brothers Ltd., photographers [1] · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bloody Sunday 1972
tokens.title: Civil rights march in Derry
tokens.description: Bloody Sunday, or the Bogside Massacre, was the shooting of 26 unarmed civilians by British soldiers during a civil rights march in Derry on 30 January 1972. Thirteen were killed outright, and another man died four months later from his wounds.
tokens.image_credit: SeanMack · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Good Friday Agreement
tokens.title: Peace accord for Northern Ireland
tokens.description: The Good Friday Agreement, also called the Belfast Agreement, is a pair of agreements signed on 10 April 1998. It ended most of the violence of the Troubles in Northern Ireland and was a major step in the peace process.

tokens.name: Pan Am Flight 103
tokens.title: Pan Am 103 destroyed over Scotland
tokens.description: Pan Am Flight 103 was a Boeing 747 destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, Scotland, on 21 December 1988. The attack killed 270 people, including 11 residents of the town on the ground.
tokens.image_credit: Air Accident Investigation Branch · OGL 2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aberfan disaster
tokens.title: Colliery tip engulfs a school
tokens.description: The Aberfan disaster was the collapse of a colliery spoil tip onto the Welsh village of Aberfan on 21 October 1966. It killed 116 children and 28 adults, engulfing Pantglas Junior School and a row of houses.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hillsborough disaster
tokens.title: Crush at an FA Cup semi-final
tokens.description: The Hillsborough disaster was a fatal crowd crush at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield on 15 April 1989. It occurred at an FA Cup semi-final between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.
tokens.image_credit: Superbfc · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heysel Stadium disaster
tokens.title: European Cup final tragedy in Brussels
tokens.description: The Heysel Stadium disaster was a crowd disaster at the 1985 European Cup final in Brussels, Belgium, on 29 May 1985. Juventus fans were pressed against a collapsing wall while escaping an attack by Liverpool fans.
tokens.image_credit: Pmk58 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Munich air disaster
tokens.title: Manchester United team plane crash
tokens.description: The Munich air disaster was the crash of British European Airways Flight 609 on 6 February 1958 at Munich-Riem Airport, West Germany. The aircraft was carrying the Manchester United team, and 20 of the 44 people on board died at the scene.
tokens.image_credit: PeeJay2K3 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1966 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: England win at Wembley
tokens.description: The 1966 FIFA World Cup final was played at Wembley Stadium in London on 30 July 1966. England beat West Germany 4-2 after extra time to win the Jules Rimet Trophy.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Four-minute mile
tokens.title: Roger Bannister breaks the barrier at Oxford
tokens.description: Roger Bannister ran the first sub-four-minute mile at the Iffley Road track in Oxford on 6 May 1954, in 3:59.4. The milestone gave its name to the four-minute mile benchmark in athletics.
