tokens.image_credit: Photograph by user:Jonathan Bowen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dolly the sheep
tokens.title: First mammal cloned from an adult cell
tokens.description: Dolly, a Finn-Dorset sheep, was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, by researchers at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh. She was born in 1996 and died in 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Toni Barros from São Paulo, Brasil · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Discovery of penicillin
tokens.title: Fleming notices mould killing bacteria
tokens.description: In 1928 Alexander Fleming, working at St Mary's Hospital in London, showed that a Penicillium mould secretes an antibacterial substance, which he named penicillin. Earlier societies had already used moulds to treat infections.
tokens.image_credit: Vera de Kok · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of Elizabeth II
tokens.title: Westminster Abbey ceremony broadcast live
tokens.description: The coronation of Elizabeth II as queen of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms took place on 2 June 1953 at Westminster Abbey in London. She had acceded on 6 February 1952, on the death of George VI.
tokens.image_credit: Antiquary · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Death of Diana, Princess of Wales
tokens.title: Car crash in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel
tokens.description: Diana, Princess of Wales, died on 31 August 1997 from injuries sustained in a car crash in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris. Dodi Fayed and the driver Henri Paul were also killed, and the bodyguard Trevor Rees-Jones survived.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Case · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Funeral of Queen Elizabeth II
tokens.title: State funeral at Westminster Abbey
tokens.description: Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022 at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. Her state funeral was held at Westminster Abbey in London, under the plan known as Operation London Bridge.
tokens.aliases: Southbank Centre, National Theatre, Waterloo station, Shell Centre
tokens.image_credit: No 10 Downing Street · OGL 3 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum
tokens.title: UK votes to leave the European Union
tokens.description: On 23 June 2016 voters in the United Kingdom chose to leave the European Union, by 51.89% to 48.11%. The final result was declared at Manchester Town Hall on 24 June 2016.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Andrew. · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grenfell Tower fire
tokens.title: Tower block blaze in West London
tokens.description: A fire broke out on 14 June 2017 in the 24-storey Grenfell Tower block of flats in North Kensington, London. A total of 72 people died, making it the deadliest structural fire in the United Kingdom since the Piper Alpha disaster in 1988.
tokens.image_credit: Natalie Oxford · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 7 July 2005 London bombings
tokens.title: Attacks on the transport network
tokens.description: Four coordinated suicide bombings by Islamist terrorists struck London's public transport during the morning rush hour on 7 July 2005. Three bombs exploded on Underground trains and one on a bus.
tokens.image_credit: Francis Tyers · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: London 2012 Olympics
tokens.title: Games opened at Olympic Stadium
tokens.description: The 2012 Summer Olympics, also known as London 2012, were held from 27 July to 12 August 2012 in London, England, with 10,518 athletes from 206 National Olympic Committees. The Olympic Stadium in Stratford, east London, hosted the opening ceremony and athletics.
tokens.image_credit: cdephotos · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lindbergh lands in Paris
tokens.title: First solo nonstop transatlantic flight
tokens.description: Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis at Le Bourget airport near Paris on 21 May 1927, completing the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight. The flight had taken off from Roosevelt Field, New York, about 33 hours and 30 minutes earlier.

tokens.name: Concorde crash
tokens.title: Air France Flight 4590 at Gonesse
tokens.description: Air France Flight 4590, a Concorde charter from Paris to New York, crashed shortly after take-off near Gonesse on 25 July 2000. All 109 people on board and four on the ground were killed.

tokens.name: May 68
tokens.title: Student protests and general strike
tokens.description: May 68 was a period of student demonstrations, riots and nationwide general strikes in France that began in May 1968. The unrest brought the country close to revolution and profoundly shaped French politics, labor relations and culture.
tokens.image_credit: André Cros · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dreyfus affair
tokens.title: Conviction that divided France
tokens.description: The Dreyfus affair was a political scandal that divided the Third French Republic from 1894 until 1906. Captain Alfred Dreyfus, wrongly convicted of treason in December 1894, was sent to the penal colony on Devil's Island.
tokens.image_credit: Henri Meyer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paris Commune
tokens.title: Radical government seizes the capital
tokens.description: The Paris Commune was a revolutionary government that seized power in Paris on 18 March 1871 and held parts of the city until 28 May 1871. It rose after the French army's defeat in the Franco-Prussian War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: July Revolution
tokens.title: Three Glorious Days topple Charles X
tokens.description: The July Revolution, also called the Three Glorious Days, overthrew King Charles X of France in 1830. It brought Louis Philippe of the House of Orleans to the throne under a restored constitutional monarchy.
tokens.image_credit: Eugène Delacroix · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tennis Court Oath
tokens.title: Deputies swear not to disband
tokens.description: The Tennis Court Oath was taken on 20 June 1789 by the French Third Estate in an indoor tennis court in the grounds of Versailles. Their vow not to separate until a constitution was established became a pivotal event in the French Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Jacques-Louis David · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Execution of Louis XVI
tokens.title: King guillotined on Place de la Révolution
tokens.description: Louis XVI, the deposed king of France, was publicly executed on 21 January 1793 at the Place de la Révolution in Paris. The National Convention had convicted him of high treason four days earlier.
tokens.image_credit: Isidore Stanislas Helman / After Charles Monnet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Valmy
tokens.title: Revolutionary army holds the line
tokens.description: The Battle of Valmy was fought on 20 September 1792 near the village of Valmy in Champagne. French generals Kellermann and Dumouriez halted the Prussian advance on Paris, the first major French victory of the Revolutionary Wars.
tokens.image_credit: Horace Vernet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of Napoleon
tokens.title: Emperor crowns himself at Notre-Dame
tokens.description: Napoleon was crowned Emperor of the French on 2 December 1804 at Notre-Dame de Paris. The ceremony was meant to establish the legitimacy of his new imperial dynasty and nobility.
tokens.image_credit: Jacques-Louis David / Georges Rouget · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hundred Days
tokens.title: Napoleon lands from Elba
tokens.description: The Hundred Days ran from Napoleon's return from exile on Elba until Louis XVIII's second restoration on 8 July 1815. The period included the Waterloo campaign and the War of the Seventh Coalition.
tokens.image_credit: Ruedi33a · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Leipzig
tokens.title: Battle of the Nations
tokens.description: The Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations, was fought from 16 to 19 October 1813. Coalition armies of Austria, Prussia, Russia and Sweden decisively defeated Napoleon's Grande Armée.
tokens.image_credit: Vladimir Moshkov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Jena-Auerstedt
tokens.title: Prussia crushed by Napoleon
tokens.description: The Battle of Jena-Auerstedt was fought on 14 October 1806 near Jena and Auerstedt in what is now Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt. Napoleon's Grande Armée defeated the combined Prussian and Saxon armies, the decisive engagement of the War of the Fourth Coalition.
tokens.image_credit: Horace Vernet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Congress of Vienna
tokens.title: Europe redrawn after Napoleon
tokens.description: The Congress of Vienna was a series of diplomatic meetings held in Vienna from September 1814 to June 1815. Chaired by Metternich, it set a new political order for Europe after Napoleon's downfall.
tokens.image_credit: After Jean-Baptiste Isabey · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Sedan
tokens.title: Napoleon III captured
tokens.description: The Battle of Sedan on 1 and 2 September 1870 was fought during the Franco-Prussian War. The capture of Napoleon III and over 100,000 troops effectively decided the war in favour of Prussia.
tokens.image_credit: Wilhelm Camphausen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Königgrätz
tokens.title: Prussia defeats Austria
tokens.description: The Battle of Königgrätz on 3 July 1866 was the decisive battle of the Austro-Prussian War. Prussia defeated the Austrian Empire near Hradec Králové, now in the Czech Republic.
tokens.image_credit: Georg Bleibtreu · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Proclamation of the German Empire
tokens.title: Declared in Versailles
tokens.description: The proclamation of the German Empire took place at Versailles on 18 January 1871, after the German states' joint victory in the Franco-Prussian War. It created the empire that unified the German states.
tokens.image_credit: Anton von Werner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kristallnacht
tokens.title: Nationwide pogrom across Germany
tokens.description: Kristallnacht, the Night of Broken Glass, was a pogrom against Jews carried out by SA and SS forces across Nazi Germany on 9 and 10 November 1938. Jewish shops and synagogues were smashed throughout the country.
tokens.image_credit: Center for Jewish History, NYC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Beer Hall Putsch
tokens.title: Failed coup in Munich
tokens.description: The Beer Hall Putsch was a failed coup led by Adolf Hitler and Erich Ludendorff in Munich, Bavaria, on 8 and 9 November 1923. It began with an SA march on the Bürgerbräukeller beer hall.
tokens.image_credit: UnknownUnknown · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reichstag fire
tokens.title: Blaze used to curtail civil liberties
tokens.description: The Reichstag fire was an arson attack on the Reichstag building in Berlin on 27 February 1933. The Nazi government used it to justify the Reichstag Fire Decree, which suspended civil liberties.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berlin Blockade
tokens.title: Airlift supplies the city
tokens.description: The Berlin Blockade, from 24 June 1948 to 12 May 1949, was one of the first major crises of the Cold War. The Soviet Union blocked Western Allied rail, road and canal access to the Western-controlled sectors of Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: USAF · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Construction of the Berlin Wall
tokens.title: Barbed wire divides the city overnight
tokens.description: The construction of the Berlin Wall began on 13 August 1961, when the GDR government sealed the border between East and West Berlin. The concrete barrier encircled West Berlin until its opening in November 1989.
tokens.image_credit: National Archives · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: German reunification
tokens.title: East and West Germany unite
tokens.description: German reunification was the process that re-established Germany as a single sovereign state, from 9 November 1989 until the dissolution of the GDR on 3 October 1990. East and West Berlin were reunified into one city on the same date.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown photographer, Reproduction by Lear 21 at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Munich massacre
tokens.title: Olympic Games hostage crisis
tokens.description: The Munich massacre was a terrorist attack at the 1972 Summer Olympics, when eight Black September militants killed two Israeli team members and took nine others hostage. The hostages were later killed during a failed rescue attempt.
tokens.image_credit: AP Photo/Kurt Strumpf (? – 2014) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1936 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Jesse Owens wins four golds
tokens.description: The 1936 Summer Olympics were held from 1 to 16 August 1936 in Berlin, Germany. Jesse Owens won four gold medals in athletics at the Games.
tokens.image_credit: Frankl, A. · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1954 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: West Germany stuns Hungary
tokens.description: The 1954 FIFA World Cup final was played at the Wankdorf Stadium in Bern on 4 July 1954. West Germany beat the heavily favoured Hungary by 3 goals to 2, an upset known as the Miracle of Bern.
tokens.image_credit: Sandstein · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gutenberg Bible
tokens.title: Movable-type printing in Mainz
tokens.description: The Gutenberg Bible, also called the 42-line Bible, is the earliest major book printed in Europe using mass-produced metal movable type. It marked the start of the Gutenberg Revolution and of the age of printed books in the West.
tokens.image_credit: NYC Wanderer (Kevin Eng) · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ninety-five Theses
tokens.title: Luther's challenge at Wittenberg
tokens.description: The Ninety-five Theses are a list of propositions on indulgences written by Martin Luther in 1517 for an academic disputation at the University of Wittenberg. They are considered to have launched the Protestant Reformation.
tokens.image_credit: Julius Hübner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Diet of Worms
tokens.title: Luther refuses to recant
tokens.description: The Diet of Worms of 1521 was an imperial assembly of the Holy Roman Empire, convened by Emperor Charles V in the free city of Worms. Martin Luther refused to recant his views there, and the Edict of Worms then condemned him as a heretic.
tokens.image_credit: Anton von Werner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peace of Westphalia
tokens.title: Thirty Years' War ends
tokens.description: The Peace of Westphalia is two treaties signed in October 1648 in the Westphalian cities of Osnabrück and Münster. They ended the Thirty Years' War and brought peace to the Holy Roman Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Dietmar Rabich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of White Mountain
tokens.title: Habsburgs defeat Bohemian rebels
tokens.description: The Battle of White Mountain was fought on 8 November 1620 outside Prague in the early stages of the Thirty Years' War. Forces of Ferdinand II defeated an army backing Frederick V, who then fled into Silesia.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Snayers · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Defenestrations of Prague
tokens.title: Officials thrown from the castle window
tokens.description: The Defenestrations of Prague were three incidents in Bohemian history in which people were thrown out of windows. In 1618 Protestant estates threw two royal governors and their secretary out of Hradčany Castle.
tokens.image_credit: Johann Philipp Abelinus · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Velvet Revolution
tokens.title: Peaceful end to communist rule
tokens.description: The Velvet Revolution was a non-violent transition of power in Czechoslovakia from 17 to 28 November 1989. Mass demonstrations ended 41 years of one-party Communist rule.
tokens.image_credit: ŠJů (cs:ŠJů) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
tokens.title: Uprising against Soviet control
tokens.description: The Hungarian Revolution of 1956 was an attempted countrywide revolt against the Hungarian People's Republic and its subordination to the USSR. Soviet tanks and troops crushed it in early November 1956, and nearly a quarter of a million Hungarians fled the country.
tokens.image_credit: Házy Zsolt · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pan-European Picnic
tokens.title: Border gate opens near Sopron
tokens.description: The Pan-European Picnic was a peace demonstration held on the Austro-Hungarian border near Sopron, Hungary, on 19 August 1989. The opening of the border gate there was a step in the chain of events that ended the Cold War.
tokens.image_credit: Cuchulainn 17:15, 20. Jun. 2009 (CEST) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Solidarity founded
tokens.title: Gdańsk shipyard strike birth of a union
tokens.description: Solidarity was founded in August 1980 at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk, Poland. It was the first independent trade union in a Warsaw Pact country to be recognised by the state.
tokens.image_credit: Zygmunt Błażek · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
tokens.title: Jewish fighters resist deportation
tokens.description: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising was a revolt by Jewish resistance in the Warsaw Ghetto in 1943 against the final deportation of the remaining ghetto population. It was the largest single revolt by Jews against the Nazis during World War II.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author (Franz Konrad confessed to taking some of the photographs, the rest was probably taken by photographers from Propaganda Kompanie nr 689.[1][2]) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Invasion of Poland
tokens.title: Start of the Second World War in Europe
tokens.description: The invasion of Poland, also known as the September Campaign, began on 1 September 1939 when Nazi Germany attacked Poland. The Soviet Union joined on 17 September, and the campaign ended on 6 October 1939 with Poland partitioned.
tokens.image_credit: Central Photographic Agency Warsaw / Centralna Agencja Fotograficzna (CAF), Military Photographic Agency Warsaw (WAF) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Grunwald
tokens.title: Poland-Lithuania defeats Teutonic Knights
tokens.description: The Battle of Grunwald, also known as the Battle of Tannenberg, was fought on 15 July 1410. A Polish-Lithuanian army led by Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas defeated the Teutonic Order.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Matejko · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Mohi
tokens.title: Mongols crush the Hungarian army
tokens.description: The Battle of Mohi, fought on 11 April 1241, ended in a Mongol victory over the Kingdom of Hungary during the Mongol invasion of Europe. Batu Khan's forces defeated the army of King Béla IV at Muhi, near the Sajó River.
tokens.image_credit: Anonymous illumination · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Mohács
tokens.title: Ottomans destroy Hungarian army
tokens.description: The Battle of Mohács was fought on 29 August 1526 near Mohács in the Kingdom of Hungary. The Ottoman army under Suleiman the Magnificent decisively defeated the Hungarian army led by King Louis II.
tokens.image_credit: Mór Than · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Katyn massacre
tokens.title: Polish officers executed
tokens.description: The Katyn massacre was the mass execution of nearly 22,000 Polish officers, police, border guards and members of the intelligentsia by the Soviet NKVD in April and May 1940. The killings were ordered by Stalin and are named after the Katyn forest near Smolensk.
tokens.image_credit: Goku122 at Polish Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Srebrenica massacre
tokens.title: Genocide in eastern Bosnia
tokens.description: The Srebrenica massacre was the killing of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys in and around the town of Srebrenica in July 1995, during the Bosnian War. It was mainly carried out by units of the Bosnian Serb Army under Ratko Mladić.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Büker · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Sarajevo
tokens.title: Longest siege of a capital in modern war
tokens.description: The siege of Sarajevo was a blockade of the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina during the Bosnian War, from 5 April 1992 to 29 February 1996. It is the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare.
tokens.image_credit: LT. STACEY WYZKOWSKI · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia
tokens.title: Kosovo air campaign
tokens.description: NATO's aerial bombing campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia during the Kosovo War ran from 24 March to 10 June 1999. It ended with an agreement that led to the withdrawal of Yugoslav forces from Kosovo and a UN mission there.
tokens.image_credit: Albert Horáček · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Vukovar
tokens.title: Three-month siege in Croatia
tokens.description: The Battle of Vukovar was an 87-day siege of the town of Vukovar in eastern Croatia by the Yugoslav People's Army and paramilitary forces from Serbia. It lasted from August to November 1991.
tokens.image_credit: anjči from London, UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
tokens.title: Cortés takes the Aztec capital
tokens.description: Between 1519 and 1521, Hernan Cortes and his Indigenous allies overthrew the Aztec Empire. The capital Tenochtitlan stood in what is now the historic centre of Mexico City.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Cajamarca
tokens.title: Pizarro seizes the Inca ruler at Cajamarca
tokens.description: On 16 November 1532 Francisco Pizarro and a small Spanish force ambushed and seized the Inca ruler Atahualpa in the plaza of Cajamarca. The capture opened the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Lepiani · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grito de Dolores
tokens.title: Hidalgo's call to arms
tokens.description: On 16 September 1810 the priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla rang his church bell in Dolores and gave the call to arms. The Cry of Dolores triggered the Mexican War of Independence.
tokens.image_credit: Paigemorrison at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mexican Revolution
tokens.title: Uprising against Porfirio Díaz
tokens.description: The Mexican Revolution was an extended series of armed regional conflicts in Mexico from 20 November 1910 to 1 December 1920. It is described as the defining event of modern Mexican history.
tokens.image_credit: Osuna · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Puebla
tokens.title: Origin of Cinco de Mayo
tokens.description: On 5 May 1862 Mexican forces repulsed French troops attacking the forts of Loreto and Guadalupe near Puebla de los Angeles. The battle is also known as the Battle of the Fifth of May.
tokens.image_credit: anonymous · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tlatelolco massacre
tokens.title: Students shot before the Olympics
tokens.description: On 2 October 1968 Mexican armed forces attacked students and others at a protest in the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Tlatelolco, Mexico City. It happened ten days before the 1968 Summer Olympics opened.
tokens.image_credit: Ralf Roletschek · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1985 Mexico City earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 8.0 strikes the capital
tokens.description: The main shock of magnitude 8.0 on 19 September 1985 caused serious damage across Greater Mexico City. It killed at least 5,000 people.
tokens.image_credit: United States Geological Survey · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1968 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: First Games in Latin America
tokens.description: The 1968 Summer Olympics were held from 12 to 27 October 1968 in Mexico City. They were the first Olympic Games staged in Latin America, and the main venue was the Estadio Olímpico Universitario.
tokens.image_credit: Edgar Efrén López Ramos · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zapatista uprising
tokens.title: Rebels seize towns in Chiapas
tokens.description: On 1 January 1994 the Zapatista Army of National Liberation launched a 12-day uprising in Chiapas, Mexico, against NAFTA. The rebels occupied towns in the state until a ceasefire on 12 January.
tokens.image_credit: AnonymousUnknown author · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chicxulub crater
tokens.title: Asteroid ends the age of dinosaurs
tokens.description: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater buried beneath the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico. It formed slightly over 66 million years ago when an asteroid about 10 km wide struck Earth.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY date

tokens.image_credit: Donald E. Davis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Chapultepec
tokens.title: Niños Héroes defend the castle
tokens.description: The Battle of Chapultepec was fought on 13 September 1847 between U.S. troops and Mexican forces holding Chapultepec Castle on the outskirts of Mexico City. It took place during the Mexican-American War.
tokens.image_credit: Adolphe Jean-Baptiste Bayot / Carl Nebel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of San Jacinto
tokens.title: Texas wins independence
tokens.description: The Battle of San Jacinto was fought on 21 April 1836 in present-day La Porte and Deer Park, Texas. Sam Houston's Texian Army defeated Santa Anna's Mexican army, the decisive battle of the Texas Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Henry Arthur McArdle · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haitian Revolution
tokens.title: Enslaved people overthrow French rule
tokens.description: The Haitian Revolution was an armed uprising by enslaved people against French colonial rule in Saint-Domingue, beginning with the slave revolt of 21 August 1791. It ended with Haiti's independence on 1 January 1804.
tokens.image_credit: Aaron Martinet / Alphonse-Charles Masson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Vertières
tokens.title: Final victory over Napoleon's army
tokens.description: The Battle of Vertières was fought on 18 November 1803 at Vertières, just south of Cap-Français in northern Haiti. It was the last major battle of the Haitian Revolution, between the rebel army under Jean-Jacques Dessalines and French forces under Rochambeau.
tokens.image_credit: Kitanago · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Haiti earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.0 near Port-au-Prince
tokens.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Haiti on 12 January 2010, with its epicentre near Leogane, about 25 km west of Port-au-Prince. It was a catastrophic disaster for the country.
tokens.image_credit: Trocaire from Ireland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Boyacá
tokens.title: Bolívar secures Colombia
tokens.description: The Battle of Boyacá in 1819 was a decisive victory by a combined army under Simón Bolívar over Spanish forces commanded by José María Barreiro. It secured the liberation campaign of New Granada.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Tovar y Tovar · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Carabobo
tokens.title: Venezuelan independence won
tokens.description: The Battle of Carabobo, fought on 24 June 1821, was won by Simón Bolívar's independence forces over the royalist army led by Miguel de la Torre. The victory led to the independence of Venezuela.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Ayacucho
tokens.title: End of Spanish rule in South America
tokens.description: The Battle of Ayacucho was the decisive encounter of the Peruvian War of Independence, fought against Spanish royalist forces. Its patriot victory secured Peru's independence and is considered the end of the Spanish American wars of independence in Peru.
tokens.image_credit: Martín Tovar y Tovar · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Pichincha
tokens.title: Sucre frees Quito
tokens.description: The Battle of Pichincha, fought on 24 May 1822 on the slopes of the Pichincha volcano near Quito, was a Patriot victory under Antonio José de Sucre over Royalist forces under Melchor Aymerich. It led to the liberation of Quito.

tokens.name: Battle of Maipú
tokens.title: San Martín secures Chilean independence
tokens.description: The Battle of Maipú, fought on 5 April 1818 near Santiago, was won by the Patriot army of José de San Martín over the Spanish royalist forces of Mariano Osorio. It completed the independence of central Chile.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Subercaseaux · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Crossing of the Andes
tokens.title: San Martín's army crosses the mountains
tokens.description: The Crossing of the Andes in January and February 1817 was led by José de San Martín, whose army marched from Mendoza over the mountains into Chile. The campaign led to the liberation of Chile from Spanish rule.
tokens.image_credit: Julio Vila y Prades · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guayaquil Conference
tokens.title: Bolívar meets San Martín
tokens.description: The Guayaquil Conference, held on 26 and 27 July 1822 in the port city of Guayaquil, was a meeting between Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín on the future of Peru and South America. It is considered a turning point in South American independence.
tokens.image_credit: Padaguan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: May Revolution
tokens.title: Buenos Aires sets up its own government
tokens.description: The May Revolution was a week of events from 18 to 25 May 1810 in Buenos Aires that removed the Viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros. It led to the First Junta, a local government set up on 25 May.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Manuel Blanes · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Argentine Declaration of Independence
tokens.title: Signed at Tucumán
tokens.description: On 9 July 1816 the Congress of Tucumán declared the independence of the United Provinces of South America, the origin of Argentina's national independence. The congress met in San Miguel de Tucumán.
tokens.image_credit: Francisco Fortuny · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Falklands War
tokens.title: Argentina invades the islands
tokens.description: The Falklands War was a ten-week war in 1982 between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands and its dependencies. Argentina invaded the islands on 2 April 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Ken Griffiths · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of ARA General Belgrano
tokens.title: Cruiser sunk by HMS Conqueror
tokens.description: The Argentine cruiser ARA General Belgrano was sunk on 2 May 1982 by the British nuclear submarine HMS Conqueror during the Falklands War. The attack killed 323 Argentine sailors, almost half of Argentina's casualties in the conflict.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dirty War
tokens.title: Military coup in Argentina
tokens.description: The Dirty War was the period of state-sponsored violence in Argentina from 1974 to 1983, carried out by the military junta and death squads. An estimated 13,000 to 30,000 people were killed or disappeared.
tokens.image_credit: WikiLaurent · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1978 FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: Hosts win the title
tokens.description: The 1978 FIFA World Cup was the 11th FIFA World Cup, held in Argentina from 1 to 25 June 1978. Argentina defeated the Netherlands 3 to 1 after extra time in the final.

tokens.name: Goal of the Century
tokens.title: Maradona dribbles past half the England side
tokens.description: Diego Maradona scored this goal in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England at the Estadio Azteca, Mexico City, on 22 June 1986. It is one of the most famous goals in football history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown, photographer from El Gráfico · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maracanazo
tokens.title: Uruguay stuns Brazil in Rio
tokens.description: Uruguay beat Brazil in the decisive match of the 1950 FIFA World Cup, played at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro on 16 July 1950. The result gave Uruguay the title and is known as the Maracanazo.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1970 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: Brazil wins its third title
tokens.description: The final of the 1970 FIFA World Cup was played at the Estadio Azteca, Mexico City, on 21 June 1970. Brazil beat Italy 4-1 to win its third title.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1950 FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: First tournament after the war
tokens.description: The 1950 FIFA World Cup was the fourth edition of the football championship, held in Brazil from 24 June to 16 July 1950. It was the first World Cup in 12 years, after the 1942 and 1946 editions were cancelled because of the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2016 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: First Games in South America
tokens.description: The 2016 Summer Olympics were an international multi-sport event held from 5 to 21 August 2016 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Some 11,238 athletes from 207 nations took part in the Games.
tokens.image_credit: Agência Brasil · CC BY 3.0 br · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Proclamation of the Republic of Brazil
tokens.title: Empire ends in a bloodless coup
tokens.description: The Proclamation of the Republic was a military coup of 15 November 1889 in Rio de Janeiro that ended the Empire of Brazil. It established the First Brazilian Republic and deposed Emperor Pedro II.
tokens.image_credit: Benedito Calixto · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Independence of Brazil
tokens.title: Grito do Ipiranga
tokens.description: On 7 September 1822 Prince Regent Pedro declared Brazil's independence from Portugal beside the Ipiranga brook in Sao Paulo, the Cry of Ipiranga. Portugal gave formal recognition in the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro of 1825.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Américo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: War of Canudos
tokens.title: Millenarian settlement destroyed in Bahia
tokens.description: The War of Canudos was a conflict from 1896 to 1897 between the First Brazilian Republic and the residents of Canudos in Bahia. It arose from a millenarian cult led by Antonio Conselheiro.
tokens.image_credit: Flávio de Barros · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: War of the Pacific
tokens.title: Chile, Peru and Bolivia fight over nitrates
tokens.description: The War of the Pacific was fought from 1879 to 1884 between Chile and a Bolivian and Peruvian alliance. It was fought over Bolivia's coastal territory in the Atacama Desert, and Chile gained resource-rich territory from both countries.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Somerscales · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Iquique
tokens.title: Prat sacrifices the Esmeralda
tokens.description: The Battle of Iquique was a naval engagement on 21 May 1879 in the War of the Pacific, fought off the port of Iquique. The Chilean corvette Esmeralda was sunk by the Peruvian ironclad Huascar, a Peruvian victory.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Somerscales · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chaco War
tokens.title: Bolivia and Paraguay in the Gran Chaco
tokens.description: The Chaco War was fought from 1932 to 1935 between Bolivia and Paraguay over the northern Gran Chaco, a region then thought to be rich in petroleum. It is also called the War of Thirst because of the semi-arid terrain.
tokens.image_credit: Doctor Carlos De Sanctis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1973 Chilean coup d'état
tokens.title: La Moneda palace bombed
tokens.description: On 11 September 1973 a military coup led by General Augusto Pinochet overthrew the socialist government of President Salvador Allende in Chile. The coup ended civilian rule, and the La Moneda Palace in Santiago was bombed during the assault.
tokens.image_credit: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de Chile · CC BY 3.0 cl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Chile earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 8.8 and tsunami
tokens.description: A magnitude 8.8 megathrust earthquake struck off the coast of the Maule Region in central Chile on 27 February 2010. It was one of the most powerful earthquakes ever recorded.
tokens.image_credit: Claudio Núñez · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1960 Valdivia earthquake
tokens.title: Strongest earthquake ever recorded
tokens.description: On 22 May 1960 an earthquake and tsunami devastated the city of Valdivia in southern Chile. Most studies place its magnitude at 9.4 to 9.6, the strongest earthquake ever recorded.
tokens.image_credit: Pierre St. Amand · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Copiapó mining accident
tokens.title: Thirty-three miners trapped 69 days
tokens.description: A cave-in on 5 August 2010 trapped 33 miners 700 metres underground at the San José copper-gold mine in the Atacama Desert. All 33 were rescued 69 days later.
tokens.image_credit: desierto_atacama · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Cusco
tokens.title: Manco Inca besieges the Spanish
tokens.description: The 10-month siege of Cusco by the Inca army under Sapa Inca Manco Inca Yupanqui began on 6 May 1536 and ended in March 1537. The Spanish garrison was led by Hernando Pizarro.

tokens.name: Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II
tokens.title: Great Andean uprising against Spain
tokens.description: An uprising by Aymara, Quechua and mestizo rebels against Spanish colonial rule in Peru lasted from 1780 to 1783. It was led by the kuraka Túpac Amaru II, who was captured and executed in 1781.
tokens.image_credit: Tadeo Escalante · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bolivian National Revolution
tokens.title: Mines nationalised, vote extended
tokens.description: The Bolivian Revolution of 1952 was a series of political demonstrations led by the Revolutionary Nationalist Movement that sought to overthrow the Bolivian oligarchy. The MNR government it brought to power lasted from 9 April 1952 until a coup in 1964.
tokens.image_credit: Carwil Bjork-James · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cochabamba Water War
tokens.title: Protests over water privatisation
tokens.description: A series of protests in Cochabamba, Bolivia, between December 1999 and April 2000 opposed the privatization of the city's municipal water company SEMAPA. The dispute centred on the Aguas del Tunari consortium, which included Bechtel.
tokens.image_credit: Antonio Abal Oña · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace of Justice siege
tokens.title: M-19 attack in Bogotá
tokens.description: The Palace of Justice siege was an attack on 6 and 7 November 1985 in which M-19 guerrillas seized the Supreme Court building in Bogota. Hundreds of hostages were held until the army stormed the building, and many people died in the fighting.
tokens.image_credit: National Police of Colombia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bogotazo
tokens.title: Riots after Gaitán assassination
tokens.description: The Bogotazo was a wave of rioting in Bogota that followed the assassination of Liberal leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan on 9 April 1948. The riot lasted about ten hours and left much of downtown Bogota destroyed.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Pradilla Holguin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Armero tragedy
tokens.title: Nevado del Ruiz mudflows bury a town
tokens.description: The Armero tragedy followed the eruption of the Nevado del Ruiz volcano in Tolima, Colombia, on 13 November 1985. Lahars swept down its slopes and buried the town of Armero, causing a catastrophic loss of life.
tokens.image_credit: N. Banks (w:United States Geological Survey) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vargas tragedy
tokens.title: Floods and landslides on the coast
tokens.description: The Vargas tragedy was a natural disaster in Vargas State, Venezuela, in December 1999, when torrential rains caused flash floods and debris flows. The disaster killed tens of thousands of people and destroyed coastal communities.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Copyrighted free use · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United States invasion of Panama
tokens.title: Noriega ousted
tokens.description: The United States invasion of Panama, codenamed Operation Just Cause, began in December 1989 to depose General Manuel Noriega. The operation ended in late January 1990 with Noriega's surrender.
tokens.image_credit: SPEC. MORLAND · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nicaraguan Revolution
tokens.title: Sandinistas topple Somoza
tokens.description: The Nicaraguan Revolution was an armed conflict from 1961 to 1990 that began with opposition to the Somoza dictatorship. The Sandinistas overthrew Somoza in 1979, and fighting with the Contras continued until 1990.
tokens.image_credit: Puskechina · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Football War
tokens.title: Honduras and El Salvador clash after matches
tokens.description: The Football War was a brief military conflict between El Salvador and Honduras that began on 14 July 1969. Existing tensions and rioting around a 1970 World Cup qualifier gave it its nickname.

tokens.name: United States invasion of Grenada
tokens.title: US-led Operation Urgent Fury
tokens.description: The United States and a coalition of Caribbean countries invaded Grenada at dawn on 25 October 1983 in Operation Urgent Fury. The invasion followed the execution of former Prime Minister Maurice Bishop and led to a military occupation within a few days.
tokens.image_credit: photographer: TSgt. M. J. Creen, USAF · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1902 eruption of Mount Pelée
tokens.title: Saint-Pierre destroyed
tokens.description: The 1902 eruption of Mount Pelée on Martinique was one of the deadliest eruptions in recorded history. Eruptive activity began on 23 April 1902 as a series of phreatic eruptions from the summit.
tokens.image_credit: B.L. Singley, Keystone View Company · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1900 Galveston hurricane
tokens.title: Deadliest US natural disaster
tokens.description: The 1900 Galveston hurricane was the deadliest natural disaster in United States history, with between 6,000 and 12,000 fatalities. The storm surge inundated the city of Galveston, Texas, where most of the deaths occurred.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Maria
tokens.title: Category 4 landfall in Puerto Rico
tokens.description: Hurricane Maria was an extremely powerful tropical cyclone that struck Puerto Rico in September 2017. It accounted for 2,975 of the 3,059 storm deaths in Puerto Rico, the deadliest hurricane to hit the island.
tokens.image_credit: SC National Guard · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Andrew
tokens.title: Category 5 strike on South Florida
tokens.description: Hurricane Andrew was a compact but extremely powerful tropical cyclone that struck South Florida in 1992. It was the most destructive hurricane ever to hit Florida in terms of structures damaged or destroyed.
tokens.image_credit: NOAA / National Weather Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Sandy
tokens.title: Superstorm floods New York
tokens.description: Hurricane Sandy, also called Superstorm Sandy, was an extremely large and devastating tropical cyclone that ravaged the Caribbean and the US Mid-Atlantic coast in October 2012. It killed 254 people in eight countries and caused nearly US$70 billion in damage.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Master Sgt. Mark C. Olsen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Mitch
tokens.title: Central America devastated by floods
tokens.description: Hurricane Mitch was an extremely powerful and deadly tropical cyclone that struck in 1998 and caused 11,374 fatalities in Central America. It was the deadliest hurricane in Central American history.
tokens.image_credit: United States Geological Survey · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Landing at Anzac Cove
tokens.title: Anzac troops land at Gallipoli
tokens.description: Night landing of mostly Australian and New Zealand Army Corps troops on the western coast of the Gallipoli Peninsula on 25 April 1915. It opened the land phase of the Gallipoli campaign of the First World War.
tokens.image_credit: Published by Brookes · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Beersheba 1917
tokens.title: Australian Light Horse charge
tokens.description: On 31 October 1917 British Empire forces captured the Ottoman garrison of Beersheba, opening the Southern Palestine Offensive. The final attack included a mounted charge by Australian Light Horse regiments.
tokens.image_credit: AWM Credit reads: Lent by Brigadier General Wilson, CMG. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kokoda Track campaign
tokens.title: Jungle fight in Papua
tokens.description: A series of battles fought between July and November 1942 in the Australian Territory of Papua. The Japanese South Seas Detachment tried to reach Port Moresby by crossing the Owen Stanley Range on the Kokoda Track.
tokens.image_credit: Parer, Damien Peter · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bombing of Darwin
tokens.title: Japan's largest attack on Australia
tokens.description: On 19 February 1942 Japanese aircraft made two raids on the Australian town of Darwin, its harbour and airfields. It was the largest single attack ever mounted by a foreign power on Australia.
tokens.image_credit: RAN Historical Collection · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eureka Rebellion
tokens.title: Gold miners rise at the Eureka Stockade
tokens.description: Gold miners revolted against the British colonial administration of Victoria, culminating in the Battle of the Eureka Stockade at Ballarat on 3 December 1854. The fighting left 27 official deaths, most of them rebels.
tokens.image_credit: John Black Henderson (1827-1918) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Federation of Australia
tokens.title: Colonies unite as the Commonwealth
tokens.description: The process by which the six British self-governing colonies of Australia united to form the Commonwealth of Australia as a federation. The Commonwealth was inaugurated in Sydney on 1 January 1901.
tokens.image_credit: W. A. Gullick · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Fleet
tokens.title: Settlement begins at Sydney Cove
tokens.description: The First Fleet was eleven British ships that carried convicts, marines and settlers to Australia under Captain Arthur Phillip. They reached Botany Bay in January 1788 and settled at Sydney Cove, starting the British colonisation of Australia.
tokens.image_credit: William Bradley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mabo v Queensland
tokens.title: High Court recognises native title
tokens.description: Decision of the High Court of Australia on 3 June 1992 that recognised Native Title in Australia. It was brought by Eddie Mabo and others against the State of Queensland.
tokens.image_credit: Bidgee · CC BY-SA 3.0 au · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2000 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Cathy Freeman lights the cauldron
tokens.description: The 2000 Summer Olympics were an international multi-sport event held from 15 September to 1 October 2000 in Sydney, Australia. Teams from 199 countries took part in the Games.
tokens.image_credit: TSGT Rick Sforza · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1956 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: First Games in the Southern Hemisphere
tokens.description: The 1956 Summer Olympics were an international multi-sport event held in Melbourne, Australia, from 22 November to 8 December 1956. They were the first Games staged in the Southern Hemisphere and Oceania.

tokens.name: 1975 Australian constitutional crisis
tokens.title: Governor-General sacks the prime minister
tokens.description: The 1975 Australian constitutional crisis ended with the dismissal of Prime Minister Gough Whitlam by Governor-General Sir John Kerr on 11 November 1975. It is described as the greatest political and constitutional crisis in Australian history.
tokens.image_credit: Tirin also known as Takver - www.takver.com · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black Saturday bushfires
tokens.title: Victoria's deadliest bushfires
tokens.description: The Black Saturday bushfires were a series of bushfires that burned across the Australian state of Victoria on 7 February 2009. They caused Australia's highest loss of human life from a bushfire, with 173 deaths.
tokens.image_credit: Nick carson at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2019-20 Australian bushfire season
tokens.title: Catastrophic Australian fire season
tokens.description: The 2019-20 Australian bushfire season, also known as the Black Summer, was one of the most intense fire seasons on record in Australia. Over ten thousand fires burnt, mainly in the south-east of the country, until March 2020.
tokens.image_credit: NASA ISS · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burke and Wills expedition
tokens.title: First south-north crossing attempt
tokens.description: The Burke and Wills expedition, originally the Victorian Exploring Expedition, was organised in 1860-61 by the Royal Society of Victoria. It aimed to cross Australia from Melbourne to the Gulf of Carpentaria, about 3,250 kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Ludwig Becker · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port Arthur massacre
tokens.title: Led to national gun law reform
tokens.description: The Port Arthur massacre was a mass shooting on 28 April 1996 at Port Arthur, Tasmania, in which 35 people were murdered. The attack led to fundamental changes in Australia's gun laws.
tokens.image_credit: Elzbenz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Waitangi
tokens.title: Māori chiefs and the Crown sign
tokens.description: The Treaty of Waitangi is an 1840 agreement between the British Crown and Māori rangatira. It is a document of importance to the history of New Zealand and its national identity.
tokens.image_credit: Archives New Zealand from New Zealand · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Rangiriri
tokens.title: Waikato War clash
tokens.description: The Battle of Rangiriri was fought on 20 and 21 November 1863 during the New Zealand Wars, in the British invasion of Waikato. More than 1400 British troops defeated about 500 Kingitanga warriors at the Rangiriri pa.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Heaphy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New Zealand Wars
tokens.title: Conflicts over land and sovereignty
tokens.description: The New Zealand Wars took place from 1845 to 1872 between the colonial government and allied Māori, and Māori and Māori-allied settlers. They were triggered by disputed land purchases and escalated from 1860 over Crown sovereignty.
tokens.image_credit: VPassau · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Women's suffrage in New Zealand
tokens.title: First self-governing country to do so
tokens.description: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing nation in which all women could vote in parliamentary elections. The campaign was led by Kate Sheppard and other suffrage campaigners.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Cutts · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake
tokens.title: Napier destroyed
tokens.description: The 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake struck New Zealand on 3 February 1931 with a magnitude of about 7.8 and killed 256 people. It remains New Zealand's deadliest natural disaster, devastating Napier and the Hawke's Bay region.
tokens.image_credit: Archives New Zealand from New Zealand · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2011 Christchurch earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 6.2 hits the city
tokens.description: A Mw 6.2 earthquake struck Christchurch on 22 February 2011, centred 6.7 km south-east of the central business district. The shaking caused severe damage across the city and the Canterbury Region.
tokens.image_credit: Greg O'Beirne · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Christchurch mosque shootings
tokens.title: Attacks on two mosques
tokens.description: On 15 March 2019, two terrorist mass shootings took place during Friday prayer. They targeted the Al Noor Mosque in Riccarton and the Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch.
tokens.image_credit: Michal Klajban · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Erebus disaster
tokens.title: Air New Zealand flight crashes in Antarctica
tokens.description: On 28 November 1979 Air New Zealand Flight 901 flew into Mount Erebus on Ross Island, Antarctica, killing all 257 people on board. It was a scheduled Antarctic sightseeing flight from Auckland.
tokens.image_credit: Phantomwiki · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of the Rainbow Warrior
tokens.title: Greenpeace ship bombed in Auckland
tokens.description: The Greenpeace flagship Rainbow Warrior was sunk by French DGSE agents at the Port of Auckland on 10 July 1985. The operation, codenamed Opération Satanique, targeted the ship before it could protest a French nuclear test at Moruroa.
tokens.image_credit: Kiwi Flickr from Auckland, New Zealand · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Singapore
tokens.title: Largest British surrender
tokens.description: Japan captured the British base at Singapore between 8 and 15 February 1942 during the Pacific War. Singapore was then the foremost British military base and port in South-East Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Photographer not identified. "Official photograph". Post-Work: User:W.wolny · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malayan Emergency
tokens.title: Communist insurgency in Malaya
tokens.description: The Malayan Emergency was a guerrilla war from 1948 to 1960 between communist insurgents of the Malayan National Liberation Army and the Federation of Malaya with Commonwealth forces. The British used the word Emergency to avoid calling it a war.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Disappearance of MH370
tokens.title: Boeing 777 vanishes over the Indian Ocean
tokens.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, a Boeing 777 flying from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, disappeared from radar on 8 March 2014 with 239 people aboard. The cause of the disappearance has not been determined.
tokens.image_credit: مانفی · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Khe Sanh
tokens.title: Marines besieged near the DMZ
tokens.description: The Siege of Khe Sanh lasted from 21 January to 9 July 1968 in Quang Tri Province, South Vietnam, during the Vietnam War. A United States Marine Corps regiment and an ARVN battalion defended Khe Sanh Combat Base against North Vietnamese forces.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tet Offensive
tokens.title: Surprise attacks across South Vietnam
tokens.description: The Tet Offensive was a surprise attack by North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces on South Vietnam and its allies, launched on 30 and 31 January 1968. It was one of the largest military campaigns of the Vietnam War.
tokens.image_credit: US military personnel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gulf of Tonkin incident
tokens.title: Incident that escalated US involvement
tokens.description: The Gulf of Tonkin incident was a naval clash in August 1964 between US Navy destroyers and North Vietnamese vessels off North Vietnam. It led the United States to engage more directly in the Vietnam War.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Navy sailor aboard USS Maddox (DD-731) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: My Lai massacre
tokens.title: US troops kill civilians
tokens.description: The My Lai massacre was a war crime committed by US Army soldiers on 16 March 1968 in Son My village, Quang Ngai province, South Vietnam. Between 347 and 504 civilians, almost all women, children and elderly men, were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Ronald L. Haeberle · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Bạch Đằng 1288
tokens.title: River stakes trap the Mongol fleet
tokens.description: The Battle of Bạch Đằng in 1288 was a naval battle in which Đại Việt forces ambushed and destroyed the Yuan fleet on the Bạch Đằng River during the third Mongol invasion of Vietnam. It is counted among the greatest victories in Vietnamese military history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trưng sisters rebellion
tokens.title: Two sisters lead revolt against Han
tokens.description: The Trưng sisters, Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị, led a rebellion in AD 40 against the first Chinese domination of Vietnam. They then ruled for three years as Lạc Việt military leaders.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thích Quảng Đức self-immolation
tokens.title: Protest in Saigon
tokens.description: Thích Quảng Đức, a Vietnamese Buddhist monk, died by self-immolation at a busy Saigon road intersection on 11 June 1963. He was protesting against the persecution of Buddhists by the Diệm government, and photographs of the act circulated worldwide.

tokens.name: Fall of Phnom Penh
tokens.title: Khmer Rouge enter the capital
tokens.description: The Khmer Rouge captured Phnom Penh, capital of the Khmer Republic, on 17 April 1975. The capture effectively ended the Cambodian Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: United States Air Force photo 110342 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cambodian genocide
tokens.title: Killing fields of Democratic Kampuchea
tokens.description: The Cambodian genocide was the systematic persecution and killing of Cambodian citizens by the Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot. It killed approximately 2 million people between 1975 and 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tham Luang cave rescue
tokens.title: Boys' football team rescued after 18 days
tokens.description: In June 2018 a junior football team and their coach became trapped in the Tham Luang Nang Non cave system in Chiang Rai province, northern Thailand. They were rescued after 18 days.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Air Force Capt. Jessica Tait 353rd Special Operations Group Public Affairs · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siamese revolution of 1932
tokens.title: Absolute monarchy ends
tokens.description: On 24 June 1932 the Khana Ratsadon staged a coup in Siam that ended the absolute monarchy of the Chakri dynasty. The transition was largely bloodless and introduced the first constitution and a National Assembly.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Ayutthaya
tokens.title: Burmese army sacks the capital
tokens.description: Burmese forces captured the Siamese capital Ayutthaya on 7 April 1767, after a siege of about fourteen months. The city was sacked and burned, and the war ended the Ayutthaya Kingdom.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel R. Witte · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 8888 Uprising
tokens.title: Mass protests across Burma
tokens.description: The 8888 Uprising was a series of nationwide protests, marches and riots in Burma that peaked in August 1988. It began as a student movement, and its key events took place on 8 August 1988.

tokens.name: Saffron Revolution
tokens.title: Monks lead protests in Burma
tokens.description: The Saffron Revolution was a series of economic and political protests in Myanmar from August to October 2007, joined by many Buddhist monks. The protests began after the military government removed fuel subsidies, sharply raising fuel prices.
tokens.image_credit: racoles · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cyclone Nargis
tokens.title: Irrawaddy Delta devastated
tokens.description: Cyclone Nargis was a tropical cyclone that struck Myanmar on 2 May 2008, causing the worst natural disaster in the country's recorded history. The storm surge devastated the Irrawaddy Delta and killed at least 138,000 people.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
tokens.title: Military seizes power
tokens.description: The 2021 Myanmar coup d'état began on 1 February 2021, when the military deposed the elected government of the National League for Democracy. The Tatmadaw then vested power in a military junta and declared a state of emergency.
tokens.image_credit: VOA Burmese · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Imphal
tokens.title: Japanese advance into India halted
tokens.description: The Battle of Imphal was fought from March to July 1944 around Imphal, capital of Manipur in north-east India. The Japanese invasion of India was halted and driven back into Burma, a turning point of the Burma campaign.
tokens.image_credit: British Information Service, information service operated by UK government during WW2. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kohima
tokens.title: Fight over a tennis court
tokens.description: The Battle of Kohima was fought from April to June 1944 around the town of Kohima in north-east India. It was the turning point of the Japanese U-Go offensive into British India during the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: Official photographer of No.9 Army Film and Photographic Unit. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Kabul 2021
tokens.title: Taliban retake the capital
tokens.description: On 15 August 2021 the Taliban captured Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan, after an insurgent offensive that began in May. The capture ended the War in Afghanistan and led to the collapse of the Islamic Republic government.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Central Command Public Affairs · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Destruction of the Buddhas of Bamiyan
tokens.title: Taliban demolish giant statues
tokens.description: In March 2001 the Taliban destroyed the two monumental Buddhist reliefs carved into the cliffs of the Bamiyan Valley in Afghanistan. The statues, dating from about the 6th century, were destroyed after a Taliban order to remove all statues in the country.
tokens.image_credit: James Gordon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1842 retreat from Kabul
tokens.title: British column destroyed
tokens.description: The 1842 retreat from Kabul was the withdrawal of British and East India Company forces from Kabul during the First Anglo-Afghan War. Attacked by Afghan tribesmen in January 1842, the army and its dependants marched towards the British garrison at Jalalabad.
tokens.image_credit: Elizabeth Thompson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Maiwand
tokens.title: Afghan victory over British brigade
tokens.description: The Battle of Maiwand was fought on 27 July 1880 during the Second Anglo-Afghan War, near Maiwand in Kandahar Province. An Afghan army under Mohammad Ayub Khan defeated a British and Indian force under George Burrows.
tokens.image_credit: Archives New Zealand from New Zealand · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Tora Bora
tokens.title: Search for al-Qaeda leaders
tokens.description: The Battle of Tora Bora was fought from 30 November to 17 December 2001 around the Tora Bora cave complex in eastern Afghanistan, during the United States invasion of Afghanistan. US, British, German and allied Afghan forces fought al-Qaeda and Taliban fighters there.

tokens.name: Battle of Yamen
tokens.title: Song dynasty ends at sea
tokens.description: The Battle of Yamen was a naval battle fought on 19 March 1279 in southern China. It is considered the last stand of the Song dynasty against the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty.
tokens.image_credit: (Long night without wind) 长夜无风 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Red Cliffs
tokens.title: Fire attack decides the Three Kingdoms
tokens.description: The Battle of Red Cliffs, also known as the Battle of Chibi, was a decisive naval battle fought on the Yangtze River in 208 to 209 AD. Allied forces under Sun Quan and Liu Bei defeated the larger army of Cao Cao.
tokens.image_credit: User Jie on en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Changping
tokens.title: Qin crushes Zhao
tokens.description: The Battle of Changping was fought from 262 to 260 BC between the Qin and Zhao states during the Warring States period. Qin won a decisive victory, and most of the Zhao captives were executed.

tokens.name: Battle of Gaixia
tokens.title: Liu Bang defeats Xiang Yu
tokens.description: The Battle of Gaixia was fought in December 203 BC between the Han forces of Liu Bang and the Western Chu forces of Xiang Yu. It was the final major battle of the Chu-Han Contention, after which Liu Bang became emperor of the Han dynasty.

tokens.name: Battle of Fei River
tokens.title: Jin repels Former Qin
tokens.description: The Battle of Fei River in 383 AD saw the outnumbered Eastern Jin army defeat the Former Qin forces. The battle is seen as decisive for the survival of the Eastern Jin and Han-ruled regimes in South China.

tokens.name: Battle of Muye
tokens.title: Zhou overthrows the Shang
tokens.description: The Battle of Muye, fought around 1046 BC, saw the Zhou forces of King Wu defeat the Shang army of Di Xin. The victory ended the Shang dynasty and established the Zhou dynasty.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY date

tokens.name: Burning of books and burying of scholars
tokens.title: Qin suppresses dissenting writings
tokens.description: The burning of books and burying of scholars were acts of intellectual suppression attributed to Qin Shi Huang from 213 BCE. They targeted texts praising the defeated states and scholars accused of keeping forbidden books.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown (18??–18??) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: An Lushan rebellion
tokens.title: Rebellion shakes the Tang dynasty
tokens.description: The An Lushan rebellion was a civil war in China from 755 to 763, at the midpoint of the Tang dynasty. Rebel forces captured the capital Chang'an before Tang and allied armies defeated them.

tokens.name: Taiping Rebellion
tokens.title: Civil war with tens of millions dead
tokens.description: The Taiping Rebellion (1850 to 1864) was a civil war between the Qing dynasty and the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Death toll estimates range from 20 million to 100 million, making it the deadliest civil war in history.
tokens.image_credit: Wu Youru · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Opium War
tokens.title: Britain and Qing China at war
tokens.description: The First Opium War (1839 to 1842) was a series of military engagements between the British Empire and Qing China. It began over Chinese seizures of opium at Canton and ended with the Treaty of Nanking.
tokens.image_credit: Edward Duncan · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Nanking
tokens.title: Hong Kong ceded to Britain
tokens.description: The Treaty of Nanking was signed on 29 August 1842 aboard HMS Cornwallis at Nanjing, ending the First Opium War. It ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain and opened several Chinese ports to trade.
tokens.image_credit: Painted by Captain John Platt, Bengal Volunteers. Engraved by John Burnet. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of the International Legations
tokens.title: Boxers besiege the Beijing quarter
tokens.description: The Siege of the International Legations was a 1900 episode of the Boxer Rebellion in Peking. About 900 foreign soldiers, sailors and civilians sheltered in the Legation Quarter until an international relief force broke the siege in August 1900.
tokens.image_credit: H. Charles McBarron, Jr. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1911 Revolution
tokens.title: Wuchang uprising ends Qing rule
tokens.description: The 1911 Revolution, also known as the Xinhai Revolution, ended the 267-year Qing dynasty, China's last imperial dynasty. It led to the establishment of the Republic of China.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: May Fourth Movement
tokens.title: Student protests in Beijing
tokens.description: The May Fourth Movement was a Chinese cultural and anti-imperialist movement that grew out of student protests in Beijing on 4 May 1919. The protests against the Treaty of Versailles spread nationwide and boosted Chinese nationalism.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Xi'an Incident
tokens.title: Chiang Kai-shek detained
tokens.description: The Xi'an Incident was a political crisis from 12 to 26 December 1936, when Generals Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng detained Chiang Kai-shek in Xi'an. It led to a united front of the Nationalists and the Chinese Communist Party against Japan.
tokens.image_credit: Timshi · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marco Polo Bridge incident
tokens.title: Start of full-scale war with Japan
tokens.description: The Marco Polo Bridge incident was a three-day battle that began on 7 July 1937 near Beijing, between the Chinese 29th Army and the Imperial Japanese Army. It is commonly regarded as the start of full-scale war between China and Japan.
tokens.image_credit: User:Vmenkov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mukden incident
tokens.title: Pretext for Japan's invasion of Manchuria
tokens.description: The Mukden incident was a false flag event staged by Japanese military personnel near Mukden (now Shenyang) on 18 September 1931. It served as the pretext for the Japanese invasion of Manchuria.

tokens.name: Battle of Shanghai
tokens.title: Three-month fight for the city
tokens.description: The Battle of Shanghai was fought from 13 August to 26 November 1937 between Japan and the Republic of China in and around Shanghai. It ended with the Japanese capture of the city and is regarded as one of the largest and longest battles of the Second Sino-Japanese War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1976 Tangshan earthquake
tokens.title: One of the deadliest quakes of the century
tokens.description: The 1976 Tangshan earthquake struck Tangshan, Hebei, China, at 03:42 local time on 28 July 1976. Rated Mw 7.6 with maximum Mercalli intensity XI, it is one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: Zinderboff · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 Sichuan earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.9 in Wenchuan
tokens.description: The 2008 Sichuan earthquake struck Sichuan province, China, on 12 May 2008 at 14:28 local time. It measured 7.9 Mw, with its epicentre about 80 km west-northwest of Chengdu, and ruptured a fault over 240 km long.
tokens.image_credit: 人神之间 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1931 China floods
tokens.title: Possibly the deadliest flood in history
tokens.description: The 1931 China floods were a series of floods from June to August 1931 along the Yangtze and Huai rivers, hitting cities including Wuhan and Nanjing. Death toll estimates vary widely, from about 140,000 to 2 million.

tokens.name: Banqiao Dam
tokens.title: Typhoon-driven dam collapses
tokens.description: The Banqiao Reservoir Dam on the River Ru in Zhumadian, Henan province, China, was among 62 dams in the area that failed in 1975 during Typhoon Nina. The dam was subsequently rebuilt.

tokens.name: Handover of Hong Kong
tokens.title: British rule ends after 156 years
tokens.description: The transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong from the United Kingdom to the People's Republic of China took place at midnight on 1 July 1997. It ended 156 years of British rule that began with the capture of Hong Kong Island in 1841.

tokens.name: 2014 Hong Kong protests
tokens.title: Occupy protests for democracy
tokens.description: A series of sit-in street protests in Hong Kong from 26 September to 15 December 2014, also known as the Umbrella Movement. They were sparked by a decision of the National People's Congress Standing Committee on electoral reform.
tokens.image_credit: STUDIO KANU · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Bird's Nest opening ceremony
tokens.description: The 2008 Summer Olympics were held from 8 to 24 August 2008 in Beijing, China, with 10,942 athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees. It was the first Summer Games held in China.
tokens.image_credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shenzhou 5
tokens.title: China's first crewed spaceflight
tokens.description: Shenzhou 5 was the first human spaceflight of the Chinese space program, launched on 15 October 2003 on a Long March 2F rocket. It was the first crewed mission of the Shenzhou spacecraft series.

tokens.name: Chang'e 4
tokens.title: First soft landing on the Moon's far side
tokens.description: Chang'e 4 is a Chinese robotic lunar mission that made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon on 3 January 2019. It was launched on a Long March 3B rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center.
tokens.image_credit: CSNA/Siyu Zhang/Kevin M. Gill · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chang'e 5
tokens.title: Lunar samples returned to Earth
tokens.description: Chang'e 5 was China's first lunar sample-return mission, launched on 23 November 2020 from Wenchang on Hainan Island. It collected about 1.7 kg of lunar samples and returned to Earth on 16 December 2020.
tokens.image_credit: China News Service · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Project 596
tokens.title: Project 596 at Lop Nur
tokens.description: Project 596 was China's first nuclear test, detonated on 16 October 1964 at the Lop Nur test site in Xinjiang. The implosion device had a yield of about 22 kilotons.
tokens.image_credit: 《人民画报》 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Taiwan Strait Crisis
tokens.title: Shelling of Kinmen
tokens.description: The First Taiwan Strait Crisis was a brief armed conflict in 1954 and 1955 between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of China over islands near the mainland. The PRC bombarded Kinmen from September 1954, and shelling later extended to the Matsu and Tachen islands.
tokens.image_credit: AnonymousUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: February 28 incident
tokens.title: Uprising and crackdown in Taiwan
tokens.description: The February 28 incident was an anti-government uprising in Taiwan in 1947 that was violently suppressed by the Nationalist government. Thousands of civilians were killed beginning on February 28.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1999 Jiji earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.7 in central Taiwan
tokens.description: The 1999 Jiji earthquake, also called the Chi-Chi or 921 earthquake, was a magnitude 7.7 Mw earthquake that struck central Taiwan on September 21, 1999. It killed 2,415 people and is the second-deadliest earthquake in Taiwan's recorded history.
tokens.image_credit: Hsu.shihhung · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sunflower Student Movement
tokens.title: Students occupy the legislature
tokens.description: The Sunflower Student Movement was a 2014 protest in which students and civic groups occupied Taiwan's Legislative Yuan from March 18 to April 10. They opposed the Cross-Strait Service Trade Agreement with China, which the ruling KMT passed without clause-by-clause review.
tokens.image_credit: MrWiki321 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battles of Khalkhin Gol
tokens.title: Zhukov defeats Japan on the steppe
tokens.description: The Battles of Khalkhin Gol were the decisive 1939 engagements of the Soviet-Japanese border conflict, fought on the Mongolia-Manchukuo border. The Soviet offensive under Georgy Zhukov used tanks, aircraft and infantry.
tokens.image_credit: Dōmei Tsushin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Kalka River
tokens.title: Mongols defeat Rus' princes
tokens.description: The Battle of the Kalka River was fought on May 31, 1223 between the Mongol army of Jebe and Subutai and a coalition of Rus' princes with Cumans. It ended in a decisive Mongol victory on the Kalka River in present-day Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine.

tokens.name: Battle of Legnica
tokens.title: Mongols defeat Polish-German force
tokens.description: The Battle of Legnica was fought on 9 April 1241 near Legnica in Silesia between the Mongol Empire and a combined Polish and Moravian force led by Duke Henry II the Pious. The Mongols won, two days before their victory at Mohi.
tokens.image_credit: unknown / (of the reproduction) Wroclaw University Library / T. Zoltowska-Huszcza (sorry for ignoring diacritics) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Kulikovo
tokens.title: Moscow-led army defeats the Golden Horde
tokens.description: The Battle of Kulikovo was fought on 8 September 1380 at Kulikovo Field near the Don River between the forces of Mamai of the Golden Horde and Russian troops led by Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow. Dmitry won and became known as Donskoy after the battle.
tokens.image_credit: Adolphe Yvon · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle on the Ice
tokens.title: Alexander Nevsky on frozen Lake Peipus
tokens.description: The Battle on the Ice, also called the Battle of Lake Peipus, was fought on 5 April 1242 on the frozen lake. Novgorod and Vladimir-Suzdal forces under Prince Alexander Nevsky defeated the Livonian Order and the Bishopric of Dorpat.
tokens.image_credit: Messir · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Stand on the Ugra River
tokens.title: Mongol yoke ends
tokens.description: The Great Stand on the Ugra River was a 1480 standoff on the Ugra River between Ivan III of Moscow and Akhmat Khan of the Great Horde. Akhmat withdrew without a battle, and the event is traditionally seen as the end of the Mongol yoke over Rus'.
tokens.image_credit: Anonymous Russian manuscript illuminators, 1560-1570s Facial Chronicle (Illustrated Chronicle of Ivan the Terrible) (in 10 volumes: pdf, pdf with translation)Public domain image · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Christianization of Kievan Rus'
tokens.title: Prince Vladimir adopts Christianity
tokens.description: The Christianization of Kievan Rus' was the long process by which the Rus' adopted Christianity. The traditional date of the definitive conversion, recorded in the Primary Chronicle, is 988 under Prince Vladimir I of Kiev.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Klavdy Lebedev · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Napoleon's invasion of Russia
tokens.title: Grande Armée crosses the Niemen
tokens.description: The French invasion of Russia was launched by Napoleon in June 1812 to force the Russian Empire to comply with the Continental Blockade. The Grande Armée crossed the Neman at Kaunas on 24 June 1812, and the campaign cost about a million lives.
