tokens.image_credit: Albrecht Adam · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fire of Moscow 1812
tokens.title: City burns as Napoleon occupies it
tokens.description: The Fire of Moscow burned the city from 14 to 18 September 1812, during the French occupation that followed the Battle of Borodino. Most of the city's wooden buildings were destroyed while Napoleon's army was in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: A. Smirnov (Смирнов А.Ф.) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emancipation reform of 1861
tokens.title: Tsar Alexander II frees the serfs
tokens.description: The Emancipation reform of 1861 effectively abolished serfdom across the Russian Empire under Emperor Alexander II. It was the first and most important of the liberal reforms enacted during his reign.
tokens.image_credit: Boris Kustodiev · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Alexander II of Russia
tokens.title: Bomb on the Catherine Canal
tokens.description: Alexander II of Russia was assassinated on 13 March 1881 in Saint Petersburg, while returning to the Winter Palace in a closed carriage. The plot was carried out by members of the revolutionary group Narodnaya Volya.
tokens.image_credit: Interfase · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Murder of the Romanov family
tokens.title: Imperial family shot in Yekaterinburg
tokens.description: The Romanov family and four of their attendants were shot and stabbed by Bolshevik revolutionaries in Yekaterinburg on the night of 16 to 17 July 1918. The bodies were taken to the Koptyaki forest and buried.
tokens.image_credit: Alexei Nametkin (?—1919) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kronstadt rebellion
tokens.title: Sailors rise against the Bolsheviks
tokens.description: The Kronstadt rebellion was a 1921 uprising of Soviet sailors, naval infantry and civilians against the Bolshevik government, centred on the naval fortress of Kronstadt on Kotlin Island. The revolt lasted sixteen days in March 1921 before it was crushed by Red Army troops.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Holodomor
tokens.title: Famine in Soviet Ukraine
tokens.description: The Holodomor was a man-made famine in Soviet Ukraine from 1932 to 1933 that killed millions of Ukrainians. It was part of the wider Soviet famine of 1930 to 1933 that hit the major grain-producing areas of the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: Kaiser matias · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1980 Summer Olympics
tokens.title: Games marked by a US-led boycott
tokens.description: The 1980 Summer Olympics were held from 19 July to 3 August 1980 in Moscow, Soviet Union. They were the first Summer Olympics staged in an Eastern Bloc country and were marked by a boycott led by the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Главархив Москвы · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1991 Soviet coup attempt
tokens.title: Hardliners fail to oust Gorbachev
tokens.description: Between 18 and 22 August 1991 hardliners in the Communist Party of the Soviet Union tried to seize power from Mikhail Gorbachev. The coup collapsed in Moscow within days and accelerated the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: ITAR-TASS · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Russo-Ukrainian war 2022-present
tokens.title: Full-scale invasion begins
tokens.description: On 24 February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, starting the largest conflict in Europe since World War II. It is the current phase of the Russo-Ukrainian war that began in 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Oleksandr Ratushniak · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Euromaidan
tokens.title: Protests on Kyiv's Independence Square
tokens.description: Euromaidan was a wave of demonstrations and civil unrest that began on 21 November 2013 in Kyiv, after President Viktor Yanukovych decided not to sign the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement. The main protests were held on Maidan Nezalezhnosti (Independence Square).
tokens.image_credit: Sasha Maksymenko · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Orange Revolution
tokens.title: Mass protests over a disputed election
tokens.description: The Orange Revolution was a series of protests in Ukraine from late November 2004 to January 2005. They followed the disputed presidential election runoff, and Kyiv was the focal point of the civil resistance.
tokens.image_credit: Serhiy · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2014 Russian annexation of Crimea
tokens.title: Russia annexes the peninsula
tokens.description: In February and March 2014 Russian forces seized the Crimean Peninsula of Ukraine, which was then annexed after a referendum widely regarded as illegitimate. The annexation marked the start of the Russo-Ukrainian war.
tokens.image_credit: Elizabeth Arrott · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Mariupol
tokens.title: Months-long siege of the port city
tokens.description: The siege of Mariupol lasted from 24 February to 20 May 2022, during the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Russian and Donetsk People's Republic forces took control of the southeastern city after Ukrainian troops surrendered at the Azovstal steelworks.
tokens.image_credit: Chad Nagle · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Sevastopol 1854
tokens.title: Crimean War's longest siege
tokens.description: The Siege of Sevastopol lasted from October 1854 to September 1855 during the Crimean War. The allied French, Sardinian, Ottoman and British armies besieged the Russian naval fortress in Crimea.
tokens.image_credit: Valentin Ramirez · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Charge of the Light Brigade
tokens.title: Cavalry charge at Balaclava
tokens.description: The Charge of the Light Brigade was a British light cavalry attack against Russian artillery on 25 October 1854 during the Battle of Balaclava in the Crimean War. The charge caused heavy cavalry casualties after a misunderstood order.
tokens.image_credit: William Simpson (painter, 1823-1899) E. Walker (lithographer, unknown) Published by Goupil & Cie, Paris, and Day & Son, London. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Balaclava
tokens.title: Thin Red Line and a doomed charge
tokens.description: The Battle of Balaclava was fought on 25 October 1854 during the Crimean War, as part of the Siege of Sevastopol. It included the Charge of the Light Brigade against Russian artillery in the Balaclava valley.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Caton Woodville Jr. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apollo 1 fire
tokens.title: Launch rehearsal fire kills three astronauts
tokens.description: Apollo 1 was the first crewed Apollo mission, planned for 1967. A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal at Launch Complex 34 on 27 January 1967 killed astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project
tokens.title: US and Soviet spacecraft dock in orbit
tokens.description: The Apollo-Soyuz Test Project was the first crewed international space mission, a joint US and Soviet docking in orbit in July 1975. The Apollo spacecraft launched from Launch Complex 39 at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alan Shepard's flight
tokens.title: First American in space
tokens.description: Mercury-Redstone 3, also called Freedom 7, flew on 5 May 1961 with astronaut Alan Shepard, the first American in space. It was the first crewed flight of Project Mercury, launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Friendship 7
tokens.title: John Glenn orbits the Earth
tokens.description: Mercury-Atlas 6 on 20 February 1962 carried astronaut John Glenn in the Friendship 7 capsule, the first American crewed orbital flight. The Atlas rocket launched from Launch Complex 14 at Cape Canaveral, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/photographer unknown · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: STS-1
tokens.title: First Space Shuttle flight
tokens.description: STS-1 was the first orbital flight of NASA's Space Shuttle program, with the orbiter Columbia launching on 12 April 1981. The crew of John Young and Robert Crippen landed after 54.5 hours in orbit.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hubble launch
tokens.title: Telescope deployed from Discovery
tokens.description: Space Shuttle Discovery launched mission STS-31 from Kennedy Space Center on 24 April 1990. The crew deployed the Hubble Space Telescope into low Earth orbit.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/IMAX · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mars Pathfinder landing
tokens.title: Sojourner rover rolls onto Mars
tokens.description: Mars Pathfinder was launched from Cape Canaveral Space Launch Complex 17 in December 1996. Its lander reached Mars in July 1997 and carried the Sojourner rover, the first rover to operate on Mars.
tokens.image_credit: Photo credit: NASA/George Shelton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Curiosity landing
tokens.title: Seven minutes of terror at Gale Crater
tokens.description: The Mars Science Laboratory mission launched the Curiosity rover from Cape Canaveral Space Launch Complex 41 on 26 November 2011. Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on Mars on 6 August 2012.

tokens.name: Perseverance landing
tokens.title: Rover touches down in Jezero Crater
tokens.description: The Perseverance rover launched from Cape Canaveral on 30 July 2020 aboard an Atlas V rocket. It landed in Jezero Crater on Mars on 18 February 2021.

tokens.name: Ingenuity first flight
tokens.title: First powered flight on another planet
tokens.description: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered and controlled flight on another planet on 19 April 2021, over Mars. The helicopter had travelled to Mars attached to the Perseverance rover.

tokens.name: Viking 1 landing
tokens.title: First successful Mars lander
tokens.description: Viking 1 was launched from Cape Canaveral on 20 August 1975 on a Titan IIIE rocket. Its lander touched down on Mars on 20 July 1976, the first successful Mars lander.

tokens.name: Voyager 1 launch
tokens.title: Probe now in interstellar space
tokens.description: Voyager 1 was launched by NASA on 5 September 1977 from Cape Canaveral on a Titan IIIE-Centaur rocket. It was launched 16 days after its twin, Voyager 2.

tokens.name: New Horizons Pluto flyby
tokens.title: First close look at Pluto
tokens.description: New Horizons was launched from Cape Canaveral Space Launch Complex 41 on 19 January 2006 on an Atlas V rocket. In July 2015 it became the first spacecraft to make a close flyby of Pluto.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rosetta and Philae comet landing
tokens.title: First landing on a comet
tokens.description: ESA's Rosetta probe, launched from Kourou, released the Philae lander, which touched down on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 12 November 2014. It was the first landing on a comet nucleus.
tokens.image_credit: ESA/Rosetta/NAVCAM, CC BY-SA IGO 3.0 · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: James Webb Space Telescope launch
tokens.title: Launched from Kourou on Ariane 5
tokens.description: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana, on 25 December 2021. It is the largest telescope in space.
tokens.image_credit: Bill Ingalls · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Crew Dragon Demo-2
tokens.title: First crewed commercial orbital launch
tokens.description: Demo-2 was the first crewed test flight of SpaceX's Crew Dragon spacecraft, named Endeavour. It launched from Kennedy Space Center on 30 May 2020 and carried NASA astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken to the International Space Station.
tokens.image_credit: Joel Kowsky · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Starship first integrated flight
tokens.title: Largest rocket ever flown
tokens.description: Starship flight test 1 was the maiden flight of the integrated Starship launch vehicle, lifting off from Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas on 20 April 2023. The prototype was destroyed less than four minutes after liftoff.
tokens.image_credit: Osunpokeh · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First ISS module launch
tokens.title: Zarya begins the station
tokens.description: Zarya, the first module of the International Space Station, was launched on 20 November 1998 on a Proton-K rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. It supplied the station's early power, propulsion and guidance.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skylab launch
tokens.title: First American space station
tokens.description: Skylab, the first United States space station, was launched by NASA in May 1973 on a Saturn V rocket from Kennedy Space Center. It was occupied by three crews between 1973 and 1974.

tokens.name: Explorer 1
tokens.title: First US satellite and Van Allen belts
tokens.description: Explorer 1 was the first satellite launched by the United States, in 1958, as part of the International Geophysical Year. Its instruments detected the Van Allen radiation belts.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ariane 5 flight 501
tokens.title: Rocket self-destructs after a software error
tokens.description: Ariane flight V88, also known as Ariane 5 Flight 501, was the failed maiden flight of the Ariane 5 rocket on 4 June 1996 from Kourou. The rocket was destroyed after launch, and its Cluster payload of four ESA satellites was lost.
tokens.image_credit: Deadpan · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mars Climate Orbiter loss
tokens.title: Units mix-up doomed the probe
tokens.description: NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter was destroyed on 23 September 1999 when it entered the Martian atmosphere too low, after a units mix-up in its navigation data. The probe had been launched from Cape Canaveral on 11 December 1998.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/KSC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hayabusa
tokens.title: Sample-return mission to an asteroid
tokens.description: Hayabusa was a JAXA robotic spacecraft launched on 9 May 2003 from Uchinoura that studied the asteroid 25143 Itokawa and returned a sample of its material to Earth. It rendezvoused with the asteroid in September 2005.
tokens.image_credit: JGarry at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hayabusa2 sample return
tokens.title: Capsule lands in the Australian outback
tokens.description: Hayabusa2 is a JAXA asteroid sample-return mission, launched on 3 December 2014, that rendezvoused with Ryugu in June 2018. Its sample capsule landed at the Woomera Test Range in South Australia in December 2020.

tokens.name: SLIM Moon landing
tokens.title: Japan's precision lunar landing
tokens.description: SLIM, the Smart Lander for Investigating Moon, was a JAXA lunar lander launched from Tanegashima on 6 September 2023. It soft-landed on the Moon on 19 January 2024, making Japan the fifth country to do so.
tokens.image_credit: Hms1103 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chandrayaan-1
tokens.title: India's first lunar probe
tokens.description: Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar probe, launched by ISRO in October 2008 from Sriharikota. It operated until August 2009 with an orbiter and an impactor.

tokens.name: Tianwen-1 Mars landing
tokens.title: Zhurong rover lands on Utopia Planitia
tokens.description: Tianwen-1 was China's first Mars mission, launched in July 2020 from Wenchang. Its Zhurong rover landed on Utopia Planitia in May 2021.

tokens.name: Tiangong core module launch
tokens.title: China's permanent station begins
tokens.description: Tianhe, the core module of China's Tiangong space station, was launched into orbit on 29 April 2021. It was the first launch of the final construction phase of the station.
tokens.image_credit: China News Service · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kosmos 954 crash
tokens.title: Soviet satellite scatters debris over Canada
tokens.description: Kosmos 954, a Soviet reconnaissance satellite with an onboard nuclear reactor, re-entered the atmosphere in 1978 and scattered radioactive debris over northern Canada. Some debris fell into Great Slave Lake next to Fort Resolution, Northwest Territories.

tokens.name: Trinity nuclear test
tokens.title: First nuclear explosion
tokens.description: Trinity was the first detonation of a nuclear weapon, conducted by the United States Army on 16 July 1945 as part of the Manhattan Project. It used an implosion-design plutonium bomb, the same design as the Fat Man bomb.
tokens.image_credit: Berlyn Brixner / Los Alamos National Laboratory · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chicago Pile-1
tokens.title: First self-sustaining nuclear reaction
tokens.description: Chicago Pile-1 was the first artificial nuclear reactor, where Enrico Fermi's team achieved the first human-made self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction on 2 December 1942. It was built under the west stands of Stagg Field at the University of Chicago.
tokens.image_credit: Melvin A. Miller of the Argonne National Laboratory · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castle Bravo
tokens.title: Largest US thermonuclear test
tokens.description: Castle Bravo was the first in a series of high-yield thermonuclear tests by the United States at Bikini Atoll, detonated on 1 March 1954. It remains the most powerful nuclear device ever detonated by the United States, with a yield of 15 megatons.
tokens.image_credit: United States Department of Energy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Crossroads
tokens.title: Bikini Atoll atomic tests
tokens.description: Operation Crossroads was a pair of United States nuclear weapon tests at Bikini Atoll in mid-1946, the first nuclear tests since Trinity. They were conducted to study the effect of nuclear weapons on warships.
tokens.image_credit: United States Department of Defense (either the U.S. Army or the U.S. Navy) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Three Mile Island accident
tokens.title: Partial reactor meltdown in Pennsylvania
tokens.description: The Three Mile Island accident was a partial nuclear meltdown of the Unit 2 reactor on 28 March 1979, releasing radioactive gases and iodine into the environment. The plant stands on the Susquehanna River near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.
tokens.image_credit: Z22 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Windscale fire
tokens.title: Britain's worst nuclear accident
tokens.description: The Windscale fire of 10 October 1957 was the worst nuclear accident in the United Kingdom's history, rated level 5 on the International Nuclear Event Scale. It occurred in Unit 1 of the Windscale site, now Sellafield, in Cumberland, north-west England.

tokens.name: Kyshtym disaster
tokens.title: Secret nuclear accident at Mayak
tokens.description: The Kyshtym disaster was a radioactive contamination accident on 29 September 1957 at the Mayak plutonium plant, near Ozyorsk in Russia. An underground tank of high-level nuclear waste exploded, contaminating thousands of square kilometers of land.

tokens.name: Goiânia accident
tokens.title: Stolen radiation source contaminates a city
tokens.description: The Goiânia accident was a radioactive contamination incident on 13 September 1987, when scavengers opened an abandoned caesium-137 radiotherapy source in Goiânia, Brazil. Four people died and many others were contaminated.
tokens.image_credit: IAEA Imagebank · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piper Alpha disaster
tokens.title: North Sea platform explodes
tokens.description: Piper Alpha was a North Sea oil platform operated by Occidental Petroleum. It exploded and collapsed on 6 July 1988, killing 167 people, including two rescuers.

tokens.name: Exxon Valdez oil spill
tokens.title: Tanker runs aground in Alaska
tokens.description: The Exxon Valdez oil spill was a 1989 disaster in Alaska's Prince William Sound, when the supertanker Exxon Valdez struck Bligh Reef. The tanker spilled more than 10 million US gallons of crude oil.
tokens.image_credit: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amoco Cadiz oil spill
tokens.title: Supertanker wrecks off Brittany
tokens.description: The Amoco Cadiz oil spill followed the grounding of the tanker Amoco Cadiz on Portsall Rocks off Brittany on 16 March 1978. The ship broke up and sank, and NOAA estimates about 220,000 tonnes of oil was spilled, the largest of its kind at the time.
tokens.image_credit: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seveso disaster
tokens.title: Dioxin cloud over Lombardy
tokens.description: The Seveso disaster was an industrial accident on 10 July 1976 at a small chemical plant north of Milan, Italy. It released a dioxin (TCDD) cloud that caused the highest known residential exposure to the chemical.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Minamata disease
tokens.title: Mercury poisoning recognised in Kumamoto
tokens.description: Minamata disease is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning, with symptoms such as ataxia, numbness and loss of peripheral vision. It is named after the city of Minamata in Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan.

tokens.name: Halifax Explosion
tokens.title: Munitions ship blows up in the harbour
tokens.description: The Halifax Explosion occurred on 6 December 1917, when the cargo ship Mont-Blanc, loaded with explosives, collided with the Imo in Halifax harbour and detonated. At least 1,782 people were killed.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Molasses Flood
tokens.title: Wave of molasses sweeps through Boston
tokens.description: The Great Molasses Flood was a disaster on 15 January 1919 in Boston's North End, when a storage tank burst and a wave of molasses swept through the streets. It killed 21 people and injured about 150.
tokens.image_credit: BPL · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire
tokens.title: Factory fire leads to safety reform
tokens.description: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire broke out on 25 March 1911 in the Asch Building in Manhattan's Greenwich Village. It killed 146 garment workers and was the deadliest industrial disaster in New York City's history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Johnstown Flood
tokens.title: Dam failure destroys a Pennsylvania town
tokens.description: The Johnstown Flood of 31 May 1889 followed the failure of the South Fork Dam upstream of Johnstown, Pennsylvania. The flood killed 2,208 people.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tay Bridge disaster
tokens.title: Bridge collapses under a train
tokens.description: The Tay Bridge disaster of 28 December 1879 saw the first Tay Rail Bridge collapse in a storm as a passenger train crossed it, killing everyone aboard. The bridge was designed by Sir Thomas Bouch.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse
tokens.title: "Galloping Gertie" twists apart
tokens.description: The 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge opened on 1 July 1940 and collapsed into Puget Sound on 7 November 1940. Its collapse has drawn the attention of engineers, physicists and mathematicians since.
tokens.image_credit: University of Washington Libraries Digital Collections · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tenerife airport disaster
tokens.title: Deadliest accident in aviation history
tokens.description: On 27 March 1977 two Boeing 747 jets collided on the runway at Los Rodeos Airport, Tenerife, in dense fog. The disaster killed 583 people, the third deadliest accident in aviation history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown; uploaded to commons by User:Mr.Nostalgic in light of a donation by the Dutch National Archives · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Japan Air Lines Flight 123
tokens.title: Deadliest single-aircraft accident
tokens.description: Japan Air Lines Flight 123, a domestic Boeing 747 service from Tokyo to Osaka, suffered explosive decompression on 12 August 1985. After 32 minutes of minimal control, it crashed on Mount Takamagahara, Japan.
tokens.image_credit: nattou · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: US Airways Flight 1549
tokens.title: Flight 1549 ditches in the river
tokens.description: US Airways Flight 1549 ditched in the Hudson River near Midtown Manhattan on 15 January 2009 after a bird strike caused a double engine failure. The Airbus A320 landed on the water with no significant damage to the aircraft.
tokens.image_credit: Greg L · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gimli Glider
tokens.title: Airliner glides to a safe landing
tokens.description: On 23 July 1983 Air Canada Flight 143, a Boeing 767 flying from Montreal to Edmonton, ran out of fuel midway through the flight. The airliner glided to a safe landing at Gimli, Manitoba.
tokens.image_credit: FAA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Breaking the sound barrier
tokens.title: Chuck Yeager flies faster than sound
tokens.description: On 14 October 1947 Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 rocket-powered research aircraft faster than the speed of sound over the Mojave Desert. The flight was made from Muroc, now Edwards Air Force Base.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcock and Brown transatlantic flight
tokens.title: First nonstop crossing of the Atlantic
tokens.description: John Alcock and Arthur Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919, in a Vickers Vimy bomber. They flew from St. John's, Newfoundland, to Clifden, County Galway, Ireland.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blériot crosses the Channel
tokens.title: First flight across the English Channel
tokens.description: On 25 July 1909 Louis Blériot became the first to fly a heavier-than-air aircraft across the English Channel, in a Blériot XI monoplane. It is one of the most famous feats of the pioneer era of aviation.
tokens.image_credit: Bain News Service, publisher · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 14-bis flight
tokens.title: Santos-Dumont's powered flight in Paris
tokens.description: In 1906 Alberto Santos-Dumont made a manned powered flight near Paris in his canard-style biplane, the 14-bis. It was the first such flight publicly witnessed by a crowd and filmed.
tokens.image_credit: Jules Beau · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Voyager nonstop round-the-world flight
tokens.title: Unrefuelled circumnavigation by air
tokens.description: Voyager, a Burt Rutan designed aircraft piloted by Dick Rutan and Jeana Yeager, became the first to fly around the world without stopping or refueling. It took off from Edwards Air Force Base in California in December 1986.
tokens.image_credit: NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center / NASA/Thomas Harrop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Solar Impulse round-the-world flight
tokens.title: Sun-powered flight completes the circuit
tokens.description: The Solar Impulse project, led by André Borschberg and Bertrand Piccard, aimed to make the first circumnavigation of the Earth by a piloted fixed-wing aircraft using only solar power. The flight used the Solar Impulse 2 aircraft.
tokens.image_credit: Anthony Quintano · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Breitling Orbiter 3
tokens.title: First nonstop balloon circumnavigation
tokens.description: Breitling Orbiter 3, piloted by Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones, made the first nonstop flight around the world by balloon in March 1999. The Rozière balloon was built by Cameron Balloons in Bristol.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. BetacommandBot assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red Bull Stratos
tokens.title: Felix Baumgartner free-falls from the stratosphere
tokens.description: Red Bull Stratos was a high-altitude skydiving project in which Felix Baumgartner flew about 39 km into the stratosphere over New Mexico on 14 October 2012. He then free fell back to Earth in a pressure suit.
tokens.image_credit: Balon Greyjoy · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flight 19
tokens.title: Navy bombers vanish off Florida
tokens.description: Flight 19 was a group of five US Navy Grumman TBF Avenger torpedo bombers that vanished over the Bermuda Triangle on 5 December 1945. The training flight had departed from Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
tokens.image_credit: Anynobody · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mary Celeste found adrift
tokens.title: Ship discovered without its crew
tokens.description: The Canadian-built brigantine Mary Celeste was found adrift and deserted in the Atlantic off the Azores on 4 December 1872, with no one aboard. Its crew's fate remains unexplained.

tokens.name: Surgeon's Photograph
tokens.title: Famous Loch Ness hoax picture
tokens.description: The Surgeon's Photograph, published by the Daily Mail in April 1934, purported to show the Loch Ness Monster. It was shown to be an elaborate hoax in the 1990s.
tokens.image_credit: M. A. Wetherell · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piltdown Man hoax
tokens.title: Fake fossil fooled scientists for decades
tokens.description: Piltdown Man was a fraudulent early human fossil, made of bone fragments found near Piltdown in Sussex and announced in 1912. The hoax was exposed in 1953, and a 2016 review attributed it to Charles Dawson.
tokens.image_credit: James Howard McGregor · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Discovery of Lucy
tokens.title: Fossil hominin found in Afar
tokens.description: Lucy, a partial skeleton of the hominin Australopithecus afarensis about 3.2 million years old, was found in 1974 at Hadar in the Afar Triangle of Ethiopia. Donald Johanson led the discovery.
tokens.image_credit: Radosław Botev · CC BY 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taung Child discovery
tokens.title: First Australopithecus fossil
tokens.description: The Taung Child, the fossilised skull of a young Australopithecus africanus, was discovered at Taung in South Africa in 1924. Raymond Dart described it as a new species in 1925.
tokens.image_credit: Didier Descouens · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls
tokens.title: Shepherd finds scrolls at Qumran
tokens.description: The Dead Sea Scrolls, ancient Jewish biblical manuscripts dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE, were discovered between 1946 and 1956 in the Qumran Caves. The caves lie near the northern shore of the Dead Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Discovery of Ötzi the Iceman
tokens.title: 5,300-year-old mummy found in the Alps
tokens.description: Ötzi, the natural mummy of a man who lived in the 4th millennium BC, was discovered on 19 September 1991 in the Ötztal Alps at the Austria-Italy border. He is Europe's oldest known natural human mummy.
tokens.image_credit: Alex Lozupone · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sutton Hoo ship burial found
tokens.title: Anglo-Saxon treasure uncovered
tokens.description: The Sutton Hoo ship burial, rich in Anglo-Saxon treasure, was uncovered in 1938 near Woodbridge in Suffolk. The site also holds an Anglo-Saxon cemetery dating from the 6th and 7th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Alex Healing · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Raising of the Mary Rose
tokens.title: Tudor warship lifted from the Solent
tokens.description: The Mary Rose was a Tudor carrack of Henry VIII's navy that sank off Spithead in 1545. Her wreck was raised from the Solent on 11 October 1982.

tokens.name: Sinking of the Vasa
tokens.title: Warship sinks within minutes of launching
tokens.description: The Swedish warship Vasa sank about 1,300 m into her maiden voyage in Stockholm harbour on 10 August 1628. The ship was later located, raised and is displayed in the Vasa Museum.
tokens.image_credit: JavierKohen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of the Bismarck
tokens.title: Pursuit ends in the Atlantic
tokens.description: The German battleship Bismarck was sunk by the Royal Navy in the North Atlantic on 27 May 1941, while trying to reach the port of Brest after sinking HMS Hood.

tokens.name: Sinking of the Wilhelm Gustloff
tokens.title: Deadliest maritime disaster in history
tokens.description: The transport MV Wilhelm Gustloff was torpedoed by the Soviet submarine S-13 in the Baltic Sea on 30 January 1945. One estimate of 9,343 deaths makes it the deadliest maritime disaster in modern history.

tokens.name: Sinking of the Edmund Fitzgerald
tokens.title: Freighter lost in a Lake Superior storm
tokens.description: The freighter SS Edmund Fitzgerald sank in a storm on Lake Superior on 10 November 1975, with the loss of all 29 crew. A memorial to the wreck stands at Whitefish Point, Michigan.
tokens.image_credit: Rklawton · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of the Andrea Doria
tokens.title: Liners collide off Nantucket
tokens.description: The Italian liner SS Andrea Doria sank on 26 July 1956 after a collision with the liner Stockholm off Nantucket. Of 1,706 passengers and crew, 1,660 were rescued.
tokens.image_credit: Harry A. Trask · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Costa Concordia disaster
tokens.title: Cruise ship capsizes off Giglio
tokens.description: The cruise ship Costa Concordia struck a rock off Isola del Giglio, Italy, on 13 January 2012 and partly sank. Of the 32 people who died, 27 were passengers and five were crew.
tokens.image_credit: Rvongher · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: MV Doña Paz disaster
tokens.title: Ferry collision in the Philippines
tokens.description: The passenger ferry Doña Paz sank after colliding with the oil tanker MT Vector in the Tablas Strait on 20 December 1987. It is counted among the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters, with an estimated death toll above 4,000.
tokens.image_credit: lindsaybridge · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of USS Indianapolis
tokens.title: Cruiser sunk after delivering the atomic bomb parts
tokens.description: The heavy cruiser USS Indianapolis was torpedoed by the Japanese submarine I-58 on 30 July 1945, after delivering parts for the Little Boy atomic bomb, and sank in about 12 minutes. The survivors' ordeal in the water over the following days is one of the worst episodes in US naval history.

tokens.name: Dambusters raid
tokens.title: Bouncing bombs breach the Möhne Dam
tokens.description: Operation Chastise, the Dambusters raid, was flown by No. 617 Squadron RAF on the night of 16/17 May 1943 to breach German dams with bouncing bombs. The Möhne and Edersee dams were breached, flooding the Ruhr valley and villages in the Eder valley.
tokens.image_credit: Flying Officer Jerry Fray RAF · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Great Escape
tokens.title: Seventy-six prisoners break out of Stalag Luft III
tokens.description: In March 1944, 76 Allied prisoners escaped from Stalag Luft III, a Luftwaffe prisoner-of-war camp near Sagan, now Żagań, Poland. Of the 73 recaptured, 50 were executed.
tokens.image_credit: CSvBibra · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 20 July plot
tokens.title: Bomb at Hitler's Wolf's Lair
tokens.description: The 20 July plot was a failed attempt on 20 July 1944 to assassinate Adolf Hitler and overthrow the Nazi government, led by German resistance officers around Claus von Stauffenberg. The bomb exploded at Hitler's Wolf's Lair headquarters in East Prussia.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Bulge
tokens.title: Last major German offensive in the west
tokens.description: The Battle of the Bulge was a German offensive on the Western Front, fought through the Ardennes from 16 December 1944 to 25 January 1945. It aimed to split the Allied armies and stop the Allied use of the port of Antwerp.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Army · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Market Garden
tokens.title: A bridge too far at Arnhem
tokens.description: Operation Market Garden was an Allied airborne and armoured operation in the German-occupied Netherlands from 17 to 25 September 1944. It aimed to seize nine bridges over the Lower Rhine, including the bridge at Arnhem, to open a route into northern Germany.
tokens.image_credit: This file is a work of a U.S. Army soldier or employee, taken or made as part of that person's official duties. As a work of the U.S. federal government, it is in the public domain in the United State · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Monte Cassino
tokens.title: Four assaults on the abbey ridge
tokens.description: The Battle of Monte Cassino was a series of four Allied assaults on the German defences in central Italy in 1944. The aim was to break the Winter Line and advance towards Rome.
tokens.image_credit: War Office official photographer, Tanner (Capt) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
tokens.title: Montgomery turns the tide in the desert
tokens.description: The Second Battle of El Alamein, fought from 23 October to 4 November 1942, was a turning point of the Western Desert campaign. Montgomery's Eighth Army broke the Axis lines and pushed Rommel back.
tokens.image_credit: Len Chetwyn · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Tobruk
tokens.title: Australian garrison holds out
tokens.description: The Siege of Tobruk lasted from 10 April to 27 November 1941 during the Western Desert campaign. An Allied garrison, mostly the 9th Australian Division, held the Libyan port against German and Italian forces.
tokens.image_credit: British Army · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Torch
tokens.title: Allied landings in North Africa
tokens.description: Operation Torch, from 8 to 16 November 1942, was the Allied invasion of French North Africa during the Second World War. Landings at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers opened the campaign against the Axis in North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Hudson, F A (Lt), Royal Navy official photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Allied invasion of Sicily
tokens.title: Operation Husky opens the Italian campaign
tokens.description: The Allied invasion of Sicily, also called Operation Husky, began in July 1943 and took the Italian island from the Axis forces. It paved the way for the Allied invasion of mainland Italy.
tokens.image_credit: No 2 Army Film & Photographic Unit, Stubbs (Sgt) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Liberation of Paris
tokens.title: Free French enter the capital
tokens.description: The Liberation of Paris was a battle of the Second World War fought from 19 to 25 August 1944. The German garrison surrendered the French capital on 25 August 1944, ending the occupation.
tokens.image_credit: Jack Downey, U.S. Office of War Information · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Doolittle Raid
tokens.title: Carrier-launched bombers strike Tokyo
tokens.description: The Doolittle Raid was an air raid by United States Army Air Forces bombers on Tokyo and other places in Honshu on 18 April 1942. It was the first American air attack on the Japanese home islands in the Second World War.
tokens.image_credit: USAAF · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Coral Sea
tokens.title: First carrier battle without ships sighting
tokens.description: The Battle of the Coral Sea, fought in May 1942, was the first naval battle in which aircraft carriers fought each other. It stopped the Japanese attempt to take Port Moresby by sea.

tokens.name: Guadalcanal campaign
tokens.title: Marines land in the Solomon Islands
tokens.description: The Guadalcanal campaign, fought from 7 August 1942 to 9 February 1943, was the first major Allied land offensive against Japan in the Pacific War. It centred on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Tarawa
tokens.title: Costly amphibious assault
tokens.description: The Battle of Tarawa was fought from 20 to 23 November 1943 between the United States and Japan on Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands. It ended in a decisive American victory, with most of the fighting on the island of Betio.
tokens.image_credit: USMC Archives from Quantico, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Surrender of Japan
tokens.title: Signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay
tokens.description: The surrender of Japan ending the Second World War was signed on 2 September 1945 aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay. The instrument of surrender was announced by Emperor Hirohito on 15 August 1945.
tokens.image_credit: Army Signal Corps photographer LT. Stephen E. Korpanty; restored by Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Victory in Europe Day
tokens.title: German surrender takes effect
tokens.description: Victory in Europe Day marks the Allied acceptance of Nazi Germany's unconditional surrender on 8 May 1945, ending all German military operations. Russia and some other countries celebrate it on 9 May.
tokens.image_credit: War Office official photographer, Major W. G. Horton · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: German Instrument of Surrender
tokens.title: Signed at Reims
tokens.description: The German Instrument of Surrender was signed at 22:43 CET on 8 May 1945 and took effect at 23:01 CET the same day, ending World War II in Europe. It was signed in Berlin, after a separate surrender at Reims on 7 May was not recognized by the Soviet Union.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Potsdam Conference
tokens.title: Allied leaders shape postwar Europe
tokens.description: The Potsdam Conference was held at Potsdam in the Soviet occupation zone from 17 July to 2 August 1945. The Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and the United States met there to plan the postwar peace.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown official photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tehran Conference
tokens.title: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet
tokens.description: The Tehran Conference was held from 28 November to 1 December 1943 at the Soviet embassy in Tehran. Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill met there, the first wartime conference of the Big Three.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Signal Corps photo. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casablanca Conference
tokens.title: Allies demand unconditional surrender
tokens.description: The Casablanca Conference was held from 14 to 24 January 1943 in Casablanca, French Morocco. Roosevelt and Churchill set Allied strategy for the next phase of the war and demanded the unconditional surrender of the Axis powers.
tokens.image_credit: National Museum of the U.S. Navy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atlantic Charter
tokens.title: Roosevelt and Churchill at sea off Newfoundland
tokens.description: The Atlantic Charter was a joint statement by Roosevelt and Churchill issued on 14 August 1941, setting out postwar goals months before the United States entered the war. It was agreed at the Atlantic Conference in Placentia Bay, off Newfoundland.
tokens.image_credit: Leslie Cornish Priest · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bretton Woods Conference
tokens.title: IMF and World Bank are conceived
tokens.description: The 1944 United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference of 730 delegates from 44 allied nations met at the Mount Washington Hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire. It set up the IMF and the World Bank.
tokens.image_credit: Barry Livingstone · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United Nations Conference on International Organization
tokens.title: Charter drafted in San Francisco
tokens.description: The United Nations Conference on International Organization met in San Francisco from 25 April to 26 June 1945. Delegates from 50 Allied nations drafted and signed the Charter of the United Nations there.
tokens.image_credit: Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Rome
tokens.title: European Economic Community created
tokens.description: The Treaty of Rome was signed on 25 March 1957 by six European states and created the European Economic Community. It was signed in the Hall of the Horatii and Curiatii on the Capitoline Hill.
tokens.image_credit: Zinneke at lb.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maastricht Treaty
tokens.title: European Union founded
tokens.description: The Maastricht Treaty, or Treaty on European Union, was signed in Maastricht on 7 February 1992. It is the foundation treaty of the European Union.
tokens.image_credit: Dozura · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Schengen Agreement
tokens.title: Border-free travel begins
tokens.description: The Schengen Agreement was signed on 14 June 1985 near the town of Schengen in Luxembourg. It led to the Schengen Area, where internal border checks have largely been abolished.
tokens.image_credit: Zinneke · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
tokens.title: Spain and Portugal divide the world
tokens.description: The Treaty of Tordesillas was signed in Tordesillas, Spain, on 7 June 1494. It divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and the Crown of Castile along a meridian west of Cape Verde.
tokens.image_credit: Original: Biblioteca Nacional de Lisboa Photo: User:Joserebelo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huygens probe
tokens.title: First landing in the outer Solar System
tokens.description: Huygens was an ESA-built probe carried by the Cassini orbiter and launched from Cape Canaveral in 1997. It landed on Titan, Saturn's moon, on 14 January 2005, the first landing in the outer Solar System.
tokens.image_credit: David Monniaux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Rumble in the Jungle
tokens.title: Ali versus Foreman in Kinshasa
tokens.description: The Rumble in the Jungle was the heavyweight title fight between George Foreman and Muhammad Ali on 30 October 1974. It was held at the 20th of May Stadium in Kinshasa, Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Drew · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fight of the Century
tokens.title: Ali versus Frazier at Madison Square Garden
tokens.description: The Fight of the Century was a heavyweight boxing match between Joe Frazier and Muhammad Ali on 8 March 1971 at Madison Square Garden in New York City. It is widely considered the most publicised boxing match in history.
tokens.image_credit: United Press International · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1968 Olympics Black Power salute
tokens.title: Smith and Carlos on the podium
tokens.description: On 16 October 1968 Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black-gloved fists on the podium during the US anthem at the Mexico City Olympics. The protest followed the medal ceremony in the Olympic Stadium, Mexico City.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Angelo Cozzi (Mondadori Publishers) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nadia Comăneci's perfect ten
tokens.title: First perfect score in Olympic gymnastics
tokens.description: On 18 July 1976 Nadia Comaneci, aged 14, was awarded the first perfect score of 10.0 in Olympic gymnastics at the Montreal Forum. She went on to win five Olympic gold medals.

tokens.name: Montreal 1976 Olympics
tokens.title: Games with a perfect ten
tokens.description: The 1976 Summer Olympics were held from 17 July to 1 August 1976 in Montreal, Canada, the only Summer Olympic Games held in Canada. The Olympic Stadium, the main venue, was built for the Games.
tokens.image_credit: Bobjagendorf (talk · contribs) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Barcelona 1992 Olympics
tokens.title: Archer lights the cauldron
tokens.description: An archer lit the Olympic cauldron at the opening of the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona. The Games were held from 25 July to 9 August 1992.
tokens.image_credit: Karsten Knöfler · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atlanta 1996 Olympics
tokens.title: Centennial Games
tokens.description: The 1996 Summer Olympics were held from 19 July to 4 August 1996 in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. They marked the 100th anniversary of the first modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896.
tokens.image_credit: ViennaUK · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Centennial Olympic Park bombing
tokens.title: Bomb during the Atlanta Games
tokens.description: A pipe bomb exploded in Centennial Olympic Park in Atlanta on 27 July 1996, during the Summer Olympics. One person was killed directly and 111 were injured, and another person later died of a heart attack.
tokens.image_credit: Don Ramey Logan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Athens 2004 Olympics
tokens.title: Olympics return home to Greece
tokens.description: The 2004 Summer Olympics were held from 13 to 29 August 2004 in Athens, Greece. They marked the return of the Games to Athens, the birthplace of the modern Olympics, which had last been hosted in the city in 1896.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Athens 1896 Olympics
tokens.title: First modern Olympic Games
tokens.description: The 1896 Summer Olympics were the first modern Olympic Games, held in Athens, Greece, from 6 to 15 April 1896. Fourteen nations and 241 athletes took part.
tokens.image_credit: Docpix · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Placid 1980 Olympics
tokens.title: Home of the Miracle on Ice
tokens.description: The 1980 Winter Olympics were held from 13 to 24 February 1980 in Lake Placid, New York, United States. It was the second Winter Games hosted by the village, after 1932.
tokens.image_credit: Aaron danielg at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lillehammer 1994 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Games in snow-clad Norway
tokens.description: The 1994 Winter Olympics, also known as Lillehammer '94, were held from 12 to 27 February 1994 in and around Lillehammer, Norway. The Games were hosted in Norway's Lillehammer region.
tokens.image_credit: Tokle · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nagano 1998 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Winter Games in Japan
tokens.description: The 1998 Winter Olympics, also known as Nagano 1998, were held from 7 to 22 February 1998, mainly in Nagano Prefecture, Japan. Some events took place in nearby mountain communities such as Hakuba and Karuizawa.

tokens.name: Sarajevo 1984 Winter Olympics
tokens.title: Torvill and Dean score perfect marks
tokens.description: The 1984 Winter Olympics, known as Sarajevo '84, were held from 8 to 19 February 1984 in Sarajevo, Yugoslavia. They were the first Winter Olympics held in a Slavic language-speaking country.
tokens.image_credit: Post of Soviet Union · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paris 2024 Olympics
tokens.title: Opening ceremony on the Seine
tokens.description: The 2024 Summer Olympics, branded Paris 2024, were held in France from 26 July to 11 August 2024. Paris was the host city, with events in 16 other cities in metropolitan France.
tokens.image_credit: DarDarCH · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: Uruguay hosts and wins
tokens.description: The 1930 FIFA World Cup was the first FIFA World Cup, held in Uruguay from 13 to 30 July 1930. FIFA selected Uruguay as the host nation.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Italia 90
tokens.title: West Germany wins in Rome
tokens.description: The 1990 FIFA World Cup, known as Italia 90, was the 14th FIFA World Cup. It was held in Italy from 8 June to 8 July 1990.

tokens.name: 1994 FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: Brazil win on penalties at the Rose Bowl
tokens.description: The 1994 FIFA World Cup was the 15th men's World Cup, hosted by the United States from June 17 to July 17, 1994. Brazil beat Italy on penalties in the final at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
tokens.image_credit: Pyro Spectaculars by Souza · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1998 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: France beat Brazil at Stade de France
tokens.description: France beat Brazil 3-0 in the final of the 1998 FIFA World Cup on 12 July 1998 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, near Paris. It was France's first World Cup title.
tokens.image_credit: Archives nationales · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2006 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: Italy beat France on penalties
tokens.description: Italy beat France 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the final of the 2006 FIFA World Cup on 9 July 2006 at the Olympiastadion in Berlin. Zidane was sent off in extra time.
tokens.image_credit: David Ruddell · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2022 FIFA World Cup final
tokens.title: Argentina beat France on penalties
tokens.description: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the final of the 2022 FIFA World Cup on 18 December 2022 at Lusail Stadium in Qatar. It was watched by a record audience of about 1.5 billion people.
tokens.image_credit: Sebas · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup final
tokens.title: US wins on penalties before 90,000
tokens.description: The United States beat China 5-4 on penalties after a 0-0 draw in the final of the 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup on 10 July 1999. The match was played at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California.
tokens.image_credit: Ted Eytan · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: UEFA Euro 2004 final
tokens.title: Underdogs beat hosts Portugal
tokens.description: Greece beat hosts Portugal 1-0 in the final of UEFA Euro 2004 on 4 July 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon. It was Greece's first major international tournament title.
tokens.image_credit: Jarrett Campbell · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2005 UEFA Champions League final
tokens.title: Liverpool come back from 3-0
tokens.description: Liverpool beat Milan 3-2 on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the 2005 UEFA Champions League final on 25 May 2005 at the Ataturk Olympic Stadium in Istanbul. Milan led 3-0 at half-time.
tokens.image_credit: Валерий Дед · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1999 UEFA Champions League final
tokens.title: Manchester United score twice in stoppage time
tokens.description: Manchester United beat Bayern Munich 2-1 in the 1999 UEFA Champions League final on 26 May 1999 at Camp Nou in Barcelona. Both United goals came in injury time.
tokens.image_credit: Photo by Seán Murray Cropped and retouched by Danyele · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matthews Final
tokens.title: Blackpool beat Bolton 4-3
tokens.description: The 1953 FA Cup final was played at Wembley Stadium, where Blackpool beat Bolton Wanderers 4-3. The match is known as the Matthews Final after the performance of winger Stanley Matthews.
tokens.image_credit: User:Gary Watson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Match of the Century
tokens.title: Mighty Magyars win at Wembley
tokens.description: The Match of the Century was a football match played at Wembley Stadium on 25 November 1953, when Hungary beat England 6-3. The result led England to review its training and tactics.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: 1958 FIFA World Cup
tokens.title: Seventeen-year-old Pelé stars
tokens.description: The 1958 FIFA World Cup was the sixth FIFA World Cup, held in Sweden from 8 to 29 June 1958. Brazil won the tournament, where 17-year-old Pele was one of the stars.
tokens.image_credit: Scanpix · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 Wimbledon Championships Men's singles final
tokens.title: Nadal beats Federer in near darkness
tokens.description: Rafael Nadal beat Roger Federer 6-4, 6-4, 6-7, 6-7, 9-7 in the men's singles final of the 2008 Wimbledon Championships. The match lasted 4 hours and 48 minutes.
tokens.image_credit: David Underdown · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Sexes
tokens.title: Billie Jean King defeats Bobby Riggs
tokens.description: The Battle of the Sexes was a 1973 tennis match at the Houston Astrodome, where Billie Jean King beat Bobby Riggs in three sets. The match was watched by an estimated fifty million people in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Associated Press, photographer uncredited · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isner-Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
tokens.title: Longest tennis match, 11 hours 5 minutes
tokens.description: John Isner beat Nicolas Mahut 6-4, 3-6, 6-7, 7-6, 70-68 in a first-round match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships. At 11 hours and 5 minutes over three days, it was the longest tennis match in professional history.
tokens.image_credit: Jonotennis · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2012 Australian Open Men's singles final
tokens.title: Nearly six-hour Djokovic-Nadal epic
tokens.description: Novak Djokovic beat Rafael Nadal 5-7, 6-4, 6-2, 6-7, 7-5 in the men's singles final of the 2012 Australian Open at Melbourne Park. At 5 hours 53 minutes, it was the longest Australian Open match.
tokens.image_credit: Rob Keating from Canberra, Australia, Australia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Super Bowl III
tokens.title: Joe Namath guarantees a Jets win
tokens.description: Super Bowl III was the American football championship game of 12 January 1969, played at the Miami Orange Bowl. The New York Jets beat the Baltimore Colts 16-7 in one of the greatest upsets in sports history.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Haaron755 at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Super Bowl I
tokens.title: First AFL-NFL championship game
tokens.description: The first AFL and NFL championship game, played on January 15, 1967, at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The Green Bay Packers beat the Kansas City Chiefs 35 to 10.
tokens.image_credit: Jimberg13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Immaculate Reception
tokens.title: Franco Harris's miracle catch
tokens.description: A touchdown play in the 1972 AFC divisional playoff game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Oakland Raiders at Three Rivers Stadium. Franco Harris caught a deflected pass with the Steelers trailing 7 to 6.
tokens.image_credit: dbking · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Catch
tokens.title: Dwight Clark and the 49ers beat Dallas
tokens.description: The game-winning touchdown reception by Dwight Clark from a Joe Montana pass in the 1981 NFC Championship Game. The San Francisco 49ers beat the Dallas Cowboys 28 to 27 at Candlestick Park.
tokens.image_credit: User Fds527 on en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shot Heard 'Round the World
tokens.title: Bobby Thomson's pennant-winning home run
tokens.description: Bobby Thomson's ninth-inning three-run home run that won the 1951 National League pennant for the New York Giants over the Brooklyn Dodgers. It was hit on October 3, 1951, at the Polo Grounds in New York City.

tokens.name: Babe Ruth's called shot
tokens.title: Legendary home run at Wrigley Field
tokens.description: A home run hit by Babe Ruth of the New York Yankees against the Chicago Cubs in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series. It was hit on October 1, 1932, at Wrigley Field in Chicago.

tokens.name: Don Larsen's perfect game
tokens.title: Only perfect game in a World Series
tokens.description: On October 8, 1956, Don Larsen of the New York Yankees pitched a perfect game against the Brooklyn Dodgers in Game 5 of the World Series. It was played at Yankee Stadium in New York City.

tokens.name: Jackie Robinson breaks the colour barrier
tokens.title: First Black player in the modern majors
tokens.description: Jackie Robinson started at first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947, becoming the first African American to play in the modern Major League Baseball era. The debut took place at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn.

tokens.name: Black Sox Scandal
tokens.title: 1919 World Series fixed
tokens.description: A game-fixing scandal in which eight Chicago White Sox players were accused of deliberately losing the 1919 World Series to the Cincinnati Reds for gambling payments. It led to Kenesaw Mountain Landis becoming the first commissioner of baseball.

tokens.name: Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game
tokens.title: Highest NBA single-game score
tokens.description: On March 2, 1962, Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169 to 147 win over the New York Knicks at Hershey Sports Arena, Pennsylvania. It remains the NBA single-game scoring record.
tokens.image_credit: Paul Vathis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dream Team at Barcelona
tokens.title: NBA stars debut at the Olympics
tokens.description: The United States men's basketball team, the first American Olympic team with active NBA players, won the gold medal at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona. The team won every game by an average of 44 points.
tokens.image_credit: Ken Hackman, U.S. Air Force · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malice at the Palace
tokens.title: Brawl in Auburn Hills
tokens.description: Malice at the Palace was a brawl between players and fans during an NBA game between the Indiana Pacers and the Detroit Pistons on November 19, 2004, at the Palace of Auburn Hills, Michigan. The AP called it the most infamous brawl in NBA history.
tokens.image_credit: Kevin Ward from Eastpointe, U.S. · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1983 Cricket World Cup final
tokens.title: India stuns the West Indies at Lord's
tokens.description: India defeated the West Indies in the final of the 1983 Cricket World Cup at Lord's, London, on 25 June 1983. It was India's first World Cup title and the West Indies' third consecutive final.
tokens.aliases: 2019 Cricket World Cup final, 1975 Cricket World Cup final

tokens.name: 2011 Cricket World Cup final
tokens.title: India win in Mumbai
tokens.description: India beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in the final of the 2011 Cricket World Cup, played at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on 2 April 2011. It was India's second World Cup title and the first won by a host nation on home soil.
tokens.image_credit: G patkar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bodyline series
tokens.title: England's controversial fast leg theory
tokens.description: Bodyline was the fast leg theory bowling tactic England used in the 1932-33 Ashes tour of Australia to counter Don Bradman. The series caused a major dispute between the two cricket boards.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tied Test
tokens.title: Australia and West Indies finish level
tokens.description: A Tied Test is a Test cricket match finishing with scores level. The first was played at the Gabba in Brisbane from 9 to 14 December 1960 between Australia and the West Indies, and the second in 1986.

tokens.name: The Ashes
tokens.title: Australia beats England at The Oval
tokens.description: The Ashes is a Test cricket series played between England and Australia. The name began with a satirical obituary after Australia's 1882 win at The Oval, its first Test victory on English soil.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: danielgreef/Dan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1903 Tour de France
tokens.title: Maurice Garin wins the inaugural race
tokens.description: The 1903 Tour de France was the first cycling race set up and sponsored by the newspaper L'Auto. It ran from 1 to 19 July in six stages over 2,428 km and was won by Maurice Garin.
tokens.image_credit: Jules Beau · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boston Marathon bombing
tokens.title: Explosions at the finish line
tokens.description: The Boston Marathon bombing was a terrorist attack during the 117th Boston Marathon on 15 April 2013. Two homemade pressure cooker bombs exploded near the finish line in central Boston.
tokens.image_credit: Aaron Tang · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: INEOS 1:59 Challenge
tokens.title: Kipchoge breaks two hours for the marathon
tokens.description: The INEOS 1:59 Challenge on 12 October 2019 was an attempt by Eliud Kipchoge to run a marathon under two hours. He finished in 1:59:40.2 in Vienna, Austria.

tokens.name: Usain Bolt's 9.58 in Berlin
tokens.title: World record 100 m in Berlin
tokens.description: The men's 100 metres final at the 2009 World Championships in Athletics was held at the Olympic Stadium in Berlin on 16 August 2009. Usain Bolt won in a world record 9.58 seconds, ahead of Tyson Gay.
tokens.image_credit: , attribution: Erik van Leeuwen (bron: Wikipedia). · GFDL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bolt's 2008 Olympic 100 m
tokens.title: 9.69 at the Bird's Nest
tokens.description: The men's 100 metres at the 2008 Summer Olympics was held at the Beijing National Stadium on 15 and 16 August 2008. Usain Bolt won the gold medal in a world record 9.69 seconds.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Giles · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Concert for Bangladesh
tokens.title: First major benefit rock concert
tokens.description: The Concert for Bangladesh was a pair of benefit concerts organised by George Harrison and Ravi Shankar at Madison Square Garden in New York City on 1 August 1971. They raised funds for refugees from East Pakistan.

tokens.name: The Beatles' rooftop concert
tokens.title: Final public performance on Savile Row
tokens.description: On 30 January 1969 the Beatles gave their final public performance, a 42-minute rooftop concert on the Apple Corps headquarters at 3 Savile Row, London. Billy Preston joined them before police ended the set.
tokens.image_credit: Misterweiss at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Beatles at Shea Stadium
tokens.title: First major stadium rock concert
tokens.description: The Beatles played a concert at Shea Stadium in New York City on 15 August 1965, the highlight of their 1965 tour. The show was filmed for the documentary The Beatles at Shea Stadium.

tokens.name: Isle of Wight Festival 1970
tokens.title: Hendrix's last major UK show
tokens.description: The Isle of Wight Festival 1970 was a music festival held from 26 to 30 August 1970 at Afton Down on the Isle of Wight, England. Guinness World Records estimated 600,000 to 700,000 attendees.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Godefroy · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Altamont Free Concert
tokens.title: Free concert marked by violence
tokens.description: The Altamont Speedway Free Festival was a rock concert held on 6 December 1969 at Altamont Speedway near Tracy, California. Around 300,000 people attended, and the event is remembered for the violence that occurred during it.
tokens.image_credit: Associated Press · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monterey International Pop Festival
tokens.title: Hendrix, Joplin and The Who break through
tokens.description: The Monterey International Pop Festival was a three-day music festival held 16 to 18 June 1967 at the Monterey County Fairgrounds in California. It is regarded as one of the beginnings of the Summer of Love.
tokens.image_credit: Monterey International Pop Festival · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Summer of Love
tokens.title: Haight-Ashbury hippie gathering
tokens.description: The Summer of Love was a social phenomenon in San Francisco during the summer of 1967, when as many as 100,000 young people gathered in the Haight-Ashbury district and Golden Gate Park. It spread counterculture ideas across the West Coast and beyond.
tokens.image_credit: Greenville News/Associated Press · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Live 8
tokens.title: Concerts ahead of the G8 summit
tokens.description: Live 8 was a series of benefit concerts held on 2 July 2005 in the G8 states and South Africa, timed to precede the G8 summit at Gleneagles. It also marked the 20th anniversary of Live Aid.

tokens.name: The Concert for New York City
tokens.title: Tribute after 9/11
tokens.description: The Concert for New York City was a benefit concert held at Madison Square Garden in response to the September 11 attacks. It honored first responders, the victims and the rescue workers.

tokens.name: The Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert
tokens.title: Wembley salute to Queen's singer
tokens.description: The Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert, also called A Concert for Life, was a benefit concert for AIDS awareness held at Wembley Stadium in London on 20 April 1992. It was a posthumous tribute by Queen to their singer Freddie Mercury, who died in November 1991.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rock in Rio 1985
tokens.title: Largest music festival in the world
tokens.description: Rock in Rio 1985 was the first edition of the Rock in Rio music festival, held in 1985 at the City of Rock (Cidade do Rock) in Rio de Janeiro. The festival later branched into other cities, including Lisbon and Madrid.
tokens.image_credit: Flaviohmg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Three Tenors concert
tokens.title: Baths of Caracalla on the eve of the World Cup final
tokens.description: Concert by the Three Tenors, Luciano Pavarotti, Placido Domingo and Jose Carreras, at the Baths of Caracalla in Rome on 7 July 1990. It was held on the eve of the 1990 FIFA World Cup final and launched the trio.
tokens.image_credit: Ethan Doyle White · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dylan goes electric at Newport
tokens.title: Folk purists boo the amplified set
tokens.description: Bob Dylan played an amplified electric set at the Newport Folk Festival on 25 July 1965, departing from the festival's acoustic folk tradition. Part of the audience booed the performance.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Death of Elvis Presley
tokens.title: The King dies at Graceland
tokens.description: Elvis Presley died at Graceland, his home in Memphis, Tennessee, on 16 August 1977, aged 42. Fans gathered outside the estate's gates.
tokens.image_credit: Associated Press · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Murder of John Lennon
tokens.title: Shot outside the Dakota
tokens.description: John Lennon, formerly of the Beatles, was shot dead in the archway of The Dakota, his Manhattan residence, on 8 December 1980. Mark David Chapman was convicted of the murder.
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Death of Michael Jackson
tokens.title: Pop star dies in Los Angeles
tokens.description: Michael Jackson died at his North Carolwood Drive home in Holmby Hills, Los Angeles, on 25 June 2009, aged 50. The cause was acute propofol intoxication.

tokens.name: One Love Peace Concert
tokens.title: Marley joins the hands of rival leaders
tokens.description: The One Love Peace Concert was held on 22 April 1978 at the National Stadium in Kingston, Jamaica. During Bob Marley's performance he joined the hands of political rivals Michael Manley and Edward Seaga.
tokens.image_credit: Cm 1962 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zaire 74 festival
tokens.title: Soul and funk in Kinshasa before the Rumble
tokens.description: Zaire 74 was a three-day music festival held from 22 to 24 September 1974 at the Stade du 20 Mai in Kinshasa. It was meant to promote the Rumble in the Jungle boxing match between Ali and Foreman.
tokens.image_credit: Yallahbye · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eurovision 1974 and ABBA
tokens.title: Waterloo launches a pop dynasty
tokens.description: The Eurovision Song Contest 1974 was held on 6 April 1974 at the Brighton Dome in Brighton, England. The Swedish group ABBA won the contest with Waterloo.
tokens.image_credit: The Voice of Hassocks · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Eurovision Song Contest
tokens.title: Seven nations in Lugano
tokens.description: The first Eurovision Song Contest was held on 24 May 1956 at the Teatro Kursaal in Lugano, Switzerland. It was presented by Lohengrin Filipello and organised by the European Broadcasting Union.

tokens.name: Gangnam Style
tokens.title: First video to reach a billion YouTube views
tokens.description: Gangnam Style is a K-pop song by South Korean singer Psy, released on 15 July 2012 by YG Entertainment. The term refers to the nouveau riche lifestyle associated with the Gangnam district of Seoul.

tokens.name: Star Wars opening at Grauman's Chinese Theatre
tokens.title: A new hope opens at Grauman's Chinese Theatre
tokens.description: Star Wars, later subtitled Episode IV: A New Hope, opened on 25 May 1977 and was shown at Grauman's Chinese Theatre in Hollywood, Los Angeles. The movie palace stands on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First commercial film screening
tokens.title: Lumière brothers at the Salon Indien du Grand Café
tokens.description: The Lumière brothers gave their first commercial public film screening on 28 December 1895 in the Salon Indien, a basement room of the Grand Café. The room was on Boulevard des Capucines near the Place de l'Opéra in Paris.

tokens.name: The Jazz Singer premiere
tokens.title: First feature with synchronised dialogue
tokens.description: The Jazz Singer, a Warner Bros. film, premiered at the Warners' Theatre on Broadway at 52nd Street in New York City on 6 October 1927. It is the first feature-length film with synchronised recorded music and sung and spoken dialogue in several sequences.

tokens.name: First Academy Awards
tokens.title: Private dinner at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel
tokens.description: The first Academy Awards honoured films from August 1927 to July 1928 at a private dinner on 16 May 1929 at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel in Los Angeles. It is the only Academy Awards ceremony not broadcast on radio or television.
tokens.image_credit: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parasite wins Best Picture
tokens.title: First non-English film to win the top Oscar
tokens.description: Parasite, a South Korean film directed by Bong Joon-ho, won Best Picture at the 92nd Academy Awards on 9 February 2020 at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood. It was the first non-English-language film to win the top Oscar.
tokens.image_credit: Busition · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Theft of the Mona Lisa
tokens.title: Louvre painting vanishes for two years
tokens.description: On 21 August 1911 Vincenzo Peruggia, a former glazier, stole the Mona Lisa from the Louvre in Paris. The stolen painting is a half-length portrait by Leonardo da Vinci.
tokens.image_credit: Benh LIEU SONG (Flickr) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft
tokens.title: Largest unsolved art theft
tokens.description: Thirteen works of art were stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston on March 18, 1990. The case is unsolved, no arrests have been made and no works have been recovered.
tokens.image_credit: Federal Bureau of Investigation · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Armory Show
tokens.title: Modern art shocks New York
tokens.description: The 1913 Armory Show, formally the International Exhibition of Modern Art, was the first large exhibition of modern art in America. It opened at New York's 69th Regiment Armory on February 17, 1913.
tokens.image_credit: Dmadeo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salon des Refusés
tokens.title: Rejected painters hold their own show
tokens.description: The Salon des Refusés is an exhibition of artworks rejected by the jury of the official Paris Salon, most famously the 1863 show. The 1863 exhibition was held at the Palais de l'Industrie in Paris.
tokens.image_credit: Édouard Baldus · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bombing of Guernica
tokens.title: Air raid on the Basque town
tokens.description: On 26 April 1937 the Basque town of Guernica was bombed from the air during the Spanish Civil War. The raid was carried out for Franco's Nationalists by the German Condor Legion and the Italian Aviazione Legionaria.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish Civil War
tokens.title: Military uprising divides Spain
tokens.description: The Spanish Civil War was fought in Spain from 1936 to 1939 between the Republicans and the Nationalist rebels. It began with a military uprising in July 1936 that started at Melilla in Spanish North Africa.

tokens.name: Siege of the Alcázar
tokens.title: Toledo's fortress holds out
tokens.description: The Siege of the Alcázar was a Nationalist victory in Toledo in the opening stages of the Spanish Civil War. Popular Front militias began the siege of the Alcázar fortress on 21 July 1936.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Ebro
tokens.title: Largest battle of the Spanish Civil War
tokens.description: The Battle of the Ebro was fought from July to November 1938 on the lower Ebro River in Catalonia and Aragon. It was the longest and largest battle of the Spanish Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: Xufanc · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Granada War
tokens.title: Final campaign of the Reconquista
tokens.description: The Granada War was a series of seasonal military campaigns from 1482 to 1492 by the Catholic Monarchs against the Nasrid Emirate of Granada. It ended with the surrender of Granada and the annexation of its territory by Castile.
tokens.image_credit: Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
tokens.title: Christian kings defeat the Almohads
tokens.description: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa was fought on 16 July 1212 between Christian kings led by Alfonso VIII of Castile and the Almohad Caliphate. The Christian victory was a turning point in the Reconquista.
tokens.image_credit: Francisco de Paula Van Halen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Guadalete
tokens.title: Muslim army overruns Visigothic Spain
tokens.description: The Battle of Guadalete was fought in July 711 between the Visigoths under King Roderic and the Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad. The Umayyad victory opened the way to the Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula.
tokens.image_credit: Salvador Martínez Cubells · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Covadonga
tokens.title: Traditional start of the Reconquista
tokens.description: The Battle of Covadonga took place in 722 near Covadonga in the Picos de Europa, where Christian forces under Pelagius defeated an Umayyad army. It is traditionally seen as the start of the Reconquista.
tokens.image_credit: CanBea87 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Columbus lands in the Americas
