tokens.title: Landfall in the Bahamas
tokens.description: On 12 October 1492 Christopher Columbus made landfall in the Americas on Guanahani, a Lucayan island in the Bahamas. Guanahani is traditionally identified with San Salvador Island.
tokens.image_credit: Alain Manesson Mallet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation
tokens.title: First voyage around the world
tokens.description: The Magellan-Elcano expedition sailed from Sanlúcar de Barrameda in 1519 and returned to Spain in 1522 as the first voyage around the world. It was begun by Ferdinand Magellan and completed by Juan Sebastián Elcano.
tokens.image_credit: Johannes Stradanus (Jan van der Straet) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vasco da Gama reaches India
tokens.title: Sea route from Europe to Calicut
tokens.description: In May 1498 Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on the Malabar Coast, completing the first sea route from Europe to India around the Cape of Good Hope. The voyage opened direct European maritime trade with India.
tokens.image_credit: Roque Gameiro · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zheng He's treasure fleets
tokens.title: Ming armada sails to the Indian Ocean
tokens.description: Between 1405 and 1433 Ming China sent seven large treasure fleets, commanded by the admiral Zheng He, on far-reaching voyages through the South China Sea and the Indian Ocean. The fleets were built at Nanjing.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Diu
tokens.title: Portugal wins control of the Indian Ocean
tokens.description: The Battle of Diu was a naval battle fought on 3 February 1509 in the port of Diu, India, between the Portuguese Empire and a joint Gujarat, Mamluk and Calicut fleet. The Portuguese victory secured their control of Indian Ocean trade.
tokens.image_credit: Maurício José do Carmo Sendim (1786-1870) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Malacca 1511
tokens.title: Albuquerque takes the spice port
tokens.description: In 1511 Afonso de Albuquerque captured the port city of Malacca, which controlled the Strait of Malacca. The conquest gave Portugal a foothold on the sea route between China and India.
tokens.image_credit: Ernesto Ferreira Condeixa · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
tokens.title: Portuguese king killed in Morocco
tokens.description: The Battle of Alcácer Quibir was fought on 4 August 1578 near Ksar el-Kebir in northern Morocco. A Moroccan victory, it killed Portuguese King Sebastian I and ended Portugal's attempts to reconquer its Moroccan territories.

tokens.name: Battle of Tondibi
tokens.title: Moroccan guns end the Songhai Empire
tokens.description: The Battle of Tondibi was the decisive clash of the Moroccan invasion of the Songhai Empire. The Moroccan army under Judar Pasha defeated the Songhai forces of Askia Ishaq II, guaranteeing the empire's downfall.

tokens.name: Battle of Kirina
tokens.title: Sundiata founds the Mali Empire
tokens.description: The Battle of Kirina, around 1235, was a confrontation between Sosso king Sumanguru Kante and Mandinka prince Sundiata Keita. Sundiata's victory established the Mali Empire as the leading power in West Africa.

tokens.name: Algerian War
tokens.title: Toussaint Rouge attacks
tokens.description: The Algerian War was fought from 1954 to 1962 between France and the Algerian National Liberation Front. It began with the Toussaint Rouge attacks of 1 November 1954 and ended with Algerian independence.
tokens.image_credit: Zdravko Pečar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Algiers
tokens.title: Urban guerrilla war in the Casbah
tokens.description: The Battle of Algiers was a campaign of urban guerrilla warfare and repression in Algiers from 1956 to 1957, during the Algerian War. The FLN and French forces both targeted civilians in the city.
tokens.image_credit: Saber68 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bombardment of Algiers 1816
tokens.title: Anglo-Dutch fleet strikes pirate port
tokens.description: On 27 August 1816 an Anglo-Dutch fleet under Admiral Lord Exmouth bombarded the harbour defences of Algiers. The attack aimed to end the enslavement of Europeans by the Dey of Algiers.
tokens.image_credit: Martinus Schouman Martinus Schouman died 1848-10-30 Ministerie van Marine · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Évian Accords
tokens.title: Ceasefire ends the Algerian War
tokens.description: The Évian Accords were declarations signed on 18 March 1962 in Évian-les-Bains between the French Government and the Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic. They set out Algeria's independence and ended the Algerian War with a ceasefire declared on 19 March 1962.
tokens.image_credit: UtCon Collection · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mau Mau rebellion
tokens.title: Anti-colonial revolt in Kenya
tokens.description: The Mau Mau rebellion (1952 to 1960), also called the Kenya Emergency, was an armed conflict in the British colony of Kenya. The Kenya Land and Freedom Army, made up mainly of Kikuyu, Meru and Embu fighters, fought the British colonial authorities.
tokens.image_credit: MINISTRY OF DEFENCE POST 1945 OFFICIAL COLLECTION · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1998 United States embassy bombings
tokens.title: Nairobi and Dar es Salaam attacked
tokens.description: On 7 August 1998, truck bombs exploded almost at the same time at the United States embassies in Nairobi, Kenya and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. More than 220 people were killed, and Fazul Abdullah Mohammed and Abdullah Ahmed Abdullah were named as responsible for planning the attacks.
tokens.image_credit: Zweifel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Westgate shopping mall attack
tokens.title: Siege in Nairobi
tokens.description: On 21 September 2013, four gunmen attacked the Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi, Kenya. The attack and the siege that followed killed 71 people, including 62 civilians, and part of the mall collapsed after a fire.
tokens.image_credit: Anne Knight · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Mogadishu 1993
tokens.title: Black Hawk Down
tokens.description: The Battle of Mogadishu was fought on 3 and 4 October 1993 in Mogadishu, Somalia. United States forces, supported by UNOSOM II, fought Somali National Alliance fighters in the south of the city, and it is also known as Black Hawk Down.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Somali Civil War
tokens.title: Siad Barre ousted
tokens.description: The Somali Civil War grew out of resistance to the military junta of Siad Barre during the 1980s. From 1988 the Somali Armed Forces fought several armed rebel groups, and Wikipedia describes the war as ongoing.
tokens.image_credit: Fataho dhaadsan · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ethiopian famine of 1983 to 1985
tokens.title: Famine prompts global aid response
tokens.description: A widespread famine affected Ethiopia from 1983 to 1985, the worst the country had seen in a century. It affected about 7.75 million people and left an estimated 300,000 to 1.2 million dead.
tokens.image_credit: Talskiddy at English Wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ethiopian Revolution
tokens.title: Haile Selassie deposed
tokens.description: The Ethiopian Revolution was a period of civil, police and military upheaval against the government of Haile Selassie. It is generally considered to have begun on 12 January 1974, when soldiers mutinied in Negele Borana in southern Ethiopia.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Italian invasion of Ethiopia
tokens.title: Mussolini attacks Ethiopia
tokens.description: A war of aggression waged by Italy against Ethiopia from October 1935 to May 1936. Wikipedia regards it as the largest colonial campaign in history.
tokens.image_credit: Foto luce – ediz. d’arte v.e. Boeri – v. f. Corridoni, 7 Roma · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Magdala
tokens.title: British expedition ends Tewodros's reign
tokens.description: The Battle of Magdala in April 1868 concluded the British Expedition to Abyssinia. British forces led by Robert Napier defeated the army of Emperor Tewodros II at Magdala.
tokens.image_credit: William Barnes Wollen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Omdurman
tokens.title: Kitchener's army routs the Mahdists
tokens.description: The Battle of Omdurman was fought on 2 September 1898 at Kerreri, north of Omdurman, during the Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Sudan. A British-Egyptian force under Horatio Herbert Kitchener defeated the Mahdist army.
tokens.image_credit: Edward Matthew Hale (1852-1924). Original uploader was Raoulduke47 4 January 2007 (original upload date) at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fashoda Incident
tokens.title: British and French armies meet on the Nile
tokens.description: The Fashoda Incident was the climax of Anglo-French rivalry in East Africa, lasting from 10 July to 3 November 1898. A French expedition at Fashoda on the White Nile sought control of the Upper Nile and met a British-Egyptian force there.

tokens.name: Battle of Blood River
tokens.title: Voortrekkers defeat the Zulu army
tokens.description: The Battle of Blood River was fought on 16 December 1838 on the Ncome River, in present-day KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. About 464 Voortrekkers led by Andries Pretorius defeated a Zulu army of an estimated 25,000 to 30,000.
tokens.image_credit: Renier Maritz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Trek
tokens.title: Boer families leave the Cape Colony
tokens.description: The Great Trek was a migration of Dutch-speaking Boer settlers by wagon from the Cape Colony into the interior of present-day South Africa from 1836 onwards. It was driven by tensions with the British colonial administration.
tokens.image_credit: JMK · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Boer War
tokens.title: Boer republics fight Britain
tokens.description: The Second Boer War was fought from 1899 to 1902 between the British Empire and the Boer republics, the South African Republic and the Orange Free State. It was triggered by the discovery of gold on the Witwatersrand and a dispute over voting rights for British expatriates.
tokens.image_credit: Reinhold Thiele · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Mafeking
tokens.title: 217 days of siege
tokens.description: The siege of Mafeking was a 217-day siege of the town now called Mahikeng, during the Second Boer War from October 1899 to May 1900. The defence under Colonel Robert Baden-Powell turned him into a national hero.
tokens.image_credit: G W Bacon & Co London · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Spion Kop
tokens.title: Costly British defeat in Natal
tokens.description: The Battle of Spion Kop was fought on 23 and 24 January 1900 during the Second Boer War. Boer forces held the hilltop against British troops trying to relieve the siege of Ladysmith.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Majuba Hill
tokens.title: Boer victory ends the First Boer War
tokens.description: The Battle of Majuba Hill on 27 February 1881 was the decisive battle of the First Boer War. Boer forces defeated British troops under Sir George Pomeroy Colley on the hill near Volksrust.
tokens.image_credit: Fidodog14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1995 Rugby World Cup final
tokens.title: Mandela hands the trophy to François Pienaar
tokens.description: The 1995 Rugby World Cup Final was played at Ellis Park Stadium in Johannesburg on 24 June 1995. South Africa beat New Zealand by three points after extra time, the first final to need extra time.
tokens.image_credit: Leglo09 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Truth and Reconciliation Commission
tokens.title: Hearings on apartheid abuses begin
tokens.description: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission was set up in South Africa in 1996 after apartheid, chaired by Desmond Tutu. It took statements from victims of gross human rights violations and from perpetrators seeking amnesty.

tokens.name: Rivonia Trial
tokens.title: Mandela and comrades sentenced to life
tokens.description: The Rivonia Trial ran from October 1963 to June 1964 at the Palace of Justice in Pretoria. Nelson Mandela and other leaders of uMkhonto we Sizwe were sentenced to life imprisonment.
tokens.image_credit: Cvanrooyen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
tokens.title: Decisive battle in the Angolan Bush War
tokens.description: The Battle of Cuito Cuanavale was fought from August 1987 to March 1988 in southern Angola, between FAPLA and Cuban forces on one side and South African and UNITA forces on the other. It was the largest engagement of the Angolan conflict.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Angolan Civil War
tokens.title: Independence leads to decades of conflict
tokens.description: The Angolan Civil War began in 1975, immediately after Angola became independent from Portugal in November of that year. It was a power struggle between the MPLA and UNITA that lasted, with interludes, until 2002.

tokens.name: 2000 Mozambique flood
tokens.title: Cyclone and rivers inundate the south
tokens.description: The 2000 Mozambique flood occurred in February and March 2000 after about four weeks of heavy rain from Cyclone Leon-Eline. Approximately 800 people died and many were left homeless.
tokens.image_credit: USAID U.S. Agency for International Development · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Congo Crisis begins
tokens.title: Independence followed by turmoil
tokens.description: The Congo Crisis was a period of political upheaval and civil war in the Republic of the Congo from 1960 to 1965, starting soon after independence from Belgium. It became a Cold War proxy conflict between the Soviet Union and the United States.

tokens.name: Assassination of Patrice Lumumba
tokens.title: Congo's first prime minister killed
tokens.description: Patrice Lumumba, the first prime minister of the Republic of the Congo, was assassinated on 17 January 1961 in Katanga, near Elisabethville. The killing took place during the Congo Crisis.
tokens.image_credit: Henri van der Noot · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Congo War
tokens.title: Africa's deadliest modern conflict
tokens.description: The Second Congo War began on 2 August 1998 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and drew in several neighbouring countries. It is also known as Africa's World War.

tokens.name: Nigerian Civil War
tokens.title: Biafra secedes from Nigeria
tokens.description: The Nigerian Civil War, also known as the Biafran War, was fought from 1967 to 1970 between Nigeria and the secessionist Republic of Biafra. Biafra had declared independence from Nigeria in 1967.

tokens.name: Chibok schoolgirls kidnapping
tokens.title: Mass abduction by Boko Haram
tokens.description: On the night of 14 to 15 April 2014, 276 schoolgirls were kidnapped by the militant group Boko Haram from the Government Girls Secondary School in Chibok, Borno State, Nigeria. Some girls escaped and others were later rescued.
tokens.image_credit: Yaroh Dauda · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amistad revolt
tokens.title: Captives take control of the schooner
tokens.description: In July 1839, Mende captives on the Spanish-owned schooner La Amistad seized control of the ship off Cuba. They had been illegally sold into slavery in Cuba, in violation of European treaties against the Atlantic slave trade.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Dahomey
tokens.title: Abomey falls to French forces
tokens.description: Abomey, the royal capital of the Kingdom of Dahomey, fell to French forces during the Second Franco-Dahomean War, which ran from 1892 to 1894. France then incorporated Dahomey into French West Africa.

tokens.name: Battle of Ulundi
tokens.title: British break Zulu power
tokens.description: The Battle of Ulundi was fought on 4 July 1879 at the Zulu capital of Ulundi. It was the last battle of the Anglo-Zulu War, in which the British Army broke the military power of the Zulu Kingdom.
tokens.image_credit: Archibald Forbes, Arthur Griffiths and others. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anglo-Zulu War
tokens.title: British invasion of Zululand
tokens.description: The Anglo-Zulu War was fought from January to July 1879 between the British Empire and the Zulu Kingdom in present-day South Africa. Its best known battles are the Zulu victory at Isandlwana and the British defence of Rorke's Drift.
tokens.image_credit: Alphonse de Neuville · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anglo-Zanzibar War
tokens.title: Shortest war in recorded history
tokens.description: The Anglo-Zanzibar War was fought on 27 August 1896 between the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Zanzibar. It lasted about 38 to 45 minutes and is recorded as the shortest war in history.
tokens.image_credit: Fred T. Jane · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maji Maji Rebellion
tokens.title: Uprising against German East Africa
tokens.description: The Maji Maji Rebellion was an armed uprising of Africans against German colonial rule in German East Africa, today Tanzania. It lasted from 1905 to 1907 and caused widespread famine and very heavy loss of life.

tokens.name: Zanzibar Revolution
tokens.title: Sultan overthrown
tokens.description: The Zanzibar Revolution began on 12 January 1964 and overthrew Sultan Jamshid bin Abdullah and his Arab-led government. It followed Zanzibar's independence from Britain in December 1963.

tokens.name: Expulsion of Asians from Uganda
tokens.title: Amin gives 90 days to leave
tokens.description: In August 1972 Ugandan President Idi Amin ordered the expulsion of the country's Asian minority, mostly of Indian origin, giving them 90 days to leave. Many were resettled in Britain, Canada and other countries.
tokens.image_credit: Bert Verhoeff for Anefo · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uganda-Tanzania War
tokens.title: Tanzanian forces topple Idi Amin
tokens.description: The war between Uganda and Tanzania was fought from October 1978 to June 1979. It ended with Tanzanian forces and Ugandan exiles overthrowing President Idi Amin.

tokens.name: First Liberian Civil War
tokens.title: Conflict begins with Taylor's invasion
tokens.description: The First Liberian Civil War lasted from 1989 to 1997 and was the first of two civil wars in Liberia. It was triggered by political, economic and ethnic tensions under the regime of President Samuel Doe.
tokens.image_credit: James G. Antal, R. John Vanden Berghe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Plataea
tokens.title: Greek alliance ends the Persian invasion
tokens.description: The Battle of Plataea took place in August 479 BC near Plataea in Boeotia. A Greek alliance led by Sparta defeated the Persian army of Mardonius, ending the second Persian invasion of Greece.
tokens.image_credit: John Steeple Davis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sicilian Expedition
tokens.title: Athens' Sicilian expedition fails
tokens.description: The Sicilian Expedition was an Athenian military campaign against Syracuse in Sicily from 415 to 413 BC during the Peloponnesian War. It ended in a devastating Athenian defeat that severely weakened Athens in the war.
tokens.image_credit: Ward & Lock’s Illustrated History of the World (Drawing by Hermann Vogel) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Leuctra
tokens.title: Thebes breaks Spartan power
tokens.description: The Battle of Leuctra was fought on 6 July 371 BC, when the Thebans under Epaminondas defeated the Spartans in Boeotia. The Theban victory ended Sparta's dominance over the Greek world.
tokens.image_credit: Edmund Ollier Publication date 1882 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Chaeronea
tokens.title: Philip II wins control of Greece
tokens.description: The Battle of Chaeronea was fought in 338 BC in Boeotia between Philip II of Macedon and an alliance of Athens and Thebes. Philip's decisive victory gave Macedon control over mainland Greece.
tokens.image_credit: Philipp Pilhofer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Granicus
tokens.title: Alexander's first victory in Asia
tokens.description: The Battle of the Granicus was fought in May 334 BC, the first major battle between Alexander the Great and the Persian Achaemenid Empire. Alexander's victory at the Granicus river opened the way into Asia Minor.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Le Brun / Abraham Genoels · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Issus
tokens.title: Alexander routs Darius
tokens.description: The Battle of Issus was fought on 5 November 333 BC in southern Anatolia, where Alexander the Great defeated Darius III of Persia. Darius fled, leaving his family and treasury to Alexander.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Tyre
tokens.title: Alexander builds a causeway to the island
tokens.description: The Siege of Tyre was carried out by Alexander the Great in 332 BC during his campaigns against Persia. After seven months he took the island city by building a causeway from the mainland.
tokens.image_credit: André Castaigne · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
tokens.title: Alexander defeats King Porus
tokens.description: The Battle of the Hydaspes was fought in May 326 BC on the Jhelum River in the Punjab, where Alexander the Great defeated King Porus. Porus was captured, then reinstated by Alexander as a ruler.
tokens.image_credit: André Castaigne · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Ipsus
tokens.title: Alexander's successors divide the empire
tokens.description: The Battle of Ipsus was fought in 301 BC near Ipsus in Phrygia between the Diadochi successors of Alexander the Great. Antigonus I was killed and his realm was divided among the victors.

tokens.name: Battle of Asculum
tokens.title: Pyrrhus wins at heavy cost
tokens.description: The Battle of Asculum was fought in 279 BC near modern Ascoli Satriano, between the Roman Republic and Pyrrhus of Epirus, during the Pyrrhic War. Pyrrhus won the battle at heavy cost to his own army.
tokens.image_credit: Heinrich Leutemann · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Pharsalus
tokens.title: Caesar defeats Pompey
tokens.description: The Battle of Pharsalus was fought on 9 August 48 BC near Pharsalus in Thessaly, where Julius Caesar defeated Pompey. It was the decisive battle of Caesar's Civil War.

tokens.name: Battle of Philippi
tokens.title: Caesar's assassins defeated
tokens.description: The Battle of Philippi was fought in 42 BC on the plain west of Philippi in Macedonia, between the forces of Mark Antony and Octavian and the assassins of Julius Caesar. It was the final battle of the Liberators' civil war.

tokens.name: Crossing of the Rubicon
tokens.title: Caesar starts a civil war
tokens.description: In January 49 BC Julius Caesar led his legion across the Rubicon river, defying the law that barred him from commanding an army in Italy. The crossing started the civil war against Pompey and the Senate.
tokens.image_credit: Jacob Abbott · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Third Servile War
tokens.title: Gladiators and slaves defy Rome
tokens.description: The Third Servile War, also called the Gladiator War, was a slave revolt led by Spartacus against the Roman Republic from 73 to 71 BC. It was the only Servile War that directly threatened the Italian heartland of Rome.

tokens.name: Great Fire of Rome
tokens.title: Blaze consumes much of the city
tokens.description: The Great Fire of Rome began on the evening of 18 July 64 AD near the Circus Maximus. It burned for about nine days and destroyed ten of the city's fourteen districts.
tokens.image_credit: Hubert Robert · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boudican revolt
tokens.title: Iceni queen burns Roman Colchester and London
tokens.description: The Boudican revolt was an uprising of Celtic Britons led by Boudica, queen of the Iceni, against the Roman Empire in about AD 60 to 61. Rebels burned the Roman towns of Colchester and London before the revolt was crushed.

tokens.name: Roman conquest of Britain
tokens.title: Claudius's legions land in Kent
tokens.description: The Roman conquest of Britain began in earnest in AD 43 under Emperor Claudius. It was largely completed in southern Britain, most of present-day England and Wales, by AD 87.

tokens.name: Building of Hadrian's Wall
tokens.title: Rome fixes its northern frontier
tokens.description: Hadrian's Wall is a Roman defensive fortification begun in AD 122 under Emperor Hadrian. It runs across northern England from Wallsend on the Tyne to Bowness-on-Solway.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin Smith · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Council of Nicaea
tokens.title: Bishops define Christian doctrine
tokens.description: The First Council of Nicaea was a council of Christian bishops convened by Emperor Constantine I in 325 at Nicaea, now Iznik in Turkey. It is also known as the First Ecumenical Council.
tokens.image_credit: C messier · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Foundation of Constantinople
tokens.title: Constantine's new capital dedicated
tokens.description: Constantine I dedicated his new capital on the site of Byzantium in 330. The city, today's Istanbul, served as capital of the Roman and Byzantine empires until 1453.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry A. Mottl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
tokens.title: Romulus Augustulus deposed
tokens.description: The fall of the Western Roman Empire was the loss of central political control over its Western provinces, which were divided among successor states. The token marks the deposition of the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, in 476.

tokens.name: Nika riots
tokens.title: Uprising nearly topples Justinian
tokens.description: The Nika riots were a week of violent revolt against Byzantine emperor Justinian I in Constantinople in 532. They are often regarded as the most violent riots in the city's history.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Constantinople 717-718
tokens.title: Arab assault repelled
tokens.description: In 717-718 the Umayyad Caliphate besieged Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire. The Arab assault was repelled and the city held.
tokens.image_credit: en:User:Bigdaddy1204 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hijrah
tokens.title: Muhammad migrates from Mecca to Medina
tokens.description: The Hijrah was the journey of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina, dated to 622. The year of the journey is the epoch of the Islamic lunar and solar calendars.
tokens.image_credit: Adiput (talk) · PD · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Uhud
tokens.title: Early Muslims face the Quraysh
tokens.description: The Battle of Uhud was fought in 625 between the early Muslims and the Quraysh in a valley north of Medina, near Mount Uhud. It followed the Muslim migration to Medina and the Quraysh defeat at Badr in 624.
tokens.image_credit: CR Guru PK · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Trench
tokens.title: Medina defended behind a ditch
tokens.description: The Battle of the Trench was a 627 conflict in which the Quraysh advanced on Medina, whose Muslim defenders dug a defensive trench on the advice of Salman the Persian. The siege lasted about two weeks and caused few casualties on either side.
tokens.image_credit: Md iet · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abbasid revolution
tokens.title: Umayyad dynasty overthrown
tokens.description: The Abbasid revolution overthrew the Umayyad Caliphate, the second major caliphate, through the Hashimiyya movement, which established the Abbasid Caliphate in 750. The revolt began in the eastern province of Khorasan in the mid-8th century.
tokens.image_credit: Abu Ali Bal'ami · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: House of Wisdom
tokens.title: Baghdad's centre for scholarship
tokens.description: The House of Wisdom was a major Abbasid-era academy and library in Baghdad during the Islamic Golden Age. Under caliph al-Ma'mun (r. 813 to 833) it became a public academy and centre of scholarship.

tokens.name: Battle of Lechfeld
tokens.title: Otto I crushes the Magyars
tokens.description: The Battle of Lechfeld was fought from 10 to 12 August 955 on the Lechfeld plain near Augsburg, where Otto I's German army defeated the Hungarian Magyar invaders. The victory ended further major Magyar invasions of Western Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Hektor Mülich[1] (d. 1490) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Clontarf
tokens.title: Brian Boru defeats the Vikings at Dublin
tokens.description: The Battle of Clontarf took place on 23 April 1014 at Clontarf, near Dublin. An army led by Brian Boru, High King of Ireland, fought a Norse-Irish alliance that included the forces of Sigtrygg Silkbeard, King of Dublin, and ended in a rout of the Viking and Leinster armies.
tokens.image_credit: Hugh Frazer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Stamford Bridge
tokens.title: Harold defeats Harald Hardrada
tokens.description: The Battle of Stamford Bridge was fought on 25 September 1066 at Stamford Bridge in the East Riding of Yorkshire. English forces under King Harold Godwinson defeated the Norwegian invaders led by Harald Hardrada, who was killed, and Tostig Godwinson.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Nicolai Arbo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Domesday Book
tokens.title: William's great survey of England
tokens.description: The Domesday Book is a manuscript record of the Great Survey of much of England and parts of Wales, made at the behest of William the Conqueror. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle dates the order for the survey to 1085, and the book was first kept at Winchester.

tokens.name: Council of Clermont
tokens.title: Urban II calls the First Crusade
tokens.description: The Council of Clermont was a synod of the Catholic Church called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, in Auvergne. It is known mainly for the speech Urban gave on the final day, which called for the First Crusade.
tokens.image_credit: Jean Colombe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Antioch
tokens.title: Crusaders take the city
tokens.description: The Siege of Antioch was fought during the First Crusade from October 1097 to June 1098. The Crusaders took the Seljuk-held city on 3 June 1098.
tokens.image_credit: Jean Colombe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Acre 1189-1191
tokens.title: Third Crusade's great siege
tokens.description: The Siege of Acre lasted from August 1189 to July 1191 and formed part of the Third Crusade. It was the first major counterattack by Guy of Jerusalem against Saladin.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Arsuf
tokens.title: Richard the Lionheart defeats Saladin
tokens.description: The Battle of Arsuf took place on 7 September 1191 during the Third Crusade. Richard I of England led the Crusaders to victory over a larger army led by Saladin.
tokens.image_credit: Éloi Firmin Féron · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sack of Constantinople 1204
tokens.title: Crusaders sack the Christian capital
tokens.description: The Sack of Constantinople in April 1204 marked the culmination of the Fourth Crusade. Crusaders sacked most of the Byzantine capital, and the Latin Empire was established after the capture.

tokens.name: Siege of Montségur
tokens.title: Cathar fortress falls
tokens.description: The siege of Montségur lasted from May 1243 to March 1244 during the Albigensian Crusade. The Cathar stronghold surrendered after a nine-month siege.
tokens.image_credit: Jean-Yves Didier The original uploader was Jydidier at French Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Muret
tokens.title: Crusaders defeat the Cathars' allies
tokens.description: The Battle of Muret was fought on 12 September 1213 near Toulouse, in the Albigensian Crusade. A small force of French knights under Simon de Montfort defeated a larger army led by Peter II of Aragon and Raymond VI of Toulouse.

tokens.name: Siege of Acre 1291
tokens.title: Last Crusader stronghold lost
tokens.description: The siege of Acre took place in 1291 and ended with the capture of the city by the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt. The Crusaders lost control of Acre, and further crusades to the Levant ended.
tokens.image_credit: Louis-Dominique Papety · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Children's Crusade
tokens.title: Young pilgrims set out for Jerusalem
tokens.description: The Children's Crusade was a failed popular crusade by European Christians in the early 13th century, aimed at the Holy Land. It never received papal approval as an official crusade.
tokens.image_credit: Gustave Doré · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arrest of the Templars
tokens.title: Friday the 13th arrests across France
tokens.description: On Friday 13 October 1307, agents of King Philip IV of France arrested members of the Knights Templar across France on the king's orders. The arrests opened the trials that led to the order's suppression.

tokens.name: Battle of the Golden Spurs
tokens.title: Flemish militia defeat French knights
tokens.description: On 11 July 1302, Flemish militia defeated the royal army of France near Kortrijk during the Franco-Flemish War. It was an unexpected Flemish victory in the 1297-1305 conflict.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Sluys
tokens.title: English fleet destroys the French navy
tokens.description: On 24 June 1340, the English fleet of Edward III defeated the French fleet in the roadstead of Sluys, in the county of Flanders. It was a major naval battle of the early Hundred Years' War.
tokens.image_credit: Loyset Liédet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Calais 1346
tokens.title: Burghers surrender the keys
tokens.description: The English army of Edward III besieged the French town of Calais from 4 September 1346 to 3 August 1347, during the Hundred Years' War. The siege is commemorated by Rodin's statue The Burghers of Calais in front of the town hall.
tokens.image_credit: Romainberth · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jacquerie
tokens.title: Peasant revolt in northern France
tokens.description: In the early summer of 1358, peasants rose in revolt in the Oise valley north of Paris during the Hundred Years' War. The Jacquerie was suppressed after more than two months of violence.
tokens.image_credit: Loyset Liédet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peasants' Revolt
tokens.title: Wat Tyler's rebels enter London
tokens.description: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was a major uprising across large parts of England, led by Wat Tyler's rebels who entered London. It was driven by the Black Death, high taxes for the Hundred Years' War and unrest in London.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown medieval artist illustrating Froissart's Chronicles · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hussite Wars
tokens.title: Defenestration of Prague sparks religious war
tokens.description: The Hussite Wars were a series of civil wars fought from 1419 to about 1434 between the Hussites and the forces of Holy Roman Emperor Sigismund, the Papacy and Catholic monarchs.
tokens.image_credit: Adolf Liebscher · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Orléans
tokens.title: Joan of Arc relieves the city
tokens.description: The siege of Orléans, from 12 October 1428 to 8 May 1429, was a turning point of the Hundred Years' War. The English siege was repulsed by French forces inspired by the arrival of Joan of Arc.
tokens.image_credit: Eugène Lenepveu · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Joan of Arc burned at Rouen
tokens.title: Burned at the stake in the Old Market
tokens.description: Joan of Arc, the French military leader and saint, was burned at the stake in the Old Market of Rouen on 30 May 1431. She was executed after a trial held during the Hundred Years' War.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Battle of Castillon
tokens.title: Last battle of the Hundred Years' War
tokens.description: The Battle of Castillon was fought on 17 July 1453 near Castillon-sur-Dordogne in Gascony. The French victory killed the English commander John Talbot and ended the Hundred Years' War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Bosworth Field
tokens.title: Richard III killed, Tudors begin
tokens.description: The Battle of Bosworth Field was fought on 22 August 1485 in Leicestershire. Henry Tudor's victory, in which Richard III was killed, ended the Wars of the Roses and began the Tudor dynasty.
tokens.image_credit: Philip James de Loutherbourg · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Towton
tokens.title: Bloodiest battle on English soil
tokens.description: The Battle of Towton was fought on 29 March 1461 near Towton in North Yorkshire during the Wars of the Roses. The Yorkist victory secured the English throne for Edward IV, and the battle is probably the bloodiest ever fought on English soil.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Caton Woodville Jr. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Flodden
tokens.title: James IV of Scotland killed
tokens.description: The Battle of Flodden was fought on 9 September 1513 near Branxton in Northumberland. The English army under the Earl of Surrey defeated the invading Scots, and King James IV of Scotland was killed.
tokens.image_credit: Paul Barlow · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Field of the Cloth of Gold
tokens.title: Henry VIII and Francis I meet in splendour
tokens.description: The Field of the Cloth of Gold was a summit between Henry VIII of England and Francis I of France held from 7 to 24 June 1520. It took place at Balinghem, between Ardres and Guines, in a display of wealth by both kings.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Pavia
tokens.title: Francis I captured by Charles V
tokens.description: The Battle of Pavia was fought on 24 February 1525 near Pavia in northern Italy. The Habsburg army of Charles V defeated the French force, and Francis I was captured in the decisive engagement of the Italian War of 1521 to 1526.
tokens.image_credit: Rupert Heller · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sack of Rome 1527
tokens.title: Imperial troops sack the Eternal City
tokens.description: The Sack of Rome took place from 6 May 1527, when mutinous troops of Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, captured and plundered the city, then part of the Papal States. It was part of the War of the League of Cognac.
tokens.image_credit: Flemish school · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Rhodes 1522
tokens.title: Ottomans take the Knights' island
tokens.description: The Ottoman Empire besieged and took Rhodes from the Knights Hospitaller in 1522, after about six months of artillery fire and mining. The fall ended the Knights' rule over the island.
tokens.image_credit: Fethullah Çelebi Arifi (historian, poet and painter) and/or Matrakçı Nasuh (painter of landscape) and/or other painters at the court of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Siege of Malta
tokens.title: Knights hold the island against the Ottomans
tokens.description: The Ottoman Empire attacked Malta, held by the Knights Hospitaller, from 18 May to 8 September 1565. The Knights and Maltese defenders repelled the attack.
tokens.image_credit: Mattia Perez d'Aleccio · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Szigetvár
tokens.title: Suleiman dies during the siege
tokens.description: An Ottoman army besieged the fortress of Szigetvár in Hungary in 1566. The Habsburg garrison under Nikola Zrinski blocked the Ottoman advance towards Vienna.
tokens.image_credit: Johann Peter Krafft · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Lützen 1632
tokens.title: Gustavus Adolphus killed
tokens.description: On 16 November 1632 a Swedish army under Gustavus Adolphus narrowly defeated an Imperial army under Albrecht von Wallenstein near Lützen. Gustavus Adolphus was killed in the battle.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Snayers · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sack of Magdeburg
tokens.title: City destroyed in the Thirty Years' War
tokens.description: Imperial and Catholic League forces destroyed the Protestant city of Magdeburg from 20 to 24 May 1631. Around 20,000 people died, and the city did not regain its former importance until the 18th century.
tokens.image_credit: Workshop of Matthäus Merian · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Rocroi
tokens.title: End of Spanish infantry's aura
tokens.description: On 19 May 1643 a French army under the Duke of Enghien defeated a Spanish army under Francisco de Melo at Rocroi. The battle broke the reputation of the Spanish tercios.
tokens.image_credit: Sauveur Lecomte · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Glorious Revolution
tokens.title: William of Orange lands at Brixham
tokens.description: In November 1688 William of Orange landed at Brixham in Devon with a Dutch army, and King James II was deposed. William and his wife Mary II then ruled as joint monarchs.
tokens.image_credit: Johan Herman Isings · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Boyne
tokens.title: William III defeats James II
tokens.description: In 1690 the forces of William III defeated those of the deposed James II at the River Boyne near Drogheda. The victory helped secure Protestant ascendancy in Ireland.
tokens.image_credit: Jan van Huchtenburgh · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Blenheim
tokens.title: Marlborough's great victory
tokens.description: The Allied army of Marlborough and Eugene of Savoy defeated the Franco-Bavarian army near Höchstädt an der Donau on 13 August 1704. The victory secured Vienna and held the Grand Alliance together in the War of the Spanish Succession.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
tokens.title: Wolfe and Montcalm both die at Quebec
tokens.description: The British Army defeated the French Army on the Plains of Abraham outside Quebec City on 13 September 1759. The battle was a decisive moment in the Seven Years' War and shaped the future of New France.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin West · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Rossbach
tokens.title: Frederick the Great routs a larger army
tokens.description: Frederick the Great of Prussia defeated a larger Franco-Imperial army near Rossbach in Saxony on 5 November 1757. The battle was part of the Third Silesian War within the Seven Years' War.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown artistUnknown artist · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
tokens.title: Quake, tsunami and fire destroy the capital
tokens.description: A magnitude 7.7 or greater earthquake struck on the morning of 1 November 1755, followed by fires and a tsunami that almost completely destroyed Lisbon. The disaster is a landmark event in the history of the Portuguese capital.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kościuszko Uprising
tokens.title: Poles rise against partition
tokens.description: An uprising led by Tadeusz Kościuszko against Russian and Prussian influence in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth began in Kraków on 24 March 1794. Russian forces under Alexander Suvorov suppressed it after the Battle of Praga later that year.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Matejko · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reign of Terror
tokens.title: Guillotine at the Place de la Révolution
tokens.description: The Reign of Terror was a period of the French Revolution marked by mass executions and public guillotinings. The killings followed revolts and accusations of treason by the Committee of Public Safety.

tokens.name: Fall of Maximilien Robespierre
tokens.title: Robespierre arrested and guillotined
tokens.description: Maximilien Robespierre addressed the National Convention on 26 July 1794, was arrested the next day and guillotined on 28 July 1794 at the Place de la Révolution. His fall ended the most radical phase of the French Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Max Adamo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coup of 18 Brumaire
tokens.title: Napoleon seizes power
tokens.description: Napoleon Bonaparte seized power in France on 9 November 1799, the 18 Brumaire of the Republican calendar, overthrowing the Directory. The coup set up the Consulate with Napoleon as First Consul, and most historians regard it as the end of the French Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: François Bouchot · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Marengo
tokens.title: Napoleon wins in Italy
tokens.description: The Battle of Marengo was fought on 14 June 1800 between French forces under Napoleon Bonaparte and Austrian forces near Alessandria, Piedmont. The French victory drove the Austrians out of Italy and consolidated Bonaparte's political position in Paris.
tokens.image_credit: Louis-François, Baron Lejeune · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Wagram
tokens.title: Napoleon defeats Austria again
tokens.description: The Battle of Wagram was fought on 5 and 6 July 1809 in Lower Austria, north-east of Vienna. Napoleon's French army defeated the Austrian army under Archduke Charles, which led to the breakup of the Fifth Coalition.
tokens.image_credit: Horace Vernet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dos de Mayo Uprising
tokens.title: Madrid rises against French occupation
tokens.description: The Dos de Mayo Uprising took place in Madrid on 2 and 3 May 1808 against the French occupation of the city. The French repression, with hundreds of executions, helped spark the Peninsular War.
tokens.image_credit: Simon Burchell · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Bailén
tokens.title: First major defeat of a Napoleonic army in the field
tokens.description: The Battle of Bailén was fought from 16 to 19 July 1808 near Bailén in Andalusia. It was the first open-field defeat of a Napoleonic army, when Spanish forces under Castaños forced General Dupont's French corps to surrender.
tokens.image_credit: José Casado del Alisal · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Berezina
tokens.title: Remnants of the Grande Armée escape
tokens.description: The Battle of Berezina took place from 26 to 29 November 1812 between Napoleon's Grande Armee and Russian forces at the Berezina River near Borisov. Napoleon got the surviving remnants of his army across the river and continued his retreat from Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Hoynck van Papendrecht · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of New Orleans
tokens.title: Jackson's victory after the peace treaty
tokens.description: The Battle of New Orleans was fought on 8 January 1815 at Chalmette, near New Orleans, Louisiana. American forces under Andrew Jackson defeated the British army under Edward Pakenham, although the Treaty of Ghent had already been signed.
tokens.image_credit: Painting by Jean Hyacinthe de Laclotte (1766 - 1829), a member of the Louisiana Militia who participated in the battle; painted by him after the victory based on his sketches made at the scene. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burning of Washington
tokens.title: British troops burn the White House and Capitol
tokens.description: On 24 August 1814, British forces under Robert Ross and George Cockburn set fire to public buildings in Washington, including the White House and the Capitol. It was the only time since the Revolutionary War that a foreign power captured and occupied a United States capital.
tokens.image_credit: George Munger · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Baltimore
tokens.title: Fort McHenry inspires the national anthem
tokens.description: The Battle of Baltimore took place from 12 to 14 September 1814 during the War of 1812. American defenders repulsed British sea and land attacks, including the bombardment of Fort McHenry, which inspired the Star-Spangled Banner.
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was Dr.frog at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Lake Erie
tokens.title: "We have met the enemy"
tokens.description: The Battle of Lake Erie was fought on 10 September 1813 during the War of 1812. A United States Navy squadron under Oliver Hazard Perry defeated the British fleet and secured American control of the lake.
tokens.image_credit: NPS Photo · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Greek War of Independence
tokens.title: Revolt against Ottoman rule
tokens.description: The Greek War of Independence was fought from 1821 to 1829 by Greek revolutionaries against the Ottoman Empire. The war led to the formation of the modern Greek state.
tokens.image_credit: Theodoros Vryzakis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Navarino
tokens.title: Last major battle between sailing fleets
tokens.description: The Battle of Navarino was a naval battle fought on 20 October 1827 in Navarino Bay, now Pylos, during the Greek War of Independence. An Allied British, French and Russian fleet destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian armada.
tokens.image_credit: Ambroise Louis Garneray · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Third Siege of Missolonghi
tokens.title: Heroic exodus of the defenders
tokens.description: The third siege of Missolonghi was fought from 15 April 1825 to 10 April 1826 during the Greek War of Independence. The Greek defenders ran out of food and their mass breakout ended in heavy losses.
tokens.image_credit: Kapoios2026 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belgian Revolution
tokens.title: Brussels opera riot sparks independence
tokens.description: The Belgian Revolution was a conflict that led to the secession of the southern provinces from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. It established the independent Kingdom of Belgium.
tokens.image_credit: Trougnouf (Benoit Brummer) · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Revolutions of 1848
tokens.title: Europe's year of revolt begins in Paris
tokens.description: The Revolutions of 1848 were a series of revolts across Europe between January 1848 and October 1849. They opposed absolute monarchy and feudalism and sought to establish constitutional nation states.

tokens.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
tokens.title: Pest rises with the "12 Points"
tokens.description: The Hungarian Revolution of 1848 began in Pest on 15 March 1848 and led to the Hungarian War of Independence of 1848 to 1849. It is the cornerstone of modern Hungarian national identity.

tokens.name: Battle of Solferino
tokens.title: Bloodshed inspires the Red Cross
tokens.description: The Battle of Solferino was fought on 24 June 1859 during the Second Italian War of Independence. The Franco-Sardinian army under Napoleon III and Victor Emmanuel II defeated the Austrian army.
tokens.image_credit: This picture belongs to Xavier Caré. Please credit : Xavier Caré / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA. If you would like special permission to use, license, or purchase the image please contact me to negoti · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expedition of the Thousand
tokens.title: Garibaldi lands at Marsala
tokens.description: The Expedition of the Thousand was an 1860 campaign in which Giuseppe Garibaldi's volunteers landed at Marsala, Sicily, to conquer the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. It was a decisive step in the unification of Italy.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Rome
tokens.title: Italian unification completed
tokens.description: The capture of Rome on 20 September 1870 by the Royal Italian Army ended the Papal States. Rome became capital of unified Italy in 1871, completing the Risorgimento.
tokens.image_credit: pic: Ludovico Tuminello scan: Carlomorino · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Crimean War
tokens.title: Russia and Ottoman Empire at war
tokens.description: The Crimean War was fought from October 1853 to February 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, the United Kingdom and Sardinia. Its causes included the Eastern question and Russia's claim to protect the Ottoman Empire's Orthodox subjects.
tokens.image_credit: William Simpson, artist (1823-1899) E[dmond]. Morin, lithographer (1824 - 1882), working for "Day & Son, lithrs. to the Queen" Published by: Paul & Dominic Colnaghi & Co., 13 & 14 Pall Mall East, publ · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Opening of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway
tokens.title: First intercity passenger railway
tokens.description: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened on 15 September 1830, linking Liverpool and Manchester 35 miles apart. It was the first locomotive-hauled railway to connect two major cities and the first to offer a scheduled passenger service.
tokens.image_credit: I Shaw, Junior · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stockton and Darlington Railway
tokens.title: First public steam railway
tokens.description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway was officially opened on 27 September 1825 in north-east England. It was the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives, and was later extended to a new port at Middlesbrough.
tokens.image_credit: John Dobbin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Spike at Promontory
tokens.title: Transcontinental Railroad completed
tokens.description: The golden spike ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah Territory, on 10 May 1869 marked the completion of the first transcontinental railroad across the United States. Leland Stanford drove the ceremonial spike linking the Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Hill · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1889 Exposition Universelle
tokens.title: World's fair debuts the Eiffel Tower
tokens.description: The Exposition Universelle of 1889 was a world's fair held in Paris from 6 May to 31 October 1889. It was the fifth of ten major expositions held in the city between 1855 and 1937 and drew more than thirty-two million visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Louis Béroud · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Centennial Exposition
tokens.title: First official US world's fair
tokens.description: The Centennial International Exhibition was held in Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, from 10 May to 10 November 1876. It was the first official world's fair held in the United States and marked the centennial of the Declaration of Independence.
tokens.image_credit: James D. McCabe · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: World's Columbian Exposition
tokens.title: Chicago's White City
tokens.description: The World's Columbian Exposition was a world's fair held in Chicago from May 1 to October 30, 1893, in Jackson Park. It marked the 400th anniversary of Columbus's arrival in the New World.
tokens.image_credit: C. D. Arnold (1844-1927); H. D. Higinbotham · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expo 67
tokens.title: Montreal world's fair
tokens.description: Expo 67 was a world's fair held in Montreal from April 28 to October 29, 1967, with 62 nations participating. It is considered one of the most successful world's fairs of the 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: Philipp Hienstorfer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expo 2010
tokens.title: Largest world exposition ever
tokens.description: Expo 2010 was a World Expo held on both banks of the Huangpu River in Shanghai from 1 May to 31 October 2010. It had the theme Better City, Better Life.
tokens.image_credit: 凌智 (Suzuki) · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expo '70
tokens.title: Osaka fair and the Tower of the Sun
tokens.description: Expo '70 was a world's fair held in Suita, Osaka Prefecture, Japan, from 15 March to 13 September 1970. It was the first world's fair held in Japan and in Asia.
tokens.image_credit: takato marui · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1939 New York World's Fair
tokens.title: World of Tomorrow
tokens.description: The 1939 New York World's Fair was an international exposition held at Flushing Meadows-Corona Park in Queens, New York City. About 45 million people attended across two seasons in 1939 and 1940.
tokens.image_credit: Daily Worker · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Century 21 Exposition
tokens.title: Space Needle debuts
tokens.description: The Century 21 Exposition, also known as the Seattle World's Fair, was held in Seattle, Washington, from 21 April to 21 October 1962. Nearly 10 million people attended.
tokens.image_credit: Seattle Municipal Archives from Seattle, WA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish flu
tokens.title: First recorded cases at Fort Riley
tokens.description: The Spanish flu was a 1918 to 1920 H1N1 influenza pandemic that infected an estimated 500 million people, nearly a third of the world's population. The first documented cases among U.S. soldiers were at Camp Funston, Fort Riley, Kansas, in March 1918.
tokens.image_credit: Otis Historical Archives, National Museum of Health and Medicine · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: COVID-19 pandemic
tokens.title: Outbreak first identified in Wuhan
tokens.description: The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. The World Health Organization assessed it as a pandemic on 11 March 2020.
tokens.image_credit: Gustavo Basso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Western African Ebola epidemic
tokens.title: Largest Ebola outbreak on record
tokens.description: The 2013-2016 Ebola epidemic centred in West Africa was the most widespread outbreak of the disease in history. It began in Guinea in December 2013 and mainly affected Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.
tokens.image_credit: CDC Global · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1854 Broad Street cholera outbreak
tokens.title: John Snow removes the pump handle
tokens.description: A severe cholera outbreak in 1854 around Broad Street in Soho, London, killed about 420 people. John Snow's study of it showed that contaminated water, not miasma, spread the disease.
tokens.image_credit: Jamzze · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plague of Justinian
tokens.title: First great pandemic of plague
tokens.description: The Plague of Justinian (AD 541 to 549) was an epidemic of plague that struck the Mediterranean Basin, Europe and the Near East. It killed about a fifth of the population of Constantinople, the Byzantine capital.

tokens.name: Last natural smallpox case
tokens.title: Smallpox ends in Somalia
tokens.description: Ali Maow Maalin, a hospital cook from Merca, Somalia, was diagnosed in October 1977 with the last known naturally occurring case of smallpox. He recovered, and a containment campaign prevented any outbreak.

tokens.name: First smallpox vaccination
tokens.title: Jenner inoculates James Phipps
tokens.description: In May 1796 Edward Jenner, a physician from Berkeley in Gloucestershire, inoculated the boy James Phipps with cowpox material. The procedure laid the foundation of vaccination against smallpox.

tokens.name: Discovery of insulin
tokens.title: Banting and Best in Toronto
tokens.description: In 1921 Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolated insulin at the University of Toronto, in the laboratory of John Macleod. The discovery led to insulin treatment for diabetes and the 1923 Nobel Prize.

tokens.name: First human heart transplant
tokens.title: Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town
tokens.description: On 3 December 1967 surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first human-to-human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town. The recipient, Louis Washkansky, survived for 18 days.

tokens.name: Birth of Louise Brown
tokens.title: First IVF baby born
tokens.description: Louise Brown was born on 25 July 1978 at Oldham General Hospital in England. She was the first human born after conception by in vitro fertilisation (IVF), a procedure pioneered in Britain.

tokens.name: Human Genome Project completed
tokens.title: Sequence of human DNA published
tokens.description: The Human Genome Project was an international research project to determine and map the base pairs of human DNA. It started in 1990 and was completed in 2003.

tokens.name: Higgs boson discovery
tokens.title: CERN announces the particle
tokens.description: The Higgs boson is an elementary particle of the Standard Model, produced by the excitation of the Higgs field. Its discovery was announced at CERN near Geneva in July 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Lucas Taylor / CERN · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: World Wide Web invented
tokens.title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes it at CERN
tokens.description: The World Wide Web is a global information system for sharing content over the Internet using HTTP. Tim Berners-Lee invented it at CERN in 1989, and it was opened to the public in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Arnold · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First ARPANET message
tokens.title: "LO" sent from UCLA
tokens.description: ARPANET was the first wide-area packet-switched network and an early base of the Internet, using the TCP/IP suite. Its first message, LO, was sent from UCLA in October 1969.

tokens.name: ENIAC unveiled
tokens.title: First general-purpose electronic computer
tokens.description: ENIAC was the first programmable, electronic, general-purpose digital computer, completed in 1945 at the University of Pennsylvania. It was publicly unveiled in Philadelphia in February 1946.
tokens.image_credit: Unidentified U.S. Army photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
tokens.title: Computer defeats the world chess champion
tokens.description: Deep Blue, an IBM supercomputer, won the 1997 rematch against world chess champion Garry Kasparov in New York City. It was the first defeat of a reigning world champion by a computer under tournament conditions.

tokens.name: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
tokens.title: AI wins at Go in Seoul
tokens.description: AlphaGo, a Go program by DeepMind, won four of five games against Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul in March 2016. The match is widely compared with the 1997 Deep Blue chess match.

tokens.name: Dartmouth workshop
tokens.title: Artificial intelligence named
tokens.description: The Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence was a 1956 summer workshop at Dartmouth College in Hanover, New Hampshire. It is widely regarded as the founding event of artificial intelligence as a field.

tokens.name: iPhone unveiled
tokens.title: Steve Jobs presents at Macworld
tokens.description: Apple introduced the first iPhone at Macworld in San Francisco on January 9, 2007. The smartphone was released in the United States on June 29, 2007.
tokens.image_credit: ArnoldReinhold · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mt. Gox collapse
tokens.title: Largest Bitcoin exchange fails
tokens.description: Mt. Gox was a bitcoin exchange based in Shibuya, Tokyo, that handled over 70% of bitcoin transactions worldwide by early 2014. It ceased operations abruptly in 2014 after the loss or theft of hundreds of thousands of bitcoin.

tokens.name: Lehman Brothers collapse
tokens.title: Largest bankruptcy in US history
tokens.description: Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 15, 2008, in New York City. It remains the largest bankruptcy filing in US history and triggered a global financial shock.
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black Monday 1987
tokens.title: Dow falls 22 per cent in a day
tokens.description: Black Monday was a global stock market crash on October 19, 1987, with worldwide losses estimated at US$1.71 trillion. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell about 22 per cent in a single day.

tokens.name: Black Wednesday
tokens.title: Pound forced out of the ERM
tokens.description: Black Wednesday, on 16 September 1992, was the day the UK government was forced to withdraw sterling from the European Exchange Rate Mechanism. The crisis damaged the credibility of the second Major ministry.

tokens.name: Collapse of Barings Bank
tokens.title: Rogue trader sinks a 233-year-old bank
tokens.description: Barings Bank, a London merchant bank founded in 1762, collapsed in 1995 after heavy losses from unauthorised trading by one employee, Nick Leeson, in Singapore. It was one of the oldest banks in England.

tokens.name: Tulip mania
tokens.title: Early speculative bubble in Amsterdam
tokens.description: Tulip mania was a period in the Dutch Golden Age when contract prices of some tulip bulbs reached extraordinary levels from 1634. The bubble collapsed in February 1637 and is generally considered the first recorded speculative bubble.
tokens.image_credit: Hendrik Gerritsz Pot · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: South Sea Bubble
tokens.title: Share bubble bursts in London
tokens.description: The South Sea Bubble was a speculative bubble in London in 1720, when shares of the South Sea Company rose sharply and then collapsed. Many investors were ruined, and the episode became a classic example of a financial bubble.
tokens.image_credit: Edward Matthew Ward · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1997 Asian financial crisis
tokens.title: Baht floated, crisis spreads
tokens.description: The 1997 Asian financial crisis began in Thailand in July 1997 and spread across East and Southeast Asia. It raised fears of a wider global meltdown, but the recovery in 1998 and 1999 was rapid.

tokens.name: Argentine great depression
tokens.title: Corralito and the "que se vayan todos"
tokens.description: The Argentine great depression was an economic depression that began in 1998 and lasted until 2002. It brought mass unemployment, riots, the fall of the government, a default on foreign debt and the end of the peso's fixed link to the US dollar.
tokens.image_credit: Taken by the uploader, w:es:Usuario:Barcex · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hyperinflation in Zimbabwe
tokens.title: Hundred-trillion-dollar banknotes
tokens.description: Zimbabwe's economy underwent hyperinflation from February 2007, peaking in November 2008 at an estimated 790.6 billion percent month-on-month. The government stopped publishing official inflation statistics during the peak.
tokens.image_credit: en:User:Discott · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
tokens.title: Currency collapses to trillions of marks
tokens.description: Hyperinflation affected the German Papiermark, the currency of the Weimar Republic, between 1921 and 1923, peaking in 1923. It was driven by wartime borrowing and by reparations payments under the 1921 London Schedule of Payments.
tokens.image_credit: Bain News Service, publisher · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Buttonwood Agreement
tokens.title: Brokers start Wall Street trading
tokens.description: The Buttonwood Agreement was signed on 17 May 1792 by 24 stockbrokers outside 68 Wall Street in New York City. It organized securities trading and is the founding document of the New York Stock Exchange.
tokens.image_credit: Gottscho-Schleisner, Inc. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nixon shock
tokens.title: Dollar decoupled from gold
tokens.description: The Nixon shock was a set of economic measures announced by US President Richard Nixon on 15 August 1971, including wage and price freezes, import surcharges and the end of the dollar's convertibility into gold. It effectively ended the Bretton Woods system.

tokens.name: 1973 oil crisis
tokens.title: OPEC embargo shocks the West
tokens.description: In October 1973 the Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries announced an oil embargo against countries that had supported Israel in the Yom Kippur War. Canada, Japan, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States were the first targets.
tokens.image_credit: David Falconer, Photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spindletop gusher
tokens.title: Texas oil boom begins
tokens.description: The Lucas gusher struck oil at Spindletop near Beaumont, Texas, on 10 January 1901. The strike opened the Texas oil boom and the modern American oil industry.
tokens.image_credit: Note: Image is available at [1] on the Paleontological Research Institution web site. The site credits the American Petroleum Institute; however, a Texas roadside historical marker credits John Trost  · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Drake Well
tokens.title: First commercial oil well in the US
tokens.description: The Drake Well, drilled by Edwin Drake in 1859 along Oil Creek, was the first commercial oil well in the United States. It sparked the first American oil boom and stands in Cherrytree Township, Pennsylvania.
tokens.image_credit: Niagara · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dammam No. 7
tokens.title: Oil found in Saudi Arabia
tokens.description: Dammam No. 7, also called the Prosperity Well, is an oil well in Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Commercial quantities of oil were first found there on 3 March 1938, the start of the country's oil industry.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1953 Iranian coup
tokens.title: Mosaddegh overthrown
tokens.description: On 19 August 1953 a coup d'etat overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh and strengthened the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. The United Kingdom (MI6) and the United States (CIA) instigated it, partly to protect British oil interests after the 1951 nationalisation.
tokens.image_credit: William Arthur Cram · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
tokens.title: Qajar Iran gets a parliament
tokens.description: The Persian Constitutional Revolution took place between 1905 and 1911 during the Qajar era. It led to the establishment of a parliament in Iran, the first such movement in the Islamic world.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iran-Iraq War
tokens.title: Eight-year conflict
tokens.description: The Iran-Iraq War began with the Iraqi invasion of Iran in September 1980. After eight years of conflict, a UN-brokered ceasefire took effect in August 1988, with around 500,000 deaths.
tokens.image_credit: Mhsheikholeslami · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Halabja massacre
tokens.title: Chemical weapons used on a Kurdish town
tokens.description: The Halabja massacre took place on 16 March 1988, when a large Iraqi chemical attack killed thousands of Kurds in Halabja, Iraqi Kurdistan. It was carried out during the Anfal campaign.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Jones, Ph.D. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
tokens.title: Gulf War is triggered
tokens.description: The Iraqi invasion of Kuwait began on 2 August 1990 and marked the start of the Gulf War. Iraq occupied Kuwait for the next seven months, and the UN Security Council condemned the invasion.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Mosque seizure
tokens.title: Armed group seizes the Masjid al-Haram
tokens.description: Up to 600 militants led by Juhayman al-Otaybi seized the Grand Mosque of Mecca from 20 November to 4 December 1979. Saudi forces retook the complex, the holiest site in Islam, after a two-week siege.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Not cited. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lebanese Civil War
tokens.title: Ain el-Rummaneh bus incident
tokens.description: The Lebanese Civil War was a multifaceted armed conflict fought in Lebanon from 1975 to 1990. It killed an estimated 120,000 people and displaced nearly one million.
tokens.image_credit: James Case from Philadelphia, Mississippi, U.S.A. · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2020 Beirut explosion
tokens.title: Ammonium nitrate blast at the port
tokens.description: On 4 August 2020, 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate detonated in the Port of Beirut. The blast killed at least 218 people and injured about 7,000.
tokens.image_credit: Freimut Bahlo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cedar Revolution
tokens.title: Protests after the Hariri assassination
tokens.description: The Cedar Revolution was a chain of largely peaceful demonstrations in Beirut and across Lebanon after the assassination of former prime minister Rafic Hariri. The protesters demanded the withdrawal of Syrian troops that had occupied Lebanon since 1976.
tokens.image_credit: Elie Ghobeira · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Syrian civil war
tokens.title: Protests in Daraa lead to war
tokens.description: The Syrian civil war began with the Syrian revolution in March 2011, when protests against the Assad regime spread across Syria. The conflict lasted almost 14 years and ended with the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024.
tokens.image_credit: Voice of America News: Scott Bobb reports from Aleppo, Syria · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Aleppo
tokens.title: Divided city fights for four years
tokens.description: The Battle of Aleppo was a major confrontation in Aleppo between Syrian opposition militias and the Syrian government forces, which began on 19 July 2012. The stalemate ended in July 2016 when government troops closed the rebels' last supply line into the city.

tokens.name: Ghouta chemical attack
tokens.title: Sarin used outside Damascus
tokens.description: The Ghouta chemical attack was carried out by Syrian government forces in the early hours of 21 August 2013. Sarin rockets struck opposition-held suburbs of Damascus, the deadliest use of chemical weapons in the Syrian conflict.

tokens.name: Siege of Kobanî
tokens.title: Kurdish forces hold the Syrian border town
tokens.description: Islamic State forces launched the siege of Kobanî, the main city of the Kurdish-led Kobanî Canton in northern Syria, on 13 September 2014. By January 2015 about 400,000 Kurdish refugees had fled into Turkey.

tokens.name: Yazidi genocide
tokens.title: Attack on Sinjar
tokens.description: The Yazidi genocide was carried out by the Islamic State between 2014 and 2017, with massacres, genocidal rape and forced conversions. Sinjar, the Yazidi homeland in northern Iraq, was the main site of the attacks.
tokens.image_credit: Levi Clancy · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of the Assad regime
tokens.title: Opposition forces enter Damascus
tokens.description: On 8 December 2024 the Assad regime collapsed during an offensive by opposition forces led by HTS, the SNA and the Southern Operations Room. The capture of Damascus ended the Assad family's rule over Syria.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.image_credit: Voice of America · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: October 7 attacks
tokens.title: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel
tokens.description: On 7 October 2023 Hamas and other Palestinian militant groups launched coordinated attacks from the Gaza Strip into southern Israel. Israel responded with a major military operation in Gaza.
tokens.image_credit: Yoav Keren · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip
tokens.title: Settlements evacuated
tokens.description: In 2005 Israel withdrew its ground forces from the Gaza Strip and evacuated the 21 settlements it had built there. Israel kept control of Gaza's airspace, territorial waters and most crossings.
tokens.image_credit: Israel Defense Forces · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Intifada
tokens.title: Palestinian uprising begins in Gaza
tokens.description: The First Intifada was a Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, from December 1987 until the Madrid Conference of 1991. It combined mass protests, civil disobedience, riots and attacks.
tokens.image_credit: Efi Sharir · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Second Intifada
tokens.title: Uprising follows Sharon's Temple Mount visit
tokens.description: The Second Intifada was a major Palestinian uprising against Israel and its occupation that began in 2000 and spread across Israel, the West Bank and Gaza. It ended with the Sharm el-Sheikh Summit of 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Nadav Ganot (נדב גנות) / Israel Defense Forces · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sabra and Shatila massacre
tokens.title: Killings in Beirut camps
tokens.description: From 16 to 18 September 1982, an estimated 1,300 to 3,500 civilians were killed in Beirut's Sabra district and the Shatila refugee camp. The Lebanese Forces militia carried out the killings with Israel Defense Forces support.

tokens.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
tokens.title: Neighbouring armies enter Palestine
tokens.description: The 1948 Arab-Israeli War ran from 15 May 1948 to 10 March 1949, after Israel's declaration of independence and the entry of Arab states into Mandatory Palestine. It formally ended with the 1949 Armistice Agreements, which established the Green Line.

tokens.name: Operation Opera
tokens.title: Israel destroys Osirak reactor
tokens.description: Operation Opera was an Israeli Air Force airstrike on 7 June 1981 that destroyed an unfinished Iraqi nuclear reactor near Baghdad. The strike established the Begin Doctrine, which called it a precedent for future Israeli governments.

tokens.name: Eichmann trial
tokens.title: Nazi organiser tried in Jerusalem
tokens.description: The Eichmann trial was held in Jerusalem in 1961 against Nazi official Adolf Eichmann, captured in Argentina by Israeli agents. Eichmann was convicted and executed in 1962 for his role in organising deportations in the Holocaust.
tokens.image_credit: Israeli GPO photographer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Adolf Eichmann's capture
tokens.title: Mossad agents seize him in Buenos Aires
tokens.description: Operation Finale was a May 1960 Mossad operation that seized Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann in San Fernando, Buenos Aires. Agents flew him secretly to Israel, where he was tried in 1961.

tokens.name: King David Hotel bombing
tokens.title: Irgun bombs British headquarters
tokens.description: The King David Hotel bombing was a 22 July 1946 attack by the Irgun on the British administrative headquarters of Mandatory Palestine in Jerusalem. The explosion killed 91 people.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Balfour Declaration
