tokens.title: British support for a Jewish national home
tokens.description: The Balfour Declaration was a letter of 2 November 1917 from British Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour to Lord Rothschild. It stated the British government's support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
tokens.image_credit: United Kingdom Government signed by Arthur Balfour · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sykes-Picot Agreement
tokens.title: Secret plan to divide the Ottoman Middle East
tokens.description: The Sykes-Picot Agreement was a 1916 secret treaty between the United Kingdom and France, with assent from Russia and Italy, defining spheres of influence in the Ottoman Empire. Negotiators Mark Sykes and François Georges-Picot initialled it in January 1916.

tokens.name: Arab Revolt
tokens.title: Sharif Hussein rises against the Ottomans
tokens.description: The Arab Revolt was an uprising by Hejaz Arabs under Sharif Hussein against the Ottoman Empire during the First World War. It was officially launched at Mecca on 10 June 1916 with British military backing.
tokens.image_credit: Maurice Bauche (1878–1956) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Aqaba
tokens.title: Lawrence and Arab forces take the port
tokens.description: The Battle of Aqaba was fought on 6 July 1917 for the Red Sea port of Aqaba, then held by the Ottoman Empire. Arab forces led by Sherif Nasir and Auda abu Tayi, advised by T. E. Lawrence, won the battle.

tokens.name: Battle of Megiddo 1918
tokens.title: Allenby's cavalry sweep Palestine
tokens.description: The Battle of Megiddo was fought from 19 to 25 September 1918 on the Plain of Sharon and nearby areas. It was the final Allied offensive of the Sinai and Palestine Campaign of World War I.
tokens.image_credit: George Westmoreland · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Noche Triste
tokens.title: Cortés flees Tenochtitlan
tokens.description: La Noche Triste was the episode in the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire when Hernan Cortes and his army were driven out of the Mexica capital Tenochtitlan. It is a key setback of the conquest.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Otumba
tokens.title: Spanish defeat Aztec army
tokens.description: The Battle of Otumba was fought on 7 July 1520 on the plain of Temalcatitlan near modern Otumba. The Spanish under Hernan Cortes defeated the Aztec army, allowing Cortes to reorganise after the retreat from Tenochtitlan.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
tokens.title: Three-month siege of the Aztec capital
tokens.description: The fall of Tenochtitlan, capital of the Mexica, took place in 1521 in the Spanish conquest of Mexico. Hernan Cortes and his Tlaxcaltec allies took the Aztec capital after extensive negotiations and fighting.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caste War of Yucatán
tokens.title: Maya uprising lasts half a century
tokens.description: The Caste War of Yucatan was a revolt of Indigenous Maya people against the Yucatecan elite, which began in 1847. It is considered one of the most successful modern Native American revolts and lasted into the 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: Inri · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cristero War
tokens.title: Catholic revolt against the state
tokens.description: The Cristero War was a rebellion in central and western Mexico from 3 August 1926 to 21 June 1929. Catholic rebels opposed the anticlerical articles of the 1917 Constitution and the Calles Law enforcing them.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pancho Villa Expedition
tokens.title: Villa attacks US border town
tokens.description: The Pancho Villa Expedition was a United States Army operation against Mexican revolutionary Francisco Villa from 14 March 1916 to 7 February 1917. It was launched after Villa's raid on Columbus, New Mexico.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zimmermann telegram
tokens.title: German proposal to Mexico intercepted
tokens.description: The Zimmermann telegram was a secret message issued by the German Foreign Office on 17 January 1917. It proposed a military alliance between the German Empire and Mexico if the United States entered World War I, and British intelligence intercepted it.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mexican-American War
tokens.title: Thornton Affair on the Rio Grande
tokens.description: The Mexican-American War was fought from 1846 to 1848 after the United States annexed Texas, and the first clash came on the Rio Grande. Under the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, Mexico ceded about half of its territory.
tokens.image_credit: Adolphe Jean-Baptiste Bayot / Carl Nebel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Veracruz
tokens.title: Scott's amphibious landing
tokens.description: On 9 March 1847 United States forces made an amphibious landing and besieged the Mexican seaport of Veracruz during the Mexican-American War. The port surrendered twenty days later, and the US army then marched inland to Mexico City.
tokens.image_credit: Adolphe Jean-Baptiste Bayot / After Carl Nebel · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
tokens.title: Mexico cedes half its territory
tokens.description: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed on 2 February 1848 in Villa de Guadalupe Hidalgo, now part of Mexico City, and ended the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded about half of its territory to the United States.

tokens.name: Alaska Purchase
tokens.title: US buys Alaska from Russia
tokens.description: The Alaska Purchase transferred Russian America to the United States for $7.2 million in 1867. The treaty was signed on 30 March 1867 and American sovereignty over the territory took effect on 18 October 1867.
tokens.image_credit: Emanuel Leutze · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Canadian Confederation
tokens.title: Dominion of Canada formed
tokens.description: Canadian Confederation united the Province of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into one federation, the Dominion of Canada, on 1 July 1867. It was enacted through the British North America Act, 1867, based on resolutions from the Quebec and London conferences.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Vimy Ridge
tokens.title: Canadian Corps takes the ridge
tokens.description: The Battle of Vimy Ridge was fought from 9 to 12 April 1917 near Arras in the Pas-de-Calais, France, during the First World War. The four divisions of the Canadian Corps attacked three divisions of the German 6th Army to take the ridge.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Jack · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dieppe Raid
tokens.title: Costly Allied raid on a French port
tokens.description: The Dieppe Raid, also called Operation Jubilee, was an Allied amphibious attack on 19 August 1942 on the German-occupied port of Dieppe in northern France. Over 6,050 infantry, mostly Canadian, were landed by a Royal Navy task force.
tokens.image_credit: Jörgensen · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: October Crisis
tokens.title: FLQ kidnappings in Quebec
tokens.description: The October Crisis began in October 1970, when the Front de libération du Québec kidnapped Quebec Labour Minister Pierre Laporte and British diplomat James Cross in Montreal. Trudeau invoked the War Measures Act, and Laporte was later killed.
tokens.image_credit: Jimderkaisser · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oka Crisis
tokens.title: Mohawk standoff in Quebec
tokens.description: The Oka Crisis was a 78-day land dispute in 1990 between Mohawk people and the town of Oka, Quebec, over a golf course planned on a burial ground. It was the first well-publicized violent conflict between First Nations and a provincial government in the late 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: SamuelFreli · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red River Rebellion
tokens.title: Métis led by Louis Riel resist annexation
tokens.description: The Red River Rebellion was the 1869 to 1870 uprising led by Louis Riel, which produced a Metis provisional government at the Red River Colony. It was the first crisis the new federal government faced after Canadian Confederation in 1867.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author, believed to be Joseph Langevin.[3][4] · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: North-West Rebellion
tokens.title: Batoche and Riel's last stand
tokens.description: The North-West Rebellion was an 1885 armed uprising of Metis under Louis Riel, with Cree and Assiniboine allies, against the Canadian government in the District of Saskatchewan. It ended with the Battle of Batoche.
tokens.image_credit: Seargent Grundy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Summit Series 1972
tokens.title: Canada versus USSR hockey
tokens.description: The Summit Series was an eight-game ice hockey series between Canada's Team Canada of NHL professionals and the Soviet Union national team, held in September 1972. Canada won the series four games to three with a late winning goal in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: Spudgun67 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Terry Fox's Marathon of Hope
tokens.title: Cross-country run begins in St. John's
tokens.description: Terry Fox began his Marathon of Hope, a cross-Canada run to raise money for cancer research, at St. John's, Newfoundland, on 12 April 1980. A bronze statue of him marks the start at Mile 0.
tokens.image_credit: Gordon Leggett · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: École Polytechnique massacre
tokens.title: Attack at École Polytechnique
tokens.description: The École Polytechnique massacre was a mass shooting on 6 December 1989 at the École Polytechnique de Montréal, in which fourteen women were killed. It is also known as the Montreal massacre.
tokens.image_credit: Rémi St-Onge, Moment Factory · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1995 Quebec referendum
tokens.title: Sovereignty rejected by a hair
tokens.description: The 1995 Quebec referendum asked voters whether Quebec should become sovereign, with an offer of partnership with Canada. The No side won 50.58 per cent to 49.42 per cent on 30 October 1995.

tokens.name: Franklin's lost expedition
tokens.title: Arctic expedition vanishes
tokens.description: Franklin's lost expedition was a British Arctic voyage led by John Franklin in 1845 aboard HMS Erebus and HMS Terror. Both ships were trapped in the ice near King William Island, and all 129 men died.
tokens.image_credit: Illustrated London News - Getty · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
tokens.title: Norwegian team wins the race
tokens.description: Roald Amundsen and four companions reached the geographic South Pole on 14 December 1911, five weeks ahead of Scott's British party. The first expedition to reach the pole was Norwegian.
tokens.image_credit: Olav Bjaaland (1863-1961)[1] · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition
tokens.title: Ship crushed by pack ice
tokens.description: The Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition of 1914 to 1917, led by Ernest Shackleton, aimed to cross the Antarctic continent. Its ship Endurance was crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea in 1915.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Hurley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Norge flight over the North Pole
tokens.title: Amundsen's airship crosses the Arctic
tokens.description: The airship Norge, piloted by Umberto Nobile, flew over the North Pole from 11 to 14 May 1926 on the Amundsen and Ellsworth transpolar flight. It was the first verified trip to the North Pole and started from Ny-Ålesund in Svalbard.
tokens.image_credit: Bain News Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Italia airship crash
tokens.title: Nobile expedition wrecked on the ice
tokens.description: The airship Italia crashed on the pack ice northeast of Nordaustlandet, Svalbard, in May 1928 on its return from the North Pole. Seventeen people died in the wreck and the rescue attempts.
tokens.image_credit: Sparrow (麻雀) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kon-Tiki expedition
tokens.title: Raft crosses the Pacific
tokens.description: The Kon-Tiki expedition was a 1947 raft voyage across the Pacific Ocean from South America to the Polynesian islands, led by Thor Heyerdahl. The raft left Callao, Peru, and ended on Raroia atoll in the Tuamotus.
tokens.image_credit: Nasjonalbiblioteket from Norway · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trieste dives to Challenger Deep
tokens.title: Deepest point of the ocean reached
tokens.description: In 1960 the bathyscaphe Trieste became the first crewed vessel to reach the bottom of the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench. The dive was the final goal of Project Nekton, run from Guam.

tokens.name: Cameron's Challenger Deep dive
tokens.title: Solo descent to the Mariana Trench floor
tokens.description: On 26 March 2012 film director James Cameron piloted the Deepsea Challenger submersible alone to the bottom of the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point on Earth. The craft was launched from Apra Harbor in Guam.
tokens.image_credit: Z22 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens
tokens.title: Largest landslide in recorded history
tokens.description: On 18 May 1980 Mount St. Helens in Skamania County, Washington, erupted explosively with a volcanic explosivity index of 5. It was the first such eruption in the contiguous United States since the 1915 eruption of Lassen Peak.
tokens.image_credit: Donald A. Swanson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 eruptions of Eyjafjallajökull
tokens.title: Ash cloud grounds European flights
tokens.description: Between March and June 2010 a series of eruptions at Eyjafjallajökull in Iceland sent ash over Western Europe. The ash disrupted air travel across the region for several days in April 2010.
tokens.image_credit: Árni Friðriksson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Laki eruption
tokens.title: Fissure eruption poisons Europe
tokens.description: The Laki eruption came from Lakagígar, a volcanic fissure in western Vatnajökull National Park in Iceland. The fissure is part of a volcanic system centred on the Grímsvötn volcano.
tokens.image_credit: Chmee2/Valtameri · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Birth of Surtsey
tokens.title: New island rises from the Atlantic
tokens.description: Surtsey is an uninhabited volcanic island in the Vestmannaeyjar archipelago off southern Iceland. Its eruption began 130 metres below sea level and the new island reached the surface on 14 November 1963.
tokens.image_credit: CanonS2 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eldfell eruption
tokens.title: Heimaey evacuated overnight
tokens.description: The eruption began on 23 January 1973 on Heimaey in the Westman Islands, Iceland. Lava forced the evacuation of the whole population and destroyed part of the town, while seawater cooling saved the harbour.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1991 Unzen eruption
tokens.title: Pyroclastic flow kills volcanologists
tokens.description: A pyroclastic flow from Mount Unzen in Japan on 3 June 1991 killed 43 people, including three volcanologists. Among the dead were the French volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Fwng3431 assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2014 Mount Ontake eruption
tokens.title: Sudden eruption catches hikers
tokens.description: The eruption of Mount Ontake on Honshu, Japan, on 27 September 2014 killed 63 people. It was the first fatal volcanic eruption in Japan since Unzen in 1991 and the deadliest since 1902.
tokens.image_credit: Alpsdake · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Merapi eruption
tokens.title: Java volcano forces mass evacuation
tokens.description: A series of violent eruptions of Mount Merapi, on the border of Central Java and Yogyakarta, began in late October 2010 and continued into November. Pyroclastic flows ran down its heavily populated slopes.
tokens.image_credit: Crisco 1492 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Samalas eruption
tokens.title: Massive eruption of 1257
tokens.description: The 1257 eruption of Samalas on Lombok, Indonesia, had a probable Volcanic Explosivity Index of 7 and is among the largest Holocene eruptions. It left the caldera that now holds Lake Segara Anak.
tokens.image_credit: Petter Lindgren · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Toba supereruption
tokens.title: Possible bottleneck for early humans
tokens.description: The Toba eruption, about 74,000 years ago, had an estimated volcanic explosivity index of 8, the largest known explosive eruption of the Quaternary. It formed the caldera now occupied by Lake Toba in Sumatra, Indonesia.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY date

tokens.name: Minoan eruption
tokens.title: Santorini erupts
tokens.description: The Minoan eruption, circa 1600 BC, devastated the Aegean island of Thera (Santorini) and destroyed the Minoan settlement at Akrotiri. With a VEI of 7, it was one of the largest volcanic events in human history.

tokens.name: 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption
tokens.title: Shock wave circles the globe
tokens.description: The eruption of the submarine volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai began in December 2021 and reached its climax on 15 January 2022. The volcano lies about 65 km north of Tongatapu, Tonga's main island.

tokens.name: 1964 Alaska earthquake
tokens.title: Strongest earthquake in US history
tokens.description: The 1964 Alaska earthquake, also called the Good Friday earthquake, struck south-central Alaska on 27 March 1964. Rated magnitude 9.2 to 9.3, it is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded in North America.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Army · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kobe earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 6.9 hits Hyōgo
tokens.description: The Kobe earthquake struck southern Hyogo Prefecture, Japan, on 17 January 1995. It measured 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale and reached intensity 7 on the JMA scale.
tokens.image_credit: Akiyoshi Matsuoka (松岡明芳) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1970 Ancash earthquake
tokens.title: Landslide buries Yungay
tokens.description: The 1970 Ancash earthquake struck off the coast of Peru on 31 May 1970. The resulting landslide buried Yungay and is considered the world's deadliest avalanche, with an estimated 66,794 to 70,000 deaths.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Geological Survey · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1999 İzmit earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.6 strikes northwest Turkey
tokens.description: A moment magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck Kocaeli Province, Turkey, on 17 August 1999. Official figures give at least 18,373 deaths and 48,901 injured, with 155 deaths linked to the tsunami.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquakes
tokens.title: Twin earthquakes devastate the border region
tokens.description: Two earthquakes struck southern and central Turkey and northern and western Syria on 6 February 2023. The first measured moment magnitude 7.8, with its epicentre about 37 km west-northwest of Gaziantep.
tokens.image_credit: Mahmut Bozarslan (VOA)/VOA TURKICE · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2001 Gujarat earthquake
tokens.title: Republic Day earthquake
tokens.description: A moment magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck India and Pakistan on 26 January 2001, with its epicentre near Chobari in Kutch district, Gujarat. It had a maximum Mercalli intensity of XII (Extreme).
tokens.image_credit: Nizil Shah · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2005 Kashmir earthquake
tokens.title: Magnitude 7.6 in the Himalayas
tokens.description: A Mw 7.6 earthquake struck Azad Kashmir in northern Pakistan on 8 October 2005. Its epicentre was in the Patikka tehsil near Muzaffarabad, and tens of thousands died across Kashmir.
tokens.image_credit: Gregory Takats/AusAID · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2003 Bam earthquake
tokens.title: Ancient citadel destroyed
tokens.description: A Mw 6.6 strike-slip earthquake struck Kerman province, Iran, on 26 December 2003. It was especially destructive in Bam and Baravat, with about 34,000 deaths officially reported.
tokens.image_credit: Mojtaba Takin · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1908 Messina earthquake
tokens.title: Earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina
tokens.description: The 1908 Messina earthquake struck Sicily and Calabria on 28 December 1908, with its epicentre in the Strait of Messina. Messina and Reggio Calabria were nearly destroyed and around 120,000 people died.
tokens.image_credit: Wilhelm von Gloeden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1693 Sicily earthquake
tokens.title: Val di Noto rebuilt in baroque style
tokens.description: The 1693 Sicily earthquake struck parts of southern Italy near Sicily on 11 January 1693, with an estimated magnitude of 7.4. It destroyed at least 70 towns and killed about 60,000 people.

tokens.name: 2009 L'Aquila earthquake
tokens.title: Medieval city damaged
tokens.description: The 2009 L'Aquila earthquake struck the Abruzzo region of southern Italy on 6 April 2009, measuring 6.3 on the moment magnitude scale. Its epicentre near L'Aquila, the regional capital, caused the most damage.
tokens.image_credit: Original uploader was TheWiz83 at it.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1556 Shaanxi earthquake
tokens.title: Deadliest earthquake in history
tokens.description: The 1556 Shaanxi earthquake struck Huaxian in Shaanxi, China, on 23 January 1556 during the Ming dynasty. It is among the deadliest earthquakes in history, with modern estimates of roughly 100,000 direct deaths.

tokens.name: Great storm of 1703
tokens.title: Hurricane-force winds across southern England
tokens.description: The Great storm of 1703 was a destructive extratropical cyclone that struck south Wales and southern England on 26 November 1703. High winds collapsed about 2,000 chimney stacks in London, and over 1,000 seamen died on the Goodwin Sands alone.
tokens.image_credit: William Rayner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: North Sea flood of 1953
tokens.title: Dikes fail in the Netherlands
tokens.description: The North Sea flood of 1953 was caused by a storm surge that struck the low-lying coasts of the Netherlands, Belgium and the United Kingdom. More than 2,000 people were killed on land, and it was the worst Dutch flood disaster since the Middle Ages.
tokens.image_credit: Agency for International Development · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Smog of London
tokens.title: Four days of deadly pollution
tokens.description: The Great Smog was a severe air pollution event that affected London in December 1952. Cold, windless weather trapped smoke from coal use over the city from 5 to 9 December.
tokens.image_credit: N T Stobbs · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Blizzard of 1888
tokens.title: Snowstorm paralyses the Northeast
tokens.description: The Great Blizzard of 1888 (March 11 to 14, 1888) was one of the deadliest blizzards in American history. It paralysed the East Coast from Chesapeake Bay to Maine, with snowdrifts over 50 feet in places.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph collection of The Museum of the City of New York · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1925 Tri-State tornado
tokens.title: Deadliest tornado in US history
tokens.description: The 1925 Tri-State tornado on 18 March 1925 killed 695 people across Missouri, Illinois and Indiana. It is the deadliest tornado in United States history and was widely rated equivalent to F5.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author or not provided · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1974 Super Outbreak
tokens.title: 148 tornadoes in 18 hours
tokens.description: The 1974 Super Outbreak on 3 and 4 April 1974 produced 148 tornadoes across much of the United States in about 18 hours. It was the most violent tornado outbreak on record, with 30 F4 or F5 tornadoes.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Typhoon Vera
tokens.title: Typhoon Vera floods Nagoya
tokens.description: Typhoon Vera, also called the Isewan Typhoon, struck Japan in September 1959 as the strongest and deadliest typhoon on record to make landfall there. Its impact was catastrophic in Nagoya and the Ise Bay region.
tokens.image_credit: 京都大学防災研究所 (Disaster Prevention Research Institute at Kyoto University) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cyclone Tracy
tokens.title: Darwin devastated on Christmas Day
tokens.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Tracy devastated the city of Darwin in the Northern Territory of Australia in December 1974. The small but destructive storm turned toward the city and struck overnight on 24 and 25 December.
tokens.image_credit: Bidgee · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Dorian
tokens.title: Category 5 stalls over the Bahamas
tokens.description: Hurricane Dorian, in September 2019, was the most intense tropical cyclone on record to strike the Bahamas. It is regarded as the worst natural disaster in the Bahamas' recorded history.
tokens.image_credit: ABI imagery from NOAA'S GOES-16 Satellite · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2003 European heatwave
tokens.title: Record temperatures across Europe
tokens.description: The 2003 European heatwave produced the hottest summer recorded in Europe since at least 1540. Spain, France and Italy were hit especially hard, with health crises in several countries and crop shortfalls in southern Europe.

tokens.name: 2010 Russian wildfires
tokens.title: Smoke blankets Moscow
tokens.description: The 2010 Russian wildfires were several hundred fires across Russia, mainly in the west, from late July to early September 2010. Record heat and drought pushed thick smog over Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2022 Pakistan floods
tokens.title: A third of the country underwater
tokens.description: From June to October 2022, monsoon rains and melting glaciers caused floods in Pakistan that killed 1,739 people. Damage was estimated at about US$40 billion and the government declared an emergency in August.
tokens.image_credit: Ali Hyder Junejo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2010 Pakistan floods
tokens.title: Indus overflows
tokens.description: The 2010 floods began in late July after heavy monsoon rain in the Indus River basin. About one-fifth of Pakistan's land area was affected, and 1,985 people died nationwide.
tokens.image_credit: DVIDSHUB · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2011 Thailand floods
tokens.title: Bangkok suburbs inundated
tokens.description: Severe monsoon flooding in Thailand began in late July 2011 after Tropical Storm Nock-ten. The floods spread along the Chao Phraya and Mekong basins, reaching Bangkok's northern suburbs.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Robert J. Maurer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1938 Yellow River flood
tokens.title: Dikes breached to halt Japan
tokens.description: In June 1938 the Chinese National Revolutionary Army breached Yellow River levees at Huayuankou, Henan, to slow the Japanese advance. The man-made flood displaced large numbers of people until 1947.
tokens.image_credit: Sweeper tamonten · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1887 Yellow River flood
tokens.title: One of the deadliest natural disasters
tokens.description: The 1887 Yellow River flood began in late September 1887 during the Qing dynasty. It killed at least 930,000 people and is the deadliest flood in Chinese history.

tokens.name: Great Mississippi Flood of 1927
tokens.title: Levees fail along the river
tokens.description: The Great Mississippi Flood of 1927 was the most destructive river flood in United States history, inundating about 27,000 square miles over several months in early 1927. About 500 people died and over 630,000 were affected, mostly in Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana.
tokens.image_credit: Archival Photography by Steve Nicklas, NOS, NGS · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kurukshetra War
tokens.title: Epic battle of the Mahabharata
tokens.description: The Kurukshetra War, also called the Mahabharata War, is the great war described in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. It was fought between the Kauravas and Pandavas over the throne of Hastinapura, and the Bhagavad Gita is set during it.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY date

tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of the Ten Kings
tokens.title: Vedic battle on the Parushni
tokens.description: The Battle of the Ten Kings is a Vedic battle on the Parushni river, the Rigvedic name of the modern Ravi in Punjab. Sudas of the Bharata tribe defeated a confederation of ten tribes, an event tied to the rise of the Kuru polity.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY date

tokens.name: Second Battle of Tarain
tokens.title: Ghurid victory opens northern India
tokens.description: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 near Tarain (modern Taraori), Haryana. Ghurid forces under Muhammad Ghuri defeated the Rajput confederacy of Prithviraj Chauhan, opening the north Indian plain.
tokens.image_credit: Allan Stewart · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Khanwa
tokens.title: Babur defeats Rana Sanga
tokens.description: The Battle of Khanwa was fought on 16 March 1527 near Khanwa in Rajasthan. Babur's Mughal army defeated the forces of Rana Sanga of Mewar, a decisive event in early Mughal rule over northern India.

tokens.name: Battle of Chausa
tokens.title: Sher Shah Suri defeats Humayun
tokens.description: The Battle of Chausa was fought on 26 June 1539 at Chausa, about 10 miles southwest of Buxar in Bihar. Sher Shah Suri defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun, with support from local Rajput allies.

tokens.name: Siege of Chittorgarh
tokens.title: Akbar takes the Rajput fortress
tokens.description: The siege of Chittorgarh lasted from October 1567 to February 1568. Mughal forces under Akbar captured the hill fortress of Chittor, capital of the Sisodia rulers of Mewar, after months of mining and cannon fire.
tokens.image_credit: Composition designed by the Mughal court artist Miskina, with details painted by Bhura for the left side and Sarwan for the right side. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Delhi
tokens.title: British recapture the city
tokens.description: The siege of Delhi in 1857 was a decisive episode of the Indian Rebellion. British forces recaptured the city from rebel sepoys and the restored Mughal court of Bahadur Shah II.

tokens.name: Siege of Cawnpore
tokens.title: Garrison massacred after surrender
tokens.description: The siege of Cawnpore in June 1857 was a key episode of the Indian Rebellion. Besieged British forces and civilians left under a promise of safe passage and were massacred at the Cawnpore ghat.
tokens.image_credit: TuckDB · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black Hole of Calcutta
tokens.title: Prisoners held in Fort William
tokens.description: The Black Hole of Calcutta was a small dungeon in Fort William where Siraj-ud-Daulah's troops held British prisoners on the night of 20 June 1756. Many of the prisoners died overnight, and the episode became a celebrated event of early British rule in Bengal.

tokens.name: Bengal famine of 1943
tokens.title: Millions die in wartime Bengal
tokens.description: The Bengal famine of 1943 was a wartime famine in the Bengal and Orissa provinces of British India. Estimates of deaths range from 800,000 to 3.8 million, from starvation and disease.
tokens.image_credit: Kalyani Bhattacharyee, and Sj. Manoj Sarbadhikar, Servants of Bengal Society, at 153/3N, Upper Circular Road, Calcutta; All Rights Reserved. First edition 1944. Printed by Manindra Chandra Dutta at Sa · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Direct Action Day
tokens.title: Calcutta riots precede Partition
tokens.description: Direct Action Day, 16 August 1946, was called by the All-India Muslim League to demand a separate Muslim homeland. It led to large-scale communal violence in Calcutta before Partition.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lahore Resolution
tokens.title: Demand for separate Muslim states
tokens.description: The Lahore Resolution was adopted by the All-India Muslim League on 23 March 1940 in Lahore. It called for independent states in the Muslim-majority regions of British India and became the basis of the Pakistan Movement.
tokens.image_credit: Irfan0552007 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Purna Swaraj declaration
tokens.title: Congress demands complete independence
tokens.description: The Declaration of Purna Swaraj was a resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in 1930. It demanded complete independence from British rule after rejecting the British offer of dominion status.

tokens.name: Chauri Chaura incident
tokens.title: Violence ends Gandhi's non-cooperation
tokens.description: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district, British India. Protesters of the non-cooperation movement set fire to a police station after police fired on them, killing its occupants.
tokens.image_credit: Nitishkumarojha · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Champaran Satyagraha
tokens.title: Gandhi's first campaign in India
tokens.description: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was Mahatma Gandhi's first satyagraha campaign in British India. Farmers in Champaran district of Bihar protested against being forced to grow indigo for very little payment.

tokens.name: Tryst with Destiny speech
tokens.title: Nehru greets India's independence
tokens.description: Tryst with Destiny was Jawaharlal Nehru's speech to the Indian Constituent Assembly around midnight on 14 August 1947, on the eve of India's independence. It is considered one of the great speeches of the 20th century.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Constitution of India adopted
tokens.title: Republic proclaimed two months later
tokens.description: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. It is the longest written national constitution in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Emergency
tokens.title: Indira Gandhi suspends civil liberties
tokens.description: The Emergency was a 21 month period from 25 June 1975 to 21 March 1977, when Prime Minister Indira Gandhi ruled by decree. It was declared under Article 352 of the Constitution of India and civil liberties were suspended.

tokens.name: Demolition of the Babri Masjid
tokens.title: Mosque razed in Ayodhya
tokens.description: The Babri Masjid, a 16th-century mosque in Ayodhya, India, was destroyed on 6 December 1992 by activists of the Vishva Hindu Parishad and allied organisations. The mosque had been at the centre of a long socio-political dispute.
tokens.image_credit: Samuel Bourne[1][2] (1834–1912) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Economic liberalisation in India
tokens.title: Reforms open the Indian economy
tokens.description: The 1991 reforms opened the Indian economy to foreign trade and investment and gave private enterprise a larger role. They followed a balance-of-payments crisis in which foreign exchange reserves fell to about three weeks of imports.

tokens.name: India's first general election
tokens.title: World's largest democratic exercise begins
tokens.description: India's first general elections were held between 25 October 1951 and 21 February 1952, the first national elections after independence in 1947. Voters elected 489 members of the first Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament.

tokens.name: Chipko movement
tokens.title: Villagers hug trees in Uttarakhand
tokens.description: The Chipko movement is a forest conservation movement in India in which protesters in the 1970s hugged trees to stop them being felled. It opposed commercial logging and government deforestation policies.

tokens.name: Narmada Bachao Andolan
tokens.title: Protests over the Sardar Sarovar dam
tokens.description: Narmada Bachao Andolan is an Indian social movement founded by Medha Patkar in 1985 against large dam projects on the Narmada River. Its early focus was the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat.
tokens.image_credit: Supreet patel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
tokens.title: Second war over Kashmir
tokens.description: The Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 was an armed conflict between India and Pakistan from August to September 1965, which began after Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar in Kashmir. A ceasefire under UNSC Resolution 211 and the Tashkent Declaration ended it.
tokens.image_credit: Abhinayrathore at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971
tokens.title: Two-week war creates Bangladesh
tokens.description: The India-Pakistan war of 1971 was a two-week military conflict during the Bangladesh Liberation War. It ended with Pakistan's surrender in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and the creation of Bangladesh.
tokens.image_credit: Indian Navy · GODL-India · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sino-Indian War
tokens.title: Himalayan border conflict
tokens.description: The Sino-Indian War was an armed conflict between China and India from October to November 1962. Fighting took place along the disputed Himalayan border, in the North-East Frontier Agency and the Aksai Chin region.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siachen conflict
tokens.title: War on the world's highest battlefield
tokens.description: The Siachen conflict was a military conflict between India and Pakistan over the Siachen Glacier in Kashmir, started in 1984 by India's Operation Meghdoot. It is fought at very high altitude on the Saltoro Ridge and the glacier.
tokens.image_credit: Abhishek_Kumar · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chagai-I tests
tokens.title: Pakistan's first nuclear tests
tokens.description: Chagai-I was the code name of five underground nuclear tests conducted by Pakistan on 28 May 1998 at the Ras Koh Hills in Balochistan. It was Pakistan's first public test of nuclear weapons, carried out in response to India's Pokhran-II tests.
tokens.image_credit: Khalid Mahmood · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Gibraltar
tokens.title: Infiltration into Kashmir
tokens.description: Operation Gibraltar was a covert military operation planned by the Pakistan Army in August 1965. Infiltrators crossed the Line of Control into Indian-administered Kashmir to incite a local uprising against Indian rule.

tokens.name: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
tokens.title: Attack at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi
tokens.description: Benazir Bhutto, former prime minister of Pakistan, was assassinated on 27 December 2007 at Liaquat Bagh in Rawalpindi. Shots were fired after a political rally, and a suicide bomb followed.
tokens.image_credit: Khalid Mahmood · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peshawar school massacre
tokens.title: Attack on the Army Public School
tokens.description: The 2014 Peshawar school massacre was a terrorist attack on the Army Public School in Peshawar, Pakistan, on 16 December 2014. Six Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan gunmen killed 149 people, 132 of them schoolchildren.
tokens.image_credit: Voice of America · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shooting of Malala Yousafzai
tokens.title: Schoolgirl activist shot in Swat
tokens.description: Malala Yousafzai, a schoolgirl and education activist, was shot on her school bus in Mingora, Swat, Pakistan, on 9 October 2012. The Pakistani Taliban claimed the attack, which made her a global figure for girls' education.

tokens.name: Siege of Lal Masjid
tokens.title: Operation Silence in Islamabad
tokens.description: The siege of Lal Masjid was an armed confrontation in July 2007 between an Islamist militia and the government of Pakistan. The focal points were the Red Mosque and the Jamia Hafsa madrasah complex in Islamabad.
tokens.image_credit: BBC News اردو · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Eagle Claw
tokens.title: Failed rescue of hostages in Iran
tokens.description: Operation Eagle Claw was a failed United States attempt in April 1980 to rescue 52 embassy staff held captive in Tehran. The mission was aborted at Desert One after aircraft failures.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iran Air Flight 655
tokens.title: Airliner shot down over the Strait of Hormuz
tokens.description: Iran Air Flight 655 was a scheduled Airbus A300 passenger flight shot down by USS Vincennes over the Persian Gulf on 3 July 1988, killing all 290 people on board. The flight had departed from Bandar Abbas.
tokens.image_credit: Irna · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stuxnet
tokens.title: Worm sabotages Natanz centrifuges
tokens.description: Stuxnet is a computer worm first uncovered in 2010 that damaged centrifuges at the Natanz Nuclear Facility in Iran. It is widely regarded as the first known cyberweapon to cause physical destruction.
tokens.image_credit: Hamed Saber · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Qasem Soleimani
tokens.title: Drone strike at Baghdad airport
tokens.description: Qasem Soleimani, commander of Iran's Quds Force, was killed by a United States drone strike near Baghdad International Airport on 3 January 2020. The strike was ordered by President Donald Trump.
tokens.image_credit: US Special Operations Forces · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mahsa Amini protests
tokens.title: Women-led protests across Iran
tokens.description: Protests against the Islamic Republic of Iran began in September 2022 after the death in police custody of Mahsa Amini. They were described as the most widespread revolt in Iran since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Darafsh · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2009 Iranian presidential election protests
tokens.title: Disputed vote triggers mass rallies
tokens.description: Protests broke out in cities across Iran from 12 June 2009, after Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was declared the winner of the presidential election. Supporters of Mir-Hossein Mousavi and Mehdi Karroubi later called the movement the Green Movement.
tokens.image_credit: Hamed Saber · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Expulsion of the Moriscos
tokens.title: Spain expels its converted Muslims
tokens.description: King Philip III of Spain decreed the expulsion of the Moriscos, descendants of forced-converted Muslims, on 9 April 1609. The expelled were shipped from Spanish Mediterranean ports, mainly in Valencia.
tokens.image_credit: Vicente Mestre · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish Inquisition founded
tokens.title: Catholic Monarchs establish the tribunal
tokens.description: The Tribunal of the Holy Office was authorized by Pope Sixtus IV in 1478 and the Catholic Monarchs appointed its first inquisitors. Its first tribunal sat in Seville from 1480.

tokens.name: Alhambra Decree
tokens.title: Jews expelled from Spain
tokens.description: The Alhambra Decree was issued on 31 March 1492 by the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon. It ordered unconverted Jews to leave the Crowns of Castile and Aragon by 31 July 1492.
tokens.image_credit: Emilio Sala · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Gravelines
tokens.title: Fire ships scatter the Armada
tokens.description: The Battle of Gravelines of 29 July 1588 (Julian calendar) was the decisive engagement of the Spanish Armada campaign. English fireships scattered the Spanish fleet off the Flemish coast.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Brielle
tokens.title: Sea Beggars launch the Dutch revolt
tokens.description: On 1 April 1572 Sea Beggars, Dutch rebel privateers, captured the undefended port of Brielle. It gave the rebels their first foothold on land during the Dutch Revolt against Spain.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Luyken · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Act of Abjuration
tokens.title: Dutch declare independence from Spain
tokens.description: The Act of Abjuration was signed in The Hague on 26 July 1581 by the Dutch provinces. It freed their magistrates from their oaths to Philip II of Spain, a declaration of independence during the Dutch Revolt.
tokens.image_credit: Johannes Hinderikus Egenberger · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Raid on the Medway
tokens.title: Dutch fleet burns English ships
tokens.description: In June 1667 the Dutch navy raided the English fleet at anchor off Chatham and Gillingham on the River Medway. Dutch ships burned or captured several English warships during the Second Anglo-Dutch War.
tokens.image_credit: Willem van der Stoop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capture of Gibraltar
tokens.title: British take the Rock
tokens.description: An Anglo-Dutch force of the Grand Alliance seized the Rock of Gibraltar between 1 and 4 August 1704. The capture took place during the War of the Spanish Succession.

tokens.name: Great Siege of Gibraltar
tokens.title: Longest siege endured by the British
tokens.description: The Great Siege of Gibraltar was a failed Spanish and French attempt to take Gibraltar from Britain during the American Revolutionary War. It lasted from 1779 to 1783 and was the largest battle of that war by number of combatants.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battles of Saratoga
tokens.title: American victory brings French alliance
tokens.description: The Battles of Saratoga were fought on 19 September and 7 October 1777 near Saratoga, New York, during the American Revolutionary War. The American victory and British surrender in the second battle persuaded France to ally with the Americans.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valley Forge
tokens.title: Washington's army endures the cold
tokens.description: Valley Forge was the winter encampment of the Continental Army under George Washington from 19 December 1777 to 19 June 1778. The camp lay in eastern Pennsylvania along the Schuylkill River.
tokens.image_credit: John Ward Dunsmore · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Trenton
tokens.title: Surprise attack on Trenton
tokens.description: The Battle of Trenton was fought on the morning of 26 December 1776 in Trenton, New Jersey. It followed George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River the night before, and almost two-thirds of the Hessian garrison was captured.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
tokens.title: "Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes"
tokens.description: The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought on 17 June 1775 during the siege of Boston, in the first campaign of the American Revolutionary War. Most of the combat took place on the adjacent Breed's Hill rather than Bunker Hill.
tokens.image_credit: John Trumbull · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Constitutional Convention
tokens.title: Framers draft the US Constitution
tokens.description: The Constitutional Convention met in Philadelphia from 25 May to 17 September 1787. Its delegates, with George Washington as president, produced the framework of the United States Constitution.
tokens.image_credit: Howard Chandler Christy · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Whiskey Rebellion
tokens.title: Tax revolt tests the federal government
tokens.description: The Whiskey Rebellion was a violent protest against the federal whiskey tax in the United States, lasting from 1791 to 1794 during the presidency of George Washington. The tax was the first levied on a domestic product by the new federal government.

tokens.name: Marbury v. Madison
tokens.title: Judicial review established
tokens.description: Marbury v. Madison was a decision of the United States Supreme Court in 1803 that established judicial review, the power of American courts to strike down laws that violate the Constitution. It is regarded as the most important decision in American constitutional law.

tokens.name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
tokens.title: Corps of Discovery sets out
tokens.description: The Corps of Discovery, led by Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, set out from Camp Dubois in Illinois on May 14, 1804. The expedition crossed the Louisiana Purchase to the Pacific coast and returned in 1806.
tokens.image_credit: Kbh3rd · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trail of Tears
tokens.title: Cherokee forced west
tokens.description: The forced removal of about 60,000 Native Americans of the Five Civilized Tribes from the southeastern United States to Indian Territory between 1830 and 1850. The 1838 Cherokee removal was the last forced removal east of the Mississippi.
tokens.image_credit: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Cculber007 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seneca Falls Convention
tokens.title: First women's rights convention
tokens.description: The first women's rights convention, held in the Wesleyan Chapel in Seneca Falls, New York, on July 19 and 20, 1848. Its organizers called it a convention to discuss the social, civil and religious rights of women.

tokens.name: Battle of Fort Sumter
tokens.title: First shots of the American Civil War
tokens.description: The bombardment of Fort Sumter near Charleston, South Carolina, on April 12 and 13, 1861, ended with the surrender of the U.S. Army garrison. It is generally regarded as the start of the American Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: Currier & Ives. Uploaded by Christophe cagé 12:52, 6 September 2006 (UTC) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: First Battle of Bull Run
tokens.title: First major land battle of the war
tokens.description: The first major land battle of the American Civil War, fought on July 21, 1861, in Prince William County, Virginia. Confederate forces called it the Battle of First Manassas.
tokens.image_credit: William Ridgway after Felix Octavius Carr Darley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Antietam
tokens.title: Bloodiest single day in American history
tokens.description: Fought near Antietam Creek and Sharpsburg, Maryland, on September 17, 1862, between Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia and George McClellan's Army of the Potomac. It remains the bloodiest single day in American history.
tokens.image_credit: Thure de Thulstrup / Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Vicksburg
tokens.title: Union takes the Mississippi
tokens.description: The siege of Vicksburg, May 18 to July 4, 1863, in which Ulysses S. Grant's Army of the Tennessee forced the Confederate garrison to surrender. Vicksburg was the last major Confederate stronghold on the Mississippi River.
tokens.image_credit: Thure de Thulstrup · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Chancellorsville
tokens.title: Lee's boldest victory
tokens.description: The Battle of Chancellorsville was fought from April 30 to May 6, 1863, in Virginia during the American Civil War. Robert E. Lee divided his army and won a major Confederate victory despite heavy casualties.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sherman's March to the Sea
tokens.title: Atlanta to Savannah
tokens.description: Sherman's March to the Sea was a Union military campaign through Georgia from November 15 to December 21, 1864, led by William T. Sherman. It ended with the capture of the port of Savannah and damaged the Confederacy's economy and transport.
tokens.image_credit: George N. Barnard · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Surrender at Appomattox
tokens.title: Lee surrenders to Grant
tokens.description: On April 9, 1865, Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Union General Ulysses S. Grant at the McLean House near Appomattox Court House, Virginia. The surrender effectively ended the main Confederate army in the American Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: The Major & Knapp Eng. Mfg. & Lith. Co. 71 Broadway · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
tokens.title: Shot at Ford's Theatre
tokens.description: On April 14, 1865, President Abraham Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C. He died the following day, shortly before the end of the American Civil War.
tokens.image_credit: Adam Cuerden · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emancipation Proclamation
tokens.title: Slaves in rebel states declared free
tokens.description: The Emancipation Proclamation was an executive order issued by President Abraham Lincoln on January 1, 1863, during the American Civil War. It declared that enslaved people in the Confederate states in rebellion were free.
tokens.image_credit: Engraving by W. Roberts, restoration by Bammesk · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
tokens.title: Thirty seconds in Tombstone
tokens.description: The gunfight at the O.K. Corral took place on October 26, 1881, in Tombstone, Arizona Territory. Lawmen fought members of the Cochise County Cowboys in a clash lasting less than a minute that became an archetype of the American Old West.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan
tokens.title: Shot outside the Washington Hilton
tokens.description: On March 30, 1981, President Ronald Reagan was shot and wounded by John Hinckley Jr. outside the Washington Hilton in Washington, D.C. Reagan survived the attack, which came as he walked back to his limousine after a speech.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Evans · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy
tokens.title: Shot at the Ambassador Hotel
tokens.description: Senator Robert F. Kennedy was shot by Sirhan Sirhan at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles on June 5, 1968, after winning the California primary. He died the following day.
tokens.image_credit: Sven Walnum · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assassination of Malcolm X
tokens.title: Shot at the Audubon Ballroom
tokens.description: Malcolm X, a Black power activist and minister, was shot dead on February 21, 1965, while preparing to speak at the Audubon Ballroom in Manhattan. Three Nation of Islam members were convicted, and two of them were exonerated in 2021.

tokens.name: Murder of Emmett Till
tokens.title: Killing that galvanised the civil rights movement
tokens.description: Emmett Till, a 14-year-old Black boy, was abducted and lynched in Mississippi in August 1955. The acquittal of his killers drew national attention and is widely credited with sparking the American civil rights movement.
tokens.image_credit: Eames Heard · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brown v. Board of Education
tokens.title: Supreme Court bans school segregation
tokens.description: In 1954 the US Supreme Court ruled that state laws establishing racial segregation in public schools violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. The decision partially overruled the 1896 Plessy v. Ferguson ruling.

tokens.name: Little Rock Nine
tokens.title: Students integrate Central High
tokens.description: In 1957 nine African American students enrolled at Little Rock Central High School in Arkansas. Governor Orval Faubus first blocked their entry, and President Dwight D. Eisenhower then intervened so they could attend.
tokens.image_credit: Ira Wilmer Counts Jr. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Greensboro sit-ins
tokens.title: Lunch counter protest spreads
tokens.description: The Greensboro sit-ins of February to July 1960 were nonviolent protests at the Woolworth store in Greensboro, North Carolina. They led the F. W. Woolworth Company to end its policy of racial segregation in its Southern stores.
tokens.image_credit: RadioFan (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Birmingham campaign
tokens.title: Protests confront segregation
tokens.description: The Birmingham campaign was a 1963 nonviolent civil rights movement in Birmingham, Alabama, led by the Southern Christian Leadership Conference. Police confrontations, including the Children's Crusade, helped prompt the 1964 Civil Rights Act.
tokens.image_credit: United Press International · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 16th Street Baptist Church bombing
tokens.title: Four girls killed in Birmingham
tokens.description: On September 15, 1963, Ku Klux Klan members bombed the 16th Street Baptist Church in Birmingham, Alabama, with 19 sticks of dynamite. Four girls were killed in the attack.
tokens.image_credit: Tom Self, Birmingham News · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Freedom Summer
tokens.title: Voter registration drive in Mississippi
tokens.description: Freedom Summer, also called Mississippi Freedom Summer, was a campaign launched in June 1964 by civil rights activists to register Black voters in Mississippi. It also set up Freedom Schools and community centers across the state.
tokens.image_credit: Robfergusonjr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
tokens.title: Segregation outlawed
tokens.description: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is a landmark US law that outlaws discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, and national origin. President Lyndon B. Johnson signed it into law on July 2, 1964.
tokens.image_credit: Cecil Stoughton, White House Press Office (WHPO) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
tokens.title: Johnson signs the landmark law
tokens.description: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 is a landmark US federal statute that prohibits racial discrimination in voting. President Lyndon B. Johnson signed it into law on August 6, 1965.
tokens.image_credit: Yoichi Okamoto · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Watts riots
tokens.title: Six days of unrest in Los Angeles
tokens.description: The Watts riots took place in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles from August 11 to 16, 1965. They were fuelled by anger at police abuse, employment discrimination, residential segregation and poverty.
tokens.image_credit: George R. Fry, Los Angeles Times · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1967 Detroit riot
tokens.title: Five days of unrest
tokens.description: The 1967 Detroit riot, also known as the 12th Street Riot, was the bloodiest of the US urban riots of summer 1967. It began on July 23, 1967, after a police raid on an unlicensed after-hours bar.
tokens.image_credit: Phil Cherner (email: phil@philcherner.com ; website: www.philcherner.com). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1968 Democratic National Convention
tokens.title: Clashes in Chicago streets
tokens.description: The 1968 Democratic National Convention was held from August 26 to 29, 1968, at the International Amphitheatre in Chicago. Hubert Humphrey and Edmund Muskie were nominated for president and vice president there.
tokens.image_credit: Warren K. Leffler · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Occupation of Alcatraz
tokens.title: Native activists claim the island
tokens.description: The Occupation of Alcatraz lasted 19 months, from November 20, 1969 to June 11, 1971. About 89 American Indians and their supporters held Alcatraz Island and its former prison until the US government ended it.
tokens.image_credit: Loco Steve · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wounded Knee Occupation
tokens.title: 71-day standoff
tokens.description: The Wounded Knee Occupation began on February 27, 1973, when about 200 Oglala Lakota and American Indian Movement members seized the town of Wounded Knee on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation. The protest criticized alleged corruption by the tribal president and US failure to honour treaties.
tokens.image_credit: Jim Mone · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Roe v. Wade
tokens.title: Supreme Court ruling on abortion
tokens.description: Roe v. Wade was a 1973 ruling of the US Supreme Court holding that the Constitution protected a woman's right to an abortion before fetal viability. The decision struck down many state abortion laws and fuelled the ongoing US abortion debate.

tokens.name: Resignation of Richard Nixon
tokens.title: First US president to resign
tokens.description: Richard Nixon announced his resignation in a televised address from the Oval Office of the White House on 8 August 1974. He left office the next day amid the Watergate scandal, the only US president ever to resign.
tokens.image_credit: Oliver Atkins · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iran-Contra affair
tokens.title: Secret arms deals exposed
tokens.description: The Iran-Contra affair was a US political scandal over arms trafficking to Iran between 1981 and 1986, facilitated by senior Reagan administration officials. The proceeds were used to fund the Contra rebels in Nicaragua despite a congressional ban.
tokens.image_credit: Series: Reagan White House Photographs, 1/20/1981 - 1/20/1989 Collection: White House Photographic Collection, 1/20/1981 - 1/20/1989 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oklahoma City bombing
tokens.title: Federal building truck bomb
tokens.description: The Oklahoma City bombing was a truck bomb attack on 19 April 1995 that destroyed much of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building. Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols killed 167 people in the domestic terrorist attack.
tokens.image_credit: Staff Sergeant Preston Chasteen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Columbine High School massacre
tokens.title: School shooting in Colorado
tokens.description: The Columbine High School massacre was a school shooting on 20 April 1999 at Columbine High School in Columbine, Colorado. Students Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold killed 13 people, 12 students and one teacher, before dying by suicide.
tokens.image_credit: Denverjeffrey · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waco siege
tokens.title: 51-day standoff at Mount Carmel
tokens.description: The Waco siege was a 51-day standoff from 28 February to 19 April 1993 between US federal and Texas officials and the Branch Davidian group at its Mount Carmel Center compound near Waco, Texas. It resulted in the deaths of 86 people, including 28 children.
tokens.image_credit: the Federal Bureau of Investigation · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ruby Ridge standoff
tokens.title: Idaho siege and shootout
tokens.description: The Ruby Ridge standoff was an August 1992 siege of the Weaver family home in Boundary County, Idaho. It began when US Marshals Service deputies came to arrest Randy Weaver on federal firearms charges.
tokens.image_credit: Dave Hunt · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bush v. Gore
tokens.title: Supreme Court ends the Florida recount
tokens.description: Bush v. Gore was the 12 December 2000 United States Supreme Court decision that halted the statewide recount of disputed Florida ballots. The ruling settled the 2000 presidential election in favour of George W. Bush.

tokens.name: United Airlines Flight 93
tokens.title: Passengers fight back over Pennsylvania
tokens.description: United Airlines Flight 93 was hijacked on 11 September 2001 as part of the September 11 attacks. Passengers revolted, and the plane crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all 44 aboard.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Government · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Harvey
tokens.title: Record rain floods Houston
tokens.description: Hurricane Harvey made landfall in Texas and Louisiana in August 2017 and caused catastrophic rainfall flooding in Greater Houston. It is tied with Hurricane Katrina as the costliest tropical cyclone on record, at about $125 billion.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos Malcolm McClendon/Texas Military Department · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting
tokens.title: Elementary school in Newtown, Connecticut
tokens.description: The Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting on 14 December 2012 in Newtown, Connecticut killed 26 people, 20 of them first-grade children. The gunman had earlier killed his mother at home and then took his own life.
tokens.image_credit: Liam Enea · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 United States presidential election
tokens.title: First Black US president
tokens.description: The 2008 United States presidential election was held on 4 November 2008. Democrat Barack Obama defeated Republican John McCain and became the first African American elected president.

tokens.name: First inauguration of Barack Obama
tokens.title: Two million on the National Mall
tokens.description: Barack Obama was inaugurated as the 44th president of the United States on 20 January 2009 at the West Front of the United States Capitol. The ceremony drew a record attendance for any event held in Washington, D.C.
tokens.image_credit: Master Sgt. Cecilio Ricardo, U.S. Air Force · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: January 6 United States Capitol attack
tokens.title: Rioters storm the Capitol
tokens.description: On 6 January 2021 a mob of supporters of President Donald Trump attacked the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. The attack came two months after Trump's defeat in the 2020 presidential election.
tokens.image_credit: Tyler Merbler from USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2016 United States presidential election
tokens.title: Trump wins the Electoral College
tokens.description: The 2016 United States presidential election was held on 8 November 2016. Republican Donald Trump and Mike Pence defeated Democrats Hillary Clinton and Tim Kaine, winning the Electoral College while losing the popular vote.
tokens.image_credit: Corey Taratuta · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2020 United States presidential election
tokens.title: Record turnout during the pandemic
tokens.description: Presidential election held in the United States on November 3, 2020, won by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris over incumbent Donald Trump and Mike Pence. It had the highest voter turnout by percentage since 1900.
tokens.image_credit: Sdkb · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: George Floyd protests
tokens.title: Nationwide protests begin in Minneapolis
tokens.description: Protests against police brutality began in Minneapolis on May 26, 2020, after George Floyd was killed by city police during an arrest. They spread across the United States and internationally.
tokens.image_credit: Dan Aasland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Occupy Wall Street
tokens.title: Zuccotti Park encampment
tokens.description: Occupy Wall Street was a protest movement against economic inequality and the influence of money in politics. It began in Zuccotti Park in New York City's Financial District on September 17, 2011, and lasted until November 15, 2011.
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Snowden disclosures
tokens.title: NSA leaks revealed from Hong Kong
tokens.description: Starting in 2013, media outlets published classified documents leaked by former NSA contractor Edward Snowden. The reports exposed global surveillance programmes and secret intelligence-sharing agreements.

tokens.name: United States diplomatic cables leak
tokens.title: US diplomatic cables published
tokens.description: On 28 November 2010 WikiLeaks began publishing classified US State Department cables sent by 274 diplomatic missions worldwide. The cables, dated 1966 to 2010, contain diplomats' assessments of world leaders and host countries.

tokens.name: Panama Papers
tokens.title: Mossack Fonseca leak
tokens.description: The Panama Papers are 11.5 million leaked documents from the Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, published from April 3, 2016. They detail financial information for more than 214,000 offshore entities.

tokens.name: Facebook Cambridge Analytica data scandal
tokens.title: Facebook data harvested
tokens.description: In the 2010s, personal data of millions of Facebook users was collected by the British consulting firm Cambridge Analytica for political advertising without informed consent. The data was gathered through the app This Is Your Digital Life, built by Aleksandr Kogan.

tokens.name: Battle of Bouvines
tokens.description: The Battle of Bouvines was fought on 27 July 1214 near the town of Bouvines in Flanders. A French army under King Philip Augustus defeated a larger allied army led by Holy Roman Emperor Otto IV.
tokens.image_credit: Horace Vernet · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Falkirk
tokens.title: Wallace defeated by Edward I
tokens.description: The Battle of Falkirk, fought on 22 July 1298, was a major battle of the First War of Scottish Independence. Edward I of England's army defeated the Scottish forces led by William Wallace.
tokens.image_credit: Euan Nelson · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Edgehill
tokens.title: First battle of the Civil War
tokens.description: The Battle of Edgehill was fought on 23 October 1642 near Edge Hill and Kineton in southern Warwickshire. It was the first pitched battle of the First English Civil War, between the forces of King Charles I and Parliament.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph Swain · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Marston Moor
tokens.description: The Battle of Marston Moor was fought on 2 July 1644 during the Wars of the Three Kingdoms. Parliamentarian and Scottish Covenanter forces defeated the Royalist army commanded by Prince Rupert and the Marquess of Newcastle.
tokens.image_credit: John Barker (1811-1886) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Sedgemoor
tokens.description: The Battle of Sedgemoor was fought on 6 July 1685 at Westonzoyland near Bridgwater in Somerset. It was the final and decisive engagement of the Monmouth Rebellion, in which forces loyal to James II defeated the rebels led by the Duke of Monmouth.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Garlick · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Massacre of Glencoe
tokens.description: The Massacre of Glencoe took place on 13 February 1692 in Glen Coe in the Scottish Highlands. About 30 members of Clan MacDonald of Glencoe were killed by government forces, allegedly for failing to swear allegiance to William and Mary.
tokens.image_credit: Kim Traynor · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siege of Derry
tokens.description: The Siege of Derry in 1689 was the first major event of the Williamite War in Ireland. Jacobite forces under James II besieged the walled city until it was relieved by ships that broke the boom on the River Foyle.
tokens.image_credit: James Grant · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Irish Famine
tokens.description: The Great Famine in Ireland, from 1845 to 1852, was a period of mass starvation and disease caused mainly by potato blight. It caused an estimated 775,000 to 1.5 million excess deaths and led to mass emigration of over 1 million people.
tokens.image_credit: User AlanMc on en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bloody Sunday 1920
tokens.title: Croke Park shootings
tokens.description: Bloody Sunday, 21 November 1920, was a day of violence in Dublin during the Irish War of Independence. An IRA operation to assassinate British intelligence agents was followed by shootings that killed or fatally wounded more than 30 people.
tokens.image_credit: Self (Scolaire) Uploaded by Domer48 at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Omagh bombing
tokens.description: A car bomb planted by the Real IRA exploded in Omagh, County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, on 15 August 1998. It killed 29 people and injured about 220, the deadliest incident of the Troubles.
tokens.image_credit: Ardfern · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brighton hotel bombing
tokens.description: On 12 October 1984 the Provisional IRA bombed the Grand Hotel in Brighton, England, in an attempt to kill the British cabinet. Five people were killed, including MP Sir Anthony Berry, and more than thirty were injured.
tokens.image_credit: D4444n at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gordon Riots
tokens.title: Consumer goods giant
tokens.description: The Gordon Riots were several days of anti-Catholic unrest and violence in London, beginning on 2 June 1780 with a protest against the Papists Act 1778.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Green · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Stink
tokens.description: The Great Stink was an episode in July and August 1858 in which hot weather intensified the smell of untreated human waste and industrial effluent on the River Thames in central London.
tokens.image_credit: Punch Magazine · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Cable Street
tokens.description: The Battle of Cable Street was a series of clashes on 4 October 1936 in London's East End. Local residents rallied to block a British Union of Fascists march led by Oswald Mosley.
tokens.image_credit: Spudgun67 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dunblane massacre
tokens.description: The Dunblane massacre was a school shooting at Dunblane Primary School, Scotland, on 13 March 1996. Thomas Hamilton killed 16 pupils and one teacher, and it remains the deadliest mass shooting in British history.

tokens.name: Manchester Arena bombing
tokens.description: On 22 May 2017 a suicide bomber attacked the Manchester Arena in Manchester, England, after a concert by Ariana Grande. Twenty-two people were killed and 1,017 injured, the deadliest terrorist attack in the UK since 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Tomasz "odder" Kozlowski · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal
tokens.title: Novichok attack in Salisbury
tokens.description: On 4 March 2018 Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned with the Novichok nerve agent in Salisbury, England. Both spent several weeks in hospital in a critical condition before being discharged.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Curbishley · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wedding of Charles and Diana
tokens.description: Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer married at St Paul's Cathedral in London on 29 July 1981. The Church of England ceremony was watched by a global audience.
tokens.image_credit: United Press International · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wedding of William and Catherine
tokens.description: Prince William and Catherine Middleton married at Westminster Abbey in London on 29 April 2011. The ceremony was broadcast to a worldwide audience.
tokens.image_credit: Robbie Dale · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coronation of Charles III and Camilla
tokens.description: Charles III and Camilla were crowned king and queen of the United Kingdom at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023. The Anglican service included the anointing and the coronation regalia.
tokens.image_credit: HM Government · OGL 3 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1948 Summer Olympics
tokens.description: The 1948 Summer Olympics were held in London from 29 July to 14 August 1948. They were the first Summer Games since the 1936 Berlin Games, after the Second World War hiatus.
tokens.image_credit: National Media Museum from UK · No restrictions · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iranian Embassy siege
tokens.description: Six armed men seized the Iranian Embassy on Prince's Gate in London from 30 April to 5 May 1980, taking 26 people hostage. The siege ended with an assault by British special forces.
tokens.image_credit: Steve White2008 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre
tokens.description: The St. Bartholomew's Day massacre began in Paris on 24 August 1572. Catholic mobs and royal soldiers killed Huguenots in the days that followed, during the French Wars of Religion.

tokens.name: Edict of Nantes
tokens.description: King Henry IV of France signed the Edict of Nantes in April 1598. It granted the Calvinist Huguenots substantial rights and religious tolerance, while Catholicism stayed the established religion.
tokens.image_credit: Henry IV of France. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Women's March on Versailles
tokens.description: The Women's March on Versailles, on 5 October 1789, was a crowd of Parisian women and revolutionaries who marched to the royal palace at Versailles. The royal family was taken back to Paris afterwards, an early turning point of the French Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: September Massacres
tokens.description: The September Massacres were killings of prisoners in Paris from 2 to 6 September 1792, during the French Revolution. Between 1,176 and 1,614 people were killed in the city's prisons and convents.
tokens.image_credit: Attributed to Marie-Marc-Antoine Bilcocq (1755-1838) · CC BY-SA 2.0 fr · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Aspern-Essling
tokens.description: The Battle of Aspern-Essling, 21 to 22 May 1809, was fought on the Danube near Vienna during the Napoleonic Wars. Archduke Charles and the Austrians forced Napoleon's French back across the river, his first major battle defeat in person.

tokens.name: Siege of Paris 1870
tokens.description: The Siege of Paris ran from 19 September 1870 to 28 January 1871 during the Franco-Prussian War. It ended with the capture of the city by the Prussian-led North German states, the culmination of that war.
tokens.image_credit: Fred Barnard · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paris Peace Conference 1919
tokens.description: The Paris Peace Conference of 1919 to 1920 was a series of meetings where the Allied victors of World War I set the peace terms for the defeated Central Powers. It produced five treaties, including Versailles, and reshaped the map of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Pacific.
tokens.image_credit: Edward N. Jackson (US Army Signal Corps) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Amiens 1918
tokens.description: The Battle of Amiens began on 8 August 1918 as the opening phase of the Allied Hundred Days Offensive on the Western Front. The Allies advanced more than 11 kilometres on the first day, which Ludendorff called the black day of the German Army.
tokens.image_credit: William Rider-Rider · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Battle of Mons
