tokens.description: The 1922 British Mount Everest expedition was the first mountaineering expedition aimed at the first ascent of Everest. It attempted the mountain from the north side in Tibet and was the first to use bottled oxygen on the mountain.

curation.notes: coords north side

tokens.image_credit: Book author Charles Granville Bruce. Photographer unattributed, probably John Baptist Lucius Noel · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2008 K2 disaster
tokens.title: Deadly day on K2
tokens.description: The 2008 K2 disaster on 1 August 2008 killed 11 mountaineers from international expeditions on K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth. It was the worst single episode in the mountain's climbing history.

tokens.name: 2014 Mount Everest ice avalanche
tokens.title: Avalanche in the Khumbu Icefall
tokens.description: On 18 April 2014 ice seracs on the western spur of Mount Everest collapsed in the Khumbu Icefall, killing sixteen climbing Sherpas. It was the deadliest accident on the mountain at that time.

tokens.name: MS Estonia
tokens.title: Ferry sinks in the Baltic
tokens.description: MS Estonia was a car-passenger ferry on the Tallinn to Stockholm route when she sank in the Baltic Sea on 28 September 1994. The disaster killed 852 people and is one of the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters of the 20th century.

tokens.name: MS Herald of Free Enterprise
tokens.title: Ferry capsizes at Zeebrugge
tokens.description: MS Herald of Free Enterprise was a roll-on/roll-off ferry that capsized moments after leaving the port of Zeebrugge on 6 March 1987. The disaster killed 193 passengers and crew.

tokens.name: RMS Empress of Ireland
tokens.title: Liner lost in the St. Lawrence
tokens.description: RMS Empress of Ireland was a British-built ocean liner that sank in the Saint Lawrence River after a collision in fog on 29 May 1914. Of the 1,477 people aboard, 1,012 died, the worst peacetime maritime disaster in Canadian history.

tokens.name: SS Eastland
tokens.title: Capsized on the Chicago River
tokens.description: SS Eastland was a Great Lakes passenger steamship that capsized while moored at a dock in the Chicago River on 24 July 1915. The disaster killed 844 passengers and crew, the largest loss of life from a shipwreck on the Great Lakes.
tokens.image_credit: Bob Satterfield · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: PS General Slocum
tokens.title: Fire on the East River
tokens.description: PS General Slocum was an American sidewheel passenger steamboat built in Brooklyn in 1891. On 15 June 1904 she caught fire and sank in the East River of New York City.
tokens.image_credit: Angelo Agostini · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sultana
tokens.title: Steamboat explosion on the Mississippi
tokens.description: The steamboat Sultana exploded and sank on the Mississippi River on 27 April 1865. About 1,164 people died, the worst maritime disaster in United States history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: HMHS Britannic
tokens.title: Titanic's sister sinks off Kea
tokens.description: HMHS Britannic was the third Olympic-class liner of the White Star Line, used as a hospital ship from 1915. She sank in the Aegean Sea near the Greek island of Kea in November 1916.

tokens.name: Batavia shipwreck
tokens.title: Wreck on the Houtman Abrolhos
tokens.description: Batavia was a Dutch East India Company ship wrecked on the Houtman Abrolhos, a chain of islands off Western Australia, on 4 June 1629. Survivors on the islands later faced mutiny and killings before rescue.

tokens.name: Whydah Gally
tokens.title: Pirate ship wrecked off Cape Cod
tokens.description: Whydah Gally was a ship built as a passenger, cargo and slave vessel that was captured by the pirate Samuel Bellamy in 1717. The ship was lost in a storm off Cape Cod that year, and its wreck was later found off Wellfleet.

tokens.name: Nuestra Señora de Atocha
tokens.title: Treasure galleon off the Keys
tokens.description: Nuestra Señora de Atocha was a Spanish treasure galleon that sank in a hurricane off the Florida Keys in 1622 while sailing from Havana for Spain. The ship carried copper, silver, gold and gems from the New World.

tokens.name: SS Thistlegorm
tokens.title: Wreck in the Red Sea
tokens.description: SS Thistlegorm was a British cargo steamship built in Sunderland in 1940 and sunk by German bombers in the Red Sea in 1941. Her wreck near Ras Muhammad National Park is a well-known diving site.
tokens.image_credit: Woodym555 at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse
tokens.title: Battleships lost off Malaya
tokens.description: The sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse was a naval engagement on 10 December 1941 in the South China Sea off Malaya. Japanese land-based bombers and torpedo bombers sank both British capital ships of Force Z.

tokens.name: HMS Royal Oak
tokens.title: Sunk at anchor in Scapa Flow
tokens.description: HMS Royal Oak was a Revenge-class battleship of the Royal Navy, completed in 1916 and fought at the Battle of Jutland. She was sunk at her anchorage in Scapa Flow, Orkney, in 1939 with heavy loss of life.

tokens.name: USS Maine explosion
tokens.title: Explosion in Havana Harbor
tokens.description: The explosion and sinking of the United States Navy ship Maine in Havana Harbor on 15 February 1898 contributed to the outbreak of the Spanish-American War. Evidence points to an accident in a coal bunker, although the cause was disputed at the time.

tokens.name: Torrey Canyon oil spill
tokens.title: Tanker on the Seven Stones reef
tokens.description: The Torrey Canyon oil spill followed the grounding of the supertanker SS Torrey Canyon on rocks off south-west England in 1967. An estimated 25 to 36 million gallons of crude oil were spilled, one of the most serious oil spills in the world.

tokens.name: 2021 Suez Canal obstruction
tokens.title: Ever Given blocks the canal
tokens.description: The Ever Given, a 400-metre container ship, ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days from 23 to 29 March 2021. The obstruction halted traffic on one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes.
tokens.image_credit: NASA JSC ISS image library · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
tokens.title: Bridge struck by a container ship
tokens.description: On 26 March 2024 the container ship Dali struck a pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore, and the main spans collapsed. Six maintenance workers died, and the collapse blocked most shipping to the Port of Baltimore for 11 weeks.
tokens.image_credit: NTSBgov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Titan submersible implosion
tokens.title: Lost on a dive to the Titanic
tokens.description: On 18 June 2023 the OceanGate submersible Titan imploded during a dive to the Titanic wreck in the North Atlantic off Newfoundland. The five people on board were killed.

tokens.name: Antikythera wreck
tokens.title: Ancient ship found by sponge divers
tokens.description: The Antikythera wreck is a Roman-era shipwreck from the first century BC, found by sponge divers off Point Glyphadia on Antikythera in 1900. Its finds include statues, coins and the Antikythera mechanism.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uluburun shipwreck
tokens.title: Bronze Age cargo ship
tokens.description: Uluburun is a Late Bronze Age shipwreck from the late 14th century BC, found in 1982 by sponge diver Mehmed Çakir off Kaş, Turkey. The ship carried over 20 tons of cargo and was excavated from 1984 to 1994.

tokens.name: Exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England
tokens.title: King found under a car park
tokens.description: On 25 August 2012 the remains of Richard III, killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485, were found in Leicester at the former Greyfriars Friary. They were reinterred at Leicester Cathedral on 26 March 2015.

tokens.name: Staffordshire Hoard
tokens.title: Largest Anglo-Saxon gold hoard
tokens.description: The Staffordshire Hoard is the largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold and silver metalwork yet found, with almost 4,600 items and fragments. It contains about 5.1 kg of gold, 1.4 kg of silver and some 3,500 pieces of garnet cloisonne jewellery.
tokens.image_credit: David Rowan, Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoxne Hoard
tokens.title: Late Roman treasure
tokens.description: The Hoxne Hoard is the largest hoard of late Roman silver and gold discovered in Britain, with 14,865 coins and about 200 items of tableware and jewellery. It was found with a metal detector at Hoxne, Suffolk, in 1992.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mildenhall Treasure
tokens.title: Roman silver tableware
tokens.description: The Mildenhall Treasure is a hoard of over thirty pieces of fourth-century Roman silver tableware. It was found at West Row, near Mildenhall, Suffolk, in 1942, and includes the Great Dish, which weighs over 8 kg.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lewis chessmen
tokens.title: Medieval chess pieces
tokens.description: The Lewis chessmen are a group of 12th-century chess pieces, most carved from walrus ivory. They were discovered in 1831 on the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
tokens.image_credit: National Museums Scotland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vindolanda tablets
tokens.title: Letters from Hadrian's Wall
tokens.description: The Vindolanda tablets are some of the oldest surviving handwritten documents in Britain. Written on thin wooden leaves, they date to the 1st and 2nd centuries AD and document life on the Roman northern frontier.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seahenge
tokens.title: Timber circle on a beach
tokens.description: Seahenge, also known as Holme I, was a prehistoric timber circle with an upturned tree root at its centre. It was built in the early Bronze Age, around 2049 BC, at Holme-next-the-Sea in Norfolk.
tokens.image_credit: -JvL- · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amesbury Archer
tokens.title: Rich Bronze Age burial
tokens.description: The Amesbury Archer was an early Bronze Age man who lived around 2340 to 2300 BC. His grave was discovered during excavations at a housing development in Amesbury, near Stonehenge.

tokens.name: Nebra sky disc
tokens.title: Bronze Age star map
tokens.description: The Nebra sky disc is a bronze disc of about 30 cm with gold symbols usually read as the Sun or full moon, a lunar crescent and stars. It was found near Nebra in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, and is shown in the Landesmuseum fur Vorgeschichte in Halle.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Vincentz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venus of Willendorf
tokens.title: Palaeolithic figurine
tokens.description: The Venus of Willendorf is an 11.1 cm Venus figurine estimated to be about 30,000 years old. It was found in 1908 at a Palaeolithic site near Willendorf in Lower Austria.
tokens.image_credit: User:MatthiasKabel · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venus of Hohle Fels
tokens.title: Oldest known human figurine
tokens.description: The Venus of Hohle Fels is a mammoth ivory figurine dated to about 42,000 to 40,000 years ago, unearthed in 2008. It was found in Hohle Fels cave near Schelklingen, Germany, and is the oldest undisputed depiction of a human being.

tokens.name: Chauvet Cave
tokens.title: Cave paintings rediscovered
tokens.description: The Chauvet-Pont d'Arc Cave in the Ardeche department of France contains some of the best-preserved figurative cave paintings in the world. It was rediscovered on 18 December 1994 and granted UNESCO World Heritage status in 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mask of Agamemnon
tokens.title: Gold mask from Mycenae
tokens.description: The Mask of Agamemnon is a gold funerary mask found at the Bronze Age site of Mycenae in southern Greece by Heinrich Schliemann in 1876. It is displayed in the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.
tokens.image_credit: Gleb Simonov · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Priam's Treasure
tokens.title: Schliemann's find at Troy
tokens.description: Priam's Treasure is a cache of gold artifacts found by Frank Calvert and Heinrich Schliemann at Hisarlik in northwestern Turkey in the late 19th century. Schliemann linked the find to the Homeric king Priam, and most of it is now in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: sailko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Riace bronzes
tokens.title: Bronze warriors from the sea
tokens.description: The Riace bronzes are two full-size Greek bronze statues of nude, bearded men, cast by the lost-wax process. They were found in the sea off Riace Marina in Calabria in 1972 and are displayed in Reggio Calabria.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin Smith · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lady of Elche
tokens.title: Iberian stone bust
tokens.description: The Lady of Elche is a limestone bust discovered in 1897 at La Alcudia, an archaeological site near Elche in Spain. It is generally dated to the 4th century BC and is exhibited in the National Archaeological Museum of Spain in Madrid.
tokens.image_credit: Luis Fernández García · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gundestrup cauldron
tokens.title: Silver vessel from a bog
tokens.description: The Gundestrup cauldron is a richly decorated silver vessel dated to roughly 200 BC to 300 AD, the largest known European Iron Age silver work. It was found dismantled in a peat bog near Gundestrup, Denmark, in 1891.

tokens.name: Oseberg ship
tokens.title: Viking ship burial
tokens.description: The Oseberg ship is a well-preserved Viking Age longship found in a burial mound at Oseberg farm near Tonsberg, Norway, in 1904. It is now displayed at the Viking Ship Museum in Oslo.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tollund Man
tokens.title: Bog body from Jutland
tokens.description: The Tollund Man is a naturally mummified bog body of a man who died between 405 and 384 BCE. He was found in 1950 in a peat bog near Silkeborg in Jutland, Denmark.

tokens.name: Lindow Man
tokens.title: Bog body from Cheshire
tokens.description: Lindow Man is the preserved bog body of a man found on 1 August 1984 by peat cutters at Lindow Moss near Wilmslow in Cheshire, England. The remains are dated to the Iron Age or Roman period.

tokens.name: Peking Man
tokens.title: Fossils at Zhoukoudian
tokens.description: Peking Man is a subspecies of Homo erectus whose fossils were found in a cave at Zhoukoudian, about 50 km southwest of Beijing. The first tooth was found in 1921, and the site has become the most productive H. erectus site in the world.

tokens.name: Java Man
tokens.title: Fossils at Trinil
tokens.description: Java Man is an early human fossil, a skullcap, tooth and thighbone, found in 1891 and 1892 at Trinil on the Solo River in East Java, Indonesia. It is the type specimen for Homo erectus.

tokens.name: Homo floresiensis
tokens.title: The hobbit of Flores
tokens.description: Homo floresiensis is an extinct species of small archaic humans, nicknamed the Hobbit, that lived on Flores, Indonesia, until about 50,000 years ago. Its remains were discovered in 2003 at Liang Bua cave.
tokens.image_credit: Rosino · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Homo naledi
tokens.title: Fossils in the Rising Star Cave
tokens.description: Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng, South Africa, in the Cradle of Humankind. The fossils date to about 335,000 to 236,000 years ago.

tokens.name: Neanderthal 1
tokens.title: Type specimen from the Neander Valley
tokens.description: Neanderthal 1, also called Feldhofer 1, is the roughly 40,000-year-old type specimen of Homo neanderthalensis. It was found in August 1856 in the Kleine Feldhofer Grotte in the Neander Valley near Düsseldorf.

tokens.name: Nag Hammadi library
tokens.title: Codices found in a jar
tokens.description: The Nag Hammadi library is a collection of early Christian and Gnostic texts, twelve papyrus codices in a sealed jar. A farmer and others found it near the Upper Egyptian town of Nag Hammadi in 1945.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cyrus Cylinder
tokens.title: Clay cylinder from Babylon
tokens.description: The Cyrus Cylinder is a broken clay cylinder with an Achaemenid royal inscription in Akkadian cuneiform in the name of Cyrus the Great. It was found in 1879 in the foundations of the Esagila temple at Babylon, now in Iraq, and is held by the British Museum.
tokens.image_credit: Prioryman · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Code of Hammurabi
tokens.title: Law stele found at Susa
tokens.description: The Code of Hammurabi is a Babylonian legal text composed around 1753 BC, inscribed on a basalt stele 2.25 m tall. The primary copy was found at Susa in present-day Iran and is now in the Louvre.
tokens.image_credit: Mbzt · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nefertiti Bust
tokens.title: Bust found at Amarna
tokens.description: The Nefertiti Bust is a painted stucco-coated limestone bust of Nefertiti, the Great Royal Wife of Akhenaten. It was found in the sculpture workshop of Thutmose at Amarna in Egypt and is displayed in the Neues Museum in Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: Giovanni from Firenze, Italy · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Benin Expedition of 1897
tokens.title: Sack of Benin City
tokens.description: The Benin Expedition of 1897 was the British conquest of the Kingdom of Benin after a British party was attacked in January 1897. Benin City was taken and the kingdom was annexed into colonial Nigeria.
tokens.image_credit: Reginald Kerr Granville (d.1912) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coyolxauhqui Stone
tokens.title: Disc that revealed the Templo Mayor
tokens.description: The Coyolxauhqui Stone is a carved circular Aztec relief of the mythical being Coyolxauhqui, dismembered by Huitzilopochtli. It was rediscovered in 1978 at the base of the Templo Mayor in Mexico City.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aztec sun stone
tokens.title: Found in the Zócalo
tokens.description: The Aztec sun stone, also called Piedra del Sol, is a Mexica monolith weighing about 24.6 tonnes. It was found buried in the Zocalo, Mexico City's main square, and is now housed in the National Museum of Anthropology.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY exact title capitalisation

tokens.image_credit: Jonathan Cardy · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heinkel He 178
tokens.title: First jet aircraft flight
tokens.description: The Heinkel He 178 was an experimental aircraft that became the first to fly using a turbojet engine. It first flew on 27 August 1939 from the Heinkel airfield at Rostock-Marienehe.

tokens.name: Gloster E.28/39
tokens.title: First British jet flight
tokens.description: The Gloster E.28/39 was the first British turbojet-engined aircraft, built to test Frank Whittle's jet propulsion designs. It first flew in 1941 from RAF Cranwell in Lincolnshire.

tokens.name: Vought-Sikorsky VS-300
tokens.title: Pioneering helicopter
tokens.description: The Vought-Sikorsky VS-300 was a single-rotor helicopter designed by Igor Sikorsky. Its first free flight took place on 13 May 1940 at Sikorsky's works in Stratford, Connecticut.

tokens.name: Zeppelin LZ 1
tokens.title: First Zeppelin flight
tokens.description: The Zeppelin LZ 1 was the first successful experimental rigid airship. It first flew on 2 July 1900 from a floating hangar on Lake Constance near Friedrichshafen, Germany.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Scherer · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hughes H-4 Hercules
tokens.title: The Spruce Goose flies once
tokens.description: The Hughes H-4 Hercules, nicknamed the Spruce Goose, was a wooden flying boat built by Howard Hughes. It made its only brief flight over Long Beach harbour, California, on 2 November 1947.

tokens.name: R101
tokens.title: Airship crash near Beauvais
tokens.description: R101 was a British rigid airship, the largest flying craft of its time, that crashed on 5 October 1930 during its first flight to India. The crash at Allonne, near Beauvais, killed 48 people.

tokens.name: MacCready Gossamer Albatross
tokens.title: Pedal-powered Channel crossing
tokens.description: The MacCready Gossamer Albatross, a human-powered aircraft, was pedalled across the English Channel on 12 June 1979. The flight from near Folkestone, England, ended on the beach at Cap Gris-Nez, France.

tokens.name: Concorde first flight
tokens.title: Supersonic airliner first flight
tokens.description: Concorde made its first flight from Toulouse on 2 March 1969. The Anglo-French supersonic airliner was jointly developed by Sud Aviation and the British Aircraft Corporation.
tokens.image_credit: André Cros · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boeing 747 first flight
tokens.title: First flight of the jumbo jet
tokens.description: The Boeing 747 made its first flight on 9 February 1969 from Paine Field in Everett, Washington. The wide-body jumbo jet was designed by Boeing for long-range airline service.

tokens.name: Airbus A380 first flight
tokens.title: First flight of the superjumbo
tokens.description: The Airbus A380 made its maiden flight on 27 April 2005 from Toulouse-Blagnac airport in France. It is the world's largest passenger airliner and the only full-length double-deck jet airliner.

tokens.name: de Havilland Comet first jet airliner
tokens.title: First jet airliner
tokens.description: The de Havilland Comet 1 prototype first flew in 1949, making the Comet the world's first commercial jet airliner. The four-engine aircraft was developed and manufactured by de Havilland in the United Kingdom.

tokens.name: Rainhill trials
tokens.title: Rocket wins the locomotive contest
tokens.description: The Rainhill trials were held from 6 to 14 October 1829 at Rainhill, Lancashire, to choose the locomotive for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway. George Stephenson's Rocket was the only entrant to complete the trials and was declared the winner.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Benz Patent-Motorwagen first automobile patent
tokens.title: The first automobile patent
tokens.description: Carl Benz received German patent DRP 37435 in 1886 for the belt-drive layout of his Patent-Motorwagen. The three-wheeled car with a single-cylinder four-stroke engine is known as the world's first practical production automobile.

tokens.name: First words over the telephone wire
tokens.title: First words over the wire
tokens.description: On 10 March 1876 Alexander Graham Bell transmitted the first intelligible sentence over a telephone wire, from a laboratory at 5 Exeter Place in Boston. The invention was contested by several inventors, including Antonio Meucci, Philipp Reis and Elisha Gray.

tokens.name: Transatlantic telegraph cable
tokens.title: Wire across the ocean
tokens.description: The first transatlantic telegraph cable was laid from Valentia Island, off the west coast of Ireland, to Newfoundland, starting in 1858. The Atlantic Telegraph Company led by Cyrus West Field built the cable, and a successful link followed in 1866.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Charles Dudley · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Metropolitan Railway
tokens.title: World's first underground railway
tokens.description: The Metropolitan Railway opened in 1863 as the world's first underground railway, linking the London main-line termini at Paddington, Euston and King's Cross with the City. It was built mainly by cut-and-cover beneath the New Road.
tokens.image_credit: Percy William Justyne · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2018 lower Puna eruption
tokens.title: Lava through Leilani Estates
tokens.description: The 2018 lower Puna eruption began on 3 May 2018 on the East Rift Zone of Kilauea volcano on Hawaii island. Lava fountains and flows reached the Leilani Estates subdivision.
tokens.image_credit: United States Government · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1994 Northridge earthquake
tokens.title: Quake in the San Fernando Valley
tokens.description: The 1994 Northridge earthquake struck Greater Los Angeles on 17 January 1994 with a moment magnitude of 6.7. Its epicentre lay beneath the San Fernando Valley, and it is the largest recorded earthquake in the area's history.
tokens.image_credit: Robert A. Eplett · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1963 Skopje earthquake
tokens.title: City largely destroyed
tokens.description: The 1963 Skopje earthquake struck the city of Skopje in present-day North Macedonia with a moment magnitude of 6.1 and Mercalli intensity X. More than 1,000 people died and over 200,000 were left homeless.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1980 Irpinia earthquake
tokens.title: Quake in southern Italy
tokens.description: The 1980 Irpinia earthquake struck southern Italy on 23 November 1980 with a moment magnitude of 6.9 and Mercalli intensity X. It killed at least 2,483 people and left about 250,000 homeless.
tokens.image_credit: Pro Loco Compsa · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1977 Vrancea earthquake
tokens.title: Bucharest buildings collapse
tokens.description: The 1977 Vrancea earthquake struck on 4 March 1977 with a magnitude of 7.5 and was felt throughout the Balkans. Its hypocentre lay 85 km deep in the Vrancea Mountains, Romania's most seismically active zone.
tokens.image_credit: Uncredited photograph, National Bureau of Standards · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1960 Agadir earthquake
tokens.title: Moroccan city destroyed
tokens.description: The 1960 Agadir earthquake struck near the city of Agadir in western Morocco on 29 February 1960, with a magnitude of 5.8 and Mercalli intensity X. It killed between 12,000 and 15,000 people, the deadliest earthquake in Moroccan history.
tokens.image_credit: American Red Cross, Boston Metropolitan Chapter · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2018 Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
tokens.title: Tsunami hits Palu
tokens.description: On 28 September 2018 a shallow magnitude 7.5 to 7.6 earthquake struck Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, and triggered a tsunami that hit the Palu area. The epicentre lay in Donggala Regency, about 70 km from Palu.
tokens.image_credit: Devina Andiviaty · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Francis Dam disaster
tokens.title: Dam collapse near Los Angeles
tokens.description: The St. Francis Dam was a concrete gravity-arch dam in San Francisquito Canyon, northern Los Angeles County, built from 1924 to 1926. Its failure in 1928 sent a flood down the canyon that killed at least 431 people.
tokens.image_credit: Los Angeles Daily News · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malpasset Dam disaster
tokens.title: Dam burst above Fréjus
tokens.description: The Malpasset Dam was an arch dam on the Reyran River north of Fréjus on the French Riviera. Its collapse on 2 December 1959 sent a flood that killed 423 people.

tokens.name: Teton Dam failure
tokens.title: Dam fails on first filling
tokens.description: The Teton Dam was an earthen dam on the Teton River in eastern Idaho, built by the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation. It failed catastrophically on 5 June 1976 while filling for the first time.
tokens.image_credit: WaterArchives.org from Sacramento, California, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1991 Bangladesh cyclone
tokens.title: Cyclone strikes Chittagong
tokens.description: The 1991 Bangladesh cyclone was a super cyclonic storm that struck the coast near Chittagong on 29 April 1991. It is one of the deadliest tropical cyclones in recorded history.
tokens.image_credit: Airman 1st Class Cheryl Sanzi (USAF) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1999 Odisha cyclone
tokens.title: Super cyclone hits the coast
tokens.description: The 1999 Odisha cyclone was the most intense tropical cyclone ever recorded in the North Indian Ocean. It made landfall on the Odisha coast near Paradip on 29 October 1999.
tokens.image_credit: MVIRI imagery on the Meteosat-5 satellite, colorized by Sanoxel 2.0 · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Camille
tokens.title: Landfall in Mississippi
tokens.description: Hurricane Camille was a Category 5 hurricane that made landfall in southern Mississippi in August 1969. It was one of the most powerful hurricanes to strike the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Image taken by the Coast and Geodetic Survey · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Ian
tokens.title: Landfall in southwest Florida
tokens.description: Hurricane Ian was a catastrophic tropical cyclone that made landfall at Cayo Costa, Florida, on 28 September 2022. It was the deadliest hurricane to strike Florida since 1935 and the third costliest weather disaster on record worldwide.
tokens.image_credit: University of Wisconsin-Madison, Space Science and Engineering Center · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Helene
tokens.title: Floods in the Appalachians
tokens.description: Hurricane Helene struck the southeastern United States in late September 2024, causing catastrophic floods in the southern Appalachians. It was the deadliest Atlantic hurricane since Hurricane Maria in 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Bill McMannis · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurricane Otis
tokens.title: Rapid intensification at Acapulco
tokens.description: Hurricane Otis made landfall near Acapulco, Mexico, as a Category 5 storm in October 2023. It was the strongest Pacific hurricane to reach land and the costliest tropical cyclone to strike Mexico on record.
tokens.image_credit: ProtoplasmaKid · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1935 Labor Day hurricane
tokens.title: Strikes the Florida Keys
tokens.description: The 1935 Labor Day hurricane struck the Florida Keys and the southeastern United States in early September 1935 as a Category 5 storm. It was the most intense Atlantic hurricane on record for several decades.
tokens.image_credit: Florida Keys--Public Libraries · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1938 New England hurricane
tokens.title: The Long Island Express
tokens.description: The 1938 New England hurricane, also called the Long Island Express, made landfall on Long Island as a Category 3 storm on September 21, 1938. It is estimated to have killed 682 people and destroyed or damaged more than 57,000 homes.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Hurricane of 1780
tokens.title: Deadliest Atlantic hurricane
tokens.description: The Great Hurricane of 1780 crossed the Lesser Antilles from 10 to 16 October 1780. An estimated 22,000 people died, making it the deadliest tropical cyclone in the Western Hemisphere.

tokens.name: 2013 Moore tornado
tokens.title: EF5 tornado in Oklahoma
tokens.description: The 2013 Moore tornado was an EF5 tornado that struck Moore, Oklahoma, on May 20, 2013, killing 24 people. Peak winds were estimated at 200 to 210 mph.
tokens.image_credit: Ks0stm · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Joplin tornado
tokens.title: Tornado through Joplin
tokens.description: The Joplin tornado was an EF5 tornado that struck Joplin, Missouri, on May 22, 2011, causing catastrophic damage across the city. It tracked through the southern part of Joplin before dissipating in rural counties.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2013 El Reno tornado
tokens.title: The widest tornado recorded
tokens.description: The 2013 El Reno tornado was a large, erratic multiple-vortex tornado that struck rural central Oklahoma on May 31, 2013. It was the widest tornado ever recorded, peaking at 2.6 miles across.

tokens.name: 2021 European floods
tokens.title: Floods in the Ahr valley
tokens.description: In July 2021 heavy rain caused severe flash floods in several European countries, killing many people. The Ahr valley in western Germany, where this token sits, was among the worst hit areas.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Seifert (CnndrBrbr at German Wikipedia) · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1966 flood of the Arno
tokens.title: Florence's art under water
tokens.description: The flood of the Arno on 4 November 1966 killed 35 people in Florence and damaged or destroyed millions of works of art and rare books. Volunteers known as the Mud Angels helped restore many of them.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 1910 Great Flood of Paris
tokens.title: The Seine floods Paris
tokens.description: In January 1910 the Seine rose about eight metres above its ordinary level and flooded the Paris conurbation. The token sits at the centre of Paris, on the river.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2013 North India floods
tokens.title: Kedarnath swept by flood
tokens.description: A cloudburst in June 2013 centred on Uttarakhand caused devastating floods and landslides, the worst natural disaster in India since the 2004 tsunami. The token sits at Kedarnath, a pilgrimage town badly hit by the flood.

tokens.name: 2023 Hawaii wildfires
tokens.title: Lahaina burns
tokens.description: Wind-driven wildfires in August 2023 killed at least 102 people, most of them in the town of Lahaina on Maui. The token sits at Lahaina, where the fire destroyed much of the historic town.
tokens.image_credit: Dominick Del Vecchio · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peshtigo fire
tokens.title: Deadliest US wildfire
tokens.description: The Peshtigo Fire of 8 October 1871 burned about 1.2 million acres in northeastern Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. It is the deadliest wildfire in recorded history, with an estimated 1,500 to 2,500 deaths.
tokens.image_credit: G. J. Tisdale · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mann Gulch fire
tokens.title: Smokejumpers caught by fire
tokens.description: The Mann Gulch fire started on 5 August 1949 in western Montana, where the fire overran a team of smokejumpers and 13 of the 16 men died. The token sits at the gulch in the Gates of the Mountains Wilderness.

tokens.name: 2018 Attica wildfires
tokens.title: Fire reaches Mati
tokens.description: A series of wildfires in the Attica region of Greece, during the 2018 European heat wave, killed 104 people, mostly in the Mati area. At the time they were the second-deadliest wildfire event of the 21st century.

tokens.name: 1999 Galtür avalanche
tokens.title: Avalanche hits an Alpine village
tokens.description: A powder avalanche struck the Alpine village of Galtür in Austria on 23 February 1999, burying 57 people. By the time rescue crews arrived, 31 people had died.

tokens.name: 2014 Oso landslide
tokens.title: Hillside collapses on a village
tokens.description: A hillside collapsed on 22 March 2014 near Oso, Washington, sending mud and debris across the North Fork Stillaguamish River. The slide engulfed a rural neighborhood and covered about one square mile.
tokens.image_credit: Spc. Samantha Ciaramitaro · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Peigneur
tokens.title: Lake drains into a salt mine
tokens.description: Lake Peigneur is a brackish lake in Louisiana, USA, north of Delcambre near Vermilion Bay. A human-caused disaster on 20 November 1980 changed the lake and the land around it.

tokens.name: Centralia mine fire
tokens.title: Fire burning under a town
tokens.description: A coal-seam fire has burned in abandoned mines beneath the borough of Centralia, Pennsylvania, since at least 1962. It burns up to 300 feet deep across about 3,700 acres.
tokens.image_credit: LaesaMajestas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quecreek Mine rescue
tokens.title: Nine miners rescued
tokens.description: Nine miners were trapped for over 77 hours in the Quecreek Mine in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, from 24 to 28 July 2002. All nine were rescued.

tokens.name: Rescue of the Danish Jews
tokens.title: Boats across the Øresund
tokens.description: During the Second World War, the Danish resistance and many Danish citizens evacuated about 7,500 of Denmark's 8,000 Jews by sea to neutral Sweden. It is considered one of the largest acts of collective resistance in Nazi-occupied Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Nationalmuseet - National Museum of Denmark from Denmark · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Solomon
tokens.title: Airlift from Addis Ababa
tokens.description: Operation Solomon was a covert Israel Defense Forces airlift from 24 to 25 May 1991. Non-stop flights carried 14,325 Ethiopian Jews to Israel in 36 hours.
tokens.image_credit: Tsvika Israeli · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Operation Frequent Wind
tokens.title: Helicopter evacuation of Saigon
tokens.description: Operation Frequent Wind was the final phase of the evacuation of American civilians and at-risk Vietnamese from Saigon. More than 7,000 people were lifted out by helicopter on 29 and 30 April 1975, during the last days of the Vietnam War.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Marines (Official Marine Corps Photo)(http://www.tecom.usmc.mil/HD/Home_Page.htm) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Air Florida Flight 90
tokens.title: Crash into the frozen Potomac
tokens.description: Air Florida Flight 90 was a scheduled domestic flight from Washington National Airport that struck the 14th Street Bridge just after takeoff on 13 January 1982. The Boeing 737 then plunged through the ice into the Potomac River, with heavy loss of life.
tokens.image_credit: FAA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pacific Southwest Airlines Flight 182
tokens.title: Mid-air collision over San Diego
tokens.description: Pacific Southwest Airlines Flight 182 was a scheduled flight from Sacramento to San Diego that collided mid-air with a private Cessna 172 over San Diego on 25 September 1978. It remains the deadliest air disaster in California history.

tokens.name: 1956 Grand Canyon mid-air collision
tokens.title: Airliners collide over the canyon
tokens.description: On 30 June 1956 a TWA Lockheed Constellation was struck by a United Air Lines DC-7 over Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. All 128 people on both aircraft died, the first commercial airline accident to exceed one hundred fatalities.
tokens.image_credit: National Park Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aloha Airlines Flight 243
tokens.title: Roof torn away in flight
tokens.description: Aloha Airlines Flight 243 was a scheduled Boeing 737 flight from Hilo to Honolulu that suffered explosive decompression in flight on 28 April 1988. The aircraft, with a large section of its roof torn away, landed safely at Kahului Airport on Maui.
tokens.image_credit: Federal Aviation Administration · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: United Airlines Flight 232
tokens.title: Crash landing at Sioux City
tokens.description: United Airlines Flight 232 was a DC-10 flight from Denver to Philadelphia whose tail engine failure destroyed all flight controls. It crash-landed at Sioux Gateway Airport in Sioux City, Iowa, on 19 July 1989, and 112 of the 296 people on board died.
tokens.image_credit: FAA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: British Airways Flight 009
tokens.title: Engines stall in volcanic ash
tokens.description: British Airways Flight 009 was a Boeing 747 from London to Auckland that flew into the volcanic ash cloud of the Mount Galunggung eruption in Java on 24 June 1982. All four engines failed, and the aircraft was later landed safely at Jakarta.

tokens.name: Eschede train disaster
tokens.title: High-speed derailment
tokens.description: The Eschede train disaster occurred on 3 June 1998, when an ICE 1 high-speed train derailed near Eschede, Lower Saxony, and crashed into an overpass. It killed 101 people and is the world's worst high-speed rail disaster.
tokens.image_credit: Nils Fretwurst · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santiago de Compostela derailment
tokens.title: Derailment on a curve
tokens.description: On 24 July 2013, an Alvia high-speed train from Madrid to Ferrol derailed on a curve near Santiago de Compostela, Spain. The accident killed 79 people and injured 178.
tokens.image_credit: Xosema · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quintinshill rail disaster
tokens.title: Britain's worst rail crash
tokens.description: A multi-train rail crash on 22 May 1915 at Quintinshill near Gretna Green, Scotland, killed over 200 people. It remains the worst rail disaster in British history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Train Robbery 1963
tokens.title: Mail train robbed at Bridego Bridge
tokens.description: On 8 August 1963 a gang of 15, led by Bruce Reynolds, stopped a Royal Mail train at Bridego Railway Bridge near Mentmore, Buckinghamshire, and stole £2.61 million.

tokens.name: Hatton Garden safe deposit burglary
tokens.title: Elderly gang drills a vault
tokens.description: In April 2015 burglars broke into the Hatton Garden Safe Deposit vault in London over the Easter weekend. Official estimates put the stolen value at up to £14 million.

tokens.name: June 1962 Alcatraz escape
tokens.title: Escape from the Rock
tokens.description: On the night of 11 June 1962 Frank Morris and the brothers John and Clarence Anglin escaped from Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in San Francisco Bay, using dummy heads in their beds. Their fate remains uncertain.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY exact title

tokens.image_credit: FBI · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ponte Morandi collapse
tokens.title: Viaduct collapses in Genoa
tokens.description: On 14 August 2018 a section of the Ponte Morandi motorway viaduct in Genoa, Italy, collapsed during a rainstorm, killing 43 people. The remains were demolished in 2019.

tokens.name: Surfside condominium collapse
tokens.title: Champlain Towers collapse
tokens.description: On 24 June 2021 the 12-storey Champlain Towers South condominium in Surfside, near Miami, Florida, partially collapsed. The collapse killed 98 people.
tokens.image_credit: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Department. The original uploader was TheEpicGhosty at English Wikipedia. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hyatt Regency walkway collapse
tokens.title: Walkways fall in Kansas City
tokens.description: On 17 July 1981 two overhead walkways in the Hyatt Regency Hotel in Kansas City, Missouri, collapsed onto a tea dance in the lobby. The collapse killed 114 people and injured 216.

tokens.name: I-35W Mississippi River bridge collapse
tokens.title: Bridge collapse in Minneapolis
tokens.description: The I-35W Mississippi River bridge in Minneapolis, Minnesota, collapsed during the evening rush hour on August 1, 2007, killing 13 people and injuring 145. The eight-lane steel truss arch bridge had opened in 1967.
tokens.image_credit: Eric from Minneapolis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iroquois Theatre fire
tokens.title: Deadliest theatre fire in the US
tokens.description: The Iroquois Theatre fire broke out in Chicago, Illinois, on December 30, 1903, during a performance attended by about 1,700 people. It killed 602 people and is the worst theatre fire in United States history.
tokens.image_credit: Charles N. Landon · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cocoanut Grove fire
tokens.title: Nightclub fire in Boston
tokens.description: The Cocoanut Grove fire was a nightclub fire in Boston, Massachusetts, on November 28, 1942, which killed 492 people. It is the deadliest nightclub fire in history.

tokens.name: National Museum of Brazil fire
tokens.title: Collections lost to fire
tokens.description: A large fire broke out at the National Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro on 2 September 2018. About 92 percent of its archive of 20 million items is believed to have been destroyed.
tokens.image_credit: Felipe Milanez · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: King's Cross fire
tokens.title: Fire in the Underground station
tokens.description: The King's Cross fire broke out on 18 November 1987 at King's Cross St Pancras Underground station in London. It began under a wooden escalator and spread into the ticket hall, killing 31 people.
tokens.image_credit: Christopher Newberry · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bradford City stadium fire
tokens.title: Stand catches fire during a match
tokens.description: The Bradford City stadium fire broke out during a Football League Third Division match at Valley Parade in Bradford, England, on 11 May 1985. It killed 56 spectators and injured at least 265.

tokens.name: Texas City disaster
tokens.title: Ship explosion in the port
tokens.description: The Texas City disaster was an explosion on 16 April 1947 in the port of Texas City, Texas, after the French ship Grandcamp detonated its cargo of ammonium nitrate. It was the deadliest industrial accident in United States history.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port Chicago disaster
tokens.title: Munitions explosion
tokens.description: The Port Chicago disaster was a munitions explosion on July 17, 1944, at the Port Chicago Naval Magazine in California. The blast of the ship SS E. A. Bryan killed 320 sailors and civilians and injured at least 390 others.
tokens.image_credit: Mare Island Navy Yard · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 2015 Tianjin explosions
tokens.title: Blasts at a port warehouse
tokens.description: On 12 August 2015, a series of explosions at a container storage station in the Port of Tianjin, China, killed 173 people according to official reports. Hundreds of others were injured.
tokens.image_credit: Voice of America/美国之音 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Enschede fireworks disaster
tokens.title: Fireworks depot explodes
tokens.description: The Enschede fireworks disaster was a fireworks explosion on 13 May 2000 in Enschede, Netherlands. It killed 23 people, including four firefighters, injured about 950 others and destroyed 400 homes.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Bartflikweert at Dutch Wikipedia.. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Silvertown explosion
tokens.title: Munitions factory explosion
tokens.description: The Silvertown explosion occurred on 19 January 1917 at a munitions factory in Silvertown, West Ham, Essex. About 50 tonnes of TNT exploded, killing 73 people and injuring around 400 more.
tokens.image_credit: Avery, John · PD-US · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kiyomizu-dera
tokens.title: Wooden temple stage over Kyoto
tokens.description: Kiyomizu-dera is a Buddhist temple in eastern Kyoto, Japan, belonging to the Kita-Hosso sect. Its wooden stage projects over the hillside and it is part of the UNESCO Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sensō-ji
tokens.title: Tokyo's oldest temple
tokens.description: Sensō-ji is an ancient Buddhist temple in Asakusa, Tokyo, dedicated to Kannon, the bodhisattva of compassion. It is Tokyo's oldest established temple.
tokens.image_credit: Akonnchiroll · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokyo Tower
tokens.title: Red lattice tower
tokens.description: Tokyo Tower is a communications and observation tower in Shiba-koen, Minato, Tokyo, completed in 1958. At 332.9 metres it was Japan's tallest tower until Tokyo Skytree opened in 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Akonnchiroll · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Osaka Castle
tokens.title: Castle of Toyotomi Hideyoshi
tokens.description: Osaka Castle is a Japanese castle in Chuo-ku, Osaka, built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in the late 16th century. It played a major role in the unification of Japan during the Azuchi-Momoyama period.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matsumoto Castle
tokens.title: Black crow castle
tokens.description: Matsumoto Castle is a historic castle in Matsumoto, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is one of Japan's premier historic castles, along with Himeji and Kumamoto, and was the seat of Matsumoto Domain.
tokens.image_credit: Lightning toothed whale (稲妻ノ歯鯨) This photo was taken with Canon EOS 500D · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nijō Castle
tokens.title: Shogun palace in Kyoto
tokens.description: Nijō Castle is a flatland castle in Kyoto, Japan, built by the Tokugawa shogunate as its Kyoto residence. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.
tokens.image_credit: Keith Pomakis · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kumamoto Castle
tokens.title: Fortress of Kumamoto
tokens.description: Kumamoto Castle is a hilltop Japanese castle in Chuo-ku, Kumamoto, Kumamoto Prefecture. Its keep is a concrete reconstruction built in 1960, and several original wooden buildings remain.
tokens.image_credit: Suicasmo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shirakami-Sanchi
tokens.title: Primeval beech forest
tokens.description: Shirakami-Sanchi is a UNESCO World Heritage wilderness area in the Tohoku region of northern Honshu, Japan, straddling Aomori and Akita prefectures. It includes the last virgin forest of Japanese beech that once covered much of northern Japan.
tokens.image_credit: らんで · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yakushima
tokens.title: Ancient cedar island
tokens.description: Yakushima is one of the Osumi Islands in Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan. Its ancient cedar forest is part of a natural UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Σ64 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Aso
tokens.title: Giant caldera volcano
tokens.description: Mount Aso is an active volcano on Kyushu in Aso Kuju National Park, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan. It is the second largest active volcano in Japan after Mount Fuji, with a large caldera.
tokens.image_credit: Miya.m · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sakurajima
tokens.title: Active volcano of Kagoshima
tokens.description: Sakurajima is an active stratovolcano in Kagoshima Prefecture on Kyushu, Japan. Formerly an island, it is now a peninsula and is the most active volcano in Japan.
tokens.image_credit: TANAKA Juuyoh (talk) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ise Shrine
tokens.title: Shinto shrine to Amaterasu
tokens.description: Ise Shrine is a complex of Shinto shrines in Ise, Mie Prefecture, dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu. It is widely regarded as the most important Shinto shrine and is rebuilt on a 20-year cycle.
tokens.image_credit: N yotarou · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kegon Falls
tokens.title: Nikko waterfall
tokens.description: Kegon Falls is a waterfall at Lake Chuzenji in Nikko National Park, Tochigi Prefecture. The main fall is about 97 metres high and it was formed when lava flows rerouted the Daiya River.
tokens.image_credit: くろふね · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Biwa
tokens.title: Largest lake in Japan
tokens.description: Lake Biwa is the largest freshwater lake in Japan, located entirely within Shiga Prefecture. It is an ancient lake, more than four million years old.
tokens.image_credit: Luka Peternel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shiretoko National Park
tokens.title: Wild northern Hokkaido
tokens.description: Shiretoko National Park covers most of the Shiretoko Peninsula at the northeastern tip of Hokkaido, Japan. The peninsula is one of the most remote regions in Japan and is reachable only on foot or by boat.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kushiro-shitsugen National Park
tokens.description: Kushiro-shitsugen National Park is located in eastern Hokkaido, Japan, and was designated a national park in 1987. The park is known for its wetland ecosystems, centred on one of the largest marshes in Japan.
tokens.image_credit: 欅 (Keyaki) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bonin Islands
tokens.title: Galapagos of the East
tokens.description: The Bonin Islands, also known as the Ogasawara Islands, are a group of more than 30 subtropical islands about 1,000 km south-southeast of Tokyo. They were inscribed as a UNESCO natural World Heritage site in 2011.
tokens.image_credit: しんかわな · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hōryū-ji
tokens.title: Oldest wooden buildings on Earth
tokens.description: Hōryū-ji is a Buddhist temple in Ikaruga, Nara Prefecture, Japan, built shortly after Buddhism reached the country. Its wooden buildings are among the oldest surviving wooden structures in the world.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Byōdō-in
tokens.title: Phoenix Hall
tokens.description: Byōdō-in is a Buddhist temple in Uji, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan, founded in 1052 by Fujiwara no Yorimichi. Its Phoenix Hall is a well-known Heian-period building, and the temple is part of the Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto UNESCO site.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ginkaku-ji
tokens.title: Silver Pavilion
tokens.description: Ginkaku-ji, officially Jisho-ji, is a Zen temple in Sakyo ward, Kyoto, Japan. It is one of the constructions representing the Higashiyama Culture of the Muromachi period and part of the UNESCO Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.
tokens.image_credit: 掬茶 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ryōan-ji
tokens.title: Zen rock garden
tokens.description: Ryōan-ji is a Zen temple in northwest Kyoto, Japan, of the Myōshin-ji school of Rinzai Zen Buddhism. Its dry landscape garden is considered one of the finest surviving examples of kare-sansui.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tenryū-ji
tokens.description: Tenryū-ji is the head temple of the Tenryū-ji branch of the Rinzai sect of Zen Buddhism, in Ukyō Ward, Kyoto, Japan. It was founded by Ashikaga Takauji in 1339 and is part of the UNESCO Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.
tokens.image_credit: osakaosaka · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kenroku-en
tokens.title: Garden of Kanazawa
tokens.description: Kenroku-en is a strolling garden in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, Japan, built during the Edo period by the Maeda clan. It is one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan, along with Kairaku-en and Kōraku-en.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kōraku-en
tokens.title: Garden of Okayama
tokens.description: Kōraku-en is a Japanese garden in Okayama, Okayama Prefecture, built in 1700 by Ikeda Tsunamasa, lord of Okayama. It is one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan, along with Kenroku-en and Kairaku-en.
tokens.image_credit: 663highland · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Heaven
tokens.title: Ming-Qing sacrificial altar
tokens.description: The Temple of Heaven is a complex of imperial Confucian religious buildings in southeastern central Beijing, China. The Ming and Qing emperors used it for annual prayers to Heaven for a good harvest, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Shujianyang · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang
tokens.title: Tomb of Qin Shi Huang
tokens.description: The Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang is a tomb complex built for Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China, in Lintong District, Xi'an, Shaanxi. It was constructed from 246 to 208 BC beneath a 76-metre tomb mound and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Aaron Zhu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wulingyuan
tokens.title: Sandstone pillar scenic area
tokens.description: Wulingyuan is a scenic and historical site in Wulingyuan District, Hunan Province, China. It is known for more than 3,000 quartzite sandstone pillars and peaks, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huanglong Scenic and Historic Interest Area
tokens.title: Travertine terraces
tokens.description: Huanglong is a scenic and historic interest area in northwest Sichuan, China, in the southern Minshan range. It is known for its travertine terraces and turquoise limestone pools, and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Kounosu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yangtze
tokens.title: Longest river of Asia
tokens.description: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and the third-longest river in the world, flowing about 6,300 km from the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea. It is the fifth-largest river by discharge volume.
tokens.image_credit: Tan Wei Liang Byorn · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yellow River
tokens.title: Cradle of Chinese civilization
tokens.description: The Yellow River, also called Huang He, is the second-longest river in China and the sixth-longest in the world, about 5,464 km long. It rises in the Bayan Har Mountains and flows into the Bohai Sea.
tokens.image_credit: fading · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: West Lake
tokens.title: Hangzhou's poetic lake
tokens.description: West Lake is a freshwater lake in Hangzhou, eastern China, with a surface area of 6.39 square kilometres. Its shores and islands hold temples, pagodas and gardens, and the West Lake Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Louisa Salazar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Classical Gardens of Suzhou
tokens.title: Scholar gardens
tokens.description: The Classical Gardens of Suzhou are a group of scholars' gardens in Suzhou, Jiangsu, built between the Northern Song and the late Qing dynasties. They are a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Jakub Hałun · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Tai
tokens.title: Sacred eastern peak
tokens.description: Mount Tai is a mountain of historical and cultural significance north of Tai'an in Shandong province, China. Its highest point, the Jade Emperor Peak, is about 1,545 metres high, and the mountain is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Wutai
tokens.title: Buddhist sacred mountain
tokens.description: Mount Wutai is a sacred Buddhist mountain site in Shanxi Province, China. Its north peak, Beitai Ding, is 3,061 metres high and is the highest point in North China, and the site is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Zcm11 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Hua
tokens.title: Western sacred peak
tokens.description: Mount Hua is a mountain near Huayin in Shaanxi Province, China, about 120 km east of Xi'an. It is the Western Mountain of the Five Great Mountains of China and has a long religious history.
tokens.image_credit: Ondřej Žváček · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shaolin Monastery
tokens.title: Birthplace of Shaolin kung fu
tokens.description: Shaolin Monastery is a Buddhist monastery at the foot of Wuru Peak in the Mount Song range, Dengfeng, Henan, China. It is associated with the development of Chan Buddhism and Shaolin kung fu.
tokens.image_credit: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wudang Mountains
tokens.title: Taoist mountain complex
tokens.description: The Wudang Mountains are a mountain range in northwestern Hubei, China, home to a famous complex of Taoist temples and monasteries. The Ancient Building Complex in the Wudang Mountains has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lingyin Temple
tokens.title: Hangzhou Buddhist temple
tokens.description: Lingyin Temple is a prominent Chan Buddhist temple near Hangzhou, China, known for its many pagodas and grottos. It is the largest of several temples in the Wulin Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Tyg728 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: White Horse Temple
tokens.title: First Buddhist temple in China
tokens.description: White Horse Temple is a Buddhist temple in Luoyang, Henan Province, China. According to tradition it was founded in 68 AD and is the first Buddhist temple established in China.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dujiangyan
tokens.title: 2,000-year-old irrigation system
tokens.description: Dujiangyan is an ancient irrigation and flood control system on the Min River in Sichuan, China, begun around 256 BC and still in use. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Mount Qingcheng and the Dujiangyan Irrigation System.
tokens.image_credit: 星星 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fujian tulou
tokens.description: The Fujian tulou are round and square earthen buildings in the mountains of southeastern Fujian, China, built by the Hakka people mostly between the 12th and 20th centuries. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Scott Edmunds · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kaiping Diaolou
tokens.description: Diaolou are fortified multi-storey watchtowers in rural villages, mostly in Kaiping, Guangdong, China. The Kaiping Diaolou and Villages have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Fussan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pingyao
tokens.title: Walled Ming city
tokens.description: Pingyao is a walled city in central Shanxi, China, with its Ming and Qing street plan and buildings largely intact. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Nicor · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taklamakan Desert
tokens.title: Sea of death
tokens.description: The Taklamakan Desert is a desert in northwestern China, inside the Tarim Basin of southern Xinjiang. It is bounded by the Kunlun Mountains to the south and the Tian Shan range to the north.

tokens.name: Badain Jaran Desert
tokens.title: Tallest dunes on Earth
tokens.description: The Badain Jaran Desert is a desert in Gansu and Inner Mongolia, China, covering about 49,000 square kilometres. It is known for its very tall dunes and lakes between them, and it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.
tokens.image_credit: Sjoerd van Oort · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flaming Mountains
tokens.description: The Flaming Mountains, or Huoyan Mountains, are barren, eroded red sandstone hills in the Tian Shan of Xinjiang. They lie near the northern rim of the Taklamakan Desert, east of Turpan.

tokens.name: Karakul
tokens.description: The Karakul is a high glacial lake on the Karakoram Highway in Akto County, Xinjiang, China, about 196 km southwest of Kashgar. It lies near Muztagh Ata, one of the Pamir peaks.
tokens.image_credit: Yoshi Canopus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Qinghai Lake
tokens.description: Qinghai Lake is the largest lake in China, in Qinghai Province, which it gave its name to. It is an alkaline endorheic salt lake whose size has changed over the last century.
tokens.image_credit: Sergio Tittarini from Shanghai, China · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Namtso
tokens.title: Sacred Tibetan lake
tokens.description: Namtso is a high mountain lake on the Tibetan Plateau, about 112 km north-northwest of Lhasa, on the border of Damxung and Baingoin counties. It is also called Tengri Nor, the Heavenly Lake.
tokens.image_credit: Peter Vigier · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yamdrok Lake
tokens.title: Turquoise holy lake
tokens.description: Yamdrok Lake is a freshwater lake in southern Tibet, one of the three largest lakes in the region. It is more than 72 km long and lies south-west of Lhasa.
tokens.image_credit: Kkkwylin · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Kailash
tokens.title: Sacred peak of four religions
tokens.description: Mount Kailash is a 6,638 m mountain in Ngari Prefecture, Tibet, in the Gangdise Shan range. It is a sacred peak in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Bon.
tokens.image_credit: Ondřej Žváček · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Namcha Barwa
tokens.description: Namcha Barwa is a mountain peak in Nyingchi Prefecture, southeastern Tibet, at the eastern end of the Himalaya. It is the easternmost peak over 7,600 metres on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Cherry933 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huangguoshu Waterfall
tokens.title: Largest waterfall in China
tokens.description: Huangguoshu Waterfall is the largest waterfall in China and one of the largest in East Asia. It is located on the Liuzhi River in Anshun, Guizhou province.
tokens.image_credit: Kcx36 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tian Tan Buddha
tokens.title: Big Buddha of Lantau
tokens.description: The Tian Tan Buddha is a large bronze statue of Gautama Buddha, completed in 1993. It stands at Ngong Ping near Po Lin Monastery on Lantau Island, Hong Kong.
tokens.image_credit: Béria Lima de Rodríguez · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Historic Centre of Macau
tokens.title: Portuguese Chinese quarter
tokens.description: The Historic Centre of Macau is a UNESCO World Heritage collection of over twenty sites in Macau. It shows the blend of Chinese and Portuguese cultures through squares, streetscapes, churches and temples.
tokens.image_credit: Sdee at zh.wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ruins of Saint Paul's
tokens.title: Facade of Macau
tokens.description: The Ruins of Saint Paul's are the remnants of a 17th-century Catholic religious complex in Santo Antonio, Macau. The famous facade is all that remains of the former St. Paul's College and church.
tokens.image_credit: GG001213 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries
tokens.title: Panda homeland
tokens.description: The Sichuan Giant Panda Sanctuaries are a UNESCO World Heritage group of seven nature reserves and nine scenic parks in southwest Sichuan, China. They are home to more than 30% of the world's giant pandas.

tokens.name: Shennongjia
tokens.title: Primeval forest
tokens.description: Shennongjia is a forestry district in northwestern Hubei, China, covering about 3,253 square kilometres of mountain primeval forest. The area was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016 for its exceptional plant and animal biodiversity.
tokens.image_credit: Evilbish · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stone Forest
tokens.title: Karst stone forest
tokens.description: The Stone Forest, or Shilin, is a set of limestone pillars covering about 500 square kilometres in Shilin Yi Autonomous County, Yunnan, China. The site is part of the South China Karst UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jiayu Pass
tokens.title: End of Great Wall
tokens.description: Jiayu Pass is the first frontier fortress at the west end of the Ming dynasty Great Wall, near Jiayuguan city in Gansu province, China. It forms part of the Great Wall of China UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Zhangzhugang · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shanhai Pass
tokens.description: Shanhai Pass is a major fortified gateway at the eastern end of the Great Wall of China, in Qinhuangdao, Hebei. It commands the narrow Liaoxi Corridor between the Yan Mountains and the Bohai Sea and forms part of the Great Wall UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Nyx Ning · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oriental Pearl Tower
tokens.title: Shanghai icon
tokens.description: The Oriental Pearl Tower is a television tower in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai, built from 1991 to 1994. It is one of the best-known landmarks of the city and has fifteen observation decks.
tokens.image_credit: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images, but please mention me as the author and may send me a message. (สามารถใช้ภาพได้อิสระ แต่กรุณาใส่เครดิตผู้ถ่ายและอาจส่งข · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ming tombs
tokens.title: Imperial tombs
tokens.description: The Ming tombs are a collection of mausoleums built by the emperors of the Ming dynasty of China. The majority of them lie in a cluster near Beijing, known as the Thirteen Tombs of the Ming dynasty.
tokens.image_credit: Charlie fong · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hanging Temple
tokens.title: Temple clinging to a cliff
tokens.description: The Hanging Temple is a temple built into a cliff near Mount Heng in Hunyuan County, Datong City, Shanxi Province, China. Along with the Yungang Grottoes, it is one of the main tourist attractions in the Datong area.
tokens.image_credit: Charlie fong · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dazu Rock Carvings
tokens.title: Chongqing rock carvings
tokens.description: The Dazu Rock Carvings are a series of Chinese religious sculptures and carvings in Dazu District, Chongqing, China. The carvings date back to the 7th century AD and reflect Buddhist, Confucian and Taoist beliefs.
tokens.image_credit: G41rn8 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
tokens.title: Great mosque of Old Delhi
tokens.description: The Jama Masjid, also called Masjid-i-Jehan-Numa, is one of the largest mosques in India. Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built it between 1644 and 1656 as the imperial mosque of Shahjahanabad, today's Old Delhi.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Mahdi Karim · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: India Gate
tokens.title: War memorial of Delhi
tokens.description: India Gate is a war memorial arch near Rajpath in New Delhi. It commemorates 74,187 Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army who died between 1914 and 1921.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lotus Temple
tokens.title: Bahai house of worship
tokens.description: The Lotus Temple, also known as the Bahai House of Worship, is a Bahai house of worship at Bahapur in south Delhi, India. It was designed by architect Fariborz Sahba and dedicated on 24 December 1986.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Mahdi Karim · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
tokens.description: Swaminarayan Akshardham is a Hindu temple and campus in Delhi, India. The temple lies close to the border with Noida and displays traditional and modern Hindu culture and architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Swaminarayan Sanstha · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Agra Fort
tokens.title: Mughal red sandstone fort
tokens.description: Agra Fort, also called the Red Fort of Agra, is a historic fort in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. It was rebuilt in red sandstone by the Mughal emperor Akbar from 1565 to 1573 and was the main Mughal residence until 1638.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amber Fort
tokens.title: Hilltop fort near Jaipur
tokens.description: Amer Fort, also called Amber Fort, is a hilltop fort in Amer, Rajasthan, India. It lies about 11 kilometres from Jaipur and is part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan site.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hawa Mahal
tokens.title: Palace of Winds
tokens.description: The Hawa Mahal, also called the Palace of Winds, is a palace in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it was constructed in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.
tokens.image_credit: Donvikro · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: City Palace, Jaipur
tokens.description: The City Palace is a royal residence and former administrative seat of the rulers of Jaipur State in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Construction began after Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II moved his court to Jaipur from Amber in 1727.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
tokens.title: Maharaja's astronomical park
tokens.description: The Jantar Mantar is a collection of 19 astronomical instruments built by Sawai Jai Singh in Jaipur, completed in 1734. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Knowledge Seeker · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mehrangarh
tokens.title: Fort above Jodhpur
tokens.description: Mehrangarh is a historic fort on a hilltop in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, rising about 122 m above the plains. It was begun around 1459 by Rao Jodha, and most of the existing structure dates from the 17th century.
tokens.image_credit: Knowledge Seeker · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kumbhalgarh
tokens.title: Great wall of India
tokens.description: Kumbhalgarh is a 15th-century fortress on the Aravalli Hills in Rajasthan, India, built by Rana Kumbha. Its wall, about 36 km long, is one of the longest continuous walls in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Shivam Chaturvedi – Aryarakshak at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: City Palace, Udaipur
tokens.description: City Palace, also called Raj Mahal, is a palace complex in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India. Construction began in 1553 under Maharana Udai Singh II and continued over nearly 400 years.
tokens.image_credit: Henrik Bennetsen · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Pichola
tokens.title: Udaipur's lake
tokens.description: Lake Pichola is an artificial freshwater lake in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India, created in 1362. It is one of several lakes around the city, built by dams to supply drinking water and irrigation.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
tokens.description: The Jagannath Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Jagannath, a form of Vishnu. It is located in Puri, Odisha, on the eastern coast of India.
tokens.image_credit: Prachites · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Meenakshi Temple
tokens.title: Madurai temple city
tokens.description: Meenakshi Temple, also known as Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, is a historic Hindu temple on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva).
tokens.image_credit: Kumar Appaiah · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brihadisvara Temple
tokens.title: Chola temple
tokens.description: Brihadisvara Temple is a Shaivite Hindu temple in Chola architectural style on the south bank of the Cauvery river in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India. It is one of the largest Hindu temples and an exemplar of Tamil architecture.
tokens.image_credit: KARTY JazZ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Elephanta Caves
tokens.title: Shiva cave temples
tokens.description: The Elephanta Caves are a collection of cave temples predominantly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva, on Elephanta Island in Mumbai Harbour, India. UNESCO has designated them as a World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gateway of India
tokens.title: Mumbai's colonial arch
tokens.description: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument completed in 1924 on the waterfront of Mumbai, India. It was erected to commemorate the 1911 landing of King George V, the first British monarch to visit India.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
tokens.title: Victorian Gothic station
tokens.description: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus is a historic railway terminus and UNESCO World Heritage Site in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Designed by Frederick William Stevens in an Indo Gothic style, it was completed in 1887.
tokens.image_credit: Sailko · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mahabodhi Temple
tokens.title: Where the Buddha attained enlightenment
tokens.description: The Mahabodhi Temple is a restored Buddhist temple in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, India, marking the place where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the most revered pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide.
tokens.image_credit: Bpilgrim · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nalanda mahavihara
tokens.title: Ancient Buddhist university
tokens.description: Nalanda mahavihara was a renowned Buddhist monastery and centre of learning in Bihar, eastern India, operating from about 427 CE until around 1400 CE. Its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 2016.
tokens.image_credit: Odantapuribs · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ganges
tokens.title: Sacred river of India
tokens.description: The Ganges, called Ganga in India and Padma in Bangladesh, is a trans-boundary river of Asia. It rises in the western Himalayas in Uttarakhand, India, and is about 2,525 kilometres long.
tokens.image_credit: Wedstock 2011 · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kedarnath Temple
tokens.title: Himalayan Shiva shrine
tokens.description: Kedarnath Temple is a Hindu temple and one of the twelve jyotirlinga of Shiva. It stands in the Garhwal Himalaya near the Mandakini River in Uttarakhand, India, and is open only from April to November.
tokens.image_credit: Shivam Kumar 766 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Badrinath
tokens.description: Badrinath is a town in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, India, and a Hindu holy place. It is one of the four sites of India's Char Dham pilgrimage and takes its name from the Badrinath Temple.
tokens.image_credit: Arpita Tripathy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
tokens.title: Richest temple in the world
tokens.description: The Venkateswara Swami Temple, also known as Tirumala Temple, is a Hindu temple in the hills of Tirumala, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, India. It is dedicated to Venkateswara, a form of Vishnu.
tokens.image_credit: Adityamadhav83 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Somnath Temple
tokens.description: Somanatha Temple is a Hindu temple in Prabhas Patan, Veraval, Gujarat, India. It is the first of the twelve jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva and one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for Hindus.
tokens.image_credit: B. SurajPatro1997 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
tokens.description: The Dwarkadhish Temple, also known as the Jagat Mandir, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Krishna in Dwarka, Gujarat, India. It is one of the destinations of the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit.
tokens.image_credit: Vishnupranay.k · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Victoria Memorial, Kolkata
tokens.description: The Victoria Memorial is a large marble monument in the Maidan in central Kolkata, India. It was built between 1906 and 1921 by the British Raj and is dedicated to Queen Victoria, Empress of India from 1876 to 1901.
tokens.image_credit: Subhrajyoti07 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gol Gumbaz
tokens.title: Dome of Bijapur
tokens.description: The Gol Gumbaz is a dark grey basalt mausoleum in Bijapur, Karnataka, India. It holds the tomb of Adil Shah, seventh ruler of the Sultanate of Bijapur, and was left unfinished after his death in 1656.
tokens.image_credit: Meesanjay · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Charminar
tokens.title: Hyderabad's landmark
