tokens.description: The Charminar is a monument built in 1591 in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It is a symbol of Hyderabad and appears in the official emblem of Telangana.
tokens.image_credit: DidierTais · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golconda Fort
tokens.description: Golconda is a fortified citadel and ruined city on the western outskirts of Hyderabad, Telangana, India. The fort was first built in the 11th century and later expanded into a stone citadel by the Qutb Shahs.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nanda Devi
tokens.description: Nanda Devi is the second-highest mountain in India and the highest located entirely within the country. It is the 23rd-highest peak in the world, in Chamoli Garhwal district of Uttarakhand.
tokens.image_credit: Sumod K Mohan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kaziranga National Park
tokens.title: One-horned rhino refuge
tokens.description: Kaziranga National Park is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site in Assam, India. It hosts populations of the Indian rhinoceros, Asian elephant, wild water buffalo, swamp deer and tiger.
tokens.image_credit: Diganta Talukdar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jim Corbett National Park
tokens.description: Jim Corbett National Park is a national park in Nainital district, Uttarakhand, India. Established in 1936 as the country's first national park, it was the first reserve to come under Project Tiger.
tokens.image_credit: Timothy Gonsalves · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bandhavgarh National Park
tokens.description: Bandhavgarh National Park is a national park in Umaria district, Madhya Pradesh, India. Declared a national park in 1968, it became a Tiger Reserve in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Prithwiraj Dhang · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kanha Tiger Reserve
tokens.description: Kanha Tiger Reserve is one of India's tiger reserves and the largest national park in Madhya Pradesh. It covers about 940 km2 across the Mandla and Balaghat districts.
tokens.image_credit: Sangeetha Balaji · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Keoladeo National Park
tokens.description: Keoladeo National Park, also called Keoladeo Ghana, is a national park in Rajasthan, India. It hosts thousands of resident and migratory birds, with at least 400 species recorded, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Nikhilchandra81 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gir National Park
tokens.title: Asiatic lions
tokens.description: Gir National Park, also known as Sasan Gir, is a national park and wildlife sanctuary in Gujarat, India. It was established in 1965 and is part of the Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests ecoregion.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Periyar National Park
tokens.description: Periyar National Park is a protected area in Idukki and Pathanamthitta districts, Kerala, India, known as an elephant and tiger reserve. The national park was declared in 1982 within a larger wildlife sanctuary.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Himalayan National Park
tokens.description: The Great Himalayan National Park is a national park in Himachal Pradesh, India, established in 1984 across 1,171 km2. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with more than 375 fauna species recorded.
tokens.image_credit: Suresh Karia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loktak Lake
tokens.title: Floating phumdis
tokens.description: Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India. It lies at Moirang in Manipur state, with a typical surface area of 287 km2 that varies through the year.
tokens.image_credit: Sudiptorana · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dal Lake
tokens.title: Srinagar's lake
tokens.description: Dal Lake is a freshwater lake in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir. It is the second largest lake in Jammu and Kashmir and the most visited place in Srinagar.
tokens.image_credit: Suhail Skindar Sofi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pangong Tso
tokens.title: High altitude lake
tokens.description: Pangong Tso is an endorheic lake in eastern Ladakh, India, extending into Ngari Prefecture in Tibet, at about 4,300 m elevation. It covers approximately 604 km2 and stretches for 134 km.
tokens.image_credit: Stanzin1945 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chilika Lake
tokens.description: Chilika Lake is a brackish lagoon on the east coast of India, spread over Odisha state at the mouth of the Daya River. The article describes it as the second largest coastal lagoon in the world, and it was an early Indian Ramsar wetland in 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Government of Odisha · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thar Desert
tokens.description: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is an arid region in north-western India and Pakistan. It covers about 264,091 km2 and is one of the largest subtropical deserts in Asia.
tokens.image_credit: sushmita balasubramani · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Majuli
tokens.title: Largest river island
tokens.description: Majuli is the largest river island in Assam, in northeast India, bordered by the Brahmaputra River. It is a hub of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture.
tokens.image_credit: Dhrubazaan Photography · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jog Falls
tokens.description: Jog Falls is a series of segmented waterfalls on the Sharavati River in Karnataka, India. The river drops about 253 metres and splits into four cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket.
tokens.image_credit: Arkadeep Meta · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dudhsagar Falls
tokens.description: Dudhsagar Falls is a four-tiered waterfall on the Mahadayi River in Goa, India. At about 310 m high, it is among India's tallest waterfalls.
tokens.image_credit: Hsp wiki · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Western Ghats
tokens.description: The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri, is a mountain range about 1,600 km long along the west coast of India. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and crosses six Indian states.
tokens.image_credit: Mdmadhu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pir Panjal Range
tokens.description: The Pir Panjal Range is a mountain range in the Lower Himalayas, running between the Beas and Neelam rivers. It lies in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir in India, with its north-western end in Pakistan-administered territory.

tokens.name: Gangotri Glacier
tokens.description: Gangotri Glacier is located in Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand, India, near the border with Tibet. It is one of the primary sources of the Ganges and is about 30 kilometres long.
tokens.image_credit: Atarax42 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zemu Glacier
tokens.description: Zemu Glacier is the largest glacier in the Eastern Himalaya, about 26 kilometres long. It lies at the base of Kangchenjunga in Sikkim, India.

tokens.name: Rohtang Pass
tokens.description: Rohtang Pass is a high mountain pass at 3,980 metres on the eastern end of the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas. It connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys in Himachal Pradesh, India.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khardung La
tokens.description: Khardung La is a mountain pass at 5,359 metres on the Ladakh Range, about 40 km north of Leh in Ladakh, India. It connects the Indus and Shyok river valleys and carries a road built in 1976.

tokens.name: Statue of Unity
tokens.title: World's tallest statue
tokens.description: The Statue of Unity is the world's tallest statue, 182 metres high, in the Narmada valley near Kevadia in Gujarat, India. It depicts the independence activist and politician Sardar Patel.
tokens.image_credit: Snehrashmi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chand Baori
tokens.description: Chand Baori is a stepwell in the village of Abhaneri in Rajasthan, India, extending about 30 metres into the ground. It is named after Raja Chanda of the Nikumbh dynasty and dated to the 8th to 9th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Harappa
tokens.description: Harappa is an archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan, about 24 kilometres west of Sahiwal. It was a major Indus Valley city, believed to have had as many as 23,500 residents in the Mature Harappan phase.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Bin Naveed · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Badshahi Mosque
tokens.title: Mughal mosque of Lahore
tokens.description: The Badshahi Mosque is a Mughal imperial mosque in Lahore, Pakistan, built between 1671 and 1673 by the emperor Aurangzeb. It stands opposite the Lahore Fort and is widely considered an iconic landmark of the country.
tokens.image_credit: Romero Maia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shalamar Gardens, Lahore
tokens.description: Shalamar Gardens is a Mughal charbagh-style garden complex in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan, dating from the 17th century. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Fort and Shalamar Gardens in Lahore, inscribed in 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Ashar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Faisal Mosque
tokens.title: Islamabad's modern mosque
tokens.description: The Faisal Mosque is the national mosque of Pakistan, located in Islamabad at the foothills of the Margalla Hills. It is the sixth-largest mosque in the world and is named after King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
tokens.image_credit: Ali Mujtaba · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rohtas Fort
tokens.description: Rohtas Fort is a 16th-century fortress near Dina in Jhelum district, Punjab, Pakistan, commissioned by Sher Shah Suri. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Hussain Khalid · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Makli Necropolis
tokens.description: Makli Necropolis is one of the largest funerary sites in the world, spread over about 10 km near Thatta in Sindh, Pakistan. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1981 as Historical Monuments at Makli, Thatta.
tokens.image_credit: Gajus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Broad Peak
tokens.description: Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world, at 8,051 metres, and one of the eight-thousanders. It lies in the Karakoram range, spanning Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, and Xinjiang, China.
tokens.image_credit: Kogo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Karakoram
tokens.description: The Karakoram is a mountain range in Asia that spans the borders of Pakistan, China and India. It contains four of the fourteen eight-thousanders, including K2, the second highest mountain on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Guilhem Vellut · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baltoro Glacier
tokens.description: The Baltoro Glacier is a glacier in the Karakoram range, in Shigar District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is surrounded by some of the world's highest peaks, including K2, the second highest mountain on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Thsulemani · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Deosai National Park
tokens.description: Deosai National Park is a high-elevation alpine plain national park in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, with plains averaging about 4,114 metres. It lies between the Skardu and Astore districts in the western Himalayas.
tokens.image_credit: Qammer Wazir · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khunjerab Pass
tokens.description: Khunjerab Pass is a high-altitude mountain pass at 4,693 metres on the Karakoram Highway. It forms a border crossing between Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan and China's Xinjiang region.
tokens.image_credit: Sheikh Danish Ejaz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khyber Pass
tokens.title: Gateway to South Asia
tokens.description: The Khyber Pass is a mountain pass in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, along the border with Afghanistan. It connects Landi Kotal to the Valley of Peshawar and has long been a trade route and a strategic military choke point.

tokens.name: Lake Saiful Muluk
tokens.description: Lake Saiful Muluk is a mountain lake at 3,224 metres at the northern end of the Kaghan Valley, near Naran in Pakistan. It lies in Saiful Muluk National Park and is one of the highest lakes in Pakistan.
tokens.image_credit: Muzaffar Bukhari · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Indus River
tokens.description: The Indus is a 3,180 km transboundary river of South and Central Asia that rises in Tibet and flows through Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Its drainage area is about 1,120,000 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Akbar Khan Niazi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Adam's Peak
tokens.title: Adam's Peak pilgrimage
tokens.description: Adam's Peak is a 2,243 metre conical sacred mountain and place of pilgrimage in central Sri Lanka. It is named after the Sri Pada, a footprint-like rock formation near the summit that several religions revere.
tokens.image_credit: Rehman Abubakr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galle Fort
tokens.description: Galle Fort is a fortified old town on the southwest coast of Sri Lanka, first built by the Portuguese in 1588 and later fortified by the Dutch. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications.
tokens.image_credit: Rovin Shanila · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Horton Plains National Park
tokens.description: Horton Plains National Park is a national park in the central highlands of Sri Lanka, designated in 1988. It covers 31 square kilometres of montane grassland and cloud forest at 2,100 to 2,300 metres.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
tokens.description: Sinharaja Forest Reserve is the last virgin rainforest in Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is home to many rare endemic plants and animals.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Swayambhunath
tokens.description: Swayambhunath is an ancient religious complex atop a hill in the Kathmandu Valley, west of Kathmandu city in Nepal. The hill has been an ancient pilgrimage site considered the home of the primordial Buddha.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sagarmatha National Park
tokens.description: Sagarmatha National Park is a national park in the Himalayas of eastern Nepal, established in 1976. It includes Mount Everest and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lhotse
tokens.description: Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain on Earth, at 8,516 metres. It forms the apex of the Everest massif, with its main summit on the border between Tibet and the Khumbu region of Nepal.
tokens.image_credit: Uwe Gille · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Makalu
tokens.description: Makalu is the fifth-highest mountain on Earth, at 8,485 metres. It is an isolated four-sided pyramid peak on the China-Nepal border, about 19 km southeast of Mount Everest.
tokens.image_credit: Ben Tubby · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manaslu
tokens.description: Manaslu is the eighth-highest mountain in the world, at 8,163 metres. It lies in the Mansiri Himal of west-central Nepal, and its name means mountain of the spirit.
tokens.image_credit: Pratapgrg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Langtang National Park
tokens.description: Langtang National Park is a national park in north-central Nepal. It was established in 1976 as Nepal's first Himalayan national park and covers 1,710 square km.

tokens.name: Rara Lake
tokens.description: Rara Lake is the largest fresh water lake in the Nepalese Himalayas. It is the main feature of Rara National Park, located in Jumla and Mugu Districts of Karnali Province.
tokens.image_credit: Prajina Khatiwada · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kali Gandaki Gorge
tokens.description: The Kali Gandaki Gorge or Andha Galchi is the gorge of the Kali Gandaki river in the Himalayas in Nepal. By some sources, it may be one of the deepest gorges in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Waglebaba · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khumbu Glacier
tokens.description: The Khumbu Glacier is located in the Khumbu region of northeastern Nepal between Mount Everest and the Lhotse-Nuptse ridge. It is the world's highest glacier, from 4,900 m at its terminus to 7,600 m at its source.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tengboche Monastery
tokens.description: Tengboche Monastery, also known as Dawa Choling Gompa, is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Sherpa community in the Khumbu region of eastern Nepal. Built in 1916, it is the largest gompa in the Khumbu region.
tokens.image_credit: Billjones94 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tashichho Dzong
tokens.description: Tashichho Dzong is a Buddhist monastery and fortress on the northern edge of Thimphu in Bhutan. It has traditionally been the seat of Bhutan's civil government and the summer capital of the country.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jomolhari
tokens.description: Jomolhari or Chomolhari is a mountain in the Himalayas, straddling the border between Tibet, China and the Paro district of Bhutan. It is the source of the Paro Chu river, which flows from its south side.
tokens.image_credit: Martyn Smith · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gangkhar Puensum
tokens.title: Highest unclimbed mountain
tokens.description: Gangkhar Puensum is the highest mountain in Bhutan and the highest unclimbed mountain in the world, at 7,570 metres. It lies on the border between Bhutan and Tibet.
tokens.image_credit: Gradythebadger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Manas National Park
tokens.description: Royal Manas National Park is Bhutan's oldest national park, with an area of 1,057 square kilometres. It covers eastern Sarpang District, the western half of Zhemgang District and western Pemagatshel District.

tokens.name: Mahasthangarh
tokens.description: Mahasthangarh is the earliest urban archaeological site discovered so far in Bangladesh. It contains the remains of the ancient city of Pundranagara, dated to at least the 3rd century BCE.
tokens.image_credit: Picture taken by P.K.Niyogi, people removed by GreenComputer · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Somapura Mahavihara
tokens.title: Buddhist monastery
tokens.description: Somapura Mahavihara, also known as Paharpur Buddhist Vihara, is a major Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhist monastery in Paharpur, Naogaon, Bangladesh. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
tokens.image_credit: Abdulmominbd · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ahsan Manzil
tokens.description: Ahsan Manzil is a historic palace on the bank of the Buriganga River in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It was the official residence and administrative seat of the Nawab of Dhaka in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Mahbub Hossain Shaheed (mahosha) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cox's Bazar
tokens.title: Longest natural sea beach
tokens.description: Cox's Bazar is a city, fishing port and tourism centre in south-eastern Bangladesh, and the headquarters of Cox's Bazar District. Its long sea beach is a major tourist attraction.

tokens.name: Lalbagh Fort
tokens.description: Lalbagh Fort is a historic Mughal fort in the old city of Dhaka, Bangladesh. Work began in 1678 under Prince Muhammad Azam and the fort was left unfinished.
tokens.image_credit: Farha Fawzia Atashi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ari Atoll
tokens.description: Ari Atoll, also called Alif or Alifu Atoll, is one of the natural atolls of the Maldives. It lies in the west of the archipelago and is one of the biggest atolls there.
tokens.image_credit: European Space Agency · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Banteay Srei
tokens.description: Banteay Srei is a 10th century CE Cambodian temple dedicated to the Hindu gods Shiva and Parvati. It lies in the Angkor area and is part of the Angkor World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Tsui · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Complex of Huế Monuments
tokens.title: Imperial city of Nguyen dynasty
tokens.description: The Complex of Huế Monuments is a UNESCO World Heritage relic complex in the city of Huế, central Vietnam. It includes the Imperial City, the Citadel and the tombs of the emperors of the Nguyen dynasty.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mekong
tokens.title: River of Southeast Asia
tokens.description: The Mekong is a transboundary river in East and Southeast Asia, the world's twelfth-longest river. It rises on the Tibetan Plateau and flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and southern Vietnam.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fansipan
tokens.title: Roof of Indochina
tokens.description: Fansipan is a mountain in Vietnam and the highest mountain on the Indochinese peninsula, nicknamed the Roof of Indochina. Its height was later adjusted to 3,147.3 metres.

tokens.name: Tràng An Scenic Landscape Complex
tokens.description: The Tràng An Scenic Landscape Complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Ninh Bình Province, northern Vietnam. It covers karst limestone peaks, caves and river channels, known for its boat cave tours.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Củ Chi tunnels
tokens.description: The Củ Chi tunnels are an extensive network of connecting tunnels in Củ Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. They were a base for Viet Cong operations during the Vietnam War, including the 1968 Tết Offensive.
tokens.image_credit: Mkckim · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Literature, Hanoi
tokens.description: The Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu) in Hanoi is a temple dedicated to Confucius, first built in 1070. It hosted the Imperial Academy, Vietnam's first national university, from 1076 to 1779.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Chuoibk at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kyaiktiyo Pagoda
tokens.title: Balancing golden boulder
tokens.description: Kyaiktiyo Pagoda, also known as Golden Rock, is a Buddhist pilgrimage site in Mon State, Myanmar. It is a small pagoda built on a granite boulder covered with gold leaf applied by male worshippers.
tokens.image_credit: Hybernator · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mandalay Palace
tokens.description: The Mandalay Palace in Mandalay, Myanmar, is the last royal palace of the last Burmese monarchy. It was built between 1857 and 1859 as part of King Mindon's founding of the royal capital city of Mandalay.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Irrawaddy River
tokens.description: The Irrawaddy River is the principal river of Myanmar, running through the centre of the country. It is about 2,170 km long and empties through the Irrawaddy Delta into the Andaman Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Wagaung (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hkakabo Razi
tokens.description: Hkakabo Razi is believed to be Myanmar's highest mountain, at 5,881 m. It is also the highest mountain in Southeast Asia, in Kachin State near the tripoint with India and China.

tokens.name: Mergui Archipelago
tokens.description: The Mergui Archipelago is located in far southern Myanmar, in the Tanintharyi Region. It consists of around 800 islands lying in the Andaman Sea off the western shore of the Malay Peninsula.
tokens.image_credit: Go-Myanmar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Palace
tokens.title: Royal residence in Bangkok
tokens.description: The Grand Palace is a complex of buildings at the heart of Bangkok, Thailand. It has been the official residence of the Kings of Siam, and later Thailand, since 1782.
tokens.image_credit: Preecha.MJ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wat Pho
tokens.title: Reclining Buddha
tokens.description: Wat Pho is a Buddhist temple complex in the Phra Nakhon District of Bangkok, Thailand, directly south of the Grand Palace. It is also known as the Temple of the Reclining Buddha.
tokens.image_credit: Mastertongapollo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wat Phra Kaew
tokens.title: Temple of the Emerald Buddha
tokens.description: Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, is regarded as the most sacred Buddhist temple in Thailand. It lies within the Grand Palace precincts in Bangkok and houses the Emerald Buddha statue.
tokens.image_credit: Original image: Ninara from Helsinki, Finland. Edit: TSP · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
tokens.description: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is a Theravada Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, on the Doi Suthep mountain west of Chiang Mai. It is a sacred site to many Thai people.
tokens.image_credit: JJ Harrison (https://www.jjharrison.com.au/) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phang Nga Bay
tokens.description: Phang Nga Bay is a 400 square km bay in the Andaman Sea between the island of Phuket and the mainland of southern Thailand. Since 1981 much of it has been protected as Ao Phang Nga National Park, known for its limestone karst cliffs.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khao Sok National Park
tokens.description: Khao Sok National Park is a protected area in Surat Thani Province, southern Thailand, covering about 739 square kilometres. It includes Cheow Lan Lake and is described as the largest area of virgin forest in southern Thailand.
tokens.image_credit: BerryJ · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Erawan National Park
tokens.description: Erawan National Park is a protected area in the Tenasserim Hills of Kanchanaburi Province, western Thailand. Founded in 1975, it was the 12th national park of Thailand.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phanom Rung Historical Park
tokens.description: Phanom Rung Historical Park is an archaeological site in Buriram Province, Isan, Thailand. It covers the ruins of a Buddhist-Hindu Khmer temple complex on the rim of an extinct volcano, built of sandstone and laterite between the 10th and 13th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Philip Nalangan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bridge over the River Kwai
tokens.description: The Bridge over the River Kwai is a steel railway bridge at Kanchanaburi, Thailand, on the Burma Railway built from 1940 to 1943 by captured Allied soldiers and abducted Southeast Asian civilians. The 1957 film of the same name is fiction.
tokens.image_credit: PumpkinSky · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ko Samui
tokens.description: Ko Samui is an island off the east coast of Thailand in the Chumphon Archipelago, part of Surat Thani Province. At 228.7 square kilometres it is Thailand's second largest island after Phuket.

tokens.name: Sarawak Chamber
tokens.description: Sarawak Chamber is the largest known cave chamber in the world by area, and the second largest by volume after the Miao Room in China. It lies in Gua Nasib Bagus (Good Luck Cave) in Gunung Mulu National Park, Sarawak, on Borneo.

tokens.name: Kinabatangan River
tokens.description: The Kinabatangan River is a river of eastern Sabah, Malaysia, and the second longest river in Malaysia, at 560 km. It flows to the Sulu Sea east of Sandakan and is known for its high biodiversity.
tokens.image_credit: Mike Prince from Bangalore, India · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Langkawi
tokens.description: Langkawi is a duty-free island and archipelago of 99 islands in the Strait of Malacca, about 30 km off northwestern Malaysia. It is an administrative district of Kedah, with Kuah as its largest town.
tokens.image_credit: Ttt.Osakanman · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marina Bay Sands
tokens.description: Marina Bay Sands is an integrated resort fronting Marina Bay in Singapore and a landmark of the city. It includes a hotel, a casino, a shopping mall, a convention centre and an ArtScience museum.
tokens.image_credit: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images, but please mention me as the author and may send me a message. (สามารถใช้ภาพได้อิสระ แต่กรุณาใส่เครดิตผู้ถ่ายและอาจส่งข · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sentosa
tokens.title: Sentosa island resort
tokens.description: Sentosa is an island off the southern coast of Singapore's main island, separated from it by the Keppel Harbour channel. The island is developed and managed by the Sentosa Development Corporation, a statutory board.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ijen
tokens.title: Blue fire crater
tokens.description: The Ijen volcano complex is a group of composite volcanoes on the border between Banyuwangi and Bondowoso regencies in East Java, Indonesia. It is known for its blue fire, acidic crater lake and sulfur mining.
tokens.image_credit: Sémhur (talk) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Agung
tokens.description: Mount Agung is an active volcano in Karangasem Regency, Bali, Indonesia. It is the highest point on Bali and dominates the surrounding area, influencing the climate and rainfall patterns.
tokens.image_credit: Michael W. Ishak (www.myreefsdiary.com) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Batur
tokens.description: Mount Batur is an active volcano at the centre of two concentric calderas on Bali, Indonesia. The southeast side of the larger caldera contains a caldera lake.
tokens.image_credit: TropicaLiving · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Semeru
tokens.description: Semeru is the highest mountain on the Indonesian island of Java and an active volcano in East Java. At 3,676 m it is the third tallest volcano in Indonesia, after Kerinci and Rinjani.
tokens.image_credit: Pambudiyoga · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uluwatu Temple
tokens.description: Uluwatu Temple is a Balinese Hindu temple on the south-western tip of the Bukit Peninsula in Bali, Indonesia. It is the only Balinese sea temple that is also one of the nine directional temples.
tokens.image_credit: Paskuu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Besakih Temple
tokens.title: Mother Temple of Bali
tokens.description: Besakih Temple is a Hindu temple complex on the slopes of Mount Agung in eastern Bali, Indonesia. It is the largest and holiest temple of Balinese Hinduism, made up of 23 related temples.
tokens.image_credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tirta Empul
tokens.description: Tirta Empul is a Hindu Balinese water temple near Tampaksiring, Bali, Indonesia. Balinese Hindus bathe in its holy spring water for the purification ritual Melukat.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jatiluwih
tokens.description: Jatiluwih is a village and rice terrace landscape on the slopes of Mount Batukaru in Tabanan Regency, Bali, Indonesia. It is part of the UNESCO-listed Cultural Landscape of Bali Province, inscribed in 2012.

tokens.name: Ujung Kulon National Park
tokens.description: Ujung Kulon National Park is a national park at the westernmost tip of Java, in Pandeglang Regency, Banten, Indonesia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its large remaining lowland rainforest and for the Javan rhino.

tokens.name: Tanjung Puting National Park
tokens.description: Tanjung Puting National Park is a national park along the Sekonyer River in Central Kalimantan, Borneo, Indonesia. The park is famous for its orangutan conservation.

tokens.name: Lorentz National Park
tokens.description: Lorentz National Park is an Indonesian national park across Central Papua, Highland Papua and South Papua on western New Guinea. It is the largest national park in Southeast Asia and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

tokens.name: Mount Kerinci
tokens.description: Mount Kerinci is an active stratovolcano and the highest mountain in Sumatra, Indonesia, at 3,805 metres. It is surrounded by the forest of Kerinci Seblat National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Uprising · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gunung Leuser National Park
tokens.description: Gunung Leuser National Park covers about 7,927 km2 in northern Sumatra, Indonesia, straddling the Aceh and North Sumatra provinces. It is part of the UNESCO Tropical Rainforest Heritage of Sumatra and contains an orangutan sanctuary at Bukit Lawang.
tokens.image_credit: Junaidi Hanafiah · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bunaken National Park
tokens.description: Bunaken National Park is a marine park off the north of Sulawesi Island, Indonesia, near the centre of the Coral Triangle. It protects about 390 coral species, seagrass plains, coral reefs and coastal ecosystems.
tokens.image_credit: Btv70 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wakatobi National Park
tokens.description: Wakatobi National Park is a marine national park in Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, established in 2002. Its name combines the four main Tukangbesi Islands: Wangi-wangi, Kaledupa, Tomia and Binongko.

tokens.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
tokens.description: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park is a protected area on the western coast of Palawan, Philippines, about 80 km north of Puerto Princesa city. It contains the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River, also known as the Underground River.
tokens.aliases: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
tokens.image_credit: Ron Van Oers · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
tokens.description: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine and bird sanctuary in the middle of the Sulu Sea, Philippines. It covers two large atolls, North Atoll and South Atoll, and the smaller Jessie Beazley Reef, and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: El Nido, Palawan
tokens.description: El Nido is a municipality in the province of Palawan, Philippines, and the gateway to the Bacuit archipelago. It is known for its white-sand beaches, coral reefs and limestone cliffs.
tokens.image_credit: Kalithecat00 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boracay
tokens.description: Boracay is a resort island in the Western Visayas region of the Philippines, located 0.8 km off the northwest coast of Panay Island. It had a population of 37,802 in 2020.
tokens.image_credit: Jhun Sacapano · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vigan
tokens.description: Vigan is a component city and the capital of Ilocos Sur province, on the western coast of Luzon, Philippines. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the few Spanish colonial towns in the Philippines whose old structures have mostly remained intact.
tokens.image_credit: Ralff Nestor Nacor · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paoay Church
tokens.description: Saint Augustine Parish Church, commonly known as Paoay Church, is a Roman Catholic church in Paoay, Ilocos Norte, Philippines. Completed in 1710, it is known for its huge buttresses and is part of the UNESCO-listed Baroque Churches of the Philippines.
tokens.image_credit: Brynht · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Changdeokgung
tokens.title: Secret Garden palace
tokens.description: Changdeokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is among the best preserved of all Korean palaces.
tokens.image_credit: 문화재청 · KOGL Type 1 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bulguksa
tokens.title: Silla Buddhist temple
tokens.description: Bulguksa is a Buddhist temple on Tohamsan in Gyeongju, South Korea, and a head temple of the Jogye Order. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1995 together with Seokguram Grotto.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seokguram
tokens.description: Seokguram is a hermitage and grotto that is part of the Bulguksa temple complex in Gyeongju, South Korea, overlooking the East Sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1995 together with Bulguksa.
tokens.image_credit: Seok-Hong, Han · KOGL Type 1 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
tokens.title: Sunrise Peak
tokens.description: Seongsan Ilchulbong, also called Sunrise Peak, is a 182 meter tuff cone volcano on eastern Jeju Island, South Korea. It is one of the components of the UNESCO World Heritage Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes.
tokens.image_credit: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jirisan
tokens.description: Jirisan is a mountain in southern South Korea, the second-tallest in the country and the tallest on the mainland, at 1915 meters. It is located in Jirisan National Park.
tokens.image_credit: by eimoberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hahoe Folk Village
tokens.description: Hahoe Folk Village is a traditional Joseon dynasty village in Andong, North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Historic Villages of Korea: Hahoe and Yangdong, inscribed in 2010.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Panmunjom
tokens.description: Panmunjom was a village just north of the de facto border between North and South Korea, where the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement that ended the Korean War was signed. The building where the armistice was signed still stands.
tokens.image_credit: Department of Defense. Department of the Army. Office of the Chief Signal Officer. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lotte World Tower
tokens.title: Indoor theme park in Seoul
tokens.description: Lotte World Tower is a 123-storey supertall skyscraper of 555 metres in Sincheon-dong, Songpa District, Seoul. It is the tallest building in South Korea and the sixth-tallest in the world.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Paektu
tokens.title: Sacred volcano of Korea
tokens.description: Mount Paektu is an active stratovolcano on the Chinese and North Korean border, known in China as Changbai Mountain. At 2,744 m it is the tallest mountain in North Korea and Northeast China.
tokens.image_credit: Laika ac from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ryugyong Hotel
tokens.description: The Ryugyong Hotel is a 330 m unfinished pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea. Its name is also one of the historical names for Pyongyang.
tokens.image_credit: John Pavelka from Austin, TX, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
tokens.description: The Kumsusan Palace of the Sun is the mausoleum where Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il are displayed, near the northeast corner of Pyongyang. It was renovated from the Kumsusan Assembly Hall, Kim Il Sung's former residence and office.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Scott Johnson from Sydney, Australia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Khövsgöl
tokens.title: Mongolia's blue pearl
tokens.description: Lake Khövsgöl is a lake in Khövsgöl Province, Mongolia. It is the largest freshwater lake in the country by volume and the second largest by area after Uvs Lake.
tokens.image_credit: Bgelo777 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Orkhon Valley
tokens.description: Orkhon Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape along the Orkhon River in central Mongolia, about 320 km west of Ulaanbaatar. It represents the development of nomadic pastoral traditions over more than two millennia.
tokens.image_credit: He-ba-mue · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Erdene Zuu Monastery
tokens.description: Erdene Zuu Monastery is probably the earliest surviving Buddhist monastery in Mongolia. Built in 1585 in Kharkhorin, Övörkhangai Province, it lies within the Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Chongkian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Genghis Khan Equestrian Statue
tokens.description: The Genghis Khan Equestrian Statue is a 40-metre tall stainless steel statue of Genghis Khan on horseback, part of the Genghis Khan Statue Complex. It stands about 54 km east of Ulaanbaatar, near Tsonjin Boldog, and is described as the world's tallest equestrian statue.
tokens.image_credit: Vaiz Ha · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Altai Tavan Bogd National Park
tokens.description: Altai Tavan Bogd National Park is a national park in Bayan-Olgii Province of western Mongolia. It covers 6,362 square kilometres of the Mongolian side of the Tavan Bogd massif in the Altai Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Altaihunters · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gandantegchinlen Monastery
tokens.description: Gandantegchinlen Monastery, also known as Gandan Monastery, is a Buddhist monastery in Bayangol District, Ulaanbaatar. It was founded in 1809 and was the country's only active monastery from 1944 to 1989.
tokens.image_credit: Chongkian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burkhan Khaldun
tokens.description: Burkhan Khaldun is one of the Khentii Mountains in Khentii Province of northeastern Mongolia. The mountain or its locality is believed to be the birthplace of Genghis Khan as well as his tomb.

tokens.name: Mount Kinabalu
tokens.title: Borneo's highest peak
tokens.description: Mount Kinabalu is the highest mountain in Malaysia and Maritime Southeast Asia, on the island of Borneo in Sabah. At 4,095 metres it rises in Ranau district and is the third-highest peak of an island on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kelimutu
tokens.title: Tricolor crater lakes
tokens.description: Kelimutu is a volcano close to the small town of Moni in central Flores island, Indonesia. It has three volcanic crater lakes that differ in colour.
tokens.image_credit: LukeTriton · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jongmyo
tokens.title: Royal ancestral shrine
tokens.description: Jongmyo is a Confucian royal ancestral shrine in Jongno District, Seoul. It was built during the Joseon period for memorial services for deceased kings and queens.
tokens.image_credit: 문화재청 · KOGL Type 1 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue Mosque, Istanbul
tokens.title: Sultan Ahmed Mosque
tokens.description: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is an Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul, Turkey. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I.
tokens.image_credit: Moonik · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basilica Cistern
tokens.description: The Basilica Cistern is the largest of several hundred ancient cisterns beneath Istanbul, Turkey. Built in the 6th century under Byzantine emperor Justinian I, it is kept with little water for public access.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galata Tower
tokens.description: Galata Tower is a tower in the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul, Turkey, named after the Galata neighborhood where it stands. Built as a watchtower within the Walls of Galata, it has been a museum and exhibition venue since 2020.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Göreme Historical National Park
tokens.description: Göreme Historical National Park is a national park in Cappadocia, central Turkey, covering nearly 100 square km in Nevşehir Province. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985 as Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia.
tokens.image_credit: Emrahuygun · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Artemis
tokens.title: Wonder of the ancient world
tokens.description: The Temple of Artemis, also called the Artemision, was a Greek temple to Artemis at Ephesus, near modern Selçuk in Turkey. It is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and only foundations and fragments remain today.
tokens.image_credit: Arkiyolok · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
tokens.description: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus was a tomb built between 353 and 351 BC in Halicarnassus, present Bodrum in Turkey, for the satrap Mausolus and his sister-wife Artemisia II. It was about 45 m high and its reliefs were carved by four Greek sculptors.
tokens.image_credit: FollowingHadrian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mevlâna Museum
tokens.description: The Mevlâna Museum in Konya, Turkey, started as the dervish lodge of the Mevlevi order, known as the whirling dervishes. It houses the mausoleum of the Sufi mystic Jalal ad-Din Muhammad Rumi.
tokens.image_credit: User:دانقولا · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Selimiye Mosque, Edirne
tokens.description: The Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, Turkey, is an Ottoman imperial mosque commissioned by Sultan Selim II and built by Mimar Sinan between 1568 and 1575. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered Sinan's masterpiece.
tokens.image_credit: rob Stoeltje from loenen, netherlands · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Van
tokens.description: Lake Van is the largest lake in Turkey, in the Eastern Anatolia region across the provinces of Van and Bitlis. It is a saline soda lake fed by streams descending from the surrounding mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Erciyes
tokens.description: Mount Erciyes is an inactive stratovolcano in Kayseri Province, central Turkey. Its bulk is built of andesitic and dacitic lava flows, with many monogenetic vents and lava domes around it.
tokens.image_credit: Carole Raddato from FRANKFURT, Germany · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Termessos
tokens.description: Termessos, also called Termessos Major, was a Pisidian city built at about 1000 metres in the Taurus Mountains. It lies 17 kilometres northwest of Antalya.
tokens.image_credit: Ingo Mehling · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Library of Celsus
tokens.description: The Library of Celsus is an ancient Roman building in Ephesus, near Selcuk in western Turkey. It was commissioned in the 110s CE as a funerary monument for Tiberius Julius Celsus Polemaeanus.
tokens.image_credit: Austrian Archaeological Institute · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maiden's Tower
tokens.description: The Maiden's Tower is a tower on a small islet at the southern entrance of the Bosphorus, about 200 m from the coast of Uskudar in Istanbul. It appeared on the reverse of the Turkish 10 lira banknote from 1966 to 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rumeli Fortress
tokens.description: Rumeli Fortress, also called Rumelihisarı or Boğazkesen, is a medieval Ottoman fortress on the European bank of the Bosphorus in Istanbul. Sultan Mehmed II had it built in 1451 to 1452 to cut off sea relief for Constantinople.
tokens.image_credit: Dosseman · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saqqara
tokens.description: Saqqara is an ancient necropolis about 30 km south of Cairo that served the Egyptian capital Memphis. It contains numerous pyramids, including the Step Pyramid of Djoser, and many mastaba tombs.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyramid of Djoser
tokens.title: First pyramid
tokens.description: The Pyramid of Djoser, also called the Step Pyramid, is an archaeological site in the Saqqara necropolis northwest of the ruins of Memphis. It was the first Egyptian pyramid, a six-tier stone structure.
tokens.image_credit: Olaf Tausch · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dahshur
tokens.description: Dahshur is an ancient Egyptian pyramid complex and necropolis on the Western Desert plateau near Memphis. It forms part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of the pyramid fields of Memphis.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Mayer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bent Pyramid
tokens.description: The Bent Pyramid is an ancient Egyptian pyramid at the royal necropolis of Dahshur, built under the Old Kingdom pharaoh Sneferu. Its upper section is built at a shallower angle than the lower, giving it a visibly bent shape.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Láscar from Melbourne, Australia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valley of the Queens
tokens.description: The Valley of the Queens is a site in Egypt where queens, princes, princesses and other high-ranking officials were buried from roughly 1560 BC to 1130 BC. Excavation of its tombs was pioneered by Ernesto Schiaparelli and Francesco Ballerini in the early 1900s.

tokens.name: Mortuary temple of Hatshepsut
tokens.description: The mortuary temple of Hatshepsut was built during the reign of Pharaoh Hatshepsut of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt. It is located opposite the city of Luxor, in the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Philae temple complex
tokens.description: The Philae temple complex is an island-based temple complex in the reservoir of the Aswan Low Dam, Egypt. Originally on Philae Island, it was moved to the nearby island of Agilkia between 1977 and 1980 and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae.
tokens.image_credit: Moh hakem · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Edfu
tokens.description: The Temple of Edfu is an Egyptian temple on the west bank of the Nile in Edfu, Upper Egypt. The city was known in Greek as Apollonopolis Magna, after the chief god Horus, and the temple is one of the best preserved shrines in Egypt.
tokens.image_credit: Ad Meskens · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Kom Ombo
tokens.description: The Temple of Kom Ombo is an unusual double temple in the town of Kom Ombo in Aswan Governorate, Upper Egypt. It was constructed during the Ptolemaic dynasty, 180 to 47 BC, with later additions in the Roman period.
tokens.image_credit: Olaf Tausch · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Colossi of Memnon
tokens.description: The Colossi of Memnon are two large stone statues of the Pharaoh Amenhotep III, standing at the front of the ruined Mortuary Temple of Amenhotep III in the Theban Necropolis. They have stood since about 1350 BC.
tokens.image_credit: MusikAnimal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Nasser
tokens.description: Lake Nasser is a large reservoir in southern Egypt and northern Sudan. It was created by the Aswan High Dam and is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nile
tokens.title: Longest river in Africa
tokens.description: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea. It is the longest river in the world, at about 7,088 kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: Fiktube · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Sinai
tokens.title: Where Moses received the law
tokens.description: Mount Sinai, also known as Jabal Musa, is a 2,285 metre mountain on the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt. It is one of several locations claimed to be the biblical Mount Sinai, where Moses is said to have received the Ten Commandments.
tokens.image_credit: Mcstafford at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
tokens.description: Saint Catherine's Monastery is a Christian monastery at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt's Sinai Peninsula. Built between 548 and 565, it is the world's oldest continuously inhabited Christian monastery and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Sand Sea
tokens.description: The Great Sand Sea is a sand desert of about 72,000 square kilometres in the Sahara, stretching from western Egypt to eastern Libya. Most of the area is covered by sand dunes.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Unger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wadi al Hitan
tokens.title: Valley of the Whales
tokens.description: Wadi al Hitan is a paleontological site in Egypt's Faiyum Governorate, about 150 kilometres south-west of Cairo. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005 for its fossils of early whales.
tokens.image_credit: AhmedMosaad · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cairo Citadel
tokens.description: The Cairo Citadel, also called the Citadel of Saladin, is a medieval Islamic fortification in Cairo, Egypt. Construction began under Saladin in 1176, and it was the seat of government and residence of Egypt's rulers for nearly 700 years.
tokens.image_credit: Ahmed Al.Badawy from Cairo, Egypt · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
tokens.description: Al-Azhar Mosque is a mosque in the historic Islamic core of Cairo, Egypt. Commissioned in 970 CE as the new capital of the Fatimid Caliphate, it was the first mosque established in the city.
tokens.image_credit: Wildoo78 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Muhammad Ali Mosque
tokens.description: The Muhammad Ali Mosque is a mosque in the Citadel of Cairo, Egypt, commissioned by Muhammad Ali Pasha and built between 1832 and 1857. It is one of the most visible landmarks on the Cairo skyline.
tokens.image_credit: Mohamed abdelzaher · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
tokens.description: The Pharos of Alexandria was a lighthouse built by the Ptolemaic Kingdom during the reign of Ptolemy II Philadelphus, from 280 to 247 BC. One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, it was for centuries one of the tallest man-made structures.
tokens.image_credit: Prof. Hermann Thiersch (1874–1939) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amman Citadel
tokens.description: The Amman Citadel is an archaeological site on Citadel Hill, overlooking downtown Amman, Jordan. It is considered among the world's oldest continuously inhabited places, with evidence of settlement since the Neolithic period.
tokens.image_credit: David Bjorgen · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Nebo
tokens.description: Mount Nebo is an elevated ridge in Jordan, about 700 metres above sea level, and part of the Abarim range. The Bible places it as the spot where Moses was granted a view of the Promised Land before his death.
tokens.image_credit: Thaler Tamas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Maghtas
tokens.description: Al-Maghtas, officially Baptism Site Bethany Beyond the Jordan, is an archaeological World Heritage Site on the east bank of the Jordan River. It is reputed to be the place of the Baptism of Jesus and has been venerated as such since the Byzantine period.
tokens.image_credit: Bob McCaffrey · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kerak Castle
tokens.description: Kerak Castle is a large medieval castle in al-Karak, Jordan, and one of the largest castles in the Levant. Construction began in the 1140s under Pagan and Fulk, King of Jerusalem.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dome of the Rock
tokens.title: Jerusalem's golden shrine
tokens.description: The Dome of the Rock is an octagonal Islamic shrine at the centre of the Al-Aqsa compound on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem's Old City. It is the world's oldest surviving work of Islamic architecture, built in 691 to 692 CE.
tokens.image_credit: Ludvig14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Western Wall
tokens.title: Holiest prayer site of Judaism
tokens.description: The Western Wall is an ancient retaining wall of the built-up hill known as the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. Its most famous section is used for Jewish prayer and is known in the West as the Wailing Wall.
tokens.image_credit: Golasso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
tokens.title: Site of Crucifixion and Resurrection
tokens.description: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre, also known as the Church of the Resurrection, is a fourth-century church in the Christian Quarter of the Old City of Jerusalem. It is the holiest site in Christianity.
tokens.image_credit: https://www.flickr.com/photos/jlascar/ · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Aqsa Mosque
tokens.title: Third holiest site in Islam
tokens.description: The Aqsa Mosque, also known as the Qibli Mosque, is the main congregational mosque in the Al-Aqsa compound in the Old City of Jerusalem. According to Islamic tradition, a small prayer hall on this site was built by Caliph Umar.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount of Olives
tokens.description: The Mount of Olives is a mountain ridge in East Jerusalem, east of the Old City. It is named for the olive groves that once covered its slopes.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Qumran
tokens.title: Dead Sea Scrolls site
tokens.description: Qumran is an archaeological site in the West Bank, managed by Israel's Qumran National Park. It lies on a marl plateau about 1.5 km from the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sea of Galilee
tokens.description: The Sea of Galilee, also called Lake Tiberias or Kinneret, is a freshwater lake in northeast Israel. Its surface lies between 209 and 215 metres below sea level, the lowest freshwater lake on Earth.
tokens.image_credit: Zachi Evenor and User:MathKnight · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Carmel
tokens.description: Mount Carmel is a coastal mountain range in northern Israel, stretching from the Mediterranean Sea towards the southeast. Haifa, Israel's third largest city, lies on its northern and western slopes.
tokens.image_credit: Chadner · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahá'í Terraces
tokens.title: Terraces of Haifa
tokens.description: The Bahá'í Terraces, or Hanging Gardens of Haifa, are garden terraces on Mount Carmel in Haifa. Completed in 2001, they have 19 terraces and over 1,500 steps, with the Shrine of the Báb at the centre.
tokens.image_credit: Юкатан · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Acre
tokens.title: Crusader city
tokens.description: Acre, known in Hebrew as Akko, is a coastal city in northern Israel on the Bay of Haifa. Its Old City is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: CristianChirita · GPL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ein Gedi Nature Reserve
tokens.description: Ein Gedi is an oasis and nature reserve on the west side of the Dead Sea in Israel, near Masada and the Qumran Caves. The site attracts about one million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Helebrant · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Makhtesh Ramon
tokens.description: Makhtesh Ramon, also called the Ramon Crater, is a geological feature of Israel's Negev desert. Its Hebrew name is makhtesh Ramon, meaning Ramon crater.
tokens.image_credit: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bethlehem
tokens.description: Bethlehem is a city in the West Bank, Palestine, about ten kilometres south of Jerusalem, and the capital of the Bethlehem Governorate. It is revered as the birthplace of Jesus, and the Church of the Nativity is there.
tokens.image_credit: Bukvoed · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Church of the Nativity
tokens.description: The Church of the Nativity, or Basilica of the Nativity, is a basilica in Bethlehem in the West Bank. It holds the grotto that Christians revere as the birthplace of Jesus, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Neil Ward · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cave of the Patriarchs
tokens.description: The Cave of the Patriarchs, also called the Ibrahimi Mosque, is a series of caves in the Old City of Hebron in the West Bank. It is considered a holy place in Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
tokens.image_credit: Utilisateur:Djampa - User:Djampa · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jericho
tokens.title: Oldest inhabited city
tokens.description: Jericho is a city in the West Bank, Palestine, and the capital of the Jericho Governorate. It lies in the Jordan Valley and is among the oldest cities in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Fullo88 at Italian Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Krak des Chevaliers
tokens.title: Crusader castle
tokens.description: Krak des Chevaliers is a medieval castle in Syria and one of the most important preserved medieval castles in the world. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Crac des Chevaliers and Qal'at Salah El-Din.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Umayyad Mosque
tokens.description: The Umayyad Mosque, also called the Great Mosque of Damascus, stands in the old city of Damascus, Syria. It is one of the largest and oldest mosques in the world and is considered the oldest mosque still in use in its original form.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bosra
tokens.description: Bosra is a town in southern Syria, historically Bostra, and an ancient city mentioned in 14th century BC Egyptian sources. It was the northern capital of the Nabataean kingdom and later the provincial capital of the Roman province of Arabia Petraea.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ebla
tokens.description: Ebla, also called Tell Mardikh, is an ancient site about 55 km southwest of Aleppo in Syria. It was one of the earliest kingdoms in Syria and an important centre throughout the 3rd millennium BC.
tokens.image_credit: Inge at en.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Apamea, Syria
tokens.description: Apamea is an ancient Hellenistic and Roman city on the right bank of the Orontes River in northwestern Syria. It was founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator and later became capital of the Roman province of Syria Secunda.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dura-Europos
tokens.description: Dura-Europos was a Hellenistic, Parthian and Roman border city on an escarpment above the Euphrates river in present-day Syria. It was founded around 300 BC by Seleucus I Nicator.
tokens.image_credit: Heretiq · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ugarit
tokens.description: Ugarit was an ancient Levantine coastal city in what is today northern Syria, at the site known as Ras Shamra. Since its discovery in 1928 the site has revealed the oldest known systematic use of an alphabet.
tokens.image_credit: Haubi|Gerhard Haubold · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tyre, Lebanon
tokens.description: Tyre is a city in Lebanon and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It was one of the earliest Phoenician metropolises and was added as a whole to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1984.
tokens.image_credit: RomanDeckert · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anjar, Lebanon
tokens.description: Anjar is an Umayyad palace-city ruin in the Bekaa Valley near the Syrian border, founded in the early 8th century by Caliph al-Walid I. The site was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1984.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kadisha Valley
tokens.description: Kadisha Valley is a gorge in the Bsharri and Zgharta districts of northern Lebanon, carved by the Kadisha River. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Qadisha Valley and the Forest of the Cedars of God.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Prophet's Mosque
tokens.title: Mosque in Medina
tokens.description: The Prophet's Mosque is the second mosque built by the Islamic prophet Muhammad in Medina, after the Quba Mosque. It is the second holiest site in Islam, after the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca.
tokens.image_credit: Bluemangoa2z at Malayalam Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Arafat
tokens.description: Mount Arafat, also called Jabal al-Rahmah or Mountain of Mercy, is a granodiorite hill about 20 km southeast of Mecca in Saudi Arabia. It is a central site of the Hajj pilgrimage.
tokens.image_credit: Al Jazeera English · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cave of Hira
tokens.description: Cave of Hira is the grotto on Jabal al-Nour, a mountain near Mecca in Saudi Arabia. Tradition holds that the Islamic prophet Muhammad received his first revelation of the Quran there.
tokens.image_credit: saudipics · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nafud desert
tokens.description: The Nafud desert is an erg, a sand desert region in north-central Saudi Arabia. It occupies a great oval depression of about 65,000 square kilometres in the northern Arabian Peninsula.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Qasr Al Watan
tokens.description: Qasr Al Watan is the presidential palace of the United Arab Emirates, located in Abu Dhabi. It hosts state receptions and Council of Ministers meetings, and it is also open to visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Renek78 · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Liwa Oasis
tokens.description: The Liwa Oasis is a large oasis area in the Western Region of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It is a desert oasis within the emirate's Western Region.

tokens.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
tokens.description: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque is a Friday mosque in Muscat, the capital of Oman. Completed in 2001, it is the largest mosque in the country and can accommodate 20,000 worshippers.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Bartz · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahla Fort
tokens.description: Bahla Fort is one of four historic fortresses at the foot of the Jebel Akhdar highlands in Oman. It was the country's first fort inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in 1987.
tokens.image_credit: Francisco Anzola · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wadi Shab
tokens.description: Wadi Shab is a canyon in the Eastern Hajar mountains of Oman's Ash Sharqiyah region. It opens onto the Gulf of Oman near the village of Ash Shab and is known for its rock pools and grotto.

tokens.name: Shibam
tokens.title: Manhattan of the desert
tokens.description: Shibam is a town in Wadi Hadhramaut in eastern Yemen, known for its mudbrick high-rise buildings, some reaching eleven stories. The Old Walled City of Shibam is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Maria Gropa · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old City of Sanaa
tokens.description: The Old City of Sanaa is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Yemen, inhabited for more than 2,500 years. Its fortified old town contains many intact architectural sites.
tokens.image_credit: ai@ce · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al Fateh Grand Mosque
tokens.description: The Al-Fateh Mosque is a large mosque in Manama, Bahrain, built in 1987 and named after Ahmed Al Fateh. It can accommodate over 7,000 worshippers and was once one of the largest mosques in the world.
tokens.image_credit: XIDME · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kuwait Towers
tokens.description: The Kuwait Towers are a group of three towers in Kuwait City, standing on a promontory into the Persian Gulf. They were officially inaugurated in March 1979 and are regarded as a symbol of modern Kuwait.
tokens.image_credit: Richard Bartz · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shah Mosque, Isfahan
tokens.description: The Shah Mosque, also called the Imam Mosque, stands on the south side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square in Isfahan, Iran. Construction began in 1611 under Abbas the Great and was completed around 1630.
tokens.image_credit: Patrickringgenberg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque
tokens.description: The Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque is a Shi'ite mosque on the eastern side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square in Isfahan, Iran. Construction ran from 1602 or 1603 to 1618 or 1619, during the Safavid era.
tokens.image_credit: Nicolas Hadjisavvas · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ali Qapu
tokens.description: Ali Qapu is an imperial palace in Isfahan, Iran, on the western side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square. It was designed as a vast portal entrance to the grand palace that stretched from the square to Chaharbagh Boulevard.
tokens.image_credit: Amir Pashaei · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Si-o-se-pol
tokens.description: Si-o-se-pol, also called the Allahverdi Khan Bridge, is the largest of the eleven historical bridges on the Zayanderud river in Isfahan, Iran. It was built in the early 17th century to serve as both a bridge and a dam.
tokens.image_credit: Wikinewis1377q · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khaju Bridge
tokens.description: The Khaju Bridge is a historic bridge on the Zayanderud river in Isfahan, Iran. It serves as both a bridge and a weir, linking the Khaju quarter with the Zoroastrian quarter across the river.
tokens.image_credit: Gire 3pich2005 with special thanks to Hossein Majidi · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vank Cathedral
tokens.description: The Holy Savior Cathedral, commonly called the Vank, is an Armenian Apostolic cathedral in the New Julfa district of Isfahan, Iran. The word Vank means monastery or convent in Armenian.
tokens.image_credit: User:Ggia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golestan Palace
tokens.description: The Golestan Palace is the former official royal Qajar complex in Tehran, Iran, consisting of eight palatial royal structures inside a wall. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and today houses museums.
tokens.image_credit: ZarlokX · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vakil Mosque
tokens.description: The Vakil Mosque is a Shi'ite mosque in Shiraz, in the Fars province of southern Iran. It stands west of the Vakil Bazaar, next to the bazaar entrance, and is on the Iran National Heritage List.
tokens.image_credit: dynamosquito from France · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fatima Masumeh Shrine
tokens.description: The Fatima Masumeh Shrine is the mausoleum of Fatima bint Musa, located in Qom, Iran. Qom is considered a holy city in Shia Islam and is the world's largest center for Shia Islamic scholarship.
tokens.image_credit: Mahdi Fathi Arjmand · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Susa
tokens.description: Susa was an ancient city in the lower Zagros Mountains of Iran, one of the most important cities of the Ancient Near East. It served as the capital of Elam and the winter capital of the Achaemenid Empire.
tokens.image_credit: Carole Raddato from Frankfurt, Germany · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bam, Iran
tokens.description: Bam is a city in Kerman province, Iran, and the capital of Bam County. The modern city surrounds its ancient citadel, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Arad Mojtahedi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arg-e Bam
tokens.description: Arg-e Bam is a large adobe citadel in the city of Bam, Kerman province, Iran. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Bam and its Cultural Landscape.
tokens.image_credit: Safa.daneshvar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jameh Mosque of Yazd
tokens.description: The Jameh Mosque of Yazd is a Friday mosque in the city of Yazd, Iran. It was built on the site of a 9th-century fire temple and completed during the 14th and 15th centuries.
tokens.image_credit: Ebrahimlotfi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Salt Desert
tokens.description: The Great Salt Desert, also called Dasht-e Kavir, is a large desert in the middle of the Iranian Plateau. At about 77,600 square km it is the world's 24th largest desert.
tokens.image_credit: Klára Nováková · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Urmia
tokens.description: Lake Urmia is an endorheic salt lake in the Iranian region of Azerbaijan, near the Armenian border. At its greatest extent it was the largest lake in West Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Solmaz Daryani · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alamut Castle
tokens.title: Assassins' fortress
tokens.description: Alamut Castle is a ruined mountain fortress near Gazor Khan in Qazvin province, Iran. From 1090 it was held by Hassan-i Sabbah and served as the headquarters of the Nizari Ismaili state until 1256.
tokens.image_credit: Ninara from Helsinki, Finland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Takht-e Soleymān
tokens.description: Takht-e Soleymān is a fortified Sasanian-era archaeological site in West Azerbaijan province, Iran, on a hill formed by a calcium-rich spring pond. It was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Elaheabed · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bisotun
tokens.description: Bisotun is a town in Kermanshah province, Iran, and the centre of a UNESCO World Heritage site inscribed in 2006. The site holds the Behistun Inscription and remains from prehistoric to Ilkhanid periods.
tokens.image_credit: Ninara from Helsinki, Finland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Behistun inscription
tokens.title: Rosetta stone of cuneiform
tokens.description: The Behistun inscription is a multilingual Achaemenid royal inscription and rock relief on a cliff at Mount Behistun in Kermanshah Province, Iran. It is the longest known trilingual cuneiform inscription and helped decipher cuneiform.
tokens.image_credit: PersianDutchNetwork · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bazaar of Tabriz
tokens.description: The Bazaar of Tabriz is a historic market in central Tabriz, Iran, and one of the oldest bazaars in the Middle East. It is one of Iran's UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
tokens.image_credit: Navid Alizadeh Sadighi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ziggurat of Ur
tokens.description: The Ziggurat of Ur is a Neo-Sumerian ziggurat in the ancient city of Ur near Nasiriyah, Dhi Qar Province, Iraq. It was built in the Early Bronze Age by King Ur-Nammu and restored by King Nabonidus.
tokens.image_credit: Tla2006 at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nimrud
tokens.description: Nimrud is an ancient Assyrian city, originally called Kalhu, in the Nineveh Plains of Iraq, about 30 km south of Mosul. It was a major Assyrian capital between roughly 1350 BC and 610 BC.
tokens.image_credit: Staff Sgt. JoAnn Makinano · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Assur
tokens.description: Assur, also known as Ashur, was the capital of the Middle Assyrian Empire for a time and later of the Neo-Assyrian Empire. Its remains lie on the Tigris in Iraq, and the site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Véronique Dauge · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Samarra
tokens.title: Malwiya spiral minaret
tokens.description: Samarra is a city in Saladin Governorate, Iraq, on the east bank of the Tigris about 125 km north of Baghdad. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered a holy site in Shia Islam because of the Al-Askari Shrine.
tokens.image_credit: Jim Gordon · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imam Ali Shrine
tokens.description: The Imam Ali Shrine is a Shia mosque and mausoleum in Najaf, Iraq. Shia and Sunni Muslims believe it contains the tomb of Ali ibn Abi Talib, a cousin and companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
tokens.image_credit: Goudarz.memar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Imam Husayn Shrine
tokens.description: The Imam Husayn Shrine is the mausoleum of Husayn ibn Ali in the holy city of Karbala, Iraq. It is one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam, and millions of pilgrims visit it, especially for Ashura.
tokens.image_credit: Safa.daneshvar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Kazimiyya Mosque
tokens.description: The Kadhimiyya Mosque is a Twelver Shia mosque and shrine in the Kadhimiya suburb of Baghdad, Iraq. It contains the tombs of the seventh and ninth Shia Imams, Musa al-Kadhim and Muhammad al-Jawad.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Mahdi Karim · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lalish
tokens.description: Lalish is a valley and temple complex in the Shekhan district of northern Iraq. It is the central temple of the Yazidis, who are expected to make a pilgrimage there once in their lifetime where possible.
tokens.image_credit: Levi Clancy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tigris
tokens.description: The Tigris is the eastern of the two great rivers that define Mesopotamia, the other being the Euphrates. It flows south from the Armenian Highlands and passes historical cities such as Mosul, Tikrit, Samarra and Baghdad.
tokens.image_credit: Dûrzan cîrano · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Euphrates
tokens.description: The Euphrates is the longest and one of the most historically important rivers of West Asia. Together with the Tigris, it defines Mesopotamia, flowing from Turkey through Syria and Iraq.
tokens.image_credit: Carole Raddato from Frankfurt, Germany · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mesopotamian Marshes
tokens.description: The Mesopotamian Marshes, also known as the Iraqi Marshes, are a wetland area in southern Iraq and southwestern Iran. Historically they were the largest wetland ecosystem of western Eurasia.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uruk
tokens.description: Uruk, known today as Warka, was an ancient city of Sumer in southern Iraq and the type site of the Uruk period. At its peak around 3100 BC it may have been the largest urban area in the world.
tokens.image_credit: SAC Andy Holmes (RAF) · OGL v1.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lut Desert
tokens.title: Hottest surface on Earth
tokens.description: Lut Desert is a desert with extensive salt flats and dunes in the provinces of Kerman and Sistan-Baluchestan, Iran. It is the world's 33rd-largest desert and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2016.
tokens.image_credit: Ninaras · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
tokens.description: The Bibi-Khanym Mosque is one of the most important monuments of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. In the 15th century it was one of the largest and most magnificent mosques in the Islamic world.
tokens.image_credit: David Stanley from Nanaimo, Canada · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kalyan Minaret
tokens.description: The Kalyan Minaret is a 12th-century minaret of the Po-i-Kalyan mosque complex in Bukhara, Uzbekistan. It was completed in 1127 and is one of the most prominent landmarks of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moynaq
tokens.title: Ship graveyard
tokens.description: Moynaq is a city in northern Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, and the seat of Moynaq district. Formerly a sea port on the Aral Sea, it now lies about 150 km from the water in the Aralkum Desert.
tokens.image_credit: THORSTEN · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Balkhash
