tokens.description: Parícutin is a cinder cone volcano in Michoacán state, near Uruapan. It surged from a cornfield in 1943 and gave modern science its first chance to document the full life cycle of this type of eruption.
tokens.image_credit: Karla Yannín Alcázar Quintero (photographer) · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Volcán de Colima
tokens.description: Volcán de Colima, also called Volcán de Fuego, is a 4,260 metre stratovolcano and part of the Colima Volcanic Complex. It is one of the most active volcanoes in Mexico and North America.
tokens.image_credit: Jrobertiko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sumidero Canyon
tokens.description: Sumidero Canyon is a deep natural canyon just north of Chiapa de Corzo in Chiapas, southern Mexico. Its vertical walls reach as high as 1,000 metres, and the Grijalva River runs through the gorge.
tokens.image_credit: Jan Harenburg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ik Kil
tokens.description: Ik Kil is a cenote outside Pisté in Yucatán, Mexico, near Chichén Itzá. It lies in the Ik Kil Archeological Park and is open to the public for swimming.
tokens.image_credit: Dmadeo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sistema Sac Actun
tokens.description: Sistema Sac Actun is an underwater cave system on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatán Peninsula, with passages north and west of Tulum. As of January 2023 it is the second longest underwater cave system in the world.

tokens.name: Cave of the Crystals
tokens.title: Giant selenite crystals
tokens.description: Cave of the Crystals is a chamber connected to the Naica Mine, about 300 metres deep, in Naica, Chihuahua, Mexico. It holds giant selenite crystals, some of the largest natural crystals ever found.
tokens.image_credit: Alexander Van Driessche · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hierve el Agua
tokens.description: Hierve el Agua is a set of natural travertine rock formations in San Lorenzo Albarradas, Oaxaca, Mexico, about 70 km east of Oaxaca City. The white formations look like frozen waterfalls, built up by mineral-rich fresh springs.
tokens.image_credit: Adrián Cerón · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Agua Azul
tokens.description: Agua Azul is a series of waterfalls on the Xanil River in Chiapas, Mexico, in the municipality of Tumbalá, about 69 km from Palenque. The falls form many cataracts one after another.
tokens.image_credit: Own work · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve
tokens.description: The Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the border of Michoacan and the State of Mexico, about 100 km northwest of Mexico City. It contains most of the overwintering sites of the eastern monarch butterfly population.
tokens.image_credit: Charles J. Sharp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isla Mujeres
tokens.description: Isla Mujeres is an island about 13 km off the Yucatan Peninsula coast in Quintana Roo, Mexico, where the Gulf of Mexico meets the Caribbean Sea. Its namesake town had 12,642 inhabitants in the 2010 census.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cozumel
tokens.description: Cozumel is an island and municipality in the Caribbean Sea off the eastern coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, opposite Playa del Carmen. It is separated from the mainland by the Cozumel Channel.

tokens.name: Revillagigedo Islands
tokens.description: The Revillagigedo Islands are a group of four volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean, lying south and southwest of Cabo San Lucas, Baja California. The archipelago is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its unique ecosystem.
tokens.image_credit: Lieutenant Debora Barr, NOAA Corps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isla Holbox
tokens.description: Holbox is an island in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo, off the north coast of the Yucatan Peninsula. It is about 42 km long and is separated from the mainland by a shallow lagoon.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Chapala
tokens.description: Lake Chapala is Mexico's largest freshwater lake, bordering the states of Jalisco and Michoacan. It has been the country's largest lake since Lake Texcoco dried up in the early 17th century.

tokens.name: Cabo San Lucas
tokens.description: Cabo San Lucas is a resort city on the southern tip of the Baja California peninsula, in the Mexican state of Baja California Sur. The 2020 Census recorded a population of 202,694.
tokens.image_credit: User:Stan Shebs · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Pinacate y Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve
tokens.description: El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Sonoran Desert of northwest Mexico, just south of the Arizona border. It is managed by the Mexican federal government with the state of Sonora and the Tohono O'odham.
tokens.image_credit: Presidencia de la República Mexicana · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sierra Gorda
tokens.description: Sierra Gorda is an ecological region and mountain range in the northern third of the Mexican state of Queretaro, extending into Guanajuato, Hidalgo and San Luis Potosi. The area is rugged, with high steep mountains and deep canyons.
tokens.aliases: Franciscan Missions in the Sierra Gorda
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Diógenes89 assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taxco
tokens.description: Taxco de Alarcon is a small city in the Mexican state of Guerrero, known for silver mining and for its silver jewelry and silverware crafts. It is the administrative centre of Taxco de Alarcon Municipality.
tokens.image_credit: María Quezada Aranda · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Miguel de Allende
tokens.description: San Miguel de Allende is a city in the Bajio region of the Mexican state of Guanajuato, about 274 km from Mexico City. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Protective Town of San Miguel and the Sanctuary of Jesus Nazareno de Atotonilco.
tokens.image_credit: https://www.flickr.com/photos/jiuguangw/ · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morelia Cathedral
tokens.description: Morelia Cathedral, formally the Metropolitan Cathedral of Morelia, is the seat of the Archdiocese of Morelia in the capital of the Mexican state of Michoacan. It stands on the first square of the city, within the UNESCO Historic Centre of Morelia.
tokens.image_credit: L. Raul Chavez G. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puebla Cathedral
tokens.description: The Basilica Cathedral of Puebla is the episcopal see of the Archdiocese of Puebla de los Angeles in Mexico. Consecrated in 1649, it stands in the historic centre of Puebla, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuicuilco
tokens.description: Cuicuilco is an archaeological site on the southern shore of Lake Texcoco in Mexico City. Its circular pyramid was begun a few centuries BCE, and the site was destroyed by the eruption of Xitle around 245 to 315 CE.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew T. Bradley · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Pyramid of Cholula
tokens.title: Largest pyramid by volume
tokens.description: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, also called Tlachihualtepetl, is in Cholula, Puebla, Mexico. It is the largest pyramid by volume known in the world, and the largest archaeological site of a pyramid in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Xcaret
tokens.description: Xcaret is a Maya archaeological site on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatan Peninsula in Quintana Roo, Mexico. The site functioned as a Maya port and trading centre, and some of its structures lie within the Xcaret Park tourism development.
tokens.image_credit: AMAPO · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Havana Cathedral
tokens.description: Havana Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception of Mary, is the seat of the Archdiocese of San Cristobal de la Habana. It stands on Plaza de la Catedral in Old Havana, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: akasenn · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: National Capitol of Cuba
tokens.description: The National Capitol of Cuba, also known as El Capitolio, is a public edifice in Havana, the capital of Cuba. It was built from 1926 to 1929 under the direction of Eugenio Rayneri Piedra.
tokens.image_credit: Yomangani · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castillo de los Tres Reyes Del Morro
tokens.description: The Castillo de los Tres Reyes del Morro, also called Morro Castle, is a fortress guarding the entrance to Havana harbor. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Old Havana and its Fortification System.
tokens.image_credit: National Photo Company Collection · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cienfuegos
tokens.description: Cienfuegos is a city on the southern coast of Cuba and the capital of Cienfuegos Province. Its Urban Historic Centre was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage property in 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Burkhard Mücke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca
tokens.description: The Castillo de San Pedro de la Roca is a fortress on the coast of Santiago de Cuba, overlooking the bay. UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 1997 as the best preserved example of Spanish-American military architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Glogg, Peter, Switzerland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Desembarco del Granma National Park
tokens.description: Desembarco del Granma National Park is a national park in south-western Cuba, in Granma Province. Named after the yacht Granma that brought Fidel Castro's group to Cuba in 1956, it was listed by UNESCO in 1999 for its uplifted marine terraces and karst.

tokens.name: Sierra Maestra
tokens.description: The Sierra Maestra is a mountain range running westward across the south of south-eastern Cuba, rising abruptly from the coast. It lies mainly within Santiago de Cuba and Granma Provinces.

tokens.name: Jardines de la Reina
tokens.description: Jardines de la Reina is an archipelago of cays and coral reefs in southern Cuba, in Camagüey and Ciego de Ávila provinces. A marine reserve covering a large part of the archipelago was established in 1996.

tokens.name: Blue Mountains, Jamaica
tokens.description: The Blue Mountains are the longest mountain range in Jamaica. They include Blue Mountain Peak, the island's highest point at 2,256 m (7,402 ft).

tokens.name: Dunn's River Falls
tokens.description: Dunn's River Falls is a famous waterfall near Ocho Rios, Jamaica. It is a well-known visitor site on the island.
tokens.image_credit: Breakyunit at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Port Royal
tokens.description: Port Royal is a small town at the end of the Palisadoes, at the mouth of Kingston Harbour, Jamaica. Founded by the Spanish in 1494, it was destroyed by an earthquake in 1692 and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Sans-Souci Palace
tokens.description: Sans-Souci Palace was the principal royal residence of Henri Christophe, King of Haiti, in Milot. The palace and the neighbouring Citadelle were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Rémi Kaupp · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcázar de Colón
tokens.description: The Alcázar de Colón is the first fortified European palace built in the Americas, in the colonial area of Santo Domingo. It was built between 1511 and 1514 and forms part of the Ciudad Colonial UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cathedral of Santo Domingo
tokens.description: The Cathedral of Santo Domingo is the oldest existing cathedral in the Americas, begun in 1504 and completed in 1550. It stands in the Colonial City of Santo Domingo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Georg Karl Ell · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pico Duarte
tokens.description: Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the Dominican Republic and in the Caribbean, at 3,101 m above sea level on Hispaniola. It lies about 85 km northeast of Lake Enriquillo, the region's lowest point.

tokens.name: Lake Enriquillo
tokens.description: Lake Enriquillo is a hypersaline lake in southwestern Dominican Republic. It is the largest lake in both the Dominican Republic and the Caribbean, and its waters are shared by the Bahoruco and Independencia provinces.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Alberto Silver · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Yunque National Forest
tokens.description: El Yunque National Forest is a tropical rainforest in the Sierra de Luquillo, northeast of San Juan, Puerto Rico, managed by the U.S. Forest Service since 1903. It is the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System.
tokens.image_credit: Harvey Barrison · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Juan National Historic Site
tokens.description: San Juan National Historic Site preserves the Spanish colonial fortification system of San Juan, Puerto Rico, including the San Felipe del Morro and San Cristobal fortresses. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
tokens.image_credit: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User:Jmoliver · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Mosquito
tokens.title: Brightest bioluminescent bay
tokens.description: Puerto Mosquito, also called Mosquito Bio Bay, is a bay on the island of Vieques, Puerto Rico. It is famous for the bioluminescence produced by the dinoflagellate Pyrodinium bahamense.

tokens.name: Parque Nacional de las Cavernas del Río Camuy
tokens.description: The Parque Nacional de las Cavernas del Río Camuy is a limestone cave system in northwestern Puerto Rico, carved by the Río Camuy. The park lies between the municipalities of Camuy, Hatillo and Lares.
tokens.image_credit: Per Aspera · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gros Piton
tokens.description: Gros Piton is a volcanic plug of about 798 m in Saint Lucia, one of the two Pitons. The Pitons are a UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Petit Piton
tokens.description: Petit Piton is a volcanic plug of about 743 m in Saint Lucia, the smaller of the two Pitons. The Pitons are a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Jayen466 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soufrière Hills
tokens.description: The Soufrière Hills is an active stratovolcano with many lava domes on the Caribbean island of Montserrat, a British overseas territory. It erupted from 1995 to 2010 and last erupted in 2013.
tokens.image_credit: CommonismNow · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Soufrière
tokens.description: La Soufrière is an active volcano on the Caribbean island of Saint Vincent and the highest peak on the island. It has had eight recorded eruptions since 1718, the latest in 2020 and 2021.

tokens.name: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park
tokens.description: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park is a well-preserved fortress on a hill on the island of Saint Kitts. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Ukexpat · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boiling Lake
tokens.description: The Boiling Lake is a flooded fumarole in Morne Trois Pitons National Park on the island of Dominica. It is the second-largest hot lake in the world, after Frying Pan Lake in New Zealand.
tokens.image_credit: Bayukjdr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morne Trois Pitons National Park
tokens.description: Morne Trois Pitons National Park is a national park in Dominica, established in July 1975 as the first legally established park in the country. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

tokens.name: Nelson's Dockyard
tokens.description: Nelson's Dockyard is a cultural heritage site and marina in English Harbour on the island of Antigua. It is the only continuously working Georgian era dockyard in the world, built in the early 18th century.
tokens.image_credit: David Stanley · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pitch Lake
tokens.title: World's largest natural asphalt lake
tokens.description: The Pitch Lake is the largest natural deposit of bitumen in the world, estimated to contain 10 million tons. It is located in La Brea in southwest Trinidad.
tokens.image_credit: Martina Jackson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tobago Cays
tokens.description: The Tobago Cays are an archipelago of five small islands and extensive coral reefs in the Southern Grenadines of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. They form the key element of the Tobago Cays Marine Park.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Schäfer, Lich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Baths
tokens.description: The Baths is a beach area on Virgin Gorda in the British Virgin Islands, known for its granite boulders and white sand beaches. It is part of The Baths National Park managed by the BVI National Parks Trust.
tokens.image_credit: Calyponte · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belize Barrier Reef
tokens.title: Second largest barrier reef
tokens.description: The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs along the coast of Belize, the second largest coral reef system in the world after the Great Barrier Reef. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Bernt Rostad · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caracol
tokens.description: Caracol is a large ancient Maya archaeological site in the Cayo District of Belize. It lies on the Vaca Plateau in the foothills of the Maya Mountains, about 40 km south of Xunantunich.
tokens.image_credit: Pgbk87 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Xunantunich
tokens.description: Xunantunich is an ancient Maya archaeological site in the Cayo District of western Belize, about 110 km west of Belize City. It sits on a ridge above the Mopan River, within sight of the Guatemala border.
tokens.image_credit: Denis Barthel · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Altun Ha
tokens.description: Altun Ha is the ruins of an ancient Maya city in the Belize District of Belize, about 50 km north of Belize City. The site came to the attention of archaeologists only in 1963.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Lazarev (Asmadeus) · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Actun Tunichil Muknal
tokens.description: Actun Tunichil Muknal is a cave near San Ignacio in Belize's Cayo District. It is a Maya archaeological site with ceramics and skeletal remains, including the calcified skeleton known as the Crystal Maiden.
tokens.image_credit: Jkolecki · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bermuda
tokens.title: Bermuda Triangle
tokens.description: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is an archipelago of 181 islands, with the main islands joined by bridges.
tokens.image_credit: Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kata Tjuta
tokens.description: Kata Tjuta is a group of large, domed rock formations about 360 km southwest of Alice Springs in central Australia. It is part of the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Sterry2607 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nitmiluk National Park
tokens.description: Nitmiluk National Park is in the Northern Territory of Australia, about 23 km northeast of Katherine. It is built around a series of gorges on the Katherine River and Edith Falls, and is of great ceremonial significance to the Jawoyn people.

tokens.name: Karijini National Park
tokens.description: Karijini National Park is centred in the Hamersley Ranges of the Pilbara region in north-western Western Australia. It lies about 1,055 km from Perth, the state capital.
tokens.image_credit: Graeme Churchard from Bristol (51.4414, -2.5242), UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Purnululu National Park
tokens.title: Bungle Bungle Range
tokens.description: Purnululu National Park is a World Heritage Site in the East Kimberley region of Western Australia. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 2003 and lies about 300 km south of Kununurra.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Kimberley
tokens.description: The Kimberley is the northernmost of the nine regions of Western Australia. It is bordered by the Indian Ocean to the west, the Timor Sea to the north and the Northern Territory to the east.

tokens.name: Shark Bay
tokens.description: Shark Bay is a World Heritage Site in the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, about 800 kilometres north of Perth. It is known for one of the largest and most diverse seagrass beds in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Paul Harrison · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve
tokens.title: Stromatolites
tokens.description: Hamelin Pool Marine Nature Reserve is a protected marine nature reserve in the Gascoyne region of Western Australia. It lies within the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Shark Bay.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Kraft · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Three Sisters, Australia
tokens.description: The Three Sisters are an unusual rock formation in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia, on the north escarpment of the Jamison Valley. They are located close to the town of Katoomba.
tokens.image_credit: MrActiniuM · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wineglass Bay
tokens.description: Wineglass Bay lies on the Freycinet Peninsula within Freycinet National Park, on the east coast of Tasmania. The park is about 125 kilometres northeast of Hobart.
tokens.image_credit: aussiejeff from Perth, WA, Australia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area
tokens.description: The Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area is a World Heritage Site in Tasmania, Australia. It covers about 15,800 square kilometres, almost 25 per cent of the island, and is one of the last expanses of temperate wilderness in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ball's Pyramid
tokens.description: Ball's Pyramid is an uninhabited islet in the Pacific Ocean about 20 kilometres southeast of Lord Howe Island, between Australia and New Zealand. It is 572 metres high, making it the tallest volcanic stack in the world.
tokens.image_credit: PotMart186 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Willandra Lakes Region
tokens.description: The Willandra Lakes Region is a World Heritage Site in the Far West region of New South Wales, Australia. It is the traditional meeting place of the Muthi Muthi, Ngiyampaa and Paakantyi Aboriginal peoples.

tokens.name: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre
tokens.description: Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre, known as Lake Eyre, is an endorheic lake in the Far North region of South Australia, about 700 kilometres north of Adelaide. It is the largest ephemeral endorheic lake on the Australian continent.
tokens.image_credit: NASA/STS-35 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Simpson Desert
tokens.description: The Simpson Desert is a large area of dry, red sandy plain and dunes in the Northern Territory, South Australia and Queensland in central Australia. It is the fourth-largest Australian desert, with an area of 176,500 km2.
tokens.image_credit: User:Phanly (talk) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nullarbor Plain
tokens.description: The Nullarbor Plain is a flat, almost treeless, arid to semi-arid region of southern Australia on the Great Australian Bight coast. It is the world's largest single exposure of limestone bedrock.

tokens.name: Great Victoria Desert
tokens.description: The Great Victoria Desert is a sparsely populated desert ecoregion and interim Australian bioregion in Western Australia and South Australia.

tokens.name: Devils Marbles
tokens.description: Karlu Karlu / Devils Marbles Conservation Reserve is a protected area in the Northern Territory of Australia, about 105 km south of Tennant Creek. The nearest settlement is the small town of Wauchope.
tokens.image_credit: Iain Whyte (Iainwhyte) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kings Canyon
tokens.description: Kings Canyon, also known as Watarrka, is a canyon in the Northern Territory of Australia at the western end of the George Gill Range. It lies within Watarrka National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Zoharby · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: MacDonnell Ranges
tokens.description: The MacDonnell Ranges, or Tjoritja, is a mountain range in southern Northern Territory. It is a 644 km long series of parallel ridges running east and west of Alice Springs.
tokens.image_credit: Toby Hudson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Kosciuszko
tokens.description: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain of mainland Australia, at 2,228 metres above sea level. It is located on the Main Range of the Snowy Mountains in Kosciuszko National Park, New South Wales.

tokens.name: Mount Wellington, Tasmania
tokens.description: Mount Wellington, also known as Kunanyi, is a mountain in south-east Tasmania, Australia. It is the summit of the Wellington Range, and Hobart lies at its foot.
tokens.image_credit: neiloz · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fremantle Prison
tokens.description: Fremantle Prison is a former Australian prison in Fremantle, Western Australia, and a World Heritage Site. It was first used for convicts transported from Britain and passed to the colonial government in 1886.
tokens.image_credit: Gnangarra · CC BY 2.5 au · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kangaroo Island
tokens.description: Kangaroo Island, known as KI, is Australia's third-largest island, after Tasmania and Melville Island. It lies in South Australia, about 112 km southwest of Adelaide.

tokens.name: Flinders Ranges
tokens.description: The Flinders Ranges are the largest mountain ranges in South Australia, stretching over 430 km from Port Pirie to Lake Callabonna. The Adnyamathanha people have inhabited the range for tens of thousands of years.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew Summerton · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coober Pedy
tokens.description: Coober Pedy is a town in northern South Australia, 846 km from Adelaide via the Stuart Highway. It is known as the opal capital of the world because of its opal mining.
tokens.image_credit: qwesy qwesy · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Augustus, Western Australia
tokens.description: Mount Augustus is a large monolith about 1,000 km north of Perth, in Mount Augustus National Park in Western Australia. The local Wadjari people call it Burringurrah.
tokens.image_credit: Graeme Churchard from Bristol, UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
tokens.description: Heard Island and McDonald Islands is an Australian external territory of sub-Antarctic volcanic islands in the southern Indian Ocean. The territory was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Tristannew (original) Derivative: SHB2000 (cropped) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cocos Islands
tokens.description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are an Australian external territory of two atolls with 27 coral islands in the Indian Ocean, midway between Australia and Sri Lanka. Only West Island and Home Island are inhabited.

tokens.name: Mount Ngauruhoe
tokens.title: Mount Doom
tokens.description: Mount Ngauruhoe is a volcanic cone in the Tongariro complex on the Central Plateau of New Zealand's North Island. It is the youngest vent of the Tongariro stratovolcano and first erupted about 2,500 years ago.
tokens.image_credit: Eusebius · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Taranaki
tokens.description: Mount Taranaki is a dormant stratovolcano in the Taranaki region on the west coast of New Zealand's North Island. At 2,518 metres it is the second highest mountain in the North Island.
tokens.image_credit: Ulrich Lange, Bochum, Germany · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Wakatipu
tokens.description: Lake Wakatipu is an inland finger lake in the South Island of New Zealand, in the southwest corner of the Otago region. It lies near the boundary with Southland.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Gadfium assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Taupō
tokens.description: Lake Taupō is a large crater lake in the caldera of Taupō Volcano on New Zealand's North Island. With a surface area of 616 square kilometres, it is the largest lake in New Zealand by surface area.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Bo-deh~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pancake Rocks and Blowholes
tokens.description: Pancake Rocks and Blowholes is a coastal rock formation at Punakaiki on the West Coast of New Zealand's South Island. It is a popular visitor attraction.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Whakaari / White Island
tokens.description: Whakaari / White Island is an active andesite stratovolcano about 48 km off the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, in the Bay of Plenty. It is the peak of a much larger submarine volcano.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Routeburn Track
tokens.description: The Routeburn Track is a 32 km tramping (hiking) track in the South Island of New Zealand. The Department of Conservation classifies it as a Great Walk.

tokens.name: Mitre Peak
tokens.description: Mitre Peak (Māori: Rahotu) is a mountain in the South Island of New Zealand. It stands on the shore of Milford Sound.
tokens.image_credit: Szilas · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stewart Island
tokens.description: Stewart Island (Māori: Rakiura) is the third-largest and southernmost inhabited island of New Zealand. It lies about 30 km south of the South Island, across Foveaux Strait.

tokens.name: Huka Falls
tokens.description: Huka Falls is a set of waterfalls on the Waikato River, which drains Lake Taupō in New Zealand. Upstream, the river narrows from about 100 metres across to a canyon only 15 metres wide.
tokens.image_credit: Avenue · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waimangu Volcanic Rift Valley
tokens.description: The Waimangu Volcanic Rift Valley is a hydrothermal system created by the 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera on New Zealand's North Island. It contains Frying Pan Lake, which is described as the largest hot spring in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Otemanu
tokens.description: Mount Otemanu is a mountain on the island of Bora Bora in the South Pacific. At 727 metres it is the highest point of the island, and it is an extinct volcano.
tokens.image_credit: Borabora.jpg: User:Taka-0905 derivative work: Alvaro qc (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marquesas Islands
tokens.description: The Marquesas Islands are a group of volcanic islands in French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of France in the southern Pacific Ocean. Their highest point is Mount Oave on Ua Pou, at 1,230 metres. The islands are a UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Taveuni
tokens.description: Taveuni is the third-largest island in Fiji, after Viti Levu and Vanua Levu. It is a massive shield volcano located 6.5 km east of Vanua Levu, across the Somosomo Strait.

tokens.name: Sigatoka Sand Dunes
tokens.description: Sigatoka Sand Dunes is a national park at the mouth of the Sigatoka River on Viti Levu in Fiji. The dunes lie about 3 km west of the town of Sigatoka.

tokens.name: Ambrym
tokens.description: Ambrym is a volcanic island in Malampa Province in the archipelago of Vanuatu. It hosts one of the most active volcanoes in the world, with lava lakes in two craters near the summit.
tokens.image_credit: Geophile71 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sepik
tokens.description: The Sepik is the longest river on the island of New Guinea and the third largest in Oceania by discharge volume, after the Fly and Mamberamo. Most of its course flows through Papua New Guinea.

tokens.name: Kuk Swamp
tokens.description: Kuk Swamp is an archaeological site in the Wahgi Valley of the Papua New Guinea highlands, near Mount Hagen. Early agricultural drainage systems found here date back about 9,000 years, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: Marovo Lagoon
tokens.description: Marovo Lagoon is the largest double-barrier enclosed lagoon in the world. It lies between Vangunu and Nggatokae islands in the New Georgia Islands, Western Province, Solomon Islands.

tokens.name: Guadalcanal
tokens.description: Guadalcanal is the principal island of Guadalcanal Province in the Solomon Islands. It is the largest island in the country by both area and population.
tokens.image_credit: StewyOz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haʻapai
tokens.description: Haʻapai is a group of islands, islets, reefs and shoals in the central part of Tonga. Its administrative centre is Pangai on Lifuka island.
tokens.image_credit: David Broad · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Banaba
tokens.description: Banaba is an island of Kiribati in the Pacific Ocean, a solitary raised coral island west of the Gilbert Island Chain. Its highest point, 81 metres, is also the highest point in Kiribati.

tokens.name: Phoenix Islands Protected Area
tokens.description: The Phoenix Islands Protected Area is a marine protected area in Kiribati covering 408,250 square kilometres. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2010.

tokens.name: Kiritimati
tokens.description: Kiritimati, also known as Christmas Island, is a Pacific Ocean atoll in the northern Line Islands. It is part of the Republic of Kiribati.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palmyra Atoll
tokens.description: Palmyra Atoll is a small, low-lying, uninhabited atoll in the central Pacific Ocean. It is a territory of the United States.

tokens.name: Midway Atoll
tokens.description: Midway Atoll is a 6.2 square kilometre atoll in the North Pacific Ocean, made up of three islands. It is an unorganized and unincorporated territory of the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown authorUnknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument
tokens.description: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument is a United States national monument of ocean waters and ten islands and atolls of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands. It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Henderson Island
tokens.description: Henderson Island is an uninhabited island in the south Pacific Ocean, part of the Pitcairn Island Group. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: European Space Agency · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
tokens.title: Onion domes on Red Square
tokens.description: Saint Basil's Cathedral, officially the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Most Holy Theotokos on the Moat, is a Russian Orthodox church on Red Square in Moscow. It is one of the most popular cultural symbols of Russia.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moscow Kremlin
tokens.title: Fortress at Russia's heart
tokens.description: The Moscow Kremlin is a fortified complex in Moscow, Russia, and one of the country's most recognizable landmarks. It comprises five palaces, four cathedrals, and an enclosing wall along with numerous towers.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lenin's Mausoleum
tokens.description: Lenin's Mausoleum is a mausoleum on Red Square in Moscow, Russia, and the resting place of Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin. His preserved body has been on public display since shortly after his death in 1924, with rare exceptions in wartime.
tokens.image_credit: Staron · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour
tokens.description: The Cathedral of Christ the Saviour is a Russian Orthodox cathedral on the northern bank of the Moskva River in Moscow, a few hundred metres southwest of the Kremlin. At 103 metres it is the third tallest Orthodox church building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Alvesgaspar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bolshoi Theatre
tokens.description: The Bolshoi Theatre is a historic opera house in Moscow, Russia, originally designed by architect Joseph Bové. Before the October Revolution it was part of the Imperial Theatres of the Russian Empire.
tokens.image_credit: DmitriyGuryanov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Novodevichy Convent
tokens.description: Novodevichy Convent is probably the best-known cloister in Moscow, Russia. It was founded by Grand Duke Vasily III in 1524 and is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Ivtorov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moscow State University
tokens.description: Moscow State University, officially M. V. Lomonosov Moscow State University, is a public research university in Moscow, Russia. It includes 15 research institutes, 43 faculties and more than 300 departments.
tokens.image_credit: I.s.kopytov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tretyakov Gallery
tokens.description: The State Tretyakov Gallery is an art gallery in Moscow, Russia, considered the foremost depository of Russian fine art in the world. Pavel Tretyakov presented his collection to the Russian nation in 1892.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kolomenskoye
tokens.description: Kolomenskoye is a former royal estate on the steep banks of the Moskva River, southeast of central Moscow, Russia. Its Church of the Ascension is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1994.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Winter Palace
tokens.description: The Winter Palace is a palace in Saint Petersburg, Russia, that served as the official residence of the House of Romanov from 1732 to 1917. It now houses the Hermitage Museum and is part of the UNESCO Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peterhof Palace
tokens.description: Peterhof Palace is a series of palaces and gardens in Petergof, Saint Petersburg, commissioned by Peter the Great as a response to the Palace of Versailles. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Ninara from Helsinki, Finland · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Catherine Palace
tokens.title: Amber Room palace
tokens.description: The Catherine Palace is a Rococo palace in Tsarskoye Selo (Pushkin), south of Saint Petersburg, that was the summer residence of the Russian tsars. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Church of the Savior on Blood
tokens.description: The Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood is a Russian Orthodox church in Saint Petersburg, built between 1883 and 1907. It functions as both a church and a secular museum, and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Je-str · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint Isaac's Cathedral
tokens.description: Saint Isaac's Cathedral is a large cathedral in Saint Petersburg, dedicated to Saint Isaac of Dalmatia. It has been a museum since 1931, with church services since the 1990s. It is a component of the UNESCO Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg property.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peter and Paul Fortress
tokens.description: The Peter and Paul Fortress is the original citadel of Saint Petersburg, founded by Peter the Great in 1703. It served as a political prison until the early 1920s and has been a museum since 1924. It is a component of the UNESCO Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg property.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kazan Cathedral, Saint Petersburg
tokens.description: Kazan Cathedral is a Russian Orthodox cathedral on Nevsky Prospekt in Saint Petersburg, dedicated to Our Lady of Kazan. It is a component of the UNESCO World Heritage property Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Reshinna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mariinsky Theatre
tokens.description: The Mariinsky Theatre is a historic opera house in Saint Petersburg, opened in 1860. Many stage works by Tchaikovsky, Mussorgsky and Rimsky-Korsakov premiered there, and it was known as the Kirov Theatre through most of the Soviet era.
tokens.image_credit: Ninaras · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bronze Horseman
tokens.description: The Bronze Horseman is an equestrian statue of Peter the Great in Senate Square, Saint Petersburg, Russia. Commissioned by Catherine the Great, it was opened in 1782 and created by the French sculptor Etienne Maurice Falconet.
tokens.image_credit: Godot13 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pavlovsk Palace
tokens.description: Pavlovsk Palace is an 18th-century Russian Imperial residence built by order of Catherine the Great for her son Grand Duke Paul, in Pavlovsk within Saint Petersburg. The palace and its English garden are now a Russian state museum and public park.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kizhi Pogost
tokens.title: Wooden churches of Kizhi
tokens.description: Kizhi Pogost is a historical site dating from the 17th century on Kizhi island in Lake Onega, Republic of Karelia, Russia. It holds two large wooden churches, the 22-dome Transfiguration Church and the 9-dome Intercession Church, and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Laban66 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valaam Monastery
tokens.description: Valaam Monastery is a stauropegic Orthodox monastery on Valaam, the largest island in Lake Ladoga in Russian Karelia. Lake Ladoga is the largest lake in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Пресс-служба Президента Российской Федерации · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Solovetsky Monastery
tokens.description: The Solovetsky Monastery is a fortified monastery on the Solovetsky Islands in the White Sea, northern Russia. It was converted into a Soviet prison camp in 1926, and it is part of the UNESCO-listed Cultural and Historic Ensemble of the Solovetsky Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Алексей Задонский · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Novgorod Detinets
tokens.description: Novgorod Detinets, also called the Novgorod Kremlin, is a fortified complex in Veliky Novgorod, Russia, on the left bank of the Volkhov River. It is a component of the UNESCO-listed Historic Monuments of Novgorod and Surroundings.
tokens.image_credit: EkaterinaKhomichenko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius
tokens.description: The Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius is the most important Russian Orthodox monastery and the spiritual centre of the Russian Orthodox Church. It stands in the town of Sergiyev Posad, about 70 km northeast of Moscow, and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Sergey Ashmarin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Suzdal
tokens.description: Suzdal is a town in Vladimir Oblast, Russia, on the Kamenka river, 26 km north of the city of Vladimir. Its medieval churches, monasteries and Kremlin are part of the UNESCO-listed White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal.
tokens.image_credit: Ludvig14 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kul Sharif Mosque
tokens.description: The Kul Sharif Mosque is a mosque inside the Kazan Kremlin in Kazan, Russia. At the time of its construction it was reputed to be one of the largest mosques in Russia and in Europe outside Istanbul.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rostov Kremlin
tokens.description: The Rostov Kremlin is an architectural ensemble of four complexes built in the 16th and 17th centuries in Rostov, Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia. It was the residence of the Metropolitans of the Rostov diocese.
tokens.image_credit: G.-U. Tolkiehn · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sochi Olympic Park
tokens.description: Sochi Olympic Park is an Olympic Park in Sochi, Russia, on the Black Sea coast in the Imeretinsky Valley. It houses the main Olympic Stadium, used for the Games' ceremonies, and venues for indoor sports such as hockey, figure skating, curling and speed skating.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Olkhon Island
tokens.description: Olkhon is by far the largest island in Lake Baikal in eastern Siberia, Russia. With an area of 730 square kilometres it is the fourth-largest lake island in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valley of Geysers
tokens.description: The Valley of Geysers is a geyser field on the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East. It has approximately ninety geysers and many hot springs, and the second-largest concentration of geysers in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Malupasic · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Klyuchevskaya Sopka
tokens.title: Highest active volcano in Eurasia
tokens.description: Klyuchevskaya Sopka is an active stratovolcano, the highest mountain of Siberia and the highest active volcano of Eurasia. It is part of the Volcanoes of Kamchatka UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Tamten at cs.wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kronotsky Nature Reserve
tokens.description: The Kronotsky Nature Reserve is a Russian zapovednik on the coast of the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East, created in 1934. It covers 10,990 square kilometres and contains Lake Kronotskoye, the largest lake in the reserve.

tokens.name: Koryaksky
tokens.description: Koryaksky is an active volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East, within sight of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky. It is considered a Decade Volcano, worthy of particular study because of its explosive eruptions and its proximity to populated areas.
tokens.image_credit: kuhnmi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Avachinsky
tokens.description: Avachinsky is an active stratovolcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East. It lies within sight of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, the capital of Kamchatka Krai.
tokens.image_credit: kuhnmi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lena River
tokens.description: The Lena is a river in the Russian Far East and the easternmost of the three great rivers of Siberia flowing into the Arctic Ocean. At 4,294 km long, it is the longest river entirely within Russia.
tokens.image_credit: Geographyinitiative · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Putorana Plateau
tokens.description: The Putorana Plateau, also called the Putorana Mountains, is a large mountainous massif in Russia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the nearest large settlement is Norilsk.
tokens.image_credit: jxandreani · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wrangel Island
tokens.description: Wrangel Island is an island of the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug in the Arctic Ocean, the 92nd-largest island in the world. It lies astride the 180th meridian.

tokens.name: Franz Josef Land
tokens.description: Franz Josef Land is a Russian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean, made up of 192 islands. It has never had a permanent population and is inhabited only by military personnel.
tokens.image_credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center from Greenbelt, MD, USA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Severnaya Zemlya
tokens.description: Severnaya Zemlya is a 37,000 km2 archipelago in the Russian high Arctic. It lies off Siberia's Taymyr Peninsula, separated from the mainland by the Vilkitsky Strait.

tokens.name: Belukha Mountain
tokens.description: Belukha Mountain, also called Üç-Sümer, is the highest mountain of the Altai Mountains and of the South Siberian Mountains system. It is part of the Golden Mountains of Altai UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Vitecek~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ural Mountains
tokens.description: The Ural Mountains are a mountain range running north to south mostly through Russia, from the Arctic Ocean to northwestern Kazakhstan. The range forms part of the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.

tokens.name: Manpupuner rock formations
tokens.description: The Manpupuner rock formations are a set of seven stone pillars in the Komi Republic, west of the Ural Mountains. They stand in the Pechoro-Ilychski Reserve on the mountain Man-Pupu-nyor.
tokens.image_credit: Kasimys · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Volga
tokens.description: The Volga is the longest river in Europe and the longest endorheic basin river in the world. It flows through Russia into the Caspian Sea.

tokens.name: Don River
tokens.description: The Don is the fifth-longest river in Europe. It flows from Central Russia to the Sea of Azov in southern Russia.

tokens.name: Yenisei
tokens.description: The Yenisei is the fifth-longest river system in the world and the largest to drain into the Arctic Ocean. It flows north from Mongolia through Krasnoyarsk Krai into the Kara Sea.

tokens.name: Ob
tokens.description: The Ob is a major river in western Siberia, Russia. With its tributary the Irtysh it forms the world's seventh-longest river system, at 5,410 km.

tokens.name: Amur
tokens.description: The Amur is a river in Northeast Asia that forms the border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China. Including its tributary the Argun, it is the world's tenth-longest river.

tokens.name: Oymyakon
tokens.title: Coldest inhabited place
tokens.description: Oymyakon is a rural locality in the Sakha Republic, Russia, on the Indigirka River. It is the coldest permanently inhabited human settlement on Earth.

tokens.name: Mamayev Kurgan
tokens.description: Mamayev Kurgan is a hill and memorial complex overlooking the city of Volgograd (formerly Stalingrad) in Southern Russia. The hill is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (July 1942 to February 1943).
tokens.image_credit: Mike1979 Russia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Motherland Calls
tokens.description: The Motherland Calls is a colossal war memorial sculpture on Mamayev Kurgan in Volgograd, Russia. It commemorates the casualties of the Battle of Stalingrad and stands 85 metres (279 ft) tall from the base of its pedestal to its peak.
tokens.image_credit: VladFedotov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brest Fortress
tokens.description: Brest Fortress is a 19th-century fortress in Brest, Belarus. In 1965 it was given the title Hero Fortress to commemorate the defence of the frontier stronghold during the first week of Operation Barbarossa in June 1941.

tokens.name: Mir Castle Complex
tokens.description: The Mir Castle Complex is a historic fortified castle in the town of Mir, Belarus. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karelichy District of Grodno Oblast.
tokens.image_credit: Sergey Sebelev · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nesvizh Castle
tokens.description: Nesvizh Castle is a residential castle of the Radziwiłł family in Nyasvizh (Nesvizh), Belarus. The castle, church and surroundings form part of the Radziwill family complex inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Alena by · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park
tokens.description: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park lies within the Brest and Grodno regions of Belarus, on the Polish border. Since 1992 it has been a preserved part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Białowieża Forest, the last primeval forest fragment of the European woodlands.

tokens.name: Khortytsia
tokens.description: Khortytsia is the largest island on the Dnieper River, about 12.5 km long and up to 2.5 km wide. It forms part of the Khortytsia National Reserve within the city limits of Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine.
tokens.image_credit: Alexey Tolmachov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral, Kyiv
tokens.description: The Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv, Ukraine, is an architectural monument of Kyivan Rus' and one of the city's best known landmarks. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List together with the Kyiv Cave Monastery complex.
tokens.image_credit: Rbrechko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
tokens.description: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra is a historic lavra, a large monastery of Eastern Christianity, in the Pechersk district of Kyiv. Founded as a cave monastery in the 11th century, it was an early centre of printing in Ukraine.
tokens.image_credit: Роман Наумов · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Michael's Golden-Domed Monastery
tokens.description: St. Michael's Golden-Domed Monastery is a monastery in Kyiv, Ukraine, dedicated to Saint Michael the Archangel. It stands on an elevated hill above the Dnipro river, northeast of Saint Sophia Cathedral.
tokens.image_credit: Rbrechko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St Andrew's Church, Kyiv
tokens.description: St Andrew's Church is a historic Orthodox church in Kyiv, Ukraine. It was built between 1747 and 1754 to a design by the Italian architect Bartolomeo Rastrelli, and is a rare example of Ukrainian Baroque.
tokens.image_credit: Imadanat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Gate, Kyiv
tokens.description: The Golden Gate of Kyiv was the main gate of the 11th-century fortifications of Kyiv, capital of Kievan Rus'. It was dismantled in the Middle Ages, leaving few vestiges of its existence.
tokens.image_credit: George Chernilevsky · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maidan Nezalezhnosti
tokens.description: Maidan Nezalezhnosti, translated as Independence Square, is the central town square of Kyiv, Ukraine. It is located on Khreshchatyk Street and contains the iconic Independence Monument.
tokens.image_credit: Juan Antonio Segal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet
tokens.description: The Lviv Theatre of Opera and Ballet is an opera house in Lviv, Ukraine, designed by the Polish architect Zygmunt Gorgolewski and built between 1897 and 1900. It stands on Freedom Avenue in the historic centre of Lviv, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Oleksandr Samoylyk · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lychakiv Cemetery
tokens.description: Lychakiv Cemetery is a historic cemetery in Lviv, Ukraine. It is officially titled the State History and Culture Museum-Reserve Lychakiv Cemetery.

tokens.name: Khotyn Fortress
tokens.description: The Khotyn Fortress is a fortification complex on the right bank of the Dniester River in Khotyn, Chernivtsi Oblast, southwestern Ukraine. It lies near the Kamianets-Podilskyi Castle.
tokens.image_credit: Rbrechko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kamianets-Podilskyi Castle
tokens.description: The Kamianets-Podilskyi Castle is a former Ruthenian-Lithuanian castle and later Polish fortress in the historic city of Kamianets-Podilskyi, Ukraine. Historical accounts date it to the early 14th century.
tokens.image_credit: Grzegorz Gołębiowski · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carpathian Mountains
tokens.description: The Carpathian Mountains form an arc of about 1,500 km across Central and Southeast Europe. Their highest peaks are in the Tatra Mountains, exceeding 2,600 m.

tokens.name: Hoverla
tokens.description: Hoverla is the highest mountain in Ukraine, at 2,061 metres, and part of the Ukrainian Carpathians. It lies in the Chornohora region of the Eastern Beskids.
tokens.image_credit: Olexdj · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dnieper
tokens.description: The Dnieper is one of the major transboundary rivers of Europe, about 2,200 km long, flowing from Russia through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea. It is the longest river of Ukraine and Belarus.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry A. Mottl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Danube Delta
tokens.description: The Danube Delta is the second largest river delta in Europe and the best preserved on the continent. Most of it lies in Romania's Tulcea County, with a small part in Ukraine's Odesa Oblast.

tokens.name: Chernobyl exclusion zone
tokens.description: The Chernobyl exclusion zone was established after the 1986 Chernobyl disaster in the Ukrainian SSR. Its original 30 km radius has since been enlarged, and it adjoins a radioecological reserve in Belarus.
tokens.image_credit: Jesse Allen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pripyat
tokens.description: Pripyat is an abandoned industrial city in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, near the border with Belarus. It was founded on 4 February 1970 for workers at the nearby Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant.
tokens.image_credit: Omar David Sandoval Sida · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Swallow's Nest
tokens.description: Swallow's Nest is a decorative neo-Gothic castle built in 1911 to 1912 on the Aurora Cliff at Gaspra, on the Crimean Black Sea coast. It overlooks the Cape of Ai-Todor between Yalta and Alupka.
tokens.image_credit: Novoklimov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vorontsov Palace
tokens.description: The Vorontsov Palace, also called the Alupka Palace, is a historic palace at the foot of the Crimean Mountains near Alupka. It was built between 1828 and 1848 for Prince Mikhail Vorontsov as his summer residence.
tokens.image_credit: Flamel123 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chersonesus
tokens.description: Chersonesus was an ancient Greek colony founded about 2,500 years ago on the southwestern Crimean coast, on the outskirts of present-day Sevastopol. The site is part of the Tauric Chersonesos National Preserve and a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry A. Mottl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soroca Fort
tokens.description: Soroca Fort is a historic fortress in the city of Soroca in northern Moldova. It was established by Prince Stephen the Great of Moldavia in 1499 and is known for its well-preserved stronghold.
tokens.image_credit: Photobank MD from Chisinau, Moldova · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old Orhei
tokens.description: Old Orhei, known in Romanian as Orheiul Vechi, is a historical and archaeological complex in Trebujeni on the Răut River. It lies about 60 km north-east of Chișinău in the Republic of Moldova.
tokens.image_credit: Julian Nyča · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Sofia
tokens.description: Saint Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is a Bulgarian Orthodox cathedral in Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria. It is built in the Neo-Byzantine style, serves as the cathedral of the Patriarch of Bulgaria, and is one of the largest Christian church buildings by volume in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Plamen Agov (user:MrPanyGoff) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boyana Church
tokens.description: Boyana Church is a medieval Bulgarian Orthodox church on the outskirts of Sofia, in the Boyana quarter. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Todor Bozhinov / Тодор Божинов · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rila
tokens.description: Rila is the highest mountain range in Bulgaria and the Balkan Peninsula. Its highest summit is Musala, at 2,925 m, and the range lies in southwestern Bulgaria as part of the Rila-Rhodope Massif.

tokens.name: Musala
tokens.description: Musala is the highest peak in the Rila Mountains, in Bulgaria and on the Balkan Peninsula, at 2,925 metres. It has a topographic prominence of 2,473 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Deyan Vasilev ( Dido3 ) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pirin National Park
tokens.description: Pirin National Park covers most of the Pirin Mountains in southwestern Bulgaria, over 403 square kilometres. It was established in 1962 and is a UNESCO World Heritage natural site since 1983.

tokens.name: Madara Rider
tokens.description: The Madara Rider is a large early medieval rock relief carved on the Madara Plateau near Shumen in northeastern Bulgaria. It is dated to the late 7th or early 8th century and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Dom2002 assumed (based on copyright claims). · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nesebar
tokens.description: Nesebar is an ancient city and seaside resort on the Bulgarian Black Sea coast, in Burgas Province. Its old town, with churches from several eras, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Chrumps · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belogradchik Rocks
tokens.description: The Belogradchik Rocks are sandstone and conglomerate rock formations on the western slopes of the Balkan Mountains, near the town of Belogradchik in northwest Bulgaria. Some rise up to 200 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Fonvan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seven Rila Lakes
tokens.description: The Seven Rila Lakes are a group of glacial tarns in the northwestern part of the Rila Mountains in Bulgaria, at 2,100 to 2,500 metres. They are the most visited group of lakes in Bulgaria.
tokens.image_credit: Aski at en.wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsarevets
tokens.description: Tsarevets is a medieval stronghold on a hill in Veliko Tarnovo, northern Bulgaria. It was the primary fortress of the Second Bulgarian Empire from 1185 to 1393, housing the royal and patriarchal palaces.
tokens.image_credit: RKold · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak
tokens.description: The Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak is a vaulted brick tholos tomb near Kazanlak in central Bulgaria. It is part of a large royal Thracian necropolis and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Roweromaniak · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace of the Parliament
tokens.title: Heaviest building on Earth
tokens.description: The Palace of the Parliament is the seat of the Parliament of Romania, on Dealul Spirii in Bucharest. It is the heaviest building in the world and the largest civilian administrative building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo · CC-BY-2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bran Castle
tokens.title: Dracula's castle
tokens.description: Bran Castle is a castle in Bran, about 25 km southwest of Brasov in Transylvania, Romania. It was built by Saxons in 1377 and is a national monument and landmark.
tokens.image_credit: Todor Bozhinov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Corvin Castle
tokens.description: Corvin Castle, also known as Hunyadi Castle, is a Gothic-Renaissance castle in Hunedoara, Romania. It is considered one of the largest castles in Europe and one of the Seven Wonders of Romania.
tokens.image_credit: Carcea Daniel · CC BY-SA 3.0 ro · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sighișoara
tokens.description: Sighișoara is a city on the Târnava Mare River in Mureș County, central Romania. Its well-preserved old town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.
tokens.image_credit: Bogdan Muraru · CC BY-SA 3.0 ro · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Churches of Moldavia
tokens.description: Eight Romanian Orthodox churches in Suceava County, built from the late 15th to the late 16th century, form a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993. The painted churches of northern Moldavia are known for their exterior frescoes.
tokens.image_credit: Cosmin Cornea from Timisoara, Romania · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Merry Cemetery
tokens.description: The Merry Cemetery is a cemetery in the village of Săpânța, Maramureș County, Romania. It is known for its brightly coloured tombstones with naive paintings and has become an open-air museum and a national tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bucegi Mountains
tokens.description: The Bucegi Mountains are a range of the Southern Carpathians in central Romania, south of Brasov. Omu, at 2,505 m, is their highest point.

tokens.name: Făgăraș Mountains
tokens.description: The Făgăraș Mountains are the highest mountains of the Southern Carpathians, in Romania. The range forms the highest section of the Transylvanian Alps in south-central Romania.

tokens.name: Retezat National Park
tokens.description: Retezat National Park is a protected area in the Retezat Mountains in Hunedoara County, Romania. Founded in 1935, it is the oldest national park in the country.

tokens.name: Scărișoara Cave
tokens.description: Scărișoara Cave is one of the biggest ice caves in the Apuseni Mountains of Romania. It is considered a show cave and one of the natural wonders of Romania.

tokens.name: Salina Turda
tokens.description: Salina Turda is a salt mine in the Durgău-Valea Sărată area of Turda, Cluj County, Romania. Opened for tourists in 1992, it was visited by about 618,000 tourists in 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Rkoster · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iron Gates
tokens.description: The Iron Gates is a gorge on the Danube that forms part of the boundary between Romania and Serbia. It holds two hydroelectric dams with power stations, Iron Gate I and Iron Gate II.

tokens.name: Sarmizegetusa Regia
tokens.description: Sarmizegetusa Regia was the capital and main military and religious centre of the Dacians before the wars with Rome. The site lies in Grădiștea de Munte, Hunedoara County, Romania, and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: FDominec · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Krka National Park
tokens.description: Krka National Park is one of the Croatian national parks, named after the Krka River that it encloses. It lies in central Dalmatia, just northeast of the city of Šibenik, in Šibenik-Knin county.
tokens.image_credit: Rkoster · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Diocletian's Palace
tokens.description: Diocletian's Palace is an ancient Roman palace and fortress complex in Split, Croatia. It was built at the end of the third century AD by the Roman Emperor Diocletian as his retirement residence.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pula Arena
tokens.description: The Pula Arena is a Roman amphitheatre in Pula, Istria, Croatia, built between 27 BC and AD 14 and later expanded under Vespasian. It is one of the best-preserved Roman amphitheatres in the world and once held up to 23,000 spectators.
tokens.image_credit: Olgierd Rudak · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Euphrasian Basilica
tokens.description: The Euphrasian Basilica is a Roman Catholic basilica in Poreč, Istria, Croatia, and an excellent example of early Byzantine architecture in the Mediterranean region. The episcopal complex is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trogir
tokens.description: Trogir is a historic town and harbour on an island off the Adriatic coast of Croatia, 27 km west of Split. The Historic City of Trogir has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997.
tokens.image_credit: VitVit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Šibenik Cathedral
tokens.description: The Cathedral of St. James in Šibenik, Croatia, is a triple-nave Catholic cathedral with three apses and a dome. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Berthold Werner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kornati
tokens.description: The Kornati is an archipelago of 89 islands in the Adriatic Sea, south of Zadar and west of Šibenik on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia. It is described as the densest archipelago in the Mediterranean Sea.

tokens.name: Mljet National Park
tokens.description: Mljet National Park covers the western part of the Adriatic island of Mljet in southern Croatia. Its central features are the lakes Veliko jezero and Malo jezero.
tokens.image_credit: Patrick Rouzet · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hvar
tokens.description: Hvar is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea off the Dalmatian coast, between the islands of Brač, Vis and Korčula. It is about 68 km long and has a high limestone ridge and a large fertile coastal plain.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paklenica
tokens.description: Paklenica is a karst river canyon national park in Croatia, near Starigrad on the southern slopes of the Velebit mountain. It contains the Mala (Small) and Velika (Big) Paklenica canyons.
tokens.image_credit: optimatyi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brijuni
tokens.description: Brijuni is a group of fourteen small islands in the Croatian part of the northern Adriatic Sea, off the west coast of the Istrian peninsula. The largest island, Veli Brijun, lies about 2 kilometres from the coast.

tokens.name: Zlatni Rat
tokens.description: Zlatni Rat, the Golden Cape, is a pebble spit about 2 km west of the harbour town of Bol on the southern coast of Brac island, Croatia. It extends into the Hvar Channel, which is known for strong currents.
tokens.image_credit: Szabolcs Emich (cropped by DIREKTOR) · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Predjama Castle
tokens.title: Castle built into a cliff
tokens.description: Predjama Castle is a Renaissance castle built within a cave mouth in south-central Slovenia, in the village of Predjama. It lies about 11 kilometres from the town of Postojna.
tokens.image_credit: Lettkemann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Triglav
tokens.description: Triglav is the highest mountain in Slovenia, at 2,863.65 metres, and the highest peak of the Julian Alps. It appears on the coat of arms and flag of Slovenia and is the centrepiece of Triglav National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Andrej Jakobčič · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vintgar Gorge
tokens.description: Vintgar Gorge is a 1.6 km gorge carved by the Radovna River in northwestern Slovenia, about four kilometres northwest of Bled. It lies on the edge of Triglav National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Zairon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Bohinj
tokens.description: Lake Bohinj, covering 318 hectares, is the largest permanent lake in Slovenia. It lies in the Bohinj Valley of the Julian Alps and is part of Triglav National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Stephen Turner · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ljubljana Castle
tokens.description: Ljubljana Castle is a castle complex on Castle Hill above downtown Ljubljana, the capital of Slovenia. Originally a medieval fortress, it was probably built in the 11th century and rebuilt in the 12th century.
tokens.image_credit: LjGrad · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Savica Waterfall
tokens.description: Savica Waterfall is a 78 metre high waterfall in Triglav National Park, Slovenia. Its stream flows into Lake Bohinj.

tokens.name: Kravica Waterfall
tokens.description: Kravica Waterfall is a large tufa cascade on the Trebizat River in Herzegovina, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its height is about 25 metres, and it lies about 40 km south of Mostar.
tokens.image_credit: Matěj Baťha · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Latin Bridge
tokens.description: Latin Bridge is an Ottoman-era bridge over the Miljacka river in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its northern end is where Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914.
tokens.image_credit: sundeviljeff · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Una National Park
tokens.description: Una National Park was established in 2008 around the Una, Krka and Unac rivers in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is the largest national park in the country.

tokens.name: Sutjeska National Park
tokens.description: Sutjeska National Park was established in 1962 and is Bosnia and Herzegovina's oldest national park. It includes the country's highest peak, Maglic, on the border with Montenegro.

tokens.name: Bosnian pyramid claims
tokens.description: The Bosnian pyramid claims are pseudoarchaeological theories that natural hills near Visoko are ancient man-made pyramids. Scientists have overwhelmingly refuted them, but the area is promoted as a tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: TheBIHLover · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vjetrenica Cave
tokens.description: Vjetrenica Cave is the largest cave in Bosnia and Herzegovina and is known for its exceptional biodiversity. It lies in the Popovo field near Ravno and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.
tokens.image_credit: InDoRoN · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
tokens.description: The Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque is a Sunni mosque built in the 16th century in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is the largest historical mosque in the country and one of the most representative Ottoman structures in the Balkans.
tokens.image_credit: Bjoertvedt · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Skadar
tokens.description: Lake Skadar, also called Lake Scutari or Lake Shkodra, lies on the Albania and Montenegro border. It is the largest lake in Southern Europe and a karst lake.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor
tokens.description: The Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Montenegro, inscribed in 1979. It covers the old town of Kotor, its fortifications and the surrounding inner Bay of Kotor.
tokens.image_credit: Clay Gilliland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Durmitor National Park
tokens.description: Durmitor National Park in northwestern Montenegro is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1980. It centres on the Durmitor massif of the Dinaric Alps, whose highest peak, Bobotov Kuk, reaches 2,523 metres.

tokens.name: Tara River Canyon
tokens.description: The Tara River Canyon, also called the Tara River Gorge, is the canyon of the Tara river, mostly in Montenegro and partly in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its high rocks lie within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Durmitor National Park.

tokens.name: Ostrog Monastery
tokens.description: Ostrog Monastery is a Serbian Orthodox monastery near Danilovgrad, Montenegro, built high in the rock of Ostroška Greda. It is dedicated to Saint Basil of Ostrog and is the most visited pilgrimage site within the Serbian Orthodox Church.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sveti Stefan
tokens.description: Sveti Stefan is a town on the Adriatic coast of Montenegro, about 6 km southeast of Budva. It stands on a small islet now joined to the mainland by a narrow tombolo, and is known for the Aman Sveti Stefan resort.
tokens.image_credit: Marcin Konsek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Biogradska Gora
tokens.description: Biogradska Gora is a forest and national park in Montenegro, within Kolašin Municipality. It is recognised as part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

tokens.name: Lovćen
tokens.description: Lovćen is a mountain and national park in southwestern Montenegro. Its name gave rise to the names Montenegro and Crna Gora, both meaning Black Mountain.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · GPL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parthenon
tokens.description: The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis, dedicated to the goddess Athena and built in the 5th century BC. It is part of the UNESCO-listed Acropolis of Athens.
tokens.image_credit: Steve Swayne · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Erechtheion
tokens.description: The Erechtheion is an ancient Greek Ionic temple on the north side of the Acropolis in Athens. It was primarily dedicated to the goddess Athena.
tokens.image_credit: Jebulon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus, Athens
tokens.description: The Temple of Olympian Zeus is a colossal temple in the centre of Athens, now in ruins. Construction began in the 6th century BC and was completed under Roman Emperor Hadrian in the 2nd century AD.
tokens.image_credit: Ava Βabili · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ancient Agora of Athens
tokens.description: The Ancient Agora of Athens is an ancient Greek agora located northwest of the Acropolis. Its initial use was as a commercial, assembly or residential gathering place.
tokens.image_credit: Chabe01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Panathenaic Stadium
tokens.description: The Panathenaic Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Athens, built on a former racecourse around 330 BC. It is the only stadium in the world built entirely of marble.
tokens.image_credit: George E. Koronaios · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Hephaestus
tokens.description: The Temple of Hephaestus is a well-preserved Doric temple on the Agoraios Kolonos hill, at the northwest side of the Agora of Athens. It remains standing largely intact today.
tokens.image_credit: Julian Lupyan · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple of Apollo, Delphi
tokens.description: The Temple of Apollo was a major part of the Panhellenic sanctuary at Delphi, dedicated to the god Apollo. The visible ruins are of the temple built in the 4th century BC, and it was home to the Pythia, the Oracle of Delphi.
tokens.image_credit: Skyring · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tiryns
tokens.description: Tiryns is a Mycenaean archaeological site in Argolis in the Peloponnese, and the location from which the mythical hero Heracles was said to have performed his Twelve Labours. It lies 20 km south of Mycenae.
tokens.image_credit: Nick Stenning · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vergina
tokens.title: Royal tombs of Macedon
tokens.description: Vergina is a small town in Greek Macedonia, part of the Veroia municipality in Imathia. It is the site of ancient Aigai, the first capital of Macedon, where Philip II was assassinated in 336 BC.
tokens.image_credit: Panegyrics of Granovetter (Sarah Murray) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Athos
tokens.title: Monastic republic
tokens.description: Mount Athos is a mountain on the Athos peninsula in northeastern Greece directly on the Aegean Sea. It is an important center of Eastern Orthodox monasticism.

tokens.name: Phaistos
tokens.description: Phaistos is a Bronze Age archaeological site at modern Faistos, a municipality in south central Crete. It is notable for the remains of a Minoan palace and the surrounding town.
