tokens.description: The Faiyum Oasis is a depression in the desert immediately west of the Nile, about 62 miles south of Cairo. Its basin floor is irrigated by the Bahr Yussef, a channel of the Nile.

tokens.name: Monastery of Saint Anthony
tokens.description: The Monastery of Saint Anthony is a Coptic Orthodox monastery in an oasis in the Eastern Desert of Egypt, in the Red Sea Mountains. It was established by followers of Anthony the Great, an early Christian monk.
tokens.image_credit: Tentoila (talk) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hasan
tokens.description: The Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hasan is a monumental mosque and madrasa in Salah al-Din Square in historic Cairo, Egypt. It was built between 1356 and 1363 during the Bahri Mamluk period.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Citadel of Qaitbay
tokens.title: Built on the Pharos ruins
tokens.description: The Citadel of Qaitbay is a 15th-century defensive fortress on Pharos Island at the mouth of the port of Alexandria, Egypt. It was built from 1477 to 1479 by Sultan al-Ashraf Sayf al-Din Qaitbay.
tokens.image_credit: Hmkree · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pompey's Pillar
tokens.description: Pompey's Pillar is a Roman triumphal column in Alexandria, Egypt, set up in honour of the emperor Diocletian between 298 and 302 AD. Its name is modern, and it stands beside the ruins of the Serapeum.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Unger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amarna
tokens.title: Akhenaten's capital
tokens.description: Amarna is an ancient Egyptian archaeological site containing the ruins of Akhetaten, the capital city of the late Eighteenth Dynasty. The city was built at the direction of Akhenaten in 1346 BC and abandoned shortly after his death.
tokens.image_credit: en:User:Markh · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ras Muhammad National Park
tokens.description: Ras Muhammad is a national park in Egypt at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, overlooking the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba. The park is becoming a centre of eco-tourism in the region.

tokens.name: Qal'at Bani Hammad
tokens.description: Qal'at Bani Hammad is a fortified palatine city in the Hodna Mountains of Algeria, now in ruins. In the 11th century it was the first capital of the Hammadid dynasty, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: R hakka · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Erg Oriental
tokens.description: The Grand Erg Oriental is a large sand sea in the Sahara Desert, covering about 185,000 square kilometres. It lies mostly in the Saharan lowlands of northeast Algeria.

tokens.name: Bulla Regia
tokens.description: Bulla Regia was a Berber, Punic and Roman town near Jendouba, Tunisia. Its ruins are noted for Hadrianic-era semi-subterranean houses built against the heat, and many of its mosaic floors remain in place.
tokens.image_credit: Meryem ATHIMNI · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sbeitla
tokens.description: Sbeitla is a town in west-central Tunisia. Next to it lie the ruins of Sufetula, whose three Capitoline temples are among the best-preserved Roman forum temples in North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Al-Zaytuna Mosque
tokens.description: Al-Zaytuna Mosque is a major mosque at the centre of the historic medina of Tunis, Tunisia. It is the oldest mosque in the city, founded at the end of the 7th century or in the early 8th century.
tokens.image_credit: T A · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ksar Ouled Soltane
tokens.description: Ksar Ouled Soltane is a fortified granary complex in the Tataouine district of southern Tunisia. Built by Berber communities on a hilltop, its two courtyards are lined with multi-story vaulted granary cellars called ghorfas.

tokens.name: Kasbah of the Udayas
tokens.description: The Kasbah of the Udayas is a kasbah, or citadel, in Rabat, Morocco. It stands on a hill at the mouth of the Bou Regreg opposite Salé and is listed as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Rabat.
tokens.image_credit: Davide Cesare Veniani · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bou Inania Madrasa
tokens.description: The Bou Inania Madrasa is a madrasa in Fez, Morocco, built in 1350 to 1355 by the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris. It is the only madrasa in Morocco that also functioned as a congregational mosque.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
tokens.description: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is an Islamic college in Marrakesh, Morocco, commissioned in 1564 to 1565 by the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib. At its height it was the largest Islamic college in the Maghreb.
tokens.image_credit: Lundeux · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Badi Palace
tokens.description: El Badi Palace is a ruined palace in Marrakesh, Morocco. The Saadian sultan Ahmad al-Mansur commissioned it shortly after his accession in 1578 to showcase the wealth and power of his rule.
tokens.image_credit: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saadian Tombs
tokens.description: The Saadian Tombs are a historic royal necropolis in the Kasbah of Marrakesh, Morocco, from the Saadian dynasty. They are known for their richly decorated interiors, mainly from the reign of Ahmad al-Mansur (1578 to 1603).
tokens.image_credit: C messier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Amera
tokens.title: Giant monolith
tokens.description: Ben Amera is a monolith in Mauritania, near the border with Western Sahara, rising 633 metres above the desert floor. It is Africa's largest monolith and the world's second largest after Uluru in Australia.
tokens.image_credit: Les3corbiers · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oualata
tokens.description: Oualata is a small oasis town in southeast Mauritania, once a caravan city on a trans-Saharan trade route in the 13th and 14th centuries. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata.

tokens.name: Senegambian stone circles
tokens.description: The Senegambian stone circles are megalithic stone circles and tumuli in Gambia and Senegal, described as the largest concentration of stone circles in the world. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Niels Broekzitter https://www.flickr.com/people/nbroekzitter86/ · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Mosque of Touba
tokens.description: The Great Mosque of Touba is a mosque in Touba, Senegal, founded by Ahmadou Bamba in 1887 and completed in 1963. Bamba died in 1927 and was interred inside the mosque.

tokens.name: Saint-Louis, Senegal
tokens.description: Saint-Louis is a city near the mouth of the Senegal River in northwest Senegal, about 320 km north of Dakar, and capital of the Saint-Louis Region. The historic island town is a UNESCO World Heritage site, inscribed in 2000.

tokens.name: Gao
tokens.description: Gao is a city in Mali on the River Niger and the capital of the Gao Region. For much of its history it was an important commercial centre in the trans-Saharan trade.

tokens.name: Fouta Djallon
tokens.description: Fouta Djallon is a highland region in the centre of Guinea, West Africa. It roughly corresponds with Middle Guinea.

tokens.name: Benin Moat
tokens.description: The Benin Moat (Edo: Iyanuwo), also known as the Benin City Iya or the Wall of Benin, is a large earthwork within Benin City in Nigeria's Edo state. Part of it formerly encircled the city at the time of the Benin Empire.

tokens.name: Kalambo Falls
tokens.description: The Kalambo Falls on the Kalambo River is a 235-metre single-drop waterfall on the border of Zambia and Tanzania, at the southeast end of Lake Tanganyika. Downstream lies the Kalambo Gorge, about 1 km wide and up to 300 m deep.

tokens.name: Chongoni Rock Art Area
tokens.description: The Chongoni Rock Art Area holds 127 rock art and painting sites on granite hills of the Malawi plateau in Malawi's Central Region. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006.

tokens.name: Quirimbas Islands
tokens.description: The Quirimbas Islands lie in the Indian Ocean off northeastern Mozambique, close to Pemba. The archipelago consists of about 32 islands, including Ibo, Matemo and Medjumbe.

tokens.name: Chinhoyi Caves
tokens.description: The Chinhoyi Caves, formerly the Sinoia Caves, are a group of limestone and dolomite caves in north central Zimbabwe. The site was designated a National Park in 1955.
tokens.image_credit: Suesen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moremi Game Reserve
tokens.description: Moremi Game Reserve is a protected area on the eastern side of the Okavango Delta in Botswana. It was named after Chief Moremi of the BaTawana tribe and lies within the Okavango Delta World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Waterberg Plateau Park
tokens.description: Waterberg Plateau Park is a national park in central Namibia, on a plateau about 68 km south-east of Otjiwarongo. The park is named after the Waterberg, a prominent table mountain that rises from the plateau.

tokens.name: Epupa Falls
tokens.description: Epupa Falls is a series of large waterfalls formed by the Cunene River on the border of Angola and Namibia, in the Kunene Region. The greatest single drop is 37 metres, and the nearby settlement is also called Epupa.

tokens.name: Dragon's Breath Cave
tokens.title: Vast underground lake
tokens.description: Dragon's Breath Cave is a flooded karst cave in the Otjozondjupa Region of Namibia, on private land and not open to the general public. It was discovered by Roger Ellis during a caving expedition in 1986.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY coords

tokens.name: Hoba meteorite
tokens.title: Largest known meteorite
tokens.description: The Hoba meteorite lies on Hoba West farm near Grootfontein in the Otjozondjupa Region of Namibia, where it fell. It has never been moved, and its main mass is estimated at more than 60 tonnes.
tokens.image_credit: Sergio Conti from Montevecchia (LC), Italia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Duwisib Castle
tokens.description: Duwisib Castle is a pseudo-medieval fortress in the hills of the Southern Namib region of Namibia, about 72 km southwest of Maltahohe. It was built in 1909 as the residence of the German officer Hans Heinrich von Wolf and has been government property since 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Bernhard Dunst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape Cross
tokens.description: Cape Cross is a headland in the South Atlantic on the Skeleton Coast of western Namibia. The cape is also known by its Afrikaans, German and Portuguese names.

tokens.name: Bourke's Luck Potholes
tokens.description: Bourke's Luck Potholes are sculpted potholes in the Blyde River gorge of Mpumalanga, South Africa, where the Treur River tumbles into the Blyde below. They lie in the Blyde River Canyon Nature Reserve on the Drakensberg escarpment.
tokens.image_credit: ErwinMeier · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Park
tokens.description: Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Park is a nature reserve of about 960 square km in central KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. It is the oldest reserve in Africa and the only state-run park in KwaZulu-Natal where all of the big five game animals occur.

tokens.name: Voortrekker Monument
tokens.description: The Voortrekker Monument is a granite monument on a hilltop just south of Pretoria, South Africa. It commemorates the Voortrekkers who left the Cape Colony between 1835 and 1854 and was designed by the architect Gerard Moerdijk.
tokens.image_credit: John Walker, Images of Africa Taken from de-Wikipedia, where it had been uploaded by Head under the same filename. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Richtersveld
tokens.description: Richtersveld is a desert landscape of rugged kloofs and high mountains in the north-western corner of South Africa's Northern Cape province. The Orange River forms its border with Namibia, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Blombos Cave
tokens.title: Early abstract art cave
tokens.description: Blombos Cave is an archaeological site in the Blombos Private Nature Reserve on the Southern Cape coast of South Africa. It holds Middle Stone Age deposits dated to about 100,000 to 70,000 years ago.

tokens.name: Wonderwerk Cave
tokens.description: Wonderwerk Cave is an archaeological site in the Kuruman Hills between Danielskuil and Kuruman in the Northern Cape, South Africa. It is a National Heritage Site managed as a satellite of the McGregor Museum in Kimberley.

tokens.name: Cape Agulhas
tokens.title: Southernmost tip of Africa
tokens.description: Cape Agulhas is a rocky headland in the Western Cape, South Africa. It is the southernmost point of Africa and the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans.

tokens.name: Thaba Bosiu
tokens.description: Thaba Bosiu is a sandstone plateau in the Maseru District of Lesotho, about 24 km east of Maseru. It was the stronghold of King Moshoeshoe I and once the capital of Lesotho.

tokens.name: Mafate
tokens.description: Mafate is a volcanic cirque on Réunion, a caldera formed by the collapse of the Piton des Neiges shield volcano. It is part of the UNESCO site Pitons, cirques and remparts of Réunion Island.

tokens.name: Longwood House
tokens.title: Napoleon's last home
tokens.description: Longwood House is a mansion on the island of Saint Helena, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic. It was the final residence of Napoleon Bonaparte during his exile there, until his death in 1821.
tokens.image_credit: Michel Dancoisne-Martineau · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Diana's Peak
tokens.description: Diana's Peak is the highest point of Saint Helena, at 818 metres, in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is of volcanic origin and lies within the island's first national park, proclaimed in 1996.

tokens.name: Gough Island
tokens.description: Gough Island is a rugged volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean, a dependency of Tristan da Cunha. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Gough and Inaccessible Islands.

tokens.name: Garajonay National Park
tokens.description: Garajonay National Park is a protected laurel forest covering the centre and north of La Gomera in the Canary Islands, Spain. It was declared a national park in 1981 and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

tokens.name: Caldera de Taburiente National Park
tokens.description: Caldera de Taburiente National Park is a national park on La Palma in the Canary Islands, Spain. It protects the Caldera de Taburiente, a large caldera that dominates the north of the island, and was designated a national park in 1954.

tokens.name: Chor Minor
tokens.image_credit: Davide Mauro · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lab-i Hauz
tokens.description: Lab-i Hauz is the area around one of the few surviving hauz pools in Bukhara, Uzbekistan. Its 16th and 17th century madrasas and khanaka surround the pool, and the ensemble is part of the Historic Centre of Bukhara, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Ymblanter · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kaltaminor
tokens.title: Unfinished turquoise minaret
tokens.description: Kaltaminor is a memorial minaret in Khiva, Uzbekistan, on the front of the Muhammad Amin Khan madrasa. It stands inside Itchan Kala, the walled old city of Khiva listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Bgag · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Islamkhodja Madrasah
tokens.description: Islamkhodja Madrasah is an architectural monument in the centre of Khiva, Uzbekistan, built by Islam Khodja, prime minister and father-in-law of Khan Isfandiyar. It stands in Itchan Kala, the walled old city of Khiva, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ustyurt Plateau
tokens.description: The Ustyurt Plateau is a transboundary clay desert shared by Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Its semi-nomadic population raises camels, goats and sheep.

tokens.name: Sawran
tokens.description: Sawran, also spelled Sauran, is an ancient city in southern Kazakhstan, about 43 km north-west of Turkistan. It lies near the Syr Darya river.
tokens.image_credit: Yakov Fedorov · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Otrar
tokens.description: Otrar, also called Farab, is an ancient city in southern Kazakhstan on the Silk Road. It was the centre of a major oasis and a key junction linking Kazakhstan with China, Europe, the Middle East and Siberia.
tokens.image_credit: Coopypasted · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arslanbob
tokens.title: Vast wild walnut forest
tokens.description: Arslanbob is a village in the Jalal-Abad Region of Kyrgyzstan, beside a large wild walnut forest. The Arslanbob walnut is recorded as Kyrgyzstan's first known export to Europe.

tokens.name: Sarazm
tokens.description: Sarazm is an archaeological site near Panjakent in north-western Tajikistan, dating to the 4th millennium BC. It was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Bertramz · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nisa, Turkmenistan
tokens.description: Nisa was an ancient Parthian settlement near Ashgabat in Turkmenistan, traditionally seen as the first seat of the Arsacid Empire. Its Parthian fortresses are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Roland Lin · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Panjshir Valley
tokens.description: The Panjshir Valley is a valley in north-eastern Afghanistan, about 150 km north of Kabul, near the Hindu Kush. It is divided by the Panjshir River and is home to more than 100,000 people.

tokens.name: Salang Pass
tokens.description: The Salang Pass is a high mountain pass in the Hindu Kush of Afghanistan, at about 3,878 m. It has long been the main road link between the northern provinces and the rest of the country.

tokens.name: Darul Aman Palace
tokens.description: Darul Aman Palace is a three-storey palace about 16 km south-west of central Kabul, Afghanistan. It was built in the 1920s during the reign of Amanullah Khan and has 150 rooms.
tokens.image_credit: Qasimmirzaie · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Uvs Lake
tokens.description: Uvs Lake is a highly saline lake in north-western Mongolia. At about 3,350 km2 it is the largest lake in Mongolia by surface area, with a smaller part in Russia.

tokens.name: Amarbayasgalant Monastery
tokens.description: Amarbayasgalant Monastery is one of the three largest Buddhist monastic centres in Mongolia. It stands in the Iven Valley near the Selenge River, at the foot of Mount Büren-Khaan.
tokens.image_credit: Bogomolov.PL · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yolyn Am
tokens.description: Yolyn Am is a deep and narrow gorge in the Gurvan Saikhan Mountains of southern Mongolia. The valley is named after the lammergeier, called yol in Mongolian.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Kizil Caves
tokens.description: The Kizil Caves are a set of Buddhist rock-cut caves on the northern bank of the Muzat River in Xinjiang, China. They are one of the components of the UNESCO Silk Roads World Heritage serial property.
tokens.image_credit: Rolfmueller · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loulan
tokens.description: Loulan was an ancient Tocharian kingdom in the Tarim Basin, now consumed by the Lop Desert. It was an oasis city on the Silk Road, known from the 2nd century BCE.

tokens.name: Ananuri
tokens.description: Ananuri is a castle complex on the Aragvi River in Dusheti Municipality, Georgia, about 72 km from Tbilisi. The fortified complex includes churches as well as a fortress.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bagrati Cathedral
tokens.description: Bagrati Cathedral is an 11th-century cathedral in Kutaisi, in the Imereti region of Georgia. It was removed from the UNESCO World Heritage list after controversial conservation works.
tokens.image_credit: Marcin Konsek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Prometheus Cave Natural Monument
tokens.description: Prometheus Cave Natural Monument is a karst cave in Tsqaltubo Municipality, Imereti region of Georgia. It is also known as Kumistavi Cave.

tokens.name: Katskhi Pillar
tokens.title: Monastery atop a rock pillar
tokens.description: The Katskhi Pillar is a natural limestone monolith about 40 metres high near the village of Katskhi in western Georgia. Church ruins stand on its flat top.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title case

tokens.image_credit: Jaba1977, improvements by Giorgi Balakhadze · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: David Gareji monastery complex
tokens.description: David Gareji monastery complex is a rock-hewn Georgian Orthodox monastery complex in the Kakheti region, on the edge of the Iori Plateau. It has hundreds of cells, churches and chapels cut into the rock face.
tokens.image_credit: Vyacheslav Argenberg · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
tokens.description: The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, known as Sameba, is the main cathedral of the Georgian Orthodox Church. Built between 1995 and 2004, it is the third-tallest Eastern Orthodox cathedral in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Alexxx1979 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sanahin Monastery
tokens.description: Sanahin Monastery is an Armenian monastery founded in the 10th century in Sanahin, Lori Province. It forms a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the nearby Haghpat Monastery.
tokens.image_credit: Steven C. Price · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Areni-1 cave
tokens.description: The Areni-1 cave complex is an ancient multicomponent site near Areni village in southern Armenia, along the Arpa River. It holds a late Chalcolithic and Early Bronze Age ritual site and settlement.

tokens.name: Carahunge
tokens.description: Carahunge, also known as Zorats Karer, is a prehistoric archaeological site of standing stones near Sisian in Syunik Province, Armenia. Tourists often call it the Armenian Stonehenge.
tokens.image_credit: Aleksey Chalabyan a.k.a Xelgen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matenadaran
tokens.description: The Matenadaran, officially the Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, is a museum, archive and research institution in Yerevan. It holds the most extensive collection of Armenian manuscripts in existence.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khinalug
tokens.description: Khinalug is an ancient mountain village in Quba District, Azerbaijan, with origins in the Caucasian Albanian period. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Cultural Landscape of Khinalig People and Köç Yolu, inscribed in 2023.

tokens.name: Orinoco Delta
tokens.description: The Orinoco Delta is a vast river delta of the Orinoco River in eastern Venezuela. It is where the river spreads into many channels before reaching the Atlantic Ocean.

tokens.name: Pico Cristóbal Colón
tokens.description: Pico Cristóbal Colón is possibly the highest mountain in Colombia, with a reported height of 5,775 metres. It and Pico Simón Bolívar are the two highest peaks in Colombia and almost equal in elevation.

tokens.name: Tatacoa Desert
tokens.description: The Tatacoa Desert is the second largest arid zone in Colombia, after the Guajira Peninsula. It covers more than 330 square kilometres north of Huila Department, near Neiva.

tokens.name: Gorgona Island, Colombia
tokens.description: Gorgona is a Colombian island in the Pacific Ocean, about 28 km off the Colombian Pacific coast. It is 9 km long and is separated from the continent by a 270 m deep underwater depression.

tokens.name: Bartolomé Island
tokens.description: Bartolomé Island is an uninhabited volcanic islet of 1.2 square kilometres in Sullivan Bay, just east of Santiago Island, in the Galápagos Islands. It is named after Sir Bartholomew James Sulivan, a lieutenant aboard HMS Beagle.
tokens.image_credit: Pete from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fernandina Island
tokens.description: Fernandina Island is the youngest and third largest island in the Galápagos, and the furthest west. It has an area of 642 square kilometres and a summit caldera about 6.5 km wide.

tokens.name: Sillustani
tokens.description: Sillustani is a pre-Inca cemetery on the shores of Lake Umayo near Puno in Peru. Its tower-like chullpas were built for the Qulla people, who were conquered by the Inca Empire in the 15th century.
tokens.image_credit: Unukorno · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taquile Island
tokens.description: Taquile Island is an island on the Peruvian side of Lake Titicaca, about 45 km offshore from Puno. About 2,200 people live on the island, which covers 5.72 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Huayna Picchu
tokens.description: Huayna Picchu is a mountain in Peru around which the Urubamba River bends. It rises over Machu Picchu, the so-called Lost City of the Incas.
tokens.image_credit: Sascha Wenninger · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monastery of Santa Catalina de Siena, Arequipa
tokens.description: The Monastery of Santa Catalina de Siena is a large Dominican Second Order monastery in Arequipa, Peru, consecrated in 1579. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Historical Centre of the City of Arequipa.
tokens.image_credit: Hans Brian Brandsberg Berg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Misti
tokens.description: Misti is a volcano in the southern Peruvian Andes, rising above Arequipa, Peru's second-largest city. It has a steep conical profile and two nested summit craters.
tokens.image_credit: Los viajes del Cangrejo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siula Grande
tokens.description: Siula Grande is a mountain in the Huayhuash range of the Peruvian Andes. It is 6,344 metres high and has a subpeak, Siula Chico, 6,260 metres high.

tokens.name: Alpamayo
tokens.description: Alpamayo is one of the most conspicuous peaks in the Cordillera Blanca of the Peruvian Andes. It lies next to the slightly higher Quitaraju.
tokens.image_credit: Brad MeringBaltimore, MD, United States · Copyrighted free use · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cordillera Blanca
tokens.description: The Cordillera Blanca is a mountain range in Peru, part of the Andes, extending about 200 kilometres. It includes several peaks over 6,000 metres and 722 glaciers, and holds Huascaran, the highest mountain in Peru.

tokens.name: Túcume
tokens.description: Túcume is a pre-Hispanic site in Peru, with 26 major pyramids and mounds covering over 220 hectares. Local people also call the area the Pyramids of Túcume or Purgatorio.

tokens.name: National Mint of Bolivia
tokens.description: The National Mint of Bolivia, known in the colonial era as the Mint of Potosí, is a former mint in the city of Potosí. The current building is a museum on the site of the colonial mint's second location, which operated from 1773 to 1951.
tokens.image_credit: Elemaki · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve
tokens.description: The Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve is a protected area in the Sud Lípez province of Potosí department, in southwestern Bolivia. It lies on the high Altiplano and Andes at 4,200 to 5,400 m and was established in December 1973.

tokens.name: Lake Poopó
tokens.description: Lake Poopó was a large saline lake in a shallow depression on the Altiplano of Oruro Department, Bolivia, at about 3,700 m. It was the second-largest lake in the country before it largely dried up.

tokens.name: Isla Incahuasi
tokens.title: Cactus island in a salt flat
tokens.description: Isla Incahuasi is a rocky outcrop and former island in the middle of the Salar de Uyuni salt flat in Potosí Department, Bolivia, at 3,656 m. It covers about 24.6 hectares and hosts large Trichocereus pasacana cacti.

tokens.name: Yungas Road
tokens.title: Death Road
tokens.description: Yungas Road, commonly called Death Road, is a 64 km cycle and vehicle route linking La Paz with the Yungas region of Bolivia. Built in the 1930s by the Bolivian government, much of it was constructed by Paraguayan prisoners during the Chaco War.
tokens.image_credit: Vaido Otsar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parinacota
tokens.description: Parinacota is a dormant stratovolcano on the border of Bolivia and Chile, forming with Pomerape the Nevados de Payachata volcanic chain. Its summit reaches 6,380 m in the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Breitenbach · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Llullaillaco
tokens.title: Inca child mummies summit
tokens.description: Llullaillaco is a dormant stratovolcano on the border between Argentina and Chile, in the Puna de Atacama. Its maximum elevation is most commonly given as 6,723 m, making it the second-highest active volcano in the world.

tokens.name: Mano del Desierto
tokens.description: The Mano del Desierto is a large-scale sculpture in Chile, about 60 km south and east of Antofagasta, on the Pan-American Highway. It stands between highway markers 1309 and 1310 km.
tokens.image_credit: Marcos Escalier from Antofagasta, Chile. · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chaitén Volcano
tokens.description: Chaitén is a volcanic caldera about 3 km in diameter in southern Chile, near the Gulf of Corcovado. Its most recent eruptive phase took place in 2008.

tokens.name: Northern Patagonian Ice Field
tokens.description: The Northern Patagonian Ice Field is the smaller of two remnant parts of the Patagonian Ice Sheet in the Andes of southern South America. It lies completely within Laguna San Rafael National Park in southern Chile.

tokens.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
tokens.description: The Southern Patagonian Ice Field lies in the Andes between Chile and Argentina. It is the world's second largest contiguous extrapolar ice field and the bigger of two remnants of the Patagonian Ice Sheet.

tokens.name: Sewell, Chile
tokens.description: Sewell is an uninhabited mining town on the slopes of the Andes in Chile, a former company town built for workers of the El Teniente copper mine. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006.

tokens.name: Upsala Glacier
tokens.description: The Upsala Glacier is a large valley glacier on the eastern side of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Its higher portion lies in a disputed territory between Chile and Argentina.

tokens.name: Salinas Grandes, Jujuy and Salta
tokens.description: The Salinas Grandes are salt flats in northern Argentina, in the provinces of Jujuy and Salta, at an average altitude of 3,450 metres. The white desert covers about 212 km2 and is about 320 km long.

tokens.name: Tren a las Nubes
tokens.description: The Tren a las Nubes, known in English as Train to the Clouds, is a tourist train service in Salta Province, Argentina. It runs on the eastern part of the Salta to Antofagasta railway, crossing the Andes at over 4,220 metres.

tokens.name: Puente del Inca
tokens.description: Puente del Inca is a natural rock arch spanning the Las Cuevas River in Mendoza Province, Argentina. It lies near the village of the same name, beside hot springs that share its name.
tokens.image_credit: Bmhcmc at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Punta Tombo
tokens.title: Huge Magellanic penguin colony
tokens.description: Punta Tombo is a peninsula on the Atlantic coast of Chubut Province, Argentina, about 110 km south of Trelew. It hosts a large colony of Magellanic penguins, the largest such colony in Argentina.

tokens.name: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse
tokens.description: Les Eclaireurs Lighthouse is a conical lighthouse on the northeasternmost of the Les Eclaireurs islets in the Beagle Channel. It stands about 9 km east of Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego, Argentina.
tokens.image_credit: Ricardo Martins · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jesuit Block and Estancias of Córdoba
tokens.description: The Jesuit Block and Estancias of Córdoba are a collection of buildings and sites formerly used by the Jesuits in Córdoba Province, Argentina. UNESCO named them a World Heritage Site in 2000.

tokens.name: Corcovado
tokens.description: Corcovado is a 710 metre granite peak in the Tijuca Forest national park, in central Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It lies just west of the city centre and is visible from great distances.
tokens.image_credit: Jay.Jarosz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pedra da Gávea
tokens.description: Pedra da Gávea is a monolithic granite and gneiss mountain in the Tijuca Forest of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. At 844 metres it is one of the highest mountains in the world that ends directly in the ocean.
tokens.image_credit: KarlaFPaiva · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dedo de Deus
tokens.description: Dedo de Deus, the Finger of God, is a granite spire of about 1,692 metres in the Serra dos Órgãos National Park near Teresópolis, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is one of the main peaks of the Serra dos Órgãos range.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Antonio de Oliveira Vicente · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rocas Atoll
tokens.description: The Rocas Atoll is the only atoll in the South Atlantic Ocean. It belongs to Rio Grande do Norte state in Brazil, about 260 km northeast of Natal.
tokens.image_credit: Marinha do Brasil · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Snake Island
tokens.title: Island ruled by golden lanceheads
tokens.description: Ilha da Queimada Grande, known as Snake Island, is an island off the coast of Brazil in the Atlantic Ocean. It is famous for its abundance of snakes and is administered by the municipality of Itanhaem, Sao Paulo.
tokens.image_credit: Prefeitura Municipal de ItanhaÃ©m · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Olinda
tokens.description: Olinda is a historic city in Pernambuco, Brazil, on the Atlantic coast near Recife. Its historic centre was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Valdiney Pimenta · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Diamantina, Minas Gerais
tokens.description: Diamantina is a municipality in central Minas Gerais, Brazil, known for its colonial historic centre. Its historic centre was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999.
tokens.image_credit: Leandro Neumann Ciuffo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Museum of Tomorrow
tokens.description: The Museum of Tomorrow is a science museum in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It was designed by Santiago Calatrava and built on the waterfront at Pier Maua.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Aparecida
tokens.description: The Basilica of Our Lady of Aparecida is a Catholic basilica in Aparecida, Brazil, dedicated to Our Lady Aparecida, the principal patroness of Brazil. Its article describes it as the largest cathedral in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Valter Campanato/ABr · CC BY 3.0 br · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cabo Polonio
tokens.description: Cabo Polonio is a hamlet on the eastern coast of Uruguay, in Rocha Department. It lies in one of the country's SNAP protected areas and draws thousands of tourists in summer.
tokens.image_credit: Pablofor · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fortaleza de Santa Teresa
tokens.description: Fortaleza de Santa Teresa is a military fortification in the Rocha Department of eastern Uruguay. It lies within Santa Teresa National Park, about 800 metres from the coast at Playa la Moza.
tokens.image_credit: Kleidas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fort Zeelandia, Paramaribo
tokens.description: Fort Zeelandia is a fortress in Paramaribo, Suriname. The French built a wooden fort on the site in 1640, and the Dutch took it in 1667 and renamed it Fort Zeelandia. It is part of the Historic Inner City of Paramaribo, a UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Grytviken
tokens.title: Shackleton's grave whaling station
tokens.description: Grytviken is a hamlet on South Georgia in the South Atlantic. Formerly a whaling station, it was the largest settlement on the island.
tokens.image_credit: Lexaxis7 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Freycinet National Park
tokens.description: Freycinet National Park is a national park on the east coast of Tasmania, 125 kilometres northeast of Hobart. It occupies a large part of the Freycinet Peninsula and Schouten Island, and was founded in 1916.

tokens.name: Mount Warning
tokens.description: Mount Warning, known as Wollumbin to the Bundjalung people, is a volcanic plug in the Tweed Range of New South Wales. It was formed by the now-extinct Tweed Volcano and lies about 14 km from Murwillumbah.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title (Mount Warning)

tokens.image_credit: KHN45 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carnarvon National Park
tokens.description: Carnarvon National Park is in the Maranoa Region of Central Queensland, Australia, about 593 km northwest of Brisbane. It was first reserved in 1932 to protect Carnarvon Gorge and its scenic, cultural and geological values.

tokens.name: Heron Island
tokens.description: Heron Island is a coral cay in the southern Great Barrier Reef, about 87 km north-east of Gladstone, Queensland. It lies on the western side of Heron Reef, which supports around 900 of the 1,500 fish species found on the Great Barrier Reef.
tokens.image_credit: Ciambue · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape York Peninsula
tokens.description: The Cape York Peninsula is in Far North Queensland, Australia. It is the largest wilderness in northern Australia, and about half of its mostly flat land is used for grazing cattle.

tokens.name: Arnhem Land
tokens.description: Arnhem Land is a region in the north-eastern corner of the Northern Territory of Australia, about 500 km from Darwin. Nearby Cape Arnhem was named after the Dutch ship Arnhem, which sailed into the Gulf of Carpentaria in 1623.

tokens.name: Monkey Mia
tokens.description: Monkey Mia is a tourist reserve on the coast of Western Australia, about 900 km north of Perth. The reserve lies in the Shark Bay Marine Park and World Heritage Site and is known for bottlenose dolphins that come close to shore.

tokens.name: Naracoorte Caves National Park
tokens.description: Naracoorte Caves National Park lies near Naracoorte in South Australia's Limestone Coast region and contains 26 caves. The park was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1994 for its fossil record, together with Riversleigh.

tokens.name: Remarkable Rocks
tokens.description: Remarkable Rocks are wind and sea eroded granite boulders on a granite dome at the south-west tip of Kangaroo Island. They lie within Flinders Chase National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grampians National Park
tokens.description: The Grampians National Park is located in the Grampians region of Victoria, about 260 km west of Melbourne. The Jardwadjali name for the mountain range is Gariwerd.
tokens.image_credit: Bingobill · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wilsons Promontory
tokens.description: Wilsons Promontory, known as Wilsons Prom, is a peninsula forming the southernmost part of the Australian mainland, in the state of Victoria. Its southernmost tip is South Point.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hanging Rock, Victoria
tokens.description: Hanging Rock is a distinctive former volcano and geological formation in central Victoria, Australia. It rises 105 m above the surrounding plain between the townships of Newham and Hesket, about 70 km north-west of Melbourne.

tokens.name: Budj Bim
tokens.description: Budj Bim, also known as Mount Eccles, is a dormant volcano in south-western Victoria, Australia, within Budj Bim National Park. It is part of the Budj Bim Cultural Landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage property.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title

tokens.name: Mungo National Park
tokens.description: Mungo National Park is a protected national park in south-western New South Wales, Australia, about 875 km west of Sydney. It is part of the Willandra Lakes Region, a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: DOMENICO STALLO · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wollemi National Park
tokens.description: Wollemi National Park is a protected national park and wilderness area in New South Wales, Australia, about 130 km north-west of Sydney. It is one of the protected areas that form part of the UNESCO World Heritage Greater Blue Mountains Area.

tokens.name: National Gallery of Australia
tokens.title: Acton Peninsula museum
tokens.description: The National Gallery of Australia is the national art museum of Australia, in Canberra. Established in 1967, it holds more than 166,000 works of art.
tokens.image_credit: Thennicke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Wānaka
tokens.description: Lake Wānaka is New Zealand's fourth-largest lake, and the seat of the town of Wānaka in the Otago region. It covers about 198 km2 and is more than 300 m deep.

curation.notes: TO VERIFY article title (macron)

tokens.name: Champagne Pool
tokens.description: Champagne Pool is a prominent geothermal hot spring in the Waiotapu geothermal area, North Island, New Zealand. It lies about 30 km southeast of Rotorua.

tokens.name: The Catlins
tokens.description: The Catlins is an area in the southeastern corner of the South Island of New Zealand, between Balclutha and Invercargill. It includes the island's southernmost point, Slope Point.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Larnach Castle
tokens.description: Larnach Castle is a mock castle on the Otago Peninsula, within the city of Dunedin, New Zealand. It was built by the entrepreneur and politician William Larnach.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cathedral Cove
tokens.description: Cathedral Cove is a beach and marine reserve on the Coromandel Peninsula, New Zealand. The Te Whanganui-o-Hei Marine Reserve lies in the southern part of Mercury Bay, near Hahei.
tokens.image_credit: Krzysztof Golik · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waipoua Forest
tokens.description: Waipoua Forest is a forest on the west coast of New Zealand's North Island. It preserves some of the best remaining kauri forest in the country, including the giant kauri Tāne Mahuta.

tokens.name: Farewell Spit
tokens.description: Farewell Spit is a narrow sand spit at the northern end of Golden Bay, South Island, New Zealand. It is the longest sand spit in New Zealand and a legally protected nature reserve.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Te Waikoropupū Springs
tokens.title: Crystal-clear sacred springs
tokens.description: Te Waikoropupū Springs are cold-water springs near Tākaka in Golden Bay on the South Island of New Zealand. They are known for exceptionally clear water and are the largest cold-water springs in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chatham Islands
tokens.description: The Chatham Islands are an archipelago about 800 km east of New Zealand's South Island, administered as part of New Zealand. The largest islands are Chatham Island and Pitt Island.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Auckland Islands
tokens.description: The Auckland Islands are an archipelago of New Zealand, lying about 465 km south of the South Island. They are part of the UNESCO World Heritage New Zealand Sub-Antarctic Islands and have no permanent inhabitants.

tokens.name: Tetiʻaroa
tokens.description: Tetiʻaroa is an atoll in the Windward group of the Society Islands of French Polynesia. It was once a holiday location for Tahitian royalty and is home to The Brando Resort, leased by the actor Marlon Brando.
tokens.image_credit: Supertoff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuku Hiva
tokens.description: Nuku Hiva is the largest of the Marquesas Islands in French Polynesia. Herman Melville based his book Typee on his experiences in the Taipivai valley on the island.

tokens.name: Hiva Oa
tokens.title: Gauguin's final island
tokens.description: Hiva Oa is the second largest island in the Marquesas Islands of French Polynesia, covering about 320 square kilometres. It is the largest island of the southern Marquesas group and has around 2,200 residents.

tokens.name: Huahine
tokens.description: Huahine is an island in the Society Islands of French Polynesia, part of the Leeward Islands group. At the 2022 census it had a population of 6,263.

tokens.name: Tuamotus
tokens.description: The Tuamotus, or Tuamotu Archipelago, are a chain of just under 80 islands and atolls in the southern Pacific Ocean, part of French Polynesia. They constitute the largest chain of atolls in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Jeff Schmaltz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Upolu
tokens.description: Upolu is an island in Samoa, formed by a massive basaltic shield volcano rising from the floor of the western Pacific Ocean. With about 145,000 inhabitants, it is by far the most populous of the Samoan Islands.

tokens.name: National Park of American Samoa
tokens.description: The National Park of American Samoa is a United States national park spread across the islands of Tutuila, Ofu and Taʻū. It protects coral reefs, tropical rainforests, fruit bats and Samoan culture.
tokens.image_credit: Tavita Togia, National Park Service · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai
tokens.description: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai is a submarine volcano in the South Pacific, about 65 km north of Tongatapu, Tonga's main island. It lies on the Kermadec-Tonga subduction zone and its volcanic arc.

tokens.name: Espiritu Santo
tokens.description: Espiritu Santo, usually called Santo, is the largest island in Vanuatu, with an area of 3,955.5 square kilometres. Luganville is the only true town on the island.

tokens.name: SS President Coolidge
tokens.title: Giant WWII wreck dive
tokens.description: SS President Coolidge was an American ocean liner completed in 1931 that served as a troopship from December 1941. She was sunk by mines at Espiritu Santo in October 1942.
tokens.image_credit: Los Angeles Times · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manam
tokens.description: Manam is an island in the Bismarck Sea off the northeast coast of Papua New Guinea, built by the Manam Volcano, one of the country's most active. The island was evacuated in 2004 and many residents have since returned.
tokens.image_credit: Jesse Allen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trobriand Islands
tokens.description: The Trobriand Islands are an archipelago of coral atolls off the east coast of New Guinea, in Milne Bay Province of Papua New Guinea. Most of the population lives on Kiriwina, where the government station Losuia is located.

tokens.name: Heart of Voh
tokens.description: The Heart of Voh is a natural heart-shaped clearing in the mangrove on the west coast of Grande Terre, New Caledonia, about 300 km from Nouméa. Its aerial shape was made famous by a photograph in Yann Arthus-Bertrand's Earth from Above.

tokens.name: Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre
tokens.description: The Tjibaou Cultural Centre, designed by Renzo Piano, opened in 1998 on the Tina Peninsula near Noumea, New Caledonia. It celebrates Kanak culture, the indigenous culture of New Caledonia.
tokens.image_credit: Wikimedia Commons user Fanny Schertzer (a.k.a User:Inisheer) · Cc-by-sa-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loyalty Islands
tokens.description: The Loyalty Islands are an archipelago in the Pacific Ocean, northeast of the New Caledonian mainland of Grande Terre. They form Loyalty Islands Province, one of the three top-level subdivisions of New Caledonia, with its seat at Lifou.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Peleliu
tokens.description: Peleliu is an island in the island nation of Palau. It forms one of the sixteen states of Palau, together with two small islands to its northeast.

tokens.name: Pohnpei
tokens.description: Pohnpei is an island of the Senyavin Islands in the Caroline Islands group. It belongs to Pohnpei State, one of the four states of the Federated States of Micronesia, and is home to the national capital Palikir.

tokens.name: Kosrae
tokens.description: Kosrae is an island in the Caroline Islands archipelago and a state of the Federated States of Micronesia. With a land area of 110 square kilometres, it is the smallest state of the country by area.

tokens.name: Yap
tokens.title: Island of stone money
tokens.description: Yap is an island group in the Caroline Islands of the western Pacific Ocean, part of Yap State in the Federated States of Micronesia. The name now also refers to the state, which includes the Yap Main Islands and their outer islands.

tokens.name: Enewetak Atoll
tokens.description: Enewetak Atoll is a large coral atoll of 40 islands in the Pacific Ocean. It forms a legislative district of the Ralik Chain of the Marshall Islands and surrounds a deep central lagoon.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hanauma Bay
tokens.description: Hanauma Bay is a marine embayment formed within a tuff ring on the southeast coast of Oahu, Hawaii. It is one of the most popular tourist destinations on the island.
tokens.image_credit: ErgoSum88 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park
tokens.description: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park is a US national historical park on the west coast of Hawaiʻi island. It preserves a place of refuge where Hawaiians who broke a kapu could flee to avoid death until the early 19th century.
tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kalaupapa National Historical Park
tokens.description: Kalaupapa National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park on the Kalaupapa peninsula of Molokaʻi, Hawaii. Congress established it in 1980 to expand the earlier Kalaupapa Leper Settlement National Historic Landmark.

tokens.name: Molokini
tokens.description: Molokini is a crescent-shaped, partially submerged volcanic crater and uninhabited islet in the ʻAlalākeiki Channel between Maui and Kahoʻolawe, Hawaii. It is the remains of one of the seven Pleistocene volcanoes that formed Maui Nui.
tokens.image_credit: Forest & Kim Starr · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tinian, Northern Mariana Islands
tokens.description: Tinian is one of the three principal islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. Together with the uninhabited Aguijan it forms Tinian Municipality, and its largest village is San Jose.

tokens.name: Orongo
tokens.title: Birdman cult village
tokens.description: Orongo is a stone ceremonial village at the southwestern tip of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), with round, sod-covered houses on the rim of the Rano Kau caldera. It is part of the Rapa Nui National Park World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: American at German Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rano Kau
tokens.description: Rano Kau is a 324 m tall extinct volcano that forms the southwestern headland of Easter Island, Chile. The volcano lies within the Rapa Nui National Park World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anakena
tokens.description: Anakena is a white coral sand beach in Rapa Nui National Park on Easter Island, Chile. It has two ahu platforms with moai statues, Ahu Ature with one moai and Ahu Nao Nao with seven.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gorges du Tarn
tokens.description: The Gorges du Tarn is a canyon cut by the Tarn river between the Causse Méjean and Causse de Sauveterre in southern France. At about 53 km long it is the longest canyon in Europe, and it lies within the Causses and Cévennes World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Hallstätter See
tokens.description: Hallstätter See, or Lake Hallstatt, is a lake in the Salzkammergut region of Austria. It lies beside the small market town of Hallstatt, known for salt mining since prehistoric times, and is part of the Hallstatt-Dachstein Salzkammergut UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.
tokens.image_credit: Tigerente · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road
tokens.description: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road is the highest surfaced mountain pass road in Austria. It connects Bruck in Salzburg with Heiligenblut in Carinthia over the Fuscher Törl and Hochtor passes, and is named after the Grossglockner, Austria's highest mountain.

tokens.name: Reichsburg Cochem
tokens.description: Reichsburg Cochem is a hilltop castle above the town of Cochem on the Moselle in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. The castle overlooks the Moselle valley.
tokens.image_credit: Steffen Schmitz (more photos) · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oeschinen Lake
tokens.description: Oeschinen Lake, or Oeschinensee, is a mountain lake in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland, located above the village of Kandersteg. The lake lies at 1,578 metres and was formed by prehistoric landslides.
tokens.image_credit: Günter Seggebäing, Coesfeld · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rhône Glacier
tokens.description: The Rhône Glacier is a glacier in the Swiss Alps in the canton of Valais. It is the source of the river Rhône and one of the main contributors to Lake Geneva.
tokens.image_credit: Jamcib · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rocamadour
tokens.description: Rocamadour is a commune in the Lot department in southwestern France, in the former province of Quercy. Its medieval pilgrimage sanctuary is a component of the UNESCO Routes of Santiago de Compostela in France.
tokens.image_credit: Dynamosquito from France · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sénanque Abbey
tokens.description: Sénanque Abbey, or Abbaye Notre-Dame de Sénanque, is a Cistercian abbey near the village of Gordes in the Vaucluse department of Provence, France. Its full French name is Abbaye Notre-Dame de Sénanque.
tokens.image_credit: Greudin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Château de Chenonceau
tokens.description: The Château de Chenonceau is a French château spanning the river Cher, near the village of Chenonceaux in Indre-et-Loire. It is one of the best-known châteaux of the Loire Valley, and its estate is first mentioned in the 11th century.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Château de Chambord
tokens.description: The Château de Chambord is a French Renaissance château in Centre-Val de Loire, built from 1519 to 1547 for Francis I as a royal hunting lodge. It is the largest château in the Loire Valley and a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Calips assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Château de Villandry
tokens.description: The Château de Villandry is a grand country house in Villandry, Indre-et-Loire, France. It is especially known for its formal Renaissance gardens.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. LonganimE assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cirque de Gavarnie
tokens.description: The Cirque de Gavarnie is a vast rock cirque in the central Pyrenees, close to the Spanish border. It lies in the Pyrenees National Park and has the Gavarnie Falls and the Brèche de Roland.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Miguel303xm~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Annecy
tokens.description: Lake Annecy is a perialpine lake in Haute-Savoie, France, at about 447 m above sea level. It is named after the city of Annecy, which marks the start of the Thiou, the lake's outflow river.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Padirac Cave
tokens.description: Padirac Cave, also called the Padirac Chasm (Gouffre de Padirac), is a cave near Gramat in the Lot department of Occitanie, France. Its French name is Gouffre de Padirac.
tokens.image_credit: Luc Viatour · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caminito del Rey
tokens.description: Caminito del Rey is a walkway pinned along the steep walls of a narrow gorge in El Chorro, near Ardales in Málaga province, Spain. It was built in the early 20th century and was partly closed for over a decade.
tokens.image_credit: Malopez 21 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montserrat, Spain
tokens.description: Montserrat is a multi-peaked mountain range near Barcelona in Catalonia, Spain, part of the Catalan Pre-Coastal Range. Its main peaks are Sant Jeroni, Montgrós and Les Agulles.
tokens.image_credit: MARIA ROSA FERRE ✿ · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gaztelugatxe
tokens.description: Gaztelugatxe is an islet on the Bay of Biscay coast in the municipality of Bermeo, Basque Country, Spain, connected to the mainland by a footbridge. A hermitage dedicated to John the Baptist, called San Juan de Gaztelugatxe in Spanish, stands on top.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park
tokens.description: Ordesa y Monte Perdido National Park is an IUCN Category II national park in the Spanish Pyrenees, protected since 1918 and enlarged in 1982 to 156 square kilometres. It is part of the transboundary Pyrenees - Mont Perdu World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Heparina1985 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcázar of Segovia
tokens.description: The Alcázar of Segovia is a medieval castle on a rocky crag at the western end of Segovia's Old City in Castile and León, Spain. It has existed since the 12th century and lies within Segovia's Old City, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985.
tokens.image_credit: Rafa Esteve · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ponta da Piedade
tokens.description: Ponta da Piedade is a headland of yellow cliffs and rock formations along the coast of Lagos in the Algarve, Portugal. Several grottos in the formations can be visited by boat, and it is one of Portugal's best known tourist attractions.
tokens.image_credit: Jose A. · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pragser Wildsee
tokens.description: Pragser Wildsee, also called Lago di Braies, is a natural lake in the Prags Dolomites of South Tyrol, Italy. It belongs to the municipality of Prags, which lies in the Prags Valley.
tokens.image_credit: STirol · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Civita di Bagnoregio
tokens.description: Civita di Bagnoregio is an outlying village of the comune of Bagnoregio in the Province of Viterbo, central Italy. The village is reached only by a footbridge from the nearby town of Bagnoregio.
tokens.image_credit: User:New2022 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Castel del Monte, Apulia
tokens.description: Castel del Monte is a 13th-century citadel and castle on a hill in Andria, in the Apulia region of southeast Italy. It was built in the 1240s by King Frederick II and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: ParisTaras · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monemvasia
tokens.description: Monemvasia is a town and municipality in Laconia, Greece, built on a tied island off the east coast of the Peloponnese. It is connected to the mainland by a sandy tombolo about 400 metres long.
tokens.image_credit: Katsikas pantelis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dunluce Castle
tokens.description: Dunluce Castle is a ruined medieval castle on a basalt outcrop on the County Antrim coast in Northern Ireland, between Portballintrae and Portrush. It is reached by a bridge from the mainland and was the seat of Clan MacQuillan.
tokens.image_credit: Iain Irwin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dark Hedges
tokens.description: The Dark Hedges is a carriage avenue of mature European beech trees along Bregagh Road near Armoy in County Antrim, Northern Ireland. The trees meet overhead to form a tree tunnel about 150 metres long.
tokens.image_credit: Colin Park · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quiraing
tokens.description: The Quiraing is a landform on the eastern face of Meall na Suiramach, the northernmost summit of the Trotternish escarpment on the Isle of Skye, Scotland. It is a hollow surrounded by a high rampart of rock.
tokens.image_credit: Colin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Durdle Door
tokens.description: Durdle Door is a natural limestone arch on the Jurassic Coast near Lulworth in Dorset, England. It is privately owned by the Weld family but open to the public.
tokens.image_credit: Saffron Blaze · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seven Sisters, East Sussex
tokens.description: The Seven Sisters are a series of chalk sea cliffs on the English Channel coast in East Sussex, south-east England. They run between the mouth of the River Cuckmere near Seaford and Beachy Head.
tokens.image_credit: Balon Greyjoy · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bamburgh Castle
tokens.description: Bamburgh Castle is a Grade I listed castle on the northeast coast of England, by the village of Bamburgh in Northumberland. The site may have been the capital of the kingdom of Bernicia.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew Hartley · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St Michael's Mount
tokens.description: St Michael's Mount is a tidal island in Mount's Bay near Penzance in Cornwall, England. It is linked to the town of Marazion by a causeway that is passable between mid-tide and low water.
tokens.image_credit: Werner Wilmes · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tintagel Castle
tokens.description: Tintagel Castle is a medieval fortification on the peninsula of Tintagel Island, next to the village of Tintagel in North Cornwall, England. It was probably a seasonal residence of the regional king of Dumnonia.
tokens.image_credit: Mustangbarry · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fountains Abbey
tokens.description: Fountains Abbey is a ruined Cistercian monastery near Ripon in North Yorkshire, England. Founded in 1132, it became one of the wealthiest monasteries in England before its dissolution in 1539.
tokens.image_credit: Benjamin Smith · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lindisfarne
tokens.description: Lindisfarne, also known as Holy Island, is a tidal island off the northeast coast of England in Northumberland. It was an important centre of Celtic Christianity from the 6th century, under Saints Aidan and Cuthbert.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Combe from York, UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Conwy Castle
tokens.description: Conwy Castle is a fortification in Conwy, North Wales, built by Edward I between 1283 and 1287. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew Woodvine · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caernarfon Castle
tokens.description: Caernarfon Castle is a medieval fortress in Gwynedd, north-west Wales, begun by King Edward I in 1283. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd.
tokens.image_credit: Llywelyn2000 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kylemore Abbey
tokens.description: Kylemore Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in Connemara, County Galway, Ireland. It was founded in 1920 on the grounds of Kylemore Castle, for Benedictine nuns who fled Belgium in the First World War.
tokens.image_credit: Alvesgaspar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rock of Cashel
tokens.description: The Rock of Cashel, also known as Cashel of the Kings and St. Patrick's Rock, is a historical site located dramatically above a plain at Cashel, County Tipperary, Ireland. The site includes Cormac's Chapel and a medieval cathedral.
tokens.image_credit: Holger Uwe Schmitt · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Glendalough
tokens.description: Glendalough is a glacial valley in County Wicklow, Ireland, known for an early medieval monastic settlement founded in the 6th century by St Kevin. The valley is also a recreational area for walking and had a lead mine from 1825 to 1957.
tokens.image_credit: Schcambo at English Wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Slieve League
tokens.description: Slieve League is a mountain on the Atlantic coast of County Donegal, Ireland, rising to 601 metres. It has some of the highest sea cliffs in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Tony Webster from Portland, Oregon, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kilchurn Castle
tokens.description: Kilchurn Castle is a ruined structure on a rocky peninsula at the northeastern end of Loch Awe, in Argyll and Bute, Scotland. It was first built in the mid-15th century as the base of the Campbells of Glenorchy.
tokens.image_credit: MHoser · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dunnottar Castle
tokens.description: Dunnottar Castle is a ruined medieval fortress on a rocky headland on the northeast coast of Scotland, about 3 km south of Stonehaven. Its surviving buildings are mostly 15th and 16th century, and it played a prominent role in Scottish history up to the Jacobite risings.
tokens.image_credit: Andrewmckie · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ring of Brodgar
tokens.description: The Ring of Brodgar is a Neolithic henge and stone circle about 6 miles north-east of Stromness on Mainland, Orkney, Scotland. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Heart of Neolithic Orkney.
tokens.image_credit: Stevekeiretsu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lysefjord
tokens.description: Lysefjord is a 42 km long fjord in the Ryfylke area of Rogaland county, southwestern Norway, about 25 km east of Stavanger. Its name means light fjord, from the light coloured granite rocks along its sides.

tokens.name: Senja
tokens.description: Senja is an island in Troms county, northern Norway, and the second largest island in Norway outside Svalbard, with an area of about 1,586 square km. Its western side faces the Atlantic with wild mountains, while the eastern side is milder and lusher.
tokens.image_credit: Ximonic (Simo Räsänen) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jostedal Glacier
tokens.description: Jostedal Glacier, or Jostedalsbreen, is the largest glacier in continental Europe. It lies mainly in Vestland county in western Norway, across the municipalities of Luster, Sogndal, Sunnfjord and Stryn.

tokens.name: Briksdalsbreen
tokens.description: Briksdalsbreen is one of the most accessible and best known arms of the Jostedalsbreen glacier. It lies in Briksdalen, at the end of the Oldedalen valley in Stryn Municipality, Vestland county, Norway.
tokens.image_credit: Jens Vinsrygg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Urnes Stave Church
tokens.description: Urnes Stave Church is a 12th-century stave church at Ornes, on the eastern side of the Lustrafjorden in Luster Municipality, Vestland county, Norway. It is among the oldest stave churches in Norway and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Superbass · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Borgund Stave Church
tokens.description: Borgund Stave Church is a former parish church in Lærdal Municipality, Vestland county, Norway, built around 1200 as the village church of Borgund. Its parish role passed to a new church in 1868, and the old church was restored and turned into a museum.
tokens.image_credit: mendhak · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hardangerfjord
tokens.description: The Hardangerfjord is the fifth longest fjord in the world and the second longest fjord in Norway. It stretches 180 km from the Atlantic Ocean into the mountainous interior along the Hardangervidda plateau.

tokens.name: Vøringsfossen
tokens.description: Vøringsfossen is the 83rd highest waterfall in Norway by total fall. It lies at the top of the Måbødalen valley in Eidfjord Municipality, Vestland county, near National Road 7.
tokens.image_credit: Netha Hussain · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jotunheimen
tokens.description: Jotunheimen is a mountainous area of roughly 3,500 square kilometres in southern Norway, part of the Scandinavian Mountains. The 29 highest mountains in Norway are located there, including Galdhøpiggen, the highest point in Norway.

tokens.name: Sørvágsvatn
tokens.title: Lake hanging above the ocean
tokens.description: Sørvágsvatn, also called Leitisvatn, is the largest lake in the Faroe Islands. It lies on the island of Vágar, between the municipalities of Sørvágur and Vágar.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Goðafoss
tokens.description: Goðafoss is a waterfall in northern Iceland, located along the country's main ring road at the junction with the Sprengisandur highland road. The river Skjálfandafljót falls 12 metres over a width of 30 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Andreas Tille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Svartifoss
tokens.description: Svartifoss is a waterfall in Skaftafell, Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland. It is surrounded by dark basalt lava columns, which gave the waterfall its name, meaning black waterfall.
tokens.image_credit: Andreas Tille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue Lagoon, Iceland
tokens.description: The Blue Lagoon is a geothermal spa in a lava field on the Reykjanes Peninsula in southwestern Iceland. It is supplied by water from the nearby Svartsengi geothermal power station and is one of the most visited attractions in Iceland.
tokens.image_credit: Bloody-libu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur
tokens.description: Fjaðrárgljúfur is a canyon in southeast Iceland, through which the Fjaðrá river flows. The canyon has steep walls and winding water.

tokens.name: Ásbyrgi
tokens.description: Ásbyrgi is a horseshoe-shaped glacial canyon and forest in northern Iceland, about 38 km east of Húsavík. It lies within Vatnajökull National Park and is split in two by the rock pillar Eyjan.
tokens.image_credit: Gummao · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Strokkur
tokens.description: Strokkur is a fountain-type geyser in a geothermal area beside the Hvítá River in southwest Iceland. It erupts every 6 to 10 minutes, usually 15 to 20 metres high.
tokens.image_credit: Christoph Strässler from Oberdorf BL, Schweiz · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dyrhólaey
tokens.description: Dyrhólaey is a small promontory on the south coast of Iceland, not far from the village of Vík. It was formerly an island of volcanic origin, and the volcano erupted about 100,000 years ago.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ilulissat Icefjord
tokens.description: Ilulissat Icefjord is a fjord in western Greenland, about 40 km long, running from the ice sheet to Disko Bay. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004 for its natural beauty and the Jakobshavn Glacier.

tokens.name: Ölüdeniz
tokens.description: Ölüdeniz is a town in the Fethiye district of Muğla Province, Turkey, with 6,132 residents in 2022. Its name means Dead Sea for its calm waters, and its official translation is Blue Lagoon.
tokens.image_credit: Dan Taylor · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rosh HaNikra grottoes
tokens.description: Rosh HaNikra is a white chalk cliff on the Mediterranean coast of the Western Galilee, on the Israel-Lebanon border. Sea action has hollowed the soft chalk into a set of spectacular grottoes.
tokens.image_credit: Chmee2 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jebel Shams
tokens.description: Jebel Shams is the highest mountain in Oman, in the Jebel Akhdar range of the Hajar Mountains, north of the town of Al-Hamra. It is a popular sightseeing area about 240 km from Muscat.

tokens.name: Dar al-Hajar
tokens.description: Dar al-Hajar is a former royal palace in Wadi Dhar, about 15 km from Sanaa, Yemen. Built in 1920 as the summer retreat of Imam Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din, it sits on a structure dating from 1786.
tokens.image_credit: yeowatzup · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hukou Waterfalls
tokens.description: The Hukou Waterfalls are the largest waterfall on the Yellow River and the second largest waterfall in China. They lie on the border of Shanxi and Shaanxi provinces.
tokens.image_credit: Leruswing · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tianmen Mountain
tokens.description: Tianmen Mountain is a mountain within Tianmen Mountain National Park in Zhangjiajie, northwestern Hunan Province, China. Its name means Heaven's Gate Mountain.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kanas Lake
tokens.description: Kanas Lake is a lake in Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang, China, in a valley of the Altai Mountains. It was formed around 200,000 years ago by glacier movement.

tokens.name: Yehliu
tokens.description: Yehliu is a cape and promontory in Wanli District, New Taipei, Taiwan, stretching about 1,700 metres into the sea. It was formed about six million years ago by the collision of the Philippine Sea and Eurasian plates.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
tokens.description: Jigokudani Monkey Park is in Yamanouchi, Nagano Prefecture, Japan, within Joshinetsu Kogen National Park. Its name means Hell's Valley, after the steam and boiling water rising from the ground.
tokens.image_credit: Yosemite · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matsushima
tokens.description: Matsushima is a group of about 260 small pine-covered islands in Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. It is considered one of the Three Views of Japan.

tokens.name: Amanohashidate
tokens.description: Amanohashidate is a pine-covered sandbar in Miyazu Bay in northern Kyoto Prefecture, one of Japan's three scenic views. It forms part of the Tango-Amanohashidate-Ōeyama Quasi-National Park.
tokens.image_credit: 808PhatBeats · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tottori Sand Dunes
tokens.description: The Tottori Sand Dunes are sand dunes outside the city centre of Tottori in Tottori Prefecture, Japan. At about 14 km long they are the largest sand dune in Japan, part of the San'in Kaigan Geopark.
tokens.image_credit: Hashi photo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nachi Falls
tokens.description: Nachi Falls is a 133 m waterfall in Nachikatsuura, Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, one of the best-known waterfalls in the country. It is worshipped at Kumano Nachi Taisha and is part of the Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range.
tokens.image_credit: Alpsdake · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Mashū
tokens.description: Lake Mashū is an endorheic crater lake in the caldera of a volcano in Akan Mashu National Park on Hokkaido, Japan. It has been called the clearest lake in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Miya.m · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ōkunoshima
tokens.description: Ōkunoshima is a small island in the Seto Inland Sea, considered part of the city of Takehara in Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan. In 1925 the Imperial Japanese Army built a poison gas factory on the island.

tokens.name: Khao Phing Kan
tokens.title: James Bond Island
tokens.description: Khao Phing Kan, commonly known as James Bond Island, is a limestone karst island in Phang Nga Bay northeast of Phuket, Thailand. It is part of Ao Phang Nga National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Haandrikman · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vat Phou
tokens.description: Vat Phou is a ruined Khmer-Hindu temple complex in southern Laos near Champasak. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Vat Phou and Associated Ancient Settlements within the Champasak Cultural Landscape, inscribed in 2001.
tokens.image_credit: Basile Morin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Popa
tokens.description: Mount Popa is a dormant volcano 1,518 m high in central Myanmar, about 50 km southeast of Bagan. It is a pilgrimage site, with numerous nat temples and relic sites on its summit.

tokens.name: U Bein Bridge
tokens.description: U Bein Bridge is a 1.2 km teakwood footbridge across Taungthaman Lake near Amarapura, Myanmar. Built around 1850, it is believed to be the oldest and longest teakwood bridge in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Heinz_Htetz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coron, Palawan
tokens.description: Coron is a municipality in Palawan, Philippines, with 69,439 inhabitants at the 2024 census. Its Coron Island Natural Biotic Area is on the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List.
tokens.image_credit: Patrickroque01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Wave, Arizona
tokens.description: The Wave is a sandstone rock formation on the slopes of the Coyote Buttes in the Paria Canyon-Vermilion Cliffs Wilderness, near the Utah border. The area is administered by the Bureau of Land Management.
tokens.image_credit: Gb11111 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Canyonlands National Park
tokens.description: Canyonlands National Park is a national park in southeastern Utah near Moab. The Colorado River, the Green River and their tributaries eroded its landscape into canyons, mesas and buttes.
tokens.image_credit: au_ears · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
tokens.description: Dead Horse Point State Park is a state park in San Juan County, Utah, with a dramatic overlook of the Colorado River and Canyonlands National Park. The park opened to the public in 1959.
tokens.image_credit: Nikater · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Delicate Arch
tokens.description: Delicate Arch is a 16 m freestanding natural arch in Arches National Park near Moab, Utah. It is the most widely recognised landmark of the park and appears on Utah license plates.
tokens.image_credit: “Jon Zander (Digon3)” · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capitol Reef National Park
tokens.description: Capitol Reef National Park is a national park in south-central Utah, established in 1971 to preserve desert landscape. The park is about 100 km long on its north-south axis.

tokens.name: Goblin Valley State Park
tokens.description: Goblin Valley State Park is a state park in Emery County, Utah, known for thousands of hoodoos called goblins. An erosion-resistant rock layer on softer sandstone gives the rocks their distinct shapes.
tokens.image_credit: CGP Grey · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valley of Fire State Park
tokens.description: Valley of Fire State Park is a recreation and nature preservation area of nearly 19,000 ha in Nevada, 26 km south of Overton. Its red Aztec Sandstone formations, shaped from dunes about 150 million years ago, give the park its name.
tokens.image_credit: Clément Bardot · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
