tokens.description: The Grand Egyptian Museum is a national archaeological museum in Giza, Egypt, dedicated to Egyptian civilization. It is described as the largest museum in the world for a single civilization.
tokens.image_credit: Mohamed abdelzaher · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sharm El Sheikh
tokens.description: Sharm El Sheikh is an Egyptian city on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, on the Red Sea coast. It is the administrative hub of South Sinai Governorate.
tokens.image_credit: Tanya Dedyukhina · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hurghada
tokens.description: Hurghada is a coastal city on the Red Sea in Egypt, and the largest city and capital of the Red Sea Governorate. It grew from a small fishing village into one of the largest resort destinations along the Red Sea coast.

tokens.name: Blue Hole, Dahab
tokens.description: The Blue Hole is a diving location on the southeast Sinai coast, a few kilometres north of Dahab, Egypt. Its maximum depth is just over 100 m, and a shallow opening called the saddle links it to the sea.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
tokens.description: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina is a major library and cultural centre on the Mediterranean shore in Alexandria, Egypt. It commemorates the ancient Library of Alexandria and was officially inaugurated in 2002.
tokens.image_credit: René Dinkel · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ostankino Tower
tokens.description: The Ostankino Tower is a television and radio tower in Moscow, Russia. Standing 540.1 metres tall, it is the tallest free-standing structure in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Klodklodklod77 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lakhta Center
tokens.description: The Lakhta Center is an 87-storey skyscraper in the Lakhta district of Saint Petersburg, Russia. At 462 metres it is the tallest building in Russia and in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Florstein (Telegram:WikiPhoto.Space) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Federation Tower
tokens.description: The Federation Tower is a complex of two skyscrapers in the Moscow International Business Center, Moscow, Russia. Its taller tower, Vostok, is the second-tallest skyscraper in Europe after the Lakhta Center.
tokens.image_credit: Saiht · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mercury City Tower
tokens.description: Mercury City Tower is a 338.8 m supertall mixed-use skyscraper on plot 14 of the Moscow International Business Center, Russia. It was formerly the tallest building in Russia and in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: AltynAsyr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moscow International Business Center
tokens.description: The Moscow International Business Center, also known as Moscow-City, is a skyscraper business district on the Presnenskaya Embankment of the Moskva River. It lies about 4 km west of Red Square in Moscow.
tokens.image_credit: mos.ru · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red Square
tokens.title: Heart of Moscow
tokens.description: Red Square is one of the oldest and largest squares in Moscow, Russia, along the eastern walls of the Kremlin. It is part of the Kremlin and Red Square, Moscow UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: mos.ru · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: GUM
tokens.description: GUM is a shopping centre facing Red Square in the Kitai-gorod area of Moscow. The Kremlin and Red Square UNESCO World Heritage property lies on the square it faces.
tokens.image_credit: Josef F. Stuefer · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: VDNKh
tokens.description: VDNKh, the Exhibition of Achievements of National Economy, is a permanent trade show and amusement park in Moscow. Between 1991 and 2014 it was called the All-Russia Exhibition Centre.
tokens.image_credit: Ignat pavlov111 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nevsky Prospect
tokens.description: Nevsky Prospect is the main street of Saint Petersburg, Russia. Its name comes from the Alexander Nevsky Lavra monastery at its eastern end.
tokens.image_credit: Vasilii Martynov · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace Square
tokens.description: Palace Square is the central city square of Saint Petersburg, Russia, linking Nevsky Prospect with Palace Bridge. Many significant events took place there, including Bloody Sunday and parts of the October Revolution of 1917.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sochi
tokens.description: Sochi is the largest resort city in Russia, on the Black Sea coast in the North Caucasus. The city proper has about 466,000 residents according to its Wikipedia article.
tokens.image_credit: Trace · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Krasnaya Polyana, Sochi
tokens.description: Krasnaya Polyana is an urban-type settlement in the Western Caucasus, under the administration of Sochi in Krasnodar Krai, Russia. It is home to the Rosa Khutor alpine ski resort.
tokens.image_credit: Legioner2016 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Baikal
tokens.description: Lake Baikal is a rift lake in southern Siberia, Russia, and the deepest lake in the world. It is the seventh-largest lake by surface area and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA/GSFC · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kamchatka Peninsula
tokens.description: The Kamchatka Peninsula is a 1,250 km long peninsula in the Russian Far East, bounded by the Sea of Okhotsk and the Bering Sea. It covers about 270,000 square km.
tokens.image_credit: Jeff Schmaltz · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trans-Siberian Railway
tokens.description: The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world, about 9,289 km from Moscow in the west to Vladivostok in the east. The token sits at Moscow Yaroslavsky station, its western terminus.
tokens.image_credit: Toen96 · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baikal-Amur Mainline
tokens.description: The Baikal-Amur Mainline is a 4,324 km railway in Eastern Siberia and the Russian Far East, built by the Soviet Union as a strategic alternative to the Trans-Siberian Railway. The token sits at the Severomuysky Tunnel, its longest tunnel.
tokens.image_credit: MOROVICTOR · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khan Shatyr Entertainment Center
tokens.description: Khan Shatyr is a transparent tent-shaped entertainment centre in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan. It was unveiled on 9 December 2006 and is 150 m tall including its spire.
tokens.image_credit: Bgag · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
tokens.description: The Heydar Aliyev Center is a cultural complex in Baku, Azerbaijan, designed by Zaha Hadid. It is named after Heydar Aliyev, first secretary of Soviet Azerbaijan from 1969 to 1982.
tokens.image_credit: lumoplank · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baku Boulevard
tokens.description: Baku Boulevard is a promenade along the Caspian seafront of Baku, Azerbaijan, established in 1909. It is also known as the National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Khortan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Batumi
tokens.description: Batumi is the second-largest city of Georgia and the capital of the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, on the Black Sea coast. Its economy relies on tourism and gambling, and it is an important seaport.
tokens.image_credit: Matti&Keti, Lorenz.King@geogr.uni-giessen.de · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gudauri
tokens.description: Gudauri is a ski resort in Georgia on the south-facing plateau of the Greater Caucasus, about 120 km north of Tbilisi. It lies at about 2,200 m above sea level in the Kazbegi Municipality.

tokens.name: Yerevan Cascade
tokens.description: The Cascade is a monumental terraced complex of stairs, fountains and sculptures in Yerevan, Armenia, linking the city centre with the Kanaker-Zeytun district. It is one of the symbols of the city and includes exhibition halls.
tokens.image_credit: Textfabrikant · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shilin Night Market
tokens.description: Shilin Night Market is a night market in Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan. It is often considered the largest and most famous night market in Taiwan.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 2.0 tw · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alishan National Scenic Area
tokens.description: Alishan National Scenic Area is a mountain resort and nature reserve located in Alishan Township, Chiayi County, Taiwan. It is a protected mountain landscape in Chiayi County.

tokens.name: Tel Aviv Promenade
tokens.description: Tel Aviv Promenade runs along the Mediterranean seashore in Tel Aviv, Israel. It is commonly referred to in Hebrew simply as the Tayelet.
tokens.image_credit: israeltourism from Israel · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ein Bokek
tokens.description: Ein Bokek is an Israeli seaside resort on the Dead Sea, near Neve Zohar. It is under the jurisdiction of the Tamar Regional Council in the Southern District.
tokens.image_credit: Tiia Monto · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dōtonbori
tokens.title: Neon canal of Osaka
tokens.description: Dōtonbori is a district in Osaka, Japan, along the Dōtonbori canal in the Namba district of Chūō ward. It is one of Osaka's principal tourist and nightlife areas, known for its large illuminated signboards.
tokens.image_credit: Type specimen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Flame Towers
tokens.description: The Flame Towers are a group of three skyscrapers in Baku, Azerbaijan. The tallest tower is 182 m (597 ft) high.
tokens.image_credit: Viceskeeni2 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre
tokens.description: The Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre is a 530-metre mixed-use supertall skyscraper completed in 2016. It is the tallest completed building in Guangzhou and houses offices, apartments, a hotel and a shopping mall.
tokens.image_credit: xiquinhosilva · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bridge of Peace
tokens.description: The Bridge of Peace is a bow-shaped pedestrian bridge over the Kura River, linking Rike Park with Old Town in Tbilisi. Opened in 2010, it is illuminated with LEDs and is one of the best-known landmarks of the Georgian capital.
tokens.image_credit: falco · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arbat Street
tokens.description: Arbat Street is a pedestrian street about one kilometre long in the historical centre of Moscow. It has existed since at least the 15th century and forms the heart of the Arbat District.
tokens.image_credit: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gorky Park, Moscow
tokens.description: Gorky Central Park of Culture and Leisure is a central park in Moscow, named after the writer Maxim Gorky. Its 90th anniversary was celebrated in 2018, and it was reconstructed in 2011.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tsukiji fish market
tokens.description: Tsukiji Market is a former seafood market and a major tourist attraction in central Tokyo, between the Sumida River and the Ginza shopping district. Before 2018 it was the largest wholesale fish and seafood market in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Kakidai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khaosan Road
tokens.title: Backpacker street of Bangkok
tokens.description: Khaosan Road is a 410-metre street in central Bangkok, constructed in 1892 during the reign of Rama V. It lies in the Bang Lamphu area of Phra Nakhon District, about 1 km north of the Grand Palace.
tokens.image_credit: Marcin Konsek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
tokens.description: The Chatuchak Weekend Market, on Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road in Bangkok, is the largest market in Thailand. It has more than 15,000 stalls in 27 sections, selling plants, antiques, electronics, clothing, pets and food.
tokens.image_credit: MikSed · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
tokens.description: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market is a floating market in Ratchaburi province, about 100 km southwest of Bangkok. It has become primarily a tourist attraction and is often considered the most famous floating market.
tokens.image_credit: Ahoerstemeier · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maya Bay
tokens.description: Maya Bay is a beach on Ko Phi Phi Le, an island of the Phi Phi Archipelago in the Andaman Sea, Krabi province, Thailand. It was used as the setting of the 2000 film The Beach.
tokens.image_credit: User:Mikecleggphoto from www.travelanddestinations.com · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phuket
tokens.description: Phuket is one of the southern provinces of Thailand, consisting of the island of Phuket, the country's largest island, and 32 smaller islands. It lies off the west coast of mainland Thailand in the Andaman Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Bennypc · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Patong
tokens.description: Patong is a beach and town on the west coast of Phuket island in Thailand. It is the main tourist resort on Phuket and the centre of the island's nightlife and shopping.
tokens.image_credit: Dvanderven · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pattaya
tokens.description: Pattaya is a city on the east coast of the Gulf of Thailand, about 150 km southeast of Bangkok. It is the largest city in Chonburi province and the eighth-largest city in Thailand.
tokens.image_credit: Sergey S. Dukachev · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Railay Beach
tokens.description: Railay Beach, also known as Rai Leh, is a small peninsula between the city of Krabi and Ao Nang in Thailand. It is reached only by boat and is known for its beaches and for limestone cliffs that attract rock climbers.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baiyoke Tower II
tokens.description: Baiyoke Tower II is an 88-story, 309 m hotel skyscraper in the Ratchathewi district of Bangkok, Thailand. It is the tallest hotel in Southeast Asia and has a public observatory and a revolving roof deck.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: MBK Center
tokens.description: MBK Center is a large shopping mall in the Siam area of Bangkok, Thailand. At eight storeys it contains around 2,000 shops, restaurants and service outlets.
tokens.image_credit: กสิณธร ราชโอรส · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siam Paragon
tokens.description: Siam Paragon is a shopping mall in Bangkok, Thailand, located in front of Siam BTS station. It is one of the largest malls in Thailand and includes a multiplex cinema and the Sea Life Bangkok Ocean World aquarium.
tokens.image_credit: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images, but please mention me as the author and may send me a message. (สามารถใช้ภาพได้อิสระ แต่กรุณาใส่เครดิตผู้ถ่ายและอาจส่งข · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ben Thanh Market
tokens.description: Ben Thanh Market is a covered market in District 1 of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It is one of the earliest surviving structures in the city and a well known destination for visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
tokens.description: Hoan Kiem Lake is a freshwater lake of about 12 hectares in the historic centre of Hanoi, Vietnam. Also called Sword Lake, it is one of the main scenic spots and public gathering places of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Bem photography: · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mui Ne
tokens.description: Mui Ne is a coastal fishing ward of Lam Dong Province, Vietnam, with about 25,000 residents. Since the mid-1990s its coast, stretching about 50 km with Phan Thiet, has developed into a resort destination.

tokens.name: Nha Trang
tokens.description: Nha Trang is a ward of Khanh Hoa province, Vietnam, one of the 65 new wards, communes and special zones formed by the 2025 reorganisation of the province. The ward forms part of the coastal city of Nha Trang.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Lewis · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Phu Quoc
tokens.description: Phu Quoc is the largest island of Vietnam and a special zone of An Giang province. The island has a total area of 575 square km and about 179,480 permanent residents in 2020.
tokens.image_credit: [//commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:Trantuonglam Trantuonglam] · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Da Lat
tokens.description: Da Lat is a former city and the former capital of Lam Dong Province, Vietnam, and the largest city of the Central Highlands. It lies about 1,500 m above sea level on the Langbiang Plateau and ceased to exist as a municipal city on 1 July 2025.
tokens.image_credit: qiv · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bukit Bintang
tokens.description: Bukit Bintang is the shopping and entertainment district of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, centred on Jalan Bukit Bintang. It is the city's most prominent retail belt, with many shopping centres, cafes, bars and night markets.
tokens.image_credit: Patrice78500 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Perhentian Islands
tokens.description: The Perhentian Islands are a group of islands off the coast of Besut District, Terengganu, Malaysia. The two main islands are Perhentian Besar and Perhentian Kecil.

tokens.name: Genting Highlands
tokens.description: Genting Highlands is a hill station and integrated resort on Mount Ulu Kali in the Titiwangsa Mountains, about an hour's drive from Kuala Lumpur. The resort was established in 1965 by Lim Goh Tong.
tokens.image_credit: Chongkian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Putrajaya
tokens.description: Putrajaya is the administrative centre of Malaysia, to which the federal government moved from Kuala Lumpur in 1999. Kuala Lumpur remains the constitutional national capital.
tokens.image_credit: Muhammad Faqih · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jalan Alor
tokens.description: Jalan Alor is a street in the Bukit Bintang district of Kuala Lumpur, known for its open-air night food stalls. It is lined with hawker stalls and restaurants serving grilled seafood, satay and other Chinese Malaysian dishes.

tokens.name: Bali
tokens.title: Island of the Gods
tokens.description: Bali is an Indonesian island and province, the westernmost of the Lesser Sunda Islands, east of Java and west of Lombok. The provincial capital is Denpasar.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kuta, Bali
tokens.description: Kuta is a tourist area and urban village in Kuta District, Badung Regency, southern Bali, part of the Denpasar metropolitan area. Originally a fishing village, it became one of the first Balinese towns to see substantial tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Simon_sees from Australia · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ubud
tokens.description: Ubud is a town in Gianyar Regency, Bali, promoted as an arts and culture centre. It has developed a large tourism industry.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gili Islands
tokens.description: The Gili Islands are three small islands, Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno and Gili Air, just off the northwest coast of Lombok, Indonesia. Together they form an administrative village in North Lombok Regency.
tokens.image_credit: Kok Leng Yeo from Singapore, Singapore · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nusa Penida
tokens.description: Nusa Penida is an island near southeastern Bali, forming a district of the same name in Klungkung Regency. The Badung Strait separates it from Bali, and its hilly interior rises to 524 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Chainwit. · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Indonesia
tokens.description: Grand Indonesia is an integrated shopping mall complex on Thamrin Road in Central Jakarta, Indonesia. The Wikipedia intro describes it as the 4th largest mall in Indonesia.
tokens.image_credit: Baqotun0023 · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jalan Malioboro
tokens.description: Jalan Malioboro is a major shopping street in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, on the north-south line between the Yogyakarta Kraton and Mount Merapi. The name is also used for the surrounding neighbourhood.
tokens.image_credit: Gunawan Kartapranata · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Siargao
tokens.description: Siargao is a teardrop-shaped island in the Philippine Sea, about 196 km southeast of Tacloban. It has a land area of approximately 437 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Rizal Park
tokens.description: Rizal Park, also called Luneta, is a historic urban park in Ermita, Manila, Philippines. At 58 hectares it is one of the largest urban parks in the country.
tokens.image_credit: Maynard Rabanal (Greedyplus) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Makati
tokens.description: Makati is a highly urbanized city in the National Capital Region of the Philippines. It is the country's leading centre for finance, commerce and diplomacy, with the largest skyline in the country.
tokens.image_credit: patrickroque01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Koh Rong
tokens.description: Koh Rong is an island in Preah Sihanouk province, Cambodia, and the second largest island of the country. It is one of the islands within the Koh Rong Marine National Park.

tokens.name: Sihanoukville
tokens.description: Sihanoukville is a coastal port city in Cambodia and the capital of Preah Sihanouk Province, on the Gulf of Thailand. The city has a string of beaches along its coastline.

tokens.name: Vang Vieng
tokens.description: Vang Vieng is a city in Vientiane Province, Laos, on the Nam Song River about 130 km north of Vientiane. It is popular with backpackers for adventure sports and its karst topography.

tokens.name: Si Phan Don
tokens.description: Si Phan Don, meaning 4,000 islands, is a riverine archipelago in the Mekong River in Champasak Province, southern Laos. Many of its islands are half submerged when the river is in flood.

tokens.name: Ngapali Beach
tokens.description: Ngapali Beach is a coastal beach in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, about 7 km from the town of Thandwe. It is considered Myanmar's premier beach destination.
tokens.image_credit: Go-Myanmar.com · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mandalay Hill
tokens.description: Mandalay Hill is a hill with an elevation of 240 m, northeast of the city centre of Mandalay in Myanmar. The city took its name from the hill.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Fussan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thamel
tokens.description: Thamel is a commercial neighborhood in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. It has been the centre of the tourist industry in Kathmandu for over four decades.
tokens.image_credit: Saddam Hussain Ansari · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pokhara
tokens.description: Pokhara is a metropolitan city in central Nepal and the capital of Gandaki Province. It is the second largest city in Nepal after Kathmandu, with 600,051 inhabitants at the 2021 census, on the shore of Phewa Lake.
tokens.image_credit: Utsab Raj Giri · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Annapurna Circuit
tokens.description: The Annapurna Circuit is a trek within the mountain ranges of central Nepal. Its length is 160 to 230 km, depending on where motor transport is used, and it encircles the Annapurna Massif.

tokens.name: Everest base camps
tokens.description: There are two base camps on Mount Everest, on opposite sides of the mountain. South Base Camp in Nepal is at 5,364 m, and North Base Camp in Tibet is at 5,150 m.
tokens.image_credit: Nirojsedhai · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Thimphu
tokens.description: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan, in the western central part of the country. It replaced Punakha as the capital in 1955, and was officially declared the capital in 1961.

tokens.name: Marine Drive, Mumbai
tokens.description: Marine Drive is a 3-kilometre promenade along the coast of a natural bay in Mumbai, India. Built in 1940 by Pallonji Mistry, it is also known as the Queen's Necklace.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Juhu Beach
tokens.description: Juhu Beach lies on the western coast of Salsette Island, on the Arabian Sea in Mumbai, India. It is the best known feature of Juhu, a coastal suburb of Mumbai.

tokens.name: Dharavi
tokens.description: Dharavi is a residential area in Mumbai, India, often considered one of the world's largest slums. It covers just over 2.39 square kilometres and has a population of about one million.
tokens.image_credit: YGLvoices · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Film City, Mumbai
tokens.description: Film City, officially Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari, is an integrated film studio complex in Goregaon East, Mumbai, India. The Maharashtra State Government established it in 1977 to serve the film industry.

tokens.name: Chandni Chowk
tokens.description: Chandni Chowk is one of the oldest and busiest markets in Delhi, located in Old Delhi, India. It was built in 1650 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and the Red Fort straddles its eastern fringe.

tokens.name: Connaught Place, New Delhi
tokens.description: Connaught Place, also known as Rajiv Chowk, is one of the main financial, commercial and business centres in New Delhi, India. It is a major shopping, nightlife and tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Kabi1990 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
tokens.description: Rashtrapati Bhavan is the official residence of the President of India, at the western end of Rajpath on Raisina Hill in New Delhi. Designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker, it was built from 1912 to 1929.
tokens.image_credit: This image was produced by me, David Castor (user:dcastor). The pictures I submit to the Wikipedia Project are released to the public domain. This gives you the right to use them in any way you like,  · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Goa
tokens.description: Goa is a state on the southwestern coast of India, within the Konkan region. It is bordered by Maharashtra and Karnataka, with the Arabian Sea forming its western coastline.

tokens.name: Calangute
tokens.description: Calangute is a town in North Goa, India, known for its long beach, the largest in North Goa. It is a popular tourist destination with peak seasons at Christmas, New Year and in May.

tokens.name: Kovalam
tokens.description: Kovalam is a beach and seaside resort in the city of Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala, India. Its beaches are popular with domestic and international travellers.
tokens.image_credit: Georgeumartin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Munnar
tokens.description: Munnar is a town in the Idukki district of Kerala, India, at about 1,600 metres in the Western Ghats. It is a former plantation settlement dominated by tea and a growing hill station.
tokens.image_credit: Kondephy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Darjeeling
tokens.title: Champagne of teas
tokens.description: Darjeeling is a city in the northernmost region of West Bengal, India, in the Eastern Himalayas, at an average elevation of 2,045 metres. It lies near Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim and the Tibet Autonomous Region.
tokens.image_credit: Users Darkone, MichaelJanich, Hph on de.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shimla
tokens.description: Shimla is the summer capital and largest city of the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. It is the state's main centre of commerce, culture and education, built across seven spurs in the Himalayas during Company rule.
tokens.image_credit: UnpetitproleX · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manali, Himachal Pradesh
tokens.description: Manali is a resort town in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh, India, at the northern end of the Kullu Valley formed by the Beas River. It lies about 270 km north of the state capital Shimla.
tokens.image_credit: Rishabh gaur · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rishikesh
tokens.description: Rishikesh is a municipal corporation and pilgrimage town in the Dehradun district of Uttarakhand, India, on the right bank of the Ganges. It is known for its many temples and ashrams along the river.
tokens.image_credit: Tylersundance · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haridwar
tokens.description: Haridwar is a city and municipal corporation in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand, India. At 228,832 residents in the 2011 census, it is the second-largest city in the state.
tokens.image_credit: Livefree2013 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ladakh
tokens.description: Ladakh is a region of northern India, administered as a union territory, forming the eastern part of the wider Kashmir region. It stretches from the Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram range to the main Great Himalayas.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Leh Palace
tokens.description: Leh Palace is a former royal palace overlooking the city of Leh in Ladakh, India. It was built around 1600 by Sengge Namgyal and abandoned in the mid-19th century after Dogra forces took control of Ladakh.
tokens.image_credit: KennyOMG · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gulmarg
tokens.description: Gulmarg is a hill station and notified area in Baramulla district of Indian-administered Kashmir, in the Pir Panjal Range of the Western Himalayas. It is a ski resort and the base of the Indian Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering.

tokens.name: Ramoji Film City
tokens.description: Ramoji Film City is an integrated film studio complex on the outskirts of Hyderabad, India. Established in 1996 by Ramoji Rao, it covers about 2,000 acres and was recognised by Guinness World Records in 2005 as the world's largest film studio complex.

tokens.name: Marina Beach
tokens.description: Marina Beach is a natural urban beach in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, along the Bay of Bengal. It runs about 6 km from near Fort St. George to Foreshore Estate and is a prominent landmark of the city.
tokens.image_credit: This Image was created by User:PlaneMad. If you are using the image under the creative commons share alike license please credit the photo CC-by-sa PlaneMad/Wikimedia and include a link to this page.  · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pondicherry
tokens.description: Pondicherry, officially known as Puducherry, is the capital and most populous city of the Union Territory of Puducherry. It lies on the southeast coast of India, on the Bay of Bengal.
tokens.image_credit: B-Pro 9 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Auroville
tokens.description: Auroville is an experimental township in Viluppuram district, mostly in Tamil Nadu, India, with parts in the Union Territory of Puducherry. It was founded in 1968 by Mirra Alfassa, known as the Mother, and designed by architect Roger Anger.
tokens.image_credit: Kaspar Konrad · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
tokens.description: Dakshineswar Kali Temple is a Hindu navaratna-style temple on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River in Dakshineswar, Kolkata, West Bengal. Built in 1855 by Rani Rashmoni, it is dedicated to Kali in the form of Bhavatarini.
tokens.image_credit: Knath · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
tokens.description: The Taj Mahal Palace is a heritage five-star hotel at Apollo Bunder in Colaba, Mumbai, next to the Gateway of India. It opened in 1903 as the Taj Mahal Hotel and was built in the Indo-Saracenic style.
tokens.image_credit: Joe Ravi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nine Arch Bridge
tokens.description: The Nine Arch Bridge is a colonial-era railway viaduct in Sri Lanka near Ella, also called the Bridge in the Sky. It was designed for a nine-degree curve and a steep gradient.
tokens.image_credit: MichaelJames2468 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maafushi, Kaafu Atoll
tokens.description: Maafushi is one of the inhabited islands of Kaafu Atoll in the Maldives. Its proximity to Male and its transport hubs has made it a popular base for tourists visiting local islands.

tokens.name: Fairy Meadows
tokens.description: Fairy Meadows, locally known as Joot, is a grassland near a Nanga Parbat base camp in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. It is the launch point for climbers on the Rakhiot face and was declared a National Park in 1995.
tokens.image_credit: M.Awais · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chitral
tokens.description: Chitral is a town on the Chitral River in the northern part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It is the capital of Lower Chitral District.
tokens.image_credit: Fassifarooq · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sa Pa
tokens.description: Sa Pa is a ward of Lào Cai Province in northwest Vietnam. Before July 2025 it was a frontier township and the capital of the former Sa Pa District.
tokens.image_credit: Bùi Thụy Đào Nguyên · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lotus Tower
tokens.description: The Lotus Tower is a 351.5 metre tower in Colombo, Sri Lanka, and a symbolic landmark of the country. As of 2019 it was the tallest self-supported structure in South Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Mohamed Rilwan1210 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carlton Centre
tokens.description: The Carlton Centre is a 50-storey skyscraper and shopping centre on Commissioner Street in central Johannesburg, South Africa. At 223 metres it was the tallest building in Africa from its completion in 1973 until 2019.
tokens.image_credit: Thuvack · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sandton City
tokens.title: Africa's richest square mile
tokens.description: Sandton City is a large shopping centre in Sandton, Gauteng, South Africa. It opened on 12 September 1973 and has about 128,000 square metres of retail space.

tokens.name: Nelson Mandela Square
tokens.description: Nelson Mandela Square is a shopping centre in Sandton, Johannesburg, South Africa, built around a large open square styled on a European town square. It was named after Nelson Mandela in 2004.
tokens.image_credit: Britfan97 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gold Reef City
tokens.description: Gold Reef City is an amusement park in Johannesburg, South Africa, built on an old gold mine that closed in 1971. The park is themed on the Witwatersrand gold rush of 1886.
tokens.image_credit: CMallwitz (talk) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soweto
tokens.description: Soweto is a township and suburb of Johannesburg, South Africa, whose name is short for South Western Townships. It was incorporated into the City of Johannesburg in 2002.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Denne from Hobart, Australia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vilakazi Street
tokens.description: Vilakazi Street is a street in Orlando West, Soweto, South Africa, named after the poet Benedict Wallet Vilakazi. It is known as the home of Nobel Peace Prize laureates Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu.

tokens.name: Apartheid Museum
tokens.description: The Apartheid Museum is a museum in Johannesburg, South Africa, illustrating apartheid and the 20th-century history of the country. It opened in November 2001 as part of the Gold Reef City complex.

tokens.name: V&A Waterfront
tokens.description: The V&A Waterfront is a mixed-use suburb in Cape Town, South Africa, with a major shopping mall, a marina, hotels and apartments. It sits on the site of the oldest working harbour in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: Andreas Tusche · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boulders Beach
tokens.description: Sheltered beach made of inlets between granite boulders, on the eastern side of the Cape Peninsula in Simon's Town, Cape Town. The name comes from the boulders that shape its coves.
tokens.image_credit: Octagon · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Camps Bay
tokens.description: Camps Bay is a small bay on the west coast of the Cape Peninsula, South Africa, after which the affluent Cape Town suburb is named. The suburb is one of 10 that form the city's Atlantic Seaboard.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew Massyn · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bo-Kaap
tokens.description: Bo-Kaap is an area of Cape Town on the slopes of Signal Hill, formerly known as the Malay Quarter. It is a historical centre of Cape Malay culture and a former racially segregated area.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Case · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
tokens.description: Botanical garden at the eastern foot of Table Mountain in Cape Town. It is one of 10 National Botanical Gardens run by SANBI, which together cover five of South Africa's six biomes.
tokens.image_credit: Discott · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stellenbosch
tokens.description: Town in the Western Cape about 50 km east of Cape Town, on the Eerste River at the foot of Stellenbosch Mountain. Founded in 1679 by Simon van der Stel, it is South Africa's second oldest town and is known for its oak trees and wine farms.
tokens.image_credit: Matthias Bethke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Franschhoek
tokens.description: Small town in the Western Cape about 75 km from Cape Town, and one of the oldest towns in South Africa. Its name is Afrikaans for French Corner, and it was formerly known as Oliphants hoek.
tokens.image_credit: Olga Ernst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Constantia, Cape Town
tokens.description: Affluent residential suburb in the Southern Suburbs of Cape Town, about 20 km south of the city centre. It lies at the foot of the Constantiaberg mountain and is one of the largest neighborhoods in Cape Town by area.
tokens.image_credit: De Zuid-Afrikaan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sun City, South Africa
tokens.title: South African resort city
tokens.description: Luxury resort and casino in the North West Province of South Africa, about 140 km northwest of Johannesburg. The complex borders the Pilanesberg National Park.
tokens.image_credit: South African Tourism from South Africa · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Knysna
tokens.description: Knysna is a coastal town of about 76,150 inhabitants (2019) in the Western Cape province of South Africa. It is one of the destinations in the Garden Route region.
tokens.image_credit: .prometheus. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hermanus
tokens.description: Hermanus is a town on the southern coast of the Western Cape province of South Africa. It is known for Southern Right whale watching during the southern winter to spring seasons.
tokens.image_credit: Olga Ernst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Table Bay
tokens.description: Table Bay is a natural bay on the Atlantic Ocean at the northern end of the Cape Peninsula, South Africa. Overlooked by Cape Town, it is dominated by the flat-topped Table Mountain, from which it takes its name.
tokens.image_credit: SkyPixels · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Johannesburg Zoo
tokens.description: The Johannesburg Zoo is a 55-hectare zoo in Johannesburg, South Africa. It houses about 2000 animals of 320 species and was established in 1904.

tokens.name: Swakopmund
tokens.description: Swakopmund is a city on the coast of western Namibia, about 352 km west of Windhoek. It is the capital of the Erongo administrative district and had 75,921 inhabitants in 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Olga Ernst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nungwi
tokens.description: Nungwi is a large village at the far northern end of Zanzibar island, Tanzania. With 30,762 inhabitants (2022 census) it is the second largest settlement on the island.
tokens.image_credit: Sansibar-freundeskreis.de · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mafia Island
tokens.description: Mafia Island, also called Chole Shamba, is an island of the Mafia Archipelago in the Pwani Region of Tanzania. It is the third largest island in Tanzanian ocean territory and forms the largest part of Mafia District.

tokens.name: Diani Beach
tokens.description: Diani Beach is a beach on the Indian Ocean coast of Kenya, in Kwale County. It lies about 30 kilometres south of Mombasa.

tokens.name: Giraffe Centre
tokens.description: The Giraffe Centre is a wildlife conservation facility in Lang'ata, about 20 kilometres from central Nairobi, Kenya. It was established to protect the vulnerable Rothschild's giraffe.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Hdahlmo~commonswiki assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mombasa Old Town
tokens.description: Mombasa Old Town is the historic quarter of Mombasa, Kenya, covering 72 hectares on the south-east side of Mombasa Island. It is inhabited by a mix of Swahili, Arab, Persian, Indian, Portuguese and British settlers.
tokens.image_credit: FredD · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ripon Falls
tokens.title: Jinja cable-stayed bridge
tokens.description: Ripon Falls were waterfalls on the northern shore of Lake Victoria near Jinja, Uganda, where the lake drained into the Victoria Nile. They were long regarded as the traditional source of the Nile and were submerged after the Owen Falls Dam was built.
tokens.image_credit: Andyessex · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
tokens.description: The Kigali Genocide Memorial commemorates the 1994 Rwandan genocide and holds the remains of over 250,000 people. It is one of the genocide memorial sites inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage serial property in 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Jim Joel · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Kivu
tokens.description: Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes, on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda. It lies in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift.

tokens.name: Addis Mercato
tokens.description: Addis Mercato, known as Merkato, is a large open-air marketplace in the Addis Ketema district of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The name also refers to the neighbourhood in which it is located.
tokens.image_credit: JanManu · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Retba
tokens.description: Lake Retba, also known as Lac Rose, lies north of the Cape Verde peninsula in Senegal, about 35 km north-east of Dakar. Its pink colour comes from Dunaliella salina algae, and its water has a very high salt content.
tokens.image_credit: Arnault · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: African Renaissance Monument
tokens.description: The African Renaissance Monument is a 50-metre bronze statue on the Collines des Mamelles hill overlooking the Atlantic in Ouakam, outside Dakar. It was designed by Pierre Goudiaby Atepa and built by the North Korean firm Mansudae Overseas Projects.
tokens.image_credit: Richard N Horne · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saloum Delta
tokens.description: Saloum Delta, also called Sine-Saloum Delta, is a river delta in Senegal where the Saloum River meets the North Atlantic Ocean. It covers about 180,000 hectares and extends 72.5 km along the coast.

tokens.name: Majorelle Garden
tokens.description: The Majorelle Garden is a one-hectare botanical and artist's landscape garden in Marrakesh, Morocco. The French Orientalist painter Jacques Majorelle created it from 1923 over almost forty years, and it includes a Cubist villa.
tokens.image_credit: Viault · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahia Palace
tokens.description: The Bahia Palace is a palace in Marrakesh, Morocco, begun in the 1860s by Si Musa, grand vizier under the Alawi sultan Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman. It was expanded between 1894 and 1900 by his son Si Ba Ahmed ibn Musa.
tokens.image_credit: Val Traveler · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kutubiyya Mosque
tokens.description: The Kutubiyya Mosque, also spelled Koutoubia, is the largest mosque in Marrakesh, Morocco. It was founded in 1147 by the Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min after he conquered Marrakesh from the Almoravids.
tokens.image_credit: Baca12 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Essaouira
tokens.description: Essaouira, known until the 1960s as Mogador, is a port city on the Atlantic coast of western Morocco. Its medina was founded in 1760 under the Alawi sultan Mohammed bin Abdallah and was inscribed by UNESCO in 2001.
tokens.image_credit: Kayaky · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Merzouga
tokens.description: Merzouga is a village in Errachidia Province, Drâa-Tafilalet, Morocco. It lies near the Erg Chebbi dunes, which are among the tallest in the Sahara and draw many tourists to the region.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ouzoud Falls
tokens.description: Ouzoud Falls is a group of waterfalls in Azilal Province, Morocco, where the El-Abid River drops into a gorge. It is a popular tourist destination about 150 km from Marrakesh.
tokens.image_credit: Alexander Leisser · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Agadir
tokens.description: Agadir is a major city on the Atlantic coast of southwestern Morocco, near the foot of the Atlas Mountains. It is the capital of the Agadir-Ida Ou Tanane Prefecture and of the Souss-Massa economic region.
tokens.image_credit: Marco Riss · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tangier
tokens.description: Tangier is a city in northwestern Morocco, on the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean. It is the capital of the Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima region and of the Tangier-Assilah Prefecture.
tokens.image_credit: Mike McBey · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atlas Corporation Studios
tokens.description: Atlas Corporation Studios is a film studio 5 km west of Ouarzazate in Morocco. Many film sets remain in place in the nearby desert and mountains, and the studio runs guided tours.

tokens.name: Sidi Bou Said
tokens.description: Sidi Bou Said is a town in northern Tunisia, about 20 km northeast of Tunis, known for its blue-and-white architecture. The village was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in July 2026.
tokens.image_credit: Habib M'henni · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Matmata, Tunisia
tokens.description: Matmata is a small Berber-speaking town in southern Tunisia. Some of its residents live in traditional underground troglodyte dwellings.

tokens.name: Djerba
tokens.description: Djerba is a Tunisian island in the Gulf of Gabes, the largest island of North Africa at 514 square kilometres. Its island settlement pattern was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2023.

tokens.name: Tozeur
tokens.description: Tozeur is a city in southwest Tunisia and the capital of Tozeur Governorate. It is located northwest of Chott el Djerid.
tokens.image_credit: BishkekRocks · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chott el Djerid
tokens.description: Chott el Djerid is a large endorheic salt lake in central Tunisia. Its name can be translated from Arabic as Lagoon of the Land of Palms.

tokens.name: Timgad
tokens.description: Timgad is a Roman city in the Aures Mountains of Algeria, founded by Emperor Trajan around 100 CE. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, nicknamed the Pompeii of North Africa.
tokens.image_credit: Dan Sloan · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ghardaïa
tokens.description: Ghardaïa is the capital city of Ghardaïa Province in northern-central Algeria, on the left bank of the Wadi Mzab. It is one of the five fortified ksour of the M'Zab Valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
tokens.image_credit: Addounya (original uploader at en.wikipedia) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coptic Cairo
tokens.description: Coptic Cairo is a part of Old Cairo that encompasses the Babylon Fortress, the Coptic Museum, the Hanging Church and the Greek Church of St George. It contains many other Coptic churches and historical sites.

tokens.name: Wadi El Rayan
tokens.description: Wadi El Rayan is a nature protectorate in Faiyum Governorate, Egypt. It is supervised by the Ministry of Environmental Affairs (EEAA).

tokens.name: Lekki
tokens.description: Lekki is a city in Lagos State, Nigeria, southeast of Lagos city proper. It is a naturally formed peninsula bordered by the Atlantic Ocean, the Lagos Lagoon and the Lekki Lagoon.

tokens.name: Tarkwa Bay Beach
tokens.description: Tarkwa Bay Beach is an artificial sheltered beach near Lagos harbour in Nigeria. It is reachable only by boat or water taxi and is popular with swimmers and water-sports enthusiasts.

tokens.name: Nike Art Gallery
tokens.description: The Nike Art Gallery is described as West Africa's most extensive art collection. Its biggest and most famous branch is in the Lekki district of Lagos, Nigeria.
tokens.image_credit: FrankvEck · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Olumo Rock
tokens.description: Olumo Rock is a large rock formation in the city of Abeokuta, Ogun State, south-western Nigeria. It was used as a natural fortress during 19th-century inter-tribal wars, and its patron spirit is venerated in the Yoruba religion.
tokens.image_credit: F.Samuel95 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yankari Game Reserve
tokens.description: Yankari Game Reserve is a large wildlife reserve of about 2,244 square kilometres in Bauchi State, north-eastern Nigeria. It has several natural warm water springs and a wide variety of flora and fauna.

tokens.name: Zuma Rock
tokens.description: Zuma Rock is a large monolith, an inselberg of gabbro and granodiorite, near Madalla in Niger State, Nigeria. It rises about 725 metres above sea level on the road from Abuja to Kaduna.
tokens.image_credit: Jeff Attaway · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aso Rock
tokens.description: Aso Rock is a large granitic monolith on the outskirts of Abuja, the capital of Nigeria. It rises 936 metres above sea level and is one of the city's most noticeable features.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Fischer · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cape Coast Castle
tokens.description: Cape Coast Castle is one of the large commercial forts built on the Gold Coast in Ghana by European traders, and was a centre of the transatlantic slave trade. It is part of the UNESCO serial site Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions.
tokens.image_credit: Rjruiziii · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Black Star Square
tokens.description: Black Star Square, also known as Independence Square, is a public square in Accra, Ghana. It is the site of the annual independence celebrations and of civic and military parades and national gatherings.
tokens.image_credit: Rjruiziii · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kakum National Park
tokens.description: Kakum National Park is a tropical rainforest reserve in Ghana's Central Region, covering 375 square kilometres. It was established as a reserve in 1931 and gazetted as a national park in 1992.
tokens.image_credit: Afus199620 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mole National Park
tokens.description: Mole National Park is Ghana's largest wildlife refuge, in the Savannah Region about 24 km from Damongo. It is one of Ghana's seven national parks.

tokens.name: Lake Volta
tokens.description: Lake Volta is the largest artificial reservoir in the world by surface area, covering 8,502 square kilometres. It lies entirely within Ghana, behind the Akosombo Dam.

tokens.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
tokens.description: The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and Mausoleum is in downtown Accra, the capital of Ghana. The mausoleum holds the remains of the first president, Kwame Nkrumah, and his wife Fathia Nkrumah.
tokens.image_credit: Erik B. Anderson · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand-Bassam
tokens.description: Grand-Bassam is a town in southeastern Ivory Coast, east of Abidjan, and was briefly the French colonial capital in the late 19th century. Its historic town was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.

tokens.name: Pointe-Noire
tokens.description: Pointe-Noire is the second largest city of the Republic of the Congo and its main economic centre, with 1,420,612 inhabitants in 2023. It sits on a headland between Pointe-Noire Bay and the Atlantic Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: user:unsonique · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tofo
tokens.description: Tofo is a small town on the Indian Ocean coast of southeastern Mozambique, on the Barra Beach peninsula in Inhambane Province. It lies about 22 km by road from Inhambane city.

tokens.name: Liwonde National Park
tokens.description: Liwonde National Park is a national park in southern Malawi, near the Mozambique border, established in 1973. It has been managed by the conservation organisation African Parks since 2015.

tokens.name: Kafue National Park
tokens.description: Kafue National Park is the largest national park in Zambia, covering about 22,400 square kilometres. It is the second largest national park in Africa.

tokens.name: Livingstone, Zambia
tokens.description: Livingstone is a city in Southern Province, Zambia, lying about 10 km north of the Zambezi River. It is a tourist gateway to Victoria Falls, with a population of 177,393 at the 2022 census.

tokens.name: Ranomafana National Park
tokens.description: Ranomafana National Park is a national park in southeastern Madagascar, established in 1991. It is one of six parks in the UNESCO World Heritage property Rainforests of the Atsinanana.

tokens.name: Nosy Be
tokens.description: Nosy Be is a volcanic island off the northwest coast of Madagascar, with an area of about 320 square kilometres. It is the largest and busiest tourist destination in Madagascar.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isalo National Park
tokens.description: Isalo National Park is a national park in the Ihorombe Region of southwestern Madagascar. Its sandstone landscape has been eroded into plateaus, outcrops and canyons up to 200 metres deep.

tokens.name: Nosy Boraha
tokens.description: Nosy Boraha, also known as Sainte-Marie, is an island off the east coast of Madagascar covering about 222 square kilometres. It forms an administrative district within Analanjirofo Region.

tokens.name: Le Morne Brabant
tokens.description: Le Morne Brabant is a peninsula at the southwestern tip of Mauritius, dominated by a basaltic monolith 556 metres high. The Le Morne Cultural Landscape, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008, recalls its history as a refuge for runaway slaves.
tokens.image_credit: "dronepicr" · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seven Coloured Earths
tokens.description: The Seven Coloured Earths are sand dunes of seven distinct colours on the Chamarel plain in south-western Mauritius. The differently coloured sands settled in layers, giving the dunes a striped appearance.
tokens.image_credit: "dronepicr" · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Baie
tokens.description: Grand Baie is a coastal village in Mauritius, located mainly in the Rivière du Rempart District. The village is administered by the Grand Baie Village Council.

tokens.name: Anse Source d'Argent
tokens.description: Anse Source d'Argent is a beach on the southwest coast of La Digue in Seychelles. It is listed by Lonely Planet as one of the world's best beaches in 2024.

tokens.name: La Digue
tokens.description: La Digue is the third most populated island of the Seychelles, with about 2,800 inhabitants. It lies east of Praslin and is the fourth largest granitic island of the archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Praslin
tokens.description: Praslin is the second largest island of the Inner Seychelles, lying 44 km northeast of Mahé. It has around 7,533 inhabitants, mainly in Baie Sainte Anne, Anse Volbert and Grand' Anse.

tokens.name: Mahé
tokens.description: Mahé is the largest island of Seychelles, with an area of 157.3 square kilometres. It contains the capital Victoria and about 86% of the country's population.

tokens.name: Pico do Fogo
tokens.description: Pico do Fogo is an active stratovolcano on Fogo island in Cape Verde, rising to 2,829 metres. Its main cone last erupted in 1680, and a subsidiary vent erupted in 1995.
tokens.image_credit: Cayambe · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sal, Cape Verde
tokens.description: Sal is an island in the Cape Verde archipelago in the central Atlantic Ocean, about 560 km off the west coast of Africa. It is known for white sand beaches and as a major tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Martikkk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Maria, Cape Verde
tokens.description: Santa Maria is a city in the southern part of the island municipality of Sal in Cape Verde. It lies on the south coast, about 16 km south of Amílcar Cabral International Airport.

tokens.name: Medina of Marrakesh
tokens.description: The Medina of Marrakesh is the walled old city of Marrakesh in Morocco, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. The medina was founded by the Almoravids in 1070 to 1072.

tokens.name: Sydney Tower
tokens.description: Sydney Tower is an observation and telecommunications tower on Market Street in the Sydney central business district. It stands 309 m above the city and is the tallest structure in Sydney.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Olszewski · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manly Beach
tokens.description: Manly Beach is a beach among the Northern Beaches of Sydney, Australia. Its three main sections are Queenscliff, North Steyne and South Steyne.

tokens.name: The Rocks, New South Wales
tokens.description: The Rocks is a suburb, tourist precinct and historic area of Sydney's city centre. It lies in New South Wales, Australia.
tokens.image_credit: Sardaka · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Darling Harbour
tokens.description: Darling Harbour is a harbour and neighbourhood adjacent to the city centre of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. It is a large recreational, retail and entertainment precinct with pedestrianised public spaces.
tokens.image_credit: Dicklyon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Taronga Zoo
tokens.description: Taronga Zoo is a government-run public zoo in the Lower North Shore suburb of Mosman, on the shores of Sydney Harbour. It has views of the harbour and the city.

tokens.name: Royal Botanic Garden, Sydney
tokens.description: The Royal Botanic Garden is a 30-hectare botanical garden at Farm Cove on the eastern fringe of Sydney's central business district. Opened in 1816, it is the oldest scientific institution in Australia.
tokens.image_credit: Harveychl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Luna Park Sydney
tokens.description: Luna Park Sydney is a heritage-listed amusement park in Milsons Point on the northern shore of Sydney Harbour, Australia. It has been a filming location for several movies and television shows.
tokens.image_credit: Tamgarat · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Queen Victoria Building
tokens.description: The Queen Victoria Building is a heritage-listed Romanesque Revival building on George Street in the Sydney central business district. Designed by George McRae, it was built between 1893 and 1898.
tokens.image_credit: Sardaka (talk) 08:15, 26 November 2010 (UTC) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue Mountains, New South Wales
tokens.description: The Blue Mountains are a mountainous region and mountain range in New South Wales, Australia, on the western outskirts of Greater Sydney. They are part of the UNESCO-listed Greater Blue Mountains Area.

tokens.name: Hunter Valley
tokens.description: The Hunter Valley is a region of central-eastern New South Wales, Australia, containing the Hunter River and its tributaries. It is most commonly known for its wineries and coal industry.

tokens.name: Byron Bay
tokens.description: Byron Bay is a beachside town in the far north-eastern corner of New South Wales, Australia. Cape Byron, the easternmost point of mainland Australia, is adjacent to the town.

tokens.name: Surfers Paradise
tokens.description: Surfers Paradise is a central suburb of the City of Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia. It is known for its many high-rise apartment buildings and a wide surf beach.
tokens.image_credit: chillmimi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Q1 Tower
tokens.description: Q1 Tower is a 322.5-metre residential skyscraper on the Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia. It is the tallest building in Australia and was the world's tallest residential building from 2005 to 2011.
tokens.image_credit: Jordan Gellie jordan_gellie · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sea World, Australia
tokens.description: Sea World is a marine mammal park, oceanarium and theme park on the Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia. It offers rides and animal exhibits and rescues and rehabilitates sick, injured or orphaned wildlife.
tokens.image_credit: Whats new? at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Whitsunday Islands
tokens.description: The Whitsunday Islands are 74 continental islands off the central coast of Queensland, Australia. Hamilton Island, the largest inhabited island of the group, is a popular year-round tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Jesse Allen · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cairns
tokens.description: Cairns is a city on the tropical northeast coast of Far North Queensland, Australia, with a population of 169,312 at the 2021 census. The city was founded in 1876 and named after Sir William Wellington Cairns.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eureka Tower
tokens.description: Eureka Tower is a 297.3-metre skyscraper in the Southbank precinct of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Construction began in August 2002 and the building was officially opened on 11 October 2006.
tokens.image_credit: Adam.J.W.C. · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Federation Square
tokens.description: Federation Square is a venue for arts, culture and public events on the edge of the Melbourne central business district, Victoria, Australia. It covers 3.2 hectares at the intersection of Flinders and Swanston Streets and houses the Ian Potter Centre and ACMI.
tokens.image_credit: DXR · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Queen Victoria Market
tokens.description: Queen Victoria Market is a public marketplace in the central business district of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Opened in 1878, it covers over seven hectares and is the largest open-air market in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: Bob T · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Exhibition Building
tokens.description: The Royal Exhibition Building is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed building in Carlton Gardens, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Built in 1879 to 1880 for international exhibitions, it is 150 metres long.
tokens.image_credit: Photograph taken by Diliff and straightened by Ian Fieggen · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Melbourne Zoo
tokens.description: Melbourne Zoo is a zoo located within Royal Park in Parkville, about 4 kilometres north of the centre of Melbourne, Australia. It is the primary zoo serving Melbourne.

tokens.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
tokens.description: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria runs botanic gardens on two sites, in the City of Melbourne and at Cranbourne, Victoria, Australia. The 38-hectare Melbourne Gardens, founded in 1846, display almost 50,000 plants.

tokens.name: Yarra Valley
tokens.description: The Yarra Valley is a region in Victoria, Australia, centred on the Yarra River. It is one of Australia's prominent wine-producing areas, stretching from the Yarra Ranges National Park towards Melbourne.

tokens.name: Phillip Island
tokens.title: Seaside MotoGP circuit
tokens.description: Phillip Island is an island about 125 km south-southeast of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. It is named after Governor Arthur Phillip and forms a natural breakwater for the shallow waters of Western Port.

tokens.name: The Twelve Apostles
tokens.description: The Twelve Apostles viewing platforms on the Great Ocean Road overlook limestone stacks off the shore of Port Campbell National Park in Victoria, Australia. Despite their name, there may never have been twelve rock stacks.
tokens.image_credit: Leonard Koh · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Barossa Valley
tokens.description: The Barossa Valley is a valley in South Australia, about 60 kilometres northeast of Adelaide. It is formed by the North Para River and is a major wine-producing region and tourist destination.

tokens.name: McLaren Vale
tokens.description: McLaren Vale is a wine region in South Australia, centred on the town of McLaren Vale about 38 km south of Adelaide. It is internationally renowned for its wines and is included in the Great Wine Capitals of the World.

tokens.name: Margaret River, Western Australia
tokens.description: Margaret River is a town in the South West region of Western Australia, in the Margaret River valley about 277 km south of Perth. Its coast to the west is a renowned surfing location with breaks such as Main Break and The Box.

tokens.name: Cable Beach
tokens.description: Cable Beach is a 22 km stretch of white sand beach on the eastern Indian Ocean, backed by low red ochre cliffs, in Broome, Western Australia. It was named after the telegraph cable laid between Broome and Java in 1889.

tokens.name: Bungle Bungle Range
tokens.description: The Bungle Bungle Range is a range of beehive-shaped sandstone karst domes and the main feature of Purnululu National Park in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. Purnululu was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage property in 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Bäras · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Litchfield National Park
tokens.description: Litchfield National Park covers about 1,500 km2 near the township of Batchelor, about 100 km south-west of Darwin in the Northern Territory of Australia. It was proclaimed a national park in 1986 and attracts over 329,000 visitors each year.

tokens.name: Wave Rock
tokens.description: Wave Rock is a natural rock formation in Western Australia, shaped like a tall breaking ocean wave about 15 m high and 110 m long. It forms the north side of a solitary hill known as Hyden Rock.
tokens.image_credit: Jonathan LaRocca from Houston, TX, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Pinnacles, Western Australia
tokens.description: The Pinnacles are thousands of weathered yellow limestone pillars within Nambung National Park, near the town of Cervantes in Western Australia. Some of the tallest reach about 3.5 m above the yellow sand.
tokens.image_credit: W. Bulach · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cradle Mountain
tokens.description: Cradle Mountain is a 1,545 metre mountain in the Central Highlands of Tasmania, Australia. It lies in Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park, part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salamanca Market
tokens.description: Salamanca Market is a street market held every Saturday at Salamanca Place in Hobart, Tasmania. It attracts over one million visitors a year and is among the most visited attractions in Tasmania.
tokens.image_credit: Nick carson at English Wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Museum of Old and New Art
tokens.description: The Museum of Old and New Art (MONA) is an art museum at the Moorilla winery on the Berriedale peninsula in Hobart, Tasmania. It is the largest privately funded museum in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: Barrylb · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parliament House, Canberra
tokens.description: Parliament House is the meeting place of the Parliament of Australia and houses the Australian Government executive in Canberra. It stands at the southern apex of the National Triangle, on Capital Hill.
tokens.image_credit: Thennicke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Australian War Memorial
tokens.description: The Australian War Memorial is a national war memorial, museum and archive in Campbell, a suburb of Canberra. It is dedicated to all Australians who have died as a result of war, including peacekeeping duties.
tokens.image_credit: Shkuru Afshar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Perisher Ski Resort
tokens.description: Perisher Ski Resort is the largest ski resort in the Southern Hemisphere, in the Australian Snowy Mountains of New South Wales. It combines four villages and their ski fields, covering about 12 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Thredbo
tokens.description: Thredbo is a village and ski resort in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales, Australia. It lies in the Thredbo River valley at the foot of the Ramshead Range, about 500 kilometres south of Sydney.

tokens.name: Waiheke Island
tokens.description: Waiheke Island is the second-largest island in the Hauraki Gulf of New Zealand, after Great Barrier Island. It has about 9,310 permanent residents, and its ferry terminal is 21.5 km from the central Auckland terminal.
tokens.image_credit: NASA image created by Jesse Allen, using Landsat data provided by the United States Geological Survey. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hobbiton Movie Set
tokens.title: Shire from Lord of the Rings
tokens.description: The Hobbiton Movie Set is a film set on a farm near Matamata in Waikato, New Zealand, built for The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit films. It is now a Tolkien tourism destination with guided tours.
tokens.image_credit: Jackie.lck (photos · photo sets) · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rotorua
tokens.description: Rotorua is a city on the southern shore of Lake Rotorua in the Bay of Plenty region of New Zealand's North Island. It is the seat of the Rotorua Lakes District and has about 58,500 residents.
tokens.image_credit: Schwede66 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
tokens.description: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing is a day tramping track across the volcanic terrain of Tongariro National Park on New Zealand's North Island. It passes the eastern base of Mount Ngauruhoe and the multi-cratered Mount Tongariro.
tokens.image_credit: Blueromulan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Ruapehu
tokens.description: Mount Ruapehu is an active stratovolcano at the southern end of the Taupo Volcanic Zone on New Zealand's North Island. It lies within Tongariro National Park and carries the North Island's major ski resorts and its only glaciers.
tokens.image_credit: Geoff McKay · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Te Papa
tokens.description: Te Papa, the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, is New Zealand's national museum in Wellington. It opened in 1998 after the merger of the National Museum of New Zealand and the National Art Gallery.
tokens.image_credit: Phillip Capper · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wētā Workshop
tokens.title: Miramar visual effects house
tokens.description: Wētā Workshop is a New Zealand creative studio and special effects house based in Miramar, Wellington. It is privately owned by Sir Richard Taylor and Tania Rodger and is independent of Wētā FX.

tokens.name: Abel Tasman National Park
tokens.description: Abel Tasman National Park is a national park at the north end of New Zealand's South Island. It covers 237.1 km2 between Golden Bay and Tasman Bay and is the smallest of New Zealand's national parks.

tokens.name: Franz Josef Glacier
tokens.description: The Franz Josef Glacier, known in Māori as Kā Roimata o Hine Hukatere, is a 12 km temperate maritime glacier descending from the Southern Alps on New Zealand's West Coast. It lies in Westland Tai Poutini National Park, part of the Te Wāhipounamu World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Hempel · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Tekapo
tokens.description: Lake Tekapo is the second-largest of three roughly parallel lakes on the northern edge of the Mackenzie Basin in New Zealand's South Island. It covers 83 km2 at an altitude of 710 m.

tokens.name: Lake Pukaki
tokens.description: Lake Pukaki is the largest of three roughly parallel alpine lakes on the northern edge of the Mackenzie Basin in New Zealand's South Island. The lake was formed when glacier moraines blocked its valley.
tokens.image_credit: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wānaka
tokens.description: Wānaka is a ski and summer resort town in the Otago region of New Zealand's South Island. It lies at the southern end of Lake Wānaka and is the gateway to Mount Aspiring National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cardrona Alpine Resort
tokens.description: Cardrona Alpine Resort is an alpine ski field in New Zealand's South Island, ranging from 1,260 m to 1,860 m in altitude. It is operated alongside Treble Cone Ski Field near Wānaka.

tokens.name: Coronet Peak
tokens.description: Coronet Peak is a commercial ski field near Queenstown in New Zealand's South Island, on the southern slopes of the 1,649 m peak that shares its name. It is a popular ski resort in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: André Richard Chalmers · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Central Otago wine region
tokens.description: The Central Otago wine region is a geographical indication in New Zealand's South Island and the world's southernmost commercial wine growing region. It is best known for Pinot Noir.

tokens.name: Marlborough wine region
tokens.description: The Marlborough wine region is New Zealand's largest, covering the Marlborough and Kaikōura Districts in the north-east of the South Island. In 2020 it accounted for three quarters of the country's wine production.

tokens.name: Hawke's Bay wine region
tokens.description: The Hawke's Bay wine region is New Zealand's oldest and second-largest wine-production region, on the east coast of the North Island. Production reached 41,000 tonnes in 2018, about 10.2% of the national total.

tokens.name: Cape Reinga
tokens.description: Cape Reinga is the northwestern tip of the Aupōuri Peninsula at the northern end of New Zealand's North Island. Its Māori name, Te Rerenga Wairua, means the leaping-off place of spirits.

tokens.name: Ninety Mile Beach, New Zealand
tokens.description: Ninety Mile Beach, New Zealand, is an 88 km beach on the western coast of the far north of the North Island. Its Māori name is Te Oneroa-a-Tōhē, and its southern end lies near Ahipara Bay, close to Kaitaia.

tokens.name: Rangitoto Island
tokens.description: Rangitoto Island is a volcanic island in the Hauraki Gulf near Auckland, New Zealand. It is the youngest and largest of the roughly 50 volcanoes of the Auckland volcanic field, erupting in two phases around 1450 and 1500 CE.
tokens.image_credit: Bruce Hayward · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nadi
tokens.description: Nadi is the third-largest city in Fiji, on the western side of Viti Levu, the main island. It had a population of 59,707 at the 2017 census.

tokens.name: Mamanuca Islands
tokens.description: The Mamanuca Islands are a volcanic archipelago of about 20 islands lying west of Nadi, in Fiji. They are a popular tourist destination known for their palm fringed beaches and live coral reefs.

tokens.name: Yasawa Islands
tokens.description: The Yasawa Islands are an archipelago of about 20 volcanic islands in the Western Division of Fiji, covering about 135 square kilometres in total. They lie north of the Mamanuca Islands.

tokens.name: Denarau Island
tokens.description: Denarau Island is a small private resort development on the western side of Viti Levu, Fiji, about 5 km northwest of Nadi. It is known for its hotels and the 18-hole Denarau Golf course.

tokens.name: Bora Bora
tokens.description: Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands of French Polynesia, in the South Pacific. Its main island is surrounded by a lagoon and a barrier reef, with a land area of about 30.55 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: NASA Johnson Space Center · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Moorea
tokens.description: Moorea is a volcanic island in French Polynesia, lying about 17 km northwest of Tahiti. It is one of the Windward Islands of the Society Islands archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: European Space Agency / CNES · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tahiti
tokens.description: Tahiti is the largest island of the Windward group of the Society Islands in French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of France. It is located in the central Pacific Ocean.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rangiroa
tokens.description: Rangiroa is the largest atoll in the Tuamotus in French Polynesia, and one of the largest atolls in the world. It is part of the Palliser group.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fakarava
tokens.description: Fakarava is an atoll in the western Tuamotu group of French Polynesia. It is the second largest of the Tuamotu atolls.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rarotonga
tokens.description: Rarotonga is the largest and most populous island of the Cook Islands. The volcanic island is home to Avarua, the capital of the Cook Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aitutaki
tokens.description: Aitutaki is the second most populous island of the Cook Islands, after Rarotonga. It is an almost atoll, with fifteen islets in a lagoon adjacent to the main island.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Champagne Beach
tokens.description: Champagne Beach is a beach on the island of Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu. It is known for its crystal clear water and powdery white sand, and is visited by tourists and cruise boats from Australia.

tokens.name: Port Vila
tokens.description: Port Vila is the capital and largest city of Vanuatu, on the island of Efate. The 2020 census counted 49,034 residents.
tokens.image_credit: Gérard Janot · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New Caledonian barrier reef
tokens.description: The New Caledonian barrier reef encircles Grande Terre and the Isle of Pines, with a length of about 1,500 kilometres. It is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: the Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus on NASA’s Landsat 7 satellite, Jesse Allen, Michon Scott. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isle of Pines, New Caledonia
tokens.description: The Isle of Pines is an island in the Pacific Ocean, in the South Province of New Caledonia. It is part of the commune of L'Ile-des-Pins and is nicknamed the island closest to paradise.

tokens.name: Nouméa
tokens.description: Nouméa is the capital and largest city of the French special collectivity of New Caledonia, on a peninsula in the south of Grande Terre. It is the largest Francophone city in Oceania.
tokens.image_credit: Balou46 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chuuk Lagoon
