tokens.description: Chuuk Lagoon is an atoll in the central Pacific Ocean, part of Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia. A protective reef about 225 kilometres around encloses a natural harbour.
tokens.image_credit: NASA and Time3000 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bikini Atoll
tokens.description: Bikini Atoll is a coral reef in the Marshall Islands, made up of 23 islands around a central lagoon of about 594 square kilometres. After the Second World War the United States used it as a nuclear weapon testing site. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kwajalein Atoll
tokens.description: Kwajalein Atoll is part of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, with Kwajalein Island as its southernmost and largest island. The atoll has a total land area of just over 16 square kilometres.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Two Lovers Point
tokens.description: Two Lovers Point is a cape and seaside cliff in Tamuning, Guam, overlooking northern Tumon Bay and the Philippine Sea. It is one of four National Natural Landmarks on Guam and is linked to a folktale of two doomed lovers.
tokens.image_credit: Gage Skidmore · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tumon Bay
tokens.description: Tumon Bay is a bay on the northwest coast of Guam, opening to the Philippine Sea between Two Lovers Point and Ypao Point. The entire bay lies within the Tumon Bay Marine Preserve, one of five marine preserves on Guam.

tokens.name: Kokoda Track
tokens.description: The Kokoda Track is a 96 km foot trail through the Owen Stanley Range in Papua New Guinea, from Owers' Corner to the village of Kokoda. It was the site of a 1942 World War II battle between Japanese and Allied forces.

tokens.name: Lake Kutubu
tokens.description: Lake Kutubu is the second-largest lake in Papua New Guinea and the largest upland body of water in the country, at about 800 m above sea level. It lies in the Southern Highlands Province, about 50 km southwest of Mendi.

tokens.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
tokens.description: Sugarloaf Mountain is a 396 m peak on a peninsula at the mouth of Guanabara Bay in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is known for its cable car and its panoramic views over the city and the bay.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Copacabana, Rio de Janeiro
tokens.title: Rio's famous beach
tokens.description: Copacabana is a neighbourhood in the South Zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It is known for its 4 km beach, which is one of the most famous in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Charles J. Sharp · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ipanema
tokens.description: Ipanema is a neighbourhood in the South Zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, between Leblon and Arpoador. Its beach became internationally known through the bossa nova song The Girl from Ipanema.

tokens.name: Escadaria Selarón
tokens.description: Escadaria Selarón is a set of steps in the Lapa neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, covered in colourful ceramic tiles. Created by Chilean-born artist Jorge Selarón, it is a world-famous tourist site.
tokens.image_credit: Donatas Dabravolskas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carioca Aqueduct
tokens.description: The Carioca Aqueduct, also known as Arcos da Lapa, is an 18th-century aqueduct in Rio de Janeiro that carried fresh water from the Carioca River to the city. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Marco Roberto Petri · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tijuca National Park
tokens.description: Tijuca National Park is an urban national park in the mountains of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Its forest is secondary vegetation from 19th-century reforestation, and it is a component of the UNESCO property Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea.

tokens.name: Historic Center of Salvador
tokens.description: The Historic Center of Salvador, also known as the Pelourinho, is a historic neighborhood in western Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. It was the city's center in the Portuguese colonial period and has many 17th to 19th century monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Matti Blume · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pipa Beach
tokens.description: Pipa Beach, or Praia de Pipa in Portuguese, is a famous village on the coast of Rio Grande do Norte state in north-east Brazil, near the city of Natal. It lies in the municipality of Tibau do Sul.

tokens.name: Porto de Galinhas
tokens.description: Porto de Galinhas is a beach town in the municipality of Ipojuca, Pernambuco, Brazil, and a major tourist destination. It is known for its bright-water beaches and natural reef pools.

tokens.name: Chapada Diamantina National Park
tokens.description: Chapada Diamantina National Park is a national park in the Chapada Diamantina region of Bahia state, Brazil. Its rugged terrain is mainly covered by the flora of the Caatinga biome.

tokens.name: Bonito, Mato Grosso do Sul
tokens.description: Bonito is a municipality in the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul, with a population of 22,190 as of 2020. Its area is 4,934 square kilometres.

tokens.name: Iguaçu National Park
tokens.description: Iguaçu National Park is a national park in Paraná State, Brazil, with a total area of 185,262.5 hectares. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

tokens.name: Paulista Avenue
tokens.description: Paulista Avenue is one of the most important avenues in São Paulo, Brazil. It stretches 2.8 kilometres and runs northwest to southeast across the city.
tokens.image_credit: ProtoplasmaKid · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ibirapuera Park
tokens.description: Ibirapuera Park is an urban park in São Paulo, Brazil. It covers 158 hectares (approx. 390 acres) in the city.
tokens.image_credit: Fernando Stankuns · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Edifício Copan
tokens.description: Edifício Copan is one of the most emblematic buildings in São Paulo, Brazil, designed by Oscar Niemeyer. It was inaugurated in 1966 and is a symbol of modern Brazilian architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Pablo Trincado · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Edifício Itália
tokens.description: Edifício Itália is a 165 metre, 46-storey skyscraper in the República district of central São Paulo, Brazil. It was built from 1956 to 1965 and designed by Franz Heep.
tokens.image_credit: Paul R. Burley · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: São Paulo Zoo
tokens.description: The São Paulo Zoo is the largest zoo in Brazil, located in the South Zone of São Paulo. It was inaugurated in 1958 and covers 824,529 square metres of former Atlantic Forest.

tokens.name: Cathedral of Brasília
tokens.description: The Cathedral of Brasília is the Roman Catholic cathedral serving Brasília, Brazil, and seat of the Archdiocese of Brasília. It was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and completed in 1970.
tokens.image_credit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palácio da Alvorada
tokens.description: The Palácio da Alvorada is the official residence of the president of Brazil, in Brasília. It was designed by Oscar Niemeyer and built between 1957 and 1958 in the modernist style.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monumental Axis
tokens.description: The Monumental Axis is the central main avenue of Brasília, Brazil, beginning at the National Congress. Its first section, the Esplanada dos Ministérios, is lined with government ministry buildings.
tokens.image_credit: Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz (modificado por Heitor Carvalho Jorge) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Botanical Garden of Curitiba
tokens.description: The Botanical Garden of Curitiba is a park in the Brazilian city of Curitiba, capital of Paraná state, laid out in the style of French formal gardens. It was established in 1991 and is one of the city's main tourist attractions.
tokens.image_credit: Alan Franco · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gramado
tokens.description: Gramado is a municipality in the Serra Gaúcha region of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The town was settled by Azorean descendants and later by German and Italian immigrants.

tokens.name: Serra Gaúcha
tokens.description: Serra Gaúcha is a cultural region of mountainous terrain in the northeast of Rio Grande do Sul state, southern Brazil. Most of its inhabitants are of German and Italian ancestry.

tokens.name: Meeting of Waters
tokens.description: The Meeting of Waters is the confluence of the dark Rio Negro and the pale Amazon, called the Solimões upstream in Brazil, near Manaus. For about 6 km the two rivers run side by side without mixing.
tokens.image_credit: Portal da Copa · CC BY 3.0 br · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anavilhanas National Park
tokens.description: Anavilhanas National Park covers a huge river archipelago in the Rio Negro in Amazonas state, northern Brazil. The park is part of a World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jason Auch from Calgary, Canada · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alter do Chão, Pará
tokens.description: Alter do Chão is one of the administrative districts of Santarém, on the right bank of the Tapajós river in Pará state, northern Brazil. It is the main tourist spot of Santarém.

tokens.name: Ver-o-peso, Belém
tokens.description: Ver-o-peso is a street market and small port area in Belém, Pará state, northern Brazil, inaugurated in 1901. It is part of the Ver-o-Peso Complex, dating from 1625, and is considered one of the oldest public markets in Brazil.

tokens.name: Elevador Lacerda, Salvador
tokens.description: The Elevador Lacerda is a public urban elevator in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, connecting the lower city (Cidade Baixa) with the upper city (Cidade Alta). Built between 1869 and 1873, it is 72 metres high and was named after Antônio de Lacerda.
tokens.image_credit: Paul R. Burley · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ouro Preto
tokens.description: Ouro Preto is a municipality in Minas Gerais, Brazil, built as a colonial gold mining town in the Serra do Espinhaço mountains. Its Baroque colonial architecture is the basis of its UNESCO World Heritage listing, inscribed in 1980.
tokens.image_credit: Raquel Mendes Silva · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Inhotim
tokens.description: Inhotim is a Brazilian contemporary art museum in Brumadinho, Minas Gerais, founded by Bernardo Paz in 2004. It is one of the largest outdoor art centres in Latin America.

tokens.name: Tiradentes, Minas Gerais
tokens.description: Tiradentes is a municipality in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, with an area of 83.5 km2. It had an estimated population of 8,056 as of 2025.

tokens.name: Paraty
tokens.description: Paraty is a municipality on the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil. Its historic centre is part of the UNESCO site Paraty and Ilha Grande, Culture and Biodiversity, inscribed in 2019.
tokens.image_credit: Vani Ribeiro · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ilha Grande
tokens.description: Ilha Grande is a forested island of 193 km2, about 12 km off the Atlantic coast of Angra dos Reis, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Ilha Grande State Park covers most of it and is part of the UNESCO site Paraty and Ilha Grande.

tokens.name: Armação dos Búzios
tokens.description: Armação dos Búzios, often called Búzios, is a municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, 173 km east of the city of Rio de Janeiro. It had 34,477 inhabitants by 2020.

tokens.name: Avenida 9 de Julio
tokens.description: Avenida 9 de Julio is a major thoroughfare in the city centre of Buenos Aires, Argentina. Its name honours Argentina's Independence Day, July 9, 1816.
tokens.image_credit: Fernando · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plaza de Mayo
tokens.description: Plaza de Mayo is the main city square of Buenos Aires, Argentina. Formed in 1884, it has been the scene of many major events in Argentine history.
tokens.image_credit: ProtoplasmaKid · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casa Rosada
tokens.description: Casa Rosada is the official workplace of the President of Argentina, located in Buenos Aires. The pink palatial mansion is officially known as Casa de Gobierno.
tokens.image_credit: Dragan · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Boca
tokens.title: Colorful tango neighbourhood
tokens.description: La Boca is a neighbourhood (barrio) of Buenos Aires, Argentina, near the city's port. In the 20th century it became a melting pot of immigrant cultures, with many settlers from Liguria in Italy.

tokens.name: Caminito
tokens.description: Caminito is a street museum and traditional alley in La Boca, a neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina. It inspired the tango Caminito, composed by Juan de Dios Filiberto in 1926.

tokens.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
tokens.description: El Ateneo Grand Splendid is a bookshop in Buenos Aires, Argentina, set in a former theatre with gilded balconies. In 2019 National Geographic named it the world's most beautiful bookstore.
tokens.image_credit: Galio · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Teatro Colón
tokens.description: The Teatro Colón is a historic opera house in Buenos Aires, Argentina. National Geographic lists it among the ten best opera houses in the world.
tokens.image_credit: EEJCC · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Madero
tokens.description: Puerto Madero is a barrio of Buenos Aires, Argentina, in the Central Business District on the Río de la Plata riverbank. It is known for its high-rise buildings and luxury hotels.
tokens.image_credit: Gonzabar77 · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Bombonera
tokens.description: La Bombonera is the football stadium of Boca Juniors in La Boca, Buenos Aires, Argentina. Officially named Estadio Alberto José Armando, it is widely regarded as one of the most iconic stadiums in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Matibro · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Estadio Monumental, Buenos Aires
tokens.description: Estadio Monumental, also known as Estadio River Plate, is a football stadium in the Belgrano neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is the home of River Plate and opened on 26 May 1938.
tokens.image_credit: Fulviusbsas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Telmo, Buenos Aires
tokens.description: San Telmo is the oldest barrio (neighbourhood) of Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is one of the birthplaces of tango and hosts some of the city's oldest buildings.

tokens.name: Palermo, Buenos Aires
tokens.description: Palermo is a barrio, or neighbourhood, of Buenos Aires, Argentina, located in the north of the city near the Rio de la Plata. It has a population of about 249,000 people.

tokens.name: El Chaltén
tokens.description: El Chaltén is a small mountain village in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina. It lies within Los Glaciares National Park, near the Cerro Torre and Cerro Fitz Roy spires, popular with climbers.

tokens.name: Ushuaia
tokens.description: Ushuaia is the capital of Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina, and claims the title of the world's southernmost city. It is located in a wide bay on the southern coast of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego.
tokens.image_credit: Deensel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bariloche
tokens.description: San Carlos de Bariloche, commonly known as Bariloche, is the largest city in Rio Negro Province, Argentina. It lies in the foothills of the Patagonian Andes on the southern shore of Nahuel Huapi Lake.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Ravazzani · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cerro Catedral
tokens.description: Cerro Catedral is a mountain and ski resort 19 km from San Carlos de Bariloche, inside Nahuel Huapi National Park, Argentina. It is one of the most important ski resorts in Argentina, with 48 km of ski runs.

tokens.name: Cafayate
tokens.description: Cafayate is a town in the central zone of the Calchaqui Valleys in Salta Province, Argentina, at 1,683 metres above sea level. It has about 12,000 inhabitants according to the 2001 census.

tokens.name: Devil's Throat, Iguazu Falls
tokens.description: The Devil's Throat is a waterfall on the Iguazu River at the border of Brazil and Argentina. It is shared by the Argentine Iguazu National Park and the Brazilian Iguacu National Park, which are part of a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Spouse of Leonard G. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Talampaya National Park
tokens.description: Talampaya National Park is a national park in the east centre of La Rioja Province, Argentina. It was designated a national park in 1997 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

tokens.name: Ischigualasto Provincial Park
tokens.description: Ischigualasto Provincial Park, also called Valle de la Luna, is a protected area in north-east San Juan Province, Argentina. It was established in 1971 and lies within the UNESCO World Heritage Ischigualasto/Talampaya Natural Parks.
tokens.image_credit: M.Bustos · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mendoza wine
tokens.description: Mendoza wine is Argentina's most important wine region, in Mendoza Province on the eastern foothills of the Andes. It accounts for nearly two-thirds of the country's wine production.

tokens.name: Los Glaciares National Park
tokens.description: Los Glaciares National Park is a federal protected area in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, and the largest national park in the country. Established in 1937, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tokens.name: Gran Torre Costanera
tokens.description: Gran Torre Costanera is a 62-story skyscraper in Santiago, Chile, and the tallest building in South America. It was designed by Alemparte Barreda & Asociados, the Argentine architect Cesar Pelli and Watt International.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plaza de Armas, Santiago
tokens.description: The Plaza de Armas is the main square of Santiago, the capital of Chile. Around it stand the Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago, the Central Post Office Building and the Palacio de la Real Audiencia de Santiago.
tokens.image_credit: Apincheira · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Cristóbal Hill
tokens.description: San Cristóbal Hill is a hill in northern Santiago, Chile, rising 880 m above sea level and about 300 m above the rest of the city. It was named by the Spanish conquistadors after Saint Christopher.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos yo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Chascona
tokens.description: La Chascona is a house in the Bellavista district of Santiago, Chile, owned by the poet Pablo Neruda. Its idiosyncratic architecture and interiors reflect Neruda's personal tastes, especially his fascination with the sea.
tokens.image_credit: Marcelo Ois Lagarde · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Viña del Mar
tokens.description: Viña del Mar is a city and commune on the Pacific coast of central Chile, along the shores of Valparaíso Bay. It is known as the Garden City and was founded under its current name in 1874.

tokens.name: Valle de la Luna, Atacama
tokens.description: Valle de la Luna is a valley in the Atacama Desert about 13 kilometres west of San Pedro de Atacama, in northern Chile. Wind and water have carved its stone and sand formations, which look like the surface of the Moon.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: El Tatio
tokens.description: El Tatio is a geothermal field with many geysers in the Andes of northern Chile, at about 4,320 metres above sea level. It is the third-largest geyser field in the world and the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Pedro de Atacama
tokens.description: San Pedro de Atacama is a town and commune in the Antofagasta Region of northern Chile, overlooking the Licancabur volcano. It has the R. P. Gustavo Le Paige Archaeological Museum, with a large collection of regional relics.

tokens.name: Chiloé Archipelago
tokens.description: The Chiloé Archipelago is a group of islands lying off the coast of Chile, in the Los Lagos Region. The token sits at Castro, the provincial capital on Chiloé Island, the best known island of the group.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pucón
tokens.description: Pucón is a city and commune in the Araucanía Region of southern Chile, on the eastern shore of Lake Villarrica. The Villarrica volcano lies about 17 kilometres to the south.

tokens.name: Villarrica Volcano, Chile
tokens.description: Villarrica is one of Chile's most active volcanoes, rising above the lake and town of the same name in southern Chile. It is the westernmost of three large stratovolcanoes and is protected within Villarrica National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Draceane · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Portillo, Chile
tokens.description: Portillo is a ski resort in the Andes of Chile's Valparaíso Region, about 160 km by road from Santiago. Its hotel sits at 2,880 m above sea level.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos yo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valle Nevado
tokens.description: Valle Nevado is a ski resort in the Andes Mountains, about 46 km east of Santiago, Chile. Founded in 1988 by French entrepreneurs, it has around 900 hectares of ski area.

tokens.name: Carretera Austral
tokens.description: The Carretera Austral is Chile's Route 7, a highway of about 1,240 km running south from Puerto Montt to Villa O'Higgins through rural Patagonia. It gives road access to the Aysén Region and the south of Los Lagos Region.

tokens.name: Mi Teleférico, La Paz
tokens.description: Mi Teleférico is an aerial cable car urban transit system serving the La Paz and El Alto metropolitan area in Bolivia. As of October 2019 it had 26 stations along ten lines.
tokens.image_credit: EEJCC · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Witches' Market
tokens.description: The Witches' Market is a popular tourist attraction in the El Rosario neighbourhood of La Paz, Bolivia, on Linares Street. It is known for stalls selling Andean folk remedies and ritual goods.

tokens.name: Laguna Colorada
tokens.description: Laguna Colorada is a shallow, hypersaline lake in the Altiplano of southwestern Bolivia, within the Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve. Its red colour comes from red sediments and pigmented algae, and it has been a Ramsar wetland since 1990.
tokens.image_credit: madras91 · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isla del Sol
tokens.description: Isla del Sol is an island in the southern part of Lake Titicaca, part of Bolivia's La Paz Department. It is a rocky, hilly island with many eucalyptus trees.

tokens.name: Sacred Valley
tokens.description: The Sacred Valley of the Incas, also called the Urubamba Valley, is a valley in the Andes of Peru, north of the Inca capital of Cusco. It lies in the Cusco Region.

tokens.name: Vinicunca
tokens.description: Vinicunca, also called Rainbow Mountain, is a mountain in the Andes of Peru with an altitude of 5,036 metres. It lies on the road to the Ausangate mountain in the Cusco region.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Aldrin Abanto Ricce · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Huacachina
tokens.description: Huacachina is a village built around a small oasis about five kilometres from the city of Ica in southwestern Peru. It has a permanent population of around 100 people and hosts many tourists each year.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Paracas National Reserve
tokens.description: Paracas National Reserve is a protected area in Ica, Peru, protecting desert and marine ecosystems. Archaeological remains of the Paracas culture are also found inside the reserve.
tokens.image_credit: Kirk39 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ballestas Islands
tokens.description: The Ballestas Islands are a group of small islands off the south coast of Peru, near the town of Paracas in the Ica Region. Boat tours to the islands, known for their seabirds and sea lions, leave from Paracas.

tokens.name: Arequipa
tokens.description: Arequipa is a city in southern Peru and the capital of Arequipa Province and the Department of Arequipa. Its historic centre has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.

tokens.name: Choquequirao
tokens.description: Choquequirao is a 16th-century Inca site in the Cusco Region of southern Peru. Often called the sister city of Machu Picchu, its terraces overlook the Apurimac River.
tokens.image_credit: Sucram Yef · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Inca Trail to Machu Picchu
tokens.description: The Inca Trail to Machu Picchu is a hiking trail in Peru that ends at Machu Picchu. It consists of three overlapping trails: Mollepata, Classic and One Day.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Miraflores District, Lima
tokens.description: Miraflores is a district of Lima, Peru. It is a residential and upscale shopping district and one of the main tourist destinations of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Mira4espina78y · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Larcomar
tokens.description: Larcomar is a shopping centre in Alfredo Salazar Park in Miraflores District, Lima, Peru. It is owned by the Chilean company Parque Arauco and is frequently visited by tourists and locals.
tokens.image_credit: Paulo JC Nogueira · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tambopata National Reserve
tokens.description: Tambopata National Reserve is a nature reserve in the southeastern Peruvian region of Madre de Dios, established on 4 September 2000. It protects several tropical rainforest ecosystems and the sustainable use of forest resources.

tokens.name: Máncora
tokens.description: Máncora is a town and beach resort in the Piura Region of northwestern Peru, in the Talara Province. It is the capital of the Máncora District and had 10,547 inhabitants in 2007.

tokens.name: Rosario Islands
tokens.description: The Rosario Islands are an archipelago off the coast of Colombia, about 20 kilometres from Cartagena. The national park covering them was founded in 1988 to protect one of the most important coral reefs of the Colombian Caribbean coast.

tokens.name: Salento, Quindío
tokens.description: Salento is a town and municipality in the north-east of the Quindío department, Colombia. It was the first settlement in Quindío of the modern era and the first municipality founded in the department.

tokens.name: Cocora Valley
tokens.description: The Cocora Valley is a valley in the Quindío Department of Colombia, located in the Central Cordillera of the Andes. Its name comes from a Quimbaya princess and means star of water.

tokens.name: Metrocable, Medellín
tokens.description: Metrocable is a gondola lift system in Medellín, Colombia, run by the city council to link informal settlements on steep hills with the Medellín Metro. It is largely considered the first cable-propelled urban transit system in South America.
tokens.image_credit: Staticshakedown · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Comuna 13, Medellín
tokens.description: Comuna 13, also called San Javier, is one of the 16 communes of Medellín, Colombia, with a population of around 160,000. The district is known for its street art, graffiti and guided tours.

tokens.name: Botero Plaza
tokens.description: Botero Plaza is a 7,000 square metre outdoor park in central Medellin with 23 bronze sculptures by Fernando Botero. Botero donated them, with other artworks, for the 2004 renovation of the neighbouring Museum of Antioquia.
tokens.image_credit: Staticshakedown · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monserrate
tokens.description: Monserrate is a mountain of 3,152 metres overlooking central Bogota, crowned by a 17th-century church with a shrine to El Senor Caido. It was a sacred site for the Muisca and is a major pilgrimage and tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Felipe Restrepo Acosta · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Candelaria, Bogotá
tokens.description: La Candelaria is the historic downtown neighbourhood of Bogotá, the 17th locality of the city. Its architecture combines Spanish Colonial, Baroque and art deco styles.

tokens.name: Gold Museum, Bogotá
tokens.description: The Gold Museum (Museo del Oro) in Bogotá is an archaeology museum holding pre-Hispanic gold objects. It is one of the most visited tourist sites in Colombia, with around 500,000 visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Felipe Restrepo Acosta · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
tokens.description: The Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá is an underground Roman Catholic church built in the tunnels of a salt mine about 200 metres below ground near Zipaquirá, Colombia. It is a major tourist destination and place of pilgrimage.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ciudad Mitad del Mundo
tokens.description: Ciudad Mitad del Mundo is a site near Quito, Ecuador, holding the Monument to the Equator, which marks the equator and commemorates the eighteenth-century Geodesic Mission. The grounds also include an ethnographic museum on Ecuador's indigenous peoples.
tokens.image_credit: Kaldari · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quilotoa
tokens.description: Quilotoa is a water-filled crater lake in the caldera of a dacite volcano in the Ecuadorian Andes. The caldera is about 3 km wide and was formed by a major eruption about 800 years ago.
tokens.image_credit: Annom · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baños de Agua Santa
tokens.description: Baños de Agua Santa is a city in eastern Tungurahua Province, Ecuador, and the second most populous city in the province. It is a major tourist centre known as the Gateway to the Amazon.

tokens.name: Cuenca, Ecuador
tokens.description: Cuenca is an Ecuadorian city, capital of Azuay Province and its largest city. Its historic centre, founded by the Spanish in 1577, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: amalavida.tv from Ecuador · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yasuní National Park
tokens.description: Yasuní National Park is a protected area of about 10,000 km2 of Amazonian rainforest in Ecuador, between the Napo and Curaray rivers. It was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1989 together with the adjacent Waorani Ethnic Reserve.

tokens.name: Canaima National Park
tokens.description: Canaima National Park is a 30,000 km2 park in Bolívar State, south-eastern Venezuela, roughly covering the Gran Sabana region. It is a UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Tyraelux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Los Roques Archipelago
tokens.description: Los Roques Archipelago is a federal dependency of Venezuela of about 350 islands, cays and islets in the Caribbean Sea, 128 km north of the port of La Guaira. Its pristine coral reef attracts many visitors.
tokens.image_credit: BIT1982 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Roraima
tokens.description: Mount Roraima is the highest of the Pacaraima chain of tepuis, a flat-topped mountain at the junction of Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela. Its highest point lies on the Venezuelan side at 2,810 m.
tokens.image_credit: Paolo Costa Baldi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Margarita Island
tokens.description: Margarita Island is the largest island in the Venezuelan state of Nueva Esparta, lying off the north-west coast of Venezuela in the Caribbean Sea. The state capital, La Asuncion, is located on the island.

tokens.name: Colonia Tovar
tokens.description: Colonia Tovar is a mountain town in Aragua state, Venezuela, about 65 km west of Caracas. It was founded in 1843 by about 390 immigrants from the Grand Duchy of Baden.

tokens.name: Pico Bolívar
tokens.description: Pico Bolívar is the highest mountain in Venezuela, at 4,978 metres, in Mérida State. It can only be reached on foot, as the Mérida cable car stops at Pico Espejo.

tokens.name: Punta del Este
tokens.description: Punta del Este is a seaside city and peninsula on the Atlantic coast of Maldonado Department, Uruguay. It grew from a small town into a resort popular with tourists from Latin and North America.
tokens.image_credit: Jimmy Baikovicius · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casapueblo
tokens.description: Casapueblo is a building at Punta Ballena, about 13 km from Punta del Este, Uruguay, constructed by the artist Carlos Páez Vilaró. It houses a museum, an art gallery, a cafeteria and a hotel.
tokens.image_credit: Talkingheads · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Colonia del Sacramento
tokens.description: Colonia del Sacramento is a city in southwestern Uruguay on the Río de la Plata, facing Buenos Aires. It is one of the oldest towns in Uruguay, and its Historic Quarter has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995.
tokens.image_credit: HalloweenHJB (talk) (Uploads) · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mercado del Puerto
tokens.description: Mercado del Puerto is a gastronomic venue in the Ciudad Vieja district of Montevideo, Uruguay. Originally a covered market, it now houses restaurants serving traditional Uruguayan asado cooked over open-fire grills.
tokens.image_credit: Felipe Restrepo Acosta · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Centrum, Paramaribo
tokens.description: Centrum is a resort in the Paramaribo District of Suriname, with 20,631 residents at the 2012 census. The historical centre of Paramaribo lies within it and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002.

tokens.name: Charles Darwin Research Station
tokens.description: The Charles Darwin Research Station is a biological research station in Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz Island, Galápagos, Ecuador. It is the headquarters of the Charles Darwin Foundation, founded in 1959 under the auspices of UNESCO.

tokens.name: The Shard
tokens.title: Glass shard above London Bridge
tokens.description: The Shard is a 95-storey mixed-use supertall skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano in Southwark, London. At 309.6 metres it is the tallest building in the United Kingdom.
tokens.image_credit: Colin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Gherkin
tokens.title: The Gherkin
tokens.description: The Gherkin, formally 30 St Mary Axe, is a commercial skyscraper in the City of London. It was completed in December 2003 and opened in April 2004.
tokens.image_credit: Aurelien Guichard from London, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 20 Fenchurch Street
tokens.title: The Walkie-Talkie
tokens.description: 20 Fenchurch Street, nicknamed The Walkie-Talkie, is a commercial skyscraper in the City of London. Construction was completed in spring 2014.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 122 Leadenhall Street
tokens.title: The Cheesegrater
tokens.description: 122 Leadenhall Street, nicknamed the Cheesegrater, is a 225-metre skyscraper in the City of London. It opened in July 2014 and was designed by Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners.
tokens.image_credit: FeydHuxtable · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: BT Tower
tokens.description: The BT Tower is a 1964 communications tower in Fitzrovia, London. It was built as the Museum Radio Tower and has been known by its current name since 1991.
tokens.image_credit: David Castor (dcastor) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: London Eye
tokens.title: Riverside observation wheel
tokens.description: The London Eye, originally the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames. It is the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel.
tokens.image_credit: Christian David · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: One Canada Square
tokens.description: One Canada Square is a 50-floor skyscraper in Canary Wharf, London. It was the tallest building in the United Kingdom from 1991 until 2012.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Gilbert · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trafalgar Square
tokens.description: Trafalgar Square is a public square in the City of Westminster in Central London. It commemorates the Battle of Trafalgar of 1805 and is home to Nelson's Column.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piccadilly Circus
tokens.description: Piccadilly Circus is a road junction and public space in London's West End, in the City of Westminster. It was built in 1819 to connect Regent Street with Piccadilly.
tokens.image_credit: Lily.Smith · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Leicester Square
tokens.description: Leicester Square is a pedestrianised square in London's West End and the centre of the capital's entertainment district. It was laid out in 1670 as Leicester Fields.
tokens.image_credit: Romazur · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Covent Garden
tokens.description: Covent Garden is a district in London's West End, associated with the former fruit and vegetable market in its central square. The market building is now a popular shopping and tourist site.

tokens.name: Oxford Street
tokens.description: Oxford Street is a major road in the City of Westminster in London's West End, running between Marble Arch and Tottenham Court Road. It is Europe's busiest shopping street, with around 300,000 daily visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Tempaccountforediting · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carnaby Street
tokens.description: Carnaby Street is a pedestrianised shopping street in Soho in the City of Westminster, close to Oxford Street and Regent Street. It is home to fashion retailers, including many independent boutiques.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Camden Market
tokens.description: Camden Market is a group of adjoining retail markets in Camden Town, London, housed in the former Pickfords stables. Stalls sell crafts, clothing, books, bric-a-brac and fast food.
tokens.image_credit: Julian vernot · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Borough Market
tokens.description: Borough Market is a wholesale and retail food market in Southwark, London. It is one of the largest and oldest food markets in London, with a market on the site dating back to at least the 12th century.
tokens.image_credit: Josep Renalias · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Portobello Road
tokens.description: Portobello Road is a street in the Notting Hill district of the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea, West London. On Saturdays it hosts Portobello Road Market, known for second-hand clothes, pastries and antiques.
tokens.image_credit: Alexrk2 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brick Lane
tokens.description: Brick Lane is a street in the East End of London, in the borough of Tower Hamlets. It runs through Spitalfields and is the most commercially active part of the area.
tokens.image_credit: Gons · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abbey Road
tokens.title: Beatles zebra crossing
tokens.description: Abbey Road is a thoroughfare through St John's Wood in London, in the boroughs of Camden and Westminster. It is best known for the Abbey Road Studios and the zebra crossing on the cover of the Beatles' 1969 album.
tokens.image_credit: m.caimary · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Harrods
tokens.description: Harrods is a luxury department store on Brompton Road in Knightsbridge, London. Opened in 1905, it is described as the largest department store in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: User:Mikegr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Savoy Hotel
tokens.description: The Savoy Hotel is a luxury hotel in the Strand in the City of Westminster, central London. Built by Richard D'Oyly Carte with profits from Gilbert and Sullivan operas, it opened on 6 August 1889.
tokens.image_credit: Photo by CVB, edited and cropped by Cart · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Ritz London
tokens.description: The Ritz London is a 5-star luxury hotel at 150 Piccadilly in London. It is considered one of the world's most prestigious and best known hotels.
tokens.image_credit: Tony Hisgett from Birmingham, UK · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Claridge's
tokens.description: Claridge's is a 5-star hotel at the corner of Brook Street and Davies Street in Mayfair, London. It is owned and managed by the Maybourne Hotel Group.
tokens.image_credit: Quintin Soloviev · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: London Zoo
tokens.description: London Zoo, also called Regent's Park Zoo, is the world's oldest scientific zoo. It opened on 27 April 1828 and was first intended as a collection for scientific study.

tokens.name: Kew Gardens
tokens.description: Kew Gardens is a botanic garden in southwest London, founded in 1759, holding one of the largest and most diverse botanical and mycological collections in the world. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Natural History Museum, London
tokens.description: The Natural History Museum in London exhibits a vast range of specimens from across natural history. It is one of three major museums on Exhibition Road in South Kensington, with the Science Museum and the Victoria and Albert Museum.

tokens.name: Tate Modern
tokens.description: Tate Modern is an art gallery in London holding the United Kingdom's national collection of international modern and contemporary art from 1900 onward. It is housed in the former Bankside Power Station in Southwark.
tokens.image_credit: Acabashi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Twickenham Stadium
tokens.description: Twickenham Stadium is a rugby union stadium in London owned by the Rugby Football Union. It is England's national rugby union stadium and the venue for the England team's home matches.
tokens.image_credit: brewbooks from near Seattle, USA; cropped by Blackcat · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wimbledon Championships
tokens.description: The Wimbledon Championships is a tennis tournament organised annually in Wimbledon, London, by the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. It is the third of the four Grand Slam events each year and the oldest tennis tournament in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Matt Morelli from Bedford, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club
tokens.description: The All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club is a private members' club at Church Road in Wimbledon, London. It is the venue of the Wimbledon Championships, the only Grand Slam tennis event still held on grass.
tokens.image_credit: Clavecin · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lord's
tokens.description: Lord's is a cricket venue in St John's Wood, London, owned by Marylebone Cricket Club. It is the home of Middlesex County Cricket Club and the England and Wales Cricket Board, and houses the world's oldest sporting museum.
tokens.image_credit: Yorkspotter · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Emirates Stadium
tokens.description: The Emirates Stadium is a football stadium in Holloway, London. It has been the home of Arsenal Football Club since its completion in 2006, and Arsenal's women's team has played there since 2024.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anfield
tokens.description: Anfield is a football stadium in Liverpool, England, and the home of Liverpool Football Club since its formation in 1892. It has a seating capacity of 61,276, the fifth-largest football stadium in England.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Etihad Stadium
tokens.description: Etihad Stadium in Manchester, England, is the home of Manchester City with a football capacity of about 61,000. It was built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games and later converted into a football stadium.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler, cropped by Blackcat · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Millennium Stadium
tokens.description: Millennium Stadium, known since 2016 as the Principality Stadium, is the national stadium of Wales in Cardiff. It has a retractable roof and a usual capacity of about 74,000, and is the home of the Wales rugby union team.
tokens.image_credit: Clint Budd from About 15 miles North of Swansea, Wales · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Murrayfield Stadium
tokens.description: Murrayfield Stadium is a rugby union stadium in Edinburgh, Scotland, owned by the Scottish Rugby Union. It is the national stadium of Scotland and, with 67,144 seats, the largest stadium in Scotland.
tokens.image_credit: Photo taken by Vclaw · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hampden Park
tokens.description: Hampden Park is a football stadium in the Mount Florida area of Glasgow, Scotland. It is the national stadium of football in Scotland and the home of the Scotland national team.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Nugent · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Cavern Club
tokens.description: The Cavern Club is a music venue on Mathew Street in Liverpool, England. It opened in 1957 as a jazz club and became closely associated with Merseybeat and the Beatles.

tokens.name: Royal Albert Dock, Liverpool
tokens.description: The Royal Albert Dock is a complex of dock buildings and warehouses in Liverpool, England. Opened in 1846 and designed by Jesse Hartley and Philip Hardwick, it was the first non-combustible warehouse system in the world.
tokens.image_credit: BCDS · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Liver Building
tokens.description: The Royal Liver Building is a Grade I listed office building at the Pier Head in Liverpool, England. With the Cunard Building and Port of Liverpool Building, it forms the Three Graces on the city's waterfront.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piccadilly Gardens
tokens.description: Piccadilly Gardens is a green space in Manchester city centre, England, on the edge of the Northern Quarter. It takes its name from the adjacent Piccadilly street and contains a bus station and a tram stop.
tokens.image_credit: Peter McDermott · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blackpool Tower
tokens.description: Blackpool Tower is a tourist attraction in Blackpool, Lancashire, England, opened to the public on 14 May 1894. Inspired by the Eiffel Tower, it is 158 metres tall.
tokens.image_credit: Nathanemmison · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blackpool Pleasure Beach
tokens.description: Pleasure Beach Resort, best known as Blackpool Pleasure Beach, is an amusement park on Blackpool's South Shore in Lancashire, England. The park was founded in 1896 by A. W. G. Bean and John Outhwaite.

tokens.name: Brighton Palace Pier
tokens.description: Brighton Palace Pier, commonly known as Brighton Pier, is a Grade II* listed pleasure pier in Brighton, England, established in 1899. It is the only one of Brighton's three piers still in operation.
tokens.image_credit: Ian Stannard from Southsea, England · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Pavilion
tokens.description: The Royal Pavilion is a Grade I listed former royal residence in Brighton, England, built in three stages from 1787. It was built as a seaside retreat for George, Prince of Wales, later King George IV.
tokens.image_credit: Qmin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Mile
tokens.description: The Royal Mile is a series of streets forming the main thoroughfare of the Old Town of Edinburgh, Scotland. It runs between Edinburgh Castle and Holyrood Palace and is almost exactly one mile long.

tokens.name: Princes Street
tokens.description: Princes Street is one of the major thoroughfares in central Edinburgh, Scotland, and the main shopping street in the capital. It is the southernmost street of the New Town and overlooks Princes Street Gardens and the Old Town.
tokens.image_credit: 瑞丽江的河水 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arthur's Seat
tokens.description: Arthur's Seat is an ancient extinct volcano and the main peak of a group of hills in Edinburgh, Scotland. The hills form most of Holyrood Park.
tokens.image_credit: David Monniaux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Edinburgh Zoo
tokens.description: Edinburgh Zoo, formerly the Scottish National Zoological Park, is an 82-acre non-profit zoological park on the slopes of Corstorphine Hill in Edinburgh, Scotland. Established in 1913, it receives over 600,000 visitors a year.

tokens.name: Glasgow Necropolis
tokens.description: The Glasgow Necropolis is a Victorian garden cemetery in Glasgow, Scotland. It sits on a prominent hill east of Glasgow Cathedral, and about fifty thousand people have been buried there.
tokens.image_credit: 瑞丽江的河水 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
tokens.description: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is a major art gallery and museum in Glasgow, Scotland, managed by Glasgow Museums. It stands in Kelvingrove Park in the city's West End.
tokens.image_credit: 瑞丽江的河水 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Loch Ness
tokens.title: Home of the monster legend
tokens.description: Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands, named after the River Ness that flows from its northern end. It is best known for claimed sightings of the Loch Ness Monster.
tokens.image_credit: Sam Fentress · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eilean Donan
tokens.description: Eilean Donan is a small tidal island at the meeting of Loch Duich, Loch Long and Loch Alsh in the western Scottish Highlands. Its castle, reached by a footbridge from the village of Dornie, is a frequent subject in photographs and film.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Isle of Skye
tokens.description: The Isle of Skye is the largest and northernmost of the major islands of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland. Its peninsulas radiate from a mountainous hub dominated by the Cuillin range.

tokens.name: The Storr
tokens.description: The Storr is a mountain on the Trotternish peninsula of the Isle of Skye in Scotland. Its steep rocky eastern face overlooks the Sound of Raasay, while its western slopes are grassy.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fairy Pools
tokens.description: The Fairy Pools are a series of natural pools and waterfalls in Glen Brittle on the Isle of Skye in Scotland. They lie at the foot of the Cuillin mountains and are known for their vivid aqua blue water.
tokens.image_credit: Drianmcdonald · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Titanic Belfast
tokens.description: Titanic Belfast is a visitor attraction in Belfast, Northern Ireland, which opened in 2012. It stands on the site of the former Harland & Wolff shipyard where RMS Titanic was built.
tokens.image_credit: Own work · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guinness Storehouse
tokens.description: Guinness Storehouse is a visitor attraction at St. James's Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland. It opened in 2000 and has received over twenty million visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Steven Lek · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temple Bar, Dublin
tokens.description: Temple Bar is an area on the south bank of the River Liffey in central Dublin, Ireland. It is promoted as the city's cultural quarter and is a centre of the city's nightlife.

tokens.name: Ha'penny Bridge
tokens.description: The Ha'penny Bridge is a pedestrian cast iron bridge over the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland. It was built in May 1816 and was originally known as the Wellington Bridge.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kilmainham Gaol
tokens.description: Kilmainham Gaol is a former prison in Kilmainham, Dublin, opened in the late 18th century. It is now a museum, and leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were imprisoned and executed there.

tokens.name: Croke Park
tokens.description: Croke Park is a Gaelic games stadium in Dublin, Ireland, named after Archbishop Thomas Croke. It is the headquarters of the Gaelic Athletic Association.
tokens.image_credit: O'Dea · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ring of Kerry
tokens.description: The Ring of Kerry is a 179 kilometre circular tourist route in County Kerry, south-western Ireland. It runs around the Iveragh Peninsula, passing through Sneem, Waterville, Cahersiveen and Glenbeigh.

tokens.name: Dingle Peninsula
tokens.description: The Dingle Peninsula is the northernmost of the major peninsulas in County Kerry, south-western Ireland. It ends at Dunmore Head, the westernmost point of mainland Ireland.

tokens.name: Slea Head
tokens.description: Slea Head is a promontory on the westernmost part of the Dingle Peninsula in County Kerry, south-western Ireland. It is reached by the R559 road, with the nearest villages Ballyickeen and Coumeenoole.

tokens.name: Aran Islands
tokens.description: The Aran Islands are a group of three islands at the mouth of Galway Bay, off the west coast of Ireland. The token sits at Kilronan, the main settlement on Inishmore, the largest island.
tokens.image_credit: Tuoermin · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blarney Castle
tokens.description: Blarney Castle is a medieval stronghold in Blarney, a town near Cork, Ireland. The current keep dates from 1446 and the Blarney Stone is set among its machicolations.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Champs-Élysées
tokens.title: The world's most beautiful avenue
tokens.description: The Avenue des Champs-Élysées is a 1.9 km avenue in the 8th arrondissement of Paris, running from the Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe. It is known for its theatres, cafés, luxury shops and the Bastille Day military parade.
tokens.image_credit: SoWhat · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Place de la Concorde
tokens.description: The Place de la Concorde is a public square in Paris and the largest square in the city, at the eastern end of the Champs-Élysées. Measuring 7.6 hectares, it was originally the Place Louis XV.
tokens.image_credit: Cristian Bortes from Cluj-Napoca, Romania · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Place Vendôme
tokens.description: The Place Vendôme is a public square in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, known for its regular architecture by Jules Hardouin-Mansart and the Vendôme Column. It is the starting point of the Rue de la Paix.
tokens.image_credit: Giorgio Galeotti · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montmartre
tokens.description: Montmartre is a large hill and district in the northern 18th arrondissement of Paris. It is known for its artistic history, the Basilica of the Sacré-Cœur on its summit and its nightclub district.

tokens.name: Moulin Rouge
tokens.description: The Moulin Rouge is a cabaret in Paris on the Boulevard de Clichy at the Place Blanche. Co-founded in 1889, the original venue burned in 1915 and reopened in 1925.
tokens.image_credit: Juanedc from Zaragoza, España · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sacré-Cœur, Paris
tokens.description: Sacré-Cœur is a Catholic church and minor basilica dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, at the summit of the Montmartre butte in Paris. Its dome overlooks the entire city and its suburbs.
tokens.image_credit: Tonchino · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pigalle, Paris
tokens.description: Pigalle is an area of Paris around Place Pigalle, on the border between the 9th and 18th arrondissements. It is known as a tourist district with theatres and adult shows.

tokens.name: The Marais
tokens.description: The Marais is a historic district in Paris, on the Right Bank across the 3rd and 4th arrondissements. Once an aristocratic quarter, it has many buildings of historic and architectural importance.

tokens.name: Latin Quarter, Paris
tokens.description: The Latin Quarter is a district of Paris on the Left Bank of the Seine, around the Sorbonne, in the 5th and 6th arrondissements. It is known for its concentration of universities and grandes ecoles.

tokens.name: Shakespeare and Company
tokens.description: Shakespeare and Company is an English-language bookstore on Paris's Left Bank, opened in 1951 by George Whitman. It takes its name from Sylvia Beach's bookshop of the same name, founded in 1919.
tokens.image_credit: Shadowgate from Novara, ITALY · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Café de Flore
tokens.description: Café de Flore is one of the oldest coffeehouses in Paris, known for its emblematic shopfront. It is located in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, at the corner of Boulevard Saint-Germain and Rue Saint-Benoît.
tokens.image_credit: Celette · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Les Deux Magots
tokens.description: Les Deux Magots is a cafe and restaurant at 6 Place Saint-Germain-des-Pres in Paris's 6th arrondissement. It was once the main meeting place of the city's literary and intellectual elite and is now a popular tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Cheng-en Cheng from Taichung City, Taiwan · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galeries Lafayette
tokens.description: Galeries Lafayette is an upmarket French department store chain. Its flagship store is on Boulevard Haussmann in the 9th arrondissement of Paris, and it has been a member of the International Association of Department Stores since 1960.
tokens.image_credit: Dimitri Destugues · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Le Bon Marché
tokens.description: Le Bon Marché is a department store in the 7th arrondissement of Paris, founded in 1838. Revamped by Aristide Boucicaut in 1852, it was one of the first modern department stores.
tokens.image_credit: Guillaume Speurt from Vilnius, Lithuania · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pont Alexandre III
tokens.description: The Pont Alexandre III is a deck arch bridge over the Seine in Paris, connecting the Champs-Élysées quarter with the Invalides and the Eiffel Tower. It is widely regarded as the most ornate bridge in the city.
tokens.image_credit: Jebulon · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pont des Arts
tokens.description: The Pont des Arts is a pedestrian bridge over the Seine in Paris. It links the Institut de France with the central square of the Louvre Palace.
tokens.image_credit: Joe deSousa · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
tokens.description: The Jardin du Luxembourg is a public garden in the 6th arrondissement of Paris, created from 1612 with the Luxembourg Palace. The garden is owned by the French Senate, which meets in the palace.
tokens.image_credit: Kirua · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tuileries Garden
tokens.description: The Tuileries Garden is a public garden between the Louvre and the Place de la Concorde in Paris, created by Catherine de' Medici in 1564. It became a public park after the French Revolution.
tokens.image_credit: Tangopaso · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
tokens.description: Père Lachaise Cemetery is the largest cemetery in Paris, at 44 hectares, in the 20th arrondissement. It was the first garden cemetery and the first municipal cemetery in the city.

tokens.name: Catacombs of Paris
tokens.description: The Catacombs of Paris are underground ossuaries holding the remains of more than six million people. They were built to consolidate the city's old stone quarries and extend south from the former Barrière d'Enfer.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tour Montparnasse
tokens.description: Tour Montparnasse is a 210-metre office skyscraper in the Montparnasse area of Paris, built from 1969 to 1973. It was the tallest skyscraper in France until 2011 and remains the tallest building in Paris proper.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Défense
tokens.description: La Défense is a major business district at the western end of the historic axis of Paris, in the Île-de-France region. It is home to the headquarters of numerous French and foreign multinationals and to the Paris Bourse.
tokens.image_credit: Vincevinss · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grande Arche
tokens.description: La Grande Arche is a 110-metre cube monument and office building in the La Defense business district west of Paris. It lies on the historic axis running from the Louvre to the Arc de Triomphe.
tokens.image_credit: Cristian Bortes from Cluj-Napoca, Romania · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Disneyland Park, Paris
tokens.description: Disneyland Park is a theme park at the Disneyland Paris resort in Marne-la-Vallee, France. It opened on 12 April 1992 and was designed and built by Walt Disney Imagineering.

tokens.name: Parc Astérix
tokens.description: Parc Astérix is a theme park in northern France based on the Asterix comic book series by Albert Uderzo and René Goscinny. In 2023 it welcomed over 2.8 million visitors.

tokens.name: Stade de France
tokens.description: Stade de France is the national stadium of France, located in the commune of Saint-Denis just north of Paris. With 81,338 seats it is the largest stadium in France.

tokens.name: Parc des Princes
tokens.description: Parc des Princes is an all-seater football stadium in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, with a capacity of 47,929. It has been the home of Paris Saint-Germain since July 1974.
tokens.image_credit: c:User:Arne mueseler · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stade Roland Garros
tokens.description: Stade Roland Garros is a complex of tennis courts in Paris that hosts the French Open, a major tennis championship played in late May and early June. The complex was built in 1928 and is named after the aviator Roland Garros.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palace of Fontainebleau
tokens.description: The Palace of Fontainebleau is one of the largest French royal chateaux, located 55 km southeast of Paris. It served as a hunting lodge and autumn residence for many French monarchs and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981.
tokens.image_credit: Gzen92 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Giverny
tokens.description: Giverny is a commune in the northern French department of Eure, in Normandy. It lies on the right bank of the Seine at its confluence with the Epte, about 80 km west-northwest of Paris.

tokens.name: Promenade des Anglais
tokens.description: The Promenade des Anglais is a seafront promenade of about 7 km along the Mediterranean coast of Nice, France. It runs from Nice Côte d'Azur Airport to the Quai des États-Unis.

tokens.name: Cannes Film Festival
tokens.description: The Cannes Film Festival is an invitation-only film festival held annually, usually in May, in Cannes, France. Founded in 1946, it is held at the Palais des Festivals et des Congrès.

tokens.name: Palais des Festivals et des Congrès
tokens.description: The Palais des Festivals et des Congrès is a convention centre in Cannes, France. It is the primary venue of the Cannes Film Festival and the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity.
tokens.image_credit: Timantha102938 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Promenade de la Croisette
tokens.description: The Promenade de la Croisette is a road about 2 km long along the Mediterranean shore in Cannes, France. It is known for the Palais des Festivals et des Congrès, where the Cannes Film Festival is held.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph Plotz · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel Negresco
tokens.description: The Hotel Negresco is a luxury hotel on the Promenade des Anglais in Nice, France. Henri Negresco had it built and opened it in 1912, and it houses the restaurant Le Chantecler.
tokens.image_credit: Anna M. Stevenson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Monaco Grand Prix
tokens.description: The Monaco Grand Prix is a Formula One motor racing event held annually on the Circuit de Monaco, usually in late May or early June. Run since 1929, it is widely considered one of the most prestigious automobile races in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Charles Coates/LAT Photographic · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Circuit de Monaco
tokens.description: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3.337 km street circuit laid out on the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine around the harbour of Monaco. It is used each spring for the Monaco Grand Prix and other motor races.
tokens.image_credit: Aimelaime at French Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saint-Tropez
tokens.description: Saint-Tropez is a commune in the Var department of southern France, on the French Riviera. It is one of the best-known towns of the Riviera, with 3,582 residents as of 2023.
tokens.image_credit: Starus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Calanques National Park
tokens.description: Calanques National Park is a French national park on the Mediterranean coast of Bouches-du-Rhône, between Marseille, Cassis and La Ciotat. Established in 2012, it covers about 520 km2, of which 85 km2 is land.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lavender fields of Valensole
tokens.description: The lavender fields of the Valensole plateau in Alpes-de-Haute-Provence bloom mainly in June and July. They surround the commune of Valensole, which had 3,173 inhabitants in 2019.

tokens.name: Chamonix
tokens.description: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc is a commune in the Haute-Savoie department of the French Alps, just north of Mont Blanc. It hosted the first Winter Olympics in 1924 and is a major ski resort.
tokens.image_credit: Ximonic, Simo Räsänen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aiguille du Midi
tokens.description: The Aiguille du Midi is a 3,842 metre mountain in the Mont Blanc massif of the French Alps. A cable car from Chamonix takes visitors close to Mont Blanc.
tokens.image_credit: Garrondo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mer de Glace
tokens.description: The Mer de Glace is a valley glacier on the northern slopes of the Mont Blanc massif in the French Alps. It is 7.5 km long and, with its tributary glaciers, is regarded as the largest glacier in France.

tokens.name: Val-d'Isère
tokens.description: Val-d'Isère is a commune of the Tarentaise Valley in the Savoie department of the French Alps, about 5 km from the Italian border. It is a ski resort on the edge of the Vanoise National Park.
tokens.image_credit: André Payan-Passeron · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Les Trois Vallées
tokens.description: Les Trois Vallées is a ski region in the Tarentaise Valley of the Savoie department in southeastern France, partly inside the Vanoise National Park. Since 1971 its interlinked valleys can be skied on a single ski pass.

tokens.name: Méribel
tokens.description: Méribel is a ski resort in the Tarentaise Valley of the French Alps, near Moûtiers. Its villages lie within Vanoise National Park and form part of the Les Trois Vallées ski system.

tokens.name: Tignes
tokens.title: Alpine arch dam
tokens.description: Tignes is a commune in the Tarentaise Valley of the French Alps, known for the largest skiable area and the longest ski season in Europe. It forms a joint ski area with neighbouring Val d'Isere.
tokens.image_credit: Tiia Monto · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alpe d'Huez
tokens.description: Alpe d'Huez is a ski resort in the Grandes Rousses massif of the French Alps, in the Isere department. It is also known as a climb on the Tour de France route.
tokens.image_credit: Simdaperce · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Médoc
tokens.description: The Médoc is a region of France on the left bank of the Gironde estuary, northwest of Bordeaux. It is a well known wine growing region with around 1,500 vineyards.

tokens.name: Saint-Émilion
tokens.description: Saint-Émilion is a medieval wine town in the Gironde department of southwestern France. The town and its surrounding vineyards were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Burgundy wine
tokens.description: Burgundy wine is made in the Burgundy region of east-central France, best known for pinot noir red and chardonnay white wines. The Climats of Burgundy vineyard landscape was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.

tokens.name: Alsace wine
tokens.description: Alsace wine is mostly white wine produced in the Alsace region of northeastern France. It is the only French AOC region that makes mostly varietal wines, typically from grape varieties used in German wine.

tokens.name: Vieux Lyon
tokens.description: Vieux Lyon is the largest Renaissance district of Lyon, lying between the Fourviere hill and the Saone river. It is part of the UNESCO Historic Site of Lyon, inscribed in 1998.
tokens.image_credit: Patrick Verdier, Free On Line Photos · Copyrighted free use · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Omaha Beach
tokens.description: Omaha Beach was one of five Allied landing sectors of the Normandy landings on 6 June 1944 in the Second World War. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property The D-Day Landing Beaches, Normandy, 1944.

tokens.name: Bayeux Tapestry
tokens.description: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered cloth nearly 70 metres long that depicts the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings in 1066. It is displayed at the Centre Guillaume le Conquérant in Bayeux.
tokens.image_credit: Myrabella · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Rochelle
tokens.description: La Rochelle is a city on the west coast of France and a seaport on the Bay of Biscay. It is the capital of the Charente-Maritime department, with 78,535 inhabitants in 2021.
tokens.image_credit: Remi Jouan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Biarritz
tokens.description: Biarritz is a French commune on the Bay of Biscay in the Pyrenees-Atlantiques department of the French Basque Country. It is a seaside resort known for the Hotel du Palais and its surfing culture.
tokens.image_credit: Nicolas G. Mertens. This picture is not in the public domain. If you want to use this picture outside of Wikipedia, please read the Licensing section just below. In particular, "You must give appropri · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dune of Pilat
tokens.description: The Dune of Pilat is the tallest sand dune in Europe. It is located in La Teste-de-Buch in the Arcachon Bay area, about 60 km southwest of Bordeaux on France's Atlantic coast.
tokens.image_credit: Larrousiney at French Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Arcachon Bay
tokens.description: Arcachon Bay, also called the Arcachon Basin, is an Atlantic bay on the southwest coast of France, in the Pays de Buch. It covers about 150 square kilometres at high tide and has protected natural areas.
tokens.image_credit: Karine Deydier · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Futuroscope
tokens.description: Futuroscope, formerly Planete Futuroscope, is a French theme park based on multimedia, cinematographic and audiovisual techniques. It lies about 10 km north of Poitiers in the Vienne department.
tokens.image_credit: Koakoo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Le Puy du Fou
tokens.description: Le Puy du Fou is a theme park in Les Epesses in the Vendee region of western France. It receives more than two million visitors every year, making it one of the most popular theme parks in France.

tokens.name: Reichstag building
tokens.description: The Reichstag is a neo-Renaissance legislative government building on Platz der Republik in Berlin. It was built between 1884 and 1894 and is the seat of the Bundestag, the German parliament.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Braukmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fernsehturm Berlin
tokens.description: The Fernsehturm is a 368 metre television tower in central Berlin, built between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic. It is the tallest structure in Germany.
tokens.image_credit: L-BBE · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alexanderplatz
tokens.description: Alexanderplatz is a large public square and transport hub in the Mitte district of Berlin. It is named after the Russian Tsar Alexander I and is reputedly the most visited area of Berlin.
tokens.image_credit: Neomicro · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Potsdamer Platz
tokens.description: Potsdamer Platz is a public square and traffic intersection in the centre of Berlin, about 1 km south of the Brandenburg Gate. It is named after the city of Potsdam, some 25 km to the south west.
tokens.image_credit: Avda · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kurfürstendamm
tokens.description: The Kurfürstendamm is one of the most famous avenues in Berlin, lined with shops, hotels and restaurants. It takes its name from the former prince-electors of Brandenburg.

tokens.name: Kaufhaus des Westens
tokens.description: The Kaufhaus des Westens, known as KaDeWe, is a department store in Berlin. With over 60,000 square metres of retail space, it is the second-largest department store in Europe after Harrods in London.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Zägel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Checkpoint Charlie
tokens.description: Checkpoint Charlie was the Western Bloc's name for the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point between East and West Berlin during the Cold War. It became a symbol of the division between East and West.
tokens.image_credit: Adrian Purser from London, UK · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: East Side Gallery
tokens.description: The East Side Gallery is a permanent open-air gallery of murals on a 1,316 metre remnant of the Berlin Wall along Mühlenstraße. The murals were painted in spring 1990 by 118 artists from 21 countries.
tokens.image_credit: Freepenguin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Museum Island
tokens.description: Museum Island is a museum complex on the northern part of Spree Island in the historic heart of Berlin. Its buildings were erected from 1830 to 1930, and the site became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berghain
tokens.description: Berghain is a nightclub in Berlin, Germany, named after its location near the border between Kreuzberg and Friedrichshain. Founded in 2004, it is one of the world's best-known techno clubs.
tokens.image_credit: Arne Müseler · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tempelhofer Feld
tokens.description: Tempelhofer Feld is a large open area in southern Berlin that was historically used for military practice and as a parade ground. Its history is closely linked to German military, aviation and football history.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Berlin Zoo
tokens.description: Berlin Zoo, formally the Berlin Zoological Garden, is the oldest surviving and best-known zoo in Germany. Opened in 1844 in Berlin's Tiergarten, it covers 35 hectares and holds about 1,380 species.

tokens.name: Olympiastadion Berlin
tokens.description: Olympiastadion is a sports stadium at Olympiapark Berlin, Germany, designed by Werner March for the 1936 Summer Olympics. Its record attendance during those Games was thought to be over 100,000.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Elbphilharmonie
tokens.description: The Elbphilharmonie is a concert hall in the HafenCity quarter of Hamburg, Germany, built on top of an old brick warehouse. It was originally designed by the Swiss firm Herzog & de Meuron and is popularly nicknamed Elphi.
tokens.image_credit: Burkhard Mücke · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reeperbahn
tokens.description: The Reeperbahn is a street and entertainment district in Hamburg's St. Pauli district. It is one of the two centres of Hamburg's nightlife and the city's major red-light district.

tokens.name: Speicherstadt
tokens.description: The Speicherstadt is a warehouse district in Hamburg's HafenCity quarter, built from 1883 to 1927 on timber-pile foundations. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Speicherstadt and Kontorhaus district with Chilehaus.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marienplatz
tokens.description: Marienplatz is a central square in the city centre of Munich, Germany. It has been the city's main square since 1158.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hofbräuhaus am Platzl
tokens.description: The Hofbräuhaus am Platzl is a beer hall in Munich, Bavaria, originally built in 1589 as an extension of the Staatliches Hofbräuhaus brewery. The general public was admitted in 1828.
tokens.image_credit: Kiban · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Viktualienmarkt
tokens.description: The Viktualienmarkt is a food market and square in the centre of Munich, Germany. It has been held daily, except Sundays and holidays, since 1807.
tokens.image_credit: Helmlechner · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Englischer Garten
tokens.description: The Englischer Garten is a large public park in the centre of Munich, Germany, stretching to the northeastern city limits. Its creation began in 1789, supervised by Benjamin Thompson, later Count Rumford.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: BMW Welt
tokens.title: Bowl-shaped car museum
tokens.description: BMW Welt is a combined exhibition, delivery, adventure museum and event venue in Munich's Am Riesenfeld district, next to the Olympic Park. It was built from August 2003 to summer 2007.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Garmisch-Partenkirchen
tokens.description: Garmisch-Partenkirchen is an Alpine ski town in Bavaria, Germany, and the seat of the Garmisch-Partenkirchen district. Germany's highest mountain, the Zugspitze, is nearby.
tokens.image_credit: Octagon · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Europa-Park
tokens.description: Europa-Park is a theme park and resort in Rust, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It has twenty themed areas, around a hundred attractions and fourteen roller coasters.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Berwing · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heidelberg Castle
tokens.description: Heidelberg Castle is a ruin and landmark of Heidelberg, Germany. Its ruins are among the most important Renaissance structures north of the Alps.
tokens.image_credit: Pumuckel42 (Reinhard Wolf) at de:Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lorelei
tokens.description: The Lorelei is a steep slate rock, 132 metres high, on the right bank of the Rhine at Sankt Goarshausen, Germany. It lies inside the Upper Middle Rhine Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Braukmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Königsallee
