tokens.description: Königsallee is an urban boulevard in Düsseldorf, Germany, known for the landscaped canal along its centre. It is one of Germany's busiest upscale shopping streets, lined with luxury fashion stores.
tokens.image_credit: Stöhrfall (talk) 18:38, 8 August 2010 (UTC) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nürburgring
tokens.description: The Nürburgring is a motorsports complex in the Eifel mountains near Nürburg, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. It has a Grand Prix circuit built in 1984 and the 20.8 km Nordschleife loop built in the 1920s.
tokens.image_credit: Herranderssvensson · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Autostadt
tokens.description: Autostadt is a visitor attraction beside the Volkswagen plant in Wolfsburg, Germany, focused on automobiles. It features a museum, pavilions for the Volkswagen Group brands and a factory tour.
tokens.image_credit: Ralf Roletschek · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mercedes-Benz Museum
tokens.title: Stuttgart carmaker
tokens.description: The Mercedes-Benz Museum is an automobile museum in Stuttgart, Germany, covering the history of the Mercedes-Benz brand and its associated brands. Stuttgart is home to the international headquarters of the Mercedes-Benz Group.
tokens.image_credit: Julian Herzog (Website) · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Porsche Museum
tokens.title: Stuttgart sports car maker
tokens.description: The Porsche Museum is an automobile museum in the Zuffenhausen district of Stuttgart, Germany, on the site of carmaker Porsche. It ranks second among the most visited museums in Stuttgart, behind the Mercedes-Benz Museum.
tokens.image_credit: RudolfSimon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Semperoper
tokens.description: The Semperoper is the opera house of the Saxon State Opera Dresden and the concert hall of the Staatskapelle Dresden. It stands on the Theaterplatz near the Elbe River in the historic centre of Dresden, Germany.
tokens.image_credit: Avda · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wartburg
tokens.description: The Wartburg is a medieval castle in Thuringia, Germany, at 410 metres on a precipice overlooking the town of Eisenach. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sylt
tokens.description: Sylt is an island in the Nordfriesland district of Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, and the largest island in North Frisia. It is the northernmost island of Germany, known for its resorts and a 40 km sandy beach.

tokens.name: Rügen
tokens.description: Rügen is Germany's largest island, lying off the Pomeranian coast in the Baltic Sea. It belongs to the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and is linked to the mainland at Stralsund by the Rügen Bridge and Causeway.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Königssee
tokens.description: The Königssee is a natural lake in the Berchtesgadener Land district of Bavaria, Germany, near the Austrian border. Most of the lake lies within Berchtesgaden National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Constance
tokens.description: Lake Constance, known in German as Bodensee, refers to three bodies of water on the Rhine at the northern foot of the Alps. The lake lies in the Lake Constance Basin in the Alpine Foreland.
tokens.image_credit: NASA · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
tokens.description: Tierpark Hagenbeck is a zoo in Stellingen, Hamburg, Germany. Its collection began in 1863 with animals belonging to Carl Hagenbeck Sr., a fishmonger who became an amateur animal collector.

tokens.name: Bordeaux wine
tokens.description: Bordeaux wine is produced in the Bordeaux region of southwest France, around the city of Bordeaux on the Garonne River. The Gironde department has about 110,800 hectares of vineyards.

tokens.name: Rhine Gorge
tokens.description: The Rhine Gorge is the 65 km southern section of the Middle Rhine between Koblenz and Rüdesheim in Germany. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in June 2002 as the Upper Middle Rhine Valley cultural landscape.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Via Veneto
tokens.description: Via Vittorio Veneto, colloquially Via Veneto, is one of the best-known streets of Rome, Italy. It is named after the Battle of Vittorio Veneto (1918) in the First World War.

tokens.name: Piazza Navona
tokens.description: Piazza Navona is a public open space in Rome, Italy. It is built on the site of the 1st century AD Stadium of Domitian and keeps the elongated oval form of the stadium.
tokens.image_credit: NikonZ7II · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piazza di Spagna
tokens.description: Piazza di Spagna is a square in central Rome, at the foot of the Spanish Steps. It takes its name from the Palazzo di Spagna, the seat of the Spanish embassy to the Holy See, and holds the Column of the Immaculate Conception.
tokens.image_credit: Sergey Smirnov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spanish Steps
tokens.description: The Spanish Steps are a monumental stairway of 135 steps in Rome, climbing from the Piazza di Spagna to the Trinità dei Monti church. The stairway was designed by the architects Francesco de Sanctis and Alessandro Specchi.
tokens.image_credit: Hugo DK · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Campo de' Fiori
tokens.description: Campo de' Fiori is a rectangular square in central Rome, south of Piazza Navona. The name, meaning Field of Flowers, dates to the Middle Ages, when the area was a meadow.
tokens.image_credit: Myrabella · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trastevere
tokens.description: Trastevere is the 13th rione of Rome, located within Municipio I. Its name comes from the Latin trans Tiberim, meaning beyond the Tiber.

tokens.name: Appian Way
tokens.description: The Appian Way, also called Via Appia, is one of the earliest and most strategically important Roman roads. It connected Rome to Brindisi in southeast Italy and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.
tokens.image_credit: Livioandronico2013 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galleria Borghese
tokens.description: The Galleria Borghese is an art gallery in Rome, housed in the former Villa Borghese Pinciana. It holds a substantial part of the Borghese Collection of paintings, sculpture and antiquities, begun by Cardinal Scipione Borghese.
tokens.image_credit: Blackcat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cinecittà
tokens.description: Cinecittà is a large film studio in Rome, covering 400,000 square metres and said to be the largest in Europe. It is considered the hub of Italian cinema, and its studios were built during the Fascist era.

tokens.name: Stadio Olimpico
tokens.description: Stadio Olimpico is a multi-purpose sports venue in Rome, seating over 70,000 spectators. It is the largest sports facility in Rome and the second-largest stadium in Italy, after Milan's San Siro.
tokens.image_credit: Messapi, cropped by Blackcat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
tokens.description: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II is Italy's oldest active shopping arcade, a four-storey double arcade in the centre of Milan. Designed in 1861 by Giuseppe Mengoni and built from 1865 to 1877, it is named after Victor Emmanuel II.
tokens.image_credit: Paolobon140 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Via Monte Napoleone
tokens.description: Via Monte Napoleone is an upscale shopping street in central Milan, inside the Quadrilatero della moda fashion district. It is known for luxury fashion houses and was ranked first among the world's most expensive retail streets by prime rents in 2024.

tokens.name: Navigli
tokens.description: The Navigli are a system of interconnected canals in and around Milan, in Lombardy, dating back as far as the Middle Ages. Five canals make up the system, and the first three are linked through Milan by the Fossa Interna.
tokens.image_credit: Flavmi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pirelli Tower
tokens.description: The Pirelli Tower, nicknamed Pirellone, is a 32-storey skyscraper of 127 m in Milan, Italy. It was the tallest building in Milan for almost 80 years and is one of the city's best-known symbols.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bosco Verticale
tokens.description: The Bosco Verticale, or Vertical Forest, is a complex of two residential skyscrapers in the Porta Nuova district of Milan, Italy. Designed by Boeri Studio and inaugurated in 2014, its facades carry over ninety plant species.
tokens.image_credit: Darsheni · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: UniCredit Tower
tokens.description: The UniCredit Tower is an office skyscraper in Milan, Italy, and the headquarters of UniCredit, Italy's largest bank by assets. With its spire it reaches 238 metres, the tallest building in Italy by total height.
tokens.image_credit: Rob Oo · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piazza San Marco
tokens.description: Piazza San Marco, known in English as St Mark's Square, is the principal public square of Venice, Italy. Together with the Piazzetta it forms the social, religious and political centre of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Matthias Süßen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Murano
tokens.description: Murano is a series of islands linked by bridges in the Venetian Lagoon, about 1.5 km north of Venice, Italy. The islands are famous for their glass making.

tokens.name: Burano
tokens.description: Burano is a small island town in the Venetian Lagoon, northern Italy, known for its lace work and brightly coloured houses. Its economy is mainly tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Kasa Fue · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venice Film Festival
tokens.description: The Venice Film Festival is an annual film festival held in Venice, Italy, on the Lido. It is the world's oldest film festival and one of the Big Five international film festivals.
tokens.image_credit: dalbera from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
tokens.description: Piazzale Michelangelo is a square with a panoramic view of Florence, located in the Oltrarno district of Italy. It lies within the UNESCO-listed Historic Centre of Florence.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Wittwer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Boboli Gardens
tokens.description: The Boboli Gardens is a large park in Florence, Italy, originally designed in the mid-16th century as the garden of the Medici Pitti Palace. It is an important early Italian garden with statues, fountains and grottoes.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mercato Centrale, Florence
tokens.description: The Mercato Centrale is a covered market in Florence, Italy, housed in a 19th-century hall designed by Giuseppe Mengoni. It is located in the historic centre of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Sailko · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Piazza del Campo
tokens.description: Piazza del Campo is the main public square of the historic centre of Siena, Tuscany, Italy. It is regarded as one of Europe's greatest medieval squares and lies within the UNESCO-listed historic centre.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Sehnert · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Palio di Siena
tokens.description: The Palio di Siena is a bareback horse race held twice a year, on 2 July and 16 August, in Siena, Italy. Ten horses represent ten of the city's seventeen contrade, or wards, in a tradition dating back to the 17th century.
tokens.image_credit: Mirco · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chianti
tokens.description: Chianti is a mountainous area of Tuscany, Italy, in the provinces of Florence, Siena and Arezzo, made up mainly of hills. It gives its name to the Chianti wine produced there.

tokens.name: Piazza dei Miracoli
tokens.description: The Piazza dei Miracoli is a walled compound in central Pisa, Tuscany, dominated by the cathedral, the baptistery, the Leaning Tower and the Camposanto. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Portofino
tokens.description: Portofino is a comune on the Italian Riviera in the Metropolitan City of Genoa, clustered around its small harbour and known for its painted waterfront houses. Since the late 19th century it has been a resort for European aristocracy and the jet set.
tokens.image_credit: Quintin Soloviev · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Porto Venere
tokens.description: Porto Venere is a town and municipality on the Ligurian coast in the Province of La Spezia, with three villages and the islands of Palmaria, Tino and Tinetto. The town is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Portovenere, Cinque Terre, and the Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Aconcagua (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Capri
tokens.description: Capri is an island in the Tyrrhenian Sea off the Sorrento Peninsula, on the south side of the Gulf of Naples in Campania, Italy. It has been a resort destination since Roman times and has 13,451 inhabitants.

tokens.name: Ravello
tokens.description: Ravello is a comune on a hill above the Amalfi Coast in the province of Salerno, Campania, with about 2,500 inhabitants. Its scenic location makes it a popular tourist destination, and the town lies within the Amalfi Coast UNESCO World Heritage property.

tokens.name: Sorrento
tokens.description: Sorrento is a city and comune overlooking the Bay of Naples on the Sorrentine Peninsula, Campania, Italy. It is a popular tourist destination known for its ceramics, lacework and marquetry shops.
tokens.image_credit: Kim Traynor · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ischia
tokens.description: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Tyrrhenian Sea at the northern end of the Gulf of Naples, about 30 kilometres from Naples. It is the largest of the Phlegrean Islands.

tokens.name: Procida
tokens.description: Procida is one of the Phlegraean Islands off the coast of Naples in southern Italy, between Cape Miseno and the island of Ischia. It is a comune of the Metropolitan City of Naples, together with the tiny satellite island of Vivara.
tokens.image_credit: Jamiethearcher at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue Grotto, Capri
tokens.description: The Blue Grotto is a sea cave on the coast of Capri, southern Italy. Sunlight shining through an underwater cavity lights the water inside with a blue glow.
tokens.image_credit: Elenagm · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Vesuvius
tokens.description: Mount Vesuvius is a somma stratovolcano on the Gulf of Naples in Campania, Italy, about 9 km east of Naples. It is one of the volcanoes forming the Campanian volcanic arc.
tokens.image_credit: pietro scerrato · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Polignano a Mare
tokens.description: Polignano a Mare is a town and municipality in the Metropolitan City of Bari, Apulia, southern Italy, on the Adriatic Sea. Its local economy mostly depends on tourism, agriculture and fishing.
tokens.image_credit: Luca Margheriti · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lecce
tokens.description: Lecce is a city and comune in the region of Apulia in southern Italy, and the capital of the province of Lecce. It lies on the Salentine Peninsula, at the heel of the Italian Peninsula.

tokens.name: Taormina
tokens.description: Taormina is a comune in the Metropolitan City of Messina, on the east coast of Sicily, Italy. It has been a tourist destination since the 19th century, with beaches on the Ionian Sea.
tokens.image_credit: John Menard from Phoenix, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mount Etna
tokens.description: Mount Etna is an active stratovolcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy, between the cities of Messina and Catania. It is one of the tallest active volcanoes in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Jacopo Werther · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Scala dei Turchi
tokens.description: Scala dei Turchi is a rocky cliff of white marl on the coast of Realmonte, near Porto Empedocle, southern Sicily, Italy. It is a tourist attraction, partly because of its mention in Andrea Camilleri's Montalbano stories.
tokens.image_credit: Carnby · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aeolian Islands
tokens.description: The Aeolian Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Tyrrhenian Sea north of Sicily, said to be named after Aeolus, the mythical ruler of the winds. UNESCO inscribed the islands as a World Heritage Site in 2000.
tokens.image_credit: This image was taken by the NASA Expedition 17 crew. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Costa Smeralda
tokens.description: Costa Smeralda is a coastal area and tourist destination in northern Sardinia, Italy, with about 20 km of coast. It is known for white sand beaches, golf clubs and exclusive hotels.

tokens.name: Maddalena Archipelago
tokens.description: The Maddalena Archipelago is a group of islands in the Strait of Bonifacio between Sardinia and Corsica. The whole archipelago forms the territory of the comune of La Maddalena.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cala Goloritzé
tokens.description: Cala Goloritzé is a beach in the town of Baunei in the Gulf of Orosei, eastern Sardinia. The beach was created by a landslide in 1962 and is known for a 143 metre pinnacle above the cove.
tokens.image_credit: Mentnafunangann · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo
tokens.description: Cortina d'Ampezzo is a town and comune in the province of Belluno, in the Veneto region of northern Italy. Set in the Dolomites, it is a summer and winter resort known for its skiing trails and scenery.
tokens.image_credit: Dirgela · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Courmayeur
tokens.description: Courmayeur is a town and comune in the Aosta Valley of northern Italy. It is one of the two bases on either side of Mont Blanc, Europe's highest mountain.
tokens.image_credit: X-Weinzar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Breuil-Cervinia
tokens.description: Breuil-Cervinia is a frazione of the comune of Valtournenche in the Aosta Valley of northern Italy. It is a winter and summer tourist resort.
tokens.image_credit: qwesy qwesy · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Livigno
tokens.description: Livigno is a town, comune and special-administered territory in the province of Sondrio, Lombardy, northern Italy. It lies in the Italian Alps near the Swiss border.
tokens.image_credit: Maurizio Moro5153 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Val Gardena
tokens.description: Val Gardena is a valley in the Dolomites of South Tyrol, northern Italy. It is best known as a tourist area for skiing, rock climbing and woodcarving.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry A. Mottl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sellaronda
tokens.description: The Sellaronda is the ski circuit around the Sella group in the Dolomites of northern Italy. The massif lies between the four Ladin valleys of Badia, Val Gardena, Fascia and Fodom.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry A. Mottl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Como
tokens.description: Lake Como, also known as Lario, is a lake of glacial origin in Lombardy, northern Italy. At over 400 metres deep, it is one of the deepest lakes in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Mænsard vokser · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Garda
tokens.description: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy and a popular holiday location in northern Italy. It lies between Brescia and Milan to the west and Verona and Venice to the east.
tokens.image_credit: Photo by Guido Adler. Upload by Moroder · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Maggiore
tokens.description: Lake Maggiore is a large lake on the south side of the Alps, shared by Italy and the Swiss canton of Ticino. It is the second largest lake in Italy.
tokens.image_credit: Alessandro Vecchi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bellagio, Lombardy
tokens.description: Bellagio is a municipality on a promontory where the two southern arms of Lake Como meet, in the Province of Como, Lombardy. Its position looks across the lake towards the Alps.
tokens.image_credit: RaminusFalcon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Villa del Balbianello
tokens.description: Villa del Balbianello is a villa on a wooded peninsula on the western shore of Lake Como, in the comune of Lenno. It is known for its elaborate terraced gardens.
tokens.image_credit: Emibuzz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Barolo
tokens.title: King of Italian wines
tokens.description: Barolo is a red DOCG wine made from the nebbiolo grape in the Piedmont region of northern Italy. Its production zone covers several communes in the province of Cuneo.
tokens.image_credit: Lanthanum57 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Langhe
tokens.description: The Langhe is a hilly area south and east of the Tanaro river in the provinces of Cuneo and Asti, Piedmont. It is known for its wines, cheeses and truffles, and lies within a UNESCO vineyard landscape.
tokens.image_credit: Phalaenopsis Aphrodite from Italy · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Prosecco
tokens.description: Prosecco is an Italian DOC or DOCG white wine produced in nine provinces of Veneto and Friuli-Venezia Giulia. It is made from the Prosecco grape, renamed Glera in Italy in 2009.
tokens.image_credit: Civvì · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amarone
tokens.description: Amarone della Valpolicella, usually called Amarone, is an Italian DOCG dry red wine made from partly dried grapes in the Valpolicella area of Verona province, Veneto. Its name means great bitter in Italian.

tokens.name: Verona Arena
tokens.description: The Verona Arena is a Roman amphitheatre in the historic centre of Verona, Italy. It is among the best-preserved ancient amphitheatres to have survived into the modern era.
tokens.image_credit: Claconvr · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Museo Ferrari
tokens.title: Maranello's prancing horse
tokens.description: Museo Ferrari is a museum in Maranello, Italy, dedicated to the Ferrari sports car marque. It also holds trophies, photographs and other objects from the Italian motor racing industry.

tokens.name: Imola Circuit
tokens.description: The Imola Circuit, officially the Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari, is a 4.909 km motor racing circuit in Imola, Emilia-Romagna, 40 km east of Bologna. The first race at Imola was held in 1953.
tokens.image_credit: Jmmuguerza · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mugello Circuit
tokens.description: Mugello Circuit is a motorsport race track in Scarperia e San Piero, near Florence, Tuscany, Italy. The circuit is 5.245 km long and has 15 turns.
tokens.image_credit: Press office · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gardens of Vatican City
tokens.description: The Gardens of Vatican City are private urban gardens and parks covering about half of Vatican City, owned by the Pope. They lie within the Vatican City World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Bauer, http://www.ferras.at · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Boqueria
tokens.description: La Boqueria, officially the Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria, is a large public market in the Ciutat Vella district of Barcelona, Spain. It is one of the city's foremost tourist landmarks, with an entrance from La Rambla.
tokens.image_credit: Didier Descouens · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Passeig de Gràcia
tokens.description: Passeig de Gràcia is one of the major avenues in Barcelona, Spain, and one of its most important shopping and business areas. It runs through the Eixample district and contains several celebrated works of architecture.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casa Batlló
tokens.description: Casa Batlló is a building in central Barcelona, Spain, designed by Antoni Gaudí and considered one of his masterpieces. Redesigned in 1904, it is part of the UNESCO Works of Antoni Gaudí property.
tokens.image_credit: ChristianSchd · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Casa Milà
tokens.description: Casa Milà, popularly known as La Pedrera, is a Modernista building in Barcelona, Spain. Built between 1906 and 1912, it was the last private residence designed by Antoni Gaudí.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Ledl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Barceloneta
tokens.description: La Barceloneta is a neighborhood in the Ciutat Vella district of Barcelona, Spain, on the Mediterranean coast. It was built in the 18th century for residents displaced by the construction of the Ciutadella.
tokens.image_credit: dronepicr · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Montjuïc
tokens.description: Montjuïc is a broad, shallow hill in Barcelona, Spain, and the site where the city was born. Its position between the Mediterranean and the Llobregat River has made it strategically significant throughout history.
tokens.image_credit: Fabio Alessandro Locati · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Torre Glòries
tokens.description: The Torre Glòries, formerly Torre Agbar, is a 38-storey skyscraper in the Poblenou district of Barcelona, designed by Jean Nouvel. It was built for the Agbar Group, the holding company of the Barcelona water company Aigües de Barcelona.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: PortAventura World
tokens.description: PortAventura World is an entertainment resort in Salou and Vila-seca on the Costa Daurada in Catalonia. It is built around the PortAventura Park theme park, the most visited theme park in Spain.
tokens.image_credit: Olivier Bruchez · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerta del Sol
tokens.description: The Puerta del Sol is a public square in central Madrid and one of the busiest places in the city. It marks Km 0 of the radial network of Spanish roads and is known for its clock, whose bells mark the New Year's Eve Twelve Grapes tradition.
tokens.image_credit: Tomás Fano · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Parque del Buen Retiro
tokens.description: The Parque del Buen Retiro, known as Retiro Park, is one of the largest city parks in Madrid, covering about 1.4 square kilometres. It was a royal estate until 1868 and is the largest part of the Paseo del Prado and Buen Retiro UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: pictures Jettcom · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santiago Bernabéu Stadium
tokens.description: The Santiago Bernabéu Stadium is a football stadium in the Chamartín district of Madrid, home of Real Madrid since 1947. After its renovation completed in late 2024 it seats 83,186, the second largest capacity of any football stadium in Spain.
tokens.image_credit: Biblioteca de la Facultad de Empresa y Gestión Pública Universidad de Zaragoza from Huesca, España · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Metropolitano Stadium
tokens.description: The Metropolitano Stadium is a football stadium in the Rosas district of Madrid, home of Atlético Madrid since 2017. The original stadium opened in 1994, built for Madrid's unsuccessful bid to host the 1997 World Athletics Championships.
tokens.image_credit: Asqueladd · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Market of San Miguel
tokens.description: The Market of San Miguel is a covered market in central Madrid, originally built in 1916. Private investors renovated its iron structure and reopened it in 2009.
tokens.image_credit: Sbharris · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Palace of Madrid
tokens.description: The Royal Palace of Madrid is the official residence of the Spanish royal family, used mainly for state ceremonies. With 3,418 rooms it is the largest royal palace in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Tim Adams · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cuatro Torres Business Area
tokens.description: The Cuatro Torres Business Area is a business district on the Paseo de la Castellana in Madrid, built on the former Real Madrid sports city. It contains the four tallest skyscrapers in Spain, completed in 2008.
tokens.image_credit: Zarateman · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gate of Europe
tokens.description: The Gate of Europe, also known as the KIO Towers, is a pair of office towers near Plaza de Castilla in Madrid. Each tower is 114 metres high with 26 floors, built between 1989 and 1996.
tokens.image_credit: Deensel · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plaza de España, Seville
tokens.description: Plaza de España is a plaza in Maria Luisa Park in Seville, Spain, built in 1928 for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929. It is a landmark of Regionalism architecture mixing Baroque Revival, Renaissance Revival and Neo-Mudéjar styles.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Delgado · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seville Cathedral
tokens.description: Seville Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the See, is a Catholic cathedral in Seville, Spain, and the largest Gothic cathedral in the world. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property that includes the Alcázar and the General Archive of the Indies.
tokens.image_credit: Ingo Mehling · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Giralda
tokens.description: The Giralda is the bell tower of Seville Cathedral in Seville, Spain, originally built as the minaret of the Great Mosque of Seville. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property that includes the cathedral, the Alcázar and the General Archive of the Indies.
tokens.image_credit: Ingo Mehling · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: La Tomatina
tokens.description: La Tomatina is a festival held in Buñol, Spain, in which participants throw tomatoes at each other. It is described as the biggest food fight in the world and is a major tourist attraction.
tokens.image_credit: flydime · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: City of Arts and Sciences
tokens.description: The City of Arts and Sciences is a cultural and architectural complex in Valencia, Spain. It lies at the southeast end of the former riverbed of the Turia, which was drained after the 1957 flood.
tokens.image_credit: Jcca76 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: L'Oceanogràfic
tokens.description: L'Oceanogràfic is an oceanarium in the Garden of the Turia in Valencia, Spain, with representations of different marine habitats. It was designed by Félix Candela and is part of the City of Arts and Sciences.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fallas
tokens.description: The Fallas is a traditional celebration held each March in Valencia, Spain, when the Falla monuments are burnt. The five main days are 15 to 19 March, with a daily pyrotechnic mascletà from 1 to 19 March.
tokens.image_credit: Falconaumanni · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ibiza
tokens.description: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Mediterranean Sea, off the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula. It is the third largest of the Balearic Islands by area and the second largest by population.

tokens.name: Mallorca
tokens.description: Mallorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands and the seventh largest island in the Mediterranean Sea. Its capital, Palma, is also the capital of the Balearic Islands.
tokens.image_credit: Pierre Markuse from Hamm, Germany · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Menorca
tokens.description: Menorca, also spelled Minorca, is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean Sea and belongs to Spain. Its capital is Mahón, on the eastern end of the island.
tokens.image_credit: SentinelHub · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Formentera
tokens.description: Formentera is a Spanish island in the Mediterranean Sea and the smallest and most southerly of the Pityusic Islands. It belongs to the Balearic Islands autonomous community.
tokens.image_credit: Fabian Hurst · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Es Vedrà
tokens.description: Es Vedrà is a small uninhabited rocky island off the southwestern coast of Ibiza, Spain. It rises 413 metres and lies within the Cala d'Hort nature reserve.
tokens.image_credit: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Maspalomas
tokens.description: Maspalomas is a tourist resort in the south of Gran Canaria, in the Canary Islands, Spain. It includes the resort towns of San Agustín and Playa del Inglés.
tokens.image_credit: Marc Ryckaert (MJJR) · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Teide National Park
tokens.description: Teide National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site on Tenerife in the Canary Islands, Spain. It is centred on Mount Teide, the highest mountain in Spain at 3,718 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Ingo Mehling · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tenerife
tokens.description: Tenerife is the largest and most populous island of the Canary Islands, an autonomous community of Spain, in the Atlantic Ocean off northwest Africa. It is dominated by Teide, the highest mountain in Spain.
tokens.image_credit: European Space Agency · CC BY-SA 3.0 igo · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lanzarote
tokens.description: Lanzarote is a Spanish island, the easternmost of the Canary Islands, about 125 kilometres off the north coast of Africa. It covers 845.94 square kilometres and is the fourth-largest island in the archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Yummifruitbat assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Timanfaya National Park
tokens.description: Timanfaya National Park is a volcanic national park in the southwest of Lanzarote in the Canary Islands, Spain. It covers 51.07 square kilometres of volcanic terrain within the island's UNESCO biosphere reserve.
tokens.image_credit: MiljenkoSuljic · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fuerteventura
tokens.description: Fuerteventura is one of the Canary Islands in the Atlantic Ocean, about 97 km off the coast of North Africa, and politically part of Spain. UNESCO declared the island a biosphere reserve in 2009.
tokens.image_credit: Asybaris01 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Costa del Sol
tokens.description: The Costa del Sol is a coastal region in southern Spain, in Andalusia, along the Province of Málaga. Formerly a set of fishing settlements, it is now a world-renowned tourist destination.
tokens.image_credit: Mike McBey · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Marbella
tokens.description: Marbella is a city and municipality on the Mediterranean coast of Málaga province in southern Spain. It is a central resort town of the Costa del Sol, set in the foothills of the Sierra Blanca.
tokens.image_credit: Milan Trninic (www.wedesignmarbella.com) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Puerto Banús
tokens.description: Puerto Banús is a luxury marina and shopping complex in Nueva Andalucía, southwest of Marbella on the Costa del Sol. Built in 1970 by the developer José Banús, it is one of the region's largest entertainment centres.
tokens.image_credit: __Lolo__ · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ronda
tokens.description: Ronda is a municipality in the province of Málaga in Andalusia, southern Spain. The town sits on a plateau split by the deep gorge known as El Tajo, which is carried by the Guadalevín river.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral
tokens.description: The Santiago de Compostela Cathedral is the reputed burial place of Saint James the Great, one of the apostles of Jesus Christ. It is part of the Santiago de Compostela World Heritage Site in Galicia, Spain.
tokens.image_credit: Fernando · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
tokens.description: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is a museum of modern and contemporary art in Bilbao, Biscay, Spain. It is one of several museums affiliated to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation and opened in 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Naotake Murayama · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Sebastián
tokens.description: San Sebastián, or Donostia in Basque, is a coastal city in the Basque Autonomous Community of northern Spain. It is the capital of the province of Gipuzkoa, on the Bay of Biscay about 20 km from the French border.
tokens.image_credit: Keta · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Beach of La Concha
tokens.description: The Beach of La Concha is a crescent-shaped urban beach in the city of San Sebastián, on the Bay of La Concha in the Basque Country of northern Spain. It is often cited as one of the most famous urban beaches in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Kent Wang · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rioja DOCa
tokens.description: Rioja DOCa is a wine region in northern Spain, with grapes grown in La Rioja, Navarre and the Basque province of Álava. It holds the highest category in Spanish wine regulation and is divided into three zones.
tokens.image_credit: Adbar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ribera del Duero
tokens.description: Ribera del Duero is a Spanish wine denomination on the northern plateau of Castile and León, along the course of the Duero river. The region is centred on the town of Aranda de Duero and has a largely flat, rocky terrain.
tokens.image_credit: LBM1948 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jerez de la Frontera
tokens.description: Jerez de la Frontera is a city and municipality in the province of Cádiz, Andalusia, in southwestern Spain. With about 215,000 inhabitants it is the most populous municipality in Cádiz province.
tokens.image_credit: Tango7174 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Priorat DOQ
tokens.description: Priorat DOQ is a Denominació d'Origen Qualificada for powerful red wines from the Priorat county in the province of Tarragona, Catalonia. The appellation covers 11 municipalities.

tokens.name: Pamplona
tokens.description: Pamplona is the capital city of the Chartered Community of Navarre in northern Spain. Its population was 208,243 in 2024, making it the 29th largest city in Spain.
tokens.image_credit: José Luis Filpo Cabana · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Running of the bulls
tokens.description: A running of the bulls is an event in which people run ahead of a small group of bulls let loose on sectioned-off streets of a town, usually during a summer festival. The event is found in Spain and southern France.
tokens.image_credit: No machine-readable author provided. Johnbojaen assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Picos de Europa
tokens.description: The Picos de Europa are a mountain range about 20 km long, part of the Cantabrian Mountains in northern Spain. The range lies in Asturias, Cantabria and Castile and León, and its highest peak is Torre de Cerredo at 2,650 m.
tokens.image_credit: Evölah · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belém Tower
tokens.description: Belém Tower is a 16th-century fortification in Lisbon, Portugal, used as a departure and return point for Portuguese explorers. It is a Manueline monument and part of the UNESCO World Heritage property shared with the Jerónimos Monastery.
tokens.image_credit: Alvesgaspar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jerónimos Monastery
tokens.description: The Jerónimos Monastery is a former monastery of the Order of Saint Jerome in Belém, Lisbon, Portugal, and a leading example of Manueline architecture. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property shared with the Tower of Belém.
tokens.image_credit: Dirk Stoop · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alfama
tokens.description: Alfama is the oldest neighborhood of Lisbon, Portugal, on the slope between São Jorge Castle and the Tagus river. It is known for its historic sites and its Fado bars and restaurants.
tokens.image_credit: TeWeBs · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
tokens.description: Time Out Market Lisboa is a food hall in the Mercado da Ribeira at Cais do Sodré in Lisbon, Portugal. The market brings together restaurants, bars and food stalls under one roof.
tokens.image_credit: Sonse · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Justa Lift
tokens.description: The Santa Justa Lift is a historic iron elevator in the Baixa district of Lisbon, Portugal. It links the Rua de Santa Justa street with the Largo do Carmo square.
tokens.image_credit: Dicklyon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lisbon Oceanarium
tokens.description: The Lisbon Oceanarium is an oceanarium in the Parque das Nações district of Lisbon, Portugal. It is one of the largest indoor aquariums in Europe and receives about one million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Costa, European Commission · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Estádio da Luz
tokens.description: The Estádio da Luz is a multi-purpose stadium in Lisbon, Portugal, owned by the football club Sport Lisboa e Benfica. It opened on 25 October 2003 and hosts the club's home matches.

tokens.name: Livraria Lello
tokens.description: Livraria Lello & Irmão is a historic bookshop in Porto, Portugal, housed in a neo-Gothic building that was formerly the Livraria Chardron. It is one of the oldest bookstores in Portugal.
tokens.image_credit: Guinness323 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ribeira Square
tokens.description: Ribeira Square, known in Portuguese as Praça da Ribeira, is a historical square in Porto, Portugal. It sits on the riverside Ribeira quarter, inside the UNESCO Historic Centre of Porto.
tokens.image_credit: Alvesgaspar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Douro DOC
tokens.description: Douro DOC is a Portuguese wine region centred on the Douro River in the Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro region. It is the wine region known as the Douro Valley, with terraced vineyards along the river.
tokens.image_credit: Marco Varisco from Albany, New York, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sintra
tokens.description: Sintra is a town and municipality in the Greater Lisbon region of Portugal, on the Portuguese Riviera. The town and its hills are a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape known for Romantic palaces and gardens.
tokens.image_credit: Singa Hitam · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Quinta da Regaleira
tokens.description: Quinta da Regaleira is a manor house with gardens, built from 1904 to 1910, near the historic centre of Sintra, Portugal. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Cultural Landscape of Sintra.
tokens.image_credit: Kent Wang · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cabo da Roca
tokens.description: Cabo da Roca is the westernmost point of mainland Portugal and of continental Europe, on the Sintra Mountain Range west of Lisbon. A lighthouse has operated on the cape since 1772.
tokens.image_credit: Olga1969 · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cascais
tokens.description: Cascais is a town and municipality on the Estoril Coast in the Lisbon District of Portugal. It is a major tourist destination with about 214,000 inhabitants in the municipality.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nazaré
tokens.description: Nazaré is a resort town and municipality on the Silver Coast in the Leiria District of Portugal. The municipality has about 14,900 inhabitants.
tokens.image_credit: Kent Wang · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Praia da Marinha
tokens.description: Praia da Marinha is a beach with sea cliffs and rock arches on the Atlantic coast of the Algarve, in the Lagoa municipality. It was rated by the Michelin Guide among the most beautiful beaches in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Klugschnacker · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Algarve
tokens.description: The Algarve is the southernmost region of continental Portugal, with 16 municipalities and about 467,000 permanent inhabitants. Its administrative centre is the city of Faro.
tokens.image_credit: Steven Fruitsmaak · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Madeira
tokens.description: Madeira is an autonomous region of Portugal, an island group in the Atlantic Ocean about 805 km southwest of mainland Portugal. It is the southernmost point and region of Portugal.

tokens.name: Azores
tokens.description: The Azores is an archipelago of Portugal in the Atlantic Ocean, about 1,400 km west of mainland Portugal. It is the westernmost point and region of Portugal.
tokens.image_credit: Guillaume Baviere from Helsingborg, Sweden · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sete Cidades Massif
tokens.description: Sete Cidades Massif is a stratovolcanic complex and caldera in the western part of São Miguel island in the Azores. Its summit caldera holds the twin Lagoa das Sete Cidades lakes.
tokens.image_credit: Verónica Vasconcelos · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fátima
tokens.description: Fátima is a city in the Ourém municipality of the Santarém District of Portugal. It is the site of the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fátima, linked to the Marian apparitions of 1917 at Cova da Iria.
tokens.image_credit: Kent Wang · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Damrak
tokens.description: Damrak is an avenue and partly filled-in canal in the centre of Amsterdam, running from Amsterdam Centraal station to Dam Square. It is one of the main routes from the station into the city centre.
tokens.image_credit: M.Minderhoud · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dam Square
tokens.description: Dam Square is a town square in Amsterdam, the capital and most populous city of the Netherlands. Its notable buildings and frequent events make it one of the best-known locations in the city and the country.
tokens.image_credit: Deerpeter · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Anne Frank House
tokens.description: The Anne Frank House is a writer's house and biographical museum on the Prinsengracht canal in central Amsterdam. Diarist Anne Frank hid with her family and four others in its rear building during the Nazi occupation.
tokens.image_credit: Dietmar Rabich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heineken Experience
tokens.title: Amsterdam beer giant
tokens.description: The Heineken Experience is a corporate visitor centre in a historic brewery in Amsterdam. It presents the history of the Dutch pilsner Heineken beer.

tokens.name: Vondelpark
tokens.description: Vondelpark is a 47-hectare public urban park in the Amsterdam-Zuid borough, west of Leidseplein and Museumplein. It opened in 1865 as Nieuwe Park and was renamed after the poet Joost van den Vondel.
tokens.image_credit: Dguendel · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Albert Cuyp Market
tokens.description: The Albert Cuyp Market is a street market on the Albert Cuypstraat in the De Pijp district of Amsterdam. It grew out of an informal collection of street traders and pushcarts.
tokens.image_credit: Michiel1972 at Dutch Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rembrandtplein
tokens.description: Rembrandtplein is a major square in central Amsterdam, named after the painter Rembrandt van Rijn, who owned a house nearby from 1639 to 1656. A statue of Rembrandt stands on the square.
tokens.image_credit: Marion Golsteijn · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Keukenhof
tokens.title: Tulip garden of Europe
tokens.description: Keukenhof is one of the world's largest flower gardens, in the municipality of Lisse in the Netherlands. Its 32 hectares are planted with about 7 million flower bulbs each year, mostly tulips.
tokens.image_credit: Urdulife · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kinderdijk
tokens.description: Kinderdijk is a town in the municipality of Molenlanden in South Holland, about 15 km east of Rotterdam. Its historic windmills, the Mill Network at Kinderdijk-Elshout, have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
tokens.image_credit: Lucas Hirschegger · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zaanse Schans
tokens.description: Zaanse Schans is a neighbourhood of Zaandam near Zaandijk in the Netherlands. It is known for its historic windmills and wooden houses, moved here from the wider Zaanstreek region for preservation.
tokens.image_credit: Zairon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Giethoorn
tokens.description: Giethoorn is a village in the province of Overijssel in the Netherlands, known for its canals and thatched farmhouses with no through roads. It is a popular tourist destination often called the Venice of the Netherlands.
tokens.image_credit: Bert Knot · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Madurodam
tokens.description: Madurodam is a miniature park in the Scheveningen district of The Hague, Netherlands. It features 1:25 scale models of famous Dutch landmarks and cities and opened in 1952.
tokens.image_credit: Cqui · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Efteling
tokens.description: Efteling is a fantasy-themed theme park in Kaatsheuvel, Netherlands, with attractions based on European myths, fairy tales and folklore. The park opened on 31 May 1952.
tokens.image_credit: Rémih · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Euromast
tokens.description: Euromast is an observation tower in Rotterdam, Netherlands, built between 1958 and 1960 for the 1960 Floriade. It is a listed monument since 2010.
tokens.image_credit: F.Eveleens · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Markthal
tokens.description: Markthal is a residential and office building in Rotterdam, Netherlands, with a covered market hall beneath it. It opened on 1 October 2014 and houses 228 apartments.
tokens.image_credit: Exmpletree · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cube Houses
tokens.description: The Cube Houses are tilted cube-shaped residential buildings in Rotterdam, Netherlands, designed by architect Piet Blom. They sit on hexagonal pylons above the Blaak area and were built in the early 1980s.
tokens.image_credit: Suicasmo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zandvoort
tokens.description: Zandvoort is a municipality and beach resort on the North Sea coast in North Holland, Netherlands. It is bordered by the dunes of Zuid-Kennemerland National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Ziko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atomium
tokens.description: The Atomium is a landmark modernist structure in Brussels, Belgium, built as the centrepiece of the 1958 Brussels World's Fair. It is a steel model of an iron crystal unit cell magnified 165 billion times, and houses a museum.
tokens.image_credit: Zairon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand-Place
tokens.description: The Grand-Place is the central square of Brussels, Belgium, surrounded by Baroque guildhalls, the Flamboyant Town Hall and the King's House. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
tokens.image_credit: Celuici · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Manneken Pis
tokens.description: Manneken Pis is a bronze fountain sculpture of a urinating boy in central Brussels, Belgium, first attested in the mid-15th century. The current statue was put in place in 1619 and is one of the city's best known landmarks.
tokens.image_credit: Bruxelles_Manneken_Pis.jpg: Myrabella derivative work: Myrabella (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mini-Europe
tokens.description: Mini-Europe is a miniature park at the foot of the Atomium in Brussels, Belgium. It displays scale reproductions of about 350 buildings and 80 cities from across Europe at a scale of 1:25.
tokens.image_credit: Gellerj · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries
tokens.description: The Royal Saint-Hubert Galleries are three glazed shopping arcades in central Brussels, Belgium. They were designed by Jean-Pierre Cluysenaar and built between 1846 and 1847.
tokens.image_credit: KoS · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Delirium Café
tokens.description: Delirium Café is a bar in Brussels, Belgium, known for its long beer list. It was recorded with 2,004 beer brands in January 2004 in the Guinness Book of Records.
tokens.image_credit: Jamie Lantzy · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Markt, Bruges
tokens.description: The Markt is the central square of Bruges, West Flanders, Belgium. On its south side stands the 13th-century Belfry, one of the city's most famous landmarks.
tokens.image_credit: Wolfgang Staudt [1] · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tomorrowland
tokens.description: Tomorrowland is a large-scale annual electronic dance music festival held in Boom, Flanders, Belgium. It was first held in 2005 at the De Schorre provincial recreational park.
tokens.image_credit: Me109zito · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ostend
tokens.description: Ostend is a coastal city and municipality in West Flanders, Belgium. It is the largest city on the Belgian coast.
tokens.image_credit: Wasily at Dutch Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zermatt
tokens.description: Zermatt is a municipality and ski resort in the canton of Valais, Switzerland. It lies at the upper end of the Mattertal, at the foot of Switzerland's highest peaks.
tokens.image_credit: Chensiyuan · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Moritz
tokens.description: St. Moritz is a municipality and high Alpine resort town in the Engadine valley of the Swiss canton of Graubünden. It lies at about 1,800 metres above sea level.
tokens.image_credit: Alps · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Verbier
tokens.description: Verbier is a village and ski area in the canton of Valais in south-western Switzerland. It is recognised as one of the premier off-piste resorts in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Leo-setä · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gstaad
tokens.description: Gstaad is a town and major ski resort in the canton of Bern, southwestern Switzerland. It is part of the municipality of Saanen and is a popular destination for high society.
tokens.image_credit: GstaadTourismus · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grindelwald
tokens.description: Grindelwald is a village and municipality in the Interlaken-Oberhasli district of the canton of Bern, Switzerland. The village lies at about 1,034 m above sea level in the Bernese Oberland.
tokens.image_credit: Cristo Vlahos · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Interlaken
tokens.description: Interlaken is a town and municipality in the Interlaken-Oberhasli district of the canton of Bern, Switzerland. It lies between Lake Brienz and Lake Thun and is the main transport gateway to the Bernese Oberland.
tokens.image_credit: Rectilinium · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Staubbach Falls
tokens.description: Staubbach Falls is a waterfall in Switzerland, located just west of Lauterbrunnen in the Bernese Highlands. It drops about 297 metres from a hanging valley above the Weisse Lütschine.
tokens.image_credit: Adrian Michael · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chillon Castle
tokens.description: Chillon Castle is a medieval island castle on Lake Geneva, south of Veytaux in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland. It is one of the most visited medieval castles in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Giles Laurent · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lavaux
tokens.description: Lavaux is a region of terraced vineyards in the canton of Vaud, Switzerland, stretching about 30 km along the north shore of Lake Geneva. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the name Lavaux, Vineyard Terraces.
tokens.image_credit: Lorenz Poffet · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Geneva
tokens.description: Lake Geneva is a deep lake on the north side of the Alps, shared by Switzerland and France. It is one of the largest lakes in Western Europe and the largest on the course of the Rhone.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jet d'Eau
tokens.description: The Jet d'Eau is a large fountain in Geneva, Switzerland, where Lake Geneva leaves the lake as the Rhone. It jets about 500 litres of water per second to a height of 150 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Wikibusters · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bahnhofstrasse
tokens.description: Bahnhofstrasse is the main downtown street of Zurich, Switzerland, and one of the world's most expensive shopping avenues. In 2011 a study named it the most expensive street for retail property in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: KeanoManu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Zurich
tokens.description: Lake Zurich is a lake in Switzerland that extends southeast of the city of Zurich. Its upper part is known as the Obersee.
tokens.image_credit: Adrian Michael · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Glacier Express
tokens.description: The Glacier Express is a named panorama train in Switzerland that links Zermatt and St. Moritz via Andermatt in the central Swiss Alps. The one-seat journey covers 291 km in about eight hours.
tokens.image_credit: Kabelleger / David Gubler (http://www.bahnbilder.ch) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bernina Express
tokens.description: The Bernina Express is a named Panorama Express train that connects Chur in Switzerland with Tirano in Italy across the Engadine Alps. It is operated by the Rhaetian Railway and runs through the Albula / Bernina Landscapes World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Kabelleger / David Gubler · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Lucerne
tokens.description: Lake Lucerne is a lake in central Switzerland and the fourth largest lake in the country. It is also known by its German name Vierwaldstättersee.
tokens.image_credit: Ttrainer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chapel Bridge
tokens.description: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden footbridge spanning the river Reuss diagonally in Lucerne, Switzerland. It is named after the nearby St. Peter's Chapel and was partly destroyed by a fire in 1993.
tokens.image_credit: Simon Koopmann · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Prater
tokens.description: The Prater is a 6 square kilometre public park in Vienna's 2nd district, Leopoldstadt. The name can also refer to the Wurstelprater amusement park within the area.
tokens.image_credit: HatschiKa · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wiener Riesenrad
tokens.description: The Wiener Riesenrad is a 64.75 metre tall Ferris wheel at the entrance of the Prater amusement park in Vienna. Constructed in 1897, it was the world's tallest extant Ferris wheel from 1920 until 1985.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Ledl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Naschmarkt
tokens.description: The Naschmarkt is a popular fruit and vegetable market in Vienna, located on the Wienzeile over the Wien River. It is about 1.5 kilometres long and was originally known as Aschenmarkt.
tokens.image_credit: C.Stadler/Bwag · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vienna State Opera
tokens.description: The Vienna State Opera is an opera house and opera company in Vienna, Austria. The 1,709-seat Renaissance Revival building was built from 1861 to 1869 and was the first major building on the Ringstrasse.
tokens.image_credit: Wiener Staatsoper GmbH · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ringstrasse
tokens.description: The Ringstrasse is a 5.3 kilometre circular grand boulevard that serves as a ring road around the historic Innere Stadt of Vienna, Austria. It was built where the city walls once stood.
tokens.image_credit: Gugerell · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Café Central
tokens.description: Café Central is a traditional Viennese coffeehouse at Herrengasse 14 in the Innere Stadt, Vienna. It occupies the ground floor of the Palais Ferstel, the former Bank and Stock Exchange building designed by Heinrich von Ferstel.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Ledl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
tokens.description: Hohensalzburg Fortress is a large medieval fortress in the city of Salzburg, Austria. It sits atop the Festungsberg at an altitude of 506 metres and was erected at the behest of the prince-archbishops of Salzburg.
tokens.image_credit: C.Stadler/Bwag · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mirabell Palace
tokens.description: Mirabell Palace is a historic baroque palace with formal gardens in Salzburg, Austria. The palace and its gardens are a listed monument within the Historic Centre of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Przemek Pietrak · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kitzbühel
tokens.description: Kitzbühel is a medieval town in the Kitzbühel Alps in Tyrol, Austria, and the administrative centre of Kitzbühel District. It is a well-known ski resort that hosts the Hahnenkamm Races.
tokens.image_credit: Wolfgang Glock · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: St. Anton am Arlberg
tokens.description: St. Anton am Arlberg is a village and ski resort in the Tyrolean Alps of Austria. Aerial tramways and chairlifts rise to 2,811 metres, with a vertical drop of 1,507 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Gemeinde St. Anton am Arlberg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ischgl
tokens.description: Ischgl is a town in the Paznaun valley of Tyrol, Austria. Its ski resort is linked with Samnaun in Switzerland to form one of the largest ski areas in the Alps.
tokens.image_credit: Basotxerri · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sölden
tokens.description: Sölden is a municipality in the Ötztal valley of Tyrol, Austria. It is an Alpine village used as a base for skiing and mountain tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Leo-setä · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Roof
tokens.description: The Golden Roof is a late Gothic oriel in the Old Town of Innsbruck, Austria, and the city's best-known symbol. It was completed in 1500 with 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles on its roof.
tokens.image_credit: Daderot · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Eisriesenwelt
tokens.description: Eisriesenwelt is a limestone and ice cave in the Hochkogel mountain of the Tennengebirge, near Werfen in Austria, about 40 km south of Salzburg. It is described as the largest ice cave in the world, extending more than 42 km.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Melk Abbey
tokens.description: Melk Abbey is a Benedictine abbey above the town of Melk in Lower Austria, on a rocky outcrop overlooking the Danube. The abbey lies within the Wachau Cultural Landscape UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Ledl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wachau
tokens.description: The Wachau is an Austrian valley formed by the Danube River between Melk and Krems in Lower Austria, known for its wines. It is part of the Wachau Cultural Landscape UNESCO World Heritage property.
tokens.image_credit: C.Stadler/Bwag · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Red Bull Ring
tokens.description: The Red Bull Ring is a 4.3 km motorsport race track in Spielberg, Styria, Austria. It was founded as the Österreichring and hosted the Austrian Grand Prix from 1970 to 1987 and again from 1997 to 2003.
tokens.image_credit: Vanessa Machelett · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
tokens.description: The Louisiana Museum of Modern Art is an art museum north of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is Scandinavia's most visited museum for modern and contemporary art, with over 700,000 guests a year.
tokens.image_credit: Lars Plougmann · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tivoli Gardens
tokens.description: Tivoli Gardens is an amusement park and pleasure garden in Copenhagen, Denmark, opened on 15 August 1843. It is the second-oldest operating amusement park in the world, after Dyrehavsbakken.
tokens.image_credit: Elgaard · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Little Mermaid, Copenhagen
tokens.description: The Little Mermaid is a bronze statue by Edvard Eriksen, depicting a mermaid becoming human. It sits on a rock by the Langelinie promenade in Copenhagen, Denmark, and is 1.25 metres tall.
tokens.image_credit: Avda-berlin · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Strøget
tokens.description: Strøget is a pedestrian, car-free shopping street in the centre of Copenhagen, Denmark. At 1.1 km it is one of the longest pedestrian shopping streets in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Olga Itenberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Copenhagen Opera House
tokens.description: The Copenhagen Opera House is the national opera house of Denmark, described as one of the most modern opera houses in the world. It cost about 2.5 billion DKK to build.
tokens.image_credit: Julian Herzog (Website) · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rosenborg Castle
tokens.description: Rosenborg Castle is a Renaissance castle in Copenhagen, Denmark, first built in 1606 as a country summerhouse. It is an example of the architectural projects of King Christian IV.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kronborg
tokens.description: Kronborg is a castle and historical stronghold in Helsingør, Denmark. Immortalised as Elsinore in Shakespeare's Hamlet, it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2000.
tokens.image_credit: ArildV · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Billund
tokens.description: Billund is a town in Jutland, Denmark, with a population of 7,446 as of 1 January 2026. It is the second largest town in Billund Municipality, behind Grindsted.
tokens.image_credit: HartOve · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skagen
tokens.description: Skagen is the northernmost town in Denmark, on the Skagen Odde peninsula in northern Jutland. The Port of Skagen is Denmark's main fishing port, and the town attracts about 2 million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: De-okin (talk) 15:41, 25 July 2009 (UTC) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Møns Klint
tokens.description: Møns Klint is a 6 km stretch of limestone and chalk cliffs on the east coast of the Danish island of Møn in the Baltic Sea. Some cliffs fall a sheer 120 metres to the sea, and the site has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since July 2025.
tokens.image_credit: Bob Collowan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stockholm Archipelago
tokens.description: The Stockholm Archipelago is the largest archipelago in Sweden and the second-largest in the Baltic Sea. It comprises over 24,000 islands, islets and skerries.
tokens.image_credit: Esquilo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gamla stan
tokens.description: Gamla stan is the old town of Stockholm, Sweden, mainly on the island Stadsholmen. It has about 3,000 residents and includes the islets Riddarholmen, Helgeandsholmen and Strömsborg.
tokens.image_credit: Arild Vågen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: ABBA The Museum
tokens.description: ABBA The Museum is an interactive exhibition about the Swedish pop band ABBA. It opened in May 2013 on Djurgården in Stockholm, Sweden.
tokens.image_credit: I99pema · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skansen
tokens.description: Skansen is the oldest open-air museum and zoo in Sweden, on the island Djurgården in Stockholm. It opened on 11 October 1891 to show ways of life in different parts of Sweden before the industrial era.

tokens.name: Drottninggatan
tokens.description: Drottninggatan (Queen Street) is a major pedestrian street in Stockholm, Sweden. It runs north from the Riksbron bridge at Norrström to Observatorielunden in Vasastaden.

tokens.name: Stockholm City Hall
tokens.description: Stockholm City Hall is the seat of Stockholm Municipality, on the eastern tip of Kungsholmen island by Riddarfjärden. It houses municipal offices, conference rooms and ceremonial halls.
tokens.image_credit: ArildV · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Avicii Arena
tokens.description: Avicii Arena, formerly Ericsson Globe, is a multi-purpose arena in Stockholm, Sweden, locally called Globen. It is the second largest spherical building on Earth, after the Las Vegas Sphere.
tokens.image_credit: Alexandar Vujadinovic · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Icehotel
tokens.description: The Icehotel is a hotel in the village of Jukkasjärvi, about 17 km from Kiruna in northern Sweden. It is rebuilt each year from snow and ice and is the world's first ice hotel.
tokens.image_credit: Stephan Herz (User:Stephan_Herz) · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Abisko National Park
tokens.description: Abisko National Park is a national park in northern Sweden, established in 1909. It lies in the Abisko area of Swedish Lapland, near the Kiruna region.
tokens.image_credit: Lapplaender · CC BY-SA 2.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kebnekaise
tokens.description: Kebnekaise is the highest mountain in Sweden, in the Scandinavian mountain range. Its northern, ice-free peak is 2,096.8 metres above sea level, now higher than the glaciated southern peak.
tokens.image_credit: Photographer: Mg-k. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Åre
tokens.description: Åre is a locality and one of the leading ski resorts in Scandinavia, in Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden. Tourism, mainly downhill skiing and biking, provides about 25% of the local economy.
tokens.image_credit: Skistar (talk · contribs) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sigtuna
tokens.description: Sigtuna is a locality in the west of Sigtuna Municipality, Stockholm County, Sweden, with 9,689 inhabitants in 2020. The municipal seat is the nearby locality of Märsta.
tokens.image_credit: Arild Vågen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Liseberg
tokens.description: Liseberg is an amusement park in Gothenburg, Sweden, that opened in 1923. It is the second most visited theme park in Scandinavia, with around three million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Lennart Guldbrandsson · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Visby
tokens.description: Visby is an urban area and the seat of Gotland Municipality on the island of Gotland, Sweden, with 24,330 inhabitants in 2017. Its medieval walled town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1995 as the Hanseatic Town of Visby.
tokens.image_credit: L.G.foto · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gotland
tokens.description: Gotland is Sweden's largest island, in the Baltic Sea. It is also a province, municipality and diocese, and the province includes Fårö, Gotska Sandön and the Karlsö Islands.

tokens.name: Oslo Opera House
tokens.description: The Oslo Opera House is the home of the Norwegian National Opera and Ballet and the national opera house of Norway. It stands in the Bjørvika district of central Oslo, at the head of the Oslofjord.
tokens.image_credit: Rafał Konieczny · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Holmenkollen
tokens.description: Holmenkollen is a mountain and neighbourhood in the Vestre Aker borough of Oslo, Norway, rising to 500 metres above sea level. It is known for its international skiing competitions, including the Holmenkollen Ski Festival held there since 1892.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Härtelt · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aker Brygge
tokens.description: Aker Brygge is a neighbourhood on the waterfront of central Oslo, Norway, formerly known as Holmen. It was an industrial area before becoming a popular place for shopping, dining and entertainment from the 1980s and 1990s.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Nyborg · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bryggen
tokens.description: Bryggen is a series of Hanseatic heritage commercial buildings along the eastern side of the Vågen harbour in Bergen, Norway. It has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1979.
tokens.image_credit: Stch2022 · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fløibanen
tokens.description: Fløibanen is a funicular railway in Bergen, Norway, connecting the city centre with the mountain Fløyen. It is one of Bergen's major tourist attractions and one of Norway's most visited attractions.
tokens.image_credit: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Geirangerfjord
tokens.description: Geirangerfjord is a 15 km long branch of the Sunnylvsfjorden in Stranda Municipality, Norway. It is part of the West Norwegian Fjords UNESCO World Heritage property, inscribed in 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nærøyfjord
tokens.description: Nærøyfjord is a 17 km long branch of the Aurlandsfjord in Aurland Municipality, Norway. It is part of the West Norwegian Fjords UNESCO World Heritage property, inscribed in 2005.
tokens.image_credit: Karamell · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kjeragbolten
tokens.description: Kjeragbolten is a boulder wedged in a crevice on the Kjerag mountain in Sandnes Municipality, Norway. It is a popular tourist destination that can be reached without climbing equipment.
tokens.image_credit: Scoundrelgeo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trollstigen
tokens.description: Trollstigen is a serpentine mountain road and pass in Rauma Municipality, Norway, with eleven hairpin bends on a steep mountainside. It is part of County Road 63 between Åndalsnes and Valldal.
tokens.image_credit: Stefan Krause, Germany · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
tokens.description: The Atlantic Ocean Road is an 8.3 km section of County Road 64 that links the island of Averøya with the mainland across an archipelago. It crosses the exposed Hustadvika coast in Møre og Romsdal, Norway.
tokens.image_credit: Ernst Vikne · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: North Cape
tokens.description: North Cape is a cape on the northern coast of Magerøya in Nordkapp Municipality, Norway. The European route E69 ends there, making it the northernmost public road in Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Helsinki Cathedral
tokens.description: Helsinki Cathedral is the Evangelical Lutheran cathedral of the Diocese of Helsinki, at Senate Square in the centre of Helsinki, Finland. It was built from 1830 to 1852.
tokens.image_credit: Hans Hillewaert · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Suomenlinna
tokens.description: Suomenlinna is a sea fortress built from 1748 on islands off Helsinki, Finland. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and a popular destination for visitors.
tokens.image_credit: Migro · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Temppeliaukio Church
tokens.description: Temppeliaukio Church is a Lutheran church in the Töölö district of Helsinki, Finland, built into the granite bedrock. Designed by Timo and Tuomo Suomalainen, it was completed in 1969.
tokens.image_credit: Pertsaboy. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Claus Village
tokens.description: Santa Claus Village is an amusement park and tourist complex in Rovaniemi, a city in the Lapland region of Finland. It opened in 1980.
tokens.image_credit: Floppyjb · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rovaniemi
tokens.description: Rovaniemi is a city in Finland and the regional capital of Lapland, located near the Arctic Circle. The city has a population of approximately 66,000.
tokens.image_credit: MattiKSinisalo at Finnish Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rukatunturi
tokens.description: Rukatunturi is a 492 metre fell and ski resort in Kuusamo, Finland. It offers downhill skiing and over 500 km of cross-country ski tracks.
tokens.image_credit: Alfred Dengan at fi.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Nuuksio National Park
tokens.description: Nuuksio National Park is one of Finland's 40 national parks, established in 1994. It covers forests and lakes in Espoo, Kirkkonummi and Vihti, north-west of Helsinki.
tokens.image_credit: Christophe Badoux · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Finnish Lakeland
tokens.description: Finnish Lakeland is a large landscape region in central eastern Finland, a hilly, forest-covered lake plateau shaped by drumlins and eskers. These glacial landforms date from the ice retreat about 10,000 years ago.
tokens.image_credit: kallerna · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hallgrímskirkja
tokens.description: Hallgrímskirkja is a Lutheran parish church in Reykjavík, Iceland. At 74.5 metres it is the largest church in Iceland, completed in 1986.
tokens.image_credit: Steinninn · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Harpa Concert Hall
tokens.description: Harpa is a concert hall and conference centre in Reykjavík, Iceland. It opened with a concert on 4 May 2011, and its glass façade is inspired by the basalt landscape of Iceland.
tokens.image_credit: Ivan Sabljak, arkitekt: Hennings Larsens in Denmark · CC-BY-SA-3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gullfoss
tokens.description: Gullfoss is a waterfall in the canyon of the Hvítá river in southwest Iceland. It is one of the most popular tourist attractions in the country and lies on the Golden Circle tour route.
tokens.image_credit: Andreas Tille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Geysir
tokens.description: Geysir is a geyser in the Haukadalur valley of southwest Iceland, the source of the English word geyser. Geological studies suggest it started forming around 1150 CE.
tokens.image_credit: Chmee2/Valtameri · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skógafoss
tokens.description: Skógafoss is a waterfall on the Skógá River in southern Iceland, at the cliff that marks the former coastline. The cliff divides the coastal lowlands from the Highlands of Iceland.
tokens.image_credit: Gerd Eichmann · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Seljalandsfoss
tokens.description: Seljalandsfoss is a waterfall of about 60 metres in southern Iceland, beside Route 1. It is part of the Seljalands River, which has its origin in the Eyjafjallajökull glacier.
tokens.image_credit: Zoran Kurelić Rabko · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reynisfjara
tokens.description: Reynisfjara is a popular black sand beach in southern Iceland, near the town of Vík í Mýrdal. It lies within the Katla UNESCO Global Geopark, on privately owned land.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jökulsárlón
tokens.description: Jökulsárlón is a large glacial lake in southern Vatnajökull National Park in Iceland. It formed at the head of the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier after the glacier began receding in the late 19th century.
tokens.image_credit: Molechaser · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kirkjufell
tokens.description: Kirkjufell is a 463 metre high hill on the north coast of the Snæfellsnes peninsula in Iceland, near the town of Grundarfjörður. It is claimed to be the most photographed mountain in the country.
tokens.image_credit: Steven Diaz stevendiazphoto · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dettifoss
tokens.description: Dettifoss is a waterfall in Vatnajökull National Park in northeast Iceland, on the Jökulsá á Fjöllum river. It is reputed to be the second most powerful waterfall in Europe, after the Rhine Falls.
tokens.image_credit: Spike · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mývatn
