tokens.description: Mývatn is a shallow lake in an area of active volcanism in northern Iceland, near the Krafla volcano. The lake and its surrounding wetlands provide habitat for many waterbirds, especially ducks.
tokens.image_credit: Pjt56 --- If you use the picture outside Wikipedia I would appreciate a short e-mail to pjt56@gmx.net or a message on my discussion page · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Landmannalaugar
tokens.description: Landmannalaugar is a location in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve in the Icelandic Highlands, on the edge of the Laugahraun lava field. The lava field formed in an eruption around 1477.
tokens.image_credit: User:Chris 73 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vestmannaeyjar
tokens.description: Vestmannaeyjar, sometimes called the Westman Islands, is a municipality and archipelago off the south coast of Iceland. The largest island, Heimaey, has about 4,500 inhabitants, most living in the main town.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skaftafell
tokens.description: Skaftafell is a preservation area in Öræfi in southeast Iceland, once a major farm. It was later named a national park and is now part of Vatnajökull National Park.
tokens.image_credit: Eysteinn Guðni Guðnason · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sky Lagoon
tokens.description: Sky Lagoon is a geothermal spa in southwestern Iceland. The spa offers geothermal pools, a cold plunge and saunas.
tokens.image_credit: Laurenmcl · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: De Wallen
tokens.description: De Wallen is the largest and best known red-light district in Amsterdam. It is a network of alleys and canals where sex workers offer services from behind windows.
tokens.image_credit: Rungbachduong · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel Sacher
tokens.description: Hotel Sacher is a five-star luxury hotel in Vienna, Austria, facing the Vienna State Opera. It is famous for the Original Sachertorte, a chocolate cake with apricot filling.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Frankenstein · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Swarovski Kristallwelten
tokens.description: Swarovski Kristallwelten is an experience attraction in Wattens, Tyrol, Austria, created by André Heller for the crystal maker Swarovski. It opened in 1995 and includes a park, an art museum, a shop and a restaurant.
tokens.image_credit: Marek Śliwecki · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Globe of Science and Innovation
tokens.description: The Globe of Science and Innovation is a visitor centre at CERN in Meyrin in the Canton of Geneva, Switzerland. The wooden sphere was built for Expo.02 in Neuchâtel and moved to Meyrin in 2004.
tokens.image_credit: Tryfon Kar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rigi
tokens.description: Rigi is a mountain massif in the Alps of Central Switzerland, almost surrounded by Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz. Its main summit, Rigi Kulm, rises to 1,797 metres.
tokens.image_credit: Andrew Bossi · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belfry of Bruges
tokens.description: The Belfry of Bruges is a medieval bell tower in the centre of Bruges, Belgium. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage property Belfries of Belgium and France.
tokens.image_credit: Adiel lo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reine, Norway
tokens.description: Reine is the administrative centre of Moskenes Municipality on the island of Moskenesøya in the Lofoten archipelago, Norway. The fishing village lies above the Arctic Circle and has a church.
tokens.image_credit: Jörg Hempel · CC BY-SA 2.0 de · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Freetown Christiania
tokens.description: Freetown Christiania is an intentional community and former army barracks in the Christianshavn district of Copenhagen, Denmark. It began in 1971 as a squatted military base.
tokens.image_credit: Bruno Jargot · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Frogner Park
tokens.description: Frogner Park is a public park in the Frogner district of Oslo, Norway. It contains the Vigeland installation, a large group of sculptures by Gustav Vigeland.
tokens.image_credit: Christian David · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg
tokens.description: The Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg is a district of Salzburg, Austria, on both banks of the Salzach river. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Pintaric (= Pintaric) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Þingvellir
tokens.description: Þingvellir is a national park in southwestern Iceland, about 40 km northeast of Reykjavík. It was the site of the Alþing, Iceland's parliament, from 930 to 1798 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Andreas Tille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Caves of Han-sur-Lesse
tokens.description: The Caves of Han-sur-Lesse are a cave complex in Wallonia, Belgium, formed by the river Lesse eroding a limestone hill. They are a major Belgian tourist attraction, with around 250,000 to 300,000 visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: user:Hullie · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Strahov Monastery
tokens.description: Strahov Monastery is a Premonstratensian abbey in the Strahov district of Prague, Czech Republic. It was founded in 1143 by Jindřich Zdík, Bishop John of Prague and Vladislaus II, Duke of Bohemia.
tokens.image_credit: Matěj Baťha · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Josefov
tokens.description: Josefov is a town quarter and the smallest cadastral area of Prague, Czech Republic, formerly the Jewish ghetto of the town. It lies within the Prague Historic Centre World Heritage Site.
tokens.image_credit: Martin Pauer (Power) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Karlovy Vary
tokens.description: Karlovy Vary is a spa town in the Karlovy Vary Region of the Czech Republic, with about 49,000 inhabitants. It is located at the confluence of the Ohře and Teplá rivers.
tokens.image_credit: rboed* · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Great Market Hall
tokens.description: The Great Market Hall, also called Central Market Hall, is the largest and oldest indoor market in Budapest, Hungary. Its opening ceremony took place on 15 February 1897.
tokens.image_credit: Thaler Tamas · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Andrássy Avenue
tokens.description: Andrássy Avenue is a boulevard in Budapest, Hungary, dating back to 1872. It links Erzsébet Square with the Városliget and was recognised as a World Heritage Site in 2002.
tokens.image_credit: User Sndr on en.wikipedia · Copyrighted free use · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Margaret Island
tokens.description: Margaret Island is a 2.5 km long island in the middle of the Danube in central Budapest, Hungary. It is mostly covered by landscape parks and is a popular recreational area.
tokens.image_credit: Ralf Roletschek · CC BY-SA 1.0 fi · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tokaj wine region
tokens.description: Tokaj wine region is a historical wine region in northeastern Hungary and southeastern Slovakia, known for sweet wines such as Tokaji Aszu. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2002.
tokens.image_credit: Jerzy Kociatkiewicz from Colchester, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old Town, Warsaw
tokens.description: Old Town is the oldest district of Warsaw, Poland, with many 17th and 18th century buildings rebuilt after the Second World War. It lies within the Historic Centre of Warsaw, a UNESCO World Heritage property inscribed in 1980.
tokens.image_credit: Carlos Delgado · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Warsaw Rising Museum
tokens.description: The Warsaw Rising Museum in the Wola district of Warsaw is dedicated to the Warsaw Uprising of 1944. It opened on 31 July 2004, on the 60th anniversary of the uprising.
tokens.image_credit: Adrian Grycuk · CC BY 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews
tokens.description: The POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews in Warsaw is dedicated to the history and memory of Jews in Poland. It stands on the site of the former Warsaw Ghetto.
tokens.image_credit: Wojciech Kryński · CC BY-SA 3.0 pl · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kazimierz
tokens.description: Kazimierz is a historic district of Krakow, Poland, formerly an independent royal city and long home to a large Jewish community. It is one of the core ensembles of the UNESCO World Heritage Historic Centre of Krakow.
tokens.image_credit: Zygmunt Put Zetpe0202 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zakopane
tokens.description: Zakopane is a town in southern Poland at the foot of the Tatra Mountains, in the Podhale region. It is a well known winter sports and mountain tourism centre.
tokens.image_credit: Maksym Kozlenko · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Długi Targ
tokens.description: Długi Targ, also known as Long Market, is a historic square in Gdańsk, Poland, on the Royal Route between Długa Street and the Green Gate. It is one of the most notable tourist attractions of the city.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Market Square, Wrocław
tokens.description: The Market Square in Wrocław, Poland, is a medieval market square and pedestrian zone, one of the largest market squares in Europe. It holds two city halls, including the largest city hall in Poland.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Most SNP
tokens.description: Most SNP is a cable-stayed road bridge over the Danube in Bratislava, Slovakia. It is known as the UFO Bridge because of the restaurant on top of its single pylon.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Triple Bridge
tokens.description: The Triple Bridge comprises three bridges over the Ljubljanica River in Ljubljana, Slovenia, linking the old town with Prešeren Square. Dating back to the 13th century, it is the oldest bridge in Ljubljana.
tokens.image_credit: Luka Peternel · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vršič Pass
tokens.description: Vršič Pass is a high mountain pass across the Julian Alps in northwestern Slovenia, at 1,611 metres the highest pass in Slovenia. It connects Upper Carniola with the Trenta Valley.
tokens.image_credit: Petar Milošević · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vis, Croatia
tokens.description: Vis is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea, held in turn by the Liburnians, Venice, the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy and the Austrian Empire. Two naval battles took place to the north of the island in the 19th century.
tokens.image_credit: Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rovinj
tokens.description: Rovinj is a town on the western coast of the Istrian peninsula in western Croatia, with about 13,000 inhabitants in 2021. It is a tourist resort and an active fishing port.
tokens.image_credit: Florian Hirzinger - http://www.fh-ap.com · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Zagreb Cathedral
tokens.description: Zagreb Cathedral is a Catholic Gothic cathedral in Kaptol, Zagreb, and the tallest sacral building in Croatia. The original Romanesque church was completed in 1217 and heavily damaged during the Tatar invasion of 1242.
tokens.image_credit: Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dolac Market
tokens.description: Dolac is a farmers' market in Zagreb, Croatia, known for its red umbrella stalls. It lies above Ban Jelačić Square, between the Gradec and Kaptol districts.
tokens.image_credit: Rilegator · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Baščaršija
tokens.description: Baščaršija is the old bazaar and historical centre of Sarajevo, built from the 15th century. It is also a local community within the Stari Grad municipality.
tokens.image_credit: Yukof · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Budva
tokens.description: Budva is a town on the Adriatic coast of Montenegro, centre of Budva Municipality, with about 17,500 inhabitants in 2023. It is known for its medieval walled old town and its beaches.
tokens.image_credit: Nick Savchenko from Kiev, Ukraine · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Belgrade Fortress
tokens.description: The Belgrade Fortress is a historic citadel and cultural monument at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers, in Kalemegdan Park. It forms the historical core of Belgrade, the capital of Serbia.
tokens.image_credit: Oliver Bunic · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Knez Mihailova Street
tokens.description: Knez Mihailova Street is the main pedestrian and shopping street of Belgrade, Serbia. Named after Prince Mihailo Obrenović III, it is protected as one of the city's oldest cultural landmarks.
tokens.image_credit: DKjellby · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skadarlija
tokens.description: Skadarlija is a vintage street and urban neighborhood in Belgrade, Serbia, known as the city's bohemian quarter. It has been protected as a cultural-historical unit since 1967.

tokens.name: Ada Ciganlija
tokens.description: Ada Ciganlija is a former river island in the Sava in central Belgrade, turned into a peninsula by artificial works. It is a major recreational zone with beaches, the artificial Lake Sava and sports facilities.
tokens.image_credit: Lumen roma · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Exit Festival
tokens.description: EXIT is an annual music festival held in Serbia since 2000, traditionally staged at the Petrovaradin Fortress in Novi Sad. It attracts around 200,000 visitors in recent editions.
tokens.image_credit: Benny Gaši/EXIT Photo Team · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyramid of Tirana
tokens.description: The Pyramid of Tirana is a pyramid-shaped building in the Albanian capital. It opened as a museum in 1988, became a conference centre in 1991, and was used as a NATO base during the 1999 Kosovo War.
tokens.image_credit: BBB2021 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Skanderbeg Square
tokens.description: Skanderbeg Square is the main plaza in the centre of Tirana, the capital of Albania. It is named after the Albanian national hero Skanderbeg and covers about 40,000 square metres.
tokens.image_credit: Leeturtle · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ksamil
tokens.description: Ksamil is a village and former municipality on the Albanian Riviera in southern Albania. Since the 2015 local government reform it is a subdivision of the municipality of Sarandë.
tokens.image_credit: Cannm01 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Valbona Valley
tokens.description: The Valbona Valley is in the Albanian Alps of northern Albania. It lies within the Alps of Albania National Park and forms part of the southernmost continuation of the Dinaric Alps.
tokens.image_credit: You may re-use this image under the terms of the license using the following reference: Image: Wikipedia / Tobias Klenze / CC-BY-SA 4.0. The license must be a link! · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bansko
tokens.description: Bansko is a town in southwestern Bulgaria, near the city of Razlog. Once a stockbreeding and merchant community, it is now an international centre for winter and summer tourism.
tokens.image_credit: Интерпрайм Банско Недвижими Имоти · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Borovets
tokens.description: Borovets is a mountain resort in Samokov Municipality, Sofia Province, Bulgaria. It was known as Chamkoria until the middle of the 20th century, and the closest town is Samokov.
tokens.image_credit: Biser Todorov · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sunny Beach
tokens.description: Sunny Beach is a seaside resort on the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria, about 35 km north of Burgas. Created in 1958 as a weekend getaway, it has become the largest tourist resort in the country.
tokens.image_credit: www.vacacionesbulgaria.com · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Sands
tokens.description: Golden Sands is a major seaside resort town on the northern Bulgarian Black Sea coast, 17 km north of Varna. It is known for its fine golden sand and is one of the largest tourist destinations on the Black Sea.
tokens.image_credit: Svilen Enev · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old Town Plovdiv
tokens.description: Old Town Plovdiv is a historic architectural and historical reserve on three hills in Plovdiv, Bulgaria. It combines architecture from Antiquity, the Middle Ages and the Bulgarian Revival, and has been on UNESCO's tentative list since 2004.
tokens.image_credit: Faces&&Places · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brașov
tokens.description: Brașov is a city in Transylvania, Romania, and the county seat of Brașov County. The 2021 census counted 237,589 inhabitants, making it the sixth most populous city in Romania.
tokens.image_credit: Constantin Barbu · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Transalpina
tokens.description: Transalpina, also known as DN67C, is a 148 km national road in the Parâng Mountains of the Southern Carpathians, Romania. It links Novaci and Sebeș, and its summit at Urdele Pass, at 2,145 m, makes it the highest road in Romania.
tokens.image_credit: Saturnian · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sinaia
tokens.description: Sinaia is a town and mountain resort in Prahova County, Romania, in the historical region of Muntenia. The town grew up around the Sinaia Monastery, founded in 1695, and is home to Peleș Castle.
tokens.image_credit: TiberiuSahlean · CC BY-SA 3.0 ro · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Poiana Brașov
tokens.description: Poiana Brașov is a ski resort and neighbourhood of Brașov in Romania. After modernisation in the 2010s its ski area grew to 80 hectares, with slopes totalling 23.9 km.
tokens.image_credit: Kdanv · CC BY 3.0 ro · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cricova
tokens.description: Cricova is a town in Chișinău municipality, Moldova, about 15 km north of the capital. It is known for its vast underground wine cellars, among the largest in the world.

tokens.name: Mileștii Mici
tokens.description: Mileștii Mici is a commune in Ialoveni District, Moldova, made up of the villages Mileștii Mici and Piatra Albă. It lies about 18 km from Chișinău, and locals have long quarried white stone from beneath the village.
tokens.image_credit: Анатолий Зубанюк · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kadriorg Park
tokens.description: Kadriorg Park is a park of about 70 hectares in the Kadriorg district of Tallinn, Estonia. Its history began in 1718, when Peter the Great ordered the grounds of his Fonnenthal summer manor to be redesigned.
tokens.image_credit: Mait Metsur, aerofotod.ee · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tallinn TV Tower
tokens.description: Tallinn TV Tower is a 313 m free-standing tower with an observation deck, near the Pirita suburb about six km north-east of Tallinn's centre. It was built to improve telecommunications for the 1980 Moscow Olympic sailing regatta.
tokens.image_credit: Dmitry G · PD · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lahemaa National Park
tokens.description: Lahemaa National Park is a national park in northern Estonia, about 70 km east of Tallinn, on the Gulf of Finland. Its 747 km2 area includes 274.9 km2 of sea.
tokens.image_credit: Lysy · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saaremaa
tokens.description: Saaremaa is the largest and most populous island in Estonia, covering 2,673 km2 in the Baltic Sea. It is the main island of the Moonsund archipelago.
tokens.image_credit: Abrget47j · CC BY-SA 3.0 ee · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Old Riga
tokens.description: Vecrīga, or Old Riga, is the historic centre and a neighbourhood of Riga, the capital of Latvia. It lies on the east bank of the Daugava river and is part of the UNESCO Historic Centre of Riga.
tokens.image_credit: Jorge Franganillo from Barcelona, Spain · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Riga Central Market
tokens.description: Riga Central Market is described by Wikipedia as Europe's largest market, in Riga, Latvia. Built from 1924 to 1930, it is included in the UNESCO World Heritage listing together with Old Riga.
tokens.image_credit: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: House of the Blackheads
tokens.description: The House of the Blackheads is a guild building in the old town of Riga, Latvia. The original building was erected in 1334 as a warehouse and meeting place for merchants.
tokens.image_credit: Diliff · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Freedom Monument
tokens.description: The Freedom Monument in Riga, Latvia, honours soldiers killed in the Latvian War of Independence from 1918 to 1920. Unveiled in 1935, the 42-metre granite and copper monument is a national symbol of Latvian independence.
tokens.image_credit: Nenea hartia · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jūrmala
tokens.description: Jūrmala is a state city and seaside resort on the Gulf of Riga, about 25 kilometres west of Riga, Latvia. It has a 33 kilometre stretch of white-sand beach and is the fifth-largest city in Latvia.
tokens.image_credit: Roquai · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gauja National Park
tokens.description: Gauja National Park is the largest national park in Latvia, covering 917.86 square kilometres along the Gauja River valley in Vidzeme. It is known for its sandstone cliffs, forests and many historical and cultural monuments.
tokens.image_credit: Gatis Pāvils · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Gediminas's Tower
tokens.description: Gediminas's Tower is the surviving part of the Upper Castle on Gediminas Hill in Vilnius, Lithuania. Its viewing platform overlooks the Vilnius Old Town and it is a national symbol of Lithuania.
tokens.image_credit: BigHead · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hill of Crosses
tokens.description: The Hill of Crosses is a Catholic pilgrimage site about 12 km north of Siauliai in northern Lithuania. Pilgrims have left crosses, statues and rosaries there for generations since the 1831 Uprising.
tokens.image_credit: Thomas Stegh · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trakai Island Castle
tokens.description: Trakai Island Castle is a medieval brick castle on an island in Lake Galve, in Trakai, Lithuania. Construction began in the 14th century under Kestutis, and Vytautas the Great completed major works around 1409.
tokens.image_credit: Ana · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Užupis
tokens.description: Užupis is a bohemian neighbourhood of Vilnius, Lithuania, on the far bank of the Vilnia River. It is known for its artist community and its self-declared republic.
tokens.image_credit: Augustas Didžgalvis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Minsk Hero City Obelisk
tokens.description: Minsk Hero City Obelisk is a 45 metre monument on Victors Avenue in Minsk, Belarus. It honours the city's Hero City title, declared in 1974 for its resistance during the Nazi occupation, and opened in 1985.
tokens.image_credit: Vseslav · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Khreshchatyk
tokens.description: Khreshchatyk is the main street of Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine. It runs about 1.2 kilometres from European Square through the Maidan to Bessarabska Square.
tokens.image_credit: Київська міська рада · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mother Ukraine
tokens.description: Mother Ukraine is a monumental Soviet-era statue in Kyiv, Ukraine, part of the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War. In 2023 its shield was changed to show the Ukrainian tryzub.
tokens.image_credit: Арманов · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lviv Market Square
tokens.description: Market Square is the central square of Lviv, Ukraine, laid out in the mid-14th century as the centre of the new city. It is a rectangle of about 142 by 129 metres with two streets radiating from each corner.
tokens.image_credit: https://www.flickr.com/people/jlascar/ Jorge Láscar · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bukovel
tokens.description: Bukovel is a ski resort in the Carpathian Mountains of Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, western Ukraine. Wikipedia describes it as the largest ski resort in Eastern Europe.
tokens.image_credit: Водник at Russian Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Askania-Nova
tokens.description: Askania-Nova is a biosphere reserve in Kherson Oblast, southern Ukraine, within the dry Tauride steppe. It conserves native steppe habitat and endemic species and keeps rare and exotic animals.

tokens.name: John Hancock Center
tokens.description: The John Hancock Center is a 100-storey, 344-metre skyscraper on North Michigan Avenue in Chicago, Illinois. When it topped out in 1968 it was the second-tallest building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Chris Rycroft from Madison, Wisconsin, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Aon Center
tokens.description: The Aon Center is an 83-storey, 346-metre skyscraper at 200 East Randolph Street in the Loop, Chicago. Completed in 1973 as the Standard Oil Building, it is the fourth-tallest building in the city.
tokens.image_credit: MusikAnimal · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
tokens.description: A 100-story skyscraper condo-hotel in the Near North Side of downtown Chicago, designed by Adrian Smith of Skidmore, Owings and Merrill. Built between 2005 and 2009, it reaches 423.2 m including its spire.
tokens.image_credit: Basil D Soufi · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magnificent Mile
tokens.description: The Magnificent Mile is the roughly one-mile stretch of Michigan Avenue from the Chicago River to Oak Street on the Near North Side of Chicago. It is the main commercial corridor between the Loop and the Gold Coast.
tokens.image_credit: TonyTheTiger at English Wikipedia (Original text: en:User:TonyTheTiger) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Navy Pier
tokens.description: Navy Pier is a 1,010 m pier on the shoreline of Lake Michigan in the Streeterville neighborhood of Chicago. It holds shops, restaurants, theatres, gardens and exhibition halls, and draws over nine million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Millennium Park
tokens.description: Millennium Park is a 9.9 ha public park in the Loop of Chicago, opened in July 2004 on the northwest part of Grant Park. It features public art, gardens and venues such as the Jay Pritzker Pavilion.
tokens.image_credit: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cloud Gate
tokens.description: Cloud Gate is a public sculpture by Anish Kapoor, built between 2004 and 2006 at Millennium Park in Chicago. Nicknamed The Bean, it is made of 168 welded stainless steel plates with a highly polished surface.

tokens.name: Wrigley Field
tokens.description: Wrigley Field is a ballpark on the North Side of Chicago, first opened in 1914 as Weeghman Park. It is the home ballpark of the Chicago Cubs of Major League Baseball.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Soldier Field
tokens.description: Soldier Field is a multi-purpose stadium on the Near South Side of Chicago, opened in 1924. It has been the home of the Chicago Bears of the NFL since 1971 and of Chicago Fire FC since 2020.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shedd Aquarium
tokens.description: Shedd Aquarium is a public aquarium on the Chicago lakefront, opened on May 30, 1930. It holds about 32,000 animals and is one of the oldest continually operating non-governmental aquariums in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Sea Cow · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
tokens.description: Lincoln Park Zoo is a 14 ha zoo in Lincoln Park, Chicago, founded in 1868. It is one of the oldest zoos in the United States and one of a small number of zoos with free admission.
tokens.image_credit: Jrbarc! · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Art Institute of Chicago
tokens.description: The Art Institute of Chicago is a private, nonprofit art museum in Grant Park, founded in 1879. It is one of the oldest and largest art museums in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: ajay_suresh · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: One World Trade Center
tokens.description: One World Trade Center, also known as One WTC and the Freedom Tower, is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan. It is the tallest building in the United States.
tokens.image_credit: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chrysler Building
tokens.description: The Chrysler Building is an Art Deco skyscraper at 42nd Street and Lexington Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 1930, it was the world's tallest building for 11 months.
tokens.image_credit: Ferfive · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Woolworth Building
tokens.description: The Woolworth Building is a Neo-Gothic early skyscraper at 233 Broadway in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan, New York City. It was the tallest building in the world from 1913 to 1930.
tokens.image_credit: Copyright by The Pictorial News Co., N.Y. No. NN 98. {{PD-US}}; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 21:01, 27 September 2011 (UTC) · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hearst Tower
tokens.description: The Hearst Tower is a glass skyscraper at 57th Street and Eighth Avenue near Columbus Circle in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It is the world headquarters of the media company Hearst Communications.
tokens.image_credit: Dreamword · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: 432 Park Avenue
tokens.description: 432 Park Avenue is a residential skyscraper at 57th Street and Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 2015, it was the tallest residential building in the world at that time.
tokens.image_credit: Epistola8 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Central Park Tower
tokens.description: Central Park Tower is a residential supertall skyscraper at 217 West 57th Street on Billionaires' Row in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 2020, it is the tallest primarily residential building in the world.
tokens.image_credit: Percival Kestreltail · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: One Vanderbilt
tokens.description: One Vanderbilt is a 62-story supertall skyscraper at 42nd Street and Vanderbilt Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It opened in 2020 and is the city's fourth-tallest building.
tokens.image_credit: Percival Kestreltail · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hudson Yards
tokens.description: Hudson Yards is a neighborhood on the West Side of Midtown Manhattan, New York City, between 30th and 41st Streets. It is the site of a large-scale redevelopment that extends Midtown westward toward the Hudson River.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Vessel
tokens.description: Vessel is a 16-story honeycomb-like structure of connected staircases in the Hudson Yards Public Square in Manhattan, New York City. It was designed by Thomas Heatherwick.
tokens.image_credit: Epicgenius · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fifth Avenue
tokens.description: Fifth Avenue is a major thoroughfare in Manhattan, New York City, running from West 143rd Street in Harlem to Washington Square Park. Its Midtown section is one of the most expensive shopping streets in the world.
tokens.image_credit: A. Balet · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Broadway
tokens.description: Broadway is a major thoroughfare running about 21 km from Battery Place in lower Manhattan through the Bronx and into Westchester County, New York. Its Midtown section is home to the Broadway theatre district.
tokens.image_credit: Unknown author · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rockefeller Center
tokens.description: Complex of 19 commercial buildings covering 22 acres in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. The 14 original Art Deco buildings were commissioned by the Rockefeller family.
tokens.image_credit: David Shankbone · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Yankee Stadium
tokens.description: Baseball stadium in the Bronx, New York City, home field of the New York Yankees of Major League Baseball. It opened in April 2009, one block north of the original Yankee Stadium site.
tokens.image_credit: vtravelled.com · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: High Line
tokens.description: Elevated linear park and greenway on the West Side of Manhattan, New York City, created on a former New York Central Railroad spur. It is 1.45 miles (2.33 km) long.
tokens.image_credit: Wil Fyfordy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chelsea Market
tokens.description: Food hall, shopping mall, office building and television production facility in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. The complex occupies an entire city block.
tokens.image_credit: Beyond My Ken · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Coney Island
tokens.description: Neighborhood and entertainment area in the southwestern section of Brooklyn, New York City, on the Coney Island peninsula. The peninsula also includes Sea Gate, Brighton Beach and Manhattan Beach.
tokens.image_credit: OptimumPx · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
tokens.description: Park of 85 acres (34 ha) on the Brooklyn side of the East River in New York City. It lies along a 1.3-mile (2.1 km) stretch of waterfront from Atlantic Avenue to Jay Street.
tokens.image_credit: Jim.henderson · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bronx Zoo
tokens.description: Zoo within Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City, covering 265 acres (107 ha) of park lands and naturalistic habitats. It is one of the largest zoos in the United States by area.

tokens.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
tokens.description: Botanical garden in central Brooklyn, New York City, occupying 52 acres (21 ha). It holds over 14,000 taxa of plants and has over 800,000 visitors each year.
tokens.image_credit: Andre Carrotflower · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: New York Botanical Garden
tokens.description: Botanical garden at Bronx Park in the Bronx, New York City, established in 1891 on a 250-acre (100 ha) site. It holds over one million living plants and the Enid A. Haupt Conservatory.
tokens.image_credit: Krzysztof Ziarnek, Kenraiz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Waldorf Astoria New York
tokens.description: Luxury hotel and residential condominium building in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, at 301 Park Avenue. It is a 47-story Art Deco structure completed in 1931.
tokens.image_credit: ajay_suresh · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Plaza Hotel
tokens.description: The Plaza Hotel is a luxury hotel and condominium building on Grand Army Plaza, at the southeastern corner of Central Park in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.
tokens.image_credit: Yarl · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel Chelsea
tokens.description: The Hotel Chelsea is a historic hotel at 222 West 23rd Street in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Built in 1883 and 1884, it has been home to many writers, musicians and artists.
tokens.image_credit: Eden, Janine and Jim from New York City · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chinatown, Manhattan
tokens.description: Chinatown is a neighborhood of Lower Manhattan in New York City, home to the highest concentration of Chinese people in the Western Hemisphere. It is one of the oldest Chinese ethnic enclaves.
tokens.image_credit: Famartin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Little Italy, Manhattan
tokens.description: Little Italy is a neighborhood in Lower Manhattan in New York City, known for its Italian American population. It lies between Chinatown, Nolita, SoHo and Tribeca.
tokens.image_credit: Mario A. P. · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Greenwich Village
tokens.description: Greenwich Village, or simply the Village, is a neighborhood on the west side of Lower Manhattan in New York City, bounded by 14th Street, Broadway, Houston Street and the Hudson River. Its name comes from the Dutch Groenwijck.
tokens.image_credit: Felix Stahlberg · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: SoHo, Manhattan
tokens.description: SoHo, short for South of Houston Street, is a neighborhood in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Since the 1970s it has been home to many artists' lofts and art galleries, and to many shops.
tokens.image_credit: Axel Tschentscher · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Griffith Observatory
tokens.description: Griffith Observatory is a public observatory on the south-facing slope of Mount Hollywood in Griffith Park, Los Angeles, California. It overlooks the Los Angeles Basin and has a close view of the Hollywood Sign.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew Field · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rodeo Drive
tokens.description: Rodeo Drive is a two-mile street in Beverly Hills, California, with its southern segment in the City of Los Angeles. It is known as one of the most expensive streets in the world.
tokens.image_credit: jjron · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sunset Strip
tokens.description: The Sunset Strip is a 1.7-mile stretch of Sunset Boulevard that passes through West Hollywood, California. It is known for its boutiques, restaurants, rock clubs and colorful billboards.
tokens.image_credit: MikeJiroch · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Venice, Los Angeles
tokens.description: Venice is a neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, founded by Abbot Kinney in 1905 as a seaside resort town. Its beach and boardwalk, Venice Beach, lie on the Pacific coast.
tokens.image_credit: DanielMichaelPerry · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Santa Monica Pier
tokens.description: The Santa Monica Pier is a large pier at the foot of Colorado Avenue in Santa Monica, California. It contains a small amusement park, concession stands and areas for fishing and views.
tokens.image_credit: Jelson25 · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Malibu, California
tokens.description: Malibu is a beach city in the Santa Monica Mountains region of Los Angeles County, California, about 30 miles west of Los Angeles. It has a strip of Pacific beaches and is known as home to many Hollywood residents.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Tillman at English Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
tokens.title: Universal City backlot
tokens.description: Universal Studios Hollywood is a film studio and theme park in Universal City, California, near Hollywood, Los Angeles. It is owned by NBCUniversal and is one of the oldest Hollywood film studios still in use.
tokens.image_credit: Alec GeoSimonian · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Disney California Adventure
tokens.description: Disney California Adventure is a 72-acre theme park at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California. It is themed to Disney's interpretation of California and uses Disney Animation, Pixar and Marvel properties.
tokens.image_credit: Craig Conley · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Knott's Berry Farm
tokens.description: Knott's Berry Farm is a 57-acre amusement park in Buena Park, California, owned and operated by Six Flags. It officially opened as Knott's Berry Farm in 1947 and is among the most visited amusement parks in North America.
tokens.image_credit: METRO96 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain
tokens.description: Six Flags Magic Mountain is a 209-acre amusement park in unincorporated Los Angeles County, just outside Santa Clarita, California. It opened in 1971 as Magic Mountain and was bought by Six Flags in 1979.
tokens.image_credit: METRO96 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dodger Stadium
tokens.description: Dodger Stadium is a ballpark in the Elysian Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. It has been the home of the Los Angeles Dodgers since it opened in 1962.
tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: SoFi Stadium
tokens.description: SoFi Stadium is a multi-purpose indoor stadium in Inglewood, California, a suburb of Los Angeles. It opened in September 2020 and has a translucent ETFE roof.
tokens.image_credit: Troutfarm27 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rose Bowl Stadium
tokens.description: The Rose Bowl is an outdoor athletic stadium in Pasadena, California. Opened in October 1922, it is a National Historic Landmark.
tokens.image_credit: Ted Eytan · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Crypto.com Arena
tokens.description: Crypto.com Arena, formerly Staples Center, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in downtown Los Angeles, California. It opened in October 1999 and is the home venue of the Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Kings.
tokens.image_credit: Troutfarm27 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
tokens.description: Walt Disney Concert Hall is a concert hall in downtown Los Angeles, California, designed by Frank Gehry and opened in 2003. It is the home of the Los Angeles Philharmonic orchestra.
tokens.image_credit: Carol M. Highsmith · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Getty Center
tokens.description: The Getty Center is a museum campus in Los Angeles, California, run by the Getty Trust and home to the Getty Museum. It opened to the public in 1997 on a hill in the Santa Monica Mountains.
tokens.image_credit: Derbrauni · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grand Central Market
tokens.description: Grand Central Market is a historic public food market in downtown Los Angeles, California. It opened in 1917 in the Homer Laughlin Building and has operated continuously since then.

tokens.name: Wilshire Grand Center
tokens.description: Wilshire Grand Center is a 335 metre skyscraper in downtown Los Angeles, California, completed in 2017. With its spire it is the tallest building in the United States west of Chicago.
tokens.image_credit: Fredchang931124 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: U.S. Bank Tower
tokens.description: U.S. Bank Tower, formerly the First Interstate Bank World Center, is a 310 metre skyscraper in downtown Los Angeles, California. Completed in 1989, it was designed by Henry N. Cobb of Pei Cobb Freed and Partners.
tokens.image_credit: Selvingarcia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: The Beverly Hills Hotel
tokens.description: The Beverly Hills Hotel is a landmark hotel on Sunset Boulevard in Beverly Hills, California, known for its pink and green exterior. It has 210 guest rooms and suites and 23 bungalows.
tokens.image_credit: Minnaert · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chateau Marmont
tokens.description: Chateau Marmont is a historic hotel at 8221 Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood, California. Completed in 1929, it was designed by Arnold A. Weitzman and William Douglas Lee.
tokens.image_credit: Tony Mariotti from Los Angeles, United States · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Los Angeles Zoo
tokens.description: The Los Angeles Zoo and Botanical Gardens is a 133-acre zoo in Griffith Park, Los Angeles, California. It was founded in 1966 and is owned by the City of Los Angeles.

tokens.name: Huntington Library
tokens.description: The Huntington Library, Art Museum and Botanical Gardens is a collections-based institution in San Marino, California, founded by Henry E. and Arabella Huntington. It holds an art collection and about 120 acres of botanical gardens.

tokens.name: San Diego Zoo
tokens.description: The San Diego Zoo is a zoo in Balboa Park, San Diego, California, started from animals left over from the 1915 Panama-California Exposition. It was a pioneer of open-air exhibits without cages.

tokens.name: La Jolla Cove
tokens.description: La Jolla Cove is a small cove with a beach surrounded by cliffs in La Jolla, a community of San Diego, California. The area is protected as a marine reserve and is popular with snorkelers, swimmers and divers.
tokens.image_credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hotel del Coronado
tokens.description: The Hotel del Coronado is a historic beachfront hotel in Coronado, California, across San Diego Bay from San Diego. It is a rare surviving wooden Victorian beach resort and a National Historic Landmark since 1977.
tokens.image_credit: Armandoartist · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Transamerica Pyramid
tokens.description: The Transamerica Pyramid is a 48-story pyramid-shaped modernist skyscraper in San Francisco's Financial District. It was the city's tallest building from 1972 until 2017.
tokens.image_credit: Supercarwaar · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Salesforce Tower
tokens.description: Salesforce Tower, formerly Transbay Tower, is a 61-story supertall skyscraper in the South of Market district of San Francisco. Its main tenant is the cloud software company Salesforce.
tokens.image_credit: Dead.rabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lombard Street, San Francisco
tokens.description: Lombard Street is an east to west street in San Francisco, known for a steep one-block section with eight hairpin turns. Most of its western segment is part of U.S. Route 101.
tokens.image_credit: Érico Andrei · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco
tokens.description: Fisherman's Wharf is a neighborhood and tourist area on the northern waterfront of San Francisco. It was a working fishing port until its docks declined in the 1960s and 1970s as tourism took over.
tokens.image_credit: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, photographer not specified or unknown · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pier 39
tokens.description: Pier 39 is a shopping center and tourist attraction built on a pier in San Francisco. It has shops, restaurants, an aquarium and a marina where California sea lions haul out on the docks.
tokens.image_credit: jjron · GFDL 1.2 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Painted Ladies, San Francisco
tokens.description: The Painted Ladies are a row of Victorian houses on Steiner Street, facing Alamo Square in San Francisco. The houses are repainted in several colours that accentuate their architectural details.
tokens.image_credit: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Haight-Ashbury
tokens.description: Haight-Ashbury is a district of San Francisco named for the intersection of Haight and Ashbury streets. It is known as one of the main centers of the counterculture of the 1960s.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Schwen · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Chinatown, San Francisco
tokens.description: Chinatown in San Francisco, centered on Grant Avenue and Stockton Street, is the oldest Chinatown in North America. Established in the early 1850s, it is one of the largest Chinese enclaves outside Asia.
tokens.image_credit: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Francisco cable car system
tokens.description: The San Francisco cable car system is the world's last manually operated cable car system and an icon of the city. Of the 23 lines built between 1873 and 1890, three remain, serving Union Square, Fisherman's Wharf and California Street.
tokens.image_credit: Pi.1415926535 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Alcatraz Island
tokens.description: Alcatraz Island is a small island about 1.25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay. It hosted a lighthouse and a military fortification before becoming the federal prison Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in 1934.
tokens.image_credit: Frank Schulenburg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: San Francisco Ferry Building
tokens.description: The San Francisco Ferry Building is a terminal for ferries across San Francisco Bay, with a food hall and offices. Its 245-foot clock tower can be seen from Market Street.
tokens.image_credit: Daniel Lu (User:dllu) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Golden Gate Park
tokens.description: Golden Gate Park is an urban park on the west side of San Francisco, covering 1,017 acres. It is the third most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 24 million visitors a year.
tokens.image_credit: Dennis G. Jarvis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oracle Park
tokens.description: Oracle Park is a ballpark in the South Beach neighborhood of San Francisco, on the shore of San Francisco Bay. It has been the home of the San Francisco Giants of Major League Baseball since 2000.
tokens.image_credit: Dllu · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Napa Valley
tokens.description: Napa Valley is an American Viticultural Area in Napa County, California, established in 1981 as the nation's second. It is one of the world's premier wine regions, with viticulture dating back to the nineteenth century.
tokens.image_credit: Ebryden at English Wikipedia · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sonoma Valley
tokens.description: Sonoma Valley is a valley in southeastern Sonoma County, California, in the North Bay of the San Francisco Bay Area. It is known as the birthplace of the California wine industry, with some of the state's earliest vineyards and wineries.
tokens.image_credit: TJM97 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lake Tahoe
tokens.description: Lake Tahoe is a freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada straddling the California and Nevada border. At 6,225 feet above sea level, it is the largest alpine lake in North America.
tokens.image_credit: Lara Farhadi · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Heavenly Mountain Resort
tokens.description: Heavenly Mountain Resort is a ski resort on the California and Nevada border in southeastern Lake Tahoe, in the Sierra Nevada. It opened as Heavenly Valley in 1955 and has 97 runs and 30 lifts.

tokens.name: Palisades Tahoe
tokens.description: Palisades Tahoe is a ski resort in Olympic Valley, California, in the Sierra Nevada. Founded in 1949 as Squaw Valley, it hosted the 1960 Winter Olympics and was renamed in 2021.
tokens.image_credit: 9yz · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.description: The plains zebra (Equus quagga, formerly Equus burchellii) is the most common and geographically widespread species of zebra. Its range is fragmented, but spans much of southern and eastern Africa south of the Sahara.

tokens.name: Blue wildebeest
tokens.title: Blue wildebeest
tokens.description: The blue wildebeest (Connochaetes taurinus), also called the common wildebeest, white-bearded gnu or brindled gnu, is a large antelope and one of the two species of wildebeest. It is placed in the genus Connochaetes and family Bovidae, and has a close taxonomic relationship with the black wildebeest.

tokens.name: Giant forest hog
tokens.title: Giant forest hog
tokens.description: The giant forest hog (Hylochoerus meinertzhageni), the only member of its genus (Hylochoerus), is native to wooded habitats in Africa and is one of the largest wild members of the pig family, Suidae, along with a few subspecies of the wild boar. It was first described in 1904.

tokens.name: Scimitar oryx
tokens.title: Scimitar oryx
tokens.description: The scimitar oryx (Oryx dammah), also known as the scimitar-horned oryx and the Sahara oryx, is an Oryx species that was once widespread across North Africa and parts of West and Central Africa. In 2000 it was declared extinct in the wild on the IUCN Red List, but in 2023 it was downlisted to endangered, with a reintroduced population in Chad.
tokens.image_credit: Charles J. Sharp · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Addax
tokens.title: Addax
tokens.description: The addax (Addax nasomaculatus) is an antelope native to the Sahara, also known as the white antelope and the screwhorn antelope. The only member of the genus Addax, it was first described scientifically by Henri de Blainville in 1816.

tokens.name: Dama gazelle
tokens.title: Dama gazelle
tokens.description: The dama gazelle is a species of gazelle that lives in the Sahara desert and the Sahel of Africa. It is critically endangered, has disappeared from most of its former range due to overhunting and habitat loss, and natural populations remain only in Chad, Mali and Niger.

tokens.image_credit: Photo by David J. Stang · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Niger Delta red colobus
tokens.description: The Niger Delta red colobus is a critically endangered species of colobus monkey endemic to the western part of the Niger Delta. It is threatened by hunting and habitat loss.

tokens.name: Preuss's red colobus
tokens.title: Preuss's red colobus
tokens.description: Preuss's red colobus (Piliocolobus preussi) is a red colobus primate endemic to the Cross-Sanaga Rivers ecoregion. An important population occurs in Korup National Park, Cameroon, and the species is considered present in Cross River National Park in Nigeria.

tokens.description: The Tana River red colobus, also called the eastern red colobus, is a highly endangered species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae. It is endemic to a narrow zone of gallery forest near the Tana River in southeastern Kenya.

tokens.name: Zanzibar red colobus
tokens.title: Zanzibar red colobus
tokens.description: The Zanzibar red colobus, Piliocolobus kirkii, is a species of red colobus monkey endemic to Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago, off the coast of Tanzania. It is classified as endangered and was adopted as the flagship species for conservation in Zanzibar in the mid-1990s.

tokens.name: Angwantibo
tokens.title: Angwantibo
tokens.description: Angwantibos are two species of strepsirrhine primates in the genus Arctocebus, family Lorisidae. They are also known as golden pottos because of their yellow or golden coloration. They live in tropical Africa, with a range that includes Nigeria and Cameroon north of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

tokens.image_credit: Garst, Warren, 1922-2016, photographer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: African striped weasel
tokens.title: African striped weasel
tokens.description: The African striped weasel is a small mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa, where its range stretches from as far north as Kenya south to South Africa. It is in the family Mustelidae and is the lone member of the genus Poecilogale.

tokens.name: African clawless otter
tokens.title: African clawless otter
tokens.description: The African clawless otter, also known as the Cape clawless otter or groot otter, is the second-largest freshwater otter species. It inhabits permanent water bodies in savannah and lowland forest areas through most of sub-Saharan Africa. It is characterised by partly webbed and clawless feet, from which their name is derived.
tokens.image_credit: Mark Paxton of Shamvura Camp, Namibia, who releases it under the licenses below. JMK (talk) 20:54, 2 November 2013 (UTC) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Congo clawless otter
tokens.title: Congo clawless otter
tokens.description: The Congo clawless otter, also known as the Cameroon clawless otter, is a species in the family Mustelidae. It was formerly recognised as a subspecies of the African clawless otter. It is found in Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda and Uganda.
tokens.image_credit: IOSF1957 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: African wildcat
tokens.title: African wildcat
tokens.description: The African wildcat (Felis lybica) is a small wildcat species with sandy grey fur, pale vertical stripes on the sides and around the face. It is native to Africa, West and Central Asia, and is distributed to Rajasthan in India and Xinjiang in China. It inhabits a broad variety of landscapes ranging from deserts to savannas, shrublands and grasslands.

tokens.description: The Javan rhinoceros is a critically endangered member of the genus Rhinoceros of the family Rhinocerotidae, and one of the five remaining extant rhinoceros species. tokens.title: Malayan tapir

tokens.title: South China tiger
tokens.description: The South China tiger is a population of the Panthera tigris tigris subspecies that is native to southern China. The population mainly inhabited the Fujian, Guangdong, Hunan and Jiangxi provinces. It has been listed as Critically Endangered on China's Red List of Vertebrates and is possibly extinct in the wild since no wild individual has been recorded since the late 1980s.

tokens.name: Snow leopard
tokens.title: Snow leopard
tokens.description: The snow leopard is a felid species in the genus Panthera. It has a thick whitish to grey fur with black spots on the head and neck, with larger rosettes on the back, flanks and bushy tail. Males are larger than the females, and both sexes have long canine teeth.

tokens.name: Clouded leopard
tokens.title: Clouded leopard
tokens.description: The clouded leopard, also called mainland clouded leopard, is a wild cat that has large dusky-grey blotches and irregular spots and stripes reminiscent of clouds. It uses its long tail for balancing when moving in trees. It was first described in 1821 on the basis of a skin of an individual from China.

tokens.name: Asian black bear
tokens.title: Asian black bear
tokens.description: The Asian black bear (Ursus thibetanus), also known as the Asiatic black bear, moon bear and white-chested bear, is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia that is largely adapted to an arboreal lifestyle. It is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, and is threatened by deforestation and poaching for its body parts, which are used in traditional medicine.
tokens.image_credit: Roy Bateman · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.description: The wild water buffalo, also called Asian buffalo, Asiatic buffalo and wild buffalo, is a large bovine native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It is the most likely ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.

tokens.name: Saola
tokens.title: Saola
tokens.description: The saola (Pseudoryx nghetinhensis), also called the spindlehorn, Asian unicorn, or infrequently, Vũ Quang bovid, is a forest-dwelling bovid native to the Annamite Range in Vietnam and Laos. Saola live in restricted areas of high-altitude wet evergreen forest and have probably always had a relatively low population density.
tokens.image_credit: The original uploader was Silviculture at Vietnamese Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Kouprey
tokens.title: Kouprey
tokens.description: The kouprey, also known as the forest ox and grey ox, is a possibly extinct species of forest-dwelling wild bovine native to Southeast Asia. It was first scientifically described in 1937, and its name comes from the Khmer language and means forest ox.

tokens.title: Red Panda

tokens.title: Proboscis monkey
tokens.description: The proboscis monkey or long-nosed monkey (Nasalis larvatus) is an arboreal Old World monkey with an unusually large nose, a reddish-brown skin color and a long tail. It is endemic to the Southeast Asian island of Borneo and is found mostly in mangrove forests and on the coastal areas of the island.
tokens.image_credit: David Dennis · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Tonkin snub-nosed monkey
tokens.description: The Tonkin snub-nosed monkey or Dollman's snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus avunculus) is a slender-bodied arboreal Old World monkey endemic to northern Vietnam. It has black and white fur, a pink nose and lips, and blue patches around the eyes.

tokens.title: Myanmar snub-nosed monkey
tokens.description: The Myanmar snub-nosed monkey or black snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus strykeri) is a critically endangered species of colobine monkey described in 2010 in northern Myanmar. Two groups of the species were described in China in 2011 and 2015.

tokens.description: The siamang is an endangered arboreal, black-furred gibbon native to the tropical rainforests of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. The largest of the gibbons, the siamang can be twice the size of other gibbons, reaching 1 m in height, and weighing up to 14 kg.

tokens.name: Tapanuli orangutan
tokens.title: Tapanuli orangutan
tokens.description: The Tapanuli orangutan is a species of orangutan restricted to South Tapanuli on the island of Sumatra in Indonesia. It is one of three known living orangutan species, alongside the Sumatran and Bornean orangutans, and was described as a distinct species in 2017.

tokens.name: Mountain hare
tokens.title: Mountain hare
tokens.description: The mountain hare (Lepus timidus), also known as arctic hare, blue hare or snow hare, is a species of hare largely adapted to polar and mountainous habitats in the Palearctic realm. It is a large hare with a tail that is completely white throughout the year. Mountain hares have a brown coat in summer and white to grey in winter.
tokens.image_credit: Евгений Егорейченков · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.image_credit: Hannes Grobe/AWI · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amur hedgehog
tokens.title: Amur hedgehog
tokens.description: The Amur hedgehog (Erinaceus amurensis), also called the Manchurian hedgehog, is a hedgehog similar to the European hedgehog in appearance and behaviour, although it is more lightly coloured. It is native to Amur Oblast and Primo ryein Russia, Manchuria in China, and the Korean Peninsula.

tokens.description: The European hamster (Cricetus cricetus), also known as the common hamster, is the only living species of hamster in the genus Cricetus. It is native to grassland and similar habitats in a large part of Eurasia, extending from Belgium to Xinjiang in China.

tokens.name: Eurasian beaver
tokens.title: Eurasian beaver
tokens.description: The Eurasian beaver (Castor fiber) or European beaver is a species of beaver widespread across Eurasia, with a rapidly increasing population of 1.5 million in 2020. It was hunted to near-extinction for its fur and castoreum, and has since been reintroduced into much of its former range.

tokens.title: Wild boar
tokens.description: The wild boar (Sus scrofa), also known as the wild swine, common wild pig, Eurasian wild pig, or simply wild pig, is a suid native to much of Eurasia and North Africa and has been introduced to the Americas and Oceania. tokens.description: The sika deer (Cervus nippon), also known as the northern spotted deer or the Japanese deer, is a species of deer native to much of East Asia and introduced to other parts of the world. Previously found from northern Vietnam in the south to the Russian Far East in the north, it was overhunted to the brink of extinction in the 19th century.
tokens.image_credit: Lilly M · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Reindeer
tokens.title: Reindeer
tokens.description: The reindeer or caribou (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to the Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America. It is the only representative of the genus Rangifer.

tokens.name: Muskox
tokens.title: Muskox
tokens.description: The muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae. Native to the Arctic, it is noted for its thick coat and for the strong odor emitted by males during the seasonal rut, from which its name derives.

tokens.name: Chamois
tokens.title: Chamois
tokens.description: The chamois (Rupicapra rupicapra), or Alpine chamois, is a species of goat-antelope native to mountainous parts of Europe and Western Asia. It ranges from the Pyrenees and the Alps to the Carpathians, the Balkans and the Caucasus, and has also been introduced to the South Island of New Zealand.
tokens.image_credit: Giles Laurent · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pyrenean ibex
tokens.title: Pyrenean ibex
tokens.description: The Pyrenean ibex (Capra pyrenaica pyrenaica) was one of the four subspecies of the Iberian ibex or Iberian wild goat (Capra pyrenaica), a species native to the Iberian Peninsula and immediately adjacent southern France. The Pyrenean ibex occurred in the northeastern part of the species' range in the Cantabrian Mountains and the Pyrenees, in northern Spain and the far south of France.

tokens.name: Wolf
tokens.title: Wolf
tokens.description: The wolf (Canis lupus; pl.: wolves), also known as the grey wolf or gray wolf, is a canine native to Eurasia and North America. More than thirty subspecies of Canis lupus have been recognized, including the dog and dingo, though grey wolves, as popularly understood, include only naturally occurring wild subspecies. The wolf is the largest wild extant member of the family Canidae, and is further distinguished from other Canis species by its less pointed ears and muzzle, as well as a shorter torso and a longer tail.
tokens.image_credit: User:Mas3cf · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Ocelot
tokens.description: The ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) is a medium-sized spotted wild cat that reaches 40–50 cm (16–20 in) at the shoulders and weighs between 7 and 15.5 kg (15 and 34 lb) on average. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

It is the second largest member of the genus Urocitellus, which is part of the tribe Marmotini, along with marmots, chipmunks, prairie dogs, and other holarctic ground squirrels.

tokens.name: Peary caribou
tokens.title: Peary caribou
tokens.description: The Peary caribou (Rangifer arcticus pearyi) is a subspecies of caribou found in the Canadian high Arctic islands of Nunavut and the Northwest Territories in Canada. They are the smallest of the North American caribou, with the females weighing an average of 60 kg (130 lb) and the males 110 kg (240 lb).

tokens.description: Baird's beaked whale (Berardius bairdii), also known commonly as the northern giant bottlenose whale, North Pacific bottlenose whale, giant four-toothed whale, northern four-toothed whale and North Pacific four-toothed whale, is a species of whale in the genus Berardius of the family Ziphiidae. Baird's beaked whale and Arnoux's beaked whale are so similar that researchers have debated whether or not they are simply two populations of the same species.

tokens.title: Hubbs' beaked whale

tokens.description: The pygmy beaked whale (Mesoplodon peruvianus), also known as the bandolero beaked whale, Peruvian beaked whale and lesser beaked whale, is the smallest of the mesoplodonts and one of the newest discoveries. tokens.description: The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is a species of baleen whale and the largest marine mammal in the rorqual family Balaenopteridae. Reaching a maximum confirmed length of 29.9-30.5 m (98-100 ft) and weighing up to 190-200 t (190-200 long tons; 210-220 short tons), it is the largest animal known to have ever existed.
tokens.image_credit: NOAA Photo Library · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Magnolia
tokens.title: Magnolia
tokens.description: Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the family Magnoliaceae. Its natural range is disjunct, with a main centre in east, south and southeast Asia and a secondary centre in the Americas. Magnolias are evergreen or deciduous trees or shrubs known for their large, fragrant flowers.

tokens.description: Oncidium is a genus of about 370 species of orchid in the family Orchidaceae. It is distributed across tropical and subtropical America, from Mexico and Central America to northern Argentina, with one species, O. ensatum, extending into Florida.

tokens.title: Paphiopedilum
tokens.description: Paphiopedilum, often called the Venus slipper, is a genus of the lady slipper orchid subfamily Cypripedioideae of the flowering plant family Orchidaceae. tokens.name: Easter cactus
tokens.title: Rhipsalidopsis gaertneri
tokens.description: Rhipsalidopsis gaertneri, synonyms Schlumbergera gaertneri and Hatiora gaertneri, is a species of epiphytic cactus which belongs to the tribe Rhipsalideae within the subfamily Cactoideae of the Cactaceae. Together with the hybrid with R. rosea, Rhipsalidopsis × graeseri, it is known, in English speaking countries in the Northern Hemisphere, as Easter cactus or Whitsun cactus and is a widely cultivated ornamental plant.

tokens.name: Jade plant
tokens.title: Crassula ovata
tokens.description: Crassula ovata, commonly known as jade plant, lucky plant, money plant or money tree, is a succulent plant with small pink or white flowers that is native to the KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa, and Mozambique; it is common as a houseplant worldwide. Much of its popularity stems from the low levels of care needed; the jade plant requires little water and can survive in most indoor conditions.

tokens.description: Melaleuca is a genus of nearly 300 species of plants in the myrtle family, Myrtaceae, commonly known as paperbarks, honey-myrtles, bottlebrushes or tea-trees. They range in size from small shrubs that rarely grow to more than 1 m high, to trees up to 35 m.

It is native to East Asia, in China, Korea, Japan and the Russian Far East. It is commonly known as balloon flower, after its balloon shaped flower buds, or Chinese bellflower.

tokens.name: Fern
tokens.title: Fern
tokens.description: Ferns are a group of vascular plants that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers. They reproduce in two phases, a short lived gametophyte that reproduces sexually to develop a spore bearing leaf structure. Some ferns produce coiled fiddleheads, which expand into fronds.

tokens.name: Spider plant
tokens.title: Spider plant
tokens.description: Chlorophytum comosum, usually called spider plant, is a species of evergreen perennial flowering plant of the family Asparagaceae. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh. It is easy to grow as a houseplant because of its resilience.

tokens.description: Osmundastrum cinnamomeum, commonly known as the cinnamon fern or the buckhorn fern, is a species of royal fern native to the Americas and Asia. It is the sole living representative of the genus Osmundastrum, which was separated from Osmunda after modern phylogenetic studies demonstrated that Osmunda was not monophyletic.

tokens.name: Waterwheel plant
tokens.title: Aldrovanda vesiculosa
tokens.description: Aldrovanda vesiculosa, commonly known as the waterwheel plant, is the sole extant species in the flowering plant genus Aldrovanda of the family Droseraceae. The plant captures small aquatic invertebrates using traps similar to those of the Venus flytrap. The traps are arranged in whorls around a central, free-floating stem, giving rise to the common name.

The traps are arranged in whorls around a central, free-floating stem, giving rise to the common name.

tokens.title: Isopogon
tokens.description: Isopogon, commonly known as conesticks, conebushes or coneflowers, is a genus of about forty species of flowering plants in the family Proteaceae, and are endemic to Australia. They are shrubs with rigid leaves, bisexual flowers in a dense spike or cone and the fruit is a small, hairy nut.

tokens.description: Persoonia, commonly known as geebungs or snottygobbles, is a genus of about one hundred species of flowering plants in the family Proteaceae. tokens.name: Marsh rose
tokens.title: Orothamnus
tokens.description: Orothamnus or marsh rose is a monotypic fynbos genus in the family Proteaceae occurring in the Kogelberg and Kleinrivier Mountains of Hottentots-Holland in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It is an erect, sparsely branched shrub to 5 m tall. Orothamnus zeyheri is extremely rare and endangered and appears on CITES Appendix I.

tokens.name: Ferraria
tokens.title: Ferraria
tokens.description: Ferraria is a genus of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Iridaceae, native to tropical and southern Africa. They are herbaceous corm-bearing plants growing to 30 to 45 cm tall. Some species have an unpleasant scent similar to rotting meat and are pollinated by flies, while others have a pleasant scent.
tokens.image_credit: Winfried Bruenken (Amrum) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Hesperantha
tokens.description: Hesperantha is a genus of cormous flowering plants in the family Iridaceae. The genus name is derived from the Greek words hesperos, meaning evening, and anthos, meaning flower. There are approximately 79 species, mostly native to southern Africa, but with four species reaching tropical Africa.

tokens.name: Pillansia
tokens.title: Pillansia
tokens.description: Pillansia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Iridaceae, first described as a genus in 1914. It contains only one known species, Pillansia templemannii, which is endemic to the Western Cape province in South Africa. It is an evergreen, perennial plant with an underground corm and highly distinctive, star symmetrical, cup shaped orange flowers about 5 cm across.
tokens.image_credit: Tony Rebelo · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Ranunculus lyallii

tokens.title: Pancratium maritimum

Its range on the coasts of the Black Sea includes southern Bulgaria, northern Turkey and Georgia.

tokens.title: Sea holly
tokens.description: Eryngium maritimum, also called the sea holly or sea eryngo, is a perennial flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae, native to the coasts of most of Europe and the Mediterranean. Its prickly holly-like leaves and compact flower heads give it the appearance of a thistle. Despite its common name, it is not a holly but an umbellifer.

tokens.title: Cistus
tokens.description: Cistus is a genus of flowering plants in the rockrose family Cistaceae, containing about 34 species and a similar number of natural hybrids. tokens.name: Michelia
tokens.title: Michelia
tokens.description: Michelia is a historical genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Magnoliaceae. The genus included about 50 species of evergreen trees and shrubs, native to tropical and subtropical south and southeast Asia, including southern China. Today it is regarded as a synonym and section of the genus Magnolia.

tokens.title: Asarum europaeum

It is a creeping evergreen perennial with glossy green, kidney shaped leaves and solitary dull purple flowers hidden by the leaves.

tokens.name: Lily of the valley
tokens.title: Lily of the valley
tokens.description: Lily-of-the-valley, Convallaria majalis, is a Eurasian woodland plant. Growing to 15 to 35 cm tall, the plant produces sweetly scented racemes of pendulous, bell-shaped white flowers. Due to the concentration of potent cardiac glycosides, the plant is highly poisonous if consumed.
tokens.image_credit: Ivar Leidus · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Spring sowbread
tokens.title: Cyclamen repandum
tokens.description: Cyclamen repandum, the spring sowbread, is a species of flowering plant in the family Primulaceae, native to southern Europe and some Mediterranean islands. It is the most widespread of a group of cyclamens with wide, heart-shaped leaves, often coarsely toothed or lobed, and late spring-blooming flowers with long, slender petals.

tokens.title: Thalictrum alpinum
tokens.description: Thalictrum alpinum is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family known by the common names alpine meadow-rue and arctic meadow-rue. It is native to Arctic and alpine regions of North America and Eurasia, including Alaska, northern Canada, and Greenland, and it occurs in cold, wet, boggy habitats in high mountains further south.

tokens.name: Labrador tea
tokens.title: Labrador tea
tokens.description: Labrador Teais a common name for three closely related evergreen shrubs in the genus Rhododendron as well as a herbal tea traditionally made from their leaves. All three species belong to the heath family (Ericaceae) and are plants of the subarctic and boreal wetlands.

tokens.name: Dwarf willow
tokens.title: Salix herbacea
tokens.description: Salix herbacea, the dwarf willow, least willow or snowbed willow, is a species of tiny creeping willow adapted to survive in harsh arctic and subarctic environments. Distributed widely in alpine and arctic environments around the North Atlantic Ocean, it is one of the smallest woody plants.

tokens.name: Polar willow
tokens.title: Salix polaris
tokens.description: Salix polaris, the polar willow, is a species of willow with a circumpolar distribution in the high arctic tundra, extending north to the limits of land. South of the Arctic it grows in the mountains of Norway, the northern Ural Mountains, the northern Altay Mountains, Kamchatka, and British Columbia, Canada.

tokens.name: Dark-leaved willow
tokens.title: Salix myrsinifolia
tokens.description: Salix myrsinifolia, known as the dark-leaved willow or myrsine-leaved willow, is a species of willow native to Europe and Western Siberia. It forms a 2 to 5 m high shrub. In the north, it often becomes a tree up to 8 m tall.

tokens.name: Woolly willow
tokens.title: Salix lanata
tokens.description: Salix lanata, the woolly willow, is a subarctic species of willow native to Iceland, the Faeroe Islands and Finland, through to eastern Siberia. In Scotland it can be found in only a few localities of Perthshire, Angus and Aberdeenshire, generally on rocky mountain sides at altitudes of 600 to 900 m.
tokens.image_credit: Robert Matthews · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

In Scotland, UK, it can be found on rocky mountain slopes and cliffs, generally at altitudes of 200 to 900 m. It grows to a height of 1.5 m.

tokens.description: Alnus incana, the grey alder, tag alder or speckled alder, is a species of multi-stemmed, shrubby tree in the birch family, with a wide range across the cooler parts of the Northern Hemisphere. Tolerant of wetter soils, it can slowly spread with runners and is a common sight in swamps and wetlands.

tokens.name: Purple sage
tokens.title: Salvia dorrii
tokens.description: Salvia dorrii, the purple sage or tobacco sage, is a perennial spreading shrub in the family Lamiaceae. It is native to mountain areas in the western United States, particularly northwestern Arizona, New Mexico, and West Texas, found mainly in the Great Basin and southward to the Mojave Desert, growing in dry, well draining soils.

Its small, very dark, reddish-purple flowers generally go unnoticed, and are scented only at night.

tokens.description: Pittosporum tenuifolium is a small evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand– growing up to 10 m (33 ft) – commonly known askōhūhūandblack matipo, and by other Māorinameskohukohuandtawhiwhi. Its small, very dark, reddish-purple flowers generally go unnoticed, and are scented only at night.

tokens.description: Elodea is a genus of eight species of aquatic plants often called the waterweeds, described as a genus in 1803. It is widely used as aquarium vegetation and in laboratory demonstrations of cellular activities.

The fungus produces fruiting bodies in the summer months which are edible and popularly collected.
tokens.image_credit: Rude · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
