tokens.name: Old man of the woods
tokens.title: Strobilomyces strobilaceus
tokens.description: Strobilomyces strobilaceus, also called Strobilomyces floccopus and commonly known as old man of the woods, is a species of fungus in the family Boletaceae. Its fruit bodies are characterized by soft, dark scales on the cap surface. The species is native to Eurasia and North America.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew.M.Hayes · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Satan's bolete
tokens.title: Rubroboletus satanas
tokens.description: Rubroboletus satanas, commonly known as Satan's bolete or the Devil's bolete, is a basidiomycete fungus of the bolete family and one of its most infamous members. It was known as Boletus satanas before its transfer to the new genus Rubroboletus in 2014. Its squat, brightly coloured fruiting bodies are often massive, with a beige velvety cap up to 50 cm across and yellow to orange red pores.
tokens.image_credit: Archenzo · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pig's ears
tokens.description: Gomphus clavatus, commonly known as pig's ears or the violet chanterelle, is an edible species of fungus in the genus Gomphus. Described by Jacob Christian Schaffer in 1774, it was once classified in the genus Cantharellus, though it is not closely related to the chanterelles. The fruit body is vase or fan shaped with wavy edges to its rim.
tokens.image_credit: Vavrin · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Pinctada
tokens.title: Pinctada
tokens.description: Pinctada is a genus of saltwater oysters, marine bivalve mollusks in the family Pteriidae. These pearl oysters have a strong inner shell layer composed of nacre, also known as mother of pearl. They are not closely related to either the edible oysters of family Ostreidae or the freshwater pearl mussels.

tokens.name: Enoki mushroom
tokens.title: Flammulina filiformis
tokens.description: Flammulina filiformis, commonly called enoki mushroom or enokitake, is a species of agaric in the family Physalacriaceae. Until recently it was considered conspecific with the European Flammulina velutipes, but DNA sequencing has shown that the two are distinct. It is widely cultivated as an edible mushroom in East Asia, where it is included in Japanese and Chinese cuisine.
tokens.image_credit: Stu's Images · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Lingzhi
tokens.title: Lingzhi (mushroom)
tokens.description: Lingzhi, Ganoderma sichuanense, also known as reishi, is a polypore bracket fungus native to East Asia belonging to the genus Ganoderma. Its reddish brown, varnished, kidney shaped cap with bands and a peripherally inserted stem give it a distinct fan like appearance. When fresh, it is soft, cork like and flat.

tokens.name: Purple-spored puffball
tokens.title: Calvatia cyathiformis
tokens.description: Calvatia cyathiformis, or purple-spored puffball, is a large saprobic species of Calvatia. This terrestrial puffball has purplish or purple-brown spores, which distinguish it from other large Agaricales. It is found in North America and Australia, mostly in prairie or grassland environments.
tokens.image_credit: John Hill · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Mosaic puffball
tokens.title: Mosaic Puffball
tokens.description: Handkea utriformis, synonymous with Lycoperdon utriforme, is a species of puffball in the family Lycoperdaceae. A rather large mushroom, it may reach up to 25 cm broad by 20 cm tall. It is commonly known as the mosaic puffball, referencing the polygonal segments on the outer surface of the fruiting body as it matures.
tokens.image_credit: Luridiformis at English Wikipedia · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Shaggy ink cap
tokens.title: Coprinus comatus
tokens.description: Coprinus comatus, commonly known as the shaggy ink cap, lawyer's wig, or shaggy mane, is a species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out. The white caps are covered with scales, the origin of its common names.
tokens.image_credit: Dr. Hans-Günter Wagner · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Common ink cap
tokens.title: Common Ink Cap
tokens.description: Coprinopsis atramentaria, commonly known as the alcohol inky cap, common ink cap, tippler's bane, or inky cap, is a species of fungus. It is the second best-known ink cap after Coprinus comatus, its former congener. The grey-brown cap is initially bell-shaped before opening, after which it flattens and disintegrates.
tokens.image_credit: Michael Palmer · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cauliflower mushroom
tokens.title: Cauliflower Mushroom
tokens.description: Sparassis, also known as cauliflower mushroom, is a genus of parasitic and saprobic mushroom characterised by its unique shape and appearance and is found around the globe. Its appearance can be described as similar to a sea sponge, a brain or a head of cauliflower, hence its popular name. It is increasingly cultivated and sold in Korea, Japan, the United States and Australia.
tokens.image_credit: AL'S · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Octopus stinkhorn
tokens.title: Clathrus archeri
tokens.description: Clathrus archeri, commonly known as octopus stinkhorn or devil's fingers, is a species of fungus in the family Phallaceae. First described by Miles Joseph Berkeley in 1859 from specimens collected in Tasmania, its current binomial name was established in 1980. The fruiting bodies first resemble white eggs from which four to eight arms later emerge, reaching up to 10 cm in length.
tokens.image_credit: de:Benutzer:Oilys · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Psilocybe cubensis
tokens.title: Golden Teacher
tokens.description: Psilocybe cubensis, commonly known as the magic mushroom, golden halo or gold cap, is a species of psilocybin mushroom of moderate potency whose principal active compounds are psilocybin and psilocin. It belongs to the fungus family Hymenogastraceae and was previously known as Stropharia cubensis. It is the best known psilocybin mushroom due to its wide distribution and ease of cultivation.
tokens.image_credit: Alan Rockefeller · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Funeral bell
tokens.title: Galerina marginata
tokens.description: Galerina marginata, known colloquially as funeral bell, deadly skullcap, autumn skullcap or deadly galerina, is a species of extremely poisonous mushroom forming fungus in the family Hymenogastraceae of the order Agaricales. Before 2001, G. autumnalis, G. oregonensis, G. unicolor and G. venenata were thought to be distinct species, but phylogenetic analysis showed that they are all the same species.
tokens.image_credit: Alan Rockefeller · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sulphur tuft
tokens.title: Hypholoma fasciculare
tokens.description: Hypholoma fasciculare, commonly known as the sulphur tuft or clustered woodlover, is a common woodland mushroom, often in evidence when hardly any other mushrooms are to be found. This saprotrophic small gill fungus grows prolifically in large clumps on stumps, dead roots or rotting trunks of broadleaved trees. It is bitter and poisonous; consuming it can cause vomiting, diarrhea and convulsions.

tokens.description: Trametes versicolor, also known as Coriolus versicolor and Polyporus versicolor, is a common polypore mushroom found throughout the world. Because its shape is similar to that of a wild turkey's tail feathers when spread, it is most commonly referred to as turkey tail.
tokens.image_credit: Jerzy Opioła · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Grifola frondosa
tokens.title: Grifola frondosa
tokens.description: Grifola frondosa, also known ashen-of-the-woods, sheep's head, ram's head, ormaitake (舞茸, "dancing mushroom") in Japanese, is a polypore mushroom that grows at the base of trees, particularly old growth oaks or maples. It is native to China, Europe, and North America.

tokens.name: Birch polypore
tokens.title: Fomitopsis betulina
tokens.description: Fomitopsis betulina, previously Piptoporus betulinus, commonly known as the birch polypore, birch bracket or razor strop, is a common bracket fungus that grows almost exclusively on birch trees. The brackets burst out from the bark of the tree, and these fruit bodies can last for more than a year.

tokens.name: Hon-shimeji
tokens.title: Lyophyllum shimeji
tokens.description: Lyophyllum shimeji, commonly known as the hon-shimeji, is an edible species of fungus in the family Lyophyllaceae that grows in pine forests, often near man-made roads. It was originally only known from Japan, Korea and China, but is now also known from Russia, Scandinavia and other parts of Europe as well as North America. It is particularly widespread in lichen pine forests in Sweden, Finland and Norway.
tokens.image_credit: Tatiana Bulyonkova from Novosibirsk, Russia · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Cloud ear
tokens.title: Cloud Ear Fungus
tokens.description: Auricularia heimuer, also known as heimuer, black wood ear or cloud ear, is a species of fungus in the order Auriculariales. It is commercially cultivated for food in China at a value exceeding 4 billion US dollars per year. The species was previously referred to as the European Auricularia auricula-judae, but the latter is not known to occur in East Asia.

tokens.title: Psilocybe Ingeli

tokens.name: Bitter bolete
tokens.title: Tylopilus felleus
tokens.description: Tylopilus felleus, commonly known as the bitter bolete or the bitter tylopilus, is a fungus of the bolete family. French mycologist Pierre Bulliard described it as Boletus felleus in 1788 before it was transferred into the new genus Tylopilus. It is the type species of Tylopilus and the only member of the genus found in Europe.

tokens.name: Lion shield

tokens.description: Grifola frondosa, also known ashen-of-the-woods, sheep's head, ram's head, ormaitake (舞茸, "dancing mushroom") in Japanese, is a polypore mushroom that grows at the base of trees, particularly old growth oaks or maples. It is native to China, Europe, and North America.

tokens.name: Tinder fungus
tokens.title: Fomes fomentarius
tokens.description: Tinder fungus is a perennial wood-decay fungus found in Europe, Asia, Africa and North America. It produces large, hoof-shaped fruit bodies that are normally brown, and it grows on the trunks of various hardwood trees, causing white rot.
tokens.image_credit: George Chernilevsky · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Amadou
tokens.title: Amadou
tokens.description: Amadou is a spongy material derived from Fomes foment ariusand similar fungi that grow on the bark of coniferous and angiosperm trees, and have the appearance of a horse's hoof (thus the name "hoof fungus"). It is also known as the "tinder fungus" and is useful for starting slow-burning fires.

tokens.name: Basket stinkhorn
tokens.title: Bamboo Fungus
tokens.description: Phallus indusiatus, commonly called the basket stinkhorn, bamboo mushroom, bridal veil or veiled lady, is a species of fungus in the family Phallaceae, known as stinkhorns. The fruit body is characterised by a conical to bell-shaped cap on a stalk and a delicate lacy skirt, or indusium, that hangs from beneath the cap and reaches nearly to the ground.
tokens.image_credit: Vinayaraj · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Netted stinkhorn
tokens.title: Netted Stinkhorn
tokens.description: Phallus duplicatus, commonly known as the netted stinkhorn or wood witch, is a species of fungus in the stinkhorn family. The bell-shaped to oval cap is green-brown and the cylindrical stalk is white. When mature, the cap becomes sticky with a slimy green coating, which attracts flies that disperse its spores.
tokens.image_credit: Walt Sturgeon via Mushroom Observer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Collared earthstar
tokens.title: Collared Earthstar
tokens.description: Geastrum triplex, commonly known as the collared earthstar, saucered earthstar or triple earthstar, is the largest member of the earthstar genus Geastrum, and expanded mature specimens can reach up to 11.5 centimeters across. Immature fruit bodies are spherical, somewhat resembling puffballs with pointed beaks, and are partially or completely buried in the ground.
tokens.image_credit: JJ Harrison (https://www.jjharrison.com.au/) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.description: Geastrum triplex, commonly known as the collared earthstar, saucered earthstar or triple earthstar, is the largest member of the earthstar genus Geastrum, and expanded mature specimens can reach up to 11.5 centimeters across. Immature fruit bodies are spherical, somewhat resembling puffballs with pointed beaks, and are partially or completely buried in the ground.
tokens.image_credit: JJ Harrison (https://www.jjharrison.com.au/) · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rounded earthstar
tokens.title: Rounded Earthstar
tokens.description: Geastrum saccatum, commonly known as the sessile earthstar or rounded earthstar, is a species of mushroom in the genus Geastrum. The opening of the outer layer of the fruiting body in its characteristic star shape is thought to be due to a buildup of calcium oxalate crystals just before dehiscence. It is distinguished from other earthstars by the distinct circular ridge or depression around the central pore.
tokens.image_credit: JJ Harrison (https://www.jjharrison.com.au/) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Rosy earthstar
tokens.title: Reddening Earthstar
tokens.description: Geastrum rufescens, commonly known as the rosy earthstar, is a species of fungus in the family Geastraceae. It was first described scientifically by Christian Hendrik Persoon in 1801. It has a pale pinkish buff to pinkish exoperidium and rays.

tokens.name: Fringed earthstar
tokens.title: Fringed Earthstar
tokens.description: Geastrum fimbriatum, commonly known as the fringed earthstar or the sessile earthstar, is an inedible species of mushroom in the genus Geastrum. First described in 1829, it is distinguished from other earthstars by the delicate fibers that line the circular pore at the top of its spore sac. The species has a widespread distribution in Eurasia and the Americas.
tokens.image_credit: User:Georg_Slickers · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Beaked earthstar
tokens.title: Beaked Earthstar
tokens.description: Geastrum pectinatum is a species of fungus in the earthstar family, commonly known as the beaked earthstar or the beret earthstar for the shape of its spore sac and its prominent protruding peristome. Young specimens are spherical, then the outer layer splits open like a star into 7 to 10 pointed rays that bend back to point downward, revealing a small spore sac 1 to 2.5 cm broad.
tokens.image_credit: Lord Mayonnaise · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Saltshaker earthstar
tokens.title: Saltshaker Earthstar
tokens.description: Myriostoma coliforme, commonly known as the saltshaker earthstar or pepper pot, is a fungal species in the family Geastraceae. Its fruit bodies resemble earthstars, but the spore sac is supported by multiple columns instead of a single one and has multiple ostioles instead of a single apical ostiole.
tokens.image_credit: Michel Langeveld · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Common bird's nest
tokens.title: Common Bird%27s Nest
tokens.description: Crucibulum is a genus in the Nidulariaceae, a family of fungi whose fruiting bodies resemble tiny egg filled bird's nests. Often called splash cups, the fruiting bodies disperse their spores using the energy of falling raindrops. The eggs inside the nests are hard waxy shells containing spores that stick to nearby herbage, increasing the odds of being eaten and dispersed by herbivores.
tokens.image_credit: Paul Gregory · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Dung-loving bird's nest
tokens.title: Dung-loving Bird%27s Nest
tokens.description: Cyathus stercoreus, commonly known as the dung-loving bird's nest or the dung bird's nest, is a species of fungus in the genus Cyathus, family Nidulariaceae. Like other members of its family, its fruiting bodies resemble tiny bird's nests filled with eggs. They are called splash cups because they use the force of falling drops of water to dislodge and disperse their spores.

tokens.name: Fluted bird's nest
tokens.title: Striate Bird%27s Nest
tokens.description: Cyathus striatus, commonly known as the fluted bird's nest, is a common saprobic bird's nest fungus. It resembles a miniature bird's nest with numerous tiny eggs, which are actually lens-shaped bodies that contain spores. It is typically less than a centimeter wide and tall, and grey or brown in color.
tokens.image_credit: John Roper via Mushroom Observer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Carolina false morel
tokens.title: Carolina False Morel
tokens.description: Gyromitra caroliniana, known commonly as the Carolina false morel or big red, is an ascomycete fungus of the genus Gyromitra. It is found in hardwood forests of the southeastern United States, where it fruits in early spring soon after snowmelt. The fruit body appears on the ground in woodland and can grow to massive sizes.

tokens.name: Elfin saddle
tokens.title: Elfin Saddle
tokens.description: Helvella crispa, also known as the fluted white elfin saddle, white saddle or common helvel, is an ascomycete fungus of the family Helvellaceae. It is readily identified by its irregularly shaped whitish cap, fluted stem and fuzzy undersurfaces. It is found in eastern and western North America and in Europe, near deciduous trees in summer and autumn.
tokens.image_credit: Jean-Pol GRANDMONT · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Bleach cup
tokens.title: Veined Cup
tokens.description: Disciotis venosa, commonly known as the bleach cup, veiny cup fungus or cup morel, is a species of fungus in the family Morchellaceae. Fruiting from April, it is often difficult to locate because of its undistinguished brown color. Found in North America and Europe, it appears to favor banks, slopes and sheltered sites.
tokens.image_credit: Holger Krisp · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Oregon white truffle
tokens.title: Oregon White Truffle
tokens.description: Tuber oregonense, commonly known as the Oregon white truffle, is a species of truffle in the genus Tuber. The species was described as new to science in 2010. The fruit bodies are roughly spherical to irregular in shape and resemble small potatoes up to 5 cm in diameter.

tokens.name: Pecan truffle
tokens.title: Pecan Truffle
tokens.description: Tuber lyonii, also known as the American brown truffle or the pecan truffle, is a species of truffle native to North America. It is so named because it is most commonly found in pecan orchards, in association with the pecan tree, though the pecan is not its only symbiote.

tokens.description: Tuber lyonii, also known as the American brown truffle or the pecan truffle, is a species of truffle native to North America. It is so named because it is most commonly found in pecan orchards, in association with the pecan tree, though the pecan is not its only symbiote.

tokens.name: Chinese black truffle
tokens.title: Chinese Truffle
tokens.description: Tuber indicum, commonly known as the Chinese black truffle or the Asian black truffle, is an edible fungus with underground fruiting bodies, characteristic of the Tuber genus. It is found natively in Himalayan India and parts of China. It is sold commercially and often confused with Tuber melanosporum.

tokens.name: Kalahari truffle
tokens.title: Kalahari Truffle

tokens.name: Scarlet elf cup
tokens.title: Scarlet Cup
tokens.description: Sarcoscypha coccinea, commonly known as the scarlet elf cup, scarlet elf cap, or the scarlet cup, is a species of fungus in the family Sarcoscyphaceae of the order Pezizales. It is the type species of the genus Sarcoscypha and has been known by many names since its first appearance in the scientific literature in 1772.

tokens.name: Gemmed Amanita
tokens.title: Amanita gemmata
tokens.description: Amanita gemmata, commonly known as the gemmed amanita or the jonquil amanita, is an agaric mushroom of the family Amanitaceae and genus Amanita. The fruit body has a cap that is a dull to golden shade of yellow, typically 2.5 to 12 centimetres across. The cap surface is sticky when moist and carries white warts which are easily detached.
tokens.image_credit: Scott Darbey from Canada · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Sunshine Amanita
tokens.title: Amanita Aprica
tokens.description: Amanita aprica, also known as the sunshine amanita, is a toxic species of fungus in the family Amanitaceae. The species has a yellow to orange cap with warty remnants of the whitish universal veil. The gills are pale, as is the stipe, which may be wider at the base.
tokens.image_credit: This image was created by user Kevin Trim at Mushroom Observer, a source for mycological images.You can contact this user here. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Conocybe rickenii
tokens.title: Conocybe Rickenii
tokens.description: Conocybe rickenii is a mushroom from the genus Conocybe. Its edibility is disputed, and it has the appearance of a typical little brown mushroom with a small, conical cap and a long, thin stem. In colour it is generally a cream brown, lighter on the stem, with a thin layer of flesh with no distinct smell or taste.
tokens.image_credit: J Milburn (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Morel
tokens.title: Morchella
tokens.description: Morchella, the true morels, is a genus of edible sac fungi in the order Pezizales with a honeycomb appearance due to the network of ridges and pits on their caps. Morels are prized by gourmet cooks, particularly in Catalan and French cuisine, but can be toxic if consumed raw or undercooked.

tokens.name: Termitomyces
tokens.title: Termitomyces
tokens.description: Termitomyces is a genus of basidiomycete fungi in the family Lyophyllaceae, known as termite mushrooms, that are farmed by fungus-growing termites. The termites house and culture the fungi, which in turn provide food for the termites. After rain the fungi often grow mushrooms that are edible and highly regarded for their flavor.

tokens.name: Anemone stinkhorn
tokens.title: Red Starfish Fungus
tokens.description: Aseroe rubra, commonly known as the anemone stinkhorn, sea anemone fungus and starfish fungus, is a common and widespread basidiomycete fungus recognizable for its foul odour of carrion and its sea anemone shape when mature. Found in gardens on mulch and in grassy areas, it resembles a red star-shaped structure covered in brownish slime called gleba on a white stalk. It attracts flies, which spread its spores.
tokens.image_credit: cas Liber · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.image_credit: cas Liber · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Blue pinkgill
tokens.title: Werewere Kokako
tokens.description: Entoloma hochstetteri, also known as the blue pinkgill, sky-blue mushroom or werewere kokako, is a species of mushroom that is native to New Zealand. The small mushroom is a distinctive all-blue colour, while the gills have a slight reddish tint from the spores. The blue colouring of the fruit body is due to azulene pigments.
tokens.image_credit: Mary Smiley via Mushroom Observer · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: False Champignon

tokens.name: Deadly dapperling
tokens.title: Deadly Dapperling
tokens.description: Lepiota brunneoincarnata, the deadly dapperling, is a gilled mushroom of the genus Lepiota in the order Agaricales. Widely distributed in Europe and temperate regions of Asia as far east as China, it grows in grassy areas such as fields, parks and gardens, and is often mistaken for edible mushrooms.

tokens.name: Cordyceps
tokens.title: Cordyceps
tokens.description: Cordyceps is a genus ofascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic. Diverse variants of cordyceps have had more than 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine.

tokens.description: Plateosaurus is a genus of plateosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic epoch of the Triassic period, around 214 to 204 million years ago, in what is now Central and Northern Europe. Plateosaurus is a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, a so-called "prosauropod".

tokens.name: Massospondylus
tokens.title: Massospondylus
tokens.description: Massospondylus is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of southern Africa. It was described by Richard Owen in 1854 from remains discovered in South Africa, and is thus one of the first dinosaurs to have been named.
tokens.image_credit: Paul M. Barrett1, Kimberley E.J. Chapelle, Casey K. Staunton, Jennifer Botha & Jonah N. Choiniere · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Riojasaurus
tokens.title: Riojasaurus
tokens.description: Riojasaurus was a herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur named after La Rioja Province in Argentina where it was found in the Los Colorados Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin by José Bonaparte. It lived during the Late Triassic and grew to about 6.6 metres long.

tokens.title: Eoraptor

tokens.name: Saturnalia
tokens.description: Saturnalia is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur known from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil. It contains one species, Saturnalia tupiniquim. It is one of the earliest known dinosaurs.

tokens.title: Kentrosaurus

tokens.name: Huayangosaurus
tokens.title: Huayangosaurus
tokens.description: Huayangosaurus is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China. It lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, around 165 million years ago, some 20 million years before its famous relative Stegosaurus appeared in North America.
tokens.image_credit: giloun Original uploader was Giloun at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wuerhosaurus
tokens.title: Wuerhosaurus

tokens.name: Miragaia
tokens.title: Miragaia
tokens.description: Miragaia is a genus of long-necked stegosaurid dinosaur. Its fossils have been found in Upper Jurassic rocks in Portugal, in the Lourinha Formation, and possibly also in the Morrison Formation of Wyoming and Utah, United States. Miragaia has the longest neck known for any stegosaurian, with at least seventeen vertebrae.

tokens.name: Ankylosaurus
tokens.title: Ankylosaurus
tokens.description: Ankylosaurus is a genus of armored dinosaur. Its fossils have been found in geological formations dating to the very end of the Cretaceous Period, about 70 to 66 million years ago, in western North America, making it among the last of the non-avian dinosaurs. It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908.

tokens.description: Edmontosaurus, often colloquially and historically known as Anatosaurus or Anatotitan, is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur. It contains two known species: Edmontosaurus regalis and Edmontosaurus annectens. Its fossils are dated to about 84 to 66 million years ago.

tokens.name: Hypacrosaurus
tokens.title: Hypacrosaurus
tokens.description: Hypacrosaurus is an extinct genus of duckbill dinosaur similar in appearance to Corythosaurus. Like Corythosaurus, it had a tall, hollow rounded crest, although not as large and straight. It is known from two species that lived 75.0 to 69.5 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, Canada, and Montana, United States.

tokens.name: Saurolophus
tokens.title: Saurolophus
tokens.description: Saurolophus is a genus of large hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of North America and Asia, in what is now the Horseshoe Canyon and Nemegt formations respectively, about 71.5 to 66 million years ago. It is one of the few dinosaur genera known from multiple continents.

tokens.name: Shantungosaurus
tokens.title: Shantungosaurus
tokens.description: Shantungosaurus is an extinct genus of very large herbivorous saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Wangshi Group of the Shandong Peninsula in China, containing a single species, Shantungosaurus giganteus. Its stratigraphic interval ranges from the top of the Xingezhuang Formation to the middle of the Hongtuya Formation, middle to late Campanian in age.
tokens.image_credit: Laika ac from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Iguanodon
tokens.title: Iguanodon
tokens.description: Iguanodon, named in 1825, is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur. Its best established species, Iguanodon bernissartensis, lived during the Barremian to early Aptian ages of the Early Cretaceous in Belgium, Germany, Spain, and possibly England, between about 126 and 122 million years ago. It was a large, bulky herbivore up to 9 to 11 metres long.
tokens.image_credit: Ben2 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Ouranosaurus
tokens.title: Ouranosaurus
tokens.description: Ouranosaurus is a genus of herbivorous basal hadrosauriform dinosaur that lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous of modern-day Niger and Cameroon. It measured about 7 to 8.3 metres long and weighed 2.2 metric tons. Two rather complete fossils were found in the Elrhaz Formation, Gadoufaoua deposits, Agadez, Niger, with a third specimen from the Koum Formation of Cameroon.
tokens.image_credit: Filippo Bertozzo​​, Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia​, Matteo Fabbri · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.description: Bagaceratops is a genus of small protoceratopsid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, around 72 to 71 million years ago. Bagaceratops remains have been reported from the Barun Goyot Formation and Bayan Mandahu Formation.

tokens.name: Psittacosaurus
tokens.title: Psittacosaurus
tokens.description: Psittacosaurus is a genus of extinct ceratopsian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of what is now Asia, existing between 125 and 105 million years ago. It is notable for being the most species-rich non-avian dinosaur genus, with up to 13 species known from China, Mongolia, Russia and Thailand.

tokens.name: Yinlong
tokens.title: Yinlong
tokens.description: Yinlong is a genus of basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Period of China. By far the earliest known ceratopsian, it was a small, primarily bipedal herbivore.
tokens.image_credit: HaziiDozen · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Stenopelix
tokens.title: Stenopelix
tokens.description: Stenopelix (meaning "narrowpelvis") is a genus of basal ceratopsian from the Early Cretaceous (late Berriasianstage, approximately 140 million years ago) of Germany. The genus is based on a partial skeleton lacking the skull, and its classification is based on characteristics of the hips.

tokens.name: Pachycephalosaurus
tokens.title: Pachycephalosaurus
tokens.description: Pachycephalosaurus is a genus of pachycephalosaurid ornithischian dinosaur. The type species, P. wyomingensis, is the only known definitive species. It was among the last non-avian dinosaurs, living during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now western North America.

tokens.name: Texacephale
tokens.title: Texacephale
tokens.description: Texacephale is a possibly dubious genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous. Its fossils come from the Aguja Formation of Big Bend National Park, in Texas, and were described in 2010 by Longrich, Sankey and Tanke.
tokens.image_credit: NickLongrich · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Tylocephale
tokens.title: Tylocephale
tokens.description: Tylocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur, a group of dome-headed, herbivorous ornithischians, that lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia. It is known from a partial skull and associated mandible unearthed in 1971 by a Polish-Mongolian Expedition to the Barun Goyot Formation of the Gobi Desert.
tokens.image_credit: PaleoNeolitic · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Goyocephale
tokens.title: Goyocephale
tokens.description: Goyocephale is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurian ornithischian that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous about 76 million years ago. It was first described in 1982 by Altangerel Perle, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska for a disarticulated skeleton with most of a skull, part of the forelimbs and hindlimbs, some of the pelvic girdle, and some vertebrae.
tokens.image_credit: Eduard Solà · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Homalocephale
tokens.title: Homalocephale
tokens.description: Homalocephale is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period of what is now the Nemegt Formation, Mongolia. The genus was described in 1974 by Halszka Osmólska and Teresa Maryańska, and consists of a single species, H. calathocercos.
tokens.image_credit: J. Spencer · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Wannanosaurus
tokens.title: Wannanosaurus

tokens.name: Fruitadens
tokens.title: Fruitadens
tokens.description: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur. The name means "Fruita teeth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado, where its fossils were first found. Its fossils are dated to about 149 to 143 million years ago.

tokens.name: Tianyulong
tokens.title: Tianyulong
tokens.description: Tianyulong is an extinct genus of heterodontosaurid ornithischian dinosaur. The only species is T. confuciusi, whose remains were discovered in Jianchang County, Western Liaoning Province, China. Its fossils are dated to about 168 to 152 million years ago.

tokens.title: Emu

tokens.description: The mallard or wild duck (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout temperate and subtropical North America, Eurasia, and North Africa. It has been introduced to New Zealand, Australia, Peru, Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, the Falkland Islands, and South Africa.
tokens.image_credit: This picture was realized by Richard Bartz by using a Canon EF 70-300mm f/4-5.6 IS USM Lens · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Jeholornis
tokens.title: Jeholornis
tokens.description: Jeholornis is a genus of avialan dinosaurs that lived between approximately 122 and 120 million years ago during the early Cretaceous Period in China. Fossils were first discovered in the Jiufotang Formation and additional specimens have been found in the older Yixian Formation. It was about the size of a turkey, among the largest avialans known until the Late Cretaceous.
tokens.image_credit: Matt Martyniuk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Hesperornis
tokens.title: Hesperornis
tokens.description: Hesperornis is a genus of cormorant-like ornithurans from the Late Cretaceous, spanning the Campanian and possibly the early Maastrichtian. It is one of the lesser-known discoveries of the paleontologist O. C. Marsh in the late 19th century Bone Wars. Its fossils come from the Late Cretaceous marine limestones of Kansas and the marine shales of Canada.

tokens.description: Hesperornis is a genus of cormorant-like ornithurans from the Late Cretaceous, spanning the Campanian and possibly the early Maastrichtian. It is one of the lesser-known discoveries of the paleontologist O. C. Marsh in the late 19th century Bone Wars. Its fossils come from the Late Cretaceous marine limestones of Kansas and the marine shales of Canada.
tokens.image_credit: TotalDino · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Gansus

tokens.name: Pteranodon
tokens.title: Pteranodon
tokens.description: Pteranodon is a genus of pterosaur that included some of the largest known flying reptiles, with P. longiceps having a wingspan of over 6 m. Its fossils are dated to about 86 to 72 million years ago and come from the Niobrara Formation, Kansas and the Pierre Shale, South Dakota.

tokens.name: Pterodactylus
tokens.title: Pterodactylus
tokens.description: Pterodactylus is a genus of extinct pterosaurs, thought to contain only a single species, Pterodactylus antiquus, the first pterosaur to be named and identified as a flying reptile. Its fossil remains have primarily been found in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dating from the Late Jurassic about 150.8 to 148.5 million years ago.
tokens.image_credit: Matthew P. Martyniuk · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.title: Quetzalcoatlus

tokens.title: Hatzegopteryx

tokens.name: Tapejara wellnhoferi
tokens.description: Tapejara is a genus of pterosaur from the Cretaceous period of Brazil, known from the Santana Group, which dates to approximately 127 to 112 million years ago. It had a distinctive semicircular crest above the snout and a bony projection extending backward from the head.

tokens.name: Tupandactylus
tokens.title: Tupandactylus
tokens.description: Tupandactylus is a genus of tapejarid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Crato Formation of Brazil. It is known from two species, T. imperator and T. navigans, though it has been suggested that there is only a single, highly sexually dimorphic species.

tokens.name: Nyctosaurus
tokens.title: Nyctosaurus
tokens.description: Nyctosaurus is a genus of nyctosaurid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of what is now the Niobrara Formation of the mid-western United States, which, during the time Nyctosaurus was alive, was covered in an extensive shallow sea. Some remains of a possible species from Brazil likely belong to a different genus, Simurghia.

tokens.name: Rhamphorhynchus
tokens.title: Rhamphorhynchus
tokens.description: Rhamphorhynchus is a genus of long-tailed pterosaurs in the Jurassic period. Less specialized than contemporary, short-tailed pterodactyloid pterosaurs such as Pterodactylus, it had a long tail, stiffened with ligaments, which ended in a characteristic soft-tissue tail vane.

tokens.name: Mosasaurus
tokens.title: Mosasaurus
tokens.description: Mosasaurus is the type genus of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles. It lived from about 82 to 66 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous. The first fossils of Mosasaurus were found as skulls in a chalk quarry near the Dutch city of Maastricht in the late 18th century.

tokens.description: Liopleurodon is an extinct genus of carnivorous pliosaurid plesiosaurs that lived from the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic to the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic period. The type species is L. ferox, which is probably the only valid species.

tokens.name: Temnodontosaurus
tokens.title: Temnodontosaurus
tokens.description: Temnodontosaurus is an extinct genus of large ichthyosaurs that lived during the Lower Jurassic in what is now Europe and possibly Chile. The first known fossil, a complete skull and partial skeleton, was discovered by Joseph and Mary Anning around the early 1810s in Dorset, England, and it was the very first ichthyosaur to be scientifically described.

tokens.name: Asian lady beetle
tokens.title: Harmonia axyridis
tokens.description: Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle species most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicolored Asian lady beetle. It is one of the most variable lady beetle species in the world, with an exceptionally wide range of color forms. It is native to eastern Asia and has been introduced to North America and Europe to control aphids and scale insects.

tokens.description: The rove beetles, family Staphylinidae, are beetles with short wing covers that leave more than half of the abdomen exposed. With over 68,000 species in about 4,100 genera, they are one of the largest families in the beetle order.

tokens.name: Boll weevil
tokens.title: Boll weevil

tokens.name: Strawberry root weevil
tokens.title: Otiorhynchus ovatus
tokens.description: Otiorhynchus ovatus, the strawberry root weevil, is a weevil of the family Curculionidae, occurring across Canada and the northern United States. Its name comes from its affinity for strawberry plants, which form a large part of its diet.

tokens.description: The eastern yellow jacket or eastern yellow jacket (Vespula maculifrons) is a wasp found in eastern North America. Although most of their nests are subterranean, they are often considered a pest due to their nesting in recreational areas and buildings.

tokens.name: Vespula vulgaris
tokens.title: Vespula vulgaris

It is sometimes known in English as the European wasp, but the same name is used for the species Vespula germanic a or German wasp.

tokens.title: European hornet

tokens.name: Apple maggot
tokens.title: Apple maggot
tokens.description: The apple maggot (Rhagoletis pomonella), also known as the railroad worm (but distinct from the Phrixothrix beetle larva, also called railroad worm), is a species of fruit fly, and a pest of several types of fruits, mostly apples. This species evolved about 150 years ago through a sympatric shift from the native host hawthorn to the domesticated apple species Malus domestica in the northeastern United States.

This species evolved about 150 years ago through a sympatric shift from the native host hawthorn to the domesticated apple species Malus domestica in the northeastern United States.
tokens.image_credit: Joseph Berger, Bugwood.org · CC BY 3.0 us · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Snakefly
tokens.title: Snakefly
tokens.description: Snakeflies are a group of predatory insects comprising the order Raphidioptera, from Ancient Greek ῥαφίς (rhaphís), meaning "needle", and πτερόν (pterón), meaning "wing", with two extant families: Raphidiidae and Inocelliidae, consisting of roughly 260 species. In the past, the group had a much wider distribution than it does now; snakeflies are found in temperate regions worldwide but are absent from the tropics and the Southern Hemisphere.

tokens.description: A rchaea ( ⓘar-KEE-ə) is a domain of organisms. Traditionally, Archaea included only its prokaryotic members, but has since been found to be paraphyletic, as eukaryotes are known to have evolved from archaea.

tokens.name: Mycoplasma
tokens.title: Mycoplasma
tokens.description: Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that lack a cell wall, which makes them naturally resistant to antibiotics such as beta-lactams. They can be parasitic or saprotrophic.
tokens.image_credit: TheKnowHowe · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

tokens.name: Escherichia coli
tokens.title: Escherichia coli
tokens.description: Escherichia coli is a gram-negative, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium commonly found in the lower intestine of warm-blooded organisms. These bacteria are mostly harmless or even beneficial to humans.
tokens.image_credit: Photo by Eric Erbe, digital colorization by Christopher Pooley, both of USDA, ARS, EMU. · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
